Adversative: νῦν μὲν . . . ὕστερον αὐ. μαχήσονται Il. 7.30. Cf. Il. 3.67, etc.: νῦν αὐ. πανύστατος Od. 9.452, etc.

On the other hand, again: Τρώων αὐ. ἀγορὴ γένετο Il. 7.345. Cf. Il. 5.279, Il. 7.248, Il. 8.55, Il. 11.56, etc.: ἄλλοτε δʼ αὐ. παύομαι Od. 4.102. Cf. Od. 1.111, Od. 5.29 (for your part), Od. 12.282 (as we cannot do here), Od. 16.463, etc.

Particle of transition or continuation: Ἕκτωρ δʼ αὐ. χάρη Il. 3.76. Cf. Il. 1.237, Il. 2.407, Il. 6.73, Il. 8.26, etc.: ἡμῖν δʼ αὐ. ἐπεπείθετο θυμός Od. 2.103. Cf. Od. 2.335, 386, Od. 9.256, Od. 11.21, etc.

Hereafter, in the future, yet: εἴ ποτε δὴ αὐ. χρειὼ ἐμεῖο γένηται Il. 1.340. Cf. Il. 1.578, Il. 5.232, Il. 9.135, Il. 15.16, Il. 23.605, etc.: ἡμεῖς δʼ αὐ. τισόμεθα Od. 13.14. Cf. Od. 8.444, Od. 18.48.
To shout, cry, call Il. 20.50, Il. 21.582.
Of the sound of struck armour Il. 12.160.
To shout or call to: πάντας ἀρίστους Il. 11.258.
Shouting: εἴ ποτʼ ἀϋτῆς σχοίατο Il. 2.97.
Battle: δηΐων ἐν ἀϋτῇ Il. 17.167. Cf. Il. 1.492, Il. 5.732, Il. 6.328, Il. 11.802 = Il. 16.44, Il. 13.621, Il. 14.37, 96, Il. 16.63: Τρώων ὑπεξέφυγον ἀϋτήν Od. 11.383.
On the same day, on that day Il. 18.454: Od. 3.311.
Forthwith, straightway, at once: αὐ. ἆλτο χαμᾶζε Il. 3.29. Cf. Il. 1.118, 199, 539, Il. 2.322, etc.: αὐ. μνηστῆρας ἐπῴχετο Od. 1.324. Cf. Od. 2.367, 379, Od. 3.54, 448, etc.

In the reverse direction, backwards, back, back again: ἴτην Il. 1.347, ἐλεύσεται 425. Cf. Il. 1.522, Il. 2.208, Il. 3.36, Il. 4.19, etc.: ὑποστρέψας Od. 8.301, κυλίνδετο λᾶας Od. 11.598. Cf. Od. 1.317, Od. 3.164, Od. 4.478, Od. 5.430, Od. 9.496, etc.
Back to a former state or condition, again: αὐ. ἐμπνύνθη Il. 5.697. Cf. Il. 4.222, Il. 7.462, Il. 9.368, Il. 12.31, Il. 15.60, etc.: αὐ. ἄρʼ ἕζετο Od. 17.602. Cf. Od. 4.549, Od. 10.461, etc.

Again, once more: ἰόντα Il. 1.27. Cf. Il. 1.513, Il. 7.170, Il. 10.463 (as on former occasions), Il. 18.153, Il. 22.449 (giving changed orders), etc.: αὐ. οἱ πόρον οἶνον Od. 9.360. Cf. Od. 3.161, Od. 9.354, Od. 12.453, Od. 15.439, Od. 19.65, etc.
Adversative: ὅς σʼ αὐ. κτείναιμι (in spite of that) Od. 14.405.
Particle of transition: αὐ. δʼ ἐκ κολεοῖο ἐρυσσάμενος ξίφος (and then . . .) Il. 12.190. Cf. Od. 18.60.

At another time,
on some future occasion, another day: μεταφρασόμεσθα καὶ αὐ. Il. 1.140. Cf. Il. 3.440.
Of the wind from bellows Il. 18.471.
Of the blowing of the winds Od. 11.400 = 407.
Of the breath of fire Il. 21.366: Od. 9.389, Od. 16.290 = Od. 19.9, Od. 19.20 (in these three passages referring to smoke).
Of fragrance or odour: κνίσης αὐ. Od. 12.369. Cf. Il. 14.174.
Of the blowing of the winds Od. 3.289.
[αὐτός + ὁδός (with Aeolic smooth breathing). On or by the same way.]
In neut. αὐτόδιον as adv., straightway: αὐ. μιν λούσασθαι ἀνώγει Od. 8.449.
In neut. αὐτόετες as adv., within the same year, in a year's space Od. 3.322.

p.gloss: From the place in which one is.

div.p: With complementary words: αὐ. ἐξ ἕδρης Il. 19.77. Cf. Od. 13.56, Od. 21.420.
On the spot, at once Il. 20.120.

On the spot, there: αὐ. ὀλέσθαι Il. 3.428, λιπέτην (λεῖπε) κατʼ αὐ. (κατά adv. with the vb.) Il. 10.273, Il. 21.201. Cf. Il. 5.847, Il. 14.119, Il. 16.294, 848, Il. 19.403, Il. 20.340, Il. 21.496, Il. 24.673, 707: αὐ. μεῖνεν Od. 4.508, κατʼ αὐ. λιπόντε (see above) Od. 21.90. Cf. Od. 4.302, Od. 9.29, 496, Od. 10.132, Od. 11.187, Od. 12.161, Od. 14.285, 525, Od. 15.327, Od. 17.254, Od. 24.464.
So παρʼ αὐ. (app. by confusion with αὐτόθι, locative of αὐτός): κτενέειν παρʼ αὐ. πάντας ἀρίστους Il. 13.42. Cf. Il. 20.140, Il. 23.147, 640.
A sister of the whole blood Od. 10.137.
A brother of the whole blood Il. 2.706, Il. 3.238, Il. 11.427, Il. 13.534, Il. 14.156, Il. 16.718.
Without being asked, of one's own accord: ἦλθεν Il. 2.408.
Self-acting, self-moving, self-impelled: αὐτόμαται πύλαι μύκον Il. 5.749 = Il. 8.393. Cf. Il. 18.376.
Locative αὐτόφι Il. 12.302. This form as ablative Il. 11.44.
Crasis with ὁ gives ωὐτός Il. 5.396.

div.head: a
div.p: Myself, thyself, himself, etc.: αὐτοὺς ἑλώρια τεῦχε κύνεσσιν (the body being regarded as the real man) Il. 1.4, ὄφρʼ ὅρκια τάμνῃ αὐ. Il. 3.106, ἄστυ καὶ αὐτούς (the city and the men in it) Il. 24.499. Cf. Il. 1.133, 270, 420, 437, 487, 577, etc.: αὐτὴν ἐς θρόνον εἷσεν Od. 1.130, ἐθάμβεον αὐτόν Od. 17.367 (referring especially to his bodily presence or figure). Cf. Od. 1.108, 117, 393, Od. 2.40, 53, 64, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: Joined with the personal pronouns in emphatic use: ἔμʼ αὐτόν Il. 1.271, ἐγὼν αὐ. Il. 7.101, σὺ αὐ. Il. 14.145. Cf. Il. 1.338, Il. 5.459, Il. 6.272, Il. 9.521, etc.: Od. 1.33, 251, Od. 2.190, Od. 8.396, Od. 13.190, etc.
With sb.: αὐτὰς πύλας Il. 12.469, etc.: θεοὶ αὐτοί Od. 1.384, etc.
With proper and place names: αὐτὴν Χρυσηΐδα Il. 1.143. Cf. Il. 2.827, Il. 5.51, etc.: αὐτῆς Ἰθάκης Od. 14.98. Cf. Od. 1.207, Od. 7.70, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: With personal pronouns in reflexive sense: πυργηδὸν σφέας αὐτοὺς ἀρτύναντες Il. 12.43, εὖ ἐντύνασαν ἓ αὐτήν Il. 14.162. Cf. Il. 3.51, Il. 5.64, Il. 8.529, Il. 10.307, Il. 16.47, etc.: Od. 4.244, Od. 8.211, Od. 9.421, etc.

div.head: d
div.p: In genit. strengthening possessive pronouns: πατρὸς κλέος ἠδʼ ἐμὸν αὐτοῦ Il. 6.446, τὰ ς
[ὰ] αὐτῆς ἔργα Il. 6.490, νωΐτερον λέχος αὐτῶν Il. 15.39, etc.: αὐτῶν σφετέρῃσιν ἀτασθαλίῃσιν Od. 1.7, ἑοὶ αὐτοῦ θῆτες Od. 4.643, etc.
By oneself, alone: ὄφρα καὶ αὐ. λέξομαι Od. 23.171.
Left to one's own devices: αὐ. περ ἐὼν προμάχοισιν ἐμίχθη Il. 8.99.
By oneself, without aid or guidance: αὐ. πλάγξομαι Od. 15.311. Cf. Od. 1.53.
By its own virtue: αὐ. ἐφέλκεται ἄνδρα σίδηρος Od. 16.294 = Od. 19.13.
Without compeer: ὄφρα βασιλεύοι αὐ. Od. 22.53.
At one's own will, by one's own authority: αὐ. ἀπούρας Il. 1.356, etc.
Of one's own accord, without bidding: αὐτὼ λαὸν ἀνώγετον . . . Il. 4.287. Cf. Il. 17.254, etc.
Without change, the same: αὐτὰ κέλευθα Il. 12.225. Cf. Il. 23.480: Od. 8.107, Od. 21.366, etc.
With the article: ωὐτὸς ἀνήρ Il. 5.396. Cf. Il. 6.391: ἐκ τοκήων τῶν αὐτῶν Od. 7.55. Cf. Od. 16.334, etc.
So with ὅδε: τοῦδʼ αὐτοῦ λυκάβαντος Od. 14.161 = Od. 19.306.
The very . . .: ἄκρον ὑπὸ λόφον αὐτόν Il. 13.615. Cf. Od. 10.158.

Idiomatically with sb. in comitative dat. or instrumental, with or without σύν, just as it is(was), . . . and all: αὐτῇ κεν γαίῃ ἐρύσαιμι Il. 8.24, αὐτοῖσιν ὄχεσφιν Il. 8.290, Il. 11.699, αὐτῇ σὺν φόρμιγγι Il. 9.194. Cf. Il. 9.542, Il. 14.498, Il. 20.482, Il. 23.8: αὐτῷ φάρει ἀναΐξας Od. 8.186. Cf. Od. 13.118, Od. 14.77, Od. 20.219, Od. 21.54.
As reflexive pronoun: ἄνευ ἕθεν οὐδὲ σὺν αὐτῷ Il. 17.407. Cf. Il. 9.342, Il. 20.55: κλέος αὐτῇ ποιεῖται Od. 2.125. Cf. Od. 4.247.

In unemphatic use as anaphoric pronoun of the 3rd person (never in nom. or at the beginning of a clause), he, she, it, etc.: βούλομαι αὐτὴν οἴκοι ἔχειν Il. 1.112, μάλα τʼ ἔκλυον αὐτοῦ Il. 1.218. Cf. Il. 1.47, 360, Il. 3.25, 436, Il. 5.42, 170, etc.: κήρυκες αὐτοῖσι οἶνον ἔμισγον Od. 1.109, ἀπὸ δʼ ἔσχισεν αὐτήν Od. 4.507. Cf. Od. 1.143, Od. 2.128, 154, Od. 3.22, 249, Od. 4.110, 522, 634, etc.
stand-up (of fighting) ἐν αὐτοσταδίῃ [ὑσμίνῃ], in stand-up fighting Il. 13.325.
Adv. of acc. fem. form αὐτοσχεδίην = αὐτοσχεδόν. Il. 12.192, Il. 17.294: Od. 11.536.
From close at hand, at close quaters: αὐ. κʼ οὐτάζοντο Il. 7.273. Cf. Il. 13.496, 526, Il. 15.386, 708, 746, Il. 17.530: Od. 22.293.
In the same place, where one is or finds oneself: αὐ. ἔμειναν Il. 15.656. Cf. Il. 9.634, Il. 18.488, etc.: ἔσχετʼ αὐ. νηῦς Od. 12.204. Cf. Od. 5.274, Od. 11.152, etc.
On that spot, there: τὸν δεʼ λίπʼ αὐ. Il. 1.428. Cf. Il. 4.292, Il. 5.886, Il. 6.192, Il. 8.207, etc.: αὐ. ἰχθυάᾳ Od. 12.95. Cf. Od. 3.397, Od. 4.639, Od. 5.68, Od. 9.194, etc.
Here: αὐ. ἐνὶ Τροίῃ Il. 2.237. Cf. Il. 2.332, Il. 5.262, Il. 13.751, Il. 18.330, etc.: αὐ. τῷδʼ ἐνὶ δήμῳ Od. 2.317. Cf. Od. 3.427, Od. 5.362, Od. 10.266, Od. 11.332, etc.

On the spot, at once: αὐ. οἱ θάνατον μητίσομαι Il. 15.349. Cf. Il. 16.649,
Il. 17.416, Il. 21.114, etc.: αὐ. κε πότμον ἐπίσποι Od. 2.250. Cf. Od. 4.703, Od. 9.303, Od. 18.212, etc.
[app. for αὐτόχωνος = αὐτοχόανος, fr. αὐτός + χόανος.]
Of a mass of iron, just as it came from the smelting furnace, i.e. in the condition of pig-iron: σόλον Il. 23.826.
Without change, as before, as ever: ἔργον αὐ. ἀκράαντόν [ἐστιν] Il. 2.138. Cf. Od. 13.336.

Just as one or it is (was): αὐ. ἧσθαι δευόμενον Il. 1.133, ὅσσʼ ἔρρεξεν αὐ. (without extraneous aid) Il. 10.50, κτενέει με αὐ. (without effort) Il. 22.125, λευκὸν ἔτʼ αὐ. (fresh from the maker's hand) Il. 23.268, δίδωμί τοι τόδʼ ἄεθλον αὐ. (without a contest) 621. Cf. Il. 5.255, Il. 16.117, Il. 18.198, 338, Il. 24.413: οἴχεται αὐ. (trusting to his own resources) Od. 4.665, αὐ. ἐκείμεθα Od. 13.281, οὐδέ τις ἡμέας αὐ. ἀππέμψει (empty-handed) Od. 15.83, ἦ αὐ. κεῖται ἀκηδής; (without attention) Od. 20.130. Cf. Od. 12.284.–καὶ αὐ., even as it is, without that: καὶ αὐ. νεικεῖ Il. 1.520.
Quite, just: ἄφρονα αὐ. Il. 3.220. Cf. Il. 6.400, Il. 7.100, Il. 22.484, Il. 24.726.
Just, merely, only, doing no more: αὐ. ἐνδίεσαν κύνας Il. 18.584. Cf. Il. 14.18: φαγέμεν αὐ. (has not so much as barely eaten) Od. 16.143. Cf. Od. 6.143, Od. 14.151, Od. 17.309.

To no end or purpose, idly, uselessly, vainly: αὐ. ἐριδαίνομεν Il. 2.342, κακὸν ἤμυνε καὶ αὐ. Il. 9.599. Cf. Il. 13.104, 810, Il. 15.128, 513, Il. 17.633, Il. 21.474, Il. 23.74: αὐ. ἄχθος ἀρούρης (a useless cumberer of the ground) Od. 20.379. Cf. Od. 16.313.
Just for that, idly: εὔχεαι Il. 11.388. Cf. Il. 17.450.
Idly, without justification: αὐ. σε κλέος ἐσθλὸν ἔχει Il. 17.143. Cf. Il. 20.348.
Idly, thoughtlessly, lightly: σῖτον ἔδοντας μὰψ αὐ. Od. 16.111.
To be squalid or dirty Od. 24.250.
To get fire, get a light: ἵνα μή ποθεν ἄλλοθεν αὕῃ (αὔῃ) Od. 5.490.
Pple. ἀΰσας, -αντος (ῡ) Il. 2.334, Il. 4.508, Il. 6.66, Il. 11.285, etc.
To shout, cry, call: ἀϋσάντων ὑπʼ Ἀχαιῶν Il. 2.334, ἤϋσεν Ἥρη Il. 5.784. Cf. Il. 6.110, Il. 8.227, Il. 11.10, Il. 14.147, Il. 18.217, Il. 21.307, etc.: Od. 6.117, Od. 24.530.
Of the sound of struck armour: ἀσπὶς ἄϋσεν Il. 13.409. Cf. Il. 13.441.
To shout or call to: αὖεν ἑταίρους Il. 11.461, Il. 13.477. Cf. Od. 9.65.
Imp. mid. with hyphaeresis and uncontracted prefix ἀποαίρεο (for ἀποαιρέεο) Il. 1.275.
Infin. with uncontracted prefix ἀποαιρεῖσθαι Il. 1.230.
To take away or remove: θυρεόν Od. 9.313, σῖτον Il. 14.455.

div.head: a
div.p: To take away or remove, effect deprivation of: γέρας ἀφαιρήσεσθαι Il. 1.161. Cf. Il. 16.54, Il. 23.544: Od. 12.64.

div.head: b

p.gloss: To take away or remove from.

div.p: With genit.: τεύχεʼ ὤμοιιν ἀφελέσθαι Il. 5.622 = Il. 13.511. Cf. Il. 16.560: Od. 22.219.

div.head: c
div.p: With double acc. of what is taken away and of the person deprived of it: ὡς ἔμʼ ἀφαιρεῖται Χρυσηΐδα Il. 1.182. Cf. Il. 1.275, Il. 22.18.
With the personal acc. to be supplied: δῶρʼ ἀποαιρεῖσθαι [κεῖνον] ὅς τις . . . Il. 1.230.
With this acc. alone: ἐπεί μʼ ἀφέλεσθέ γε δόντες Il. 1.299.
Dat. sing. fem. pple. ἀφαμαρτούσῃ Il. 6.411.
To discharge a missile vainly, miss one's aim: οὐδʼ ἀφάμαρτε Il. 11.350, Il. 13.160, Il. 14.403, Il. 16.322, Il. 21.591, Il. 22.290, ἀπήμβροτε δουρί Il. 16.477.
With genit.: τοῦ Il. 8.119, 302, Il. 15.521, Il. 21.171, αὐτοῦ Il. 16.466.
With dat.: ὑμῖν ὅδε μῦθος Od. 16.387.
Caused to disappear, made away with Il. 6.60, Il. 20.303.

Quickly, speedily, soon, at once, forthwith: ἕζετο Il. 1.349, ἵπποισι τάθη δρόμος (i.e. directly they had turned) Il. 23.375. Cf. Il. 1.594, Il. 2.453 = Il. 11.13, Il. 10.537, Il. 12.221, Il. 17.392, 750, Il. 19.405, Il. 22.270, Il. 24.446: οἴχεται Od. 1.410. Cf. Od. 2.95 = Od. 24.130, Od. 3.456, Od. 4.85, Od. 5.482, Od. 6.49, Od. 8.270, 409, Od. 9.328, Od. 10.122, Od. 11.274, Od. 17.305, Od. 19.140, Od. 21.307.
Of a surety, truly: ἀ. κε δοῦναι βουλοίμην Il. 23.593. Cf. Il. 13.814, Il. 17.417: ἀ. σφι τόδε λώϊόν ἐστιν Od. 2.169.
In vague intensifying sense: ἔφθη ὀρεξάμενος . . . ὦμον ἀ. (right into the . . .) Il. 16.323, ἀ. κλονέοντο πεφυζότες (in wild confusion) Il. 21.528.
[app. comp. from, and with sense due to the notion of speed implicit in, ἄφαρ.]
In superl.: ἀφαυρότατος Ἀχαιῶν Il. 15.11. Cf. Od. 20.110.
In comp.: ἵνα μή οἱ ἀφαυρότερον βέλος εἴη Il. 12.458 (μὴ ἀ. = the more effective, being comp. in dependent form of οὐκ ἀφαυρός, which by litotes = effective).
Acc. sing. masc. pres. pple. ἁφόωντα.
To handle, turn over: ἀσπίδα Il. 6.322.
[ἀφ-, ἀπο- 1 + ἡ-, ἵημι1. The sender forth.]
The Archer. Name of Apollo Il. 9.404.
Not liable to decay, imperishable Il. 2.46, 186, Il. 5.724, Il. 13.22, Il. 14.238, Il. 18.370.
Of immaterial things: κλέος (everlasting) Il. 9.413, μήδεα (that cannot come to nought) Il. 24.88.
Fem. pl. pres. pple. ἀφιεῖσαι Od. 7.126.
3 sing. subj. ἀφήῃ Il. 17.631. ἀφέῃ Il. 16.590.
3 sing. opt. ἀφείη Il. 3.317, Il. 20.464. From ἀφιέω
To throw, hurl, launch (a missile): ἔγχος Il. 3.317. Cf. Il. 8.133, Il. 10.372, Il. 16.590, Il. 17.631, Il. 23.432: Od. 24.539.
Absol., to make one's throw Il. 23.841.
With genit. of the throwing limb: ἄκοντα χειρὸς ἀφῆκεν Il. 21.590. Cf. Il. 13.410.
To send from one-self, let fall: ἔγχος Il. 21.115. Cf. Il. 12.221.
To send forth, cause to cease: μένος [ἔγχεος] Il. 13.444 = Il. 16.613 = Il. 17.529.
To get rid of, slake (thirst): δίψαν Il. 11.642.
In mid., to loose (a part of oneself) from.
With genit.: δειρῆς οὐκ ἀφίετο πήχεε Od. 23.240.
To send away, dismiss (a person) Il. 1.25 = Il. 1.379, Il. 2.263, Il. 11.702.
To let go, set free: ζωόν Il. 20.464.
To be in the condition of having come to, arrived at, reached, to find oneself at, be at, a specified place: τίπτε δεῦρʼ ἀφικάνεις; Il. 14.43.
2 sing. aor. ἀφίκεο Od. 1.171, Od. 14.188, Od. 15.489.
To come to an indicated place: ὁπποίης ἐπὶνηὸς ἀφίκεο (came here) Od. 1.171 = Od. 14.188.
To go, proceed, take one's way.
With preps.: ἐς Ὀλυμπον Od. 20.55, γαῖαν ὕπο Od. 20.81.
With acc. of the place: ἄλλων δῆμον Od. 15.228 (fled to . . .), Od. 16.382 (be forced to flee to . . .).
To present oneself before, come into the presence of: μνηστῆρας Od. 1.332 = Od. 18.208 = Od. 21.63, Od. 16.414. Cf. Od. 21.25.

div.head: a
div.p: With notion of attainment prominent, to come to, arrive at, reach, find oneself at, be at, a specified place: οὐδʼ ἢν ἔνθʼ ἀφίκηαι Il. 8.482.

div.head: c
div.p: Of sound: ὁπότʼ ἂν νῆας ἐμὰς ἀφίκηται ἀϋτή Il. 16.63.
Of reaching a mark in a contest Od. 8.202.
Of a feeling, to come upon, seize, affect: ὅτε μʼ ἄλγος ἀφίκετο Il. 18.395.

div.head: A
div.p: 3 pl. aor. subj. mid. ἀποστήσωνται Il. 13.745.

div.head: I
div.p: In form (A) To get weighed out to oneself; hence, to exact payment of: χρεῖος Il. 13.745 (i.e. take their revenge for what they suffered).

div.head: II
div.p: In pres. mid. and the other forms (B)
To keep oneself separated (by a specified distance) from.
With genit.: ὅσσον τροχοῦ ἵππος ἀφίσταται Il. 23.517.

div.head: a
div.p: To stand apart or aloof: νόσφιν ἀφεστήκει Od. 11.544.

div.head: b
div.p: To stand idle instead of fighting: τίπτε ἀφέστατε; Il. 4.340. Cf. Il. 13.738, Il. 14.132, Il. 15.672, 675, Il. 21.391.

div.head: c
div.p: To keep apart or aloof from each other: πολλὸν ἀφεσταότες Il. 17.375.
A tall ornamental projection in which the stern of a ship ran up (app. = κόρυμβον) Il. 15.717.
With genit.: βιότοιο (in . . .) Il. 5.544, Il. 6.14, Il. 14.122.
So in comp.: ἐλαφρότεροι πόδας εἶναι ἢ ἀφνειότεροι χρυσοῖο (light of foot rather than rich in . . .) Od. 1.165.
To put off (one's armour): ἔντεα Il. 23.26.
To set forth, depart: ἀφορμηθέντος ἀκοῦσαι Od. 2.375, Od. 4.748.
acc. sing. masc. pres. pple. ἁφάω.
To act senselessly, foolishly or thoughtlessly Il. 9.32: Od. 7.294.
Senselessly, foolishly, recklessly Il. 3.436, Il. 12.62, Il. 23.320, 426.
Senseless, lacking the perceptive powers proper to the living: νεκροί Od. 11.476.
Senselessness, folly, recklessness, thoughtlessness, heedlessness: πολέμοιο (in war) Il. 2.368.
In pl. in sim. sense: παρέδραμεν ἀφραδίῃσιν Il. 10.350. Cf. Il. 5.649, Il. 10.122, Il. 16.354: αὐτῶν ἀπωλόμεθʼ ἀφραδίῃσιν Od. 10.27. Cf. Od. 9.361, Od. 14.481, Od. 17.233, Od. 19.523, Od. 22.288.
To act senselessly, foolishly or recklessly Il. 2.258, Il. 7.109.
To be out of one's mind, be beside oneself Od. 20.360.
To be covered with foam Il. 11.282.
Unworthy to be a member of a clan: ἀ. ἀθέμιστος ἀνέστιος Il. 9.63.
Sexual love: εἰς ὅ κʼ ἐκλελάθωντʼ Ἀφροδίτης Od. 22.444.
To act senselessly or foolishly: Ζηνὶ μενεαίνομεν ἀφρονέοντες Il. 15.104.
Foam formed in a lion's mouth Il. 20.168.
In pl. in sim. sense Od. 16.278, Od. 24.457.
Leafless, stripped of leaves: σχίζῃσιν Il. 2.425.
App., drift-wood; or perh., mud Il. 11.495.
3 sing. aor. ἤφυσε Il. 13.508, Il. 17.315. ἄφυσσε Il. 14.517: Od. 2.379.
1 pl. -άμεθα Od. 9.85, Od. 10.56. Masc. pl. pple. ἀφυσσάμενοι Od. 4.359.
To draw off (wine etc.): νέκταρ ἀπὸ κρητῆρος Il. 1.598. Cf. Od. 2.349, 379, Od. 9.9, 165, 204.
In mid.: ἐκ κρητῆρος ἀφυσσόμενοι δεπάεσσιν (in cups) Il. 3.295. Cf. Il. 10.579, Il. 16.230, Il. 23.220.
In pass.: πολλὸς ἠφύσσετο οἶνος Od. 23.305.
To get together, heap up (wealth) Il. 1.171.
In mid., to bring or gather together (about one): ἀμφὶ φύλλα ἠφυσάμην Od. 7.286.
Of a weapon, to let out (the entrails) like water: διὰ δʼ ἔντερα χαλκὸς ἤφυσεν Il. 13.508 = Il. 17.315. Cf. Il. 14.517.
Some kind of prickly shrub Od. 14.10.
[conn. in popular etymology with the river Acheron, from which Heracles was said to have brought the tree.]
A tree, said to be the white poplar Il. 13.389 = Il. 16.482.
To be grieved or troubled, grieve, sorrow. Only in pres. pple.: θυμὸν ἀχεύων (in his heart) Il. 5.869, Il. 18.461, Il. 23.566. Cf. Il. 9.612, Il. 24.128: Od. 2.23, Od. 4.100, Od. 11.88, Od. 21.318.
With genit. of person grieved for: ἄνακτος Od. 14.40. Cf. Od. 16.139.
3 sing. aor. ἤκαχε Il. 16.822: Od. 15.357, Od. 16.427.
In aor. act., to cause to grieve, grieve, trouble Il. 16.822: Od. 15.357.

In pres. pple. act. and aor. mid., to be grieved or troubled, be in grief or trouble, grieve, sorrow: κῆρ ἀχέων (in his heart) Il. 5.399. Cf. Il. 2.724, Il. 8.207, Il. 13.344: μνηστῆρες ἀκάχοντο Od. 16.342. Cf. Od. 11.195, Od. 15.361.
With genit. of what is grieved for: Βρισηΐδος Il. 2.694. Cf. Il. 9.567, Il. 16.16, Il. 18.446.
Of a ship, to be laden, have her cargo on board Od. 15.457.
To be weighed down, be in pain or grief: ὀδύνῃσιν Il. 5.354, ἕλκος (app. acc. of part affected, in the wound) 361, κῆρ (in his heart) Il. 11.274 = 400.
With pple. in acc. expressing the cause of grief: ἤχθετο Ἀργείους] δαμναμένους Il. 13.352.
A weight, burden, load: ἀ. ἀρούρης (cumbering the earth) Il. 18.104. Cf. Il. 12.452: Od. 20.379.
A weight or load carried: ἀ. ὕλης Od. 9.233.
The lading or cargo of a ship Il. 20.247: Od. 3.312.
A mist: ἀχλύν οἱ κατέχευεν Od. 7.41. Cf. Od. 20.357.

In reference to blinding or to the mist of death: κατʼ ὀφθαλμῶν κέχυτʼ ἀ. Il. 5.696, ἀπʼ ὀφθαλμῶν νέφος ἀχλύος ὦσεν (the cloud of mist) Il. 15.668. Cf. Il. 5.127, Il. 16.344, Il. 20.321, 341, 421: Od. 22.88.
To become shrouded in darkness: ἤχλυσε πόντος Od. 12.406 = Od. 14.304.
In pl., chaff: καρπόν τε καὶ ἄχνας Il. 5.501. Cf. Il. 5.499.
With genit. of person grieved for: ἑταίρου Il. 8.125 = 317. Cf. Il. 13.403, Il. 15.651, Il. 17.459: Od. 11.558, Od. 14.376.
With acc. expressing the cause of grief: τὸ δʼ ἐμὸν κῆρ ἄχνυται, ὅτε . . . Il. 6.524.
To be in trouble Od. 18.256 = Od. 19.129.

Pain of the mind, grief, sorrow, trouble, distress: Πηλεΐωνι ἀ. γένετο Il. 1.188, σέθεν (for thee) Il. 4.169. Cf. Il. 2.171, Il. 6.336, Il. 8.124, Il. 10.145, Il. 13.581, etc.: Od. 4.108, 716, Od. 8.541, Od. 15.358, Od. 18.274, etc.
In pl., sorrows, troubles: ἄχεʼ ἄκριτα Il. 3.412, Il. 24.91. Cf. Il. 6.413: Od. 19.167.

A subject of grief: ἀ. μοί ἐστιν Il. 16.55. Cf. Il. 5.759, Il. 9.249: Od. 22.345.–
A subject or cause of resentment: ἕνεκʼ ἀλλοτρίων ἀχέων (in a quarrel not his own) Il. 20.298.
In neut. ἀχρεῖον as adv.: ἀ. ἰδών (looking (about him) like one dazed, with helpless look) Il. 2.269: ἀ. ἐγέλασσεν (a forced laugh (to cover embarrassment in announcing her intention)) Od. 18.163.

Adv., utterly, completely: τένοντε ἀ. ἀπηλοίησεν Il. 4.522, ἀπʼ ὀστέον ἀ. ἄραξεν Il. 16.324, γράψεν οἱ ὀστέον ἀ. (app. implying that though the wound was a superficial one (a portion of) the bone was destroyed) Il. 17.599.
Prep. with genit., until, up to: κνέφαος Od. 18.370.

In the reverse direction, backwards, back, back again: ἀπονοστήσειν Il. 1.60, ἐς κουλεὸν ὦσε ξίφος 220. Cf. Il. 3.32, 35, Il. 4.392, Il. 6.467, Il. 10.211, etc.: ἐς πόντον ἐδύσετο Od. 5.352. Cf. Od. 1.276, Od. 3.307, Od. 4.261, Od. 9.314, Od. 11.18, Od. 17.461, etc.
In reference to the direction in which one looks, backwards: ὁρόων Il. 3.325.
Of a period of time completing its cycle: ἀ. περιτελλομένου ἔτεος Od. 11.295 = Od. 14.294.
Back to a former state or condition, again: ἀπέλυσεν Il. 6.427, ἐνὶ χώρῃ ἕζετο Il. 23.349. Cf. Il. 16.54, 58, 86, Il. 22.277, etc.: ἄνδρες ἐγένοντο Od. 10.395. Cf. Od. 16.175, Od. 18.152.
In reference to making atonement or effecting reconciliation: ἀρέσαι Il. 9.120 = Il. 19.138.
Again, once more: ἐπόρουσεν Il. 3.379. Cf. Il. 5.505, Il. 17.543, Il. 21.33: ὤσασκεν Od. 11.599. Cf. Od. 8.90, 92.
A mesh of a net Il. 5.487.
Of Ocean, flowing back on himself as encircling the earth Il. 18.399: Od. 20.65.
Going back, returning: ἄψορροι ἀπονέοντο Il. 3.313, Il. 24.330. Cf. Il. 21.456.

div.head: a
div.p: Back, back again: ἀ. θυμὸς ἀγέρθη Il. 4.152, ἀ. ἔβη προτὶ Ἴλιον Il. 7.413. Cf. Il. 12.74, Il. 16.376, Il. 21.382: Od. 10.558 = Od. 11.63.
[ἀ-, ἁ-, (σ)α-. Cf. ἄδην, ἅδην and L. satis.]
Also 1 pl. subj. ἕωμεν (disyllable) Il. 19.402, formed by metathesis of quantity fr. ἥομεν fr. ἡ- = (σ)α-.
To sate, satiate: κύνας Il. 11.818, Il. 24.211.
To sate with, give a fill of.
With genit.: αἵματος Il. 5.289 = Il. 20.78 = Il. 22.267. Cf. Il. 9.489, Il. 18.281.
To sate oneself with, take or have one's fill of.
With genit.: χροός (of spears personified) Il. 11.574 = Il. 15.317, Il. 21.70, 168, πολέμοιο Il. 19.402, γόοιο Il. 23.157.

div.head: a
div.p: A blanket: κεκαλυμμένος οἰὸς ἀώτῳ Od. 1.443.
App. in generalized sense: λίνοιο ἄωτον (a bed-covering of linen) Il. 9.661.

div.head: b
div.p: οἰὸς ἀ. in sense sling Il. 13.599.
To say, speak, utter: ταῦτα Il. 4.355, ἄρτια Il. 14.92: ἔπος εἴ τι βέβακται δεινόν Od. 8.408. Cf. Od. 4.32, 206, 837 = Od. 11.464, Od. 8.240, Od. 14.127, 157, Od. 17.461, Od. 18.332 = 392.
With double acc. of thing said and person addressed: ταῦτά μʼ ἐβάζετε Il. 16.207. Cf. Il. 9.58.
= βαθυδινήεις.: ποταμός Il. 20.73, Il. 21.143, 212, 228, 329: Ὠκεανῷ Od. 10.511.
Deep-girded, so girt that the upper part of the robe falls down in a deep fold (κόλπος) over the girdle.

p.gloss: Whose robe falls down in a deep fold over the girdle (cf. βαθύζωνος.).

div.p: Having meadows with deep rich grass: Ἄνθειαν Il. 9.151 = 293.
With a deep rich crop: τέμενος Il. 18.550 (v.l. βασιλήϊον).
To lower the surface of Il. 23.421.
Where we should rather say high: αὐλῆς (high-walled) Il. 5.142: Od. 9.239, 338.
Sim., app., of a storm, reaching from earth to heaven Il. 11.306.
Deep, extending far inwards: ἠϊόνος Il. 2.92.
Deeply indenting the land: κόλπον Il. 2.560.
Growing thickly, affording thick covert: ὕλης Il. 5.555. Cf. Il. 11.415, Il. 15.606, Il. 16.766, Il. 20.491, Il. 21.573: Od. 17.316.
Forming a thick deposit: ἀμάθοιο Il. 5.587.
With deep soil: νειοῖο Il. 10.353, Il. 18.547.
Forming a deep, rich crop: λήϊον Il. 2.147, Il. 11.560: Od. 9.134.
Thick, obstructing vision: ἠέρα Il. 20.446. Cf. Il. 21.7: Od. 9.144.
With banks thickly set with rushes: Ἀσωπόν Il. 4.383.

div.head: A
div.p: 3 sing. fut. in mid. form βήσεται Il. 2.339.
1 pl. ἔβημεν Od. 14.241. βῆμεν Od. 3.131, Od. 9.85, 150, Od. 10.56, etc.

div.head: B
div.p: 3 sing. aor. βῆσε Il. 1.310, Il. 5.164, Il. 16.810.
(ἀμφι-, ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, εἰσ-, εἰσανα-, ἐκ-, ἐκδια-, ἐμ-, ἐξανα-, ἐξαπο-, ἐπεμ-, ἐπι-, ἐσκατα-, κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, ὑπερ-, ὑπερκατα-.)

div.head: I
div.p: Intrans. in all forms except those under (B).

To go, go one's way, take one's way: παρὰ θῖνα θαλάσσης Il. 1.34. Cf. Il. 1.44, 311, 424, Il. 2.16, 47, Il. 4.443, 495, etc.: οἶκόνδε Od. 1.424. Cf. Od. 1.102, 119, 427, Od. 2.18, 406, Od. 3.131, Od. 9.196, etc.
Of something inanimate: ἰκμὰς ἔβη (i.e. finds its way inwards, making way for the unguent) Il. 17.392.
Of immaterial things, to go, pass. εὐχωλαί Il. 8.229. Cf. Il. 2.339.
So of time: ἐννέα βεβάασιν ἐνιαυτοί (have passed) Il. 2.134.

div.head: a
div.p: In pf. of the state or condition of going: ἔχων εὔληρα βέβηκε (is going, i.e. is driving the chariot) Il. 23.481: περὶ τρόπιος βεβαῶτα (bestriding it and being carried along with it) Od. 5.130.

div.head: b
div.p: In plupf., of being in the act or attitude of going: Οὔλυμπόνδε βεβήκει (was in motion to go, i.e. started or set out to go, took her way) Il. 1.221. Cf. Il. 6.313, 495, Il. 11.446, Il. 16.751, 856 = Il. 22.362, Il. 16.864, Il. 17.706, Il. 22.21, Il. 23.391: Od. 1.360 = Od. 21.354, Od. 8.361, Od. 10.388, Od. 13.164, Od. 15.464, Od. 17.26, 61, Od. 18.185 = Od. 19.503 = Od. 22.433, Od. 19.47 = Od. 20.144, Od. 23.292.
But in strict plupf. sense: Ἄϊδόσδε βεβήκει Od. 3.410 = Od. 6.11.
Without complementary words, strode along Il. 6.513, Il. 11.296, Il. 13.156, Il. 20.161.
To start or set out to go, run, etc.: βῆ θέειν Il. 2.183, βῆ ἰέναι Il. 4.199. Cf. Il. 5.167, Il. 6.296, Il. 13.27, Il. 20.32, Il. 23.229, etc.: Od. 1.441, Od. 2.298, Od. 4.779, Od. 14.87, 501, etc.

To move oneself into a specified position, get on to, into, out of, something: ἐς ἅρματα Il. 5.239, ἐς ἀσαμίνθους Il. 10.576. Cf. Il. 5.364, 745, Il. 6.65, Il. 17.504, Il. 18.532, Il. 23.132, etc.: ἐξ ἀσαμίνθου Od. 3.468. Cf. Od. 3.481, 492, Od. 4.48, Od. 12.229, Od. 21.51, etc.
So with acc.: βήσετο δίφρον (mounted it) Il. 3.262 = 312.
Without the acc.: ἄπιθεν βῆ Ἀχιλλεύς (mounted after him) Il. 19.397.
Of going (on board a ship): ἐπὶ νηὸς ἔβαινεν Il. 13.665. Cf. Od. 2.416, Od. 8.501, Od. 9.177, Od. 11.534, Od. 15.284, 547.
Of disembarking (from a ship): ἐκ νηὸς βῆ Il. 1.439. Cf. Od. 3.12, Od. 13.116.
Sim.: ἐπʼ ἠπείρου βῆμεν Od. 9.85 = Od. 10.56.

div.head: a
div.p: With ἀμφί as prep., to bestride: ἀμφʼ ἑνὶ δούρατι βαῖνεν Od. 5.371.
So, to bestride and protect (a fallen friend) (cf. ἀμφιβαίνω 4, περιβαίνω): ἀμφʼ αὐτῷ βαῖνεν Il. 5.299. Cf. Il. 14.477, Il. 17.4, 359, 510.
Sim. with περί: περὶ πατρόκλῳ βαῖνεν Il. 17.6. Cf. Il. 17.4, 137: Od. 20.14.
Of bestriding the body of a foe with a view to dragging it off: Τρῶες περὶ Πατρόκλῳ βέβασαν Il. 17.286.
(For the time indicated in these cases by the pf. and plupf. cf. (3).)

div.head: α
div.p: To mount a chariot, etc.: ἀνʼ ἔβη Πρίαμος Il. 3.261. Cf. Il. 3.311, Il. 17.541: Od. 6.253.
Sim. with παρά, to mount a chariot(and stand) beside another: πὰρ μαχάων βαινέτω (βαῖνεν) Il. 11.513, 518.
Also with παρά as prep.: πὰρ δέ οἱ Ἶρις ἔβαινεν Il. 5.365.

div.head: β
div.p: To go on board a ship: ἀνʼ αὐτοὶ βάντες (βαίνομεν) Od. 2.419 = Od. 4.579, Od. 11.5. Cf. Od. 13.75.

div.head: α
div.p: To dismount from a chariot: ἐκ δʼ ἔβαν αὐτοί Il. 3.113.

div.head: β
div.p: To disembark from a ship: ἐξ αὐτοὶ βαῖνον Il. 1.437. Cf. Od. 3.11,Od. 4.785, Od. 9.150 = 547 = Od. 12.6, Od. 15.499.

div.head: d
div.p: With μετά of crossing an indicated line: μετὰ δʼ ἄστρα βεβήκει (had crossed the meridian) Od. 12.312, Od. 14.483.

div.head: e
div.p: For περί, παρά see a b.
To come: τίπτε βέβηκας; (hast thou come) Il. 15.90, πόλις ἐπὶ πᾶσα βέβηκε (has come to encounter us) Il. 16.69.

div.head: II
div.p: To cause to take a specified position: ἄν Χρυσηΐδα βήσομεν (let us put her on board) Il. 1.144, ἐς ἑκατόμβην βῆσεν (put it on board) 310, ἐξ ἑκατόμβην βῆσαν (landed it) 438, τοὺς ἐξ ἵππων βῆσεν (thrust or knocked off) Il. 5.164, βήσαμεν ἵππους (brought to a stand, stopped) Il. 11.756, φῶτας βῆσεν ἀφʼ ἵππων Il. 16.810: ἐν τὰ μῆλα ἐβήσαμεν (put them on board) Od. 11.4.
The fruit of the φηγός Od. 10.242, Od. 13.409.
Dat. sing. masc. pple. βαλέοντι Od. 11.608.
3 sing. plupf. (in intensive impf. or aor. sense) βεβλήκει(ν) Il. 4.108, 492, Il. 5.66, 73, 394, 661, Il. 12.401, Il. 14.412, Il. 17.606: Od. 22.258, 275, 286.
2 sing. pf. βέβληαι Il. 5.284, Il. 11.380, Il. 13.251.

Pple. βεβλημένος, -ου Il. 11.475, 592, 659, Il. 12.2, Il. 13.764, Il. 14.63, etc.: Od. 11.535, Od. 19.69. (ἀμφι-, ἀνα-, ἐκ-, ἐμ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, παρα-, παρακατα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συμ-, ὑπερ-, ὑπο-.)
To throw or cast in general: ποτὶ σκῆπτρον βάλε γαίῃ Il. 1.245. Cf. Il. 2.183, Il. 21.51, Il. 22.468, etc.: Od. 5.349, Od. 8.508, Od. 19.63, Od. 20.65, etc.
Of winds, to beat upon so as to throw (together): πυρῆς ἄμυδις φλόγʼ ἔβαλλον Il. 23.217.
To throw or let fly (a missile): χαλκόν Il. 5.317 = 346: βέλος Od. 9.495. Cf. Od. 9.482, 539, Od. 20.62.
In mid., with reciprocal force: βαλλομένων (as they threw at one another) Il. 12.289.
With the missile in dat.: λάεσσιν Il. 3.80. Cf. Il. 12.155: Od. 10.122.
To hurl or throw (a person down): κατὰ μύνητʼ ἔβαλεν Il. 2.692. Cf. Il. 5.588, Il. 8.156: Od. 22.188.
To throw in wrestling Il. 23.727: Od. 4.344 = Od. 17.135.
To hurl from something: ἐκ δίφρου Il. 8.403, 417. Cf. Il. 11.109.
To thrust back from something: ἀπʼ αὐτάων δηΐους Il. 12.264.
To thrust or cause to go into a place: ἐς θάλαμον Od. 22.174.
In reference to things, to throw down, destroy: κατὰ βαλέειν μέλαθρον Il. 2.414. Cf. Il. 9.541.
To send flying, cause to fall: τῆλε κάρη βάλεν Il. 20.482.
To knock off from something: ἀπὸ κρατὸς κυνέην Il. 16.793.
Out of something: ἐκ χειρῶν μάστιγα Il. 23.384.
To thrust or cause to strike against something: πρὸς ἀλλήλας ἔβαλον ὄζους Il. 16.768.
To thrust or urge (one's horses in front or in advance): τοὺς σοὺς [ἵππους] πρόσθε βαλών Il. 23.572.
Intrans. of horses, to thrust themselves forward, rush Il. 23.462.
To put (a ship to sea): νῆας ἐς πόντον βάλλουσιν Od. 4.359.
Of the action of the sea, to beat, drive: ποτὶ πέτρῃ κῦμα Od. 5.415. Cf. Od. 7.279, Od. 9.284, Od. 12.71.

To cause to be somewhere or in some position, to throw, put, place, set: σύν ῥʼ ἔβαλον ῥινούς Il. 4.447, βαλέτην ἐν χερσὶν ἑταίρων Il. 5.574. Cf. Il. 2.376, Il. 5.722, Il. 13.36, Il. 19.394, etc.: θρόνοις ἔνι ῥήγεα Od. 10.352. Cf. Od. 4.455, Od. 7.97, Od. 9.470, Od. 11.194, Od. 12.221, etc.
In mid.: ἐν (ἐπὶ) κλήρους ἐβάλοντο Il. 23.352: Od. 14.209.
In mid., to put oneself in act to do something: σὺν δʼ ἐβάλοντο μάχεσθαι Il. 12.377.

In reference to immaterial things, to send, set, inspire: ἐν στήθεσσι μένος βάλεν Il. 5.513, σὺν δʼ ἔβαλον πόλεμον (joined battle) Il. 12.181. Cf. Il. 4.16, Il. 17.451, Il. 21.547: ἐν φύζαν ἑτάροισιν Od. 14.269 = Od. 17.438.
Without expressed object: ὡς ἐνὶ θυμῷ ἀθάνατοι βάλλουσιν Od. 1.201 = Od. 15.173.
To let fall: ποτὶ γαίῃ χεῖρας Od. 11.424.
To let fall or shed (tears): δάκρυ χαμάδις βάλεν Od. 4.114. Cf. Od. 4.198, 223, Od. 17.490.
Of shedding sleep: ὕπνον ἐπὶ βλεφάροισιν Od. 1.364 = Od. 16.451 = Od. 19.604 = Od. 21.358.
To let hang down: ἑτέρωσε κάρη Il. 8.306, Il. 23.697.
To lay on (the lash): ἐφʼ ἵπποιϊν μάστιν Od. 15.182.
To turn (the eyes): ἑτέρωσʼ ὄμματα Od. 16.179.
Of a river, to carry down with it and discharge (into the sea): ἀφυσγετὸν εἰς ἅλα Il. 11.495.
Absol., to discharge its waters, empty itself: εἰς ἅλα βάλλων Il. 11.722.

Of throwing or putting clothes, armour, etc., on a person, enduing him with them: ἀμφί μιν φᾶρος Il. 24.588. Cf. Il. 18.204: Od. 3.467, Od. 4.50, 440, Od. 13.434, etc.– So of putting on onesef: σπεῖρʼ ἀμφʼ ὤμοισι βαλών Od. 4.245.

In mid.: περὶ βάλλετο φᾶρος Il. 2.43, ἀμφʼ ὤμοισι βάλετο ξίφος 45 = Il. 3.334 = Il. 16.135 = Il. 19.372, Il. 11.29. Cf. Il. 5.738, Il. 10.333: περὶ ζώνην βάλετʼ ἰξυῖ Od. 5.231 = Od. 10.544. Cf. Od. 10.262, Od. 14.528, Od. 15.61, Od. 17.197 = Od. 18.108.
To cherish (in the heart): ἐν θυμῷ βάλλονται ἐμοὶ χόλον Il. 14.50.
To think of or consider as to (in one's mind): εἰ νόστον μετὰ φρεσὶ βάλλεαι Il. 9.435.
Sim.: ὡς ἐνὶ θυμῷ βάλλεαι (as thou (fondly) fanciest) Il. 20.196: ἥ τις τοιαῦτα μετὰ φρεσὶν ἔργα βάληται (conceives, contrives) Od. 11.428.

div.head: a
div.p: To strike or wound (a person, etc.) with a missile, and in pass., to be so struck or wounded: υἱὸν Πριάμοιο Il. 4.499, βεβλημένοι οὐτάμενοί τε Il. 11.659. Cf. Il. 8.81, Il. 12.391, Il. 15.249, etc.: ἀργῆτι κεραυνῷ Od. 5.128, ὁππότʼ ἀνὴρ βλήεται Od. 17.472. Cf. Od. 11.535, Od. 13.267, Od. 17.279, Od. 22.283, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: With the part of the body struck as object: αὐχένα μέσσον Il. 5.657. Cf. Il. 13.594, Il. 16.807, Il. 21.591, etc.: δεξιὸν ὦμον Od. 17.462. Cf. Od. 17.504, Od. 22.82.
With the part of the armour struck as object: Αἴαντος σάκος Il. 7.245. Cf. Il. 13.258, Il. 21.164, etc.
In pass.: πήληξ βαλλομένη καναχὴν ἔχε, βάλλετο δʼ αἰεί Il. 16.105.

div.head: c
div.p: With double acc. of the person and the part of the body struck; στῆθός μιν Il. 4.480. Cf. Il. 13.506, Il. 15.341, Il. 16.399, Il. 21.166, etc.: Od. 18.396, Od. 20.306, Od. 22.277.
With acc. of the person and of the part of the armour struck; τὸν τελαμῶνα Il. 12.401, Ἕκτορα θώρηκα Il. 17.606. Cf. Il. 5.98, etc.

div.head: d
div.p: In pass. with acc. of the part struck: βλῆτο κνήμην Il. 4.518. Cf. Il. 5.284, Il. 17.598.

div.head: e
div.p: With double acc. of the person and of the wound: ἕλκος τό μιν βάλε πάνδαρος Il. 5.795. Cf. Il. 16.511.

div.head: f
div.p: Without object, but with words indicating where the blow falls: βάλεν Ἀτρεΐδαο κατʼ ἀσπίδα Il. 3.347. Cf. Il. 3.356, Il. 5.305, etc.–

div.head: g
div.p: With the missile as subject Il. 5.17 = Il. 16.479.

Of striking inanimate objects: βάλε μέσσας [σανίδας] Il. 12.457. Cf. Il. 9.574, Il. 21.171, Il. 23.866, etc.: νῆα κεραυνῷ Od. 12.388, Od. 23.330, ἐπίτονος βέβλητο (was snapped) Od. 12.423. Cf. Od. 20.302, Od. 22.258 = 275.
Of such objects striking: ἄντυγας (ἡνίοχον) ῥαθάμιγγες Il. 11.536 = Il. 20.501, Il. 23.502.
Of the sun: ἀκτῖσιν ἔβαλλεν Od. 5.479, Od. 19.441.
Of sound: κτύπος οὔατα βάλλει Il. 10.535.
In mid. with ἀνά, to strike up, being(to sing) (cf. ἀναβάλλω 2): ἀνά σφισι βάλλετʼ ἀείδειν Od. 17.262.
An imitative formation, to stammer; or perh. redup. fr. βαίνω, to staggerIl. 10.375.
App. referring to harshness of speech = ἀγριόφωνος, Il. 2.867.
In this pple., weighed down, overcome Od. 3.139, Od. 19.122.
To be weighed down: βαρύθει μοι ὦμος (has lost its power) Il. 16.519.
To weigh down, oppress: γυῖα βαρύνεται Il. 19.165. Cf. Il. 5.664, Il. 8.308, Il. 20.480: Od. 5.321.
Sim.: δόναξ ἐβάρυνε μηρόν (app., made it painful to move) Il. 11.584.
Heavy. Of the hand or arm, heavy, powerful Il. 1.89, 219, Il. 5.81, Il. 11.235 = Il. 17.48, Il. 13.410, Il. 21.590, Il. 23.687: Od. 18.56.
Heavy to bear, grievous, dire: ἄτῃ Il. 2.111 = Il. 9.18. Cf. Il. 5.417, Il. 10.71, Il. 20.55: Od. 15.233.
Giving misery, stern, dire, grim: κῆρας Il. 21.548. Cf. Od. 7.197.
Of a voice, deep (as proceeding from a giant's throat) Od. 9.257.
In neut. βαρύ as adv., of groaning, heavily, deeply Il. 1.364 = Il. 18.78, Il. 4.153, Il. 9.16, Il. 16.20, Il. 18.70, 323, Il. 23.60: Od. 8.95 = 534.
The daughter of a βασιλεύς. Of Nausicaa Od. 6.115.
β. γυναικῶν, the peerless one among womenOd. 11.258.
One in authority, a king, chief, noble.
Of men (never of gods), sometimes as a title, sometimes as a descriptive term. Of Agamemnon Il. 1.9, 231, 340, 410, Il. 3.179, Il. 4.402, Il. 7.180, Il. 11.23, 46, 136, 262, 283, Il. 19.256.
In various contexts: κρείς σων β. ὅτε χώσεται ἀνδρὶ χέρηϊ Il. 1.80, διοτρεφέων βασιλήων 176, ὅν τινα βασιλῆα κιχείη Il. 2.188, εἷς β.
More royal, higher in rank Il. 9.160, 392, Il. 10.239: Od. 15.533.
To rule, hold sway, be king, chief or ruler Il. 2.203, Il. 9.616: Od. 1.392, Od. 2.47, Od. 19.179, Od. 22.52, Od. 24.483.
To be king or chief of or ruler over.

div.head: b
div.p: With dat.: Γιγάντεσσιν Od. 6.59. Cf. Il. 2.206 (v.l. βουλεύῃσι).
Of a woman, to enjoy rank as the wife of a βασιλεύς Il. 6.425.
Of a king or chief: τέμενος Il. 18.550 (v.l. βαθυλήϊον).
To raise. Of pushing uphill Od. 11.594.
To take into the hands, handle: τόξον Od. 21.405.
In pl., the prickles of some kind of prickly shrub or plant: βάτων ἕνεκα Od. 24.230.
acc. sing. masc. pf. pple. βαρέω.
acc. sing. masc. pf. pple. pass. βλάπτω.
acc. sing. masc. pf. pple. pass. βύω.
2 sing. βέῃ Il. 16.852, Il. 24.131 (app. for βέεαι (βέεʼ)).

To live: οὔ τι Διὸς βέομαι φρεσίν Il. 15.194 (φ. app. comitative dat., in company with . . ., in accordance with . . .; thus, will not live and move and have my being in his mind), οὐ δηρὸν βέῃ Il. 16.852, Il. 24.131, τί νυ βείομαι; (what have I now to live for?) Il. 22.431.
A spear or dart: πικρά Il. 22.206.

A spear or dart, but in pl. not necessarily excluding arrows or stones: οὐχ ἅλιον β. ἧκεν Il. 4.498, βελέων ἐρωήν 542. Cf. Il. 5.18, 316, 622, Il. 8.67, 159, etc.: Od. 16.277.–ἐκ βελέων, out of range of missiles: ὕπαγεν Il. 11.163. Cf. Il. 16.122, 668, 678, 781, Il. 18.152.
Motion not implied: ἐκ βελέων (keeping out of their range) Il. 14.130.
Of the rock thrown by the Cyclops Od. 9.495.
Of the θρῆνυς thrown by Antinous Od. 17.464.
Of the ox's foot thrown by Ktesippus Od. 20.305.
Applied to a weapon in gen. Il. 13.289.
Metaphorically of the wound inflicted by a missile: ὥς τις β. πέσσῃ Il. 8.513.
Of the pains of childbirth Il. 11.269.
In neut. βέλτερον with or without copula, it is (would be) better: β. ὃς προφύγῃ κακόν Il. 14.81 ([κείνῳ] ὅς = εἴ τις).
With complementary infin.: β. ἀπολέσθαι Il. 15.511. Cf. Il. 15.197, Il. 18.302, Il. 21.485, Il. 22.129.
With dat. and infin.: πτωχῷ β. ἐστι δαῖτα πτωχεύειν Od. 17.18.
With εἰ: β., εἰ καὐτὴ πόσιν εὗρεν ἄλλοθεν Od. 6.282.
The depth or gulf (of the sea): κατὰ β. ἁλός Il. 18.38, 49.
In pl. in sim. sense: ἐν βένθεσσιν ἁλός Il. 1.358 = Il. 18.36. Cf. Il. 13.21, 32.
In pl., the deeps or deep recesses (of the sea): θαλάσσης πάσης βένθεα οἶδεν Od. 1.53, Od. 4.386.
The recesses or coverts (of a wood): βαθείης βένθεσιν ὕλης Od. 17.316.
To the deep part (of the sea), to the deep (sea): νῆα ἁλὸς β. ἔρυσσαν Od. 4.780, Od. 8.51.
A gulf or deep recess: βάθιστον ὑπὸ χθονὸς β. Il. 8.14.
A threshold: ῥῖψεν (ῥίπτασκον) ἀπὸ βηλοῦ (i.e. of Olympus) Il. 1.591, Il. 15.23. Cf. Il. 23.202. (There is a tradition that in the first two passages it is a distinct word = οὐρανός.)
3 sing. fut. in mid. form βαίνω.
[app. βη-, βαίνω + ἁρμ-, ἁρμόζω. One who goes in measure.]
To bring one's might to bear upon, bear hard upon, press, use violence against. In mid.: βιάζεταί δε Il. 22.229. Cf. Od. 9.410.
In pass., to be pressed or driven: βελέεσσιν Il. 11.576. Cf. Il. 11.589, Il. 15.727 = Il. 16.102.
To push one's advantage against, constrain: βιάζετέ με μοῦνον ἐόντα Od. 12.297.
Forcefully, by force, with violence: γυναιξὶ παρευνάζεσθε β. Od. 22.37. Cf. Od. 2.237.
To use violence to, lay constraint upon.
In mid.: ὃ κεῖνον βιόωνται Od. 11.503. Cf. Od. 23.9.
Of something immaterial: τοῖον ἄχος βεβίηκεν Ἀχαιούς Il. 10.145 = Il. 16.22. Cf. Il. 10.172.
To prove too strong for, force, overcome.
In mid.: ὄνος ἐβιήσατο παῖδας Il. 11.558. Cf. Il. 11.467, Il. 16.823.
To force to act against one's will.
In mid.: οὔ τίς μʼ ἀέκοντα βιήσεται Od. 21.348.
To compel in a certain direction, throw upon something: ἐκβαίνοντά κέ με βιήσατο κῦμʼ ἐπὶ χέρσου Od. 7.278.
To push one's advantage against, get the better of.
In mid. with double acc.: νῶϊ βιήσατο μισθόν Il. 21.451.
To stride, stride along: μακρὰ βιβάσθων Il. 13.809, Il. 15.676, Il. 16.534.
(προ-.) = βιβάσθω.: μακρὰ βιβῶντα Il. 3.22. Cf. Il. 13.371, Il. 15.307, 686: Od. 11.539. (In all cases with βιβάντα, etc., from βίβημι. as v.l.)
(προ-.) = βιβάω.: μακρὰ βιβάντα (βιβάς) Il. 3.22, Il. 7.213, Il. 15.307, 686, ὕψι βιβάντα Il. 13.371: μακρὰ βιβᾶσα Od. 11.539.
Of a ram 450. (For vv. ll. see βιβάω.)
3 sing. fut. pf. pass. βεβρώσεται Od. 2.203.
In pf. forms in intensive sense: εἰ βεβρώθοις Πρίαμον (eat up, devour) Il. 4.35.
Sim. of χρήματα Od. 2.203 (will be consumed).
In strict pf. sense: βεβρωκὼς φάρμακα Il. 22.94.
So with partitive genit.: βεβρωκὼς βοός Od. 22.403.

Bodily strength, might, power; the exercise of this: βίην ἀμείνων (in might) Il. 1.404, Il. 15.139, πεποίθασι βίηφιν (in their strength) Il. 4.325, οὔ τίς με βίῃ δίηται Il. 7.197, σὴ β. λέλυται Il. 8.103. Cf. Il. 3.431, Il. 7.288, Il. 12.135, 341, Il. 13.572, Il. 15.106, Il. 17.569, Il. 23.315, etc.: δόλῳ ἠὲ βίηφιν Od. 9.406, βίης ἐπιδευέες Od. 21.185. Cf. Od. 4.415, Od. 6.6, Od. 13.143, Od. 18.4, Od. 20.379, Od. 21.128, etc.
In pl.: βίας Τρώων Il. 5.521. Cf. Od. 22.219.
National strength or power: Φαιήκων Od. 6.197.
The act of putting strength into exercise, effort: μεθῆκε βίης Il. 21.177. Cf. Od. 4.422, Od. 21.126.
Courage, spirit: οὐκ ἔστι β. φρεσίν Il. 3.45.

β. τινός, periphrasis for a person(the might of . . . = the mighty . . . ) (cf. ἴς 5, μένος 6, σθένος 2): Πριάμοιο βίην Il. 3.105, β. Ἑλένοιο Il. 13.770. Cf. Il. 5.781, Il. 13.758, 781, Il. 15.614, Il. 17.24, 187, Il. 18.117, Il. 20.307, Il. 21.367, Il. 22.323, Il. 23.859: Od. 10.200.

div.head: a
div.p: Wrongful exercise of strength or power, violence: ὕβρις τε β. τε Od. 15.329 = Od. 17.565. Cf. Od. 23.31.
In pl., acts of wrong or violence: βίας ἀποτίσεαι Od. 11.118, Od. 16.255. Cf. Od. 3.216, Od. 13.310, Od. 16.189, Od. 17.540.

Of an inanimate agent, violent manifestations of force: βίας ἀνέμων (the
blasts) Il. 16.213 = Il. 23.713.

div.head: b
div.p: In dat.: βίῃ, by wrongful use of force, by force, forcibly: εἴ με β. καθέξει Il. 15.186. Cf. Il. 16.387 : Od. 15.231.
With genit.: βίῃ ἀέκοντος (in spite of him unwilling) Il. 1.430: Od. 4.646.
Might, power, authority, influence Il. 9.498, Il. 23.578.
One's life, course of life, manner of living: ζώεις ἀγαθὸν βίον Od. 15.491. Cf. Od. 18.254 = Od. 19.127.
Life, existence, one's life: βιότοιο μεγήρας Il. 13.563. Cf. Il. 4.170: Od. 5.394, Od. 12.328, Od. 24.536.
The period of one's life: βιότοιο τελευτή Il. 7.104, Il. 16.787.
The fact of being alive: εἴ κεν πατρὸς βίοτον ἀκούσῃς Od. 1.287. Cf. Od. 2.218.

The means of living, substance, goods, chattels: ἀφνειὸς βιότοιο Il. 5.544. Cf. Il. 6.14, Il. 14.122: ἀλλότριον βίοτον ἔδουσιν Od. 1.160 Od. 18.280. Cf. Od. 1.377, Od. 2.49, 123, 126, Od. 3.301, Od. 4.90, 686, etc.
To live, continue to exist: ἄλλος βιώτω Il. 8.429. Cf. Il. 10.174, Il. 15.511: Od. 14.359.
Trans. in aor. mid., to give life to, rescue from death: σύ μʼ ἐβιώσαο Od. 8.468.
To cause to fail or break down: βλάβεται γούνατα Il. 19.166: Od. 13.34.
To cause (a speaker) to break down: βλάβεται λιγύς περἐὼν ἀγορητής Il. 19.82.
2 sing. aor. ἔβλαψας Il. 22.15. βλάψας Il. 23.571.
3 sing. ἔβλαψε Il. 23.782. βλάψε Il. 7.271, Il. 23.774: Od. 14.178.
3 pl. aor. pass. ἐβλάφθησαν Il. 23.387. Also ἔβλαβεν Il. 23.461. βλάβεν Il. 23.545.
Acc. sing. masc. pf. pple. βεβλαμμένον Il. 16.660.
To cause to fail or break down, make useless: γούνατα Il. 7.271. Cf. Il. 15.484, 489.
To stop, cut short the course of: ἵπποι ἔβλαβεν Il. 23.461. Cf. Il. 23.545.
Sim.: βεβλαμμένον ἦτορ (app., brought to a stop in his life, slain) Il. 16.660.
To impede the course of: ἵππους Il. 23.571.
To impede the motion of, entangle: βλαφθέντα κατὰ κλόνον Il. 16.331.
To impede in action, be in the way of: ἑταίρων τίνʼ ἐλαυνόντων Od. 13.22.
To entangle, catch: ἵππω ὄζῳ ἔνι βλαφθέντε Il. 6.39. Cf. Il. 15.647.
To trip, cause to stumble Il. 23.774.
With double acc.: ἔβλαψέ με πόδας Il. 23.782.

div.head: a
div.p: To affect the mind of adversely, smite with mental blindness. Of Ἄτη Il. 9.507, 512, Il. 19.94.
With φρένας as object : εἰ τότε βλάπτε φρένας Ζεύς Il. 15.724.

div.head: b
div.p: To deprive of good sense, put out of one's right mind: θεοί σʼ ἔβλαψαν Il. 23.14.
With φρένας as second acc.: τόν τις ἀθανάτων βλάψε φρένας Od. 14.178.

div.head: c
div.p: To foil: ἔβλαψάς μʼ , ἑκάεργε Il. 22.15.
Of wine, to drive out of one's right mind Od. 21.294.
App., to exult, bear oneself proudly, or the like: σθένεϊ βλεμεαίνων Il. 8.337. Cf. Il. 9.237, Il. 12.42, Il. 17.22, 135, Il. 20.36.

Always in dual or pl. The eyelids: οὐχ ὕπνος ἐπὶ βλεφάροισιν ἐφίζανε Il. 10.26. Cf. Il. 10.187, Il. 14.165, Il. 17.438, Il. 19.17, Il. 24.637: δάκρυ βάλεν ἐκ βλεφάροιϊν Od. 17.490. Cf. Od. 1.364, Od. 2.398, Od. 4.114, Od. 5.493, Od. 8.522, Od. 9.389, etc.
App., a clamp or clincher for fastening lengths together: ξυστὸν κολλητὸν βλήτροισιν Il. 15.678.
App., tall, stately: πίτυς Il. 13.390 = Il. 16.483: ὄγχνην Od. 24.234.
Of a period of time, to pass away Od. 17.190.
Of a period of time, to come on Il. 24.781.
[βο-, βοῦς + ἄγρη. Spoils of an ox. Cf. ἀνδράγρια.]
Dat. sing. masc. aor. pple. βώσαντι Il. 12.337.

To cry aloud, shout: κήρυκες βοόωντες ἐρήτυον Il. 2.97. Cf. Il. 2.198, 224, Il. 8.92, Il. 9.12, Il. 11.15, Il. 12.337, Il. 15.687 = 732, Il. 17.89, 334, 607 (app. for joy on seeing Hector unharmed), Il. 23.847: στὰς ἐβόησα Od. 10.311. Cf. Od. 4.281, Od. 5.400 = Od. 9.473 = Od. 12.181, Od. 6.294, Od. 8.305, Od. 9.403, Od. 24.537.
Of things, to roar, resound: θαλάσσης κῦμα Il. 14.394, ἠϊόνες Il. 17.265.

div.head: a
div.p: An ox-hide lately stripped off Od. 22.364.
An ox-hide in process of being dressed Il. 17.389.
A piece of dressed ox-leather Il. 12.296.

div.head: b
div.p: A shield of ox-hide Il. 5.452 = Il. 12.425, Il. 22.159.
A strap of ox-leather (used for hoisting a sail): ἕλκον ἱστία βοεῦσιν Od. 2.426 = Od. 15.291.

A crying out, a shouting:
βοῆς ἀΐοντες Od. 9.401, Od. 14.266 = Od. 17.435.
A hue-and-cry, a din: διὰ ἄστεος Od. 10.118. Cf. Od. 22.77, 133.

A shouting in battle: Il. 11.50, 500, 530, Il. 13.169 = 540, Il. 14.4, Il. 16.267.–βοὴν ἀγαθός, good at the battle-cry, marshalling or rallying his men with loud shout. Of Menelaus Il. 2.408, 586, Il. 3.96, Il. 4.220, Il. 6.37, etc.: Od. 3.311, Od. 4.307, 609, Od. 15.14, 57, 67, 92, 97, Od. 17.120.
Of Diomedes Il. 2.563, Il. 5.114, Il. 6.12, Il. 7.399, Il. 8.91, etc.
A loud expression of grief Il. 6.465: Od. 24.48.
The sound of musical instruments Il. 18.495.
Running to the battle-cry, coming swiftly to the fight Il. 13.477.
The epithet transferred from the warrior to his chariot Il. 17.481.
A driving off of cattle: νεῖκος ἀμφὶ βοηλασίῃ Il. 11.672.
A hole or pit dug in the ground: βόθρον ὀρύξαι Od. 10.517, ἀπεδειροτόμησα ἐς βόθρον (so that the blood ran into the pit) Od. 11.36. Cf. Od. 11.25, 42, 95.
A hollow by a river used for washing clothes Od. 6.92.
The trench in which a young tree is planted Il. 17.58.
Pf. pple. pass. βεβολημένος Il. 9.9: Od. 10.247.
Of grief, to smite: πένθεϊ βεβολήατο (were in the state of having been smitten, were tossed about or agitated) Il. 9.3. Cf. Il. 9.9: Od. 10.247.
A blow with a missile Od. 17.283, Od. 24.161.
A turn or glance (of the eyes) Od. 4.150.
With infin. and ἤ: Τρωσὶν δοῦναι ἠέ περ ἡμῖν Il. 11.319.
[imitative] To make a resounding, clanging or clashing noise Il. 13.530, Il. 16.118: Od. 12.204 (the oars knocked against each other in the wash of the sea as they hung by the τροποί), Od. 18.397.
Of the whizzing flight of a quoit Od. 8.190.
Genit. (besides Βορέαο) Βορέω Il. 14.395, Il. 23.692: Od. 14.533. Βορέης as spondee Il. 9.5. So Βορέῃ Il. 23.195.
Joined with ἄνεμος Il. 15.26: Od. 9.67, Od. 14.253, 299, Od. 19.200.
3 pl. pa. iterative pass. βοσκέσκοντο Od. 12.355.
To feed, tend (cattle, etc.) Il. 15.548: Od. 14.102.
To feed, nourish, support: γαῖα ἀνθρώπους Od. 11.365. Cf. Od. 9.124, Od. 12.97, Od. 14.325= Od. 19.294.
To fill or stuff (one's belly) Od. 17.228, 559, Od. 18.364.
In pass., of cattle, etc., to feed, graze: ξύλοχον κάτα βοσκομενάων Il. 5.162. Cf. Il. 16.151, Il. 17.62, Il. 20.223: Od. 4.338 = Od. 17.129, Od. 11.108, Od. 12.128, 355, Od. 14.104, Od. 21.49.
Grazing beasts, beasts of the herd: ἀρδμὸς πάντεσσι βοτοῖσιν Il. 18.521.
A feeding-place: ὡς εἴ θʼ ἕσπετο μῆλα ἐκ βοτάνης Il. 13.493.
A herdsman: ἀγροὺς ἐπιείσομαι ἠδὲ βοτῆρας Od. 15.504.
A bunch or cluster of grapes: μέλανες Il. 18.562.
Grazed by cattle. Of Ithaca Od. 13.246.
Explained as the insect that attacks cattle, the gadfly. By others connected with βι-βρώσκω and explained as ravenous hunger (taking βου- in an intensive sense. Cf. βουγάϊος) Il. 24.532.
[app. a compound of βοῦς, perh. in intensive sense. The second element perh. γαϝ-, γαίω.]
To feed or tend cattle: Ἀγχίσῃ βουκολέοντι Il. 5.313. Cf. Il. 14.445: Od. 10.85.
In pass., of cattle, etc., to feed, graze Il. 20.221.
[app. for βουπόλος fr. βοῦς + -πολος, conn. with πολεύω. Cf. αἰπόλος.]
A member of the βουλή, a councillorIl. 6.114.
To deliberate, consider, take counsel with oneself, concert measures, contrive, plan: ἵνα σφίσι βουλεύῃσθα (in their interests) Il. 9.99. Cf. Il. 2.206 (v.l. βασιλεύῃ): Od. 12.58, Od. 14.491.
With infin.: τὸν βούλευσα κατακτάμεν (οὐτάμεναι) (debated whether to ...) Il. 9.458: Od. 9.299.
With dependent clause: ὅπως... (how, in what manner) Od. 9.420, Od. 11.229.
In dual and pl., to take counsel together: ὣς βουλεύσαντε Il. 1.531, εἰ ἐς μίαν βουλεύσομεν (take counsel to one purpose, lay our plans in common) Il. 2.379. Cf. Od. 13.439, Od. 16.234.

With cognate acc.: ὅς κεν ἀρίστην βουλὴν βουλεύσῃ (devise the best counsel) Il. 9.75, βουλὰς βουλεύειν (to take counsel together, hold counsel, concert measures) Il. 10.327. Cf. Il. 10.147, 415, Il. 23.78, Il. 24.652: Od. 6.61.
To turn over in one's mind, ponder: ὁδόν Od. 1.444.
To meditate, purpose, propose to oneself: φύξιν Il. 10.311 = 398.
To plan, contrive, scheme to bring about: ὄλεθρον Il. 14.464. Cf. Od. 5.179 = Od. 10.344, Od. 5.187 = Od. 10.300.
To plan, contrive, devise, elaborate: ψεύδεα Od. 14.296. Cf. Od. 5.23 = Od. 24.479, Od. 23.217.
In mid.: ἀπάτην βουλεύσατο Il. 2.114 = Il. 9.21.
A select council of the most important chiefs (cf. ἀγορή 1) Il. 2.53, 194, 202, Il. 10.195, Il. 12.213: Od. 3.127.
The deliberation or discussion in the council: ὅσοι οὐ βουλῆς ἐπάκουσαν Il. 2.143.
The place of council Il. 2.84: Od. 6.55.

Counsel, concerting of measures, contriving,
planning, scheming: οἳ περί ἐστε βουλὴν Δαναῶν (in . . .) Il. 1.258. Cf. Il. 9.54, Il. 10.43, Il. 11.627, Il. 13.728, 741, Il. 16.630: ἐπίφρονι Od. 3.128. Cf. Od. 4.267, Od. 12.211, Od. 13.298, 305, Od. 16.242, 374, 420, Od. 22.230.
A conclusion, a resolve, a course to take: βουλήν, ἣ θεοῖσιν ἐφήνδανεν Il. 7.45. Cf. Il. 2.5 = Il. 10.107 = Il. 14.161, Il. 17.469: Od. 9.318 = 424 = Od. 11.230, Od. 14.337.

p.gloss: What one has contrived or planned.

div.p: In pl.: Θέτιδος ἐξήνυσε βουλάς Il. 8.370.
A plan or plot: οὐχ ἡμῖν συνθεύσεται ἥδε γε βουλή Od. 20.245.

Counsel given, advice, what one proposes or puts forward: πυκινήν Il. 2.55 = Il. 10.302. Cf. Il. 2.282, Il. 4.323, Il. 7.325 = Il. 9.94, Il. 8.36 = 467, Il. 12.109, Il. 14.102, Il. 18.313, 510: εἴ τινα βουλὴν εἴποι Od. 11.479. Cf. Od. 3.150, Od. 8.506, Od. 10.46, Od. 12.339, Od. 24.52.
In pl.: βουλέων μευ ξύνιεν Il. 1.273 Cf. Il. 2.273.
One's will, resolve, determination: Διὸς βουλή Il. 1.5. Cf. Il. 2.344, Il. 12.241, Il. 20.15, 20: Od. 1.86, Od. 2.372, Od. 5.30, Od. 11.297, Od. 13.127, Od. 14.328 = Od. 19.297.
One's mind, what one has in view or is doing Od. 2.281, Od. 11.177.
A (trusted) adviser, a leader in counsel Il. 5.180 = Il. 17.485, Il. 5.633, Il. 7.126, Il. 10.518, Il. 13.219, 255, 463, Il. 20.83.
Specifically, a member of the βουλή, a leading chief Il. 10.414, Il. 24.651: Od. 13.12.
As adj.: ἀγοραὶ βουληφόροι (in which counsel is exchanged) Od. 9.112.
To have a preference for one of two things, to wish, be minded : ἄλλῃ Il. 15.51.
To wish, desire (something): Τρώεσσι βούλετο νίκην Il. 7.21, Il. 13.347, Il. 16.121. Cf. Il. 8.204, Il. 23.682.
With infin.: Τρώεσσι κῦδος ὀρέξαι Il. 11.79. Cf. Il. 12.174 = Il. 15.596: Od. 4.275, 353 (βούλοντο here app. an aor.), Od. 15.21, 88.
With infin.: ἀπὸ λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι Il. 1.67.
To prefer: τό κε βουλοίμην Il. 3.41: Od. 11.358 = Od. 20.316.
With infin.: αὐτὴν οἴκοι ἔχειν Il. 1.112. Cf. Il. 24.39: Od. 3.143, Od. 9.96, Od. 17.187, 228, Od. 18.364.
With ἤ: ἡμῖν Ζεὺς βούλεται ἤ Δαναοῖσι νίκην Il. 17.331.
With infin. and ἤ: λαὸν σῶν ἔμμεναι ἢ ἀπολέσθαι Il. 1.117. Cf. Il. 23.594: Od. 3.232, Od. 11.489, Od. 12.350, Od. 16.106, Od. 17.81, 404.
Absol.: βούλομαι (I prefer it so, I accept the alternative) Il. 24.226.
(ῡ) [βοῦς + λύω + -δε 1. To the time for unyoking oxen.]
To or towards early afternoon: Ἠέλιος μετενίσετο β. Il. 16.779: = Od. 9.58. (The time specified is fixed for Il. 16.779, and is admissible for Od. 9.58.
The reference seems to be to a custom of stopping ploughing at or soon after mid-day.)
An ox-whip or-goad; or perh., a pole-axe: θεινόμεναι βουπλῆγι Il. 6.135.
βοός, ὁ, ἡ (βοϝ-. Cf. L. bouis).

div.head: a
div.p: Gender not determined: βοῦς ἱέρευσεν Il. 6.174, ἀγέλην βοῶν Il. 11.696, ἱμάντας βοός (i.e. of the hide) Il. 23.684. Cf. Il. 5.556, Il. 7.333, Il. 8.240, 505, Il. 9.466, Il. 18.528, etc.: νῶτα βοός Od. 4.65. Cf. Od. 2.56, Od. 3.421, Od. 6.132, Od. 11.402, Od. 13.32, Od. 15.386, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: Masculine: ἶφι κταμένοιο Il. 3.375, βόε ἶσον θυμὸν ἔχοντε Il. 13.703, ἐριμύκων Il. 20.497 (for the gender see 495). Cf. Il. 13.571, Il. 18.559, Il. 23.775, etc.: Od. 1.108, Od. 18.371.
Qualified by ἄρσην Il. 7.314, Il. 20.495: Od. 19.420.

div.head: c
div.p: Feminine: ἐμὰς βοῦς Il. 1.154, αὐτῇσι βόεσσιν Il. 7.474. Cf. Il. 6.93, Il. 8.231, Il. 10.292, Il. 11.172, Il. 17.62, Il. 18.574, etc.: στεῖραν βοῦν Od. 10.522, πολλαί Od. 12.128. Cf. Od. 3.382, Od. 10.410, Od. 11.108, Od. 12.262, Od. 20.221, etc.
A shield of ox-hide. In this sense fem.: τυκτῇσι βόεσσιν Il. 12.105. Cf. Il. 7.238, Il. 12.137, Il. 16.636.
To slay an ox or oxen for sacrifice Il. 7.466.
Of Clymene (one of Helen's handmaidens) Il. 3.144.
The constellation the Waggoner, containing the star Arcturus Od. 5.272.
Slowness, want of speed: βραδυτῆτί τε νωχελίῃ τε Il. 19.411.
Of armour, to rattle, clash, ring Il. 4.420, Il. 12.396, Il. 13.181, Il. 14.420, Il. 16.566.
Of an axle, to creak, grate Il. 5.838.
Of a river, to resound under the splash of something falling into it Il. 21.9.
Of the earth, to give forth a sound, resound Il. 21.387.
Of persons, to roar, shriek Il. 5.859, 863, Il. 16.468.
Of the sea or the wind, to roar Il. 4.425.
App., the head: ἔπεσε ἐπὶ βρεχμόν τε καὶ ὤμους Il. 5.586.
Thus, with powerful or loud voice.
Weight, load: ἔβραχεν ἄξων βριθοσύνῃ Il. 5.839, πέσε λίθος εἴσω βριθοσύνῃ (by its weight) Il. 12.460.
To be heavy, loaded or weighed down with something.
With dat.: σταφυλῇσιν Il. 18.561. Cf. Od. 16.474, Od. 19.112.
With genit.: τυρῶν Od. 9.219. Cf. Od. 15.334.
To be oppressed: ὑπὸ λαίλαπι χθών Il. 16.384.
To bring one's weight to bear, bear hard: ἰθὺς Δαναῶν βρίσαντες ἔβησαν Il. 17.233. Cf. Il. 12.346 = 359, Il. 17.512.
Fig., to be grievous or distressing Il. 21.385.
To prevail, achieve one's end: ἐέδνοισιν Od. 6.159.
Gory, blood-stained: ἔναρα Il. 6.480, Il. 8.534, Il. 10.528, 570, Il. 15.347, Il. 17.13, 540, Il. 22.245, ἀνδράγρια Il. 14.509.
Shed blood, gore: αἱματόεντα Il. 7.425, Il. 14.7, Il. 18.345, Il. 23.41: μέλανα Od. 24.189.

Absol., a mortal man, a man: θεὰ βροτῷ εὐνηθεῖσα Il. 2.821. Cf. Il. 1.272, Il. 8.428, Il. 9.159, Il. 11.2, Il. 13.244, etc.: βροτῶν θελκτήρια Od. 1.337. Cf. Od. 4.197, Od. 5.101, Od. 6.149, Od. 11.287, Od. 12.125, etc.
Qualified by θνητός Od. 3.3 = Od. 12.386, Od. 7.210, Od. 16.212.
To make gory, stain with blood: βεβροτωμένα τεύχεα Od. 11.41.
Of a wounded hero Il. 13.393 = Il. 16.486.
The partaking of food: μνησόμεθα βρώμης Od. 10.177.
The partaking of food: ἐς βρωτὺν ὀτρύνετον Il. 19.205.
Made of the fibrous coat of the papyrus Od. 21.391.
[app. fr. βυσσός + δόμος, to construct in the interior of the house, away from public view.]
To plan or ponder secretly Od. 4.676, Od. 8.273, Od. 9.316, Od. 17.66, 465 = 491 = Od. 20.184.
The depth of the sea Il. 24.80.

p.term: Acc. sing. masc. pf. pple. pass.

div.p: A clod, the clods, of earth Od. 4.374.
[prob. fr. βα-, βαίνω, something to or on which one mounts.]

p.gloss: A stand on which the body of a chariot was placed after removal of the wheels.

div.p: In pl. of a single stand: ἅρματʼ ἃμ βωμοῖσι τίθει Il. 8.441 (app. assimilated to ἅρματα, which is pl. in form only).
To call to for aid: κράταιϊν Od. 12.124.
Feeding men, rich in food: φθιῃ Il. 1.155.
The earth: στεναχιζετο γ. Il. 2.95. Cf. Il. 2.699, 782, Il. 6.19, 282, Il. 17.447, etc.: πείρατα γαίης Od. 4.563. Cf. Od. 2.131, Od. 3.16, Od. 4.417, Od. 6.167, Od. 11.239, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: From the heavens: μεσσηγὺς γαίης τε καὶ οὐρανοῦ Il. 5.769 = Il. 8.46. Cf. Il. 8.16, Il. 14.174, Il. 15.193: Od. 1.54, Od. 11.18, Od. 12.381.

div.head: b
div.p: From the sea or water: γαίης καὶ πόντοιο Il. 8.479. Cf. Il. 8.24, Il. 14.204: ἐφʼ ὑγρὴν ἠδʼ ἐπὶ γαῖαν Od. 1.98. Cf. Od. 5.294, 359, Od. 11.587, Od. 12.282, Od. 23.238, etc.
The earth considered with reference to extent: πολλὴ γαῖα, many regions or countriesIl. 15.81: Od. 2.364, Od. 4.268, Od. 14.380.
So πολλὴν ἐπʼ ἀπείρονα γαῖαν (far and wide on the . . . ) Od. 15.79. Cf. Od. 19.284.

div.head: a
div.p: A particular land or country: Ἀχαιΐδα γαῖαν Il. 1.254 = Il. 7.124. Cf. Il. 1.270, Il. 3.49, Il. 5.545, Il. 23.206: γαίῃ ἐν ἀλλοδαπῇ Od. 9.36. Cf. Od. 1.407, Od. 5.35, Od. 6.119, 177, Od. 8.301, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: One's native land: πάρος ἣν γαῖαν ἱκέσθαι Od. 1.21, ἐν σῇ ἐὼν γαίῃ Od. 13.294. Cf. Od. 1.59, Od. 4.523, Od. 8.555, Od. 20.99, etc.

The surface of the earth, the earth, the ground: ποτὶ σκῆπτρον βάλε γαίῃ Il. 1.245. Cf. Il. 3.114, Il. 4.112, Il. 11.161, Il. 13.200, Il. 20.420, Il. 23.420, etc.: κατακλίνας ἐπὶ γαίῃ Od. 10.165. Cf. Od. 2.80, Od. 8.190, Od. 9.289, Od. 11.423, Od. 18.92, etc.
Earth as a material, earth, soil: χυτή με κατὰ γαῖα καλύπτοι Il. 6.464. Cf. Il. 7.99, Il. 14.114, Il. 23.256: ἀμφὶ γαῖαν ἔναξεν Od. 21.122. Cf. Od. 3.258.
Of a corpse: κωφὴν γαῖαν (the senseless clay) Il. 24.54.

Epithet or a name of Poseidon. Prob., earth-embracing, the earth-embracer (connecting Poseidon with the earth-encircling river Ocean) Il. 13.83, 125, Il. 15.174, 201, Il. 20.34: Od. 1.68, Od. 3.55, Od. 8.322, 350, Od. 9.528.
Only in phrase κύδεϊ γαίων, of a divinity, glorying in his splendour; or perh., brilliant or glorious with splendour Il. 1.405, Il. 5.906, Il. 8.51 Il. 11.81.
Still sucking the mother's milk: νεβρούς Od. 4.336 = Od. 17.127.
Of the sea: ἐλόωσι γαλήνην (through a calm sea) Od. 7.319. Cf. Od. 5.452, Od. 10.94.
A sister-in-law, a sister of one's husband Il. 3.122, Il. 6.378, 383, Il. 22.473, Il. 24.769.
3 sing. aor. opt. γήμαιτο Od. 16.392, Od. 21.162.

In act., of a man, to marry, wed: κούρην Il. 9.388, μιν 391, Ἀδρήστοιο θυγατρῶν(partitive genit., one of his daughters) Il. 14.121. Cf. Il. 9.399, Il. 11.227, Il. 13.433: ἄλοχον μνηστήν Od. 1.36 (here of another's wife), Od. 11.179, 274, 282, Od. 15.241, 522, Od. 16.34, Od. 21.72, 158, Od. 23.149.

div.head: a
div.p: Of a woman, to give herself in marriage to, to wed.

div.head: b
div.p: App., to get (a wife for one's son): Πηλεύς μοι γυναῖκα γαμέσσεται Il. 9.394 (v.l. γε μάσσεται).

A contracting of marriage, one's marriage: ὄφρα συνώμεθα ἀμφὶ γάμῳ Il. 13.382: γάμον τεύξουσιν Od. 1.277 = Od. 2.196. Cf. Od. 1.249 = Od. 16.126, Od. 2.97 = Od. 19.142 = Od. 24.132, Od. 2.205, Od. 4.7,Od. 6.27, 66, 288, Od. 15.126, 524, Od. 17.476, Od. 18.272, Od. 19.137, 157, Od. 20.341, Od. 21.250, Od. 22.50, Od. 24.126.
A marriage, a wedding, a wedding-feast: γάμοι εἰλαπίναι τε Il. 18.491. Cf. Il. 19.299, Il. 24.62: δαινύντα γάμον Od. 4.3. Cf. Od. 1.226, Od. 4.770, Od. 11.415, Od. 20.307, Od. 23.135.
Marriage, wedlock: ἱμερόεντα ἔργα γάμοιο Il. 5.429: ἐκλελάθοιτό κε γάμοιο Od. 3.224. Cf. Od. 20.74.
The jaws of an animal. Of lions Il. 13.200, Il. 16.489.
With hooked talons: αἰγυπιοί Il. 16.428: = Od. 22.302, Od. 16.217.
Nom. pl. masc. pres. pple. γανόωντες Il. 13.265.
Of polished metal, to shine, gleam Il. 13.265, Il. 19.359.
Of vegetation, to be brightly green: πρασιαί Od. 7.128.
To rejoice or take delight in.
In reference to persons: ἀνδρὶ φίλῳ ἐλθοντι Il. 14.504. Cf. Od. 12.43.
Introducing the ground or reason for something said.

div.head: a
div.p: The γάρ clause following, for, since, seeing that Il. 1.55, 56, 63, 78, 81, 86, etc.: Od. 1.7, 29, 40, 78, 114, 152, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: The γάρ clause coming first, since, seeing that Il. 2.803, Il. 12.326, Il. 13.736, Il. 15.739, Il. 23.156, etc.: Od. 1.301, 337, Od. 5.29, Od. 10.174, Od. 12.154, etc.

Introducing an explanation, reason, amplification, or analysis of something previously said (often with καί; see καί 3) Il. 1.9, 12, 80, 262, 295, 355, Il. 2.119, Il. 4.226, 301, Il. 8.148, Il. 10.352, Il. 12.322, etc.: Od. 1.33, 260, Od. 2.89, Od. 3.89, 362, Od. 4.86, Od. 6.164, Od. 9.319, 432 (the clause here introduced parenthetically), Od. 11.69, Od. 20.42, Od. 21.232, etc.

Introducing as a kind of interjection a question or expression with something of an abrupt effect (sometimes translatable, why . . ., well . . .): πῶς γάρ τοι δώσουσι γέρας ; Il. 1.123, ἦ γάρ κεν δειλὸς καλεοίμην Il. 1.293. Cf. Il. 10.61, Il. 15.201, Il. 18.182, etc.: πῶς γάρ με κέλεαι . . .; Od. 10.337, εἰ γάρ κεν σὺ μίμνοις Od. 15.545. Cf. Od. 8.159, Od. 10.383, Od. 14.115, Od. 15.509, Od. 16.222, etc.
For αἲ γάρ, εἰ γάρ in wishes see αἴ 1, εἰ 2.b.
Idiomatically following the relative ὅς : ὃ γάρ κʼ ὄχʼ ἄριστον εἴη (for that . . .) Il. 12.344 = 357, ὃ γὰρ γέρας ἐστὶ θανόντων Il. 23.9: ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν Od. 1.286. Cf. Od. 17.172, Od. 24.190.
So following ἵνα: ἵνα γάρ σφιν ἐπέφραδον ἠγερέθεσθαι (for there . . .) Il. 10.127.

And ὡς: ὡς γὰρ ἀνώγει (for so he bade) Il. 9.690, ὡς γὰρ ἔμοιγε (for so he was to me) Il. 24.68, etc.: ὡς γάρ οἱ μοῖρʼ ἐστὶ . . . (for this is his destiny, to . . .) Od. 5.41. Cf. Od. 8.79, Od. 20.282, etc. (In such cases the demonstrative ὥ (ὧς) is also read.)
In half-personified sense: κέλεταί ἑ γ. Od. 6.133. Cf. Od. 7.216, Od. 15.344, Od. 17.228, 286, 473, 559, Od. 18.2, 53, 364, 380.
The intestine of an animal stuffed with fat and blood and forming some kind of pudding or large sausage Od. 18.44, 118, Od. 20.25.
The lower and rounded part of a vessel: τρίποδος Il. 18.348: = Od. 8.437.
Some kind of vessel for milk Od. 9.223.

Calling attention to a word or fact or distinguishing it from others: εἴ κε θάνατόν γε φύγοιμεν Il. 1.60, ἐπεί μʼ ἀφέλεσθέ γε δόντες 299 ( δόντες being here the word emphasized). Cf. Il. 1.81, 216, 286, 352, 393, 506, etc.: κεῖνός γε ἐοικότι κεῖται ὀλέθρῳ Od. 1.46, ὅτις τοιαῦτά γε ῥέζοι 47. Cf. Od. 1.10, 203, 222, 223, 229, 339, etc.–γʼ οὖν in any case: εἴ γʼ οὖν ἕτερός γε φύγῃσιν (if indeed one does escape) Il. 5.258, μὴ ἐμέ γʼ οὖν οὗν οὗτός γε λάβοι χόλος (far be it from me) Il. 16.30.
3 sing. plupf. (in impf. sense) ἐγεγώνει Il. 22.34, Il. 23.425: Od. 21.368.
From pres. γεγωνέω impf. (ἐ)γεγώνευν Od. 12.370, Od. 17.161.

To make one's voice heard: οὔ πώς οἱ ἔην βώσαντι γεγωνεῖν Il. 12.337. Cf. Il. 8.223 = Il. 11.6: Od. 5.400 = Od. 9.473 = Od. 12.181, Od. 6.294.–αὔειν γεγωνώς, to shout making oneself heard, i.e. in a sustained and loud voiceIl. 8.227 = Il. 11.275 = 586 = Il. 17.247, Il. 12.439 = Il. 13.149.
To shout (with implication that one makes oneself heard): ἐγέγωνε Πουλυδάμαντι Il. 14.469. Cf. Il. 22.34, Il. 23.425, Il. 24.703: Od. 8.305, Od. 9.47, Od. 12.370, Od. 21.368.
Tending to, conceived in a spirit of, mockery; or perh., laughable: ἔργα Od. 8.307.
Pple. γελάσας Od. 2.301. γελάσσας Il. 11.378, Il. 21.508.
Infin. γελάσαι Od. 14.465. Also pres. γελόω Od. 21.105.
Pl. pple. γελόωντες Od. 18.40, Od. 20.374. γελώωντες Od. 18.111, Od. 20.390. (ἐκ-.)
To smile: δακρυόεν Il. 6.484, χείλεσιν (i.e. with a forced smile) Il. 15.101. Cf. Od. 17.542, Od. 21.105.
Of the earth, to be bright Il. 19.362.
Of the heart, to rejoice Il. 21.389: Od. 9.413 (here app. connoting inward derisive laughter. See 2.b).

div.head: b
div.p: To laugh (at a person): ἐπʼ αὐτῷ Il. 2.270, Il. 23.784: = Od. 20.358 = Od. 21.376, ἐπὶ ξείνοις Od. 20.374.

Race, stock, family = γένος 1, γενέθλη 1: τίη γενεὴν ἐρεείνεις; Il. 6.145, Il. 21.153, πατρόθεν ἐκ γενεῆς ὀνομάζων (by his father's, that is, his family name) Il. 10.68, γενεῇ ὑπέρτερος (in birth) Il. 11.786, γενεὴν Διὸς εἶναι (by race sprung from . . .) Il. 21.187. Cf. Il. 6.151, 211 = Il. 20.241, Il. 7.128, Il. 10.239, Il. 15.141, Il. 19.105, Il. 20.203, 214, Il. 21.157, Il. 23.471: γενεῇ πατρώϊον (by right of descent) Od. 1.387. Cf. Od. 15.225.
A race or generation = γένος 3: φύλλων Il. 6.146, ἀνδρῶν 149.
A race or family: οὔ τοι γενεὴν θεοὶ νώνυμνον θῆκαν Od. 1.222. Cf. Od. 16.117.
A body of descendants, offspring: Δαρδάνου Il. 20.303. Cf. Il. 20.306, Il. 21.191: Od. 4.27.

The body of persons born at about a certain time and conceived of as living for a certain time and conceived of as living for certain period, a generation: δύο γενεαὶ ἀνθρώπων Il. 1.250. Cf. Il. 23.790: Od. 14.325 = Od. 19.294.
App., family likeness or type: αὐτῷ γενεὴν ἐῴκει (in . . .) Il. 14.474.
In reference to the date of one's birth, age, one's years = γένος 7: ὁπλότερος γενεῇ (in age) Il. 2.707. Cf. Il. 4.60 = Il. 18.365, Il. 6.24, Il. 7.153, Il. 9.161, Il. 15.166, 182: Od. 19.184.
So with instrumental: γενεῆφι νεώτατος Il. 14.112. Cf. Il. 9.58, Il. 21.439.
One's birthplace = γένος 8 Il. 20.390: Od. 1.407, Od. 15.175, Od. 20.193.
Race, stock = γενεή 1, γένος 1: σῆς ἐκ γενέθλης Il. 19.111: παιήονός εἰσι γενέθλης (of the race of . . .) Od. 4.232. Cf. Od. 13.130.
Of mares, a brood: τῶν ἓξ ἐγένοντο γ. Il. 5.270 (γ. being predicate).
Source, origin = γένος 2: ὅθεν ἀργύρου ἐστὶ γ. (whence comes . . .) Il. 2.857.
In pl., the hair on the chin, the beard: γενειάδες ἀμφὶ γένειον Od. 16.176.
To get a beard, i.e. attain manhood: παῖδα γενειήσαντα Od. 18.176. Cf. Od. 18.269.
Source, origin: Ὠκεανόν, θεῶν γένεσιν Il. 14.201 = 302. Cf. Il. 14.246.
One's birth: ἐκ γενετῆς Il. 24.535 (from his birth (onwards)): Od. 18.6 (to be his from his birth, i.e. on his birth).
Suited to (noble) birth, seemly, honourable Il. 5.253.
One's descent: γ. μοι ἔνθεν ὅθεν σοί Il. 4.58. Cf. Il. 13.354.
Source, origin = γενέθλη 3: ὅθεν ἡμιόνων γ. Il. 2.852 (whence come . . .).
A race or generation = γενεή 2: ἡμιθέων ἀνδρῶν Il. 12.23. Cf. Od. 4.62, Od. 17.523, Od. 20.212.
App., a generation considered as a period: τρὶς ἀνάξασθαι γένεʼ ἀνδρῶν (during three generations) Od. 3.245.
The members of one's family: μεθʼ αἶμά τε καὶ γ. αὐτῶν Od. 8.583.
Offspring, a child: δῖον γ. Il. 9.538, σὸν γένος Il. 19.124.
So of the Chimaera: θεῖον γ. (as being of divine origin) Il. 6.180.
In reference to the date of one's birth, age, one's years = γενεή 5: γένει ὕστερος ἦεν (was the younger) Il. 3.215.
To seize or grasp: ἱμάσθλην Il. 8.43 = Il. 13.25. Cf. Il. 13.241, Il. 18.476, 477.
Absol. in masc., an old man (always of a dignified person): ἠρᾶθʼ ὁ γ. Il. 1.35. Cf. Il. 3.191, 225, Il. 10.77, Il. 11.632, 645, Il. 14.39, Il. 24.162, 252, 279, 302, 322: Od. 3.373.
In voc. as a term of respectful address Il. 10.164, 167, 558, Il. 11.648, 653, Il. 24.390, 433, 618.
Without the notion of respect Od. 2.201, Od. 14.131, 185.
Absol. in fem., an old woman (app. referring to those of the higher classes): ξυνάγουσα γεραιάς Il. 6.87. Cf. Il. 6.270, 287, 296.

div.head: a
div.p:
Older: ὃς σεῖο γ.
εὔχομαι εἶναι Il. 9.60.

div.head: b
div.p: Old rather than young, elderly: κῆρυξ Il. 24.149, 178. Cf. Od. 3.362.
To honour, show honour to: νώτοισι διηνεκέεσσιν Il. 7.321: Od. 14.437, ἀγαθοῖσιν 441.
Acc. pl. with hyphaeresis γέρᾶ (for γέραα) Il. 2.237, Il. 9.334: Od. 4.66.

A meed of honour, a special prize apart from the general division of spoils (represented as assigned sometimes to the king or a chief by the general consent (as in Il. 1.118, 123, 135, 276, Il. 16.56, Il. 18.444: Od. 7.10), sometimes to chiefs by the king (as in Il. 9.334, 367). (But cf. Il. 9.130, 272, Il. 11.696, where the king is represented as choosing his prize)) Il. 1.118, 120, 123, 133, 135, 138, 161, 163, 167, 185, 276, 356 = 507 = Il. 2.240, Il. 2.237, Il. 9.111, 334, 344, 367, Il. 16.54, 56, Il. 18.444, Il. 19.89: Od. 7.10, Od. 11.534.
Something given by way of showing honour to a person: νῶτα βοός, τά οἱ γέρα πάρθεσαν Od. 4.66.
An honour paid: τὸ γὰρ λάχομεν γ. ἡμεῖς Il. 4.49 = Il. 24.70. Cf. Il. 16.457 = 675, Il. 23.9: Od. 4.197, Od. 24.190, 296.
The dignity or honours of a king: οὔ τοι Πρίαμος γ. ἐν χερὶ θήσει Il. 20.182. Cf. Od. 11.175, 184, Od. 15.522.
App., any hereditary honour or privilege bestowed on a king or a chief by the people: γ. ὅ τι δῆμος ἔδωκεν Od. 7.150.
Of an oath, taken by the elders or councillors (as representing the people) Il. 22.119.
Of wine, such as is served at assemblies of councillors Il. 4.259: Od. 13.8.
Dat. pl. γέρουσι Il. 4.344, Il. 6.113, Il. 9.70.

div.head: a
div.p: An old man: ἔδεισεν ὁ γ. Il. 1.33, ἠμὲν νέοι ἠδὲ γέροντες Il. 2.789. Cf. Il. 1.380, 538, Il. 3.109, 181, Il. 8.518, etc.: πείθεσθαι γέροντι Od. 2.227 (app. Laertes, as Mentor, described (225) as Ὀδυσῆος ἑταῖρος, was hardly a γ.). Cf. Od. 2.39, Od. 3.390, Od. 4.349, Od. 8.570, Od. 11.38, etc.
In apposition: παρὰ πατρὶ γέροντι Il. 1.358. Cf. Il. 2.793, Il. 5.149, Il. 7.125, etc.: Od. 1.188, Od. 2.157, Od. 3.436, etc.
As a proper adj., old, stricken by age: γ. ἐὼν πολεμιστής Il. 10.549. Cf. Od. 18.53, 81.
Of a thing, old, worn by use: σάκος Od. 22.184.

A member of the βουλή, an elder or councillor: βουλὴν γερόντων Il. 2.53. Cf. Il. 2.21, 404, Il. 4.323, 344, Il. 6.113, Il. 9.70, 89, 422, 574, Il. 15.721, Il. 18.448, Il. 19.303, 338 (here including Agamemnon, the king): γέροντας πλέονας καλέσαντες Od. 7.189. Cf. Od. 2.14, Od. 21.21, Od. 24.255.
An elder acting as one of a body of judges Il. 18.503.
With genit., to taste of, take a taste of. Fig.: δουρὸς ἀκωκῆς Il. 21.61. Cf. Od. 21.98.
Also, fig., to make trial of, try one's fortune with: ἀλλήλων Il. 20.258: Ἀχαιῶν Od. 17.413, χειρῶν Od. 20.181.
A dike or embankment to confine a river: ποταμὸς ἐκέδασσε γεφύρας Il. 5.88. Cf. Il. 5.89.
π(τ)ολέμοιο γέφυραι, app., ranks of men thought of as stemming the tide of warIl. 4.371, Il. 8.378, Il. 11.160, Il. 20.427.
In Il. 8.553 (ἐπὶ πτολέμοιο γεφύρας ἥατο) app., preserving (more or less) the stations in which they had fought.
To make (a way) by forming an embankment: γεφύρωσε κέλευθον Il. 15.357.
The earth = γαῖα 1: ὄφρʼ ἂν ἵκηται γῆν Il. 15.24, φυσίζοος Il. 21.63.
The earth as distinguished from the sea, the land = γαῖα 2..b: ἢ ἁλὸς ἢ ἐπὶ γῆς Od. 12.27. Cf. Od. 21.233.
A particular land or country = γαῖα 4: τίς γῆ; Od. 13.233.
One's native land: ἁμῆς γῆς Od. 11.167, 482.
The surface of the earth, the ground = γαῖα 5: νέρθεν γῆς Od. 11.302, ἦ πρὸς γῆν ἐλάσειε κάρη Od. 17.237.
3 sing. pf. (in pres. sense) γέγηθε Il. 8.559: Od. 6.106.
3 sing. plupf. (in impf. sense) γεγήθει Il. 11.683, Il. 13.494.
With acc. of what is rejoiced at: νῶϊ προφανέντε Il. 8.378, τάδε Il. 9.77.

p.gloss: To take pleasure or delight in doing something.

div.p: With pple.: Ἀργείων ἐρέων γενεήν Il. 7.127.
Joy, delight: ἐγέλασσέ οἱ ἦτορ γηθοσύνῃ Il. 21.390.
The period of old age: ἐς γῆρας Il. 14.86. Cf. Od. 8.226, Od. 19.368, Od. 23.286.
3 sing. impf. ἐγήρα Il. 7.148, Il. 17.197. γήρα Od. 14.67. Also non-thematic pres. pple. γηράς Il. 17.197.
To grow old: ἤδη γηράσκοντα Il. 2.663. Cf. Il. 7.148, Il. 17.197 (twice), 325, Il. 24.541: Od. 4.210, Od. 14.67, Od. 15.409.

div.head: A
div.p: With metrical lengthening of the first syllable γεινόμεθα Il. 22.477 (v.l. γιγνόμεθα).
3 sing. imp. γενέσθω Il. 8.181: Od. 5.224, Od. 17.285, Od. 22.491.
Pple. (with metrical lengthening of the first syllable) γεινόμενος, -ου (vv. ll. γιγνόμενος, -ου) Il. 10.71, Il. 20.128, Il. 23.79, Il. 24.210: Od. 4.208, Od. 7.198.
Acc. sing. masc. pple. γεγαῶτα Il. 9.456: Od. 4.112, 144, Od. 19.400.
(For these pf. forms cf. μάω, μέμονα under μάω.)

div.head: B
div.p: Infin. γείνασθαι Il. 21.160: Od. 8.312. (ἐγ-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, παρα-, περι-, προ-.)

div.head: I
div.p: In pres. and impf. and forms (A), to come into being.

To be born, take one's being: τράφεν ἠδʼ ἐγένοντο Il. 1.251, τῶν ἓξ ἐγένοντο Il. 5.270, πρότερος γενόμην (am the elder) Il. 19.219, Il. 21.440. Cf. Il. 5.548, 897, Il. 6.206, 489, Il. 10.71, etc.: τοῦ μʼ ἔκ φασι γενέσθαι Od. 1.220, γαμέοντί τε γεινομένῳ τε Od. 4.208. Cf. Od. 3.28, Od. 4.723, Od. 7.198, Od. 8.311, Od. 10.350, etc.

In pf., to be in the condition of having been born; hence simply, to exist, live, be: οἳ ὁπλότεροι γεγάασιν Il. 4.325: ἐν αἶγες γεγάασιν Od. 9.118, οἳ νῦν γεγάασιν Od. 24.84. Cf. Od. 5.35 = Od. 19.279, Od. 6.62, Od. 10.5, Od. 13.160.
In more strict pf. sense: ἤδη ἀνὴρ γέγονʼ ἐσθλός (has been born, is born) Il. 19.122.
Sim. in plupf.: Ζεὺς πρότερος γεγόνει (had been born earlier, was the elder) Il. 13.355.
So ὑπὸ τμώλῳ γεγαῶτας (born (and dwelling) there) Il. 2.866.

To come into view or notice, be seen, heard, etc.: κλαγγή Il. 1.49, ὀδμή Il. 14.415, σέλας Il. 19.374. Cf. Il. 4.456, Il. 10.375, Il. 11.50, Il. 15.607, Il. 22.150, etc.: Od. 12.87, 396, Od. 22.77, 133, Od. 23.137.

Of natural phenomena, natural products, etc., to come into being, rise, grow, be: φύλλα καὶ ἄνθεα Il. 2.468. Cf. Il. 2.397: ἐκ νυκτῶν ἄνεμοι γίγνονται Od. 12.287, ἐν οἶνος γίγνεται Od. 13.245, χιὼν γένετο (fell) Od. 14.476. Cf. Od. 9.51, Od. 12.326, Od. 17.23, Od. 22.491.
To come to or upon, fall to, befall, be the lot of, affect (a person).

With dat.: Πηλεΐωνι ἄχος Il. 1.188, αἰδώς οἱ Il. 24.45. Cf. Il. 3.323, Il. 4.245, 289, Il. 9.125, Il. 14.98, Il. 19.274, etc.: παντα οἱ γένοιτο Od. 17.355, μὴ νῶϊν ἔρις γένηται Od. 18.13. Cf. Od. 8.414, Od. 11.208, Od. 18.122 = Od. 20.199, Od. 18.366, Od. 19.569, Od. 21.412.
For ἐμὲ χρεὼ γίγνεται Od. 4.634 see χρειώ 1.a.
Without case: ποινὴ οὔ τις ἐγίγνετο Il. 13.659. Cf. Il. 1.341, Il. 9.380, Il. 21.529: Od. 22.306.

To be manifested or shown, to be, come into play, take effect: οὔ τις φειδὼ γίγνεται (there is no . . .) Il. 7.410, μνημοσύνη τις γενέσθω (let there be . . .) Il. 8.181. Cf. Il. 15.359, Il. 23.505: εἰ γὰρ ἐπʼ ἀρῇσιν τέλος γένοιτο Od. 17.496. Cf. Od. 10.202 = 568.

To happen, occur, come round, come to pass, take place: ἠώς Il. 1.493, τάδε ἔργα Il. 6.348, ἀγορή Il. 7.345. Cf. Il. 3.110, 176, Il. 8.130, Il. 17.686, Il. 24.436, etc.: νόστον γενέσθαι Od. 4.173. Cf. Od. 1.379, Od. 2.26, 374, Od. 3.129, 228, Od. 4.747, Od. 5.299, Od. 11.537, Od. 12.191, Od. 24.455, 461, etc.

To become, come to be, prove to be so and so: ὁμηγερέες Il. 1.57, ἄνεῳ Il. 2.323, ἐν πυρὶ βουλαὶ γενοίατο (be cast) 340, κλισίῃσιν ἐν Ἀτρεΐδαο γένοντο (reached the . . .) Il. 7.313. Cf. Il. 2.453, Il. 3.71, Il. 4.17, 466, Il. 8.180, Il. 20.497, Il. 22.421, etc.: λέων γένετο Od. 4.456, ὄφρʼ ἔτι δύης ἐπὶ πῆμα γενοίμην (be brought into . . .) Od. 14.338, φόνος οἱ γένοντο Od. 21.24. Cf. Od. 1.266, Od. 3.271, Od. 7.154, 316, Od. 15.446, Od. 16.175, etc.

Passes from this last sense into that, practically, of the copula, to be so and so: οὔ πώ τις ὁμοῖος γένετʼ ἀνήρ (was) Il. 2.553, ὃν κάρτιστον Ἀχαιῶν φημὶ γενέσθαι (that he is) Il. 6.98, ζαχρηεῖς γίγνοντο (were wont to be) Il. 13.684, ἀρίγνωτος Διὸς γίγνεται ἀλκή Il. 15.490. Cf. Il. 4.375, Il. 6.153, 210, Il. 13.569, Il. 16.746, Il. 20.220, etc.: οὐ νηὸς ἐπήβολος γίγνομαι Od. 2.320, τηλύγετος Od. 4.11 (after ἐκ δούλης in 12 supply γεγαώς). Cf. Od. 4.201, 362, Od. 5.224, Od. 8.586, Od. 9.35, Od. 17.223, Od. 19.344, Od. 22.130, etc.

div.head: II
div.p: In forms (B), to give (a person) being.
Of the father, to beget: παῖδα γείνατο τυδεύς Il. 5.800. Cf. Il. 4.400, Il. 5.880, Il. 15.526, Il. 21.160: υἷε κραταιώ Od. 15.242. Cf. Od. 7.61, Od. 20.202.

Of the mother, to bear: θεά σε γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 1.280. Cf. Il. 3.238, Il. 4.476, Il. 5.896, Il. 6.24, 26, Il. 24.608, etc.: ἥ ῥʼ Ἡρακλῆα γείνατο Od. 11.268. Cf. Od. 1.223, Od. 4.13, Od. 6.25, Od. 11.299, Od. 21.172.
Of both parents Il. 7.10, Il. 21.142: Od. 7.57, Od. 8.312.
2 sing. fut. in mid. form γνώσεαι Il. 2.367, Il. 10.88: Od. 16.310. γνώσῃ Il. 2.365.
Infin. γνώμεναι Il. 2.349, Il. 21.266, 609: Od. 1.411. γνῶναι Od. 2.159, Od. 13.312, Od. 24.159. (ἀνα-, δια-, ἐπι-.)

div.head: a
div.p: To perceive, mark, remark, note, find, see, know: ἣν ἄτην Il. 1.411 = Il. 16.273, Διὸς τάλαντα Il. 16.658. Cf. Il. 12.272, Il. 16.119, 362, Il. 19.84.

div.head: b
div.p: With acc. and complementary pple.: γιγνώσκω Ἄρηα κοιρανέοντα Il. 5.824. Cf. Il. 14.154, Il. 17.84: Od. 15.532, Od. 17.549, 556.
With pple. alone: ὅτε γίγνωσκε θεοῦ γόνον ἐόντα Il. 6.191: γνῶναι τὸν ἐόντα (that it was he) Od. 24.159.
With a sim. pple. in genit.: ὡς γνῶ χωομένοιο Il. 4.357.
With adj.: γνῶ. ἄνδρας δηΐους (that they were . . .) Il. 10.358.

div.head: c
div.p: With acc. and dependent clause: γιγνώσκω σε, ὅττι . . . Il. 24.563. Cf. Il. 5.85.

With clause only: γνώμεναι εἰ . . . Il. 2.349. Cf. Il. 2.365, Il. 3.53, Il. 6.231, Il. 8.17, Il. 14.58, Il. 18.125, Il. 21.609, etc.: γνοίης χʼ οἵη ἐμὴ δύναμίς [ἐστιν] Od. 20.237. Cf.
Od. 3.166, Od. 8.299, Od. 17.269, 363, Od. 22.373, etc.
To gain knowledge of, get to know, learn: Τρώων νόον Il. 22.382. Cf. Od. 1.3, Od. 16.304.
To get to know, make the acquaintance of (a person) Od. 1.411.
To become aware of the presence of, discover (a person) Il. 24.688 (twice), 691.
To experience, find: φιλότητα Od. 15.537 = Od. 17.164 = Od. 19.310.

div.head: a
div.p: To have knowledge, know: ὅσσον ἔγωγε γιγνώσκω Il. 13.223.
With dependent clause: γιγνώσκων ὅ τʼ ἄναλκις ἔην θεός Il. 5.331. Cf. Il. 5.433: Od. 21.209.

div.head: b
div.p: In aor., to know: ἔγνως ἐμὴν βουλήν (knowest) Il. 20.20.
To know (a person): αἴ κέ ποθι γνώω τοιοῦτον ἐόντα (in case I may find that I know him, seeing he was such a one, i.e. such as to be likely to be known) Od. 14.118.
To distinguish, discern: ἠμὲν θεὸν ἠδὲ καὶ ἄνδρα Il. 5.128. Cf. Il. 13.72.
With acc. and dependent clause: ἵππους οἳ δεύτεροι οἵ τε πάροιθεν Il. 23.497.

To know (a person or thing) for what he or it is, know the nature of, know: εὖ σε γιγνώσκων Il. 22.356. Cf. Il. 17.32 = Il. 20.198, Il. 18.270: ἔγνω [ποταμόν] (i.e. recognized him for a god) Od. 5.444, καλάμην γιγνώσκειν (i.e. can judge from that what I was) Od. 14.215. Cf. Od. 2.159, Od. 16.310.
Sim.: θεὸν ἔγνω (knew that it was a god) Od. 1.420.
Absol., to recognize one's claim, hold it good Il. 23.661.
To have the eyes bright or glaring. Of a lion Il. 20.172.
Bright, shining, gleaming (prob. without any notion of colour). Of the sea Il. 16.34.

p.gloss: (The) bright-eyed (maid) (prob. without any notion of colour).

div.p: Epithet or a name of Athene Il. 1.206, Il. 2.166, Il. 5.29, Il. 6.88, Il. 8.373, etc.: Od. 1.44, 156, Od. 2.433, Od. 3.13, 135, etc.
[γλάφω = γλύφω. See γλυφίς, and cf. διαγλάφω.]

Hollow, hollowed (for the most part as a conventional epithet). Of caves Il. 18.402, Il. 24.83: Od. 1.15 = Od. 9.30, Od. 1.73, Od. 2.20, Od. 4.403, Od. 5.68, 155, 194, 226, Od. 9.114, 476, Od. 12.210, Od. 23.335.
Of rocks, having a cavity or cavities Il. 2.88: Od. 14.533.
Of a harbour (referring to the curved outline) Od. 12.305.
Elsewhere epithet of ships Il. 2.454, 516, Il. 3.119, Il. 5.327, Il. 8.180, etc.: Od. 3.287, Od. 4.356, 513, Od. 9.99, Od. 10.23, etc.
The eye, the eyeball Il. 14.494: Od. 9.390.
A plaything, a doll or puppet: ἔρρε, κακὴ γλήνη Il. 8.164.
One of the buttocks: δεξιόν Il. 5.66, Il. 13.651.
In pl., the buttocks, the rump Il. 8.340.
Sweet or pleasant to the taste: σίτου Il. 11.89: συκέαι Od. 7.116 = Od. 11.590 (the tree for the fruit). Cf. Od. 4.88, Od. 14.194, Od. 20.69, Od. 24.68.
Of water, sweet, fit for drinking Od. 12.306.
Generally, sweet, pleasant, giving delight or joy: ὕπνος Il. 10.4, μολπῆς Il. 13.637. Cf. Il. 24.3, 636: Od. 4.295, Od. 5.472, Od. 16.23 = Od. 17.41, Od. 19.511, Od. 22.323, Od. 23.145, 255.
In comp.: ἧς γαίης γλυκερώτερον ἄλλο Od. 9.28.
Of gentle or kindly mind: ἀνήρ Il. 20.467.
-ύ. Comp. γλυκίων, γλύκιον Il. 1.249, Il. 2.453, Il. 11.13, Il. 18.109: Od. 9.34.
Sweet or pleasant to the taste: νέκταρ Il. 1.598.
[γλύφω, to cut out, carve. Cf. γλαφυρός.]
App., the notch in an arrow to receive the string.
In pl. (poss. referring to a double notch (i.e. two notches at right angles)) Il. 4.122: Od. 21.419.
Of the tongues of sacrificial victims Od. 3.332, 341.
A tongue or language Il. 2.804: Od. 19.175.

App., a tongue forming one of the ends of the ζυγόδεσμον or yoke-fastening, the ζ. being wound round the pole criss-cross, keeping the portion with the tongue the longer, and the tongue being tucked in under its portion after that portion had been wound over, and had so secured, the end of the other and shorter portion: ὑπὸ γλωχῖνα δʼ ἔκαμψαν Il. 24.274 (ὑπό advbl.).
