In pl., the jaws Od. 16.175, Od. 18.29, Od. 20.347.
Bent, curved: ἕλικας Il. 18.401: ἀγκίστροισιν Od. 4.369 = Od. 12.332.
Fig., that can be bent or influenced: νόημα Il. 24.41.
As epithet of the limbs, flexible, lissom Il. 11.669, Il. 24.359: Od. 11.394, Od. 13.398, 430, Od. 21.283.
Sim. of jaws, moving freely in their sockets Il. 11.416.
To bend: ἐν γόνυ γνάμψεν (app., crooked his knee round the other's leg) Il. 23.731.
(Lawfully) begotten, born in wedlock, legitimate Il. 11.102: Od. 14.202.
On the knee or the knees: ἔριπεν Il. 5.68. Cf. Il. 5.309, 357, Il. 8.329, Il. 11.355, Il. 20.417.
Absol., a friend or acquaintance Od. 16.9.
Easy to be known, evident: γνωτόν [ἐστιν] ὡς . . . Il. 7.401 Cf. Od. 24.182.

div.head: a
div.p: A kinsman or kinswoman: γνωτοὺς λιποῦσα Il. 3.174, γνωτοί τε γνωταί τε Il. 15.350. Cf. Il. 13.697 = Il. 15.336.

div.head: b
div.p: More specifically, a brother (and the word may bear this sense in the passages under a) Il. 14.485, Il. 17.35, Il. 22.234.
1 pl. opt. γοάοιμεν Il. 24.664. γοάοιεν Od. 24.190.
3 sing. fut. in mid. form γοήσεται Il. 21.124, Il. 22.353.
3 pl. aor. γόον (perh. formed fr. γόος) Il. 6.500.

To weep, wail, show signs of grief: μὴ γοόωσα οἰκῆας ἐγείρῃ Il. 5.413. Cf. Il. 6.373, Il. 18.315, 355, Il. 22.476, Il. 23.106: ἑζόμενοι γόων Od. 10.567. Cf. Od. 4.721, 800, Od. 8.92, Od. 9.467, Od. 10.209, Od. 12.234, Od. 19.119, 210, 513.
To weep for, bewail, lament, mourn for the loss of: Ἕκτορα Il. 6.500, ὃν πότμον Il. 16.857 = Il. 22.363: πόσιν Od. 19.264.
To pay mourning rites to: αὐτόν Il. 24.664. Cf. Il. 14.502, Il. 21.124, Il. 22.353: Od. 24.190.
A wooden peg, a treenail Od. 5.248.

div.head: a
div.p: The offspring, a child: διός Il. 5.635. Cf. Il. 24.59: Od. 2.274, Od. 4.207, Od. 18.218.

div.head: c
div.p: In both these senses: ὃν (i.e. Λαέρταο) καὶ Ὀδυσσῆος Od. 4.741.
One's children or family: νεώτατος γόνοιο Il. 20.409.
One's parentage: ὃν γόνον ἐξαγόρευεν Od. 11.234. Cf. Od. 1.216, Od. 19.166.
Genit. γουνός (for γονϝ-ός) Il. 11.547: Od. 19.450. γούνατος Il. 21.591.

Of clasping the knees in supplication: λαβέ [μιν] γούνων (by the knees) Il. 1.407. Cf. Il. 1.500, 512, 557, Il. 6.45, Il. 15.76, Il. 20.468, Il. 21.65, 68, 71, Il. 22.345, Il. 24.357, 465, 478: μητρὸς ποτὶ γούνασι χεῖρας βάλλειν Od. 6.310. Cf. Od. 6.142, 147, 169, Od. 7.142, Od. 10.264, 323, Od. 22.310, 339, 342, 365.
So with a word of seizing to be supplied: λισσέσκετο γούνων Il. 9.451. Cf. Od. 10.481, Od. 22.337.

Sim.: περὶ γούνατʼ ἐμὰ στήσεσθαι λισσομένους Il. 11.609. Cf. Il. 18.457, Il. 20.463: σὰ γούναθʼ ἱκάνω Od. 5.449, Od. 7.147, Ἀμφινόμου πρὸς γοῦνα καθέζετο (as putting himself under his protection) Od. 18.395. Cf. Od. 3.92 = Od. 4.322, Od. 9.266, Od. 13.231.
Of kissing the knees in supplication: ἥ οἱ γούνατʼ ἔκυσσε Il. 8.371. Cf. Od. 14.279.

By extension, in pl., the knee(s) and thigh(s) of a sitting person: ἐν γούνασι πῖπτε διώνης (on her knee) Il. 5.370, Ἀθηναίης ἐπὶ γούνασιν (on the lap, i.e., app., of a seated statue) Il. 6.92, 273, 303. Cf. Il. 5.408, Il. 9.455, 488, Il. 21.506, Il. 22.500: ἐμὲ γούνασιν οἷσιν ἐφεσσάμενος Od. 16.443. Cf. Od. 19.401, Od. 21.55.–ταῦτα θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται, the issue lies with the gods(perh. referring to the custom of placing gifts on the lap of a statue (cf. Il. 6.92, 273, 303 cited above), the gifts being irrevocably dedicated, and symbolizing complete submission to divine governance) Il. 17.514 = Il. 20.435: = Od. 1.267 = Od. 16.129, Od. 1.400.
Weeping, wailing, lamentation, mourning Il. 5.156, Il. 6.499, Il. 17.37, Il. 18.51, Il. 23.10, 14, etc.: Od. 4.102, 113, Od. 8.540, Od. 16.144, Od. 19.268, Od. 21.228, etc.
In pl.: ὀδύνας τε γόους τε Od. 1.242.
Inclination to weep: πᾶσιν ὑπέδυ γ. Od. 10.398.
Mourning rites, formal mourning or lamentation: ἦρχε γόοιο Il. 24.723. Cf. Il. 24.747, 761.
[γουν-, γόνυ. To clasp the knees, clasp by the knees, in supplication. Cf. γόνυ 3.]
To supplicate, entreat. Retaining the genitival construction of a vb. of taking hold, and with the construction extended to something appealed to: μή με γούνων γουνάζεο μηδὲ τοκήων Il. 22.345.
With this latter construction alone: τῶν ὄπιθέν σε γουνάζομαι Od. 11.66.
With prepositional clauses indicating what is appealed to: τῶν ὕπερ Il. 15.665. Cf. Od. 11.66, Od. 13.324.
With simple acc. of the person entreated: γουνάσομαί μιν Il. 1.427.
[perh. fr. γονϝ-, γόνυ, in sense swell, knoll, and, in reference to a vineyard, etc., the part best catching the sun, and therefore the most fruitful.]
γουνῷ (γουνὸν) ἀλωῆς Il. 9.534, Il. 18.57 = 438: Od. 1.193, Od. 11.193, ἐς γουνὸν Ἀθηνάων Od. 11.323 (here perh. the reference is to the citadel).

App., to supplicate (and at the same
time to vow to do something): νεκύων κάρηνα ῥέξειν . . . Od. 10.521, Od. 11.29.
contr. nom. pl. masc. pres. pple. γοάω.
To scratch, cut into, incise: δ'στέον Il. 17.599.
To form by scratching or incision: θυμοφθόρα Il. 6.169.
In apposition: γρηΐ ἀμφιπόλῳ Od. 1.191. Cf. Od. 18.27, Od. 24.211.
One of the two curved plates, front and back, of which the θώρηξ was formed. The front plate Il. 5.99, 189, Il. 13.507 = Il. 17.314, Il. 13.587.
In pl. of the two plates Il. 15.530.
The limbs: γ. ἔθηκεν ἐλαφρά Il. 5.122 = Il. 13.61 = Il. 23.772. Cf. Il. 19.385, Il. 22.448, Il. 23.691.
As that upon which fear takes hold or which it affects: τρόμος ἔλλαβε γ. Il. 3.34, Il. 8.452, Il. 14.506, Il. 24.170. Cf. Il. 7.215 = Il. 20.44, Il. 10.95, 390: Od. 6.140, Od. 11.527, Od. 18.88.
App. as the seat of yearning: ἦλθʼ ἵμερος [γόοιο] ἀπὸ γυίων Il. 24.514.
To lame, cripple: γυιώσω σθωῒν ἵππους Il. 8.402. Cf. Il. 8.416.
Without clothes, naked: σὲ εὐλαὶ ἔδονται γυμνόν Il. 22.510. Cf. Od. 6.136.
Without armour, unarmed: κτενέει με γυμνὸν ἐόντα Il. 22.124. Cf. Il. 16.815, Il. 17.122 = 693, 711, Il. 18.21, Il. 21.50.
Of a bow, out of its case Od. 11.607.
Of an arrow, out of the quiver Od. 21.417.
To become naked, strip oneself: αἰδέομαι γυμνοῦσθαι Od. 6.222. Cf. Od. 10.341.
To be left unprotected by armour or shield: οὖτα γυμνωθέντα Il. 16.312 = 400. Cf. Il. 12.389, 428.
Of a wall, to be left bare of defence Il. 12.399.
Of a woman: δώρων (given to a woman) Od. 11.521, Od. 15.247.
The mistress of a house Od. 16.334, Od. 21.86.

In pl., the female servants in a house: τετυγμένα χερσὶ γυναικῶν Il. 22.511. Cf. Il. 18.559: εἰς ὅ κʼ εἴπω γυναιξὶ δεῖπνον τετυκεῖν Od. 15.76. Cf. Od. 2.108, Od. 16.304, Od. 17.75, Od. 18.186, Od. 19.16, Od. 22.437, etc.
With ἀμφίπολος Od. 1.362, Od. 6.52, Od. 7.235, Od. 16.413, Od. 21.8, etc.
In sing., one of the servants Od. 15.417, 434, 439, Od. 19.344, etc.
With words indicating the servant's country of origin: Φοίνισσα Od. 15.417, Σικελή Od. 24.211.
Her office: ταμίη Il. 6.390: Od. 2.345, Od. 3.479, ἀλετρίς Od. 20.105.

div.head: a
div.p: A woman as distinguished from a man: γυναικὸς ἀντὶ τέτυξο Il. 8.163. Cf. Il. 7.139, 236, Il. 9.134, Il. 15.683, etc.: οὔτʼ ἄνδρʼ οὔτε γυναῖκα Od. 4.142, Od. 6.161. Cf. Od. 7.109, Od. 13.308, Od. 15.163, Od. 19.408, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: A wife: σὺν γυναιξί τε καὶ τεκέεσσιν Il. 4.162. Cf. Il. 3.48, Il. 6.160, Il. 8.57, Il. 9.394, Il. 17.36, etc.: ἀνὴρ ἠδὲ γ. Od. 6.184. Cf. Od. 1.13, 433, Od. 2.249, Od. 7.347, Od. 14.211, Od. 17.152, Od. 21.72, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: A concubine as opposed to a wife Il. 24.497.

div.head: d
div.p: A woman as distinguished from a goddess: θεᾶς οὐδὲ γυναικός Il. 14.315. Cf. Il. 16.176, Il. 24.58: ἢ θεὸς ἠὲ γ. Od. 10.228, 255.
With words indicative of mortality: θνητάων Il. 20.305: θνητήν Od. 11.244.
In voc. as a term of courteous or respectful address, lady Il. 3.204, 438, Il. 6.441, Il. 24.300: Od. 4.148, Od. 6.168, Od. 8.424, Od. 11.248, etc.
A vulture (except in Od. 11.578 always preying on carrion. Cf. αἰγυπιός) Il. 4.237, Il. 11.162, Il. 16.836, Il. 18.271, Il. 22.42: Od. 11.578, Od. 22.30.
A case for a bow Od. 21.54.
With genit.: ἄθλων (in . . .) Od. 8.159. Cf. Od. 8.263, Od. 16.253.
Genit. pl. δαέρων as spondee Il. 24.762, 769.
Emphasizing particle used after interrogatives: τίς δ. ὅμιλος; Od. 1.225. Cf. Il. 10.408 (v.l. δʼ αἱ): Od. 24.299.
To ornament curiously: σάκος Il. 18.479: χρυσῷ τε καὶ ἀργύρῳ Od. 23.200.
Something curiously wrought, an ornament Od. 19.227.
In pl., things curiously wrought, pieces of cunning workmanship, ornaments: χάλκευον δαίδαλα πολλά Il. 18.400. Cf. Il. 5.60, Il. 14.179, Il. 18.482, Il. 19.13, 19.
To rend, tear: Ἑκτόρεον χιτῶνα Il. 2.416. Cf. Il. 7.247, Il. 16.841.

To rend the flesh of,
wound, slay: δεδαϊγμένον ἦτορ (app., with the life killed in him) Il. 17.535, δαΐζων χαλκᾠ Il. 24.393. Cf. Il. 11.497, Il. 18.236, Il. 19.203, 211, 283, 292, 319, Il. 21.147, Il. 22.72.
Fig., in pass., to be in two minds, be in doubt: δαϊζόμενος ἢ . . . ἦε . . . Il. 14.20
Of the mind, etc., to be troubled or distressed: ἐδαΐζετο θυμός Il. 9.8 = Il. 15.629. Cf. Od. 13.320.
dat. of δάϊς + κτάμενος. See κτείνω.]
Under superhuman influence, possessed, whose actions are unaccountable or ill-omened.
In stern reproof Il. 1.561, Il. 6.326, Il. 9.40.
In more or less stern remonstrance Il. 2.190, Il. 3.399, Il. 4.31: Od. 18.15, Od. 19.71.
In tender or gentle remonstrance Il. 6.407, 486: Od. 10.472, Od. 23.166, 174, 264.
Conveying an implication of folly or senselessness Il. 2.200, Il. 13.448, 810: Od. 4.774, Od. 18.406.
App. indicating a degree of wonder, the person addressed showing himself superior to what his outward man would indicate: δαιμόνιε ξείνων Od. 14.443.
App., with orig. sense lost sight of, merely in affectionate address Il. 24.194.
A superhuman power, with little notion of personality (sometimes difficult to distinguish from the next sense).

div.head: a
div.p: Represented as evil or maleficent: μάχης ἐπὶ μήδεα κείρει δ. ἡμετέρης Il. 15.468. Cf. Il. 9.600, Il. 11.480, Il. 15.418, Il. 21.93: στυγερός οἱ ἔχραε δ. Od. 5.396. Cf. Od. 4.275, Od. 5.421, Od. 6.172 (cf. θεοί 174), Od. 7.248, Od. 10.64, Od. 11.587, Od. 12.169, 295, Od. 14.488, Od. 16.194, 370 (evil to the speaker), Od. 17.446, Od. 19.201, Od. 24.149.

div.head: b
div.p: As beneficent: ἄλλα δ. ὑποθήσεται Od. 3.27. Cf. Od. 9.381, Od. 17.243 = Od. 21.201 (cf. θεός τις Od. 21.196), Od. 19.10, 138.

In generalized sense, superhuman power, heaven, fate, the gods (sometimes difficult to distinguish from the δαιμόνιος. sense): σὺν δαίμονι (if heaven so wills it) Il. 11.792, Il. 15.403, πρὸς δαίμονα φωτὶ μάχεσθαι (against the will of the gods) Il. 17.98. Cf. Il. 7.291, 377 = 396, Il. 17.104: δαίμονος αἶσα Od. 11.61. Cf. Od. 2.134, Od. 16.64, Od. 18.146, 256 = Od. 19.129, Od. 19.512, Od. 20.87, Od. 24.306.–δαίμονά τοι δώσω (I will deal thee fate, i.e. death) Il. 8.166.
With more marked notion of personality: ἐπέσσυτο δαίμονι ἶσος Il. 5.438 = Il. 16.705 = 786 = Il. 20.447. Cf. Il. 5.459 = 884, Il. 20.493, Il. 21.18, 227.

div.head: a
div.p: In pl. = θεοί in gen.: βεβήκει μετὰ δαίμονας ἄλλους Il. 1.222. Cf. Il. 6.115, Il. 23.595.

div.head: b
div.p: In sing., of a particular god: οὐδʼ ἐπιορκήσω πρὸς δαίμονος (i.e. the god, or, as in the sequel, the gods, by whom he was to swear) Il. 19.188: λίσσομʼ ὑπὲρ θυέων καὶ δαίμονος (i.e. whatever god the sacrifice was being made to) Od. 15.261.
More definitely: γίγνωσκον ὃ δὴ κακὰ μήδετο δ. Od. 3.166 (the context app. showing that the reference is exclusively to Zeus).

div.head: c
div.p: Of a definite goddess present in her own person: ἦρχε δ. (i.e. Aphrodite) Il. 3.420.
2 sing. subj. mid. δαινύῃ Od. 8.243. δαινύ̆ῃ Od. 19.328.
Nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. δαισάμενοι Od. 7.188, Od. 18.408. (μετα-.)

div.head: a
div.p: To give (a meal): δαίνυ δαῖτα γέρουσιν Il. 9.70.

div.head: b
div.p: To give (a wedding-feast): δαινύντα γάμον Od. 4.3.
Sim. δαίσειν γάμον (app., to bring it about) Il. 19.299.

div.head: δ
div.p: With cognate acc. As (α): εἰλαπίνην δαίνυντο Il. 23.201. Cf. Od. 3.66 = Od. 20.280, Od. 7.50, Od. 11.186, Od. 13.26.

div.head: b
div.p: To partake of: ἑκατόμβας Il. 9.535 (i.e. of the god's share thereof): κρέα τε καὶ μέθυ Od. 9.162 = 557 = Od. 10.184 = Od. 10.468 = Od. 10.477= Od. 12.30.

A meal (often with the notion of faring well or revelling): δαίνυ δαῖτα Il. 9.70, δαῖτα πένοντο Il. 18.558 (app. a meal for the King and his retainers, that for the ἔριθοι being mentioned below), πειθώμεθα δαιτί (i.e. to hunger) Il. 23.48. Cf. Il. 1.467, 468, 575, 579, Il. 4.259, 343, etc.: ὄφρʼ ἂν δαῖτα πτωχεύῃ (i.e. beg his bread) Od. 17.11, δαιτῶν ἀπολυμαντῆρα 220. Cf. Od. 1.152, 374, Od. 2.322, Od. 3.33, Od. 7.232, Od. 10.124, etc.
Of the god's share of a sacrifice: Ζεὺς ἔβη κατὰ δαῖτα Il. 1.424. Cf. Il. 4.48 = Il. 24.69: τέρπετο δαιτὶ παρήμενος Od. 1.26 (of Poseidon). Cf. Od. 3.336, 420, Od. 8.76.
Of what a beast devours Il. 24.43.
War, battle: ἐν δαΐ λυγρῇ (λευγαλέῃ) Il. 13.286, Il. 14.387, Il. 24.739.
Of a god's share of a sacrifice Od. 3.44.
From, leaving, a meal: δαίτηθεν ἰόντα Od. 10.216.
To make an apportionment of spoil Il. 11.688, 705.
One who carves meat, a carver Od. 1.141 = Od. 4.57, Od. 17.331.
In pl.: θεράποντε δαήμονε δαιτροσυνάων Od. 16.253.
A guest at or partaker of a meal or feast Od. 4.621, Od. 7.102, 148, Od. 8.66 = 473, Od. 9.7, Od. 15.467, Od. 17.605, Od. 22.12 (in the last two passages of the self-invited guests, the suitors).
Skilled, whether in war or in the arts of peace.
3 sing. pf. (in pres. sense) δέδηε Il. 13.736, Il. 17.253, Il. 20.18: Od. 20.353.
3 sing. plupf. (in impf. sense) δεδήει Il. 2.93, Il. 12.35, 466.
3 sing. aor. subj. pass. δάηται Il. 20.316, Il. 21.375. (ἀμφι-.)
To set on fire, kindle: ξύλα Il. 18.347: Od. 8.436.
To cause (fire) to appear or blaze Il. 5.4, 7, Il. 18.206, 227.
In pf. and plupf. and in pass., to burn or blaze: πῦρ δαιετο Il. 21.343. Cf. Il. 8.75, Il. 18.227 Il. 20.316 = Il. 21.375: Od. 5.61.
Of the eyes, to blaze Il. 12.466.
So of a lion's eyes Od. 6.132.

Fig.: Ὄσσα δεδήει (spread like wild-fire) Il. 2.93, νῦν ἄγχιστα μάχη δέδηε (app., now most nearly blazes up, i.e. is on the point of blazing up) Il. 20.18. Cf. Il. 12.35, Il. 13.736, Il. 17.253: οἰμωγὴ δέδηε (is bursting forth) Od. 20.353.
In mid.: κρέα δαίετο Od. 15.140. Cf. Od. 17.332.
In pass.: Αἰθίοπας, τοὶ διχθὰ δεδαίαται (are divided) Od. 1.23, μήλων δαιομένων (in the division of the . . .) Od. 9.551.
Fig., to be troubled or distressed: δαίεταί μοι ἦτορ Od. 1.48.
Fig.: δάκε φρένας μῦθος Il. 5.493 (cf. θυμοδακής).

A tear: δεύοντο δάκρυσι κόλποι Il. 9.570. Cf. Il. 23.16, Il. 24.162: Od. 7.260, Od. 17.103 = Od. 19.596.–(κατὰ) δ. χέειν, to shed a tear, to weepIl. 1.357, 413, Il. 3.142, Il. 6.405, Il. 9.14, etc.: Od. 2.24, Od. 4.556, Od. 11.5, Od. 12.12, Od. 14.280, etc.

Sim. in various expressions: βαλέειν ἀπὸ δ. παρειῶν Od. 4.198. Cf. Od. 4.114, 223, Od. 17.490.– ἔκπεσέ οἱ δ. Il. 2.266: Od. 16.16.– κατείβετο δ. Il. 24.794: τί δ. κατείβετον; Od. 21.86.–δ. ἀπομόρξασθαι, to wipe away one's tears Il. 2.269: Od. 17.304.– δ. ἔδευε παρειάς (his tears) Od. 8.522.
As the visible feature of weeping; hence, in pl., tears, weeping: δάκρυσι θυμὸν ἐρέχθων Od. 5.83 = 157.
In neut. δακρυόεν as adv.: γελάσας (smiling through her tears) Il. 6.484.
Accompanied by tears: γόοιο Od. 4.801, Od. 17.8, Od. 24.323.
Causing tears, bringing misery: πόλεμον Il. 5.737 = Il. 8.388, Il. 17.512. Cf. Il. 11.601, Il. 13.765, Il. 16.436.
Instrumental δακρυόφι Il. 17.696, Il. 23.397: Od. 4.705, Od. 10.248, Od. 19.472, Od. 20.349.

A tear: ὄσσε δακρυόφι πλῆσθεν (with tears) Il. 17.696 = Il. 23.397: = Od. 4.705 = Od. 19.472, οὐδέ ποτʼ ὄσσε δακρυόφιν τέρσοντο (were free of tears) Od. 5.152, δάκρυα κεῦθεν Od. 19.212. Cf. Od. 10.248 = Od. 20.349, Od. 18.173.–δάκρυα χέειν, to shed tears, to weepIl. 7.426, Il. 16.3, Il. 18.17, 235: Od. 24.46.– χύτο δάκρυα Il. 23.385: δάκρυα χέοντο Od. 4.523.

Sim. in varous expressions: δάκρυʼ ἀναπρήσας Il. 9.433: Od. 2.81.–(κατὰ) δάκρυον εἴβειν, to shed a tear, to weepIl. 16.11, Il. 19.323', Il. 24.9: Od. 4.153, Od. 8.531, Od. 11.391, Od. 16.219, 332, Od. 24.234, 280.– δάκρυα λείβειν Il. 13.88, 658, Il. 18.32: Od. 5.84 = 158, Od. 8.86, 93 = 532, Od. 16.214.– δάκρυʼ ἔκβαλεν Od. 19.362.– δάκρυον ἧκεν Od. 16.191, Od. 23.33.– δάκρυα πίπτει Od. 14.129.– δάκρυα ῥέεν Il. 17.437: Od. 19.204.– δάκρυʼ ὀμόργνυσθαι (ὀμόρξασθαι) Il. 18.124: Od. 8.88, Od. 11.527, 530.
As the visible feature of weeping: τείσειαν Δαναοὶ ἐμὰ δάκρυα (my weeping, i.e. the cause thereof, my wrongs) Il. 1.42.
(ᾱ) [δάκρυ + πλώω in sense to flow. Cf. L. pluo.]
To flow with tears, be maudlin Od. 19.122.
To shed tears, weep: δακρύσας ἕζετο (with a burst of tears) Il. 1.349. Cf. Il. 10.377. Il. 19.229: δάκρυσα ἰδών Od. 11.55 = 395, 87. Cf. Od. 1.336, Od. 17.33, 38, Od. 21.82, Od. 23.207.
In pf. pass., to be in tears: τίπτε δεδάκρυσαι; Il. 16.7.
To be covered or filled with tears: δεδάκρυνται παρειαί Il. 22.491. Cf. Od. 20.204, 353.
A piece of ignited material for communicating fire, a fire-brand Il. 13.320, Il. 15.421: Od. 5.488.
A brand snatched from the fire or from a brazier Od. 19.69.
3 sing. fut. δαμάᾳ Il. 22.271. δαμᾷ Il. 1.61.
Imp. δάμασον Il. 9.496: Od. 11.562. δάμασσον Il. 3.352.
Nom. pl. δαμάσαντες Il. 18.113, Il. 19.66: Od. 9.59.
Aor. pass. δάμην Il. 20.94 [ἦ κʼ ἐδάμην Allen].
Acc. sing. masc. pple. δμηθέντα Il. 4.99, Il. 5.646.
In mid.: ἡμίονον, ἥ τʼ ἀλγίστη δαμάσασθαι Il. 23.655. Cf. Od. 4.637.
Fig.: Διὸς μάστιγι δαμέντες Il. 12.37. Cf. Il. 13.812.
To bring into subjection: σοὶ δεδμήμεσθα Il. 5.878. Cf. Od. 11.622.
Of political subjection Il. 3.183, Il. 6.159: Od. 3.305.

To subject (to a man) in marriage: ἀνδρί με
δάμασσεν Il. 18.432.
To subject (a woman to the discretion of a victor): ἄλοχοι δʼ ἄλλοισι δαμεῖεν Il. 3.301.
Of feelings, sleep, etc., to overcome: ἔρος μʼ ἐδάμασσεν Il. 14.316. Cf. Il. 10.2 = Il. 24.678, Il. 14.353: δεδμημένος ὕπνῳ Od. 7.318. Cf. Od. 13.119, Od. 15.6.
Of natural agencies, to have an overpowering effect upon, wear out, exhaust: ἁλὶ δέδμητο Od. 5.454. Cf. Od. 8.231, Od. 14.318.
To curb or restrain (one's spirit): δάμασον θυμὸν μέγαν Il. 9.496. Cf. Il. 18.113 = Il. 19.66: Od. 11.562.
In pass., to be appeased or placated: δμηθήτω Il. 9.158.
To overpower, get the better of, master: ἐπεὶ ξάνθοιο δάμη μένος Il. 21.383. Cf. Il. 16.816: Od. 4.397.
In mid.: δαμασσάμενος οἴνῳ Od. 9.454. Cf. Od. 9.516.
To defeat, rout, put to flight: κλῖναν δαμάσαντες Ἀχαιούς Od. 9.59. Cf. Il. 6.74 = Il. 17.320, Il. 10.310 = 397, Il. 13.98, Il. 16.420, Il. 17.337, Il. 20.143: Od. 23.310.

To put an end to, destroy, kill, slay: εἰ πόλεμος δαμᾷ Ἀχαιούς Il. 1.61, μὴ ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ δουρὶ δαμήῃς (by him with his spear) Il. 3.436, σοὶ δαμῆναι (by thee) Il. 13.603. Cf. Il. 2.860, Il. 4.479, Il. 5.106, Il. 11.98, Il. 14.482, Il. 19.203, etc.: μοῖρʼ ἐπέδησε δαμῆναι Od. 3.269 (app. referring to Aegisthus as fate-bound to (ultimate) ruin; or perh. to Clytaemnestra as yielding to passion (sense (3))), μή με στίβη δαμάσῃ Od. 5.468. Cf. Od. 1.237, Od. 3.90, 410, Od. 4.495, Od. 11.171, Od. 18.54, etc.
Of a shield, in pass., to be unable to resist a blow, be pierced Il. 20.266.
To do violence to, disfigure (oneself): αὐτόν μιν πληγῇσι δαμάσσας Od. 4.244.
To subject to a foe, cause to be defeated Il. 9.118.
To cause to be slain by a foe: ἐμῇς ὑπὸ χερσὶ δάμασσον
To control, keep in order: Ἥρην ἐπέεσσιν Il. 5.893.
To overcome by troubling the senses.
In mid.: φιλότητα καὶ ἵμερον, ᾧ τε σὺ πάντας δαμνᾷ Il. 14.199.
To have an overpowering effect upon, wear out, exhaust: δεσμός ἑ ἐδάμνα Il. 5.391. Cf. Il. 14.439, Il. 21.52, 270.
To defeat, rout, put to flight: Ἀχαιοὺς Τρωσὶν δαμναμένους (by the Trojans) Il. 13.16 = 353. Cf. Il. 5.746 = Il. 8.390: = Od. 1.100.
To kill, slay: Τρώεσσιν δάμνασθαι (by the Trojans) Il. 8.244 = Il. 15.376. Cf. Il. 11.309.
To destroy, consume: σάρκας πυρὸς μένος δαμνᾷ Od. 11.221.
A torch: δ. μετὰ χερσὶν ἔχουσα Od. 23.294.
Collectively, torches: δ. μετὰ χερσὶν ἔχουσαι Il. 24.647: = Od. 4.300 = Od. 7.339 = Od. 22.497.
[δα- (app. referring to the work of levelling, stamping, etc.) + πέδον, the ground.]
A levelled and prepared surface: ἐν τυκτῷ δαπέδῳ Od. 4.627 = Od. 17.169.
Of the under surface of the realm of Hades Od. 11.577.
To devour. Of wild beasts Il. 11.481, Il. 16.159.
Of rending flesh Il. 5.831, Il. 13.831, Il. 21.398.
To devour. Of wild beasts Il. 11.479.
To sleep, go to sleep, take one's rest Od. 20.143.
Thickly shaded, with thick shades: ὕλη Il. 15.273: ὕλην Od. 5.470.
A division or apportionment: ἤν ποτε δασμὸς ἵκηται Il. 1.166.
[prob. fr. δασ- (= δεσ-, house, as in δέσποινα) + πλη-, πελάζω. Cf. τειχεσιπλήτης.]
Thus, that approaches houses (with hostile intent), smiter of houses: Ἐρινύς Od. 15.234.
With thick fleece: ἄρσενες ὄϊες Od. 9.425.
App., spread so as to lie thickly: ῥῶπας Od. 14.49.
3 pl. ἐδάσαντο Od. 14.208. δάσσαντο Il. 1.368: Od. 19.423.
Pl. pple. δασσάμενοι Od. 3.66, 316, Od. 15.13, Od. 16.385, Od. 20.280.
Infin. δάσασθαι Il. 18.511, Il. 22.120, Il. 23.21: Od. 18.87, Od. 22.476. δάσσασθαι Od. 20.216.
3 sing. pf. pass. δέδασται Il. 1.125, Il. 15.189: Od. 15.412. (ἀπο-.)

To divide among themselves, make mutual apportionment of: χηρωσταὶ διὰ κτῆσιν δατέοντο Il. 5.158. Cf. Il. 1.368, Il. 9.138 = 280: τάδε δʼ αὐτοὶ δάσονται Od. 2.368. Cf. Od. 2.335, Od. 3.316 = Od. 15.13, Od. 9.42, 549, Od. 14.208, Od. 16.385, Od. 17.80, Od. 20.216.
Fig.: μένος Ἄρηος δατέονται (app., share between them, are alike filled with) Il. 18.264.
To divide, apportion: διὰ παῦρα δασάσκετο Il. 9.333. Cf. Il. 1.125, Il. 15.189, Il. 18.511, Il. 22.120: Od. 3.66 = Od. 20.280, Od. 6.10, Od. 15.412, Od. 19.423.
To divide into portions: κρέα Od. 1.112.
To divide among themselves as prey, to tear (and devour). Of dogs, etc. Il. 22.354, Il. 23.21: Od. 18.87, Od. 22.476.
To cut in pieces Il. 20.394–To cut up (the ground) Il. 23.121.
Red or tawny: δράκων Il. 2.308, δέρμα λέοντος Il. 10.23, θῶες Il. 11.474.
2 sing. fut. in mid. form δαήσεαι Od. 3.187, Od. 19.325.

2 sing. pf. δεδάηκας Od. 8.146, 3
δεδάηκε Od. 8.134.
3 sing. redup. aor. δέδαε Od. 6.233, Od. 8.448, Od. 20.72, Od. 23.160.
From this tense is formed infin. mid. δεδάασθαι (for δεδαέσθαι) Od. 16.316.
To get to know, know, learn: ἀμφοτέρων φυήν Il. 3.208, πολέμοιο δαήμεναι (about war) Il. 21.487. Cf. Il. 6.150 = Il. 20.213: Od. 3.187, Od. 4.267, 493.
With dependent clause: ἢ . . . ἦε . . . Il. 2.299. Cf. Il. 16.423, Il. 21.61: πῶς ἐμεῦ δαήσεαι εἰ . . . ; (about me) Od. 19.325.
Absol.: ὄφρα δαείω Il. 10.425: Od. 9.280. Cf. Od. 13.335, Od. 23.262.
To acquire practical knowledge of or skill in.
In pf., to have such knowledge of or skill in: εἴ τινʼ ἄεθλον δεδάηκεν Od. 8.134. Cf. Od. 2.61, Od. 8.146, Od. 17.519.
In redup. aor., to teach (something): ἔργα δʼ Ἀθηναίη δέδαεν Od. 20.72.
With double acc. of person and thing: ὃν Ἥφαιστος δέδαεν τέχνην παντοίην Od. 6.233 = Od. 23.160. Cf. Od. 8.448.
In mid., to have oneself taught; hence, to get to know, acquire knowledge of: γυναῖκας δεδάασθαι, αἵ τε . . . καὶ αἳ . . . Od. 16.316.
Adversative particle, but, yet, on the other hand, while Il. 1.29, 83, 108, 137, 167, etc.: Od. 1.13, 19, 33, 75, 212, etc.

Particle of continuation, often introducing a subordinate statement or a parenthesis: πολλὰς δὲ ψυχὰς Ἄϊδι προΐαψεν Il. 1.3, νοῦσον ὦρσεν, ὀλέκοντο δὲ λαοί 10, μύδωνα βάλεν–ὁ δʼ ὑπέστρεφε ἵππους–χερμαδίῳ Il. 5.581. Cf. Il. 1.19, 25, 33, 34, 35, etc.: Od. 1.3, 51, 53, 71, 93, etc.

Giving a reason or explanation, for: πίθεσθʼ. ἄμφω δὲ νεωτέρω ἐστὸν ἐμεῖο Il. 1.259, ἐμέθεν ξύνες. Διὸς δέ τοι ἄγγελός εἰμι Il. 2.26, μή τι ῥέξῃ κακόν. θυμὸς δὲ μέγας ἐστὶ βασιλήων 196. Cf. Il. 1.271, Il. 3.410, Il. 4.438, 478, Il. 7.259, etc.: Od. 1.168, 433, Od. 2.36, 41, Od. 3.48, etc.

Introducing a principal clause after a relative, temporal or conditional protasis: οἱ δʼ ἐπεὶ οὖν ἤγερθεν . . . τοῖσι δὲ μετέφη Il. 1.58, εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι 137, ὅν τινα βασιλῆα κιχείη, τὸν ἀγανοῖς ἐπέεσσιν ἐρητύσασκεν Il. 2.189. Cf. Il. 2.322, Il. 4.262, Il. 5.261, 439, Il. 7.314, Il. 9.167, etc.: Od. 5.425, Od. 7.109, Od. 8.25, Od. 10.366, Od. 11.148, Od. 16.274, etc.
Introducing without antecedent clause Il. 2.802, Il. 3.229, etc.: Od. 4.400, Od. 5.428, Il. 3.229, etc.: Od. 4.400, Od. 5.428, etc.

Introducing a question: τίς δὲ σύ ἐσσι; Il. 6.123, τίς δʼ οἶδʼ εἰ . . . ; Il. 15.403. Cf. Il. 6.55, Il. 10.82, Il. 11.792, Il. 14.264, Il. 15.244, etc.: Od. 2.332, 363, Od. 4.312, 681, Od. 6.276, etc.
Before an imp. or a subj. as imp.: σὺ δὲ παῦε τεὸν μένος Il. 1.282. Cf. Il. 2.344, etc.: τῶν δὲ βοῶν ἀπεχώμεθα Od. 12.321. Cf. Od. 3.247, Od. 5.346, Od. 16.130, Od. 22.312, etc.

div.head: δεδμήμην, δέδμητο1,δεδμήατο
div.p: 1 and 3 sing. and 3 pl. plupf. pass. δαμάζω.
genit. sing. masc. pf. pple. δουπέω.
Thus, conspicuous, easy to be distinguished: σῆμα Il. 10.466.
With acc. and infin.: τί δεῖ πολεμιζέμεναι Τρώεσσιν Ἀργείους; Il. 9.337.
[app. redup. fr. δικ-, δείκνυμι. Cf. δεικανάομαι.]
To pledge in drinking = δείκνυμι 5: δέπαϊ Od. 18.121.
To frighten, alarm, scare Il. 4.184, Il. 12.52, Il. 13.810 (try to . . .), Il. 20.201 = 432.
To scare (away from something): Ἕκτορʼ ἀπὸ νεκροῦ Il. 18.164.
To use threats to, threaten Il. 2.190, Il. 15.196.
Also 1 sing. δείδια (δέδϝια) Il. 13.49, 481, Il. 21.536: Od. 4.820, Od. 6.168, Od. 17.188.
3 sing. plupf. (with impf. sense) δείδιε (with secondary person-ending) Il. 18.34, Il. 24.358.
3 sing. fut. in mid. form δείσεται Il. 20.130.

3 pl. ἔδεισαν Od. 10.219,
Od. 13.184. δεῖσαν Il. 7.93.

div.head: a
div.p: In reference to the fut. with υή and subj. (or after secondary tenses opt.) : υὴ ἐρυσαίατο νεκρόν Il. 5.298, μὴ τελέσῃ ἔπος Il. 18.44. Cf. Il. 10.39, Il. 11.470, Il. 13.745, Il. 18.34, Il. 19.24, Il. 20.30, 62, Od. 21.536, Il. 22.455: Od. 4.820, Od. 5.419, 473, Od. 8.230, Od. 12.122, Od. 21.286, Od. 24.353.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to the past with μή and indic.: μὴ πάντα νημερτέα εἷπεν Od. 5.300.
In virtual reference to the past with μή and subj.: μή σε παρείπῃ (that she may prove to have..., i.e. that she has . . .) Il. 1.555. Cf. Il. 10.538.

div.head: c
div.p: With infin., to be afraid to do something, shrink from doing it: ὑποδέχθαι Il. 7.93. Cf. Il. 15.299: Od. 6.168.

To be afraid of, fear, be in fear of, dread, to anticipate with fear, shrink from: αἴσχεα Il. 3.242, μήτε σύ γʼ Ἄρηα τό γε δείδιθι Il. 5.827 (τό γε, for that matter), Ζηνὸς μῆνιν Il. 13.624. Cf. Il. 5.790, Il. 6.99, Il. 12.39, Il. 13.49, Il. 18.261, Il. 22.19, etc. : οὔτινα Od. 2.199, ἐμὴν ἐνιπήν Od. 10.448. Cf. Od. 9.72, 257, Od. 10.130, Od. 12.244, Od. 17.577, Od. 18.63, 80, 396.
With complementary infin.: οὐ δείσαντες νέμεσιν ἔσεσθαι Od. 22.39. Cf. Il. 18.342 (τό γε as in Il. 5.827 above).
In double construction with acc. and μή with subj.: ταῦτα δείδοικα, μή οἱ ἀπειλὰς ἐκτελέσωσι θεοί, ἡμῖν δʼ αἴσιμον εἴη . . . Il. 9.244 (here also with opt. of remoter consequence). Cf. Od. 17.188.
To stand in awe of, reverence, hold in awe or due respect: σημάντορας Il. 4.431. Cf. Il. 24.116, 435: Od. 9.274, Od. 14.389, Od. 16.306, Od. 22.39.
Hence, app., to sup: ἔρχεο δειελιήσας Od. 17.599.
The setting sun, the evening: δ. ὀψὲ δύων Il. 21.232.
To pledge in drinking = δείκνυμι 5 Il. 15.86.
Mid. Pres. pple. δεικνύμενος Il. 9.196, Il. 23.701: Od. 4.59.
3 pl. pf. (with pres. sense) δειδέχαται Od. 7.72.
3 sing. plupf. (with impf. sense) δείδεκτο Il. 9.224.
To manifest, exhibit, display: σῆμα βροτοῖσιν Il. 13.244. Cf. Od. 3.174.
To show, bring forward or exhibit to be looked at: αἷμα καταρρέον Il. 5.870. Cf. Il. 6.170, Il. 7.184, Il. 19.332: Od. 14.323 = Od. 19.293, Od. 21.217, Od. 24.147.
To show, point out: Ἀλέξανδρον Il. 3.452. Cf. Il. 10.476: πόλιν Od. 6.144. Cf. Od. 6.178, 194, Od. 7.29, Od. 13.344.
With dependent clause: ὅθι δένδρεα πεφύκει Od. 5.241.
To point out in words, tell, explain Od. 10.303, Od. 12.25.
In mid., to pledge in drinking (app. from a custom of pointing to the person whose health was to be drunk): δείδεκτʼ Ἀχιλῆα Il. 9.224. Cf. Il. 4.4, Il. 9.671.
In mid., to welcome, greet: τὼ δεικνύενος Il. 9.196. Cf. Il. 22.435: Od. 4.59, Od. 7.72.
Of the sun, to decline towards evening: δείλετʼ ἠέλιος Od. 7.289.
Sorry, worthless: δειλαὶ δειλῶν ἐγγύαι (given by worthless fellows) Od. 8.351.

div.head: a
div.p: Luckless, wretched, poor (in a tone of compassion or self-pity): δειλοῖσί σφι γόου κατάπαυμα Il. 17.38. Cf. Il. 5.574, Il. 17.670, Il. 19.287, Il. 21.464, Il. 22.31, 76, Il. 23.65, 105, 221, 223, Il. 24.525: ἐμοὶ δειλῷ κακὰ μήδετο Od. 14.243. Cf. Od. 9.65, Od. 11.19, Od. 12.341, Od. 15.408, Od. 20.115.
Sim.: ὤ μοι ἐγὼ δειλή Il. 18.54. Cf. Il. 22.431: Od. 5.299.

div.head: b
div.p: Tinged with hostility or contempt: ἆ δειλέ Il. 11.441, 452, Il. 16.837: Od. 18.389, Od. 21.288.– ἆ δειλώ Od. 21.86.

Causing, or such as to cause, fear, fearful, terrible, aweinspiring, dread, dire Il. 1.200, Il. 2.321, Il. 5.739, Il. 8.135, Il. 11.418, etc.: Od. 3.145, Od. 5.52, Od. 11.157, Od. 12.94, Od. 22.405, etc.
With complementary infin.: δεινὸν γένος βασιλήϊόν ἐστι κτείνειν Od. 16.401.
Of noises, troubling the hearers, terrible, dreadful: καναχήν Il. 16.104. Cf. Il. 1.49, Il. 23.688.
Of something said, calculated to trouble the hearer, out of place, unseemly: ἔπος Od. 8.409, Od. 21.169.

In neut. δεινόν as adv., so as to cause fear, fearfully, terribly, dreadfully: δ. δερκόμενοι Il. 3.342. Cf. Il. 3.337, Il. 4.420, Il. 6.182, Il. 8.133, Il. 11.10, etc.: κῦμα δ. ἐπεσσύμενον Od. 5.314. Cf. Od. 5.403, Od. 11.608, Od. 12.85, 106, 236, Od. 22.124, etc.
Troubling with excessive wonder, marvellous, strange: θαῦμα Il. 13.100.

To be regarded or treated with awe, reverence or respect: ὅρκου Il. 2.755, θεός Il. 4.514. Cf. Il. 3.172, Il. 5.839, Il. 6.380 = 385, Il. 18.394, Il. 21.25: Od. 7.41, 246, 255, Od. 8.22, Od. 10.136 = Od. 11.8 = Od. 12.150, Od. 12.322, 449, Od. 14.234.
Of armour, with notion of great power of resistance, proof against blows, stout: σάκος Il. 7.245, 266. Cf. Il. 10.254, 272, Il. 20.259.
Feeling fear: ἀγορὴ δεινὴ τετρηχυῖα (in fear and disorder) Il. 7.346.
3 sing. plupf. δεδειπνήκετ Od. 17.359. to take δεῖπνον
Of the meal taken by Hermes on arriving at Calypso's island Od. 5.95.

Of
that taken by the disguised Odysseus on arriving at Eumaeus's hut Od. 14.111.
The time for δεῖπνον: ὅτε δ. ἔην Od. 17.170 (here in sense 1.f).
To entertain at δεῖπνον: κατέπεφνε δειπνίσσας Od. 4.535 = Od. 11.411 (app. in sense 1.f, but the time is not determined).

p.gloss: The principal meal of the day.

div.head: a
div.p: Taken before beginning the day's work, whether of fighting or of a peaceful occupation Il. 2.381 = Il. 19.275, Il. 2.399, Il. 8.53, Il. 19.171, 316, 346: Od. 9.311.

div.head: b
div.p: Taken by travellers before setting out Od. 15.77 = 94.

div.head: c
div.p: Taken in an interval of occupation Il. 11.86, Il. 18.560: Od. 6.97.

div.head: e
div.p: Taken on returning from a nocturnal expedition Il. 10.578.

div.head: f
div.p: The regular principal meal, taken in the late morning or about mid-day Od. 1.124, 134, Od. 17.176, Od. 19.321, 419, Od. 20.390, Od. 24.215, 360, 386, 394, 412.–

div.head: g
div.p: A meal taken on shore by a ship's company Od. 9.86 = Od. 10.57, Od. 10.155, Od. 15.500.–

div.head: h
div.p: A meal taken in the evening (Od. 3.497) by travellers arriving at a house and finding a marriage-feast in progress Od. 4.61 (the same meal called δόρπον 213; and cf. μεταδόρπιος 194).–

div.head: i
div.p: Of an ἔρανος on the day after a marriage-feast Od. 4.624.
The material for a meal: αἷγας Od. 17.214 = Od. 20.175.
acc. pl. masc. aor. pple. δέρω.
Of the necks of Scylla Od. 12.90.
Of an eagle's neck Il. 12.204: Od. 2.153.
The neck-opening of a θώρηξ Il. 11.26.
To cut the throat of, to slay thus; or simply, to slay Il. 21.89, 555, Il. 23.174: Od. 22.349.
With another numeral: ἑπτὰ καὶ δ. Od. 5.278, Od. 7.267, Od. 24.63.
Ten times the normal, tenfold: ἄποινα Il. 22.349.
A body or company of ten: εἴ κʼ ἐς δεκάδας διακοσμηθεῖμεν Il. 2.126. Cf. Il. 2.128: Od. 16.245.

The tenth: Ἠώς Il. 6.175, ὲς δεκάτους ἐνιαυτούς (app. for ἐς δέκα ἐνιαυτούς by confusion with ἐς δέκατον ἐνιαυτόν) Od. 8.404 = 418. Cf. Il. 2.329, Il. 9.474, Il. 12.15, Il. 24.785: Od. 5.107, Od. 7.253 = Od. 14.314, Od. 12.447, Od. 14.241, 325 = Od. 19.294, Od. 16.18, Od. 19.192.
δεκάτη (sc. ἡμέρη), the tenth day: δεκάτῃ (on the tenth day) Od. 9.83.

One's bodily frame or build: οὐ δέμας οὐδὲ φυήν (the two words difficult to distinguish) Il. 1.115, μικρὸς δέμας Il. 5.801 (here app. stature), δέμας ἐϊκυῖα θεῇσιν Il. 8.305. Cf. Il. 13.45, Il. 17.323, 555, Il. 21.285, Il. 22.227, Il. 24.376: δέμας ἀθανάτοισιν ὁμοῖος Od. 3.468. Cf. Od. 2.268 = 401 = Od. 22.206 = Od. 24.503 = 548, Od. 4.796, Od. 5.212, 213, Od. 7.210, Od. 8.14, 116, 194, Od. 11.469 = Od. 24.17, Od. 13.222, 288, Od. 14.177, Od. 16.157, 174, Od. 18.251, Od. 19.124, 381, Od. 20.31, 194, Od. 23.163.
Of animals: συῶν δέμας Od. 10.240. Cf. Od. 17.307, 313.
In advbl. acc. with genit., in the build of, after the similitude of, like (as our like has developed fr. orig. Teutonic *liko-, body, form): πυρός Il. 11.596 = Il. 13.673 = Il. 18.1, Il. 17.366.

A bedstead, a bed. (In Il. 24.644 two beds are referred to. See 648. So perh. also in Od. 4.297, 301; but from Od. 15.45 it would rather appear that Telemachus and Peisistratus were then sleeping together): δέμνιʼ ὑπʼ αἰθούσῃ θέμεναι Il. 24.644: = Od. 4.297 = Od. 7.336, δέμνια κούρης Od. 6.20. Cf. Od. 4.301, Od. 8.277, 282, 296, 314, Od. 11.189, Od. 19.318, 599, Od. 20.139.
3 sing. plupf. pass. (ἐ)δέδμητο Il. 13.683: Od. 1.426, Od. 9.185, Od. 14.6.

to construct, build, form: πύργους Il. 7.337. Cf. Il. 6.245, 249, Il. 7.436, Il. 9.349, Il. 13.683, Il. 14.32, Il. 21.446; ὅθι οἱ θάλαμος δέδμητο (was in the state of having been built, i.e., simply, stood) Od. 1.426, θάλαμον Od. 23.192. Cf. Od. 9.185, Od. 14.6.
App., to turn the eyes, give meaning looks: ἐς ἕκαστον Il. 9.180.
For dat. δενδρέῳ v.l. δένδρει fr. δένδρος Il. 3.152.
Abounding in trees: νῆσος Od. 1.51, ἄλσεϊ Od. 9.200.
ἐπὶ δεξιά, to the right : νωμῆσαι βῶν Il. 7.238, εἴτʼ ἐπὶ δ. ἴωσιν (from left to right of a spectator, i.e. in the lucky direction) Il. 12.239.–ἐπὶ δεξιόφιν on the right of.
Of a bird of omen, passing as in Il. 12.239 above, boding well: δεξιὸν ἧκεν ἐρωδιόν Il. 10.274. Cf. Il. 13.821, Il. 24.294 = 312, 320: Od. 2.154, Od. 15.160 = 525, 531, Od. 15.164, Od. 24.312.
In fem. δεξιή (sc. χείρ), the right hand: δεξιῇ ἠσπάζοντο Il. 10.542.
A grasp or clasp of the right hand as the sign of a pledge Il. 2.341 = Il. 4.159.
[in form comp. of δεξιός. with changed accent.]
Fem. instrumental δεξιτερῆφι Od. 19.480. This form as locative Il. 24.284: Od. 15.148.
The right-hand part of, the part of on the right: γναθμὸν δεξιτερόν Il. 16.405.
In fem. δεξιτερή (sc. χείρ), the right hand: δεξιτερῇ ἑλοῦσα Il. 1.501. Cf. Il. 21.490, Il. 22.320.
Reason or cause for fear or apprehension: οὔ τοι ἔπι δ. Il. 1.515.
With complementary infin.: σοὶ οὐ δ. ἔστʼ ἀπολέσθαι Il. 12.246. Cf. Od. 5.347, Od. 8.563.
Pl. δέπα (for δέπαα) Od. 15.466, Od. 19.62, Od. 20.153.
Dat. δεπάεσσι Il. 1.471, Il. 3.295, Il. 8.162, etc.: Od. 3.340, Od. 7.137, Od. 18.418, etc. δέπασσι Il. 15.86.

A drinking-cup: ἐπαρξάμενοι δεπάεσσιν (locative dat., into the . . .) Il. 1.471 = Il. 9.176, ἀμφικύπελλον Il. 1.584. Cf. Il. 3.295, Il. 4.3, 262, Il. 7.480, Il. 9.203, etc.: Od. 3.41, Od. 7.137, Od. 9.10, Od. 18.152, Od. 19.62, etc.
3 sing. pf. (in press. sense) δέδορκε Il. 22.95.
To see, behold, look upon: Τρῶας Il. 13.86. Cf. Il. 14.141.
To have the power of sight as being alive: ἐμεῦ (ἐμέθεν) ἐπὶ χθονὶ δερκομένοιο Il. 1.88: Od. 16.439.
To descry, make out: καπνόν Od. 10.197.
To direct the sight, look: ἐπὶ πόντον Od. 5.84 = Od. 5.158.
To look, glance: δεινόν Il. 3.342, Il. 11.37, Il. 23.815. Cf. Il. 22.95, Il. 23.477.
Fig., with cognate acc.: πῦρ ὀφθαλμοῖσι δεδορκώς Od. 19.446.
A hide or skin stripped from a beast: συός Il. 9.548. Cf. Od. 4.436, 440, Od. 22.362.
The prepared skin of a beast: λέοντος Il. 10.23, 177. Cf. Od. 13.436, Od. 14.50, 519.
A piece of leather: βόειον Od. 14.24.
The human skin: ἔσχεθε δʼ οἷον δέρμα (the strip of skin not severed) Il. 16.341. Cf. Od. 13.431.
The membrane enclosing the intestines: γῦπε δ. ἔσω δύνοντες Od. 11.579.
3 pl. aor. ἔδειραν Il. 1.459, Il. 2.422: Od. 12.359.
Acc. pl. masc. pple. δείραντας Od. 10.533, Od. 11.46. (ἐκ-,)

Any means of securing a person, a bond, bonds: δῆσαν κρατερῷ ἐνὶ δεσμῷ Il. 5.386. Cf. Il. 5.391, Il. 10.443, Il. 15.19: δεσμὸν ἀνέγναμψαν Od. 14.348. Cf. Od. 8.317, 353, 359, 360, Od. 12.160, Od. 15.232, 444, Od. 22.189, 200.

In pl. (app., except where the idea of number is involved, used indifferently with the sing.): ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν Il. 1.401: ἐνὶ πλεόνεσσι δεσμοῖσι διδέντων Od. 12.54. Cf. Od. 1.204, Od. 8.274, 278, 296, 336, 340, Od. 11.293, Od. 12.164, 196, 200.
A halter for a horse Il. 6.507 = Il. 15.264.
A knot (in a cord put round a chest to secure the lid) Od. 8.443, 447.
A means of securing a gate: ἐπὶ δεσμὸν ἰῆλαι [θύραις] Od. 21.241 (app. not referring to a regular fastening. The gate is in fact secured with a ὅπλον νεός. See 390).
In pl., articles of head-dress in gen.: δέσματα σιγαλόεντα Il. 22.468 (the particular articles being specified in the next line).
[δεσ-, house + a second element conn. with πόσις1 Cf. δεσπότης, master, πότνια; also δασπλῆτις.]
The lady of a house, a mistress Od. 7.53, Od. 14.9 = 451, Od. 14.127, Od. 15.374, 377, Od. 19.83, Od. 23.2.
In form δεύρω Il. 3.240 (v.l. δεῦρο). Hither.
In pregnant sense: δ. παρέστης Il. 3.405.
Elliptically (withἄγε): ἄγε δ., ὄφρα. . . Il. 17.685. Cf. Od. 9.517, Od. 11.561.
With other vbs.: κάλεσσον Il. 4.193, ὁρόωντες Il. 17.637. Cf. Il. 24.106: Od. 17.529.
With imp. (with or without ἄγε), come ! ἄγε δ. παρʼ ἔμʼ ἵστασο Il. 11.314, Il. 17.179. Cf. Il. 23.581: δ. ὄρσο Od. 22.395. Cf. Od. 8.145, 205, Od. 12.184, Od. 22.233.
With 1 pl. subj. (with or without ἄγε), come ! let us ...: δ. ἐς τοὺς φύλακας καταβήομεν Il. 10.97. Cf. Il. 17.120, Il. 22.254, Il. 23.485: Od. 8.292.
Last, the last: ἦλθεν Il. 19.51: Od. 1.286, τοῦτο δεύτατον εἶπεν ἔπος Od. 23.342.
= δεῦρο. Used in dual and pl. contexts.
= δεῦρο 1 elliptically: δ. καί μʼ ἀμύνετε Il. 13.481. Cf. Od. 8.307.
= δεῦρο 3: δ. δύω μοι ἕπεσθον Il. 22.450.
= δεῦρο 4 (with or without ἄγετε): δ. ἴομεν Il. 14.128. Cf. Il. 7.350: Od. 2.410, Od. 8.133.
Coming second in a contest: γνώσεσθʼ ἵππους οἳ δεύτεροι οἵ τε πάροιθεν Il. 23.498.
With ellipse of sb.: τῷ δευτέρῳ ἵππον ἔθηκεν Il. 23.265. Cf. Il. 23.750.
In neut. pl. δεύτερα, the prize for the secondIl. 23.538.
Coming second in gaining estimation, taking a second place: ἵνα μὴ δ. ἔλθοι Il. 10.368. Cf. Il. 22.207.
(except in Il. 17.45, Il. 21.596 strengthened by αὖτε)

div.head: a
div.p: Second in doing something, following another in doing it: ἠρᾶτο Il. 10.283. Cf. Il. 23.729, 841.

div.head: b
div.p: In fighting, coming in with one's throw or stroke after an opponent: προΐει ἔγχος Il. 7.248, Il. 20.273. Cf. Il. 5.855, Il. 7.268, Il. 17.45, Il. 21.169, 596.
With genit.: ἐμεῖο δεύτεροι (left behind or surviving me) Il. 23.248.

div.head: a
div.p: With αὖ: δ. αὖ θώρηκʼ ἔδυνεν Il. 3.332 = Il. 11.19 = Il. 16.133 = Il. 19.371. Cf. Il. 6.184.

div.head: b
div.p: A second time, again: ὁρμηθείς Il. 16.402.
Sim.: ᾔτεέ με δ. αὖτις (asked for a second supply) Od. 9.354.

div.head: c
div.p: With αὖτε: δ. αὖτʼ ἀλέασθαι ἀμείνονας ἠπεροπεύειν Il. 23.605.
Again, in the future: οὔ μʼ ἔτι δ. ὦδε ἵξετʼ ἄχος Il. 23.46. Cf. Od. 18.24.

div.head: d
div.p: So as to come in as in 3.b: ὁρμηθείς Il. 16.467. Cf. Il. 3.349.
Also in form δῆσε Il. 18.100. Except in these forms as deponent δεύομαι.
To lack, be without, want, not to have.
Absol.: ἧσθαι δευόμενον (with empty hands) Il. 1.134, μηδέ τι θυμῷ δευέσθω (fail) Il. 20.122, δευόμενος (in his need) Il. 22.492.
To be in the state of having (something) fail one, be deprived of, lose.
With genit.: Ἀργείων Il. 23.484. Cf. Od. 1.254, Od. 4.264.
To be unequal to, unfitted for.
With genit.: πολέμοιο Il. 13.310. Cf. Il. 17.142.
To suffer want or be stinted in the matter of.
With infin.: ἐδεύησεν οἰήϊον ἄκρον ἱκέσθαι Od. 9.483 = 540.
3 sing. aor. δέκτο Il. 2.420, Il. 15.88: Od. 9.353.
Plupf. ἐδέγμην Od. 9.513, Od. 12.230. (ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, παρα-, ποτι-, ὑπο-.)

To receive or take something offered, given, handed over, etc., to accept: ἄποινα Il. 1.20, παιδὸς κύπελλον (from him) Il. 1.596, σκῆπτρόν οἱ (from him) Il. 2.186, χαλκὸν δέδεξο (app., be minded to accept) Il. 22.340. Cf. Il. 1.446, Il. 5.227, Il. 6.483, Il. 9.633, Il. 17.391, etc.: κρήδεμνον Od. 5.462, δῶρα (for custody) Od. 8.419, χρυσὸν ἀνδρός (as the price of the betrayal of . . .) Od. 11.327, ἔγχος οἱ (relieved him of . . .) Od. 15.282 = Od. 16.40. Cf. Od. 1.121, Od. 8.483, Od. 9.353, Od. 17.356, Od. 19.355, etc.
Of a god, to accept (a sacrifice) Il. 2.420.
To receive (a child) for nurture Il. 14.203.
To receive and undertake the charge of (a person) Il. 23.89.
To receive hospitably, entertain Od. 14.128, Od. 17.110, Od. 19.316.
To accept, resign oneself to: κῆρα Il. 18.115, Il. 22.365.
To accept, put up with, make the best of: μῦθον Od. 20.271.

div.head: a
div.p: To expect, look for: χρυσὸν Ἀλεξάνδροιο (from...) Il. 11.124.
With acc. and infin.: φῶτα μέγαν ἐδέγμην ἐλεύσεσθαι Od. 9.513. Cf. Od. 12.230.

div.head: b
div.p: With dependent clause: ὁππότʼ ἀφορμηθεῖεν (watching for the time when...) Il. 2.794, εἰς ὅ κεν ἔλθῃς Il. 10.62. Cf. Il. 18.524: Od. 20.385.
With dependent clause: Αἰακίδην ὁπότε λήξειεν Il. 9.191.
Of things: ίππῆας ἄεθλα δεδεγμένα Il. 23.273.

div.head: c
div.p: To await the attack of, stand up to, be ready for: Ἀχιλλῆα Il. 20.377. Cf. Il. 5.228, 238, Il. 12.147, Il. 15.745.
App., to succeed, come next: δέχεταί μοι κακὸν ἐκ κακοῦ Il. 19.290.
To work or knead with the hands in order to soften: κηρόν Od. 12.48.
3 sing. pa. iterative mid. δησάσκετο Il. 24.15.
3 sing. plupf. pass. δέδεντο Il. 5.387, Il. 23.866: Od. 15.232, Od. 24.229.
3 pl. δέδεντο Il. 10.475: Od. 9.443, Od. 10.92. (ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συν-.)
To tie or secure in its place, fasten: δῆσε ζυγόν Il. 5.730. Cf. Il. 24.190, 267: Od. 2.425 = Od. 15.290.
To tie into a bundle, bind together.
To tie or attach by a cord, a strap, etc.: ἐκ δίφροιο ἔδησεν [Ἕκτορα] Il. 22.398, ποδός (by the foot) Il. 23.854. Cf. Il. 23.866: Od. 9.443.
To tie or secure (a rope): πρυμνήσια Il. 1.436. Cf. Il. 24.273: Od. 10.96, Od. 15.498.
To tie or secure (a person's feet, etc.): πόδας καὶ χεῖρας Od. 21.454. Cf. Od. 21.30: Od. 22.189.
To bind or secure (a person), put (him) in bonds: δῆσαν κρατερῷ ἐνὶ δεσμῷ Il. 5.386. Cf. Il. 1.406, Il. 2.231, Il. 5.387, Il. 10.443: Od. 8.352, Od. 9.99, Od. 12.50, 161, 178, 196, Od. 15.232.
Fig.: ἡμέτερον μένος Il. 14.73: κελεύθου με (hinders from . . . ) Od. 4.380 = 469. Cf. Od. 14.61.
To halter or secure (a horse or an ox) Od. 8.544, Il. 10.475, Il. 13.572.
Sim. in pass.: περὶ κνήμῃσι κνημῖδας δέδετο (had them bound about his legs) Od. 24.229.

div.head: α
div.p: By or before this (or that) time, by now, now, already, ere this: ἐννέα δὴ βεβάασιν ἐνιαυτοί Il. 2.134. Cf. Il. 1.394, 503, Il. 2.117, Il. 3.150, Il. 5.383, Il. 8.297, etc.: ὃς δὴ γήραϊ κυφὸς ἔην Od. 2.16. Cf. Od. 1.26, 161, Od. 3.245, Od. 4.373, Od. 7.152, Od. 13.10, etc.

div.head: β
div.p: Indicating the arrival of a point of time, arrival at a result: ἐξ οὗ δὴ διαστήτην (from the time when the quarrel came to the point of braaking out) Il. 1.6, εἰδὴ ὁμοῦ πόλεμός τε δαμᾷ καὶ λοιμὸς Ἀχαιούς (if it has come to this that . . . ) Il. 1.61, νημερτὲς μὲν δή μοι ὑπόσχεο (you must now decide) 514. Cf. Il. 1.161, 574, Il. 8.34, Il. 9.202, 309, 434, Il. 19.9, Il. 20.115, etc.: ἦ μάλα δή με θέσφαθʼ ἱκάνει Od. 13.172, ὅππως δὴ μνηστῆρσι χεῖρας ἐφήσει (at this crisis of his fate) Od. 20.29, αἲ γὰρ δὴ θεοὶ τισαίατο λώβην (to such a pitch of insolence have they come) 169. Cf. Od. 14.333, 379, Od. 19.510, Od. 22.395, Od. 23.43, etc.
With ἄγε, ἄγετε. See ἄγε.–With ἄγρει Od. 21.176.

div.head: b
div.p:
Now, at this (or that ) time: καὶ δὴ τάχʼ ἔμελλε . . . Il. 6.52. Cf. Il. 1.388, Il. 2.436, Il. 9.245, Il. 11.126, 441, Il. 17.261, etc.: ὃς δή σφι σχεδόν ἐστιν
Od. 2.284. Cf. Od. 4.551, 770, Od. 5.401, 409, Od. 10.549, Od. 16.280, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: Joined with, and emphasizing or defining, other temporal words: αἰεὶ δή Il. 12.323, δὴ αὖ Il. 1.540, δὴ αὖτε Il. 1.340, ἐπεὶ δή Il. 4.124, ἐπὴν δή Il. 16.453, καί νυ δή Il. 7.273, νῦν δή Od. 2.284, ὁππότε δή Il. 16.53, ὅτε δή Il. 1.432, ὀψὲ δή Il. 7.94, τάχα δή Il. 13.120, τῆμος δή Od. 12.441, τότε δή Il. 1.92, etc.

As affirmative or emphasizing particle: μὴ δὴ οὕτως κλέπτε νόῳ Il. 1.131. Cf. Il. 1.286, 295, Il. 2.158, 301, Il. 6.476, Il. 8.491, Il. 11.314, Il. 13.260, Il. 18.364, etc.: εἰ δὴ ἐξ αὐτοῖο τόσος πάϊς εἰς Ὀδυσῆος Od. 1.207. Cf. Od. 1.253, 384, Od. 3.352, 357, Od. 4.819, Od. 5.23, Od. 11.348, Od. 14.282, etc.
Giving a touch of scorn, forsooth, to be sure: ὡς δὴ τοῦδʼ ἕνεκά σφιν ἑκηβόλος ἄλγεα τεύχει Il. 1.110. Cf. Il. 3.403, Il. 8.177, Il. 14.88, etc.: Od. 21.170.
Emphasizing superlatives: κάρτιστοι δὴ κεῖνοι τράφεν Il. 1.266. Cf. Il. 6.98, Il. 7.155, Il. 10.436, Il. 22.76, etc.: οἴκτιστον δὴ κεῖνο ἴδον Od. 12.258. Cf. Od. 8.519, Od. 11.309, etc.
[Subjunctives with strong stem answering to δᾶ- in ἐδάην, etc. See δάω. The -εις of 2 sing. app. a trace of an older inflexion, -ω, -εις, -ει, answering to -ομεν, -ετε.]
To find, to light or come upon: δούρατα δήεις (will find) Il. 13.260. Cf. Od. 6.291, Od. 7.49, Od. 13.407.
Of immaterial things: ἐν πήματα οἴκῳ Od. 11.115.
To find, get: ἄλλοθι ἕδρην Od. 16.44.
To find out by experience: τέκμωρ Ἰλίου Il. 9.418 = 685.
To attain to, bring about: ἄνυσιν Od. 4.544.

For a long time, for long, long: μηκέτι δ. λεγώμεθα Il. 2.435, ποταμῷ δ ἱερεύετε ταύρους . . . καθίετε ἵππους (the vbs. to be taken as presents, have long been sacrificing . . . ) Il. 21.131. Cf. Il. 5.104, 587, Il. 10.52, Il. 14.110, Il. 15.512: δ. πήματα πάσχει (has been suffering) Od. 1.49, δ. θύρῃσιν ἐφεστάμεν 120. Cf. Od. 2.255, 404, Od. 3.313, 336, Od. 4.373, 466, Od. 7.152, Od. 8.411, Od. 12.351, Od. 16.313, Od. 22.177.
To tarry, delay, loiter Il. 1.27, Il. 6.503, 519: Od. 12.121, Od. 17.278.
[conn. with δαίω1. Perh. orig. δά̆ϝιος. Cf. θεσπιδαής.]
Epithet of fire, blazing, consuming Il. 2.415, Il. 6.331, Il. 8.181, Il. 9.347, 674, Il. 11.667, Il. 16.127, 301, Il. 18.13.
(The first syllable scanned ⏑ when followed by ⏑–.)
Epithet of πόλεμος, destructive, deadlyIl. 4.281, Il. 5.117, Il. 7.119 = 174, Il. 17.189, Il. 19.73, Il. 21.422.
In concrete sense, the fighters, the fighting throng: θέων ἀνὰ δηϊοτῆτα Il. 15.584, Il. 17.257.
Contr. forms. Pres. pple. δῃῶν Il. 17.65.
Aor. pple. pass. δῃωθείς, -έντος Il. 4.417: Od. 9.66.
To inflict slaughter upon (a hostile force): Τρῶας Il. 4.416. Cf. Il. 4.417, Il. 9.243, Il. 13.675.
To rend or tear: βοείας Il. 5.452 = Il. 12.425. Cf. Il. 14.518.
Of beasts tearing their prey Il. 16.158, Il. 17.65.
To do harm or mischief to, hurt, injure: μή πως ἀμφοτέρους δηλήσεαι Il. 23.428.
Absol. Il. 4.236, 271. –Of a weapon: ῥινὸν δηλήσατο χαλκός Od. 22.278.
Also, absol., to do harm, lead to mischief: σή κε βουλἡ δηλήσεται Il. 14.102.
Something that brings harm, a bane: δηλήματα νηῶν Od. 12.286.
One who works for the common weal, not for himself or for a private employer Od. 17.383, Od. 19.135.
Belonging to the community, public: οἶκος Od. 20.264.
Relating to the public interests, public: πρῆξις Od. 3.82.
Absol.: ἦέ τι δήμιον πιφαύσκεται; Od. 2.32. Cf. Od. 2.44, Od. 4.314.
In neut. pl. δήμια as adv., at the public cost (cf. δημόθεν): πίνουσιν Il. 17.250.
That devours the common stock: βασιλεύς Il. 1.231.
From the common stock: δ. ἄλφιτα δῶκα Od. 19.197.
The common stock or store: ἐς δῆμον ἔδωκεν Il. 11.704.

A community or people: παντὶ δήμῳ Il. 3.50, Il. 24.706, θεὸς ὣς τίετο δήμῳ (in the . . . , among the . . . ) Il. 5.78, Il. 10.33, Il. 11.58, Il. 13.218, Il. 16.605. Cf. Il. 9.460, Il. 11.328, Il. 12.447, Il. 17.577, Il. 18.295, 500, Il. 20.166: κατὰ δῆμον Od. 2.101, δήμου ἡγήτορες Od. 13.186. Cf. Od. 2.239, 291, Od. 4.691, Od. 7.11, 150, Od. 14.205, 239, Od. 16.114, 425, etc.
A body or force of men: ἑτεραλκέα δῆμον Il. 15.738. Cf. Il. 17.330.
App., a multitude: ἐπὶ δʼ ἔστενε δ. ἀπείρων Il. 24.776.
The common people: δήμου ἄνδρα Il. 2.198.
App., one of the common people: δῆμον ἐόντα Il. 12.213.

For a long time, for long, long: ἀκέων δ. ἧστο Il. 1.512. Cf. Il. 1.416, Il. 5.412, Il. 6.131, 139, Il. 8.126, Il. 9.30 = 695, Il. 13.573, Il. 16.736, Il. 17.695, Il. 20.426, Il. 23.690: δ. ἀπεών (having been long . . .) Od. 13.189, ὀϊζὺν δ. ἔχομεν (have long been suffering . . .) Od. 14.416. Cf. Od. 1.281, Od. 2.36, Od. 4.494, Od. 5.127, Od. 6.33, Od. 20.155, Od. 22.473, etc.
What one has in one's mind, thougts, counsels: ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν Il. 4.361 (see ἤπιος 1): θεῶν Od. 23.82.
To strive, contend, struggle, in passages cited.

In neut. sing. δηρόν as adv., for a long time, for long, long: μένειν Il. 2.298. Cf. Il. 5.120, Il. 10.371, Il. 13.151, Il. 16.852, Il. 19.64, etc.: ἐσκοπίαζον Od. 10.260. Cf. Od. 1.203, Od. 2.285, Od. 5.396, Od. 16.171, Od. 21.112, etc.
Through: διὰ δʼ ἔπτατʼ ὀϊστός Il. 5.99: διὰ τάφρον ὀρύξας (i.e. stretching in a line) Od. 21.120.
Sim. κλέος διὰ ξεῖνοι φορέουσιν (through the lands they traverse) Od. 19.333.
Severing, sundering, splitting, dividing: διὰ κτῆσιν δατέοντο Il. 5.158. Cf. Il. 2.655, Il. 9.333, Il. 17.522, Il. 20.280, etc.: διὰ ξύλα κεάσσαι Od. 15.322. Cf. Od. 9.157, 291, etc.
Intensive: διὰ χρόα ἔδαψεν Il. 5.858. Cf. Il. 12.308, Il. 13.507, Il. 19.90, etc.: ἐπὴν σχεδίην διὰ κῦμα τινάξῃ Od. 5.363.

div.head: II
div.p: Prep. (sometimes, without anastrophe, following the case).

div.head: a
div.p: Through, passing through, piercing: πέλεκυς, ὅς εἶσιν διὰ δουρός Il. 3.61. Cf. Il. 3.357, Il. 4.135, 481, Il. 5.113, etc.: κόρυθος διά Od. 24.523. Cf. Od. 22.16.
With a form in -φι: διὰ στήθεσφιν Il. 22.284, Il. 5.41 = 57 = Il. 8.259 = Il. 11.448: = Od. 22.93.
In reference to pain: ὀδύνη διὰ χροὸς ἦλθεν Il. 11.398.

div.head: b
div.p: Through, traversing or passing through (a space, a passage, a throng, or the like): αἰθέρος Il. 2.458, σκαιῶν Il. 3.263, προμάχων Il. 4.495. Cf. Il. 5.250, 503, Il. 6.226, Il. 7.340, Il. 9.478, etc.: Ὠκεανοῖο Od. 10.508, νηός Od. 12.206. Cf. Od. 10.118, 391, Od. 11.581, Od. 12.335, etc.
With a form in -φι: διʼ ὄρεσφιν Il. 10.185.
Of extension: σύες (ὕες) τανύοντο διὰ φλογός Il. 9.468 = Il. 23.33. Cf. Od. 9.298.
Among: ἔπρεπε καὶ διὰ πάντων Il. 12.104.

div.head: a
div.p: Through, passing through, piercing: ἔντεα Il. 23.806. Cf. Il. 7.247, Il. 20.269.

div.head: b
div.p: Through, traversing or passing through (a space, a passage, a throng, or the like) or among (objects): δώματα Il. 1.600, ἔντεα Il. 10.298, στόμα 375. Cf. Il. 8.343, Il. 11.118, Il. 12.62, Il. 17.283, Il. 23.122, etc.: σφέας Od. 7.40, ἄκριας Od. 10.281. Cf. Od. 2.154, Od. 6.50, Od. 9.447, Od. 10.150, etc.
In reference to night regarded as a space: νύκτα διʼ ὀρφναίην Il. 10.83. Cf. Il. 2.57, Il. 8.510, Il. 24.363, 653, etc.: Od. 9.143, 404, Od. 12.284, etc.
During (the night): διὰ νύκτα μάχεσθαι Il. 10.101. Cf. Od. 15.8, Od. 19.66.
Of extension: διὰ κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας Il. 2.40.

div.head: c
div.p: Through, by means of, by virtue of, by the help or working of: μαντοσύνην Il. 1.72, ἰότητα Il. 15.41. Cf. Il. 10.497, Il. 15.71: βουλάς Od. 8.82, Ἀθήνην 520. Cf. Od. 11.276, 437, Od. 13.121, Od. 19.154, 523.

div.head: d
div.p: On account of, because of: κάλλος Od. 11.282, ἀτασθαλίας Od. 23.67.
Absol., to cross over: ἐς Ἤλιδα Od. 4.635.–εὖ διαβάς, with the legs set well apartIl. 12.458.
To distinguish, discern: ἄνδρα ἕκαστον Il. 7.424. Cf. Il. 23.240.
[δια- 10 + γλάφω = γλύφω, to cut out, carve. Cf. γλυφίς, γλαφυρός.]
To hollow out, form: εὐνὰς ἐν ψαμάθοισιν Od. 4.438.
To convey across a strait: πορθμῆες Od. 20.187.
To catch sight of, see Il. 14.344.
To do sore hurt to Od. 14.37.
3 sing. fut. in mid. form διαείσεται Il. 8.535.
In pass.: ἀρετὴ διαείδεται ἀνδρῶν Il. 13.277.
To learn the value of, know.
With acc. and dependent clause: ἣν ἀρετήν, εἰ . . . (whether . . .) Il. 8.535.
To go through in talk: μῦθοι ἔσονται διαειπέμεν ἀλλήλοισιν Od. 4.215.
With acc.: θάμνους Od. 5.478, λόχμην Od. 19.440.
To fumigate thoroughly with sulphur: μέγαρον Od. 22.494.
Nom. sing. neut. aor. pple. pass. διατρυφέν.
To break in pieces, shiver: ξίφος διατρυφὲν ἔκπεσε χειρός Il. 3.363.
To wet, moisten Il. 13.30, Il. 21.202, Il. 22.495.
To thwart, frustrate: ἐμὸν ἔπος Il. 8.8.
To break in two: τόξα Il. 5.216.
To separate out and form into suitable bodies, marshal Il. 2.476.
To divide up and form (into bodies): ἐς δεκάδας Il. 2.126.
In mid.: ἐπεὶ μέγαρον διεκοσμήσαντο Od. 22.457.
Clearly, without doubt: δ. εἶναι ἄριστοι (ἄριστος) Il. 12.103, Il. 15.108.
Pass. Fut. infin. διακρινέεσθαι Od. 18.149, Od. 20.180.
Nom. pl. fem. pf. pple. διακεκριμέναι Od. 9.220.
To separate out and form into suitable bodies, marshal Il. 2.815.
To separate out, sort out: αἰπόλια αἰγῶν Il. 2.475. Cf. Od. 9.220.
To distinguish, make out: τὸ σῆμα Od. 8.195.
[perh. fr. διακ-, lengthened fr. δι-α-, δι-, to run, as in δίεμαι.]
To go through, debate: ταῦτα Il. 11.407 = Il. 17.97 = Il. 21.562 = Il. 22.122 = 385.
To cut through: διάμησε χιτῶνα Il. 3.359 = Il. 7.253.
To divide, apportion: ἕπταχα πάντα Od. 14.434.
Right through: βέλος ἐξέρυσε Il. 5.112 (i.e. in the direction of the arrow so as not to pull against the barbs), αἰχμὴ ἦλθεν 658. Cf. Il. 5.284, Il. 13.547.
With genit.: ἀσπίδος Il. 12.429. Cf. Il. 20.362.
Right through so as to make itself felt: οὐκ ὄμβρος περάασκεν Od. 5.480, Od. 19.442.

Continuously, without break or interval: πέτρη τετύχηκεν Od. 10.88. Cf. Il. 16.640: Od. 5.256–Continuously, all the way: θρόνοι ἐρηρέδατο Od. 7.96–Right round: σταυροὺς ἔλασσεν Od. 14.11. Cf. Il. 18.563.
Right on: ἡγεμόνευε Od. 17.194. Cf. Il. 10.325.
All together, in a mass Il. 12.398.
Right through a company, in turn Il. 7.171.
So as to meet, thoroughly: πόδας χεῖράς τε ἀποστρέψαντε Od. 22.190.

Of time, continuously, without intermission, break or interval Il. 10.89, 331, Il. 15.70, Il. 16.499, Il. 19.272, Il. 22.264: Od. 4.209, Od. 8.245, Od. 11.558, Od. 13.59, Od. 15.196, Od. 20.47, Od. 23.151.
In intensive sense: ἔγχος κέ σε κατέπαυσε δ. (for good) Il. 16.618.
With divided mind: μερμήριξεν (was in two minds) Il. 1.189, Il. 13.455, (had half a mind) Il. 8.167.
To traverse a space by flight Il. 15.83, 172.
To fly away through some opening Od. 1.320.
To traverse a space, pass, advance, make one's way: πεδίοιο (local genit., along the . . .) Il. 2.785 = Il. 3.14, Il. 23.364.
To accomplish (a journey) Il. 1.483: = Od. 2.429, Od. 2.213.
With pple.: λέγων ἐμὰ κήδεα Od. 14.197.
With genit.: μίτρης Il. 4.138. Cf. Il. 5.281, Il. 14.494.
Through the whole extent: τάνυται Il. 17.393.
Of shouting, piercingly Il. 8.227 = Il. 11.275 = 586 = Il. 17.247, Il. 12.439 = Il. 13.149.
Without a break: πεδίοιο τετυχηκώς (on the . . .) Il. 17.748.
To dash in pieces, destroy, make an end of, bring to nought Il. 2.473, Il. 9.78, Il. 11.713, 733, Il. 17.727, Il. 24.355: Od. 1.251 = Od. 16.128, Od. 2.49, Od. 12.290.
To shoot (an arrow) through something Od. 19.575.
To speed or pass quickly through or across.
With genit.: τάφροιο Il. 10.194: μεγάροιο Il. 22.460: Od. 4.37.
To break up into its component parts and disperse these: σχεδίην Od. 7.275.
To scatter to the winds, make an end of: ἀγλαΐας Od. 17.244.
To sever, rend: νεῦρα διεσχίσθη Il. 16.316.
To tear in pieces: ἱστία Od. 9.71.
Aor. pple. διατμήξας Il. 21.3: Od. 3.291, Od. 5.409, Od. 12.174.
3 pl. aor. pass. διέτμαγεν Il. 1.531, Il. 7.302, Il. 12.461, Il. 16.354: Od. 13.439.
To divide into two, sever Il. 21.3 (i.e. severing the fugitives into two bodies).
So of ships sailing together and severed into two bodies by a storm Od. 3.291.

To cleave (the sea),
traverse (it) Od. 5.409, Od. 7.276.
In pass., of two persons, to leave one another, part: ἐν φιλότητι διέτμαγεν Il. 7.302. Cf. Il. 1.531: = Od. 13.439.
In pass., of the boards of a gate coming apart Il. 12.461.
With acc.: κέλευθα Od. 3.177. Cf. Od. 5.100.
To flee in all directions: θῶες Il. 11.481, ἄλλυδις ἄλλος 486.
To rub down into small fragments, crumble Il. 11.847.
To throw obstacles in the way of, put off, delay Od. 2.265, Od. 20.341.
To thwart, oppose: τὸν ἐμὸν χόλον Il. 4.42.
With double acc. of the person and of what is delayed: Ἀχαιοὺς ὃν γάμον Od. 2.204.
To put off time, loiter, delay Il. 19.150.
With genit., to hold back from, delay in undertaking: ὁδοῖο Od. 2.404.
Bearing fruit through the seasons, never failing Od. 24.342.
nom. sing. neut. aor. pple. pass. διαθρύπτω.

p.gloss: To appear or be seen through.

div.p: With genit.: ὅθι νεκύων διεφαίνετο χῶρος Il. 8.491 = Il. 10.199.
In pf., to have lost one's wits, be beside oneself Il. 15.128.
To go through, say, tell Il. 20.340: Od. 17.590.
To draw off (wine) in large quantities or constantly Od. 16.110.
To lay open or rend (flesh) (as if to draw off the life) Od. 19.450.
To dismember or divide into joints (a sacrificial victim) Il. 7.316: = Od. 19.421, Od. 3.456, Od. 14.427.
To teach, instruct (a person) Il. 11.832, Il. 23.308: Od. 8.488.
To teach, impart knowledge of (something) Il. 9.442, Il. 23.307: Od. 22.422 (ἐργάζεσθαι complementary).
With double acc. of person and thing: σφέας οἴμας Od. 8.481.
With infin. of what is taught: βάλλειν ἄγρια πάντα Il. 5.51.
With acc. of person and this infin.: ὑψαγόρην σʼ ἔμεναι Od. 1.384.
In pass., to gain knowledge of, learn: φάρμακα δεδιδάχθαι (i.e. their properties) Il. 11.831.
With genit.: διδασκόμενος πολέμοιο (concerning war, i.e. the art of war) Il. 16.811.
Only in dual and pl. Twin: διδυμάονε παῖδε Il. 5.548, Il. 6.26.– (The) twins: Ὕπνῳ καὶ Θανάτῳ διδυμάοσιν Il. 16.672 = 682.
1 sing. pres. δίδωμι Il. 23.620: Od. 15.125, Od. 20.342.
Pple. διδούς, -όντος Il. 9.699: Od. 1.390, Od. 11.117, Od. 13.378.
Pa. iterative δόσκον Il. 9.331: Od. 17.420, Od. 19.76.
1 pl. aor. ἔδομεν Od. 24.65. δόμεν Il. 17.443.
Nom. pl. masc. δόντες Il. 1.299: Od. 5.38, Od. 23.341.
3 sing. aor. opt. pass. δοθείη Od. 2.78.

To make another the owner of, give, present: τόξον ἔδωκεν Il. 2.827, δῶρα δίδωσι (offers) Il. 9.261. Cf. Il. 2.102, Il. 5.272, Il. 6.219, Il. 7.299, etc.: τάλαρον ἔδωκεν Od. 4.125, ἕδνα διδόντες (offering) Od. 11.117. Cf. Od. 1.313, 316, Od. 2.336, etc.
In reference to something immaterial: τιμῆς ἥμισυ Il. 6.193.
To assign (a share of spoil) Il. 1.162, Il. 2.228, Il. 9.334, etc.
To make over one's rights in: ἑπτὰ πτολίεθρα Il. 9.149, 291.
To give as a reward or prize: δύω χρυσοῖο τάλαντα Il. 18.508. Cf. Il. 10.305, Il. 23.537, 551, 560, 616, 620, 807, etc.
To offer (a sacrifice): θεοῖς ἑκατόμβας Il. 7.450 = Il. 12.6. Cf. Od. 1.67, Od. 16.184, Od. 19.367.

Sim. δῶρα
θεοῖσιν Il. 20.299. Cf. Il. 24.425: Od. 13.358.
To give (food or drink), put (food or drink) before a person: δέπας οἴνου Il. 18.546: ξεινήϊα Od. 3.490. Cf. Od. 6.209, Od. 7.166, Od. 9.93, etc.
To see to the due providing of (a meal): δεῖπνον ἑταίροισιν Od. 10.155.
Of an eagle feeding its young Il. 12.222.
To make over (as compensation): ἵππους υἶος ποινήν Il. 5.266.
To give or confer (something immaterial): μέγʼ εὖχος Il. 5.285: γέρας Od. 7.150. Cf. Il. 5.654 = Il. 11.445, Il. 16.625, Il. 21.473.
Sim.: δαίμονά τοι δώσω (will deal thee . . .) Il. 8.166: γαστὴρ πολλὰ κακὰ δίδωσιν Od. 17.287, 474.
To give or utter (an oath) Od. 19.302.
To resign one's claims to: ἵππον Il. 23.553, 592, 610.
To give the services of: ἐπικούρους Il. 4.379, 380: Od. 2.212 = Od. 4.669.
To give as a servant or slave Od. 17.223, 442.

To give, commit, hand over, for some purpose: σάκος χείρονι φωτί Il. 14.377. Cf. Il. 1.324, Il. 2.205, Il. 9.331, Il. 15.455, Il. 17.127, Il. 21.84, etc.: ἄλεισον Od. 3.50. Cf. Od. 3.40, 437, Od. 5.351, Od. 10.33, Od. 14.112, Od. 21.233, etc.
Sim.: ὀδύνῃσί μιν (μʼ) ἔδωκεν Il. 5.397: Od. 17.567, ἀχέεσσί με δώσεις Od. 19.167.
With infin. expressing the purpose: δός σφωϊν [κούρην] ἄγειν Il. 1.338. Cf. Il. 5.26, Il. 6.53, Il. 7.471, Il. 11.704, Il. 16.40, etc.: δὸς τούτῳ δέπας σπεῖσαι Od. 3.46. Cf. Od. 18.87, Od. 20.78.

div.head: a
div.p: To give, grant, bestow, as a boon or in answer to prayer: ναύτῃσιν οὖρον Il. 7.4. Cf. Il. 1.178, Il. 3.66, Il. 4.320, Il. 9.38, etc.: ἐπιφροσύνην Od. 5.437. Cf. Od. 2.116, Od. 3.58, Od. 4.237, Od. 7.148, Od. 8.44, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: To send or afflict with (something evil): ἄλγεα Il. 1.96. Cf. Il. 2.375, Il. 9.571, Il. 19.264, 270, Il. 24.241, etc.: ἄτην Od. 4.262. Cf. Od. 2.135, Od. 4.237, Od. 7.242, Od. 14.39, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: With infin., to empower or permit to do something, grant a person's doing it or its being done: ἐκπέρσαι πόλιν Il. 1.18, τὸν δῦναι δόμον Ἄϊδος Il. 3.322. Cf. Il. 1.129, Il. 5.118, Il. 6.307, Il. 7.203, Il. 17.646, etc.: παλίντιτα ἔργα γενέσθαι Od. 1.379, ἄλοχον ἰδέειν Od. 8.411. Cf. Od. 3.60, Od. 6.327, Od. 7.110, Od. 12.216, Od. 22.253, etc.
To appoint as one's lot: τολυπεύειν πολέμους Il. 14.86.

div.head: d
div.p: Absol.: διάνδιχα δῶκε κρόνου πάϊς Il. 9.37. Cf. Il. 22.285, Il. 24.529: Διός γε διδόντος Od. 1.390. Cf. Od. 1.348, Od. 7.35, Od. 19.396.
Absol., to accede to one's wishes: σοὶ δῶκα ἑκὼν ἀέκοντί γε θυμῷ Il. 4.43.
To restore (cf. 14.a 14.b): κτήματα Il. 7.364. Cf. Il. 7.391, 393, Il. 11.125, Il. 22.117.

div.head: a
div.p: With ἀπό, to restore(cf. (13)): πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πατρὶ δόμεναι κούρην Il. 1.98.
To make up for, give compensation for: πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πᾶσαν ἐμοὶ δόμεναι λώβην Il. 9.387. Cf. Od. 2.78.

div.head: b
div.p: With πάλιν, to restore(cf. (13)) Il. 1.116, Il. 7.79 = Il. 22.342, Il. 22.259.
To ask about at length; or simply, to ask about Il. 1.550.
With double acc. (cf. εἴρομαι 4): ταῦτά με Il. 15.93: Od. 4.492, Od. 11.463, Od. 24.478.
To drive (horses, etc.) across something Il. 12.120 (across the ditch).
To drive or thrust (a weapon) through.

p.gloss: To drive or thrust a weapon through.

div.p: To chase away, drive off or away: λῖν Il. 17.110. Cf. Il. 12.276, Il. 18.162, Il. 22.456: Od. 21.370.
To cause to retire, put to flight Il. 7.197.
To send or chase away, dismiss: ξεῖνον ἀπὸ μεγάροιο Od. 17.398. Cf. Od. 20.343.

div.head: a
div.p: To be driven off or away Il. 12.304.

div.head: b
div.p: Of horses, to be driven, race Il. 23.475.
To pass through and emerge from something: πύλας, τῇ ἔμελλε διεξίμεναι πεδίονδε Il. 6.393.
With double acc.: ἐμὲ ταῦτα Il. 10.432.
To bring into order or under control: στρατόν Il. 2.207. Cf. Il. 24.247.
To attend to, carry through: τὰ ἕκαστα Od. 12.16.
To attend to, arrange, settle Il. 11.706.
To row or propel oneself in the water through a space Od. 12.444 (through the strait), Od. 14.351 (through the water between the ship and the shore).

Of a weapon, to
pierce its way Il. 20.263, Il. 23.876: Od. 19.453.
To pass through or traverse a space: ὅπως ἵπποι ῥεῖα διέλθοιεν Il. 10.492. Cf. Il. 24.716.
With acc.: ἄστυ Il. 6.392. Cf. Il. 3.198, Il. 13.144.
To pass through, hold its way: [ὀϊστός] Il. 5.100. Cf. Il. 11.253, Il. 20.416.
To seek for, try to find (a person or a strayed animal): πάνδαρον Il. 4.88. Cf. Il. 5.168, Il. 10.84, Il. 13.760: ἵππους Od. 21.22. Cf. Od. 15.90.
To seek out, try to get the help of: ἄλλους Od. 16.239.
To seek after, try to acquire or have: φάρμακον Od. 1.261. Cf. Il. 17.221.
To strive after, seek to achieve: νόστον Od. 11.100, Od. 23.253.
To seek in marriage, woo Od. 16.391 = Od. 21.161.
Yoked, or meant to be yoked, in pairs: ἵπποι Il. 5.195, Il. 10.473.
To be in doubt, hesitate: ἠὲ . . . ἦ . . . Il. 16.713.
Right through, at length: ἀγορεῦσαι Od. 7.241.
Fully, plainly, in detail Od. 4.836, Od. 12.56.
Carried straight through, straight: ὦλκα Od. 18.375.
Without break or obstruction: ἀτραπιτοί Od. 13.195.
Continuous: νώτοισιν (slices cut the whole length of the back) Il. 7.321: Od. 14.437–Thrown out far, far-stretching: ῥίζῃσιν Il. 12.134.
Carried right round: ῥάψε ῥάβδοισι διηνεκέσιν περὶ κύκλον Il. 12.297.
To go through in speaking: πάντα Il. 9.61, Il. 19.186.
Thus, falling in the sky, i.e. rain-fed; or poss., falling by the power or ordinance of Zeus.
Nom. pl. masc. pple. διαστάντες Il. 12.86, Il. 17.391.

div.head: a
div.p: To stand apart or aside: διαστάντες (severing, parting, i.e. in order to form themselves into bodies) Il. 12.86, τὼ [ἵππω] διαστήτην (wheeled apart, i.e. with their hind quarters) Il. 16.470, διαστάντες (taking their stand at (regular) intervals) Il. 17.391, διέστησαν καὶ εἶξαν ἀπήνῃ (stood aside, parted this way and that) Il. 24.718.

div.head: b
div.p: Of the sea, to part, be cleft Il. 13.29.

div.head: c
div.p: To come into variance, quarrel Il. 1.6.
In pf., to have one's stand, stand, apart: τίη διέσταμεν; (why do we not come to close quarters ?) Il. 21.436.
dat. of Ζεύς + φίλος. Prob. better written thus than Διὶ φίλος. Cf. διιπετής, which is clearly a compound.]
To pronounce judgment, give a decision Il. 18.506, Il. 23.574, 579: Od. 11.547.
To form a decision, come to a resolve Il. 1.542, Il. 8.431 (lay down the law for . . .).
In mid., to seek a judgment or decision, plead one's cause Od. 11.545, Od. 12.440.
Conforming to the traditional order of society, observing the usages common to civilized men, civilized Od. 6.120 = Od. 9.175 = Od. 13.201, Od. 8.575.
Mindful of the usages of courtesy, well-bred Od. 3.52.
Acting with due regard to what is right, upright, honourable Od. 2.282, Od. 3.133, Od. 13.209.

Absol. in neut. δίκαιον, something right or proper: ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίῳ (when the right word has been spoken) Od. 18.414 = Od. 20.322.–οὐ δ. with infin., (it is) not right or proper to: ἀτέμβειν Od. 20.294, Od. 21.312.
In due or proper wise Od. 14.90.
acc. pl. of δίκη + -πολος, conn. with πολεύω.]
Busied about judgments, administering justice Il. 1.238: Od. 11.186.
Custom, usage, way: βασιλήων Od. 4.691. Cf. Od. 18.275, Od. 19.43.
With notion of privilege: γερόντων Od. 24.255.
Applied to a mode of existence or action imposed from without: δμώων Od. 14.59. Cf. Od. 11.218.
Something that always happens in specified circumstances Od. 19.168.
In pl., rules of right, principles of justice: οὐ δίκας εἰδότα οὐδὲ θέμιστας (having no regard for justice or the usages of (civilized) men; see εἴδω III.12) Od. 9.215. Cf. Od. 3.244.
A judgement or doom: ὃς λυκίην εἴρυτο δίκῃσιν (by his (impartial) administration of justice) Il. 16.542. Cf. Il. 18.508.
A plea of right, a claim: δίκας εἴροντο (were asking questions about their . . ., seeking decisions in regard to them) Od. 11.570. Cf. Il. 23.542.

Of gates or
doors, double: πύλας δικλίδας Il. 12.455. Cf. Od. 2.345, Od. 17.268.
To turn (one's team) this way and that Il. 18.543.
To whirl oneself about, spin round. Of acrobats Il. 18.606: = Od. 4.19.
Of a bird, to circle or wheel in flight Il. 23.875.
To wander, rove, roam. Il. 4.541, Il. 24.12: Od. 19.67.
To whirl round (before throwing): δόλον Il. 23.840.
To cause to revolve: μοχλόν Od. 9.384, 388.
To whirl oneself about, spin round. Of dancers Il. 18.494.

div.head: a
div.p: To go in a circle: πόλιν πέρι δινηθήτην Il. 22.165.

div.head: b
div.p: To wander, rove, roam Od. 9.153, Od. 16.63.

div.head: c
div.p: Of the eyes, to be turned in various directions, wander Il. 17.680.
An eddy or whirlpool (in a river) Il. 21.11, 132, 213, 239, 246, 353: Od. 6.116.
Epithet of rivers. Of the Lycian Xanthus Il. 2.877, Il. 5.479.
Of the Trojan Xanthus (Scamander) Il. 8.490, Il. 14.434 = Il. 21.2 = Il. 24.693, Il. 21.125, 206, 332, Il. 22.148.
Of other rivers Il. 20.392: Od. 6.89, Od. 11.242.
App., adorned with inlaid circles or spirals of a precious material Il. 3.391: Od. 19.56.
App., ornamented with rings or round pieces of specified materials Il. 13.407.
[Δι-ο-, fr. Δι- of oblique cases of Ζεύς + γεν-, γίγνομαι.]
In Od. always of Odysseus Od. 2.352, Od. 5.203, Od. 8.3, Od. 10.443, etc.
By his power or will Il. 15.489.
To shoot an arrow over an indicated space Od. 12.102.
To go to ruin: οἶκος ἐμὸς διόλωλε Od. 2.64.
To be afraid Il. 5.566, Il. 9.433, Il. 11.557.
With μή and opt. Il. 17.666: Od. 22.96.
[δι-, δια- 10 + ὀπτεύω fr. ὀπ-. See ὁράω.]
Of Zeus: δῖον γένος Il. 9.538 (= Διὸς κούρη 536).

div.head: a
div.p: Bright, shining. Of the sea Il. 1.141, Il. 2.152, Il. 14.76, etc.: Od. 3.153, Od. 4.577, Od. 5.261, etc.
Of rivers (or perh. rather = διιπετής) Il. 2.522, Il. 12.21.

div.head: α
div.p: Of goddesses, bright, resplendent, glorious Il. 2.820, Il. 3.389, 413, Il. 5.370, Il. 10.290 (here, of Athene, perh. rather in sense (1), = Διὸς τέκος 284): Od. 5.263, 321, 372, Od. 12.133, Od. 20.68, 73.

div.head: β
div.p: With superl. sense: δῖα θεάων, bright, etc., among goddesses(partitive genit.), brightest, etc., of goddesses (cf. 3.b.β) Il. 5.381, Il. 6.305, Il. 14.184, etc.: Od. 1.14, Od. 4.382, Od. 10.400, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: Sim. of peoples or bodies of men: Ἀχαιοί Il. 5.451. Cf. Il. 10.429, Il. 11.455, 504, Il. 18.241, Il. 20.354: Od. 3.116, Od. 19.177, 199.

div.head: α
div.p: Of women, noble, queenly, or the like Il. 5.70, Il. 6.160, Il. 17.40: Od. 3.266.

div.head: β
div.p: With superl. sense: δῖα γυναικῶν, pearl of women(cf. 2.b.β) Il. 2.714, Il. 3.171, 228, 423: Od. 1.332, Od. 4.305, Od. 20.147, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: Of horses, noble, well-bred, or the like Il. 8.185, Il. 23.346 (here perh. rather in sense (1), divine ; cf. 347).
[δι-, δισ-. For the second element cf. διπλόος.]
Double, applied in two layers: δημῷ Il. 23.243. Cf. Il. 23.253.
As fem. sb., a χλαῖνα intended to be worn double Il. 3.126, Il. 22.441: Od. 19.241.
[δι-, δισ-. For the second element cf. ἁ-πλοΐς and δίπλαξ.]
Contr. acc. sing. fem. διπλῆν Il. 10.134: Od. 19.226.

Of the θώρηξ, consisting of two plates: ὅθι ζωστῆρος ὀχῆες σύνεχον καὶ δ. ἤντετο θώρηξ Il. 4.133 = Il. 20.415 (i.e. where the two plates met (and overlapped) at the sides. But there is great confusion in these passages. The belt would naturally be fastened in front, not at the side; and in Il. 20 the wound is behind).
From δίπτυξ acc. sing. fem. δίπτυχα (cf. ὑπόβρυξ).
[κνίσην] ποιήσαντες (i.e. folding it with a double fold so as to enclose the sacrificial joints) Il. 1.461 = Il. 2.424: = Od. 3.458 = Od. 12.361.
Dying twice Od. 12.22 (i.e. with a second death to face).
To engage in a contest of throwing the δίσκος: ἀλλήλοισιν (with . . . ) Od. 8.188.
A mass of stone for distance-throwing as a trial of strength or skill Il. 23.431, Il. 2.774: = Od. 4.626 = Od. 17.168, Od. 8.129, 186.
τά Il. 23.523 = δίσκου οὖρα. See οὖρον 3.
To seek for, search for Il. 16.747.
[contr. fr. διφόρος fr. δι-, δισ- + -φορος, φέρω. Something that carries two, i. e. (in war) the ἡνίοχος and the παραιβάτης.]

div.head: a
div.p:
A chariot, whether used in war, for racing, for travel or for conveyance in general (hardly
to be distinguished from ἅρμα) Il. 3.262, 310, Il. 5.20, Il. 13.392, Il. 23.335, 370, Il. 24.322, etc.: Od. 3.324, 369, 481, 483, Od. 4.590, Od. 14.280.

div.head: b
div.p: The platform thereof, composed of straps plaited and strained tight Il. 5.727.
A seat (the notion of two app. lost) Il. 3.424, Il. 6.354, Il. 24.578: Od. 4.717, Od. 17.330, Od. 19.97, Od. 20.259, etc.
In two: δ. ἑταίρους ἠρίθμεον (into two bodies) Od. 10.203, δ. δφισὶ πάντα δέδασται (between them) Od. 15.412.
In two ways: δ. σφισὶν ἥνδανε βουλή (they were divided in opinion) Il. 18.510: Od. 3.150, βάζομεν (in disagreement, at variance) Od. 3.127.
So of favouring different sides, taking different parts: δ. θυμὸν ἔχοντες Il. 20.32. Cf. Il. 21.386.
Of doubt or hesitation: δ. μερμήριζεν (was in two minds) Od. 22.333. Cf. Od. 16.73, Od. 19.524.
In neut. pl. διχθάδια as adv. = δίχα 2. Of doubt, etc. Il. 14.21.
To be athirst: διψάων (in (his) thirst) Od. 11.584.
To tear asunder, rend: κρημνὸν [πτελέη] διῶσεν Il. 21.244.
Absol.: διωκέμεν ἠδὲ φέβεσθαι Il. 5.223 = Il. 8.107.
To send away, chase away Od. 18.409.
To pursue, seek to win: ἀκίχητα Il. 17.75.
Of a wind, to drive (a vessel) Od. 5.332.
In pass., of a vessel, to be propelled by any agency, course along: ῥίμφα διωκομένη Od. 13.162.
The subduer (cf. πανδαμάτωρ): νὺξ δ. θεῶν καὶ ἀνδρῶν Il. 14.259.
Genit. pl. δμώων Od. 1.398, Od. 9.206, Od. 14.59, Od. 17.402, etc.
Dat. δμώεσσι Od. 6.71, Od. 11.431, Od. 15.379, Od. 24.213, etc. δμωσί Od. 17.389.
App., to knock aside or about, or, to shake: ἀνὴρ ἄνδρʼ ἐδνοπάλιζεν Il. 4.472.
Of clothes, app., metaphorically, to knock them about; or perh., to flutter or flaunt them: τὰ σὰ ῥάκεα δνοπαλίξεις Od. 14.512.
Dark, devoid of light Od. 13.269, Od. 15.50.
In neut. pl. δοιά as adv., in two ways, in double wise: κακὸν ἔμπεσεν οἴκῳ Od. 2.46.
To watch, keep an eye upon: μεταστρεφθέντα (for his turning away) Il. 13.545, Ὠρίωνα Il. 18.488: = Od. 5.274. Cf. Il. 8.340, Il. 16.313, Il. 23.325.
With infin.: ὃς δοκέει χαριέστατος εἶναι Il. 6.90. Cf. Il. 23.459, 470: Od. 1.227, Od. 2.33, Od. 5.342, Od. 6.258, Od. 8.388, Od. 17.415, Od. 18.18, 125, Od. 20.93.
With fut. infin.: οὔ μοι δοκέει μύθοιο τελευτὴ κρανέεσθαι Il. 9.625.
To seem or appear to oneself, think oneself.
With infin.: δοκέεις τις μέγας ἔμμεναι Od. 18.382.
With pres. infin.: δόκησε σφίσι θυμὸς ὣς ἔμεν ὡς εἰ . . . Od. 10.415.
A beam supporting a roof Od. 19.38, Od. 22.176, 193.
A piece of timber intended to be used as such a beam Il. 17.744.
Characterized by or showing craft or guile Od. 4.455, 529, Od. 9.282.
Craftily and skilfully arranged: κύκλον Od. 4.792.
With long αὐλός: αἰγανέας Od. 9.156 (meaning simply long ; the second element not to be pressed).
Epithet of the Phaeacians Od. 8.191 = 369 = Od. 13.166.
Of time: νύκτα δολιχὴν σχέθεν (so as to be . . . ) Od. 23.243.
Of a disease, long drawn-out, protracted Od. 11.172.
In neut. sing. δολιχόν as adv., for a long time, for long, long Il. 10.52.
[doubtfully explained as fr. δολιχός + σκιή, casting a long shadow, long.]
Any cunningly made contrivance for ensnaring or bringing into one's power. Of the bonds forged by Hephaestus Od. 8.276, 282, 317.

Guile, craft, cunning, trickery: ἔπεφνε δόλῳ Il. 7.142. Cf. Il. 21.599, 604, Il. 23.585: ἠὲ δόλῳ ἢ ἀμφαδόν Od. 1.296, Od. 11.120. Cf. Od. 2.106 = Od. 24.141, Od. 2.368, Od. 9.406, 408, Od. 19.212.– (The) contrivance or plotting: ὑπʼ Αἰγίσθοιο δόλῳ Od. 3.235. Cf. Od. 4.92.
Craftiness, cunning: δόλου οὐ λήθετο Il. 23.725. Cf. Od. 23.321.
To have guile in one's heart, plan trickery Il. 3.405, Il. 14.197, 300 = 329 = Il. 19.106: Od. 10.339, Od. 18.51 = Od. 21.274.
In pl. in the same sense: δόμοις ἔνι ποιητοῖσιν Il. 5.198. Cf. Il. 6.370, Il. 11.132, Il. 14.202, Il. 23.84, etc.: Od. 1.380, Od. 3.313, Od. 6.303, Od. 15.465, etc.
A temple: Ἐρεχθῆος Od. 7.81. Cf. Il. 6.89.
Of a nest of wasps or bees Il. 12.169.
With a distinguishing word: χαλκήϊον Od. 18.328 (see χαλκήϊος).
Applied to particular parts of a house.

div.head: b
div.p: To the μέγαρον (sometime difficult to say whether the word should be taken in this restricted sense): δόμον κάτα δαινυμένοισιν Od. 17.332. Cf. Od. 2.322, Od. 7.144, Od. 22.199, 291, 381, 440, 455.
The shaft of an arrow: ἐκλάσθη δ. Il. 11.584.
To shake, cause to quiver Il. 17.55.
To drive about, put in commotion: βόας οἶστρος Od. 22.300.
Of the wind driving clouds Il. 12.157.
nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. δίδωμι.
What one expects: ἀπὸ δόξης (away from, i. e. such or so as to fall short of or disappoint, expectation) Il. 10.324: Od. 11.344.
To take δόρπον Il. 23.11: Od. 7.215, Od. 8.539, Od. 15.302 (twice).
Genit. δουρός (for δορϝός) Il. 3.61, Il. 17.295, Il. 23.529, etc.: Od. 19.453. δούρατος Il. 11.357.
Dat. δούρεσσι Il. 12.303: Od. 8.528. δούρασι Il. 21.162.
A shoot or stem of a tree Od. 6.167.
A treetrunk, a piece of timber in the rough: δοῦρα κέρσαντες Il. 24.450. Cf. Il. 3.61: Od. 5.162, 243.
A beam, plank, or log: δοῦρα νεῶν Il. 2.135. Cf. Il. 12.36, Il. 15.410, Il. 17.744: τέκτονα δούρων Od. 17.384. Cf. Od. 5.361, 370, 371, Od. 9.384, 498, Od. 12.441, 443.
Something made of beams or planks. Applied to the Trojan horse Od. 8.507.
The shaft of a spear: πῆλε κόλον δ. Il. 16.117 (perh. δ. in 114 should be taken in the same sense).
Personified: εἰ καὶ ἐμὸν δ. μαίνεται Il. 8.111.
Fig.: δουρὶ δʼ ἐμῷ κτεάτισσα Il. 16.57. Cf. Il. 16.708, Il. 18.341.
A gift: δ. ὀλίγη τε φίλη τε (i.e. even a small gift is welcome) Od. 6.208. Cf. Il. 10.213: Od. 14.58, Od. 18.287.
A giving for use, a loan Od. 4.651.
One who gives out or distributes: ταμίαι, σίτοιο δοτῆρες Il. 19.44.
Of a slave: δούλειον ἐπιπρέπει (show like a slave's) Od. 24.252.
A female slave: γέετʼ ἐκ δούλης (i.e. a captive) Od. 4.12. Cf. Il. 3.409.
Genit. sing. masc. pf. pple. δεδουπότος Il. 23.679 (app. formed direct fr. δοῦπος. Cf. ἀρημένος, κεκοπώς, πεφυζότες.) (ἐν-.)
To fall in fight, be slain Il. 13.426.
App., simply, to die: δεδουπότος οἰδιπόδαο Il. 23.679.
A sound or noise. Of the roaring of the sea Od. 5.401, Od. 12.202.
Of the roar of rushing and meeting waters Il. 4.455.

Of noise or din in battle: ἐς δοῦπον ἀκόντων (to where the sound is, i.e. to battle) Il. 11.364 = Il. 20.451, δοῦπον ἀκόντων (the whiz) Il. 16.361, τεῖχος ὕπερ δ. ὀρώρει Il. 12.289. Cf. Il. 9.573, Il. 16.635.– Of the sound of persons approaching or moving: ἐπερχομένων δ. Il. 23.234. Cf. Il. 10.354: Od. 10.556, Od. 16.10.
Made of beams or planks. Of the Trojan horse Od. 8.493, 512.
In neut. sing. δουρηνεκές as adv., as far as a spear carries, a spear-throw: ἄπεσαν Il. 10.357.

p.gloss: Famous with, i.e., for, the spear, renowned in fight.

div.p: Epithet of Idomeneus Il. 2.645, 650, Il. 5.45, Il. 13.210, 467, 476.– Of Tlepolemus Il. 2.657.
Of Diomedes Il. 11.368.– Of Odysseus Il. 11.396, 401, 661 = Il. 16.26.
Won by the spear, a captive. Of Briseis Il. 9.343.
A rack or stand for holding spears Od. 1.128.
In neut. pl. δόχμια as adv., across-hill: ἄναντα κάταντα πάραντά τε δ. τε Il. 23.116 (hardly to be distinguished from πάραντα).
Taking a slanting direction: ἀΐσσοντε (slantwise) Il. 12.148.
An armful; in reaping, the corn cut by a sweep of the sickle, a swath Il. 11.69, Il. 18.552.
In reaping, to pick up the cut corn in armfuls Il. 18.555.
To be for doing, be minded to do: εἴ τι δραίνεις Il. 10.96.
With genit.: κόνιος δεδραγμένος Il. 13.393 = Il. 16.486.
To do, accomplish: ἅσσʼ ἐθέλοιεν Od. 15.317.
A female servant: αἳ δῶμα κάτα δρήστειραι ἔασιν Od. 19.345. Cf. Od. 10.349.
Of the pains of child birth, sharp, piercing Il. 11.270.
Of fighting, bitter, keenly contested Il. 15.696.
Applied to passion manifesting itself outwardly (and app. likened to smarting tears) Od. 24.319.

A running: δρόμου ἰσχανόωσαν (for the race) Il. 23.300, ὡς μεμνέῳτο δρόμους 361 (app., the running of the various chariots. Not laps, as the course seems to be only out and home. V.l. δρόμου, the running simply), πύματον τέλεον δρόμον (the last part of the race, i.e. that from the turn home) 373, 768. Cf. Il. 23.375, 526, 758: Od. 8.121.
A piece of ground suited to horses Od. 4.605.
Thickets, coppices (prob. not nec. of oak) Il. 11.118: Od. 10.251.
The pl. app. expressing vague mass or quantity rather than plurality: ἐείσατο καπνὸς διὰ δ. Od. 10.150. Cf. Od. 10.197.
Stays or trestles supporting the keel of a ship under construction Od. 19.574.
To tear away or strip off: ἀπό κε ῥινοὺς δρύφθη (would have had his skin stripped off) Od. 5.426. Cf. Il. 16.324.
In mid. of reciprocal action Od. 2.153 (tearing each other's . . .).
[cognate with Eng. tree, doubtless the orig. sense. Cf. δρίος, δρύϊνος, δρυμά, δρύοχοι, δρυτόμος.]
A felled oak or a piece thereof: ξύλον δρυός Il. 23.328. Cf. Od. 9.186, Od. 14.12, 425.

In phrase οὐκ ἀπὸ δρυὸς οὐδʼ ἀπὸ πέτρης Il. 22.126: Od. 19.163, an obscure proverbial expression. In Il. 22. the sense seems to be giving utterance to thoughts from any source as they arise, with unconsidered or idle words. In Od. 19. the sense seems to be for you are sprung (from men) not from . . .
Suffering, misery: δ. μʼ ἔχει Od. 14.215, δύης πῆμα (sorrow of suffering, sorrow and suffering) 338. Cf. Od. 18.53, 81.
Genit. sing. masc. pple. δυναμένοιο Od. 1.276, Od. 11.414.

p.gloss: To be able, have the power, ability or strength, be in a position, to do something.

div.p: With infin.: τεύχεʼ ὤμοιιν ἀφελέσθαι Il. 5.621. Cf. Il. 1.241, Il. 2.343, Il. 3.236, Il. 6.101, Il. 13.634, etc.: ἐριδαινέμεν οἶος Od. 1.78. Cf. Od. 2.191, Od. 3.89, Od. 4.374, Od. 18.230, Od. 21.171, etc.
Of things: οὐδέ μοι αἷμα τερσῆναι δύναται (as if it was striving) Il. 16.519. Cf. Il. 14.33.
With ellipse of infin.: δύναται ἅπαντα Od. 4.237. Cf. Il. 6.229: Od. 10.306, Od. 14.445.
