div.p: ἠὲ (ἢ) . . . ἠὲ (ἢ) . . ., either . . . or . . .: ἢ νῦν δηθύνοντʼ ἢ ὕστερον αὖτις ἰόντα Il. 1.27. Cf. Il. 1.138, 395, Il. 5.484, Il. 9.78, 537, Il. 10.370, etc.: ἠὲ δόλῳ ἢ ἀμφαδόν Od. 1.296. Cf. Od. 3.99, 217, Od. 4.546, Od. 5.484, Od. 6.103, Od. 10.228, etc.
Thrice or four times Il. 1.145, Il. 7.179, Il. 10.6, etc.: Od. 10.433, Od. 15.84, etc.
In questions in disjunctive form (the second particle written ἦε, ἦ).

div.head: a
div.p: Direct: ἠέ τι βέβληαι, ἦε . . .; Il. 13.251. Cf. Il. 15.735, etc.: Od. 3.72, Od. 24.109, etc.
Without the particle in the first clause Il. 15.203, etc.: Od. 20.130, Od. 21.194, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: Indirect, whether . . . or . . .: μερμήριξεν, ἢ . . . ἦε . . . Il. 1.190. Cf. Il. 2.238, Il. 4.15, Il. 5.86, Il. 8.377, Il. 13.327, Il. 18.308 (and see whether . . .), etc.: ὄφρʼ ἐῢ εἰδῶ, ἠὲ . . . ἦ . . . Od. 1.175. Cf. Od. 1.268, Od. 3.170, Od. 4.28, Od. 6.142, Od. 11.175, Od. 16.260, Od. 19.525, etc.
Without the particle in the first clause Il. 10.546, etc.: Od. 4.837, etc.
With εἰ or αἴ in the first clause Il. 2.368, Il. 6.368, Il. 8.533, Il. 22.246: Od. 24.218.
After comparatives, than: ἀρείοσιν ἠέ περ ὑμῖν Il. 1.260. Cf. Il. 5.531, Il. 8.190, Il. 16.688, etc.: νεώτεροι ἢ πάρος ἦσαν Od. 10.395. Cf. Od. 1.322, Od. 8.154, etc.
After verbs implying comparison: βούλομαι . . . ἢ . . . Il. 1.117, etc.: ἔφθης . . . ἢ . . . Od. 11.58, etc.
-ου, ὁ. Also Ἥλιος Od. 8.271. Ἠέλιος as voc. Il. 3.277.

div.head: b
div.p: ὑπʼ αὐγὰς ἠελίοιο, in the upper world, among the livingOd. 11.498, 619, Od. 15.349.
Of seeing the sun, i.e. of living: δηρὸν ἔτʼ ὄψεσθαι φάος ἠελίοιο Il. 5.120. Cf. Il. 18.61 = 442, Il. 24.558: Od. 4.540 = Od. 10.498, Od. 4.833, Od. 14.44 = Od. 20.207.
Sim. of being born: ἠελίου ἴδεν αὐγάς Il. 16.188.
Of leaving the sun, i.e. of dying: λείψειν (λιπὼν) φάος ἠελίοιο Il. 18.11: Od. 11.93.
The quarter of the rising sun, the east: πρὸς ἠῶ τʼ ἠέλιόν τε Il. 12.239: Od. 9.26, Od. 13.240.

The sun-god: Ἠ. ὃς πάντʼ ἐφορᾷς Il. 3.277. Cf. Il. 3.104, Il. 8.480, Il. 14.344, Il. 19.197, etc.: βοῦς Ὑπερίονος Ἠελίοιο Od. 1.8. Cf. Od. 3.1, Od. 8.271, Od. 10.138, Od. 11.16, 109, Od. 12.133, Od. 19.276, Od. 24.12, etc.
To take wing: ὡς ἀκρίδες ἠερέθονται Il. 21.12.
To wave about, flutter: θύσανοι ἠερέθονται Il. 2.448.
Fig., of the mind, to be blown about by passion or caprice, to be unsteady or untrustworthy Il. 3.108.
[ἀϝερ-. Cf. ἠώς, ἄριστον, αὔριον, ἦρι, λ. aurora.]
With the early morning: ἠερίη ἀνέβη οὐρανόν Il. 1.497. Cf. Il. 1.557, Il. 3.7: Od. 9.52.
Epithet of the sea, misty, melting into the haze of distance Il. 23.744: Od. 2.263, Od. 3.105, 294, Od. 4.482, Od. 5.164, 281, Od. 8.568 = Od. 13.150 = 176, Od. 12.285.
In neut. ἠεροειδές as adv., through the haze, in the haze of distance: ὅσσον ἠ. ἀνὴρ ἴδεν Il. 5.770.
Of a rock, shrouded in mist Od. 12.233 (cf. 74).
Epithet of caves, dim, dusky, shadowy Od. 12.80, Od. 13.103 = 347, 366.
Hazy, gloomy, dark: τάρταρον Il. 8.13, ζόφον Il. 12.240, Il. 15.191, Il. 21.56, Il. 23.51: Od. 11.57, 155, Od. 13.241.
Hazy, misty: κατʼ ἠερόεντα κέλευθα (through the paths of the clouds) Od. 20.64.
[perh. fr. ἀείρω + φωνή. Cf. ἠερέθομαι, μετ-ήορος. Lifting up the voice.]
In voc. ἠθεῖε as a form of address to an elder or a master Il. 6.518 (Paris to Hector), Il. 10.37 (Menelaus to Agamemnon), Il. 22.229, 239 (the supposed Deïphobus to Hector).
Sim. in the periphrasis ἠθείη κεφαλή Il. 23.94 (Achilles to the shade of Patroclus. Patroclus was the senior Il. 11.787).
In Od. 14.147 (ἠθεῖόν μιν καλέω) Eumaeus means that he mentally addresses his absent master as ἠθεῖε.
In pl., the accustomed haunts of animals: ἤθεα ἵππων Il. 6.511 = Il. 15.268.
Provisions for a voyage: ὅπλισσον ἤϊα Od. 2.289, ἤϊα φερώμεθα 410, ἤῗά κε πάντα κατέφθιτο Od. 4.363, ἐν καὶ ᾖα κωρύκῳ Od. 5.266, Od. 9.212, νηὸς ἐξέφθιτο ἤῗα πάντα Od. 12.329.
Chaff (in this sense perh. a different word): ὡς ἄνεμος ζαὴς ἠΐων (disyllable) θημῶνα τινάξῃ Od. 5.368.
Epithet of a river, of unknown meaning: ἐπʼ ἠϊόεντι σκαμάνδρῳ Il. 5.36.
Epithet of Apollo, of unknown meaning: ἤϊε Φοῖβε Il. 15.365, Il. 20.152.
A beach or shore of the sea: ἠϊόνος προπάροιθε βαθείης Il. 2.92. Cf. Il. 7.462, Il. 12.31, Il. 14.36, Il. 20.148, Il. 23.61.

div.head: a
div.p: Portions of the shore, beaches, shores: ἀμφʼ ἄκραι ἠϊόνες βοόωσιν (to their furthest points) Il. 17.265 (v.l. ἄκραι ἠϊόνος, taking ἄκραι as sb. (see ἄκρη 3) and ἠϊόνος in sense (1), the headlands of the shore), ἠὼς φαινομένη ὑπεὶρ ἅλα τʼ ἠϊόνας τε Il. 24.13. Cf. Od. 5.156.

div.head: b
div.p: Beaches or spits projecting into the sea: ἠϊόνας παραπλῆγας Od. 5.418 = 440. Cf. Od. 6.138.

Of action, gently, without effort:
ψύξασα Il. 20.440. Cf. Il. 23.336: Od. 18.92, 94, Od. 20.301.
Gently, without violence: ἀπώσατο γέροντα Il. 24.508.
Of journeying, softly, at a foot-pace Od. 17.254.
Of speaking, softly, in an undertone Il. 3.155.
Of the soft play of light on a glossy surface: χιτῶνας ἦκα στίλβοντας ἐλαίῳ Il. 18.596.
[doubtfully explained as fr. ἠ- = ἀ-1 + -κεστος. See κεστός.]
Thus, untouched by the goad: βοῦς ἠκέστας Il. 6.94 = 275, 309.
The slowest or weakest: ἠ. ἐλαυνέμεν (in driving) Il. 23.531.
The yarn spun off from the distaff Od. 6.53, 306, Od. 7.105, Od. 17.97, Od. 18.315.
To go about or skulk in order to avoid (danger): ὅππῃ ἐμὸν μένος ἠλασκάζει Od. 9.457.
To rove or flit about: ἔλαφοι καθʼ ὕλην αὔτως ἠλάσκουσαι Il. 13.104. Cf. Il. 2.470.
In pl., beads of amber: ὅρμον ἠλέκτροισιν ἐερμένον Od. 18.296. Cf. Od. 15.460.
Crazed, distraught: φρένας ἠλέ (in your . . .) Il. 15.128. Cf. Od. 2.243.
That takes away one's wits or discretion: οἶνος Od. 14.464.
Strengthening πολλός: ἤλιθα πολλήν Il. 11.677. Cf. Od. 5.483, Od. 9.330, Od. 14.215, Od. 19.443.
Time of life: ἤν πως ἡλικίην αἰδέσσεται (may respect my age) Il. 22.419.
Those of the same age as oneself, one's fellows in years, one's contemporaries: ἡλικίην ἐκέκαστο Il. 16.808.
Of the same age: βόες Od. 18.373.
[ἀλιτ-, ἀλιταίνω + μήν. Failing in (the due number of) months.]
A nail or stud used for ornament Il. 1.246, Il. 11.29, 633.
[said to be for ἠλύθ-τιος, fr. ἠλυθ- (see ἔρχομαι). To which . . . go.]
Ἠλύσιον πεδίον, an abode of everlasting bliss assigned to mortals favoured by the godsOd. 4.563.
In pl.: ὅσσον ἥμασιν ἔπλευ ἄριστος (in throwing the spear) Il. 23.891.

p.gloss: Abounding in sand, sandy, by the sandy shore.

div.p: 3 pl. ἥαται (ἥσ-αται), also writtenεἵαται Il. 2.137, Il. 10.100, 161, 422: Od. 2.403, Od. 6.307. ἕαται Il. 3.134, Il. 9.628.
1 sing. impf. ἥμην Il. 6.336: Od. 10.374, Od. 11.49.

3 pl. ἥατο (ἥσ-ατο), also writtenεἵατο Il. 3.149, Il. 7.61, Il. 8.554, Il. 15.10, Il. 18.504, Il. 24.99, etc.: Od. 1.326, Od. 2.398, Od. 3.8, Od. 9.545, Od. 20.106, etc. ἕατο Il. 7.414. ἧντο Il. 3.153.

To sit, be seated: παρὰ κλισίῃ ἥμενον Il. 1.330, ἕαται σιγῇ Il. 3.134. Cf. Il. 2.200, Il. 4.21, Il. 6.324, Il. 8.445, Il. 9.190, Il. 13.11, etc.: ἥμενοι ἐν ῥινοῖσιν Od. 1.108. Cf. Od. 1.114, Od. 2.36, Od. 3.8, 32, Od. 6.52, Od. 8.157, Od. 10.374, etc.
To sit idle, doing nothing: ἥμενοι αὖθι ἕκαστοι ἀκήριοι Il. 7.100. Cf. Il. 1.134, Il. 13.253: οἶον ἧσθʼ ἄνεθͅ Od. 2.240. Cf. Od. 10.375, Od. 16.145.
Requiring to do nothing: ἱστία ἐρύσαντες ἥμεθα Od. 9.78 = Od. 14.256. Cf. Od. 10.507, Od. 11.10 = Od. 12.152.

To sit, abide, be, remain, doing something specified or in a specified condition or place: ἀδάκρυτος ἧσθαι Il. 1.416, ἥαται ποτιδέγμεναι Il. 2.137, τηλόθι πάτρης ἧμαι ἐνὶ Τροίῃ Il. 24.542. Cf. Il. 2.255, Il. 4.412, Il. 8.480, Il. 9.628, Il. 10.100, 161, 422, Il. 15.740, Il. 18.104: Od. 3.263, Od. 13.337, 424, Od. 14.41, Od. 19.120, Od. 21.425.
Of an army, to be set down or encamped: τὴν πόλιν ἀμφὶ δύω στρατοὶ ἥατο Il. 18.509.
Of a sentinel or scout, to be at his post Il. 10.182.
To be posted: δύω σκοποὶ ἥατο Il. 18.523. Cf. Il. 24.799.
Of a thing, to be set, fixed, placed: ἔνθα μύλαι ἥατο Od. 20.106.
Day, the day, the period of daylight: μέσον ἠ. Il. 21.111, ὄφρʼ ἀέξετο ἠ. Il. 8.66 = Il. 11.84: = Od. 9.56. Cf. Od. 7.288, Od. 10.86, 470, Od. 17.191, Od. 18.367 = Od. 22.301.

p.gloss: A day considered as a space of time.

div.p: With an adj., expressing periphrastically the substantival notion implicit in the adj.

div.head: a
div.p: αἴσιμον ἠ. (the fatal day, the fate, one's fate) Il. 8.72, Il. 21.100, Il. 22.212: Od. 16.280.

div.head: b
div.p: ἠ. ἀναγκαῖον (the day that brings compulsion, slavery) Il. 16.836.

div.head: c
div.p: δούλιον ἠ. (the day that brings slavery, slavery) Il. 6.463: Od. 14.340, Od. 17.323.

div.head: d
div.p: ἐλεύθερον ἠ. (the day or time of freedom, freedom) Il. 6.455, Il. 16.831, Il. 20.193.

div.head: e
div.p: κακὸν ἠ. (the day that brings bane, bane) Il. 9.251, 597, Il. 20.315 = Il. 21.374: Od. 10.269, 288, Od. 15.524.

div.head: f
div.p: μόρσιμον ἠ. (the fatal day, one's fate) Il. 15.613: Od. 10.175.–

div.head: g
div.p: νηλεὲς ἠ. (the day of pitiless fate, fate, bane) Il. 11.484, 588, Il. 13.514, Il. 15.375, Il. 17.511, 615, Il. 21.57: Od. 8.525, Od. 9.17.

div.head: h
div.p: νόστιμον ἠ. (the day that brings one's home-coming, one's home-coming) Od. 1.9, 168, 354, Od. 3.233 = Od. 5.220 = Od. 8.466, Od. 6.311, Od. 16.149, Od. 17.253, 571, Od. 19.369.

div.head: i
div.p: ὀλέθριον ἠ. (the day that brings bane, bane) Il. 19.294, 409.

div.head: j
div.p: ἠ. ὀρφανικόν (the day that brings orphanhood, orphanhood) Il. 22.490.
By day, in the day-time: ἠματίη ὑφαίνεσκεν Od. 2.104 = Od. 24.139. Cf. Od. 19.149.

Correlative with ἠδέ. ἠμὲν . . . ἠδὲ . . ., both . . . and . . .: ἠμὲν νέοι ἠδὲ γέροντες Il. 2.789. Cf. Il. 5.751, Il. 9.36, Il. 11.7, Il. 12.159, Il. 15.226, etc.: ἠμὲν ἀπείλησας . . . ἠδὲ . . . (you boasted that . . . and lo . . .) Od. 8.383. Cf. Od. 1.97, Od. 2.68, Od. 3.105, Od. 10.22, Od. 14.193, etc.
So ἠμὲν . . . ἠδὲ . . . ἠδὲ . . . Il. 4.258, etc.– ἠμὲν . . . δὲ . . . Il. 12.428.– ἠμὲν . . . τε . . . Od. 8.575.
Retaining something of the original emphasis (surely . . . and even so . . .) Il. 1.453, etc.
The cultivated vine, the vine Od. 5.69.
To our (my) house: ἡ. ἐλθόντες Od. 8.39. Cf. Od. 15.513, Od. 24.267.
With the article: αἱ ἡμέτεραι ἄλοχοι Il. 2.136.
Absol.: εἰς ἡμέτερον (sc. δῶμα) Od. 2.55 = Od. 17.534.–ἐφʼ ἡμέτερα (sc. δώματα) (to our homes, home) Il. 9.619.
Absol.: ἐς ἡμέτερον (sc. δῶμα) Od. 7.301.–ἐφʼ ἡμέτερα (sc. δώματα) (home) Od. 15.88. (Sometimes, esp. in uses with οἶκος and the like, it is difficult to say which sense should be preferred.)
To utter speech, speak, say: ἦ καὶ . . . Il. 1.219. Cf. Il. 1.528, Il. 3.292, 310, 355, etc.: Od. 2.321, Od. 3.337, Od. 6.198, Od. 9.371, etc.
Half-divine, of divine parentage on one side: ἀνδρῶν Il. 12.23.
A mule (doubtless including the hinny) Il. 7.333, Il. 10.352, Il. 17.742, Il. 23.121, Il. 24.150, etc.: Od. 4.636, Od. 6.37, Od. 7.2, Od. 8.124, Od. 15.85, Od. 17.298, etc.
In Il. 2.852 (ἡμιόνων ἀγροτεράων) app. not strictly mules but some species intermediate between the horse and the ass.
Like ἵππος 3: ἐφʼ ἡμιόνων κείμενον (i.e. on the waggon) Il. 24.702.
A half-axe, an axe with a single cutting edge Il. 23.851, 858, 883.
Half, half of: ἡμίσεες λαοί Od. 3.155.
Absol., half of what is specified or indicated.

div.head: a
div.p: ἡμίσεες εἰλεῦντο Il. 21.7. Cf. Od. 3.157, Od. 24.464.

div.head: b
div.p: In neut. ἥμισυ: τιμῆς ἡ. Il. 6.193. Cf. Il. 9.580 (following τὸ ἡ. 579 (see below)), Il. 17.231 (twice): Od. 9.246 (twice), Od. 13.114, Od. 17.322.
With the article: τὸ δʼ ἡ. κεῖτʼ ἐπὶ γαίης Il. 13.565. Cf. Il. 9.579
In neut. as adv., to the extent of a half: ἡ. μείρεο τιμῆς Il. 9.616.
With indic.: ἦμος δʼ ἠέλιος κατέδυ Il. 1.475. Cf. Il. 1.477, Il. 16.779, etc.: Od. 2.1, Od. 9.58, 168, etc.
With subj. in a conditional relative sentence. See Table at end III.B.a 1.
To cause to bend, bow, droop: κάρη Il. 8.308.
To bend, bow, droop: λήϊον ἠμύει ἀσταχύεσσιν (with its ears) Il. 2.148, ἤμυσε καρήατι Il. 19.405.
Of a city nodding or tottering to its fall Il. 2.373 = Il. 4.290.
One skilled in throwing (the spear): ἥμονες ἄνδρες Il. 23.886.
Introducing in protasis one of two opposed clauses, even if, even though, though, granted that = εἰ 4. For the examples see (II) of Table at end.
Introducing the protasis of conditional sentences, if, on condition that, supposing that = εἰ 5. For the examples see (III) of Table.

In final clauses, if haply, in the hope that = εἰ 9..b: ἐμὲ πρόες, ἤν πού τι φόως Δαναοῖσι γένωμαι Il. 16.39. Cf. Il. 7.39, Il. 14.78, Il. 17.245, Il. 20.172, Il. 22.419: ἤν που ἀκούσῃ (ἀκούσω) Od. 1.94, Od. 2.360, Od. 3.83. Cf. Od. 1.282, Od. 2.216, Od. 5.417.
In an object clause, whether = εἰ 10

div.head: b
div.p: : ὄφρα ἴδῃ ἤν τοι χραίσμῃ φιλότης Il. 15.32.
Blown upon or vexed by the winds: ἄκριας Od. 9.400, Od. 16.365. Cf. Il. 22.145: Od. 19.432.
The reins used in driving a chariot Il. 3.261, Il. 5.226, 262, 365, Il. 8.121, Il. 16.404, Il. 17.619, Il. 23.337, etc.: Od. 3.483, Od. 6.81.
Used loosely of the παραιβάτης (cf. ἡνίοχος 2) Il. 19.401.
To act as ἡνίοχος of a war-chariot, drive it Il. 11.103, Il. 23.641, 642.
[ἡνία + ὀχ-, ἔχω. He that holds the reins.]

The driver of a war-chariot as distinguished from the παραιβάτης or fighting man: παραιβάται ἡνίοχοί τε Il. 23.132. Cf. Il. 5.231, 580, Il. 8.119, 124 = 316, Il. 8.126, Il. 11.47 = Il. 12.84, Il. 11.161, 273 = 399, Il. 11.280, Il. 12.111, Il. 13.386, 394, 537 = Il. 14.431, Il. 17.427, 439, 610, Il. 18.225, Il. 23.280.
Used loosely of the παραιβάτης (cf. ἡνιοχεύς 2): θρασὺν ἡνίοχον φορέοντες Ἕκτορα Il. 8.89 (Eniopeus was driving, see 119, where he also is called ἡ.).
In pl. including both the ἡ. proper and the παραιβάτης: σὺν ἡνιόχοισι κακοῖσιν Il. 17.487.
One who drives his chariot in a race: μήτι ἡ. περιγίγνεται ἡνιόχοιο Il. 23.318. Cf. Il. 23.460, 465, 502.
[doubtfully explained as fr. ἔνος, cited in sense year.]
Thus, one year old, that is a yearling: δυοκαίδεκα βοῦς ἤνις Il. 6.94 = 275, 309, βοῦν ἦνιν Il. 10.292: = Od. 3.382.
Manliness, valour, mettle, prowess: ἠνορέηφι πεποιθώς Il. 4.303. Cf. Il. 6.156, Il. 8.226 = Il. 11.9, Il. 17.329: Od. 24.509.
Of unknown meaning. Perh. glittering, gleaming, or the like: ἤνοπι χαλκῷ Il. 16.408, Il. 18.349: = Od. 10.360.
Of the east, dwelling in the east, eastern Od. 8.29.
In fem. as sb., the morning: πᾶσαν ἠοίην μένομεν Od. 4.447.
Also ἕως Od. 2.78. This form scanned as a monosyllable Il. 17.727.
While, so long as: ἧος ζώει Od. 17.390. Cf. Od. 19.530.
While, during the time that: ἧος ὁ ταῦθʼ ὥρμαινεν Il. 1.193: = Od. 4.120 = Od. 5.365, ἧός μοι πάρʼ ὀϊστοί (while I still have them) Od. 22.106. Cf. Od. 13.315 = Od. 15.153, Od. 17.358.
For a time, up to a certain point of time: ἕως μὲν θέουσιν Il. 17.727. Cf. Il. 12.141, Il. 13.143, Il. 15.277, Il. 17.730: Od. 2.148, Od. 3.126 (all that time).

div.head: β
div.p: With κεν: ἧός κε τέλος κιχείω Il. 3.291. Cf. Il. 17.622, Il. 24.154, 183.

div.head: α
div.p: Pure: ἧος θερμαίνοιτο (to remain there till it should . . .) Od. 9.376. Cf. Od. 23.151.

div.head: β
div.p: With κεν: ἕως κʼ ἀπὸ πάντα δοθείη Od. 2.78.
With opt.: ἦος χυτλώσαιτο Od. 6.80. Cf. Od. 4.800, Od. 5.386.

p.gloss: After a vb. of praying, that.

div.p: With opt.: ἀρώμενος ἧος ἵκοιο γῆρας Od. 19.367.
[prob. for ἀ-πεδ-ανός fr. ἀ-1 + πεδ-, ποδ-, πούς. Not firm on the feet. Cf. ἔμπεδος.]
To or on to the land as opposed to the sea: ἐκ πόντου βὰς ἠ. Od. 5.56. Cf. Od. 5.438, Od. 9.73, 485, Od. 10.403, 423, Od. 13.116, Od. 23.236.
To the mainland as opposed to an island: πέμψω σʼ ἠ. Od. 18.84, ἀνάξομέν μιν ἠ. 115 (in both cases said in Ithaca).

The land as opposed to
the sea: νῆʼ ἐπʼ ἠπείροιο ἔρυσσαν Il. 1.485: εἴτʼ ἐπʼ ἠπείρου . . . εἴτʼ ἐν πελάγει Od. 3.90. Cf. Od. 1.162, Od. 5.348, 350, 399, 402, Od. 9.85 = Od. 10.56, Od. 9.496, Od. 13.114, Od. 14.136, Od. 16.325, 359, 367.
Inland parts as opposed to the coast Od. 9.49.

The mainland, as opposed to an island or islands: οἳ ἤπειρον ἕχον Il. 2.635 (the coast of the mainland opposite the islands): οὔτʼ ἠπείροιο οὔτʼ αὐτῆς Ἰθάκης Od. 14.97. Cf. Od. 13.235, Od. 14.100, Od. 21.109, Od. 24.378.
A cheat, deceiver, cozener, beguiler: ἠπεροπῆά τε καὶ ἐπίκλοπον Od. 11.364.
To deceive, cozen: ἵνʼ ἐμὰς φρένας ἠπεροπεύσῃς Od. 13.327.
To trick, take unfair advantage of Il. 23.605.
To beguile the heart of, lead astray (a woman) Il. 5.349: Od. 15.419.
So τάτε φρένας ἠπεροπεύει γυναιξίν Od. 15.421.
With direct and cognate acc.: τί με ταῦτα λιλαίεαι ἠπεροπεύειν; (to beguile me thus) Il. 3.399.
App., generous in giving, bountiful in supplying her children's needs, grudging them nothing: μήτηρ Il. 6.251.

Well or kindly disposed, kindly, gentle, mild, not harsh or rigorous: ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν (is well disposed towards me) Il. 4.361 (see εἴδω III.12), ἐθέλω τοι ἠ. εἶναι Il. 8.40 = Il. 22.184. Cf. Il. 24.770, 775: Od. 2.47, 230 = Od. 5.8, Od. 2.234 = Od. 5.12, Od. 10.337, Od. 11.441, Od. 13.314, Od. 14.139, Od. 15.152, 490.

Absol. in neut. pl.: εἴ μοι ἤπια εἰδείη (were well disposed towards me) Il. 16.73: ὁμῶς τοι ἤπια οἶδεν (is at one with you in loyalty of heart) Od. 13.405 = Od. 15.39, ἀνάκτεσιν ἤπια εἰδώς (loyal to them) Od. 15.557. See in reference to these εἴδω III.12.
Giving kindly tendance, solicitous for the well-being of what is committed to one Il. 23.281.
Of speech, tending to effect reconcilement or bring peace Od. 20.327.
Of medicinal applications, soothing, allaying pain Il. 4.218, Il. 11.515, 830.
(ᾰ) [ἠπύω. Prob. orig. a voc. turned into a nom.].
To call to (a person): κύκλωπας Od. 9.399. Cf. Od. 10.83.
Of the wind, to roar Il. 14.399.
Of the lyre, to sound Od. 17.271.

What is pleasing or agreeable. Only in acc. sing. ἧρα in phrase ἦρα φέρειν, to do acceptable service, make oneself agreeable, show oneself well disposed: μητρὶ φίλῃ ἐπὶ ἦρα φέρων Il. 1.572. Cf. Il. 1.578: Od. 3.164, Od. 16.375, Od. 18.56.
Sim.: θυμῷ ἦρα φέροντες (yielding to it, giving in to it) Il. 14.132.
Early in the morning Il. 9.360: Od. 19.320, Od. 20.156.
Without Ἠώς, the dawn: οὐδὲ σέ γʼ ἠ. λήσει Od. 22.197. Cf. Od. 23.347.
With ἄνδρες: στίχας ἀνδρῶν ἡρώων Il. 5.747 = Il. 8.391. Cf. Il. 9.525, Il. 13.346: Od. 1.101, Od. 4.268, Od. 11.629, Od. 24.25, 88.

Prefixed to an ethnic name, of a body of the same race in arms together: ὦ φίλοι ἥρωες Δαναοί Il. 2.110 = Il. 6.67 = Il. 15.733 = Il. 19.78. Cf. Il. 2.256, Il. 12.165, Il. 13.629, Il. 15.219, 230, 261, 702, Il. 19.34, 41: Od. 24.68.
In voc. as a form of address to a warrior Il. 10.416, Il. 20.104.
With a proper name: Εὐρύπυλʼ ἥρως Il. 11.819, 838.
Applied to warriors, but signifying little more than the man, the wight: ἔτρεψεν ἀδελφειοῦ φρένας ἡ. Il. 6.61. Cf. Il. 3.377, Il. 7.120 = Il. 13.788, Il. 10.179, Il. 23.824.
As an honourable appellation of others than warriors: ἐπὶ φᾶρος βάλετʼ ὤμοις ἡ. Od. 15.62. Cf. Od. 7.44, Od. 8.242.
With an ethnic name: ἥρωας Ἀχαιούς Od. 1.272.

Prefixed or added as a sort of title to the name or patronymic of another than a warrior: Λαέρτην ἥρωα Od. 1.189. Cf. Od. 2.15, 99 = Od. 19.144 = Od. 24.134, Od. 2.157 = Od. 24.451, Od. 3.415, Od. 4.21 = 303, 617 = Od. 15.117, Od. 6.303, Od. 7.155, Od. 8.483, Od. 11.342, Od. 14.317, Od. 15.52, 121, 131, Od. 18.423, Od. 22.185.
In voc. as a form of address to another than a warrior Od. 4.423, Od. 7.303, Od. 10.516.
With a proper name: Τηλέμαχʼ ἥρως Od. 4.312.

[for ἡκιων. Comp. fr. ἦκα. Cf.
ἤκιστος.]
Of less worth or merit, inferior Il. 16.722, Il. 23.322, 858.
In neut. ἧσσον as adv., less: ὀλίγον τί μʼ ἡ. ἐτίμα Od. 15.365.
Peace, freedom from disturbance: ἡ. ἂν ἐμοὶ καὶ μᾶλλον ἔτʼ εἴη Od. 18.22.
τό. Only in nom. and acc. sing.
The heart: πάλλεται ἠ. ἀνὰ στόμα Il. 22.452. Cf. Il. 10.93.
The heart, breast, soul, mind. As the seat or a seat

div.head: α
div.p: Of life, vitality, the vital powers, strength (cf. θυμός I 1.a): εἰ χάλκεόν μοι ἠ. ἐνείη Il. 2.490: τετιημένος ἠ. Od. 7.287. Cf. Od. 4.703 = Od. 23.205, Od. 19.136, Od. 24.345.

div.head: β
div.p: The animating principle, the vital spirit, the soul, the life, life, one's life (cf. θυμός I.1.b): μὴ ἠ. ὀλέσσῃς Il. 5.250. Cf. Il. 11.115 (of fawns), Il. 15.252, Il. 16.660, Il. 17.535, Il. 21.201, Il. 24.50: ἀπορραῖσαι ἠ. Od. 16.428.

div.head: b
div.p: Of spirit, courage, stoutness, resolution, endurance: ἄλκιμον ἠ. Il. 5.529. Cf. Il. 3.31, Il. 16.209, 242, 264 (of wasps), Il. 17.111 (of a lion), Il. 19.169, Il. 20.169 (of a lion), Il. 21.114, 425, 571, Il. 24.205, 521: μινύθει τοι ἠ. ἐταίρων Od. 4.374. Cf. Od. 4.467, 481 = Od. 10.496, Od. 5.297 = 406 = Od. 22.147, Od. 9.256, Od. 10.198 = 566 = Od. 12.277, Od. 22.68.

div.head: c
div.p: Of anger, wrath, passion: κεχολωμένος ἠ. (in his heart) Il. 14.367. Cf. Il. 10.107, Il. 24.585.

div.head: d
div.p: Of desire or appetite: σίτοιο ἄσασθαι ἠ. Il. 19.307.

div.head: e
div.p: Of volition: τίς σφῶϊν μαίνεται ἠ.; Il. 8.413. Cf. Il. 15.166, 182: δῶρον ὅττι κέ μοι δοῦναι ἠ. ἀνώγῃ Od. 1.316.

div.head: g
div.p: Of the faculty of deliberating or considering: ἠ οἱ μερμήριξεν Il. 1.188.
Of recollection: ὥς μοι ἰνδάλλεται ἠ. Od. 19.224.–

div.head: h
div.p: Of one's character or dispostion: ἀμείλιχον ἠ. ἔχουσα Il. 9.572. Cf. Il. 9.497: Od. 23.172.
Epithet of lions Il. 15.275, Il. 17.109, Il. 18.318: Od. 4.456.
Epithet of goddesses and women. Of Leto Il. 1.36, Il. 19.413: Od. 11.318.
Without expressed vb. Il. 2.469, Il. 15.618, Il. 17.737: Od. 21.48.
After a comp., than: μελάντερον ἠΰτε πίσσα Il. 4.277.
A fire: σπλάγχνʼ ὑπείρεχον Ἡφαίστοιο Il. 2.426.
Where: ἡ. ἑκάστῳ δῶμα Ἥφαιστος ποίησεν Il. 1.607. Cf. Il. 3.326, Il. 5.774, Il. 8.14, Il. 11.76: Od. 3.292, Od. 6.94, Od. 19.553.
In an object clause: ἄλλους πευθόμεθʼ, ἡ. ἕκαστος ἀπώλετο Od. 3.87.

From the dawn; hence, at dawn, in the morning. Referring to the next morning: ἠ. ἴτω ἐπὶ νῆας Il. 7.372. Cf. Il. 7.381, Il. 11.555 = Il. 17.664, Il. 18.136, Il. 23.49, Il. 24.401: ἠ. ἀγορήνδε καθεζώμεσθα κιὁντες Od. 1.372. Cf. Od. 3.153, 366, Od. 4.214, Od. 7.189, Od. 12.293, Od. 14.512, Od. 15.308, 506, Od. 17.600, Od. 18.248, Od. 19.320, Od. 21.265, 280, Od. 24.72.
A dawning or morning considered as a space of time: ὄφρʼ ἠ. ἦν Il. 8.66 = Il. 11.84, ἠοῦς ὄψεαι (in the morning) Il. 8.470, τὸν
[μῦθον] ἠοῦς (the morrow's) 525. Cf. Il. 21.111: νηῦς ἠῶ πεῖρε κέλευθον (through the morning) Od. 2.434. Cf. Od. 7.288, Od. 9.56.
A morning considered as a point or unit of time or as one of a series: δυωδεκάτη Il. 1.493 = Il. 24.31, Il. 21.80, Il. 24.413. Cf. Il. 13.794, Il. 21.156, Il. 24.781, 785: Od. 19.192, 571.
The quarter of the dawn, the east: πρὸς ἠῶ τʼ ἠέλιόν τε Il. 12.239: Od. 9.26, Od. 13.240. Cf. Od. 10.190.
To sit, be seated: ἕδος ἔνθα θάασσεν Il. 9.194. Cf. Il. 15.124: δηθὰ θεῶν ἐν δαιτὶ θαασσέμεν Od. 3.336.
App. vertical (presumably metal) pegs at the top and bottom of a side of a gate working in stone sockets and governing the opening and shutting Il. 12.459.
A female servant in charge of the sleeping-rooms, a chamber-maid Od. 7.8, Od. 23.293.
To the θάλαμος (in sense (4)) Od. 2.348, Od. 21.8, Od. 22.109, 161.

div.head: a
div.p: A sleeping-chamber, a bed-room: πρόσθεν θαλάμοιο θυράων Il. 9.473 (app. a room built in the αὐλή and opening into the αἴθουσα near the πρόδομος; or perh. a portion of the αἴθουσα next the πρόδομος walled off). Cf. Il. 9.475: ὅθι οἱ θ. αὐλῆς δέδμητο Od. 1.425 (αὐλῆς app. local genit., in the . . . ; cf. Il. 9.473 above), ἐς θάλαμον ᾧ ἔνι κούρη κοιμᾶτο Od. 6.15. Cf. Od. 1.436, 441, Od. 2.5 = Od. 4.310, Od. 3.413, Od. 7.7, Od. 10.340, Od. 19.48.

div.head: b
div.p: A bridal chamber: γήμας ἐκ θαλάμοιο μετὰ κλέος ἵκετʼ Ἀχαιῶν (leaving his just wedded wife) Il. 11.227.

div.head: c
div.p: The sleeping-chamber occupied by a married pair: θάλαμον λιποῦσα (i.e. the bed of Menclaus) Il. 3.174. Cf. Il. 3.382, 391, 423, Il. 6.244, 248, Il. 9.582, 588, Il. 17.36: νοσφισσαμένην θάλαμόν τε πόσιν τε Od. 4.263. Cf. Od. 23.178, 192, 229, 295.
Of such a room in the palace of Zeus Il. 14.166, 188, 338.
In the palace of Hephaestus Od. 8.277.

A chamber appropriated to the lady of a house and her maidens: ὡρμᾶτʼ ἐκ θαλάμοιο Il. 3.142 (the same as the μέγαρον of 125). Cf. Il. 6.316, 321, 336: ἐξ Ἑλένη θαλάμοιο ἤλυθεν Od. 4.121. Cf. Od. 4.718, 802, Od. 17.36 = Od. 19.53, Od. 17.506.

In pl. of the women's apartments generally: νύμφας ἐκ θαλάμων ἠγίνεον Il. 18.492 (cf. Od. 22.143 cited under (4); or this may be the pl. of indefiniteness like νύμφας in this line and γάμοι and εἰλαπίναι in the prec. line) (u.l. ἐς θαλάμους, which would go under 1.b): μυχῷ θαλάμων ἥμεθα Od. 23.41.

A room for storage or safe custody, a store-room, a treasure-chamber: θύρη θαλάμοιο ἀνέρος ἀφνειοῖο Il. 24.317: χηλὸν ἐξέφερεν θαλάμοιο Od. 8.439, ἀνέβαινε ἐς θαλάμους Od. 22.143 (app. meaning a single room; cf. Il. 18.492 cited under (3)). Cf. Il. 6.288, Il. 22.63, Il. 24.191, 275: Od. 2.337, Od. 3.441, Od. 6.74, Od. 15.99, Od. 16.285, Od. 19.17, 256, Od. 21.42, Od. 22.140, 155, 157, 166, 174, 179, 180, Od. 24.166.
Distinguished in terms from the land: γαίης νέρθε καὶ θαλάσσης Il. 14.204. Cf. Il. 8.24.
From the land and the heavens Il. 18.483: Od. 12.404 = Od. 14.302.
Personified: γλαυκή σε τίκτε θ. Il. 16.34.
Sea-water: θ. κήκιε πολλή Od. 5.455. Cf. Il. 10.572.
Of or pertaining to the sea: ἔργα Il. 2.614: Od. 5.67.
In pres. pple., flourishing, luxuriant: θάμνος ἐλαίης Od. 23.191.
Of youths, lusty, in prime of vigour Od. 6.63.
Of swine: θαλέθοντες ἀλοιφῇ (swelling with fat) Il. 9.467, Il. 23.32.
Lusty, in prime of vigour: αἰζηοί Il. 3.26. Cf. Il. 4.474, Il. 6.430, Il. 8.156, 190, Il. 10.259, Il. 14.4, etc.
Of a woman, blooming, in pride of beauty: παράκοιτιν Il. 3.53.
Of marriage, app. giving the notion of the union of a pair in prime of youth Od. 6.66, Od. 20.74.
Of parts of the body, well-developed, stout: μηρώ Il. 15.113.
Of a horse's mane, long, flowing Il. 17.439.
Of the voice, full, rich Il. 17.696 = Il. 23.397: = Od. 4.705 = Od. 19.472.
In pl.: τέρπεται ἐν θαλίῃς Od. 11.603.
Green stuff, fodder: θαλλὸν ἐρίφοισι φορῆναι Od. 17.224.
Of vegetation, to grow profusely, flourish, be luxuriant: ἡμερὶς τεθήλει σταφυλῇσιν (flourished with its. . .) Od. 5.69.

div.head: a
div.p: Growing profusely, flourishing, luxuriant: ἐρινεὸς φύλλοισι τεθηλώς Od. 12.103.
Sim. of a garden, etc.: τέμενος τεθαλυῖά τʼ ἀλωή Od. 6.293.
Of autumn (the season of mellow fruitfulness) Od. 11.192.

div.head: b
div.p: Of the fat or lard of swine, rich Od. 13.410.
Sim.: συὸς ῥάχιν τεθαλυῖαν ἀλοιφῇ (rich with . . .) Il. 9.208.

div.head: d
div.p: Of a feast, sumptuous, affording good cheer Od. 11.415.
A young shoot or branch. Fig. of a youthful person Il. 22.87: Od. 6.157.
To be warm: εὖ θαλπιόων Od. 19.319.
To warm, to make flexible by the application of heat Od. 21.179, 184, 246.
Comfort, consolation, cheering: οὐκ ἄλλη ἔσται θ. Il. 6.412. Cf. Od. 1.167.
Heartening, confidence: μᾶλλον θ. ἔσται Il. 10.223.
Of a feast, sumptuous, affording good cheer Il. 7.475: Od. 3.420, Od. 8.76, 99.
Absol. in neut. pl., good cheer: θαλέων ἐμπλησάμενος κῆρ Il. 22.504.
A sacrifice of first fruits: χωσαμένη ὅ οἱ οὔ τι θ. ῥέξεν Il. 9.534.

To wonder, be struck with wonder or astonishment: θάμβησεν Ἀχιλεύς Il. 1.199. Cf. Il. 3.398, Il. 8.77, Il. 23.728 = 881, Il. 24.483, 484: θαμβήσασα βεβήκει Od. 1.360 = Od. 21.354. Cf. Od. 1.323, Od. 4.638,
Od. 10.63, Od. 24.101.
To wonder or marvel at: ὄρνιθας Od. 2.155. Cf. Od. 16.178, Od. 17.367.
Wonder, astonishment, amazement: θ. ἔχεν εἰσορόωντας Il. 3.342. Cf. Il. 4.79, Il. 23.815, Il. 24.482: Od. 3.372, Od. 24.394.
Set or standing closely together: ἔνθα θαμειαὶ εἴρυντο νέες Il. 18.68. Cf. Il. 10.264, Il. 12.296, Il. 19.383 = Il. 22.316: ἀραρὼν θαμέσι σταμίνεσσιν Od. 5.252. Cf. Od. 12.92, Od. 14.12.
coming, flying, falling, thick and fast: θαμέες ἄκοντες ἀΐσσουσιν Il. 11.552 = Il. 17.661, ὥς τε νιφάδες πίπτωσι θαμειαί Il. 12.278. Cf. Il. 12.44, 287, Il. 14.422.
Occurring at short intervals over a space, numerous: πυραὶ καίοντο θαμειαί Il. 1.52.
To come often to, frequent, an indicated place: πάρος γε μὲν οὔ τι θαμίζεις Il. 18.386 = 425: Od. 5.88.
To go about, ply one's vocation: ἅμα νηῒ θαμίζων Od. 8.161.
With pass. pple., to be accustomed to treatment of an indicated kind: οὔ τι κομιζόμενος θάμιζεν (was not wont to be (so) cared for) Od. 8.451.
A bush, shrub, small tree: θάμνῳ ὑπʼ ἀμφικόμῳ Il. 17.677. Cf. Il. 11.156, Il. 22.191: δοιοὺς ὑπήλυθε θάμνους Od. 5.476, θάμνος ἐλαίης (consisting of . . .) Od. 23.190. Cf. Od. 22.469
In pl., a thicket: θάμνων ὑπεδύσετο Od. 6.127. Cf. Od. 5.471, Od. 7.285.
To one's death: ὡς εἰ θ. κιόντα Il. 24.328. Cf. Il. 16.693, Il. 22.297.
Personified: Ὕπνῳ κασιγνήτῳ Θανάτοιο Il. 14.231. Cf. Il. 16.454, 672 = 682.
A kind or mode of death: λευγαλέῳ θανάτῳ ἁλῶναι Il. 21.281: = Od. 5.312, πάντες στυγεροὶ θάνατοί [εἰσιν] Od. 12.341. Cf. Od. 11.412, Od. 15.359, Od. 18.202, Od. 22.462, Od. 24.34.
To admire, look at with admiration Od. 18.191.
To suck (the breast): γυναῖκα θήσατο μαζόν (double acc. of whole and part, a woman's breast) Il. 24.58.
To suck (milk): παρέχουσι γάλα θῆσθαι (for their young to suck) Od. 4.89.
To pay funeral rites to (a corpse): ὁπότʼ Ἀμαρυγκέα θάπτον Ἐπειοί Il. 23.630. Cf. Il. 21.323, Il. 23.71, Il. 24.612, 665: οὔ πω ἐτέθαπτο Od. 11.52. Cf. Od. 3.285, Od. 12.12, Od. 24.417.
Bold, stout, courageous, spirited, confident: πολεμιστήν Il. 5.602 = Il. 16.493 = Il. 22.269. Cf. Il. 19.169, Il. 21.430, 589: Od. 7.51.
Neut. comp. θαρσαλεώτερον in impers. construction: θ. ἔσται (one would feel more confidence, have better heart) Il. 10.223.
Over-bold, audacious, presuming: θαρσαλέος τις προΐκτης Od. 17.449. Cf. Od. 19.91.
Boldly, confidently: ἀγόρευεν Od. 1.382 = Od. 18.411 = Od. 20.269. Cf. Od. 1.385.
Too boldly or confidently: ἀγορεύεις Od. 18.330 = 390.
To be of good heart or courage, of good cheer: θαρσῶν μάχεσθαι Il. 5.124, τεθαρσήκασι λαοί (are (now) of good heart) Il. 9.420 = 687.
In aor., to take heart, pluck up courage: θαρσήσας εἰπέ Il. 1.85. Cf. Il. 1.92, Il. 20.338: Od. 3.76, 252.
Boldness, courage, spirit, confidence: σῷ θάρσει Il. 6.126. Cf. Il. 5.2, Il. 7.153, Il. 17.570, 573, Il. 21.547: Od. 1.321, Od. 3.76, Od. 6.140, Od. 9.381, Od. 14.216.
Excessive boldness or confidence: θ. ἄητον ἔχουσα Il. 21.395.
Having plucked up courage: Τρώων πόλις ἐπὶ πᾶσα βέβηκεν θ. Il. 16.70.
Taking courage: θ. οἰωνῷ (from the . . .) Il. 13.823.

To encourage, hearten, cheer, put spirit into: τοὺς θάρσυνε μύθῳ Il. 10.190. Cf. Il. 4.233, Il. 13.767 = Il. 17.117 = 683, Il. 16.242, Il. 18.325, Il. 23.682: Od. 3.361, Od. 9.377, Od. 13.323, Od. 16.448, Od. 24.448.
[for θακίων. Comp. of ταχύς with transference of aspirate.]
Swifter: ποσὶν θ. (with the feet, in running) Il. 15.570. Cf. Il. 13.819.

div.head: a
div.p: The quicker, the speedier, the sooner: ὄφρα κε θ. ἐγείρομεν Ἄρηα Il. 2.440. Cf. Il. 6.143 = Il. 20.429, Il. 12.26, Il. 23.53: Od. 2.307, Od. 10.33.

div.head: b
div.p: Quickly rather than slowly, quickly, with speed: θ. Ἀθηναίῃ ἐπιτεῖλαι Il. 4.64. Cf. Il. 13.115, Il. 16.129, Il. 17.654, Il. 19.68, Il. 20.257: ἔρρʼ ἐκ νήσου θ. Od. 10.72. Cf. Od. 7.152, Od. 10.44, 192, 228, 268, Od. 15.201, Od. 16.130, Od. 20.154, Od. 24.495.
Wonder, amazement: θ. μʼ ἔχει Od. 10.326.

A wonder or marvel: θ. ἰδέσθαι (to behold) Il. 5.725, Il. 10.439, Il. 18.83, 377, μέγα θ. τόδʼ ὁρῶμαι (this is a great wonder that I see) Il. 13.99 = Il. 15.286 = Il. 20.344 = Il. 21.54. Cf. Il. 18.549: Od. 6.306, Od. 7.45, Od. 8.366, Od. 9.190, Od. 11.287, Od. 13.108, Od. 17.306, Od. 19.36.
3 sing. fut. in mid. form θαυμάσσεται Il. 18.467.

To wonder, marvel, to feel or be struck with wonder, astonishment or admiration: γυναῖκες ἱστάμεναι θαύμαζον Il. 18.496. Cf. Il. 24.394: θαύμαζεν ὁ γεραιός Od. 3.373. Cf. Od. 4.44, Od. 7.145, Od. 8.265, Od. 13.157, Od. 16.203.
With dependent clause: θαυμάζομεν οἷον ἐτύχθη Il. 2.320.

To wonder or marvel at, look upon with wonder or eager curiousity: πτόλεμόν τε μάχην τε Il. 13.11. Cf. Il. 10.12, Il. 18.467: λιμένας καὶ νῆας Od. 7.43. Cf. Od. 1.382 = Od. 18.411 = Od. 20.269, Od. 4.655, Od. 9.153, Od. 19.229, Od. 24.370.
With infin.: οἷον θαυμάζομεν (impf.) Ἕκτορα αἰχμητὴν ἔμεναι (thinking that he was . . .) Il. 5.601.
To look upon or behold (a person) with respectful wonder and admiration: Πρίαμος θαύμαζʼ Ἀχιλῆα Il. 24.629. Cf. Il. 24.631: Od. 8.459.

Nom. pl. masc. fut. pple.
θαυμανέοντες.
To witness or watch with eager interest: ἀέθλια θαυμανέοντες Od. 8.108.
Dat. pl. θεῇσι Il. 8.305. Il. 11.638, Il. 19.286: Od. 7.291. θεῇς Il. 3.158. θεαῖς Od. 5.119.

A female divine (or semi-divine) being, a goddess: εἰ θεά σε γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 1.280 (Thetis). Cf. Il. 1.1, Il. 2.182, Il. 3.396, Il. 8.305, Il. 18.429, etc.: καλυψώ, δῖα θεάων Od. 1.14, θεά οἱ ἔκλυεν ἀρῆς Od. 4.767 (Athene). Cf. Od. 2.392, Od. 5.215, Od. 10.222, Od. 12.131, Od. 20.393, etc.
A goddess as distinguished in terms from a god: εἰρωτᾷς με θεὰ θεόν Od. 5.97. Cf. Il. 10.50.
From a woman: θεᾶς οὐδὲ γυναικός Il. 14.315.
With the name of a particular goddess.
With Ἥρη Il. 1.55, Il. 5.711, Il. 8.350, etc.
With Θέτις Il. 9.410, Il. 15.76, Il. 18.127, etc.
A goddess as distinguished from a god: πάντες τε θεοὶ πᾶσαί τε θέαιναι Il. 8.5 = Il. 19.101, Il. 8.20. Cf. Od. 8.341.
In reference to the sulphurous smell associated with a thunderbolt: δεινὴ θεείου γίγνεται ὀδμή Il. 14.415. Cf. Il. 8.135: Od. 12.417, Od. 14.307.
Used for cleansing by fumigation: ἐκάθηρε θεείῳ Il. 16.228. Cf. Od. 22.481, 493.
To cleanse with the fumes of sulphur Od. 22.482.
[app. θείλη = εἵλη, the sun's warmth + πέδον, the ground.]
A warm spot in a vineyard in which the grapes were left to be dried by the sun, a sun-trap Od. 7.123.
3 sing. aor. ἔθεινε Il. 21.491. θεῖνε Il. 16.339.
To strike, smite: μή σε ἴδωμαι θεινομένην Il. 1.588. Cf. Il. 6.135, Il. 10.484, Il. 16.339, Il. 17.430, Il. 20.481, Il. 21.21, 491: ὅς κέ σε θείνῃ Od. 18.63. Cf. Od. 9.459, Od. 22.443.
Partaking of the nature of the gods, divine, immortal: θείοιο γέροντος (Proteus) Od. 4.395.
Consisting of gods: ἀγῶνα (see ἀγών 1.a) Il. 7.298, Il. 18.376.
Connected with the gods, sacred: ἁλός Il. 9.214 (perh. as used for purifying sacrifices): χορόν Od. 8.264 (app. from the dance being regarded as a matter of ritual).
Of divine origin, from a divine source, divine: Ὄνειρος Il. 2.22, 56, ὀμφή Il. 2.41, γένος Il. 6.180, πύργου Il. 21.526 (app. as god-built; see 446 and cf. Il. 7.452, Il. 8.519): ὄνειρος Od. 14.495.

Applied to persons of divine descent: Ἴλου Il. 10.415 (he was descended from Zeus; see Il. 20.215-232), Ἡρακλῆος Il. 15.25, Il. 20.145, ἀνδρὸς θείοιο Ἀχιλλῆος Il. 16.798, Πηλεΐδαο Il. 17.199, Ἀχιλλῆος Il. 19.279, 297: Ἐνιπῆος Od. 11.238 (since all rivers spring from Zeus).
Applied to kings as holding their office from Zeus Od. 4.621, 691, Od. 16.335.
To heralds as under his special protection Il. 4.192, Il. 10.315.
Applied as a mere epithet of honour to Odysseus Il. 2.335, Il. 9.218, Il. 10.243, Il. 11.806: Od. 1.65, Od. 2.233, 259, Od. 3.398, Od. 4.682, etc.
Denoting a superlative degree of excellence or beauty: ποτόν Od. 2.341, Od. 9.205, δόμον Od. 4.43.
3 sing. pa. iterative θέλγεσκε Od. 3.264. 3 fut. θέλξει Od. 16.298.
To work upon by spells or enchantment, bewithch, charm Il. 24.343: = Od. 5.47, Od. 10.291, 318, 326, Od. 24.3.
Sim. of the operation of passion: ἔρῳ θυμὸν ἔθελχθεν Od. 18.212.
Of divine interference, to lay a spell upon, bind up from activity: Ἀχαιῶν νόον Il. 12.255. Cf. Il. 13.435, Il. 15.322, 594: Od. 16.298.
To work upon by wiles, cajole, lead on to one's hurt, prejudice, or dishonour: Ἀγαμεμνονέην ἄλοχον Od. 3.264. Cf. Od. 1.57, Od. 12.40, 44, Od. 18.282.
To beguile, deceive, cheat: δόλῳ [μιν] ἔθελγεν Il. 21.604. Cf. Il. 21.276: Od. 14.387, Od. 16.195.
In mid.: οἶα μυθεῖται, θέλγοιτό κέ τοι ἦτορ Od. 17.514.
A means of enchantment, a spell Il. 14.215.
A means of propitiating or placating: θεῶν θελκτήριον Od. 8.509.
Something that charms or delights Od. 1.337.
The root or bed (of the eye) Il. 14.493.
The lower part (of the throat) Il. 17.47.
Supports, consisting of stakes or stones, set to contain the face of an earthwork or mound (cf. στήλη 1) Il. 12.28, Il. 23.255.
In pl., a body of traditionary rules or precedents: βασιλεύς, ᾧ δῶκε κρόνου πάϊς θέμιστας Il. 2.206. Cf. Il. 1.238, Il. 9.99: Od. 9.112, 215 (see δίκη 2).
In sing.: ὃς οὔ τινα οἶδε θέμιστα Il. 5.761 (has no regard for any usage of decency; see εἴδω III.12).

What is established or sanctioned by custom or usage: ἣ θ. ἐστίν Il. 2.73 (as is my right), Il. 9.33 (do.), Il. 23.581 (as usage requires), Il. 24.652 (as the custom is), ἣ θ. ἀνθρώπων πέλει (as is the way of . . .) Il. 9.134, ἣ θ. ἐστὶν ἤ τʼ ἀνδρῶν ἤ τε γυναικῶν (as is the way of . . .) 276 = Il. 19.177, ξείνια παρέθηκεν, ἅ τε ξείνοις θ. ἐστίν (which by the customs of hospitality one . . .) Il. 11.779, ἄορ ἔχων: τῷ δʼ οὐ θ. ἐστὶ μιγῆναι (mortal must not encounter it) Il. 14.386, πάρος γʼ οὐ θ. ἦεν . . . (it was not permitted . . .) Il. 16.796, οὐ θ. ἐστὶ . . . (it must not be that . . .) Il. 23.44: ἣ θ. ἐστίν Od. 3.45 (as the custom is), 187 (as is your due), Od. 11.451 (as it is his privilege to do), ἥ τε ξείνων θ. ἐστίν (as . . . use to do) Od. 9.268, οὔ μοι θ. ἐστὶ . . . (I may not . . .) Od. 10.73, Od. 14.56, ἣ θ. ἐστὶ γυναικός (as a woman's way ever is) 130, ἐπεί μοι
. . . θ. ἐστίν (since it is my right to . . .) Od. 16.91, ἡ γὰρ θ. ὅς τις . . . (for that is due to him who . . .) Od. 24.286.
An oracular reply (in answer to an inquiry as to what is right to be done) Od. 16.403.
As proper name, a goddess with such funtions as may be gathered from the name and the context Il. 15.87, 93, Il. 20.4: Od. 2.68.
To pronounce judgments, act as judge Od. 11.569.
With genit. (like ἀνάσσω 3.a), to rule over, be master of: παίδων Od. 9.114.
To drive or carry in a specified direction: νῆα χέρσον ἱκέσθαι Od. 9.486, 542.
App., the palm of the hand Il. 5.339.
nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. τίθημι.
God - built: πύργων Il. 8.519 (cf. Il. 21.526 cited under θεῖος 4).
Epithet of persons Il. 1.131 = Il. 19.155: Od. 3.416, Od. 4.276, Od. 8.256.
From, at the hands of, the gods: θ. οὐκ ἔστʼ ἀλέασθαι [θάνατον] Od. 16.447.
To reveal the divine will Il. 1.109, Il. 2.322: Od. 2.184.
A disclosure of the divine will, the divine will as disclosed to a seer: οὐ θεοπροπίης ἐμπάζομαι Il. 16.50. Cf. Il. 11.794, Il. 16.36: Od. 1.415, Od. 2.201.
= θεοπροπίη.: εἰπὲ θεοπρόπιον ὅ τι οἶσθα Il. 1.85.
[app., one who prays to a god, fr. θεός + προπ-, perh. conn. with L. precor.]
One who reveals the divine will, a seer Il. 12.228: Od. 1.416.
With a word expressing likeness Il. 7.366, Il. 14.318, Il. 17.477: Od. 3.110, 409.
This form as ablative Il. 17.101, Il. 23.347.
A god as distinguished in terms from a goddess: εἰρωτᾷς με θεὰ θεόν Od. 5.97. Cf. Il. 10.50.
From a mortal: ἠμὲν θεὸν ἠδὲ καὶ ἄνδρα Il. 5.128. Cf. Il. 19.417, Il. 22.9, Il. 24.259, etc.: Od. 4.397, 654, etc.

Without reference to any particular god, the divine power, heaven: θεός που σοὶ τό γʼ ἔδωκεν Il. 1.178. Cf. Il. 2.436, Il. 6.228, Il. 7.4, Il. 9.49, Il. 17.327, Il. 21.47, etc.: οὐκ ἄνευ θεοῦ Od. 2.372. Cf. Od. 3.131, Od. 8.170, Od. 9.158. Od. 11.292, Od. 17.399, Od. 18.265, etc.
A goddess as distinguished in terms from a woman: ἢ θεὸς ἠὲ γυνή Od. 10.228, 255.

In pl., the gods: τίς θεῶν; Il. 1.8, θεοί μοι αἴτιοί εἰσιν Il. 3.164. Cf. Il. 1.18, Il. 2.321, Il. 4.1, Il. 6.138, Il. 7.360, Il. 9.485, Il. 12.8, etc.: Od. 1.17, Od. 2.66, Od. 4.379, Od. 5.335, Od. 7.132, Od. 11.276, Od. 12.394, etc.
In pl., the gods as distinguished in terms from the goddesses: πάντες τε θεοὶ πᾶσαί τε θέαιναι Il. 8.5 = Il. 19.101, Il. 8.20. Cf. Od. 8.341.
From mortals: πρός τε θεῶν πρός τʼ ἀνθρώπων Il. 1.339. Cf. Il. 1.403, Il. 9.239, Il. 14.233, Il. 21.264, etc.: Od. 1.338, Od. 2.211, Od. 16.265, Od. 24.64, etc.
God-fearing, reverencing the gods Od. 6.121 = Od. 9.176 = Od. 13.202, Od. 8.576, Od. 19.109, 364.

A follower, retainer or henchman: θεράποντες ἀπʼ ὤμων τεύχεʼ ἕλοντο Il. 7.122. Cf. Il. 1.321, Il. 5.48, Il. 6.53, Il. 11.843, Il. 13.600, Il. 15.401, Il. 16.272 = Il. 17.165, Il. 19.143, 281, Il. 24.396, 406, 573: ἴσθμιον ἤνεικεν θ. Od. 18.300. Cf. Od. 1.109, Od. 4.23 = 217, Od. 4.38, 784, Od. 16.253, 326 = 360, Od. 18.297, 424.
Fig. of warriors: θεράποντες Ἄρηος Il. 2.110 = Il. 6.67 = Il. 15.733 = Il. 19.78. Cf. Il. 7.382, Il. 8.79, Il. 10.228, Il. 19.47.

A warrior in honourable personal attendance on another, the relation of the two resembling generally that of squire and knight: ἠῢς θ. Ἀχιλῆος (Patroclus) Il. 16.653. Cf. Il. 7.149, Il. 11.322, 620, Il. 13.246, 331, Il. 15.431, Il. 16.165 = Il. 17.388, Il. 16.244, 279, 464, 865, Il. 17.164, 271, Il. 18.152, Il. 23.90, 113 = 124, 528, 860 = 888.
Applied to a warrior's ἡνίοχος: ἵππους θ. ἀπάνευθʼ ἔχεν Il. 4.227, ἡνίοχον θεράποντα Il. 5.580. Cf. Il. 6.18, Il. 8.104, 109, 113, 119, Il. 11.341, 488, Il. 12.76, 111, Il. 13.386, Il. 20.487.
3 sing. aor. mid. θέρμετο Il. 18.348, Il. 23.381: Od. 8.437.
In mid., to become warm or hot: θέρμετο δʼ ὕδωρ Il. 18.348: = Od. 8.437. Cf. Il. 23.381.
Genit. θέρευς Od. 7.118. Summer: θέρεϊ (in summer) Il. 22.151: χείματος οὐδὲ θέρευς (in winter or summer) Od. 7.118.
As distinguished from ὀπώρη, early summerOd. 11.192, Od. 12.76, Od. 14.384.
In mid., to warm oneself: φόως ἔμεν ἠδὲ θέρεσθαι Od. 19.64. Cf. Od. 19.507.
In pass., to be warmed: ἐπεί κε πυρὸς θερέω (genit. of material) Od. 17.23.
To be burnt: μὴ ἄστυ πυρὸς θέρηται Il. 6.331. Cf. Il. 11.667.
[the first element seems to be the same as in θέσ-φατος.]
App., marvellous, wondrous, or the like: ἔργα Il. 3.130: Od. 11.374, 610.–
So in neut. θέσκελον as adv., marvellously, in wondrous wise: ἔϊκτο θέσκελον αὐτῷ Il. 23.107.
Absol. in fem., sentence pronounced by a god, the will of heaven: εἰ καὶ θεσπεσίῃ πόλιν οὐκ ἀλαπάξεις Il. 2.367.
Of song, befitting a god, divinely sweet Il. 2.600.
Of singers, heavenly sweet of voice: σειρήνων Od. 12.158.

div.head: a
div.p: Of shouting or lamentation, such as might come from a god's throat, immense, deafening: ἠχῇ Il. 8.159 = Il. 15.590, Il. 12.252, Il. 13.834, Il. 15.355. Cf. Il. 16.295, Il. 18.149: βοή Od. 24.49. Cf. Od. 3.150, Od. 11.43, 633.

div.head: b
div.p: Of inarticulate sounds. Of the sound of branches of trees smiting each other Il. 16.769.
Of that of rushing winds Il. 13.797, Il. 23.213.

p.gloss: The force of the second element lost

div.head: a
div.p: Of or pertaining to the gods, divine: βηλοῦ Il. 1.591.

div.head: b
div.p: Indicating a high degree of some quality such as abundance, greatness, greatness of extent, completeness, swiftness, beauty, sweetness or the like: πλοῦτον Il. 2.670. Cf. Il. 2.457, Il. 9.2, Il. 15.669, Il. 17.118, Il. 20.342: ὀδμή Od. 9.211. Cf. Od. 2.12 = Od. 17.63, Od. 7.42, Od. 8.19, Od. 9.68 = Od. 12.314, Od. 9.434, Od. 13.363, Od. 20.289, Od. 24.6.
= θεσπέσιος. 4.b: θ. ἐφόβηθεν (in panic rout) Il. 15.637.
[θε-σπ- as in θεσπέσιον (with the force of the second element lost) + δα(ϝ)-, δαίω1.]
Epithet of fire, defying human efforts, devouring, consuming Il. 12.177, 441, Il. 15.597, Il. 20.490, Il. 21.342, 381, Il. 23.216: Od. 4.418.
[the second element φα-, φημί. The first explained as θεσ-, θεός.]
Pronounced or ordained by a god or by the divine will. Neut. in impers. construction: ὡς γὰρ θέσφατόν ἐστιν Il. 8.477.
With infin.: θανέειν Od. 4.561. Cf. Od. 10.473.
Absol. in neut. pl. θέσφατα, divine ordinances or decrees: οὔ τι θεῶν ἐκ θ. ᾔδη Il. 5.64. Cf. Od. 9.507 = Od. 13.172, Od. 11.151, 297, Od. 12.155.
[prob. for θή(ϝ)ω, fr. θηϝ-, long form of θεϝ-.]
2 sing. fut. in mid. form θεύσεαι Il. 23.623.

Of men, horses, etc., to run, speed: θέεις ἀκίχητα διώκων Il. 17.75, ἵπποι βάρδιστοι θείειν Il. 23.310. Cf. Il. 2.183, Il. 4.244, Il. 6.54, Il. 15.442, Il. 19.415, Il. 23.387, etc.: Od. 3.112, 370, Od. 4.202, Od. 8.123, 247, Od. 14.501, Od. 17.308, Od. 22.99, 106.
To run a race, contend in a race Il. 11.701, Il. 23.623.
Of the motion of a ship: νηῦς ἔθεεν κατὰ κῦμα Il. 1.483: = Od. 2.429. Cf. Od. 3.281, Od. 12.407, Od. 13.86, 88, Od. 14.299, Od. 15.294.
Of a person in a ship: ὅτε κεῖνος ἐν νηυσὶ Μαλειάων ὄρος ἷξε θέων Od. 3.288.
Of things, to run or extend: ἄντυξ ἣ πυμάτη θέεν ἀσπίδος Il. 6.118. Cf. Il. 6.320 = Il. 8.495, Il. 13.547, Il. 20.275: περὶ κλίσιον θέε πάντῃ Od. 24.208.
Holy as distinguished from common: [θύραι] Od. 13.111.
3 sing. aor. imp. mid. θηξάσθω Il. 2.382.
Of a boar whetting his tusks Il. 11.416, Il. 13.475.
3 sing. impf. θηεῖτο Od. 5.75, Od. 6.237, Od. 7.133, Od. 8.265.
3 pl. ἐθηήσαντο Od. 19.235. θηήσαντο Il. 15.682, Il. 22.370: Od. 8.17, Od. 10.180.

To look or gaze upon, view, behold, with interest, curiosity, wonder, admiration: πολέες ἑ θηήσαντο Il. 15.682. Cf. Il. 7.444, Il. 10.524, Il. 22.370: μαρμαρυγὰς ποδῶν Od. 8.265. Cf. Od. 2.13 = Od. 17.64, Od. 5.76 = Od. 7.134, Od. 9.218, Od. 10.180, Od. 15.132, Od. 19.235.
To look about one with wonder or admiration: στὰς θηεῖτο Od. 5.75, Od. 7.133.
To look upon something with wonder, to wonder, marvel, be astonished: λαοὶ θηεῦντο Il. 23.728 = 881: θηεῖτο κούρη Od. 6.237. Cf. Od. 5.74, Od. 8.17, Od. 17.315, Od. 24.90.
With dependent clause: θηοῖό κεν οἷον . . . Il. 24.418.
Also in regular fem. form θήλεια Il. 2.767, Il. 8.7, Il. 11.681, Il. 20.222: Od. 4.636, Od. 9.439, Od. 14.16, Od. 21.23.
Comp. θηλυτέρη, female as opposed to male: θεαί Od. 8.324, γυναικῶν Od. 11.386. Cf. Il. 8.520: Od. 11.434 = Od. 15.422 = Od. 24.202, Od. 23.166.
Characteristic of women, feminine: θῆλυς ἀϋτή Od. 6.122.
Of dew, copious: θῆλυς ἐέρση Od. 5.467.
Enclitic affirmative particle: οὔ θην δηρὸν βέῃ Il. 16.852. Cf. Il. 9.394, Il. 11.365 = Il. 20.452, Il. 15.288, Il. 17.29, Il. 21.568: Od. 3.352, Od. 16.91.
With mocking or ironical force: οὔ θήν μιν ἀνήσει θυμὸς νεικείειν Il. 2.276. Cf. Il. 8.448, Il. 10.104, Il. 13.620, 813, Il. 14.480: οὐ μέν θην κείνης γε χερείων εὔχομαι εἶναι Od. 5.211.
Dat. pl. θήρεσσι Od. 5.473, Od. 14.21. θηρσί Od. 24.292.
With κύων, a hunting dog: ἐν κυσὶ θηρευτῇσιν Il. 11.325.
To hunt, engage in hunting: ὥς μιν θηρεύοντʼ ἔλασεν σῦς Od. 19.465.
Hunting, the chase: αἵμονα θήρης Il. 5.49. Cf. Il. 10.360: Od. 19.429.
The quarry: ἔδωκε θεὸς μενοεικέα θήρην Od. 9.158.

Of a bird of
prey: αἰετοῦ, τοῦ θηρητῆρος Il. 21.252. Cf. Il. 24.316.
Of despoilers of a wasps' nest Il. 12.170.
[prob. θήρ + suffix distinguishing an individual from a class.]
A wild beast: μάλα μέγα θηρίον ἦεν Od. 10.171, 180.
To serve as a hired labourer: θητεύσαμεν μισθῷ ἔπι ῥητῷ Il. 21.444. Cf. Od. 11.489, Od. 18.357.
The beach or shore of the sea: ἐπὶ θινί Od. 2.408. Cf. Od. 7.290, Od. 9.46, 551.
App., a piece of the shore covered by shallow water: ὡς ὅτʼ ἀναπάλλεται ἰχθὺς θίνʼ ἐν φυκιόεντι Il. 23.693.
3 sing. aor. ἔθλασε Od. 18.97. θλάσσε Il. 5.307, Il. 12.384.
To smash, crush: κοτύλην Il. 5.307, κυνέην Il. 12.384, ὀστέα Od. 18.97.
To press or rub: πολλῇς φλιῇσι θλίψεται ὤμους Od. 17.221.
Fut. infin. in mid. form θανέεσθαι Il. 4.12, Il. 15.728: Od. 20.21.
Infin. τεθνάμεναι Il. 24.225. τεθνάμεν Il. 15.497, Il. 17.405, Il. 19.335: Od. 16.107, Od. 20.317, Od. 21.155. (ἀπο-, ἐκ-, κατα-.)
In a quasi- passive sense of being slain in battle: χερσὶν ὑπʼ Αἴαντος θανέειν Il. 15.289. Cf. Il. 1.243, Il. 22.426.

div.head: a
div.p: In strict aor. sense: αἶψʼ ἔθανεν Εὔρυτος Od. 8.226. Cf. Od. 3.248, Od. 9.66, Od. 11.389 = Od. 24.22, Od. 11.412, Od. 24.37.
In pple.: ἀνδρὸς τῆλε θανόντος (that met his death . . .) Od. 17.312, θανὼν φθιμένοισι μετείην (may I die and . . .) Od. 24.436.

div.head: b
div.p: To have died, be dead: θάνε Μελέαγρος Il. 2.642. Cf. Il. 12.13, Il. 21.610, Il. 22.486: ἐπεὶ θάνʼ Ὀδυσσεύς Od. 1.396, Od. 2.96 = Od. 19.141 = Od. 24.131. Cf. Od. 15.253.

In pple.: ὄφρα πυρός με λελάχωσι θανόντα (in death) Il. 7.80 = Il. 22.343, περὶ πατρόκλοιο θανόντος (the dead . . .) Il. 8.476, Il. 17.120, 182, Il. 18.195, μενοιτιάδαο θανόντος ἄχεος (for the death of . . .) Il. 17.538, οὔ μευ ζώοντος . . ., ἀλλὰ θανόντος (now that I am dead) Il. 23.70. Cf. Il. 11.453, Il. 15.350, Il. 17.379, 564, Il. 21.28, Il. 22.73, Il. 23.223, Il. 24.16, 575: οὔ κε θανόντι περ ὧδʼ ἀκαχοίμην (if he were dead) Od. 1.236, ζωὸς ἠὲ θανών (alive or dead) Od. 4.553, μή τι θανὼν ἀκαχίζευ (let not thy death grieve thee) Od. 11.486. Cf. Od. 3.258, Od. 5.310, Od. 11.554, Od. 17.115, Od. 24.77, 79, 93.
Absol. in pl. pple., the dead: γέρας θανόντων Il. 16.457 = 675, Il. 23.9: Od. 24.190, 296. Cf. Il. 22.389.

div.head: a
div.p: To be dead: τεθναίη (let him lie dead) Il. 3.102, πολλοὶ τεθνᾶσιν Il. 7.328, οὔ ποτε ἔλπετο τεθνάμεν (that the was dead) Il. 17.405. Cf. Il. 6.164, Il. 15.496, 497, Il. 18.12, 98, Il. 19.335, Il. 22.52, 365, Il. 24.225: ζώει ὅ γʼ ἦ τέθνηκεν Od. 2.132, Od. 4.110, 837 = Od. 11.464. Cf. Od. 4.199, 834 = Od. 24.264, Od. 11.304, Od. 15.350, Od. 16.107, Od. 20.208, 317, Od. 21.155.

div.head: b
div.p: In strict pf. sense: οὔ πω τέθνηκεν Ὀδυσσεύς (Ὀρέστης) Od. 1.196, Od. 11.461.
Absol., a mortal man, a man: ἕνεκα θνητῶν Il. 1.574, τί δόμεν πηλῆϊ θνητῷ; (to Peleus, to a mortal) Il. 17.444. Cf. Il. 12.242, Il. 17.547, Il. 20.64: Od. 19.593.
To entertain at table: ἐς αὐτοὺς προτέρω ἄγε θοινηθῆναι Od. 4.36.
A building, app. of no great size, within the αὐλή, of unknown nature and useOd. 22.442 = 459, 466.
Quick in movement, nimble, swift, fleet: θοός περ ἐὼν πολεμιστής Il. 5.571. Cf. Il. 5.536, Il. 12.306, Il. 15.585, Il. 16.422, 494.

div.head: c
div.p: Of night (app. thought of as a body of darkness passing swiftly over the earth) Il. 10.394, 468, Il. 12.463, Il. 14.261, Il. 24.366 = 653: Od. 12.284.

div.head: e
div.p: Of a whip, quickly making itself felt Il. 17.430.

div.head: f
div.p: Of a meal, perh., deftly served Od. 8.38.

νήσοισιν ἐπιπροέηκε θοῇσιν Od. 15.299.
Doubtfully explained (cf. θοόω) as the sharp or pointed islands, supposed to form part of the group called the Echinades.
[poss. conn. with θοός and meaning orig. to make quick or active, acquiring the sense of sharpening when applied to weapons, etc..]
To sharpen, put a point upon: ἐθόωσα
and in fem. form θοῦρις, -ιδος, with acc. -ιν

p.gloss: Rushing, impetuous, eager for the fray.

div.p: Of a shield, app. by transference of epithet from the bearer to the shield: ἀσπίδα θοῦριν Il. 11.32, Il. 20.162.
Boldness, courage: οὐκ ἔχει θράσος ὅς κεν ἴδηται Il. 14.416.
Of bold spirit, stout of heart Il. 5.639: Od. 11.267.
Of other heroes Il. 8.128, Il. 16.604: Od. 10.436.
Epithet of war, carried on with spirit, strenous Il. 6.254, Il. 10.28: Od. 4.146.
Recompense for rearing due by a child to his parents: οὐδὲ τοκεῦσι θ. ἀπέδωκεν Il. 4.478 = Il. 17.302.
To sing a dirge, wail Il. 24.722: Od. 24.61.
A funeral-song, a dirge: θρήνων ἐξάρχους Il. 24.721.
Prob. a plank or gangway connecting the forward and after ἴκρια of a ship: ἀνεχάζετο θρῆνυν ἐφʼ ἑπταπόδην, λίπε δʼ ἴκρια Il. 15.729.
An uppermost course in a wall, a coping Od. 17.267.
A frieze running along the upper part of the inner walls of a house Od. 7.87.
To finish off the upper part of the wall of (an enclosure) with something intended to give protection or to prevent exit: ἐθρίγκωσεν [αὐλὴν] ἀχέρδῳ Od. 14.10.
The hair of the head: πολιὰς τρίχας Il. 22.77. Cf. Il. 23.135 (locks of hair): Od. 13.399, 431, Od. 18.355.
The hair on the limbs: ὀρθαὶ τρίχες ἔσταν ἐνὶ μέλεσσιν Il. 24.359.
The hairs of the mane of a horse Il. 8.83.
The hairs of a horse's tail Il. 23.519.
The hair on the head of an ox Od. 3.446.
Of the wool of sheep Il. 3.273.
Of the bristles of swine Il. 19.254: Od. 10.239, 393, Od. 14.422.
Figures or designs in woven work: ἐν θρόνα ἔπασσεν (i.e. in the web) Il. 22.441.

A seat or chair: καθέζετʼ ἐπὶ θρόνου Il. 1.536. Cf. Il. 8.199, 442, Il. 11.645, Il. 14.238, Il. 15.124, 142, 150, Il. 18.389, 422, Il. 20.62, Il. 24.515, 522, 553: κατὰ κλισμούς τε θρόνους τε (the two words hardly to be distinguished) Od. 1.145. Cf. Od. 1.130, Od. 4.51, Od. 5.86, Od. 6.308, Od. 8.65, Od. 17.32, Od. 20.96, Od. 22.23, etc.
To crush, bruise: θρυλίχθη μέτωπον Il. 23.396.
(ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, ἐσ-, προ-, ὑπερ-.)

To leap, spring, bound, dart: κὰδ δʼ ἔθορʼ ἐς μέσσον Il. 4.79. Cf. Il. 5.161, Il. 8.252 = Il. 14.441, Il. 8.320 = Il. 23.509, Il. 10.528, Il. 11.70 = Il. 17.770, Il. 15.380, 573, 580, 582, 684, Il. 20.381, Il. 21.126: ἀπὸ λέκτροιο θοροῦσα Od. 23.32. Cf. Od. 22.303.
Of inanimate objects: ἐκ δʼ ἔθορε κλῆρος κυνέης Il. 7.182. Cf. Il. 13.589, Il. 15.314, 470, Il. 16.773, Il. 23.353: Od. 10.207.
Only in phrase ἐπὶ θρωσμῷ πεδίοιο, a piece of ground rising from, and somewhat above the general level of, the plainIl. 10.160, Il. 11.56 = Il. 20.3.
Genit. θυγατέρος Il. 21.504: Od. 19.400. θυγατρός Od. 4.4, Od. 7.290, Od. 11.421.
Dat. θυγατέρι Od. 10.106, Od. 15.364. θυγατρί Il. 9.148, 290.
Acc. θυγατέρας Od. 10.7. θύγατρας Il. 22.62: Od. 11.329, Od. 22.222.

A rushing or violent wind or storm: φλογὶ ἶσοι ἠὲ θυέλλῃ Il. 13.39. Cf. Il. 6.346, Il. 12.253, Il. 15.26, Il. 21.335: ἀναρπάξασά μιν θ. θέρεν Od. 4.515, Od. 23.316. Cf. Od. 4.727, Od. 5.317, 419, Od. 6.171, Od. 7.275, Od. 10.48, 54, Od. 12.288, 409, Od. 20.63, 66.
Of a dust-storm: κονίη ἵσταθʼ ὥς τε νέφος ἠὲ θ. Il. 23.366.
App. of volcanic fire: πυρὸς ὀλοοῖο θύελλαι Od. 12.68.
Fragrant with the savour of sacrifice: βωμός Il. 8.48, Il. 23.148: Od. 8.363.
App., firstlings of meat given to the gods: ἐν πυρὶ βάλλε θυηλάς Il. 9.220.
Paining or burdening the heart, painful, distressing, grievous Il. 4.513, Il. 9.260, 387, 565: Od. 8.272, Od. 16.69, Od. 18.347 = Od. 20.285, Od. 20.118, Od. 22.189, Od. 23.64, 183, Od. 24.326.
[θυμός + ἀρ-, ἀραρίσκω. Fitted to the heart.]
Such as to inspire affection, lovely, beauteous: ἄλοχον Il. 9.336: Od. 23.232.
Suited to one's taste, grateful to the senses: [ὕδωρ] θυμῆρες κεράσασα (till it became. . .) Od. 10.362.
Suited to one's needs, serviceable: σκῆπρον Od. 17.199.
Endeavouring to rally one's spirit, making a fight for life: ἐκ δʼ ἔπεσον θυμηγερέων Od. 7.283.
Pleasing to the heart, desirable, choice: χρήματα Od. 16.389.

p.gloss: Eating the heart, that will not leave the heart in peace.

div.p: Biting the heart, stinging to action: μῦθος Od. 8.185.
Life-destroying: θάνατος Il. 13.544, Il. 16.414 = 580. Cf. Il. 16.591, Il. 18.220.
-οῦ, ὁ. The heart, breast, soul, mind (cf. ἦτορ, καρδίη, κραδίη, κῆρ, φρήν).

div.head: I
div.p: As the seat or a seat (when coupled with φρήν, φρένες, κραδίη hardly to be distinguished therefrom)

div.head: a
div.p: Vitality, the vital powers, strength (cf. ἦτορ 2.a.α, κῆρ 2.a): ὀλίγος ἔτι θ. ἐνῆεν Il. 1.593. Cf. Il. 3.294 (of sacrificial victims), Il. 4.152, Il. 14.439, Il. 15.240, Il. 16.540, Il. 20.472, Il. 21.417, Il. 22.475: εἰς ὅ κεν αὖτις θυμὸν λάβητε Od. 10.461. Cf. Od. 5.458, Od. 10.78, Od. 19.263, Od. 24.349.

div.head: b
div.p: The animating principle, the vital spirit, the soul, the life, life, one's life (cf. αἰών 3, ἦτορ 2.a.β, μένος 7, ψυχή 1): τάχʼ ἂν θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ Il. 1.205. Cf. Il. 4.524, 531, Il. 5.155, 317, 673, 698, Od. 11.334, Il. 12.150 (of wild boars), Il. 17.17, Il. 21.296, etc.: κεκαφηότα θυμόν Od. 5.468. Cf.Od. 11.201, 203, Od. 12.350, Od. 13.270, Od. 14.405, Od. 15.354, Od. 17.236, Od. 20.62, Od. 21.154, 171, Od. 22.388 (of fishes), 462.

div.head: c
div.p: The spirit or soul thought of as distinct from the body and as leaving it at death (cf. ψυχή 4): θ. ᾤχετʼ ἀπὸ μελέων Il. 13.671 = Il. 16.606. Cf. Il. 4.470, Il. 7.131, Il. 12.386, Il. 16.469 (of a horse), 743, Il. 20.406, Il. 23.880 (of a bird): λίπʼ ὀστέα θ. Od. 3.455 (of a sacrificial victim), Od. 12.414. Cf. Od. 10.163 (of a deer) = Od. 19.454 (of a wild boar), Od. 11.221.
In reference to animals or insects Il. 12.300 (a lion), Il. 13.704 (oxen). Cf. Il. 16.162, 266, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: Of anger, wrath, indignation: θυμὸν χολώθη (in his heart) Il. 4.494, Il. 13.660, ἀπειλήσω τό γε θυμῷ (from my heart, in earnest) Il. 15.212. Cf. Il. 1.192, 217, 243, 429, Il. 2.196, 223, Il. 6.326, Il. 9.109, 255, 436, 496, 587, 629, 635, 675, Il. 14.50, 207 = 306, Il. 15.155, Il. 16.206, 616, Il. 18.113 = Il. 19.66, Il. 19.271, Il. 20.29: μὴ χόλον ἔνθεο θυμῷ Od. 24.248. Cf. Od. 7.306, Od. 11.562, Od. 20.266.
Hence, anger, wrath: σοὶ ἄλληκτον θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσι θεοὶ θέσαν Il. 9.637. Cf. Od. 13.148.
Evil passions: ὑμέτερος θ. καὶ ἀεικέα ἔργα φαίνεται Od. 4.694.

div.head: b
div.p: Of madness, rage, fury, wild excitement: ἀλύσσοντες περὶ θυμῷ Il. 22.70 (of dogs) (see Il. 21.65, etc., under 4.a). Cf. Il. 23.468: Od. 21.302.

div.head: a
div.p: In reference to animals Il. 8.189 (of horses), Il. 22.142 (of a hawk).
One's wishes or liking: ἄρσαντες κατὰ θυμόν Il. 1.136. Cf. Il. 9.645.

div.head: b
div.p: Of the sexual impulse: τῇ θυμὸν ὄρινεν (sought to excite . . .) Il. 3.395. Cf. Il. 14.316: ᾧ θυμῷ εἴξασα μίγη . . . Od. 5.126. Cf. Od. 18.212.

Of volition: οὐκ Ἀτρεΐδῃ ἥνδανε θυμῷ Il. 1.24 = 378, εἴ τοι θ. ἐπέσσυται Il. 1.173, ἑκὼν ἀέκοντί γε θυμῷ Il. 4.43. Cf. Il. 5.676, Il. 7.68, Il. 8.39, Il. 9.398, Il. 10.534, Il. 12.174, Il. 18.90, Il. 20.32, Il. 21.386, Il. 22.78, etc.: ἐπεπείθετο θ. Od. 2.103, τελέσαι με θ. ἄνωγεν Od. 5.89. Cf. Od. 4.140, Od. 7.187, 258, Od. 8.45, Od. 13.145, Od. 14.445, Od. 18.409, Od. 21.194, etc.
In reference to animals: οὐδὲ λύκοι τε καὶ ἄρνες ὁμόφρονα θυμὸν ἔχουσιν Il. 22.263. Cf. Il. 10.531 = Il. 11.520 (horses).
Inclination, a mind: ἐπεί τοι θ. [ἐστιν] αἰτιάασθαι Il. 13.775. Cf. Il. 20.349.

Of feelings, emotions, moods, such as joy, grief, affection, dislike, pity, hope, fear, resentment, reverence, regard, solicitude, wonder, etc.: θυμῷ φιλέουσα Il. 1.196 = 209, κεχαροίατό κε θυμῷ 256, ἄχος κραδίην καὶ θυμὸν ἵκανεν Il. 2.171, σεβάσσατο τό γε θυμῷ Il. 6.167, 417. Cf. Il. 2.142, Il. 3.438, Il. 4.208, Il. 7.189, Il. 8.138, Il. 9.8, 343 (from the bottom of my heart), 639, Il. 10.69, 355, Il. 13.82, 163, Il. 14.104, Il. 15.561, Il. 17.254, 625, Il. 19.229, Il. 21.456, Il. 23.62, etc.: θάμβησεν κατὰ θυμόν Od. 1.323, δ οὔ ποτε ἔλπετο θυμῷ Od. 3.275, κότον ἔνθετο θυμῷ Od. 11.102, δείσασʼ ἐνὶ θυμῷ Od. 16.331. Cf. Od. 1.4, Od. 2.79, 138, Od. 4.71, Od. 5.83, Od. 8.15 (their curiosity), Od. 10.63, 248, Od. 11.39, Od. 14.146 (see Il. 21.65, etc., under 4.a), Od. 18.161, 330, Od. 19.71, Od. 20.59, Od. 21.87, 218, Od. 24.90, etc.
In reference to animals Il. 10.492 (horses), Il. 11.555 = Il. 17.664 (a lion): Od. 10.217 (dogs).
One's good will or favour (cf. ἀποθύμιος): ἀπὸ θυμοῦ μᾶλλον ἐμοὶ ἔσεαι Il. 1.562, σοὶ ἐκ θυμοῦ πεσέειν Il. 23.595.

Of the faculty of perception or knowledge: ᾔδεε κατὰ θυμὸν ὡς . . . Il. 2.409. Cf. Il. 4.163 = Il. 6.447, Il. 7.44, Il. 12.228, Il. 16.119, Il. 18.224 (of horses), Il. 20.264: οὐδὲ θυμῷ ὠΐσθη δόλον εἶναι Od. 4.452. Cf. Od. 2.112, Od. 4.730, Od. 10.374, Od. 13.339, Od. 15.211, Od. 18.154, 228, Od. 19.485 = Od. 23.260, Od. 22.373, Od. 24.391.
Of memory or recollection: μνήσατο κατὰ θυμὸν Αἰγίσθοιο (Ἀντιλόχοιο) Od. 1.29, Od. 4.187, ἔπος μοι ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (came into my mind) Od. 12.266.

Of one's character or disposition: ὥς τοι θ. ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν Il. 4.360, οἶος κείνου θ. ὑπερφίαλος Il. 15.94. Cf. Il. 18.262, etc.: ἐμὸν θυμὸν γνώσεαι (what manner of man I am) Od. 16.309. Cf. Od. 5.191, Od. 9.272 = 368, Od. 9.287, Od. 15.20, 212, Od. 19.364, Od. 23.97, etc.

div.head: II
div.p: Vaguely as the seat of κῆρ 2.g: ἐμὸν κῆρ ἄχνυται ἐν θυμῷ Il. 6.524.

div.head: III
div.p: One's inward self as a region in which something takes place without outward manifestation: εὔχεθʼ ὃν κατὰ θυμόν (in to himself) Il. 23.769: θυμῷ ἐλέαιρε γυναῖκα (without letting any outward sign appear) Od. 19.210. Cf. Od. 5.444, Od. 20.301, Od. 22.411.

div.head: IV
div.p: In a more or less physical sense: ὃν θυμὸν κατέδων Il. 6.202. Cf. Il. 7.216, Il. 13.280, Il. 15.280, Il. 23.370: οὐκέτι κεύθετε θυμῷ βρωτύν Od. 18.406. Cf. Od. 9.75 = Od. 10.143, Od. 10.379.

Life-destroying: φάρμακα (poisons) Od. 2.329, ἄχος (heart-breaking, crushing) Od. 4.716, κάματον (that crushes the spirit) Od. 10.363, ὅς κε τοῦτον ἀνίαζῃ θ. (molesting or annoying beyond endurance) Od. 19.323.
Absol.: γράψας ἐν πίνακι θυμοφθόρα πολλά (much matter that was to be his death-warrant) Il. 6.169.
A tree not identified, the wood of which emits (sweet) odour when burnt Od. 5.60.
A making of sacrifice, a sacrifice or offering Il. 9.499.
In pl. of a single offering: λίσσομʼ ὑπὲρ θυέων Od. 15.261.
What is sacrificed or offered: πρὸς νηὸν ἔρχεο σὺν θυέεσσιν Il. 6.270.
App. a religious adviser skilled in divination from sacrifices, perh. from observation of the smoke thereof Od. 21.145, Od. 22.318, 321.
To impart fragrance to: ἐλαίῳ, τό ῥά οἱ τεθυωμένον ἦεν (which she had by her in (full) fragrance) Il. 14.172.
Out through a door, out of a room or house: βῆ θ. (from his smithy) Il. 18.416. Cf. Il. 24.572: ἢν ἕλκωσι θ. Od. 16.276. Cf. Od. 6.53, Od. 15.62, 451, Od. 19.69, Od. 21.238 = 384.
Of passing the gates of dreams Od. 19.566.
With ἐκ: ἐκ θ. ἔδραμον (out of doors) Il. 18.29: δόμων ἐξῆγε θ. Od. 15.465. Cf. Od. 18.386, Od. 19.68, Od. 20.179, 361, 367, Od. 21.89, 299, 388.
In pregnant sense: ἐξελθόντες μεγάρων ἕζεσθε θ. (out of doors) Od. 22.375. Cf. Od. 20.97, Od. 22.456.
Forth from a specified or indicated space or region: [ἰχθὺν] ἔρριψε θ. (out of the sea) Od. 12.254, διὰ δʼ ἀμπερὲς ἦλθε θ. ἰός (through and out from the axe-heads) Od. 21.422.
With ἐκ: οὐδὲ θ. εἴων ἐξιέναι (from the line of the ships) Il. 18.447. Cf. Il. 5.694, Il. 16.408, Il. 21.29, 237: Od. 5.410.
Watching the door, watch(-dogs): κύνας θυραωρούς Il. 22.69.
Something (in the passages cited a huge stone) placed to block up a door Od. 9.240 = 340, Od. 9.313.
A door (cf. θύρη 1..b) Il. 2.415: αὐλῆς θ. (app., a door leading to the αὐλή from the λαύρη) Od. 22.137. Cf. Od. 18.385, Od. 21.49.

div.head: a
div.p: The door of a room: θαλάμοιο Il. 24.317. Cf. Od. 1.441, Od. 22.155, 157, 201, 258 = 275, 394.

div.head: b
div.p: In pl. (properly of a double or folding door; cf. Od. 17.267), the door of a house or room: ἐπὶ Πριάμοιο θύρῃσιν Il. 2.788. Cf. Il. 6.89, 298, Il. 7.346, Il. 9.473, 475, Il. 11.644, Il. 14.167 = 339, 169, Il. 22.66: προπάροιθε θυράων (i.e. the main door of the μέγαρον) Od. 1.107, θύρας ὤϊξεν (i.e. of the house) Od. 10.230. Cf. Od. 1.255, 436 (the same as the θύρην of 441), Od. 6.19, Od. 7.88, Od. 17.530 (outside), Od. 22.76, etc.
Of the entrance to the cave of the Cyclops Od. 9.243, 304, 416, 417.
To the cave of Scylla Od. 12.256.
Of the entrances to the cave of the Naiads Od. 13.109, 370.
Of the door of a pigsty Od. 10.389.

div.head: a
div.p: The gate of the αὐλή: αὐλὴν ποίησαν θύρην δʼ ἔχε μοῦνος ἐπιβλής Il. 24.453.

div.head: b
div.p: In pl.: κληῗδα θυράων Il. 24.455. Cf. Il. 24.567 (the same as the θύρην of 453): ἔκτοσθεν αὐλῆς ὄρχατος ἄγχι θυράων Od. 7.112, αἰθούσης θύρας (see αἴθουσα (2)) Od. 18.102, ἐπʼ αὐλείῃσι θύρῃσιν (see αὔλειος) 239, Od. 23.49. Cf. Od. 1.120, Od. 16.344, Od. 17.267, Od. 21.191, 240, 389, 391, Od. 23.370.
Out of doors, abroad: κτήματα, τά τʼ ἔνδοθι καὶ τὰ θύρηφιν (i.e. cattle, sheep, etc.) Od. 22.220.
Like θύραζε 2: ὦκα θύρηθʼ ἔα (out of the water) Od. 14.352.
A tassel or pendant. Attached to the aegis: παγχρύσεοι ἐϋπλεκέες Il. 2.448 (app. of twisted wire).
App., mystic implements borne in the rites of Dionysus: θ. χαμαὶ κατέχευαν Il. 6.134.
Epithet of the aegis Il. 5.738, Il. 15.229, Il. 17.593, Il. 18.204, Il. 21.400.
To run, rush: ἔγχεϊ (spear in hand) Il. 11.180, Il. 16.699, Il. 22.272.
To run or flow (with a liquid): δάπεδον ἅπαν αἵματι θῦεν Od. 11.420, Od. 22.309 = Od. 24.185.

To offer in sacrifice portions of a
meal before partaking: θεοῖσι θῦσαι ἀνώγει Il. 9.219. Cf. Od. 9.231, Od. 15.222, 260.
To offer (such portions to the gods): ἄργματα θῦσε θεοῖς Od. 14.446.
A fine or penalty: σοὶ θωὴν ἐπιθήσομεν Od. 2.192.
Specifically, a fine in place of personal service in war: ἀργαλέην θωὴν ἀλέεινεν Ἀχαιῶν Il. 13.669 (cf. Il. 23.296).
For or with a view to a sitting or assembly: θ. καθίζανον Od. 5.3.
A sitting, session, assembly: οὔθʼ ἡμετέρη ἀγορὴ γένετʼ οὔτε θόωκος Od. 2.26 (the two words hardly to be distinguished). Cf. Od. 15.468.
Sim. in pl.: θεῶν ἐξίκετο θώκους (the assembled gods) Il. 8.439.
A breastplate or corslet, consisting of two γύαλα (see γύαλον) Il. 2.544, Il. 3.332, Il. 4.133, Il. 5.99, Il. 11.234, Il. 13.265, Il. 15.529, Il. 19.361, etc.
3 pl. aor. pass. θωρήχθησαν Il. 3.340, Il. 23.813.
In act., to cause to arm for the fray, get under arms: Ἀχαιούς Il. 2.11, 28 = 65. Cf. Il. 2.72 = 83, Il. 16.155.

div.head: a
div.p: to arm oneself for the fray, get under arms, don one's harness: τῷδε θωρήξομαι (to meet him) Il. 7.101, δός μοι τὰ σὰ τεύχεα θωρηχθῆναι (to arm myself withal) Il. 16.40. Cf. Il. 1.226, Il. 3.340, Il. 8.54, Il. 11.715, Il. 18.189, etc.: Od. 12.227, Od. 22.139, Od. 23.369.

div.head: b
div.p: App. meaning little more than to have one's station, post oneself, stand, be: ἐπʼ ἀριστερὰ θωρήσσοντο Il. 2.526, πρὸ φθίων θωρηχθέντες (acting as their leaders) Il. 13.699, ἅμα πατρόκλῳ θωρηχθέντες (following him) Il. 16.257. Cf. Il. 2.587, 818, Il. 4.252, Il. 11.709, Il. 16.218.
A beast of prey, perh. the jackal Il. 11.474, 479, 481, Il. 13.103.
3 sing. aor. subj. ἰήνῃ Il. 24.119, 147, 176, 196. Impl. pl. ἰήνατε Od. 8.426.
To warm, heat: χαλκὸν ἰήνατε Od. 8.426. Cf. Od. 10.359, Od. 12.175.

To gladden, rejoice, cheer, comfort, placate: ἵνα φρεσὶ σῇσιν ἰανθῇς Il. 19.174, τοῖο θυμὸς ἰάνθη ὡς εἴ τε περὶ σταχύεσσιν ἐέρση ληΐου Il. 23.598 (app., was gladdened as the dew upon the ears is warmed (sense (1)). V.l. ἐέρσῃ, as (the heart) of the corn is gladdened with the dew upon the ears). Cf. Il. 23.600, Il. 24.119 = 147 = 176 = 196, 321: εἰς ὅ κε σὸν κῆρ ἰανθῇ Od. 22.59. Cf. Od. 4.549, 840, Od. 6.156, Od. 15.165, 379, Od. 19.537, Od. 23.47.
To unbend (the brow): οὐδὲ μέτωπον ἰάνθη Il. 15.103.
To shoot, discharge, let fly (a missile): ὀϊστόν Il. 8.300, 309.
Hence, to send, let loose (bane): ὥς κʼ ὔμμι ἐπὶ κῆρας ἰήλω Od. 2.316.
To throw on, put on (a bond or manacle): περὶ χερσὶ δεσμὸν ἴηλα Il. 15.19.
Sim. of a means of fastening a gate Od. 21.241.
To apply or tie (a knot): ἐπὶ δεσμὸν ἴηλον Od. 8.443. Cf. Od. 8.447.
To fling at, assail: ἀτιμίῃσιν (with . . .) Od. 13.142.
To heal, cure, make whole, tend: παιήονά [μιν] ἀνώγειν ἰήσασθαι Il. 5.899. Cf. Il. 5.904, Il. 12.2: Od. 9.520, Od. 19.460.
With the injured part as object: ὀθφθαλμόν Od. 9.525.
To lie, rest, pass the night (not necessarily implying sleeping): Ζηνὸς ἐν ἀγκοίνῃσιν ἰαύεις Il. 14.213. Cf. Od. 11.261, Od. 22.464, Od. 24.209.
Of sheep, goats or swine Od. 9.184, Od. 14.16.
To pass (the night): ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον Il. 9.325. Cf. Il. 9.470: Od. 3.151, 490, Od. 5.154, Od. 15.40, 188, Od. 16.367, Od. 19.340, 342.
To keep night-watch. Of dogs Od. 14.21.

[For the impf. forms, 3 sing. ἴαχε and 3 pl. ἴαχον (with ἴαχον Il. 23.766 ), should prob. be read ϝάχε, ἔϝαχε, εὔαχε (cf. εὔαδε) and ϝάκον, ἔϝακον, εὔαχον, as aorists. But ἴαχον in Il. 4.506 = Il. 17.317 seems to be for ϝίϝαχον,
In rushing from an ambush Od. 4.454.
In assent or approval: Ἀργεῖοι μέγʼ ἴαχον Il. 2.333, 394.
On seeing an encouraging omen Il. 13.822.
In pain or grief Il. 5.343, Il. 18.29.
In terror or affright Il. 20.62: Od. 10.323.
Of the cry of a frightened infant Il. 6.468.
Of inanimate objects. Of water, to splash: κῦμα μεγάλʼ ἴαχεν Il. 1.482: = Od. 2.428.
Of a bow-string, to twang Il. 4.125.
Of a trumpet, to sound Il. 18.219.
Of heated metal plunged in water, to hiss Od. 9.392.
Of something reechoing sound: περὶ δʼ ἴαχε πέτρη Od. 9.395. Cf. Il. 21.10.
The hollow of the knee, the ham: κατʼ ἰγνύην βεβλημένος Il. 13.212.
And: ὤμοισιν ἰδὲ στέρνοισιν Il. 3.194, κνῆμαί τε ἰδὲ σφυρά Il. 4.147. Cf. Il. 2.511, 697, Il. 4.382, Il. 5.3, 171, etc.: Od. 4.604, Od. 9.186, Od. 11.337, 431, 626, etc.
App. as genit.: Ἴδηθεν μεδέων Il. 3.276 = 320 = Il. 7.202 = Il. 24.308.
Private, personal: πρῆξις ἥδʼ ἰδίη, οὐ δήμιος Od. 3.82.
To bend or double up one's body, curl oneself up: ὁ δʼ ἰδνώθη (in pain) Il. 2.266, ἰδνώθη πεσών (in the death-struggle) Il. 13.618. Cf. Od. 22.85.
To bend the body for an upward throw: ἰδνωθεὶς ὀπίσω Od. 8.375.
Sim., of an eagle bending back his head in order to use his beak Il. 12.205.
Skill: ἰδρείῃ πολέμοιο (skill in war) Il. 16.359. Cf. Il. 7.198.
With infin.: ἴδριες νῆα ἐλαυνέμεν (in propelling . . .) Od. 7.108.
Acc. sing. pres. pple. ἱδρώοντα Il. 18.372.
With cognate acc.: ἱδρῶ ὃν ἵδρωσα Il. 4.27.
To be covered with sweat: ἱδρώσει τευ τελαμών Il. 2.388
3 pl. aor. pass. ἱδρύνθησαν Il. 3.78, Il. 7.56. (καθ-.)
To cause to be seated: ἵδρυε λαούς Il. 2.191. Cf. Il. 15.142: Od. 3.37, Od. 5.86.
In aor., to sit down: τοὶ δʼ ἱδρύνθησαν ἅπαντες Il. 3.78 = Il. 7.56.
A priestess attached to the service of a particular goddess: Ἀθηναίης ἱέρειαν Il. 6.300.
ὁ. Also ἱρεύς Il. 5.10, Il. 16.604: Od. 9.198.
A priest attached to the service of a particular god: ἱερεὺς Ἀπόλλωνος Il. 1.370. Cf. Il. 1.23 = 377, Il. 1.62, Il. 5.10, Il. 9.575, Il. 16.604, Il. 24.221: Od. 9.198.
3 pl. pa. iterative ἱρεύεσκον Od. 20.3. ἱέρευτο Il. 24.125 is prob. to be taken as impf. pass. assimilated to forms like στεῦτο.
To sacrifice (an animal to a god): Ἀθηναίῃ βοῦς Il. 6.94 = 275, 309. Cf. Il. 21.131, Il. 23.147: Od. 13.182.
To the spirit of a deceased man: τειρεσίῃ ὄϊν Od. 10.524 = Od. 11.32.

To kill (an animal) for a meal, parts being offered as firstlings to a god or the gods: τοῖσι βοῦν ἱέρευσε κρονίωνι Il. 7.314. Cf. Il. 2.402, Il. 6.174, Il. 18.559, Il. 24.125: δεῖπνον συῶν ἱερεύσατε ὅς τις ἄριστος (for the meal) Od. 24.215. Cf. Od. 2.56 = Od. 17.535, Od. 8.59, Od. 13.24, Od. 14.28, 74, 94, 414, Od. 16.454, Od. 17.180 = Od. 20.250, Od. 17.181 = Od. 20.251, Od. 20.3, 391.
In mid.: δῶκα βοῦς ἱερεύσασθαι Od. 19.198.
An animal to be killed as under ἱερεύω. (2): ἑταῖροι δαίνυντʼ αὐτὰρ ἐγὼν ἱερήϊα πολλὰ παρεῖχον Od. 14.250. Cf. Od. 17.600.
So doubtless οὐχ ἱ. ἀρνύσθην Il. 22.159 (i.e. as a prize).
As object to ἱερεύω. (2): οὔ ποθʼ ἓν ἱρεύσʼ ἱ. Od. 14.94.
-ή, -όν. Also ὶρός -ή, -όν Il. 2.420, Il. 4.46, Il. 6.96, Il. 17.193, Il. 21.128, etc.: Od. 1.66, Od. 3.278, Od. 9.553, Od. 17.293, etc. Sacred, holy, set apart.
Of a temple: θύρας ἱεροῖο δόμοιο Il. 6.89.
Of the site of a sacred grove: Ὀγχηστὸν ἱερόν, Ποσιδήϊον ἄλσος Il. 2.506.
Epithet of places: Ἴλιος ἱρή Il. 4.46. Cf. Il. 1.366, Il. 2.535, 625, Il. 4.103, Il. 5.446, etc.: πύλου ἱερῆς Od. 21.108. Cf. Od. 1.2, Od. 3.278, Od. 9.165, Od. 11.86, 323, Od. 17.293.
Sim.: ἱερὰ ρείχεα Θήβης Il. 4.378. Cf. Il. 16.100.
Of rivers (as sprung from Zeus): ἱερὸν ῥόον Ἀλφειοῖο Il. 11.726. Cf. Od. 10.351.
Epithet of natural periods of time half-personified as divine controlling powers: κνέφας Il. 11.194 = 209 = Il. 17.455, ἦμαρ Il. 8.66 = Il. 11.84: = Od. 9.56.

Of things regarded as divine by connexion or relation: ἀλωάς (as being consecrated to Demeter) Il. 5.499, ἀλφίτου (as being the gift of Demeter) Il. 11.631, κύκλῳ (justice, the care of Zeus, being there dispensed) Il. 18.504. Cf. Il. 15.39, Il. 16.658: βήσσας (as being about the dwelling of Circe) Od. 10.275, ἐλαίης (as being near the nymphhaunted cave) Od. 13.372. Cf. Od. 10.426, 445, 554.
Sim.: ἰχθύν (perh. referring to a religious scruple against eating fish) Il. 16.407, δίφρῳ (app. as drawn by divine steeds) Il. 17.464.

p.gloss: Of persons regarded as divine by connexion or relation.

div.p: Epithet of King Alcinous (as holding office from Zeus) Od. 7.167, Od. 8.2, 4 = 421, Od. 8.385, Od. 13.20, 24.
Of Telemachus (as being under the special protection of Athene) Od. 2.409 = Od. 18.405 = Od. 21.101, Od. 16.476, Od. 18.60 = Od. 21.130, Od. 22.354.
Applied to persons dignified by being charged with a special function: πυλαωρούς Il. 24.681.
Sim. applied to the post occupied by such persons: φυλάκων τέλος Il. 10.56.

Extended to a whole host (perh. as being engaged in a
pious work): Ἀργείων στρατός Od. 24.81.

div.head: a
div.p: A sacred place or haunt: ἄλσος,ἱρὸν Ἀθηναίης Od. 6.322, ἄντρον, ἱρὸν νυμφάων Od. 13.104 = 348.

div.head: b
div.p: App., a sacrifice = c: ὄφρʼ ἱρὸν ἑτοιμασσαίατʼ Ἀθήνῃ (a sacrifice at which the arms were to be dedicated) Il. 10.571.

div.head: c
div.p: The actual burnt-offering: σπένδων οἶνον ἐπʼ αἰθομένοις ἱεροῖσιν Il. 11.775. Cf. Od. 12.362.
To cause to be seated: ἀγῶνα Il. 23.258.
To sit: ἐν τῷ ἵζανον Od. 24.209 (i.e. used it as a sitting-room).
Fig. of sleep: οὔ μοι ἐπʼ ὄμμασιν ὕπνος ἱζάνει Il. 10.92.
redup. fr. σ(ε)δ-, the rough breathing representing the first σ. Cf. ἕζομαι, ἱδρύω.]
3 sing. pa. iterative ἵζεσκε Il. 24.472: Od. 3.409.
Imp. mid. ἵζευ Il. 3.162, Il. 7.115. (ἐσ-, ἐφ-, καθ-, μετα-, παρ-, προκαθ-.)
To cause to seat oneself, bid be seated: μή μʼ ἐς θρόνον ἵζε Il. 24.553.
To cause (an assembly) to sit for business: βουλήν Il. 2.53.

To seat oneself, sit down: ἀντίον ἷζεν Ὀδυσσῆος Il. 9.218. Cf. Il. 2.96, Il. 9.13, 87, Il. 13.281, Il. 18.422, Il. 20.15, Il. 21.520, Il. 23.28: ἐπʼ οὐδοῦ ἶζεν Od. 4.718, Od. 17.339, ἵζʼ ἐπὶ δεῖπνον (sit down to . . .) Od. 24.394. Cf. Od. 5.198, 338, Od. 8.469, Od. 14.79, Od. 16.53, Od. 17.96, Od. 19.389.
In mid.: πάροιθʼ ἵζευ ἐμεῖο Il. 3.162. Cf. Il. 3.326, Il. 7.115, Il. 18.522, Il. 19.50: Od. 22.335.
To have one's seat, be seated, sit: ὅς οἱ πλησίον ἷζεν Od. 7.171. Cf. Il. 24.472: Od. 3.409, Od. 11.449, Od. 21.146.
Of a scout, to be posted: σκοποὶ ἷζον ἐπʼ ἄκριας Od. 16.365. Cf. Il. 2.792.
Pl. pple. ἱέντες Il. 2.774: Od. 4.626, Od. 17.168.
Mid. 3 pl. aor. ἕντο Il. 1.469, Il. 7.323, Il. 9.92, Il. 23.57, etc.: Od. 1.150, Od. 4.68, Od. 14.454, Od. 17.99, etc. Pass 3 pl. pres. ἵενται Il. 4.77.
(ἀν-, ἀποπρο-, ἀφ-, ἐν-, ἐξ-, ἐξαν-, ἐπιπρο-, ἐφ-, καθ-, μεθ-, παρ-, προ-, συν-, ὑπερ-, ὑφ-.)
Absol., to throw, make a throw, make one's throw: ἥσω καὶ ἐγώ Il. 17.515. Cf. Il. 15.359: Od. 9.499.
To shoot one's arrow: διὰ δʼ ἧκε σιδήρου Od. 21.328, Od. 24.177.
In gen., to throw, send, cause to fall: ἐέρσας ἐξ αἰθέρος Il. 11.53. Cf. Il. 13.204, Il. 21.120.
To send from oneself, let fall from one's grasp: φάσγανον ἧκε χαμᾶζε Od. 22.84. Cf. Il. 12.205, Il. 17.299.
To let (oneself) fall: ἧκα καθύπερθε πόδας καὶ χεῖρε Od. 12.442.
To send forth (the voice): ἱεῖσαι ὄπα κάλλιμον Od. 12.192. Cf. Il. 3.152, 221, Il. 14.151.
To cause (waters) to flow: ἐς τεῖχος ἵει ῥόον Il. 12.25.
Of a river, to send or roll (its waters): ᾗ πρόσθεν ἵεν [ποταμοὶ] ὕδωρ Il. 12.33. Cf. Il. 21.158.
Absol.: Ἐνιπῆος, ὃς κάλλιστος ποταμῶν ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἵησιν Od. 11.239.
So of a fountain: δύω κρῆναι ἡ μὲν . . . ἡ δ ὑπʼ αὐλῆς οὐδὸν ἵησδιν Od. 7.130.

To send or dispatch as a messenger, on a specified or indicated mission, for some purpose, to a specified destination: πρὸ γὰρ ἧκέ μιν Ἥρη Il. 18.168. Cf. Il. 1.195, 208, Il. 4.397, Il. 18.182, Il. 24.375: ἄγγελον ἧκαν Od. 15.458. Cf. Od. 10.159, Od. 21.21.
To cause (a person) to come forth, bring (him) forth: αἰνείαν ἐξ ἀδύτοιο Il. 5.513.
To send (a wind): ἴκμενον οὖρον ἵει Il. 1.479: Od. 2.420 = Od. 15.292, Od. 11.7 = Od. 12.149.
In gen., to send forth, cause to appear: δράκοντα φόωσδε Il. 2.309, τοῦ πολλοὶ ἀπὸ σπινθῆρες ἵενται Il. 4.77. Cf. Il. 4.75, Il. 8.76, 247 = Il. 24.315, Il. 10.274: Od. 21.415.
To expel by satiety, put thus away (desire, inclination or appetite, thought of as something physical): ἐπὴν γόου ἐξ ἔρον εἵην Il. 24.227.

To cause to be in a specified place or position, set, place, put, hang, throw: ἐν ἕρματα ἧκε λοβοῖσιν Il. 14.182, ὑπὸ θρῆνυν ἥσει 240, ἐκ ποδοῖιν ἄκμονας ἧκα Il. 15.19, ἐν αὐτὸν ἵει πυρί (set him on fire) Il. 21.338. Cf. Il. 18.612, Il. 19.383 = Il. 22.316: κατὰ κάρητος οὔλας ἧκε κόμας Od. 6.231 = Od. 23.158, ὑπʼ ἔμβρυον ἧκεν ἑκάστῃ Od. 9.245 = 309 = 342. Cf. Od. 10.317, Od. 19.57, Od. 21.47.
Of harnessing a horse: ἐν παρηορίῃσι πήδασον ἵει Il. 16.152.
Of applying fire: ἐν πυρὸς μένος ἧκεν Il. 23.177.
To inspire or infuse (spirit, panic): ἔν τοι στήθεσσι μένος ἧκα Il. 5.125, ἐν κυδοιμὸν ἧκεν Il. 11.539. Cf. Il. 15.327, Il. 16.291, 730, Il. 23.400.
(ϝίημι). Only in mid. Fut. εἴσομαι (ϝίσομαι) Il. 14.8, Il. 21.335, Il. 24.462: Od. 22.7.
To aim at, take one's aim at.
With acc.: σκοπὸν ἄλλον εἴσομαι Od. 22.7 (or the word may be referred to εἴδω III.10).

To desire, be eager or anxious, long, to do something specified or indicated, be set on doing it: τό οἱ οὔ τις ἐρύκακεν ἱεμένων περ Il. 15.450 = Il. 17.292. Cf. Il. 16.396, Il. 17.276: ἕεται αἰνῶς Od. 2.327. Cf. Od. 1.6, Od. 4.284, Od. 10.246, Od. 16.430, Od. 21.129, Od. 22.256, 273, 409, Od. 23.353.

With complementary infin.: ἵετʼ αἰνείαν κτεῖναι Il. 5.434, ἱέμενος Τροίην ἐξαλαπάξαι (in my eagerness to . . .) Il. 8.241. Cf. Il. 2.589, Il. 8.301 = 310, Il. 11.537, Il. 12.68, Il. 13.386, 424, 501 = Il. 16.761, Il. 13.585, Il. 16.359, 383 = 866, Il. 16.507, Il. 18.501, 547, Il. 20.469, 502: ἱέσθην ἐπὶ νῆα νέεσθαι Od. 3.344, ἐμὲ ἱέμενοι
γῆμαι Od. 21.72. Cf. Od. 1.58, Od. 4.823 = Od. 13.426 = Od. 15.30, Od. 14.142, 282, Od. 15.201.
To be eager to go or make one's way in a specified direction: οἴκαδε ἱεμένων Il. 2.154. Cf. Od. 3.160, Od. 9.261, Od. 17.5, Od. 19.187.
Of a missile weapon checked in its eager course: ἐγχείη ἐνὶ γαίῃ ἔστη ἱεμένη Il. 20.280.
So with complementary infin.: ἐγχείη ἐνὶ γαίῃ ἔστη ἱεμένη χροὸς ἄμεναι Il. 21.70.
To be eager for, strive for, be set upon.
With genit.: νίκης ἱεμένων Il. 23.371. Cf. Il. 23.718, 767: ἱέμενον νόστοιο Od. 15.69.

To hasten, speed, rush, press, make one's way: πρόσω ἵεσθε Il. 12.274, τάχα εἴσομαι Il. 14.8 (or the word may be referred to εἴδω III.1), πάλιν εἴσομαι Il. 24.462. Cf. Il. 8.313, Il. 12.118, Il. 13.291, 707, Il. 15.415, Il. 16.382: ἱεμένων Ἔρεβόσδε Od. 20.356. Cf. Od. 22.304.
With genit. of the point aimed at: ἱέμενοι πόλιος Il. 11.168: ἱέμενος ποταμοῖο ῥοάων (moving towards the river) Od. 10.529.
With fut. pple. indicating purpose: ζεφύροιο εἴσομαι ὄρσουσα θύελλαν Il. 21.335. Cf. Od. 15.213.
So with fut. infin.: ἐεισάσθην τεύχεα δυλήσειν Il. 15.544.
With aor. infin.: ἄλλος κʼ ἀνὴρ ἵετο ἰδέειν παῖδας Od. 13.334.
Of a weapon, to take its way: διαπρὸ εἴσατο χαλκός Il. 5.538 = Il. 17.518: = Od. 24.524. Cf. Il. 4.138, Il. 15.543, Il. 20.399.
With genit.: οὔ πῃ χροὸς εἴσατο Il. 13.191 (for the sense with v.l. χρώς see εἴδω II.1).
A healer, a surgeon and physician: ἕλκος ἰ. ἐπιμάσσεται Il. 4.190. Cf. Il. 2.732, Il. 4.194, Il. 11.518, 835: Od. 17.384.
Absol.: ἶσόν μʼ ἰθαγενέεσσιν ἐτίμα Od. 14.203.
Gait: πελειάσιν ἴθμαθʼ ὁμοῖαι (app., with short, quick steps) Il. 5.778.

Straight, straight on, without turning aside: μένος χειρῶν ἰθὺς φέρον Il. 5.506, ἰθὺς πρὸς τεῖχος ἔκιον Il. 12.137. Cf. Il. 8.118, Il. 11.95, Il. 12.124, 330, Il. 13.135, Il. 16.168, 492, Il. 20.79, 99, 108, 172, 386, Il. 22.143, 243, 284: Od. 3.10, Od. 17.33, Od. 23.207, Od. 24.101, 397.
Of position, straight, direct: τέτραπτο πρὸς ἰθύ οἱ Il. 14.403 (straight towards him, i.e. he had him right in the line of his throw): ἰθὺς τετραμμένος (facing the foe) Il. 17.227.

With genit.: ἰθὺς μενελάου ἤϊεν Il. 13.601. Cf. Il. 5.849, Il. 11.289, Il. 12.254, 453, Il. 16.584, Il. 21.540, etc.: βῆ δʼ ἰθὺς προθύροιο Od. 1.119. Cf. Od. 2.301, Od. 3.17, Od. 15.511, Od. 17.325, Od. 24.241.
To make straight or even: ἐπὶ στάθμην ἴθυνε [δοῦρα] Od. 5.245. Cf. Od. 17.341 = Od. 21.44, Od. 21.121, Od. 23.197.
In mid.: ἐπʼ Ἀντινόῳ ἰθύνετʼ ὀϊστόν Od. 22.8.

To direct the course of (a missile): βέλος ἴθυνε ῥῖνα παρʼ ὀφθαλμόν, λευκοὺς δʼ ἐπέρησεν ὀδόντας Il. 5.290 (to the . . ., the head app. being bent forward to avoid the blow). Cf. Il. 4.132, Il. 17.632.
App., to direct (an arrow) towards the mark (preparatory to putting it on the bow): ὀϊστὸν ἔχεν πάλαι, ὡς ἴθυνεν Il. 23.871 (had long been holding it ready as he had directed it.
App. he slips the bow under the arrow thus held).
To direct the course of (a horse, mule, chariot, waggon), drive (it): κεῖσʼ ἵππους τε καὶ ἅρμʼ ἰθύνομεν, ἔνθα . . . Il. 11.528. Cf. Il. 8.110, Il. 24.149, 178, 362.
To bring (a horse) back to its proper direction, turn its head the right way: τὼ ἰθυνθήτην Il. 16.475.
To keep (a ship) on her course, steer (her): μήτι κυβερνήτης νῆα θοὴν ἰθύνει Il. 23.317. Cf. Od. 9.78 = Od. 14.256, Od. 11.10 = Od. 12.152, Od. 12.82.
Absol., to steer one's course: πηδάλιον ποιήσατο, ὄφρʼ ἰθύνοι Od. 5.255.
In mid., of combatants, to direct their course against, charge.

div.head: ἰθύς1,
div.p: Hence just, fair, right: ἰθεῖα ἔσται [δίκη] Il. 23.580.
In superl. in neut. pl. ἰθύντατα as adv., most justly or fairly: ὃς δίκην ἰθύντατα εἴποι Il. 18.508.
A straight course: ἐπεὶ σφαίρῃ ἀνʼ ἰθὺν πειρήσαντο (in throwing straight upwards) Od. 8.377.
One's course: ἀΐσσοντος ἀνʼ ἰθύν ((steadily) pursuing his course) Il. 21.303.
