With genit. indicating that from which one restrains : φόνοιο Od. 22.63.
With genit. : ἔκ με πάντων ληθάνει Od. 7.221.
Epithet of the wild boar Od. 18.29.
To get by rapine, carry off as captives or spoil : δμῳαὶ ἃς ληΐσσατο Il. 18.28 : πολλὰ ληΐσσομαι Od. 23.357. Cf. Od. 1.398.
Standing corn : βαθὺ λ. Il. 2.147, Il. 11.560. Cf. Il. 23.599 : Od. 9.134.

Spoil, booty : ὅτε κεν δατεώμεθα ληΐδα Il. 9.138= 280. Cf. Il. 11.677, Il. 12.7, Il. 18.327 : μενοεικέα σφι ληΐδα δῶκα (booty which he had in hand) Od. 13.273. Cf. Od. 3.106, Od. 5.40= Od. 13.138, Od. 10.41, Od. 13.262, Od. 14.86.
One who sails the sea in quest of spoil, a rover : οἷά τε ληϊστῆρες [ἀλόωνται] ὑπεὶρ ἅλα Od. 3.73= Od. 9.254. Cf. Od. 16.426, Od. 17.425.
That may be carried off as spoil or booty : ληϊστοὶ βόες [εἰσὶ] καὶ μῆλα Il. 9.406. Cf. Il. 9.408.
To bend and slip away from danger : ὁ δʼ ὕπαιθα λιάσθη Il. 15.520. Cf. Il. 21.255.
To sink down, droop, fall : πρηνὴς ἐλιάσθη Il. 15.543. Cf. Il. 20.418, 420.
Of the drooping of a dying bird's wings Il. 23.879.
To slip or glide away : παρὰ κληῗδα λιάσθη Od. 4.838.
To go aside or apart, retire : ἑτάρων νόσφι λιασθείς Il. 1.349. Cf. Il. 11.80, Il. 23.231 : Od. 5.462.
To turn aside from one's proper course : σὺ δεῦρο λιάσθης Il. 22.12.
To part, open so as to afford passage : λιάζετό σφι κῦμα θαλάσσης Il. 24.96.
Of a warm soft wind : οὖρον Od. 5.268= Od. 7.266.
In clear or loud tones, loudly, with full voice : λίγʼ ἐκώκυεν Il. 19.284. Cf. Od. 4.259, Od. 8.527, Od. 10.254.
To use the full voice, make proclamation.
With infin. indicating the purport : κήρυκες λίγαινον τοὺς ἴμεν οἶσι ... Il. 11.685.
With a glancing blow, grazing the flesh : Τηλέμαχον βάλε χεῖρα λ. Od. 22.278.
In clear tones, with a clear flow of words : [ἀγόρευεν] Il. 3.214.
In loud tones, loudly : κλαίοντα Il. 19.5. Cf. Od. 10.201, Od. 11.391, Od. 16.216, Od. 21.56.
Of blowing winds, whistling : φυσῶντες λ. Il. 23.218.
Of winds or the blowing thereof, whistling Il. 5.526, Il. 13.590, Il. 23.215.
So of a whip whistling in the air Il. 11.532.
Of a bird, that utters a shrill cry Il. 14.290.
λίγεια, λιγύ. Emitting a clear or shrill sound.
Speaking in clear tones, whose words flow clearly forth : λ. ἀγορητής Il. 1.248. Cf. Il. 2.246, Il. 4.293, Il. 19.82 : Od. 20.274.
In neut. λιγύ as adv., with whistling sound Od. 4.567.
Epithet of heralds Il. 2.50, 442, Il. 9.10, Il. 23.39 : Od. 2.6.
Of a bird, that utters a shrill cry : ἅρπῃ Il. 19.350.

Exceedingly, very, very much : λ. φύλλοισιν ἐοικότες Il. 2.800 : νήπιός εἰς λ. τόσον; (so very ... as this would seem to show thee to be) Od. 4.371. Cf. Od. 8.231, 489, Od. 10.552, Od. 13.238, 243, Od. 15.405 (not so very ...).

With notion of excess : λ. πολλοί (too many for that) Il. 19.226. Cf. Il. 9.229, Il. 21.566 : λ. πινυτή (too much so for any fear of that) Od. 11.445, λ. ἑκὰς ἤλθομεν Od. 14.496. Cf. Od. 3.227, Od. 13.421, Od. 16.243.
With verbs, exceedingly, greatly : κεχολώατο λ. Od. 14.282, Od. 16.425. Cf. Od. 14.461, Od. 20.99.

With notion of excess : λ. ἄχθομαι ἕλκος (I can bear it no longer) Il. 5.361, λ. μαίνεται (his rage passes all bounds) Il. 6.100. Cf. Il. 6.486, Il. 13.284, Il. 14.368 (we can make shift to do without him), Il. 21.288 : μηδὲ δείδιθι λ. Od. 4.825. Cf. Od. 8.205 (I can contain myself no longer), Od. 16.86 (too much to let me think of that), Od. 18.20 (do not provoke me too far), Od. 23.175 (unduly).
καὶ λίην, truly, verily, of a surety : καὶ λίην κεῖνός γε ἐοικότι κεῖται ὀλέθρῳ Od. 1.46. Cf. Il. 1.553, Il. 19.408 : Od. 3.203, Od. 9.477, Od. 11.181= Od. 16.37, Od. 13.393, Od. 15.155, Od. 17.312.
Strengthening a wish : καὶ λ. οὗτός γε μένος ὀλέσειεν Il. 8.358.
Of a rock, app., studded with projecting stones, rough Od. 5.415.
A stone : σεῦεν κύνας πυκνῇσιν λιθάδεσσιν Od. 14.36.
In pl., stones used in construction Od. 23.193.
A large stone used as or shaped into a seat : ἥατʼ ἐπὶ ξεστοῖσι λίθοις Il. 18.504. Cf. Od. 8.6.
In pl. app. of several stones forming or shaped into a seat Od. 3.406.
A large stone embedded in the ground, or perh. a rock projecting above the ground, pierced for the securing of a cable Od. 13.77.
In pl., stones used in construction : ὡς ὅτε τοῖχον ἀνὴρ ἀράρῃ πυκινοῖσι λίθοισιν Il. 16.212. Cf. Od. 9.185.
Stone as a material : θάλαμοι ξεστοῖο λίθοιο Il. 6.244, 248. Cf. Il. 4.510 : Od. 23.103.
Something of stone : λαοὺς λίθους ποίησεν (turned them to stone) Il. 24.611, λίθος περ ἐοῦσα (stone though she be) 617. Cf. Od. 13.156.
To winnow grain, etc., by throwing it against the wind Il. 5.500.
Obliquely, sideways : λ. ἀΐξας Il. 14.463 : Od. 19.451.

p.gloss: To desire or be anxious to do something or for something to happen, be bent or set on doing something.

div.p: With infin. : εἰ ἐν φιλότητι λιλαίεαι εὐνηθῆναι Il. 14.331. Cf. Il. 3.399, Il. 13.253, Il. 16.89, Il. 20.76 : εἰ ἀκουέμεναι λιλαίεαι Od. 11.380. Cf. Od. 1.15= Od. 9.30, Od. 9.32, 451, Od. 15.308, 327, Od. 20.27, Od. 22.349 (find it not in thy heart to ...), Od. 23.334.
Of inanimate objects Il. 11.574= Il. 15.317, Il. 21.168.
With genit. : πολέμοιο Il. 3.133 : βιότοιο (tendering, in fear for, their lives) Od. 12.328, Od. 24.536. Cf. Od. 1.315, Od. 13.31.– φόωσδε λιλαίεο (make thy way with all speed to ...) Od. 11.223.
Dat. pl. λιμένεσσι Il. 23.745. λιμέσι Il. 12.284 : Od. 19.189.
In pl. in the same sense : στῆσαν ἐν λιμένεσσιν Il. 23.745. Cf. Od. 19.189.

p.gloss: A piece or sheet of water.

div.p: A pool : τάνταλον ἑσταότʼ ἐν λίμνῃ Od. 11.583.
Of the water spread by a river overflowing its banks Il. 21.317.
The sea Il. 13.21, 32, Il. 24.79 : Od. 3.1 (the Ocean stream), Od. 5.337.
Wearing a stout tunic of linen by way of corslet Il. 2.529, 830.
The thread of destiny : τὰ πείσεται ἅσσα οἱ αἶσα γιγνομένῳ ἐπένησε λίνῳ Il. 20.128. Cf. Il. 24.210 : Od. 7.198.
Something made of cords, a net Il. 5.487.
Linen; app. a sheet of linen wherewith to cover oneself in bed (cf. ῥῆγος) : Ὀδυσσῆϊστόρεσαν ῥῆγός τε λίνον τε Od. 13.73. Cf. Od. 13.118.–λίνοιο ἄωτος. See ἄωτος 2.a.
A song sung at the vintage (see Frazer, Golden Bough, 3rd ed. pt. v. vol. i. pp. 216, 257) Il. 18.570.
[prob. related to λιπαρός as λίγα to λιγυρός.]
In reference to anointing, richly, plenteously : ἐπεὶ ἔχρισεν λίπʼ ἐλαίῳ Od. 3.466= Od. 10.364. Cf. Il. 10.577, Il. 14.171, Il. 18.350 : Od. 6.96, 227, Od. 10.450, Od. 19.505.
With tresses glossy with oil : κεφαλῆς Il. 19.126.
Anointed with oil : αἰεὶ λιπαροὶ κεφαλὰς καὶ πρόσωπα Od. 15.332.
Bright as with oil, bright, glossy (or perh. shining with actual oil ; cf. χιτῶνας ἦκα στίλβοντας ἐλαίῳ Il. 18.596) : καλύπτρην Il. 22.406 : κρήδεμνα Od. 1.334= Od. 16.416= Od. 18.210= Od. 21.65.

Of a ‘diadem of towers,’ bright,
glittering : Τροίης λιπαρὰ κρήδεμνα Od. 13.388.
Gentle in incidence or operation, pleasant : θέμιστας Il. 9.156, 298 : γήρᾳ Od. 11.136=Od. 23.283, Od. 19.368.
Of a gentle decline into the vale of years, gently, imperceptibly: γηρασκέμεν Od. 4.210.

div.head: λίς1.
div.p: (Referring to the female Il. 18.318 (though in masc. construction).)

div.head: λίς2.
div.p: Only in dat. λιτί Il. 18.352, Il. 23.254.
This form app. as acc. pl. neut. Od. 10.353.
Used for covering a corpse laid out to await funeral rites Il. 18.352.
For covering a cinerary urn Il. 23.254.
A cloth whereon to sit : ὑπὸ λῖτα πετάσσας Od. 1.130, Od. 10.353.
3 sing. impf. ἐλ(λ)ίσσετο Il. 6.45, Il. 12.49 (v.l. εἱλίσσετο, see ἑλίσσω 6), Il. 21.71: Od. 10.264.

To make entreaty or petition to, entreat, supplicate: πάντας Ἀχαιούς Il. 1.15, Δία λίσαι 394. Cf. Il. 2.15, Il. 6.45, Il. 9.465, Il. 12.49, Il. 15.660, Il. 21.71, Il. 22.35, etc. : Od. 2.68, Od. 6.142, Od. 8.157, Od. 12.53, Od. 15.261, Od. 22.311, etc.
With complementary infin. : λίσσεται ἔμπεδον εἶναι [πομπήν] Od. 8.30.

p.gloss: To beg, entreat, pray to do.

div.p: With infin. : μένειν σε Il. 1.174. Cf. Il. 1.283, Il. 4.379, Il. 8.372=Il. 15.77, Il. 9.451, 574, Il. 19.304, Il. 22.240 : Εὐρύμαχον παῦσαι τόξον Od. 21.278.
Sim. : ἔμʼ ἕταροι λίσσοντο τυρῶν αἰνυμένους ἰέναι πάλιν (to let the party...) Od. 9.224.
With dependent clause : λίσσεθʼ Ἥφαιστον ὅπως λύσειεν Ἄρηα Od. 8.344. Cf. Od. 3.19.
With acc. of the subject of entreaty : οἷ αὐτῷ θάνατον λιτέσθαι Il. 16.47.
With double acc. of the person entreated and of the subject : ταῦθʼ ἅ με λίσσεαι Od. 4.347=Od. 17.138. Cf. Od. 2.210.
To pray to (a divinity) : θεοὺς παρατρωπῶσʼ ἄνθρωποι λισσόμενοι Il. 9.501 : πρόφρων κε δία λιτοίμην (make my peace with him (i.e. with Ζεὺς ξείνιος)) Od. 14.406.
With infin.: τῷ Ἄτην ἅμʼ ἕπεσθαι Il. 9.511.
Of addressing the shades of the dead Od. 10.526, Od. 11.35.
With unbroken surface, smooth : πέτρη Od. 3.293, Od. 5.412, Od. 10.4.
To dig round about : φυτόν Od. 24.227.
To make entreaty or petition to, entreat, supplicate : μιν Il. 9.581. Cf. Il. 22.414, Il. 24.357 : Od. 7.145, Od. 10.481.
With infin. : πολλὰ λιτάνευεν [ἀνέμους] ἐλθέμεν Il. 23.196.
A prayer : εὐχωλῇσι λιτῇσί τε ἐλλισάμην (the two words hardly to be distinguished) Od. 11.34.
Personified : λιταί εἰσι (there are such beings as...) Διὸς κοῦραι Il. 9.502 (i.e. prayers of repentance, for forgiveness, addressed by an offender to the person injured).
The lobe of the ear Il. 14.182.
In pl., talk, discourse : τὸν ἔτερπε λόγοις Il. 15.393. Cf. Od. 1.56.
In pl., water for washing or bathing Il. 14.6, Il. 22.444, 445, Il. 23.44 : Od. 8.249, 451.
Fig. : λοετρῶν Ὠκεανοῖο (the baths of ocean) Il. 18.489 : =Od. 5.275.
An attendant who poured out water for the bath Od. 20.297.– λ. τρίπος, a caldron in which to heat water for the bathIl. 18.346 : Od. 8.435.
Libation : λοιβῆς τε κνίσης τε Il. 4.49 = Il. 24.70. Cf. Il. 9.500.
Applied ironically to the wine brought for the Cyclops Od. 9.349.
Baneful : λοίγια ἔργα, sad work, a bad businessIl. 1.518, 573.
Absol. in neut. pl. λοίγια in same sense : οἴω λοίγιʼ ἔσεσθαι Il. 21.533, Il. 23.310.
Bane, evil, death, destruction : λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι Il. 1.67. Cf. Il. 1.456, Il. 5.662, Il. 8.130, Il. 13.426, Il. 16.32, Il. 21.134, etc.
Of a prize, for the last, the last Il. 23.785.
Absol. in neut. pl. λοισθήϊα, the last prizeIl. 23.751.
A husk or skin : σιγαλόεντα, οἷόν τε κρομύοιο λοπὸν κάτα ἰσχαλέοιο Od. 19.233 (glistening as (there is glistening) over the skin of ..., i.e. glistening like the skin of ...).
Nom. sing. fem. pple. λούσασα Od. 5.264.
Infin. mid. λούεσθαι Il. 6.508, Il. 15.265. λοῦσθαι Od. 6.216.
Pf. pple. λελουμένος Il. 5.6. From λοέω (λοϝέω) impf. λόεον Od. 4.252.
Fut. mid. (or aor. subj.) λοέσσομαι Od. 6.221.
Pple. λοεσσάμενος, -η Il. 10.577, Il. 21.560 : Od. 1.310, Od. 6.96, Od. 8.427. (ἀπο-)
To wash the body of, cause to bathe : Τηλέμαχον λοῦσε Πολυκάστη Od. 3.464. Cf. Il. 5.905 : Od. 4.49, Od. 5.264, Od. 6.210, Od. 8.364, Od. 19.320, Od. 23.154, etc.
In reference to cleansing a corpse Il. 16.669, 679, Il. 18.350, Il. 24.582, 587.
In reference to horses : λοέσσας [ἵππους] ὕδατι Il. 23.282.
With ἀπό, to wash away or off : εἰς ὅ κε λούσῃ ἄπο βρότον Il. 14.7.

With double acc.
of what is cleansed and of what is washed away : ὄφρα Πάτροκλον λούσειαν ἄπο βρότον Il. 18.345.

In mid., to wash one's body, bathe oneself : ἐς ἀσαμίνθους βάντες λούσαντο Il. 10.576, λοεσσάμενος ποταμοῖο (genit. of space or material, in the ...) Il. 21.560. Cf. Il. 10.577: Od. 1.310, Od. 4.48, Od. 6.96, Od. 8.427, Od. 23.131, Od. 24.254, etc.
Of a horse : εἰωθὼς λούεσθαι ποταμοῖο Il. 6.508=Il. 15.265.
Fig. of a star : λελουμένος Ὠκεανοῖο Il. 5.6.
In mid., with ἀπό, to wash away or off from one's body : λούσασθαι ἄπο βρότον Il. 23.41.
The bristly back of a wild boar: φρίξας εὖ λοφιήν Od. 19.446.

A crest or plume on a helmet: δεινὸν λόφος καθύπερθεν ἔνευεν Il. 3.337=Il. 11.42=Il. 15.481=Il. 16.138, κόρυθος φάλον ἤλασεν ὑπὸ λόφον αὐτόν (just at the base of it) Il. 13.615. Cf. Il. 6.469, Il. 15.537, Il. 18.612, Il. 19.383=Il. 22.316 : Od. 22.124.
The crest or summit of a hill Od. 11.596.
An eminence or ridge : ὅθι Ἕρμαιος λ. ἐστίν Od. 16.471.
3 pl. λοχόωσι Od. 13.425, Od. 15.28. λοχῶσι Od. 14.181.
Nom. pl. masc. ppl.e λοχόωντες Od. 4.847, Od. 16.369.
To lie in wait for, lie in ambush for: λοχόωσί μιν νέοι Od. 13.425. Cf. Od. 4.847, Od. 14.181, Od. 15.28, Od. 16.369, Od. 22.53.
Absol. : ὅθι σφίσιν εἶκε λοχῆσαι Il. 18.520.
The lair of a wild beast : ἐν λόχμῃ κατέκειτο σῦς Od. 19.439.
For, to take part in, with a view to, an ambush : λόχονδʼ ἰέναι Il. 1.227. Cf. Od. 14.217.

A body of men lying in wait or in ambush or detailed for such a purpose : εἷσε λόχον Il. 6.189, μὴ λόχος εἰσέλθῃσι πόλιν (a body detailed to effect a surprise) Il. 8.522. Cf. Il. 4.392, Il. 13.285 : Od. 4.531, Od. 14.469.

A lying in wait, an ambush : λόχῳ ὑπεθωρήσσοντο (for ...) Il. 18.513, μὴ δείσητʼ Ἀργείων λόχον (any attempt at surprise on their part) Il. 24.779. Cf. Il. 13.277 : Od. 4.395, 441, Od. 11.525, Od. 16.463.
A place of concealment with a view to hostile action, a lurking-place : ἐκ λόχου ἀμπήδησεν Il. 11.379.
Applied to the Trojan horse Od. 4.277, Od. 8.515.
App. a band or troop : εἴ περ πεντήκοντα λόχοι ἀνθρώπων νῶϊ περισταῖεν Od. 20.49.
A pliant twig, a withy Il. 11.105 : Od. 9.427, Od. 10.166.
As a term of contempt, sorry, pitiful, good for nothing, of no account : ὅς τις πολέμοιο μεθείη λ, ἐών Il. 13.119. Cf. Il. 13.237 : Od. 9.454, Od. 18.107.

Bringing or inferring wretchedness or woe, wretched, woeful, miserable, painful, distressing, baleful, disastrous: ὄλεθρον Il. 2.873, γήραϊ Il. 5.153, ἀγγελίης Il. 17.642. Cf. Il. 6.16, Il. 13.346, Il. 22.242, etc. : νόστον Od. 1.327, πένθεϊ Od. 2.70, κήδεα Od. 11.369. Cf. Od. 1.341, Od. 3.87, Od. 23.224, Od. 24.250, etc.
As epithet of war : δαϊ Il. 13.286, Il. 24.739.
Bringing evil consequences, ill-wrought : ἀνδροκτασίης Il. 23.86.
Carring bale, deadly, fatal : σήματα Il. 6.168.
Of drugs, working evil effects, bringing to ill Od. 4.230, Od. 10.236.
Of a wound, deep-struck, sore Il. 15.393, Il. 19.49.
Of garments, foul, sorry, evil Od. 16.457, Od. 17.203=Od. 24.158, Od. 17.338, 573.
Absol. in neut. pl., things of ill, evils : πόλεμοις καὶ ἄκοντες καὶ ὀϊστοί, λυγρά Od. 14.226.
Evil fortune, ill : ᾧ κε τῶν λυγρῶν δώῃ Il. 24.531. Cf. Od. 18.134.
Bane, evil : ταῦτʼ ἐμεήσατο λυγρά Od. 3.303.– In ethical sense, evil, mischief : λυγρὰ ἰδυῖα (cherishing evil in her heart) Od. 11.432 (see εἴδω III.12).
So as to inflict pain, sorely : πεπληγυῖα Il. 5.763.
Gore: λύθρῳ παλάσσετο χεῖρας Il. 11.169. Cf. Il. 6.268, Il. 3.503 : Od. 22.402=Od. 23.48.
[λυκ-, light, as in λύχνος + βα-, βαίνω. The going of light.]
Thus, prob., the period of time in which daylight goes and comes again : τοῦδʼ αὐτοῦ λυκάβαντος (within a day's space, ere the sun shall set again) Od. 19.306.
(This interpretation involves bracketing Od. 14.161-162 (=Od. 19.306-307); but is obviously superior to the interpretation a year.)
In pl., defilement, impurities : ἀπὸ χροὸς λύματα πάντα κάντα κάθηρεν Il. 14.171. Cf. Il. 1.314.
A releasing or ransoming : ἀνάβλησις λύσιος Il. 24.655.
A means of release from the toils of something, a means of escape : θανάτου λύσιν Od. 9.421.
Rage, fury, lust of battle : λύσσαν ἔχων ὀλοήν Il. 9.305. Cf. Il. 9.239, Il. 21.542.
One who is raging mad : τοῦτον κύνα λυσσητῆρα (that mad dog) Il. 8.299.
Raging, consumed with lust of battle.
3 sing. aor. pass. λύθη Il. 5.296, Il. 8.123, 315, Il. 17.298.
3 pl. plupf. ἐλέλυντο Od. 22.186. λέλυντο Il. 13.85.
(ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐξανα-, κατα-, ὑπεκπρο-, ὑπο-.)
To loosen, undo, unfasten, untie : ζωστῆρα Il. 4.215. Cf. Il. 16.804 : πρυμνήσια Od. 2.418. Cf. Od. 3.392, Od. 5.459, Od. 13.77, etc.

In mid.:
λύοντο τεύχεʼ ἀπʼ ὤμων Il. 17.318.
In proper mid. sense of unfastening something from oneself : ἀπὸ στήθεσφιν ἐλύσαθʼ ἱμάντα Il. 14.214.
Of loosening the maiden girdle Od. 11.245.
To undo the fastening of : ἀσκόν Od. 10.47.

To set free from bonds or confinement, to release, relax one's hold upon : λῦσαι γέροντα Od. 4.422, ἐπεὶ ἐκ δεσμοῖο λύθεν Od. 8.360. Cf. Od. 8.345, 347, Od. 10.298, 387, Od. 11.296, Od. 12.53, 163, 193.
In mid., to set oneself free Od. 9.463.
To rescue from bonds, effect the release of Il. 15.22.
In mid. : ἦ τοὺς λυσόμενος δεῦρʼ ἔρχεαι; Od. 10.284. Cf. Od. 10.385.
To release (from trouble or sickness) : θεοὶ κακότητος ἔλυσαν Od. 5.397. Cf. Od. 13.321.
To set free (a captive) for ransom: παῖδʼ ἐμοὶ λύσαιτε Il. 1.20. Cf. Il. 1.29, Il. 21.80.
With genit. of price : ἔλυσεν ἀποίνων Il. 11.106.
Of restoring the armour of a slain foe Il. 17.163.
In mid., to effect the ransoming of : ξεῖνός μιν ἐλύσατο Il. 21.42. Cf. Il. 1.13 = 372, Il. 10.378.
So of effecting the restoration of a corpse Il. 24.118 = 146 = 195, 175, 237, 502, 685.
To unyoke (horses, etc.) : λῦσαν ἵππους Il. 8.433. Cf. Il. 5.369, Il. 11.620, Il. 18.244, Il. 23.27, Il. 24.576, etc.: Od. 4.35, 39, Od. 7.6.
To settle or compose (a dispute, quarrel or difference) : καὶ ἀνδράσι νείκεα λύει Od. 7.74. Cf. Il. 14.205 = 304.
To dissolve or dismiss (an assembly), allow or cause (it) to disperse : λῦσαν ἀγορήν Il. 1.305. Cf. Il. 2.808, Il. 19.276, Il. 24.1 : Od. 2.69, 257.
To disperse (cares) : λύων μελεδήματα θυμοῦ Il. 23.62 : =Od. 20.56, Od. 23.343.
With notion of destruction, to resolve into the component parts, disintegrate, cause to part : σπάρτα λέλυνται (lie in decay) Il. 2.135 : ὄφρʼ ἀπὸ τοίχους λῦσε κλύδων τρόπιος Od. 12.421.
To cause (stitches) to give way or come undone : ῥαφαὶ ἐλέλυντο ἱμάντων Od. 22.186.
To bring to ruin, destroy : ὄφρα Τροίης κρήδεμνα λύωμεν Il. 16.100. Cf. Il. 2.118=Il. 9.25 : Od. 13.388.
To break up or dissipate (the vital forces), to break up, dissipate or suspend the vital forces or the strength in (the limbs, the heart, etc.), to cause (the limbs, etc.) to give way or collapse.

div.head: a
div.p: By the application of force to fatal or nearly fatal effect : οὔτησε ξυστῷ, λῦσε δὲ γυῖα Il. 4.469, τοῦ λύθη γυχή τε μένος τε Il. 5.296. Cf. Il. 5.176, Il. 7.12, Il. 13.360, Il. 16.332, Il. 17.29, etc. : Od. 14.69, 236, Od. 18.238, 242, Od. 24.381.
In reference to an animal : λῦσεν βοὸς μένος Od. 3.450.

div.head: b
div.p: By strong emotion, fear, stupor : τὸν ἄτη φρένας εἷλε, λύθεν δʼ ὑπὸ γυῖα Il. 16.805. Cf. Il. 18.31, Il. 21.114, 425 : Οδυσσῆος λύτο γούνατα καὶ ἦτορ Od. 5.297= 406= Od. 22.147. Cf. Od. 4.703, Od. 18.212, 341, Od. 22.68, Od. 23.205, Od. 24.345.

div.head: c
div.p: By weariness, exhaustion, hardship : καμάτῳ ὑπὸ γυῖα λέλυνται Il. 7.6. Cf. Il. 13.85 : Od. 8.233, Od. 20.118.
Sim. of the effects of old age Il. 8.103.
Of relaxation of the limbs in sleep Od. 4.794=Od. 18.189.
To treat without regard to right or decency, commit outrage upon.
With direct and cognate acc. : λώβης, ἣν ἐμὲ λωβήσασθε Il. 13.623.
To play a trick upon, mock, make game of: τίπτε με λωβεύεις; Od. 23.15. Cf. Od. 23.26.

Treatment without regard to right or decency, despiteful usage, outrage : πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πᾶσαν ἐμοὶ δόμεναι λώβην Il. 9.387. Cf. Il. 11.142, Il. 13.622, Il. 19.208 : Od. 18.347=Od. 20.285, Od. 19.373, Od. 20.169, Od. 24.326.
A cause or occasion of reproach or opprobrium : λώβη τάδε γʼ ἔσσεται, εἰ... Il. 7.97. Cf. Il. 18.180 : Od. 18.225, Od. 24.433.
A mark for mockery, an object of ridicule Il. 3.42.
One who utters despiteful or scurrilous words, an insulter, a foulmouthed fellow Il. 2.275, Il. 11.385.
A good-for-nothing person, a worthless fellow Il. 24.239.
App., despitefully used by fortune, wretched, miserable Il. 24.531.
Better, more profitable or advisable : τόδε λωΐτερον ἔμμεναι Od. 1.376=Od. 2.141.
Absol. : χρή σε δόμεναι καὶ λώϊον ἠέ περ ἄλλοι σίτον (a larger portion) Od. 17.417.
Better, more profitable or advisable : τόδε σφιν λ. ἐστιν Od. 2.169.
Absol. with infin. : λ. ἔστι δῶρʼ ἀποαιρεῖσθαι Il. 1.229.
So with ὧδε : δοκέει μοι ὧδε λ. ἔσσεσθαι Il. 6.339.
As adv., better, more fully : γνωσόμεθʼ ἀλλήλων καὶ λ. Od. 23.109.
Overgrown with λωτός : πεδία λωτοῦντα Il. 12.283.
(V.l. λωτεῦντα (λωτέοντα) fr. λωτέω, to teem with λωτός).
A plant, perh. some kind of trefoil or clover. Collectively : ἵπποι λωτὸν ἐρεπτόμενοι Il. 2.776. Cf. Il. 14.348, Il. 21.351 : Od. 4.603.
A fruit of some kind, described as having an irresistibly seductive taste Od. 9.93, 97, 102.– The tree producing the fruit Od. 9.94.
To make pause, cease, give over : ὅδε τάχα λωφήσει Il. 21.292.
To find respite or relief from.
A particle used in affirmations or strong protestations, followed by acc. of a deity or thing invoked. Affirmatively with ναί : ναὶ μὰ τόδε σκῆπτρον Il. 1.234 (by this...).
With οὐ in negation : οὐ μὰ Ζῆνα Il. 23.43. Cf. Il. 1.86 : Od. 20.339.
In women : γυναῖκα θήσατο μαζόν Il. 24.58. Cf. Il. 5.393, Il. 22.80, 83 : πάϊς οἱ ἦν ἐπὶ μαζῷ Od. 11.448. Cf. Od. 19.483.
In men, the mammilla : βάλε στῆθος παρὰ μαζὸν δεξιόν Il. 4.480. Cf. Il. 4.123, 528, Il. 5.145, Il. 8.121, 313, Il. 11.108, 321, Il. 15.577, Il. 17.606 : Od. 22.82.
A word of address to a woman older than the speaker, good mother, dame, gossip Od. 2.349, 372, Od. 17.499, Od. 19.16, 482, 500, Od. 20.129, Od. 23.11, 35, 59, 81, 171.

Pple. μαιμώων Il. 15.742.
Fem. μαιμώωσα Il. 5.661, Il. 15.542. (ἀνα-, περι-.)
To be eager or quiver for action, show eager alacrity in action : μαίμησέ οἱ ἦτορ Il. 5.670, μαιμώων ἔφεπʼ ἔγχεϊ Il. 15.742. Cf. Il. 13.75, 78.
Of the eager course of a weapon Il. 5.661, Il. 15.542.
A madwoman : μεγάροιο διέσσυτο μαινάσι ἴση Il. 22.460.
To rage, act like a madman, be in unreasoning rage or fury : σὺ δὲ μαίνεαι οὐκέτʼ ἀνεκτῶς Od. 9.350. Cf. Il. 8.360 : Od. 18.406, Od. 21.298.
Of the raging of fire : ὡς ὅτε πῦρ οὔρεσι μαίνηται Il. 15.606.
Of martial frenzy : εἰ οὕτω μαίνεσθαι ἐάσομεν Ἄρηα Il. 5.717. Cf. Il. 6.101, Il. 8.355, Il. 9.238, Il. 15.605, Il. 16.245, Il. 21.5 : Od. 11.537.
With cognate acc. : οὐχ ὅ γʼ ἄνευθε θεοῦ τάδε μαίνεται (makes this wild work) Il. 5.185.
In pple., a madman : τοῦτον μαινόμενον Il. 5.831.
Of a weapon : εἰ καὶ ἐμὸν δόρυ μαίνεται Il. 8.111. Cf. Il. 16.75.
To be distracted or out of one's wits.
In pple., a madman : μαινόμενε, φρένας ἠλέ Il. 15.128.
In fem., a madwoman : μαινομένῃ ἐϊκυῖα Il. 6.389.
Of the wits, etc. : τί σφῶϊν μαίνεται ἦτορ; Il. 8.413. Cf. Il. 24.114 = 135.
To make search, search, seek : μαίεσθαι προτέρω Od. 14.356.
To search through, examine : κευθμῶνας Od. 13.367.
To seek out, get : Πηλεύς μοι γυναῖκά γε μάσσεται αὐτός Il. 9.394 (v.l. γαμέσσεται (γαμέω)).
Having great resources, great, powerful, influential, wealthy : ἀνδρὸς μάκαρος κατʼ ἄρουραν Il. 11.68. Cf. Od. 1.217.
Happy, fortunate : ὦ μάκαρ Ἀτρεΐδη Il. 3.182. Cf. Il. 24.377.
Superl. μακάρτατος : σεῖο μακάρτατος (beyond thee, in reference to thee) Od. 11.483. Cf. Od. 6.158.
As epithet of the gods, happy, blessed, living at ease, dwelling serene Il. 1.339, 406, 599, etc. : Od. 1.82, Od. 5.7, Od. 8.281, etc.
Absol. in pl., the blessed gods, the gods Od. 10.299.
To pronounce blessed, esteem fortunate Od. 15.538=Od. 17.165=Od. 19.311.
Long (as applied to weapons commonly a mere epithet) : ἔγχεα Il. 3.135. Cf. Il. 3.137, Il. 5.297, Il. 13.497, etc. : οὐρῇσιν Od. 10.215. Cf. Od. 12.229, Od. 21.121, Od. 22.149, 251, 279, 293.
In superl. : τὰ μακρότατʼ ἔγχεα Il. 14.373.

High, tall, lofty (sometimes, doubtless, with connotation of sense (3)) : τείχεα Il. 4.34, Il. 22.507, δένδρεα Il. 9.541, Il. 11.88, οὔρεα Il. 13.18 : κίονας Od. 1.54, δένδρεα Od. 5.238, τείχεα Od. 7.44, πίτυσσιν Od. 9.186, κλίμακα Od. 10.558, ἐρινεόν Od. 12.432, ὄζοι 436, etc.
In superl. : ἐλάτην, ἣ μακροτάτη πεφυυῖα αἰθέρʼ ἵκανεν Il. 14.288.
In comp. : μακρότερόν μιν θῆκεν Od. 8.20. Cf. Od. 18.195.
Great, thick, stout : ἕρματα Il. 1.486, ὀχῆα Il. 12.121, 291, Il. 13.124, σανίδες Il. 18.276 : δούρατα Od. 5.162, 370, ἐπηγκενίδεσσιν Od. 5.253.
Of waves, great, big, swollen Il. 2.144 : Od. 5.109, Od. 9.147, Od. 24.110.
Wide, broad, spacious : ἠϊόνος στόμα Il. 14.36. Cf. Il. 15.358.
Of great content, great, capacious : φρείατα Il. 21.197.
In reference to periods of time, long : ἤματα Od. 10.470, Od. 18.367=Od. 22.301. Cf. Od. 11.373.
Of a desire, great, of one's heart : τόδε μακρὸν ἐέλδωρ Od. 23.54.

In neut. sing. μακρόν as adv. In reference to the utterance of sound, loudly, with full voice, at the top of one's voice : μ. ἄϋσεν Il. 3.81. Cf. Il. 5.101, Il. 6.66, Il. 11.285, Il. 20.50, etc. : Od. 6.117.
So in neut. pl. μακρά : βοῶν Il. 2.224.
Of a bull : μ. μεμυκώς Il. 18.580.

In reference to one's gait or movement, with long strides or steps, striding along or about, strutting along : μ. βιβάντα Il. 3.22. Cf. Il. 7.213, Il. 13.809, Il. 15.307, 676, 686, Il. 16.534 : Od. 11.539.

Intensively with adjectives and adverbs, very, exceedingly, quite, just, altogether, or the like : μ. ὦκα Il. 2.52, μ. νήπιος Il. 7.401. Cf. Il. 1.156, Il. 3.204, Il. 5.710, Il. 9.360, Il. 12.382, Il. 13.152, Il. 18.254, etc. : μ. ἀτρεκέως Od. 1.179, μ. καλόν 301. Cf. Od. 2.200, Od. 3.20, Od. 4.169, 439, Od. 5.26, 161, 342, Od. 10.111, Od. 18.370, etc.
Strengthening πᾶς Il. 2.10, Il. 13.741, Il. 15.546, etc. : Od. 2.306, Od. 5.216, etc.
With comp., by far : πρότερος μ. Il. 10.124.

Intensively with verbs and participles, much, greatly, in large measure, deeply, heartily, with good will, earnestly, eagerly, strongly, or the like : θαρσήσας μ. Il. 1.85, φεῦγε μ. (by all means) 173, μ. ἔκλυον 218. Cf. Il. 1.217, Il. 3.25 (greedily), Il. 4.225, 379, Il. 5.471 (bitterly), Il. 7.286, Il. 9.75 (they sorely need...), 318, 419, Il. 10.229, 251 (quickly), Il. 11.710 (well), Il. 12.51 (loudly), Il. 13.146 (to close quarters), 463 (the need is dire), 708 (keeping closely together), Il. 14.58 (closely), Il. 17.502 (from close at hand), 571 (carefully), Il. 23.63, Il. 24.663, etc. : μ. ἀσχαλόωσιν Od. 1.304, μ. χατέουσα Od. 2.249. Cf. Od. 4.472 (clearly), Od. 5.341, Od. 6.44, 319 (skilfully), Od. 7.32 (willingly), Od. 8.316, 413 (with all my heart), Od. 12.108 (very close), Od. 14.361, Od. 18.381, Od. 24.400, etc.

Emphasizing an expression generally rather than attaching itself to particular words, of a surety, surely, verily : ἦ μ. δή σε κιχάνεται ὄλεθρος Il. 11.441. Cf. Il. 2.241, Il. 5.278, Il. 6.255, Il. 9.40, Il. 17.34, Il. 18.12, etc. : ἀλλὰ μ. οὔ πως ἔστι Διὸς νόον παρεξελθεῖν Od. 5.103. Cf. Od. 1.384, Od. 2.325, Od. 5.286, Od. 14.391, Od. 16.8, Od. 19.40, etc.

Yielding to the touch, soft, into or upon which one sinks or settles down comfortably: εὐνῇ Il. 9.618, Il. 10.75, Il. 22.504. Cf. Il. 14.349 : κώεσιν Od. 3.38. Cf. Od. 4.124, Od. 20.58, Od. 22.196 (in sarcasm), Od. 23.290, 349.
Soft or yielding in texture, readily adapting itself to one's form or to what it covers : χιτῶνα Il. 2.42, πέπλοισιν Il. 24.796. Cf. Od. 1.437, Od. 19.234.
Of meadows, yielding to the tread, covered with rich grass, grassy : λειμῶνες Od. 5.72, Od. 9.133.
Of cultivated land, yielding readily to the plough, easily cultivable : νειόν Il. 18.541.
Of speech, gentle, winning, conciliatory : ἐπέεσσιν Il. 1.582, Il. 6.337. Cf. Od. 1.56, Od. 10.70, 422, Od. 16.286=Od. 19.5.
Of sleep, stealing gently upon one, sweet Il. 10.2=Il. 24.678, Il. 14.359 : Od. 15.6, Od. 18.201.

So of a gentle or
painless death : θάνατον Od. 18.202.
In reference to sleeping, softly, at ease : ἐνεύδειν Od. 3.350. Cf. Od. 24.255.
With adjectives and adverbs, in the highest degree, most : μ. λαμπρόν Il. 5.5, ἄγχι Il. 14.460. Cf. Il. 6.433, Il. 8.84, 326, Il. 13.568, 683, Il. 14.399, Il. 22.410.
With a vb., in a very high degree, greatly, much : ὅπως πετάσειε μ. θυμόν Od. 18.160.

In general intensive use, most, especially, principally, chiefly : Ἀτρεΐδα μ. [λίσσετο] Il. 1.16, τὸν μ. τῖεν Il. 2.21. Cf. Il. 2.589, Il. 3.97, Il. 4.96, Il. 8.500, etc. : ὄσσαν, ἥ τε μάλιστα φέρει κλέος Od. 1.283. Cf. Od. 1.342, 359, Od. 4.434, Od. 8.582, etc.
In reference to something on the point of happening, nearly : μέμβλωκε μ. ἦμαρ Od. 17.190.
With adjectives, in a higher degree, more : τιμήεσσα Od. 18.162.
More, rather : μ. ἐπήρατος ἱπποβότοιο (rather... than...) Od. 4.606.

div.head: a
div.p: More, yet more, rather : Ἑκτορέοις ἄρα μ. ἐπὶ φρένα θῆχʼ ἱεροῖσιν Il. 10.46, μή μοι μ. θυμὸν ὀρίνῃς Il. 24.568. Cf. Il. 8.470, Il. 13.272, 638, 776, Il. 19.200 : μ. ἔτʼ ἤ τὸ πάροιθεν Od. 1.322. Cf. Od. 1.89, 351, Od. 4.819, Od. 8.154, Od. 15.198, Od. 18.216, Od. 20.166.
Better, in better wise : μ. ἅρμα οἴσετον Il. 5.231.
Better, preferably, for choice : ἀμφοτέρω μ. Il. 12.344= 357.

div.head: b
div.p: The more, all the more, the better, all the better : ἀπὸ θυμοῦ μ. ἐμοὶ ἔσεαι Il. 1.563, ὄφρʼ ἔτι μ. μαχώμεθα Il. 19.231. Cf. Il. 2.81, Il. 5.208, Il. 9.257, 700, Il. 19.16, Il. 21.305, etc. : μ. πιέζειν Od. 4.419. Cf. Od. 2.202, Od. 9.13, Od. 18.22, Od. 19.117, 249, etc.

Affirmative particle : οὐ μὰν οὐδʼ Ἀχιλεὺς μάρναται Il. 4.512, ἄγρει μάν (nay come!) Il. 5.765, ἔσται μὰν ὅτʼ ἄν...(the time will yet come when...) Il. 8.373. Cf. Il. 8.512, Il. 13.414, etc. : οὐ μὰν ἡμῖν ἀπὸ σκοποῦ μυθεῖται Od. 11.344. Cf. Od. 17.470.
In aor., to have learned, know : ἔργα κακά Od. 17.226, Od. 18.362.
With infin., to have been brought up or trained to be : ἐπεὶ μάθον ἔμμεναι ἐσθλός Il. 6.444.
To utter prophecy or divination, prophesy, divine : ἤ ἐτεὸν μαντεύεται Il. 2.300 : νῦν τοι ἐγὼ μαντεύσομαι Od. 1.200. Cf. Od. 2.170, 178, Od. 15.172, Od. 17.154, Od. 20.380, Od. 23.251.
To be seer, act as seer : μαντευόμενος κατεγήρα κυκλώπεσσιν Od. 9.510. Cf. Od. 15.255.
To prophesy in regard to : ταῦτα μαντεύεσθαι Od. 2.180.
To foretell, prophesy, presage : ὄλεθρον Il. 16.859. Cf. Il. 1.107, Il. 19.420.
A prophetic warning : μαντήϊα τειρεσίαο κίρκης τε Od. 12.272.
The art of divination : ὃς μαντοσύνῃ ἐκέκαστο Od. 9.509. Cf. Il. 1.72.
In pl., app. referring to the various means of divination : ὃς περὶ πάντων ᾔδεε μαντοσύνας Il. 2.832=Il. 11.330.
To quench (fire) : ἐπεὶ φλὸξ ἐμαράνθη (had died down) Il. 9.212, πυρκαϊὴ ἐμαραίνετο Il. 23.228.
To behave like a madman, rage : μαργαίνειν ἐπὶ θεοῖσιν Il. 5.882.
Out of one's wits, beside oneself Od. 23.11.
Applied to the belly, raging, unappeasable Od. 18.2.
To be bright, to glitter, flash, gleam, sparkle : ἔντεα μαρμαίροντα Il. 12.195. Cf. Il. 13.22, 801, Il. 16.279, 664, Il. 18.131, 617, Il. 23.27.
Of the eyes : ὄμματα μαρμαίροντα Il. 3.397.
Bright, glittering, gleaming Il. 14.273, Il. 17.594, Il. 18.480.
A stone of some such substance as quartz Il. 12.380 : Od. 9.499.
A twinkling or flickering : μαρμαρυγὰς ποδῶν Od. 8.265.

To fight, do battle, take part in the fight : οὐδʼ Ἀχιλεὺς μάρναται Il. 4.513. Cf. Il. 5.33, Il. 7.301, Il. 11.74, Il. 16.195, Il. 18.453, etc. : πρόπαν ἦμαρ ἐμαρνάμεθα Od. 24.41. Cf. Od. 3.85, Od. 11.513, Od. 16.98 = 116, Od. 24.39, 507.
With cognate acc. : ὅσα μαρνάμεθα Od. 3.108.
With dat. : μαρνάμενον μενελάῳ Il. 3.307, μάρναντο Τρωσίν τε καὶ Ἕκτορι Il. 13.720. Cf. Il. 6.204, Il. 9.327, Il. 11.190 = 205, Il. 15.475, 557 : Od. 9.50, Od. 22.228.
With ἐπί: μάρνα-σθαι δηΐοισιν ἐπʼ ἀνδράσιν Il. 9.317=Il. 17.148.
Of fighting otherwise than with arms, to box Od. 18.31.
To fight with words, quarrel, wrangle, dispute : εἰ σφῶϊν πυθοίατο μαρναμένιϊν Il. 1.257.
With cognate acc. ἕλκεα, ἅ κεν μάρπτῃσι κεραυνός (which the thunderbolt shall make by fastening upon...) Il. 8.405= 419.
To catch up, over-take Il. 21.564, Il. 22.201.
To bring oneself in contact with, touch : οὐδὲ χθόνα μάρπτε ποδοῖιν Il. 14.228.
Of sleep, to come upon : οὐχ Ἑρμείαν ὕπνος ἔμαρπτεν Il. 24.679. Cf. Il. 23.62 : =Od. 20.56.
So of old age : ἐπεὶ κατὰ γῆρας ἔμαρψεν Od. 24.390.
A giving of information, a denouncing.
One who is to bear or can bear testimony, a witness : τὼ αὐτὼ μάρτυροι ἔστων Il. 1.338. Cf. Il. 2.302.
A witness invoked in sanction of something (cf. ἐπιμάρτυρος) : ὑμεῖς μάρτυροι ἔστε Il. 3.280. Cf. Il. 7.76, Il. 14.274, Il. 22.255 : μάρτυροι ἀμφοτέροισι θεοὶ [ἔστων] Od. 14.394. Cf. Od. 1.273.
An ever-present witness, a protector or guardian : ἱκέτας, οἶσι Ζεὺς μ. [ἐστιν] Od. 16.423.
In neut. μᾶσσον as adv., further : ἥσειν Od. 8.203.
The mouth : μάστακα χερσὶ πίεζεν Od. 4.287. Cf. Od. 23.76.
To apply the μάστιξ to, touch up (horses or mules): μάστιξεν ἵππους Il. 5.768= Il. 10.530= Il. 11.519. Cf. Il. 8.117, Il. 5.366= Il. 8.45= Il. 22.400 := Od. 3.484 = 494= Od. 15.192, Od. 6.82.

A whip (following the indications of Il. 11.532, Il. 15.352, Il. 23.362 : Od. 6.316 ; see also Il. 23.500 under μάστις and Il. 20.171 under μαστίω); but μάστιξ in Il. 23.384 and κέντρον in Il. 23.387 are evidently represented as identical, and seem to be the same as the ἱμάσθλη of 582, and there are grounds for explaining all as a pliant rod with a metal point serving both as whip and goad (which involves taking ἱμάντες in Il. 23.363 in sense reins) : μάστιγι θοῶς ἐπεμαίεθʼ ἵππους Il. 5.748= Il. 8.392. Cf. (besides as above) Il. 5.226, 840, Il. 10.500, Il. 16.430, 479, 482= Il. 24.441, Il. 19.395, Il. 23.390, 510, 642, Il. 24.326 : Od. 6.81, 316.
Fig. of the lash of Zeus : Διὸς μάστιγι δαμέντες (ἐδάμημεν) Il. 12.37, Il. 13.812.
Dat. μάστι Il. 23.500. =μάστιξ. : μάστι ἔλαυνε κατωμαδόν Il. 23.500. Cf. Od. 15.182.
To apply the μάστιξ to, touch up, one's horses : μάστιε νῦν Il. 17.622.
In mid. of a lion lashing himself with his tail Il. 20.171.
To do ineffective work, show oneself clumsy or unskilful : ἀπέκοψε παρήορον οὐδὲ μάτησεν Il. 16.474.
Of horses, to shirk their work, grow restive Il. 5.233.
To be at a loss or at fault : οὐ δηθὰ ματεύσομεν Il. 14.110.
Ill directed or ill judged action, folly Od. 10.79.
App. a dagger : μαχαίρας χρυσείας ἐξ ἀργυρέων τελαμώνων Il. 18.597.
acc. sing. masc. pple. See μάχομαι.

War, battle, armed conflict, fighting : μάχῃ Τρώεσσιν ἀρήγειν Il. 1.521, ἔσχοντο μάχης Il. 3.84. Cf. Il. 4.225, Il. 5.157, Il. 7.290, Il. 11.409, Il. 13.483, Il. 15.15, Il. 17.142, Il. 22.218, Il. 24.385, etc. : Od. 4.497.

A battle, armed conflict, fight : μάχην ἐμάχοντο Il. 12.175, ἀντιόωντες τῆσδε μάχης Il. 20.126. Cf. Il. 1.177, Il. 5.456, 763, Il. 11.336, Il. 12.436, Il. 13.789, Il. 17.261, Il. 20.18, etc. : Od. 9.54, Od. 11.612.– μάχη τινός, a fighting with a person : Αἴαντος ἀλέεινε μάχην (did not care to engage him) Il. 11.542.

In concrete sense, a force engaged in fighting, an embattled host, a battle array, a fighting throng : ἀρτύνθη μάχη (the lines were re-formed) Il. 11.216, μάχη ἐπὶ πᾶσα φαάνθη Il. 17.650. Cf. Il. 5.167, 824, Il. 13.337, Il. 14.155, Il. 24.402, etc.
In local sense, a field of battle : μάχης ἐπʼ ἀριστερά Il. 5.355. Cf. Il. 17.368, etc.
The art of war, war, fighting : μάχης εὖ εἰδότε πάσης Il. 2.823= Il. 12.100, Il. 5.11, 549. Cf. Il. 5.634, Il. 13.811.
A warrior : νέοι σε τείρουσι μαχηταί Il. 8.102.
With implied notion of stoutness or skill : μικρὸς δέμας, ἀλλὰ μ. Il. 5.801. Cf. Il. 16.186 : Od. 3.112, Od. 4.202, Od. 18.261.
With whom one may fight, to be fought with Od. 12.119.
Lust; app., satisfaction or scope for the satisfaction thereof: ἥ οἱ πόρε μαχλοσύνην ἀλεγεινήν Il. 24.30.
Fut. μαχήσομαι Il. 1.298, Il. 3.290, Il. 9.32, Il. 21.498.
Acc. sing. masc. pple. μαχεσσάμενον Il. 3.393.
Infin. μαχέσασθαι Il. 3.20, Il. 5.496, Il. 7.74, Il. 8.168, Il. 20.171, Il. 22.223, etc. μαχέσσασθαι Il. 15.633 : Od. 18.39. μαχήσασθαι Il. 5.483 : Od. 2.245. (ἀμφι-, προ-)

To fight, do battle, take part in the fight, engage in fight : μαχόμην κατʼ ἔμʼ αὐτόν Il. 1.271, μετὰ πρώτοισι μάχεσθαι Il. 5.536. Cf. Il. 1.153, Il. 3.290, Il. 7.140, Il. 12.2, Il. 15.698, Il. 20.408, Il. 22.243, etc. : οἳ ἄστυ πέρι Πριάμοιο μάχοντο Od. 5.106. Cf. Od. 11.403, Od. 14.491, Od. 16.171, Od. 17.471, Od. 22.65, 245, Od. 24.113.
Of single combat : Ἀλέξανδρος καὶ Μενέλαος μαχήσονται περὶ σεῖο Il. 3.137. Cf. Il. 3.20, Il. 7.40, Il. 20.88, Il. 21.160, etc.
To box : ὁ ξεῖνος καὶ Ἶρος ἐρίζετον ἀλλήλοιϊν χερσὶ μαχέσσασθαι Od. 18.39. Cf. Il. 23.621.
To fight, engage in fight, do battle, with.
With ἐπί: ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν Il. 5.124, Il. 11.442, Il. 20.26. Cf. Il. 5.244.
With dat. : μενοινώω καὶ οἶυς Ἕκτορι μάχεσθαι Il. 13.80. Cf. Il. 1.298, Il. 3.435, Il. 7.74, Il. 20.179, etc.
With cognate acc. : μάχην ἐμάχοντο Il. 12.175. Cf. Il. 2.121, Il. 3.435, Il. 18.533, etc. : Od. 9.54.
To contend with in manly sports.
With dat. : τίς ἂν φιλέοντι μάχοιτο; Od. 8.208.
Of fighting with a beast : θηρὶ μαχέσσασθαι Il. 15.633.

Of a beast attacking
or fighting with men : ὡς κύων ὑλάει μέμονέν τε μάχεσθαι Od. 20.15. Cf. Il. 20.171.
Of beasts or birds fighting : ὥς τʼ αἰγυπιοὶ μεγάλα κλάζοντε μάχωνται Il. 16.429. Cf. Il. 16.758, 824.
To fight with words, quarrel, wrangle, dispute, contend : ἀντιβίοισι μαχεσσαμένω ἐπέεσσιν Il. 1.304. Cf. Il. 1.8, Il. 2.377.
To oppose, set oneself against, thwart.
With dat. : οὐκ ἐθέλησα Ποσειδάωνι μάχεσθαι Od. 13.341.
To be up in arms against (a person), assume an attitude of protest in regard to (him), find fault with or upbraid (him).
With dat. : σοὶ πάντες μαχόμεσθα· σὺ γὰρ ... Il. 5.875. Cf. Il. 6.329, Il. 9.32, Il. 13.118.
In vain, to no purpose, fruitlessly : μ. ἄπρηκτον πόλεμον πολεμίζειν Il. 2.120.
For no good reason, without aim or object so far as one is concerned : μ. ἕνεκʼ ἀλλοτρίων ἀχέων Il. 20.298.
In unseemly wise, without regard for right, decency or established usage : μ., ἀτὰρ οὐ κατὰ κόσμον Il. 2.214, Il. 5.759. Cf. Il. 13.627 : Od. 3.138.
Without justification or good reason, idly, thoughtlessly, frivolously, lightly : μ. αὔτως εὐχετάασθαι Il. 20.348. Cf. Il. 15.40 : Od. 16.111.
Without determined course, idly : ἦ μ. ἀλάλησθε; Od. 3.72 = Od. 9.253.
Nom. dual μεμᾶῶτε Il. 5.569, Il. 6.120, Il. 20.159, Il. 22.243, Il. 23.814. μεμαότε Il. 13.197.
3 sing. μέμονε Il. 12.304, Il. 16.435, Il. 18.176, Il. 21.315 : Od. 15.521, Od. 20.15. (For the forms cf. γέγαα, γέγονα under γίγνομαι A.) (ἐμ-.)
To be eager, anxious or ready : ἐπεὶ μεμάασί γε πολλοί (are ready to volunteer) Il. 10.236, μέμονεν ἶσα θεοῖσιν (his heart swells like that of a god) Il. 21.315.

p.gloss: To be eager, anxious or ready, show eagerness, anxiety or readiness, strive or struggle, to do something, to be bent or set on doing something.

div.p: With pres. or aor. infin. : μέμασαν μάχεσθαι Il. 2.863, διαπραθέειν μεμαῶτες Il. 9.532. Cf. Il. 1.590, Il. 4.40, 304 (be carried away by his eagerness), Il. 5.852, Il. 13.182, Il. 18.156, Il. 22.413, etc. : Od. 4.351, Od. 5.18, Od. 11.210, Od. 17.520, Od. 20.15, etc.
With fut. infin. : μέμασαν τεῖχος ῥήξειν Il. 12.197. Cf. Il. 2.543, Il. 12.200, 218 : Od. 15.521, Od. 24.395.
With genit. : μεμαῶτα μάχης Il. 9.655, μεμαότε ἀλκῆς (eager to display ...) Il. 13.197. Cf. Il. 5.732, Il. 17.181, Il. 20.256.

div.head: a
div.p: Eager to be doing, keen for action, in eager course, pressing on, bent or set on doing something : μεμαότες ἐγχείῃσιν (with their spears, i.e. eager to use them) Il. 2.818, Ἔρις ἄμοτον μεμαυῖα Il. 4.440, στυφέλιξέ μιν μεμαῶτα (checked his fury) Il. 7.261. Cf. Il. 4.73, Il. 8.327, Il. 13.46, Il. 15.604, Il. 24.298, etc. : Od. 4.416 (struggling), Od. 13.389, Od. 22.172, Od. 24.487.
Applied to the insistent hungry belly Od. 17.286.

div.head: b
div.p: Eagerly, with eager haste, speed, alacrity or zeal : βῆ ῥρʼ ἀνʼ ὁδὸν μεμαώς Il. 10.339. Cf. Il. 5.143, Il. 11.239, 258, Il. 13.40, Il. 15.83, Il. 16.754, Il. 21.174, etc. : ἤϊξαν πεδίονδε μεμαῶτες Od. 15.183.
To hasten, speed : πῇ μέματον; (whither away so fast?) Il. 8.413. Cf. Il. 11.615, Il. 14.298.
To be minded or inclined, to purpose, design : διχθά μοι κραδίη μέμονεν (I am in two minds) Il. 16.435.
With pres. or aor. infin. : πῇ μέμονας καταδῦναι ὅμιλον; Il. 13.307, ἦε μένειν μεμάασιν Il. 22.384. Cf. Il. 7.160, Il. 10.208 = 409, Il. 10.433, Il. 12.304, Il. 24.657 : Od. 11.315.
With fut. infin. : πῶς μέμονας πόλεμον καταπαυσέμεν; Il. 7.36. Cf. Il. 9.247, Il. 14.88, Il. 15.105, Il. 21.481 (presume to . . .).
Of the royal councillors : βουλὴν μεγαθύμων γερόντων Il. 2.53.– Of peoples Il. 1.123, Il. 2.541, Il. 5.27, Il. 9.549, Il. 13.699, etc. : Od. 3.366, Od. 7.16, Od. 24.57.
To be unwilling to give or allow, to grudge.
With acc. and dat. : μέγηρέ οἱ τό γʼ Ἀπόλλων Il. 23.865.
With dat. alone : Δαναοῖσι μεγήρας Il. 15.473.
With genit. indicating that in respect of which grudging takes place and dat. : τάων οὔ τοι ἐγὼ πρόσθʼ ἵσταμαι οὐδὲ μεγαίρω Il. 4.54.
With this genit. alone : βιότοιο μεγήρας (grudging him the taking of his foe's life) Il. 13.563.
With dat. and infin. indicating what is grudged : μηδὲ μεγήρῃς ἡμῖν τελευτῆσαι τάδε ἔργα Od. 3.55.
With prepositional clause and infin. : ἀμφὶ νεκροῖσι κατακαιέμεν οὔ τι μεγαίρω Il. 7.408.
With infin. and acc. of person concerned as subject of it : μνηστῆρας οὔ τι μεγαίρω ἔρδειν ἔργα βίαια (I say nothing against their doing so) Od. 2.235.
Epithet of the sea, with mighty deeps Od. 3.158.
Epithet of ships, with mighty hollow, capacious Il. 8.222= Il. 11.5, Il. 11.600.
Epithet of the dolphin, with mighty maw Il. 21.22.

Applied to θυμός (my,
thy, his, great heart) Il. 9.109, Il. 11.403, etc. : Od. 5.298, Od. 9.299, etc.
To bear oneself proudly, be haughty Od. 23.174.
To be too proud to do something Il. 10.69.
Greatly, in a high degree, to a great extent : ἐμὲ μ. ἀκαχίζεις Od. 16.432. Cf. Il. 17.723.
=μεγάλως. Strengthening μέγας by reduplication (cf. αἰνόθεν αἰνῶς, οἰόθεν οἶος) Il. 16.776, Il. 18.26 : Od. 24.40.

The chief room of a house, the general living-room, the hall : ἐνὶ μεγάροισιν ἑκάστη πῦρ καιόντων Il. 8.520 : μέθυ νεῖμον πᾶσιν ἀνὰ μ. Od. 7.180. Cf. Od. 4.37, 300, Od. 7.230, Od. 11.420, Od. 16.343, Od. 21.229, etc.
In pl. in the same sense : ὁμάδησαν ἀνὰ μέγαρα Od. 1.365. Cf. Od. 4.238, Od. 8.242, Od. 11.334, Od. 15.77, Od. 18.183, Od. 22.172, etc.
Such a room in the abode of a god Il. 18.374.
In the hut of Achilles Il. 24.647.
Of the chief room in the hut of Eumaeus Od. 16.165.
So in pl. : παρήμενος ἐν μεγάροισιν Od. 17.521.
In pl. of such a room in the modest dwelling of Laertes Od. 24.392, 396, 412.

The house itself, one's house or home : τρεῖς μοί (οἵ) εἰσι θύγατρες ἐνὶ μεγάρῳ Il. 9.144, 286. Cf. Il. 2.661, Il. 6.91, 272, 377, Il. 13.431, Il. 24.209 (at home) : ἴτω ἐς μ. πατρός Od. 1.276. Cf. Od. 1.270, Od. 4.744, Od. 7.65, Od. 13.377, Od. 16.341, Od. 22.370, etc.

In pl. in the same sense : πατρὸς ἐν μεγάροισιν Il. 6.428. Cf. Il. 1.418, Il. 2.137, Il. 6.421, Il. 13.667, Il. 15.439, Il. 24.219, etc. : τρέφε ναυσικάαν ἐν μεγάροισιν Od. 7.12. Cf. Od. 1.269, Od. 3.213, Od. 6.62, Od. 11.68, Od. 15.231, Od. 21.30, etc.
In pl. app. including the αὐλή: χῆνες ἐκέχυντο ἀθρόοι ἐν μεγάροις Od. 19.540. Cf. Od. 19.552.
In pl. of the abodes of the gods Il. 11.76, Il. 21.475 : Od. 1.27.

A chamber or set of chambers appropriated to the lady of a house and her maidens, the women's quarters (cf. ὑπερώϊον 2) : τὴν εὗρʼ ἐν μεγάρῳ Il. 3.125 (the same as the θάλαμος of 142), μεγάροιο διέσσυτο Il. 22.460 (the same as the μυχὸς δόμου of 440) : ἐς μ. καλέασα Od. 1.416, ἦλθον ἀμφίπολοι ἐκ μεγάροιο (i.e. from the part of it from which they had been summoned) Od. 18.198. Cf. Od. 18.185, 316, Od. 19.60, Od. 20.6, Od. 21.236 = 382, Od. 22.497, Od. 23.43.
In pl. in the same sense : πηνελόπειαν ἐνὶ μεγάροισιν ἄνωχθι μεῖναι Od. 17.569. Cf. Il. 6.286 : Od. 2.94= Od. 24.129, Od. 19.16, 30= Od. 21.387, Od. 19.139, Od. 22.399.
To the μέγαρον (in sense 1): βῆ δʼ ἰέναι μ. Od. 16.413. Cf. Od. 21.58, Od. 23.20.
μεγάλη, μέγα. Comp. μείζων, -ονος. Neut. μεῖζον. Superl. μέγιστος, -η, -ον.

Of great longitudinal extent, long (as applied to weapons commonly a mere epithet) : ξίφος Il. 1.194, τάφρον Il. 7.441, Il. 9.350. Cf. Il. 3.272, Il. 4.124, Il. 15.677, Il. 22.307, etc. : ἔγχος Od. 1.100. Cf. Od. 10.262, Od. 21.74, Od. 24.172, etc.
Of great upward extent, high, tall, lofty : πύργον Il. 6.386. Cf. Il. 15.619, Il. 16.297, Il. 21.243 : ἐρινεός Od. 12.103. Cf. Od. 4.501, Od. 8.569, Od. 12.71, Od. 22.466, etc.

Of persons, tall, of large build, goodly : ἠΰς τε μέγας τε Il. 2.653. Cf. Il. 4.534, Il. 5.628, Il. 18.518, Il. 21.108, etc. : καλόν τε μέγαν τε Od. 1.301. Cf. Od. 9.508, Od. 13.289, Od. 18.4, 382, Od. 21.334, etc.
In comp. : κεφαλῇ μείζονες ἄλλοι ἔασιν Il. 3.168. Cf. Od. 6.230= Od. 23.157, Od. 10.396, Od. 24.369.
Of parts of the body, well developed, stout, strong : μηρούς Od. 18.68. Cf. Il. 15.695 : Od. 17.225.
Of the voice, great, full : ὄπα Il. 3.221.
Of horses or oxen, stout, goodly Il. 2.839= Il. 12.97, Il. 23.750. Cf. Od. 18.372.
Grown-up, come to man's estate Od. 2.314, Od. 18.217, Od. 19.532.
Of flocks : οἰῶν μέγα πῶϋ Il. 3.198, Il. 11.696, Il. 15.323 : Od. 12.299.
Of garments, wide, flowing : φᾶρος Il. 2.43, Il. 8.221 : Od. 5.230, Od. 8.84. Cf. Od. 14.521, Od. 18.292, etc.
Covering a wide space : ὀμίχλην Il. 13.336.
Sim. : κεῖτο μέγας μεγαλωστί Il. 16.776. Cf. Il. 18.26 : Od. 24.40.
Epithet of οὐρανός Il. 1.497, Il. 5.750= Il. 8.394, Il. 21.388.
Of the sea (no doubt sometimes with notion of depth also) Il. 14.16, Il. 19.267 : Od. 3.179, Od. 4.504, etc.
In comp. : μείζονα κρητῆρα Il. 9.202. Cf. Il. 7.268 : Od. 8.187, Od. 9.537, Od. 12.96.
Of springs, great, welling forth in abundance : κρουνῶν Il. 4.454.
Of a meal, abundant, sumptuous : δόρπον Il. 19.208.
Of sound, mighty, loud, resounding, far-sounding : ἀλαλητῷ Il. 12.138, Il. 14.393. Cf. Il. 15.384, Il. 21.9, 256, 387 : Od. 24.463.
In reference to a report or rumour or to fame, wide-spread, known far and wide : κλέος Il. 6.446, κῦδος Il. 8.176, etc. Cf. Od. 3.79, etc.
In comp. : μεῖζον κλέος Od. 8.147. Cf. Od. 18.255= Od. 19.128.
Great, thick, stout, strong : σάκος (his ponderous shield) Il. 3.335, κληῗδα Il. 24.455. Cf. Il. 12.57, 134, 257, etc. : τειχίον Od. 16.165. Cf. Od. 12.436, etc.
Of fire, etc., with powerful blaze, blazing strongly or fiercely : πῦρ Il. 8.521, Il. 9.211, σέλαϊ Il. 17.739. Cf. Od. 5.59, Od. 23.51.
Of wind, blustering Od. 12.408, Od. 14.458, Od. 19.200.
Of the heart, great, distended with pride, full of spirit or daring, swollen, swelling: δάμασον θυμὸν μέγαν Il. 9.496. Cf. Il. 2.196, Il. 7.25, Il. 9.184, Il. 21.395.
Of great power or influence, of might, of power, mighty, powerful : θεός (θεόν) Il. 5.434, Il. 8.200, Il. 16.531, Il. 19.410, Il. 24.90.
Sim. of the Scamander Il. 20.73, Il. 21.192, 248, 282, 329.
Epithet of gods and heroes, mighty, the mighty Il. 2.134, 816, Il. 4.295, Il. 5.39, 610, 721, Il. 7.427, Il. 11.501, Il. 12.136, etc. : Od. 4.27, Od. 8.226, etc.
Distinguishing the Salaminian from the lesser Aias : αἴας ὁ μέγας Il. 16.358.

div.head: a
div.p:
Of occurrences, emotions, qualities, etc., of great weight, efficacy, effect, significance, importance or value, great, mighty, weighty, heavy, potent, important, serious, significant of much : ὅρκον Il. 1.233, πένθος 254, σθένος Il. 11.11, etc. Cf. Il. 4.38, Il. 5.285, Il. 9.9, Il. 10.282, Il. 13.122, Il. 16.208, Il. 19.270, etc. : πῆμα Od. 2.163, ἔργων Od. 21.26, ἀρετῇ Od. 24.193. Cf. Od. 3.275, Od. 5.289, Od. 8.136, Od. 11.195,
Od. 22.149, Od. 23.188, etc.
Of great value, price or amount, valuable, costly, precious : δῶρον Il. 9.576, χρεῖος Il. 11.698. Cf. Il. 10.304, 401, Il. 22.163, etc. : ἄγαλμα Od. 8.509.
Absol. : σὺν μεγάλῳ ἀπέτεισαν (with a heavy penalty, at a grievous rate) Il. 4.161 : λίην μέγα εἶπες (too great a thing to be looked for) Od. 3.227, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: In bad sense, violent, outrageous, audacious, evil : ἔργον Od. 3.261, Od. 11.272, Od. 12.373, Od. 19.92, Od. 24.426, 458.
In neut. sing. μέγα as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Greatly, much, in a high degree, to a great extent, far : μ. κεν κεχαροίατο Il. 1.256. Cf. Il. 1.103, Il. 2.27, Il. 6.261, Il. 9.509, Il. 18.162, Il. 23.682, etc. : μ. δυναμένοιο Od. 1.276. Cf. Od. 4.30, 503, Od. 15.376, Od. 16.139, Od. 21.247, etc.

With power or might : μ. πάντων Ἀργείων ἤνασσεν Il. 10.32, μ. ἔξιδεν (with all his might) Il. 20.342. Cf. Il. 1.78, Il. 16.172 : Od. 11.485, Od. 15.274.–μ. φρονέων, with great things in the mind, at a high pitch of resolve or endeavourIl. 8.553, Il. 11.296, 325, Il. 13.156, Il. 16.258, 758, 824, Il. 22.21.–μ. εἰπεῖν, to talk bigOd. 22.288.

div.head: b
div.p: Strengthening an adj. or adv., in a high degree, exceedingly, very : μ. νήπιος Il. 16.46, ἄνευθε μ. νῶϊν Il. 22.88. Cf. Il. 1.158, etc. : Od. 9.44, etc.
Strengthening a comp. or superl., by much, by far, much : μ. ἄριστος Il. 2.82, μ. ἀμείνονες Il. 4.405. Cf. Il. 2.239, Il. 19.216, Il. 22.158, etc. : Od. 11.478, Od. 22.374, Od. 23.121, etc.
Sim. : μ. ἔξοχος Il. 2.480. Cf. Od. 15.227, Od. 21.266.

div.head: c
div.p: In reference to sound, loudly, with a loud voice or sound : μ. ἴαχον Il. 2.333. Cf. Il. 2.784, Il. 14.147, 399, Il. 16.334, Il. 20.260, Il. 22.407, etc. : μ. ἔπταρεν Od. 17.541. Cf. Od. 9.395, Od. 10.323, Od. 17.239, etc.
In neut. pl. μεγάλα as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Strengthening other words : μ. ἤλιθα πολλή Od. 9.330.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to sound, loudly, with a loud voice or sound : μεγάλʼ εὔχετο Il. 1.450. Cf. Il. 1.482, Il. 8.75, 347, Il. 16.391, 429, Il. 23.119, etc. : μεγάλʼ αὐδήσαντος (app. connoting boastfulness) Od. 4.505. Cf. Od. 2.428, Od. 9.392, 399, Od. 14.354, Od. 20.113, Od. 21.413.
Sim. in reference to the loud beating of the heart in agitation : κραδίη μ. πατάσσει Il. 13.282.
Tall stature, goodly build (cf. μέγας 3): εἶδός τε μ. τε φυήν τε Il. 2.58. Cf. Il. 7.288, Il. 23.66 : Od. 5.217, Od. 6.152, Od. 11.337= Od. 18.219, Od. 24.253, 374.
To devise, plan, contrive, meditate : κακά Il. 4.21= Il. 8.458.
To bethink oneself of, think of, take thought for, remember, make arrangements for.
A ruler or lord : ἁλὸς μέδοντος Od. 1.72.
3 sing. pa. iterative (formed fr. the stem ἑλ- of the aor. (see αἱρέω)) μεθέλεσκε.
To catch in one's turn : [σφαῖραν] Od. 8.376.
To spring or rush in pursuit of a foe or of a competitor, to spring or rush upon him : οὔτασε μετάλμενος Il. 5.336. Cf. Il. 11.538, Il. 12.305, Il. 13.362, Il. 14.443, Il. 23.345.
To direct or drive (one's horses in quest of or to join a person).
With acc. of the person : τυδεΐδην μέθεπεν ἵππους Il. 5.329.
So without the direct object : ἡνίοχον μέθεπεν (drove in quest or search of . . .) Il. 8.126.
To direct one's course towards, make for, an indicated object : [ἑταίρους] Il. 17.190. Cf. Od. 14.33.
To come to pay a visit : ἠὲ νέον μεθέπεις, ἦ . . . Od. 1.175.
Only in mid. Aor. pple. μετασπόμενος.
To follow up a foe : ἀπιόντα μετασπόμενος βάλεν Il. 13.567.
Slow to take action, remiss, careless Il. 2.241 : Od. 6.25.
[μεθ-, μετα- 1 (the senses app. developed through the notion of sending forth from oneself) + ἵημι1.]
Acc. sing. masc. pple. μεθιέντα Il. 4.516, Il. 6.330, Il. 12.268, Il. 13.229.
3 sing. μεθέηκε Il. 23.434, Il. 24.48. μεθῆκε Il. 21.177 : Od. 5.460, Od. 21.126.
3 sing. μεθήῃ Od. 5.471 (v.l. μεθείη, see below).
3 sing. opt. μεθείη Il. 13.118 : Od. 5.471 (v.l. here μεθήῃ, see above).
Infin. μεθέμεν Il. 1.283, Il. 15.138. From μεθιέω
3 sing. impf. μεθίει Il. 15.716, Il. 16.762, Il. 21.72.
To relax one's hold of something, let it go : ἐπεὶ λάβεν οὐχὶ μεθίει Il. 15.716, Il. 16.762. Cf. Il. 21.72 : ἐς ποταμὸν μεθῆκεν (let it fall into the . . .) Od. 5.460.
To let go or release (a captive) Il. 10.449.
Sim. in reference to a guest : οὔ σε μεθήσει (will not hear of thy going) Od. 15.212.
App., to relax, relieve, free (from a burden) : κῆρ ἄχεος μεθέηκα (have lightened it of my grief) Il. 17.539.

Of a state or condition, to relieve (a person) of its
presence, quit (him) : εἴ με μεθήῃ ῥῖγος Od. 5.471.
To let go or dismiss from one's mind : Ἀχιλλῆϊ μεθέμεν χόλον Il. 1.283. Cf. Il. 15.138 : Od. 1.77.

p.gloss: So, to let go, depart from.

div.p: To dismiss from one's thoughts, cease to care for, no longer interest oneself in : μὴ χωσαμένη σε μεθείω Il. 3.414.
With infin., to yield the doing of something, to suffer, allow, permit : εἰ τοῦτον Τρώεσσι μεθήσομεν ἄστυ πότι ἐρύσαι Il. 17.418.
To relax one's efforts, lose resolution, grow slack or faint-hearted, in the matter of, relax, cease, refrain, hold back from.

With genit. : ἀλκῆς Il. 4.234, Il. 12.409, Il. 13.116, πολέμοιο Il. 4.240, 351, Il. 6.330, Il. 13.97, 114, 118, μάχης Il. 12.268, βίης (relaxed from his effort) (v.l. βίῃ, in his effort) Il. 21.177 : Od. 21.126.
Sim. with infin. : μάχεσθαι Il. 13.234. Cf. Il. 23.434.
So κλαύσας καὶ ὀδυράμενος μεθέηκε [κλαίειν καὶ ὀδύρεσθαι] (ceases to weep) Il. 24.48.
To refrain from rendering friendly offices to, neglect.
With genit. : σεῖο τειρομένοιο (in thy trouble) Il. 11.841.

Absol., to relax one's efforts, become slack, cease to exert oneself, lose heart : ὅθι μεθιέντα ἴδοιτο Il. 4.516. Cf. Il. 6.523, Il. 10.121, Il. 13.229, Il. 15.553, Il. 20.361 : Od. 4.372, Od. 16.377 (will not be idle).
Only in mid. Aor. pple. μετεισάμενος (μετα(ϝ)ισάμενος).
To speed or make in an indicated direction for some purpose : μετεισάμενος ὄτρυνε φάλαγγας Il. 13.90. Cf. Il. 17.285.
In act., to set in a different manner, to change : ταῦτα μεταστήσω (will give another gift instead) Od. 4.612.
In mid., to take one's stand, come and stand, among.
In pass., to set out with an indicated object, start on an expedition : λυρνησσὸν πέρσα μεθορμηθείς Il. 20.192.
To make a dart or effort towards an indicated object : μεθορμηθεὶς ἐλλάβετο σχεδίης Od. 5.325.
To be drunken : μεθύοντι ἐοικώς Od. 18.240.
To drip, be soaked : βοείην μεθύουσαν ἀλοιφῇ (with . . . ) Il. 17.390.
=μειδάω. Only in pres. pple. μειδιόων, -ωσα : μειδιόων βλοσυροῖσι προσώπασιν (a grim smile of anticipated triumph) Il. 7.212. Cf. Il. 21.491, Il. 23.786.
Presents given with a bride by her father Il. 9.147, 289.
A sweet morsel, a titbit : μειλίγματα θυμοῦ (such as delight their hearts) Od. 10.217.
To soften, to soothe : πυρὸς μειλισσέμεν [νέκυας] (as to giving them the consolation of fire (genit. of material)) Il. 7.410.
In mid., to speak comfortably, mince one's words : μή μʼ αἰδόμενος μειλίσσεο Od. 3.96=Od. 4.326.
Slackness or backwardness in action Il. 15.741.

Of speech, winning, pleasing, mild, gentle, kindly, conciliatory : μύθοισιν Il. 6.343. Cf. Il. 9.113, Il. 10.288, 542, Il. 11.137, Il. 12.267, Il. 21.339 : Od. 6.143, 148, Od. 10.173, Od. 11.552, Od. 18.283, etc.
Absol. in pl., such speech : προσηύδα μειλιχίοισιν Il. 4.256, Il. 6.214, Il. 17.431 : Od. 20.165.
Of persons, winning, mild, gentle, kindly Il. 17.671, Il. 19.300, Il. 24.739.
3 sing. plupf. pass. εἵμαρτο Il. 21.281 : Od. 5.312, Od. 24.34.
To receive a share of, take one's part of.
With genit. : ἥμισυ μείρεο τιμῆς Il. 9.616.
In pf., to have one's share of, to have, hold, be entitled to.
With genit. : τιμῆς Il. 1.278, Il. 15.189 : Od. 5.335, Od. 11.338.
In pass. in impers. construction, to be allotted as one's portion, be fated : λευγαλέῳ με θανάτῳ εἵμαρτο ἁλῶναι (it was the fate assigned me) Il. 21.281 :=Od. 5.312. Cf. Od. 24.34.
Of dark or swarthy complexion, tanned Od. 16.175.
A roof-beam or rafter Od. 8.279, Od. 11.278, Od. 22.239.
App., a free end of such a beam projecting outside : κατʼ ἄρʼ ἕζετʼ ἐπὶ προὔχοντι μελάθρῳ Od. 19.544.
Such a beam as typifying the house, one's roof : κατὰ πρηνὲς βαλέειν Πριάμοιο μέλαθρον Il. 2.414. Cf. Il. 9.204, 640 (the obligations of hospitality) : Od. 18.150.
To make dark ; in pass., to grow dark : μελαίνετο χρόα καλόν (her flesh grew livid) Il. 5.354, νειὸς μελαίνετʼ ὄπισθεν (was represented as darkened in hue by some process of shading) Il. 18.548.
App., having the hilts bound round with dark bands.

p.gloss: In which the water wells up from dark depths.

div.p: Epithet of springs Il. 9.14, Il. 16.3, 160, Il. 21.257 : Od. 20.158.

Dark in hue, dark (not necessarily implying the absence of colour,
but sometimes to be translated black) ,
In comp. : μελάντερον ἠΰτε πίσσα Il. 4.277. Cf. Il. 24.94.

Applied to the φρένες thought of as darkened by deep emotion : μένεος φρένες ἀμφὶ μέλαιναι πίμπλαντο Il. 1.103 := Od. 4.661 (i.e. the double organ (see ἀμφί I.1.b) was filled with fury (so as to be) black in both parts). Cf. Il. 16.83, 499, 573. (In all these cases also written, with sim. sense, ἀμφιμέλαιναι.)–Absol.: τὸ μέλαν δρυός (the dark heart) Od. 14.12.

div.head: d
div.p: Of water (app. referring to the dark hue of water as seen by transmitted light with little or no reflection from the surface) : μέλαν ὕδωρ Il. 2.825, Il. 16.161, Il. 21.202 : Od. 4.359, Od. 6.91, Od. 12.104, Od. 13.409.
So of the sea : μείλανι πόντῳ Il. 24.79.
Of the surface of the sea rippled by a breeze : μέλαιναν φρῖκα Il. 21.126. Cf. Od. 4.402.

div.head: e
div.p: Of evening: μέλας ἕσπερος Od. 1.423= Od. 18.306.
Sim.: θανάτου μέλαν νέφος Il. 16.350. Cf. Il. 16.591= Il. 18.22 := Od. 24.315, Od. 4.180.

div.head: g
div.p: Applied also to pain : μελαινέων ὀδυνάων Il. 4.117. Cf. Il. 4.191, Il. 15.394.
To cause to melt, melt Il. 21.363.
In pl., cares, anxieties, grief : μελεδήματα θυμοῦ Il. 23.62 := Od. 20.56, Od. 23.343, μελεδήματα πατρός (for his ..) Od. 15.8. Cf. Od. 4.650.
Limb-meal, limb by limb : ταμών Il. 24.409 : Od. 9.291. Cf. Od. 18.339.
Vain, useless, idle, empty : εὖχος (because got without fighting) Il. 21.473, οὔ τοι μέλεος εἰρήσεται αἶνος (in vain) Il. 23.795. Cf. Od. 5.416.
In neut. sing. μέλεον as adv., in vain, idly : ἑστάμεναι μ. σὺν τεύχεσιν (doing nothing) Il. 10.480, μ. ἠκόντισαν (without result, each making a miss) Il. 16.336.
The ash: φηγόν τε μελίην τε Il. 16.767. Cf. Il. 13.178.
Applied to one's life or soul : θυμόν Il. 10.495, Il. 16.17 : Od. 11.203.
A mixture of honey and (prob.) milk Od. 10.519= Od. 11.27.
Epithet of spears, with shaft of ash Il. 5.655, 666, Il. 13.715, etc.
μέλινος οὐδός, app., a threshold of wood set upon the λάϊνος οὐδός at the entrance to the μέγαρον Od. 17.339 (see λάϊνος).
A bee : σφῆκες ἠὲ μέλισσαι Il. 12.167. Cf. Il. 2.87 : Od. 13.106.

p.gloss: To be about, be going, to do something, to be on the point of doing it (sometimes tending to pass into (2)).

div.p: With fut. infin. : θήσειν ἔτʼ ἔμελλεν ἄλγεα Il. 2.39, ἔμελλέ μιν δώσειν Il. 6.52. Cf. Il. 6.393, Il. 11.22, Il. 15.601, Il. 19.98, Il. 23.544, etc. : ὅτʼ ἔμελλε πάλιν οἶκόνδε νέεσθαι Od. 6.110, Ἀγαμέμνονος φθίσεσθαι κακὸν οἶτον ἔμελλον (I have just escaped his fate) Od. 13.384. Cf. Od. 4.514, Od. 7.18, Od. 9.378, Od. 11.596, Od. 17.364, Od. 20.393, Od. 22.9, etc.
With pres. infin. : ἔμελλε λίσσεσθαι Il. 10.454. Cf. Od. 19.94.
With aor. infin. : ὅτʼ ἔμελλον ἐπαΐξασθαι ἄεθλον Il. 23.773.

p.gloss: To be destined or fated to be or to do.

div.p: With fut. infin. : ἅ ῥʼ οὐ τελέεσθαι ἔμελλον Il. 2.36, ὣς ἄρʼ ἐμέλλετʼ ἄσειν κύνας (fate destined you to ...) Il. 11.817. Cf. Il. 2.694, Il. 5.205, Il. 10.336, Il. 12.3, Il. 15.612, Il. 20.466, Il. 21.47, Il. 24.85, etc. : μέλλον ἔτι ξυνέσεσθαι ὀϊζυῖ Od. 7.270, οὐκ ἄρʼ ἔμελλες λήξειν ἀπατάων (it could not be that you should ...) Od. 13.293. Cf. Od. 2.156, Od. 6.165, Od. 9.230, 477, Od. 11.553, Od. 21.98, Od. 23.221, Od. 24.28, etc.
Impers. : τῇ τελευτήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν (it was fated) Od. 8.510.
With pres. infin. : οὐκ ἄρʼ ἔμελλες ἀνάλκιδος ἀνδρὸς ἑταίρους ἔδμεναι Od. 9.475.
With aor. infin. : ἔμελλεν οἶ αὐτῷ θάνατον λιτέσθαι (he was fated to find that his prayer had been to his own death) Il. 16.46. Cf. Il. 18.98.

p.gloss: To be likely to be or to be doing or to do, to be presumably so and so or doing so and so.

div.p: With pres. infin. : ὅθι που μέλλουσι βουλὰς βουλεύειν (where it is likely they are conferring) Il. 10.326, ᾦ μέλλεις εὔχεσθαι (to whom you must pray) Il. 11.364= Il. 20.451, τὰ μέλλετʼ ἀκουέμεν (no doubt you know) Il. 14.125 : μέλλε ποτὲ οἶκος ὅδʼ ἀφνειὸς ἔμμεναι (all know how flourishing it was) Od. 1.232, ὄλβον θεοὶ μέλλουσιν ὀπάζειν (surely you know that it is the gods who ...) Od. 18.19, καὶ ἐγώ ποτʼ ἔμελλον ὄλβιος εἶναι (I too in my day was ...) 138, πολλάκι που μέλλεις ἀρήμεναι (no doubt you prayed) Od. 22.322. Cf. Od. 4.94, 200.
Impers. : ἐμοὶ μέλλει φίλον εἷναι (you may be sure that it is) Il. 1.564. Cf. Il. 2.116= Il. 9.23= Il. 14.69, Il. 13.226.

With aor. infin. of something likely to have taken place or that presumably has taken place : ἄλλοτε δή ποτε μᾶλλον ἐρωῆσαι πολέμοιο μέλλω (may have done so (but cannot be accused of doing so now)) Il. 13.777, μέλλει τις τελέσσαι (is likely to have done so, i.e. may be expected to do so) Il. 18.362. Cf. Il. 21.83, Il. 24.46 : Od. 4.274, 377, Od. 14.133.

With fut. infin. : τά που μέλλεν
ἀγάσσεσθαι θεὸς αὐτός (app., it must have been that he was to do so) Od. 4.181.

In pl., one's limbs, one's bodily frame : θυμὸν ἀπὸ μελέων δῦνα δόμον Ἄϊδος Il. 7.131, γναμπτοῖσι μέλεσσιν Il. 11.669, Il. 24.359. Cf. Il. 13.672= Il. 16.607, Il. 16.110, Il. 17.211, Il. 23.191, 689 : Od. 8.298, Od. 10.393, Od. 11.201, 394, 600, Od. 13.398, 430, 432, Od. 15.354, Od. 18.70= Od. 24.368, Od. 18.77, Od. 21.283.
In reference to a bird Il. 23.880.
To a sacrifice : πάντων ἀρχόμενος μελέων Od. 14.428.
In pl. : κυνῶν μέλπηθρα γένοιτο (a sport for ...) Il. 13.233. Cf. Il. 16.255= Il. 18.179.
In mid. : ἰδὼν μετὰ μελπομένῃσιν ἐν χορῷ Ἀρτέμιδος Il. 16.182.
App., to dance the war-dance. Fig. : οἷδα δʼ ἐνὶ σταδίῃ δηΐῳ μέλπεσθαι Ἄρηϊ (in honour of Ares) Il. 7.241.
In mid. : μετά σφιν ἐμέλπετʼ ἀοιδός Il. 18.604 := Od. 4.17= Od. 13.27.
To honour or celebrate in song : μέλποντες ἑκάεργον Il. 1.474.
3 sing. plupf. (in impf. sense) μεμήλει Il. 2.614 : Od. 1.151.
3 sing. thematic pf. (in pres. sense) μέμβλεται Il. 19.343.
3 sing. plupf. (in impf. sense) μέμβλετο Il. 21.516 : Od. 22.12.

In act. and mid., to be an object of care, concern, solicitude, anxiety or interest, to, to concern, be the concern of, to make anxious, interest, trouble : ἐμοί κε ταῦτα μελήσεται (I will make it my care) Il. 1.523, ᾧ τόσσα μέμηλεν (who has so many responsibilities) Il. 2.25= 62, οὔ σφι θαλάσσια ἔργα μεμήλει 614, τά κεν Διὶ μελήσει (the issue is in his hands) Il. 17.515. Cf. Il. 4.353, Il. 5.228, 490, 876, Il. 6.441, 492, Il. 9.228, Il. 10.51, Il. 15.231, Il. 19.213, Il. 21.516, Il. 24.152, etc. : τοῖσιν ἄλλα μεμήλει (they turned to ...) Od. 1.151, μέλε οἱ ἐὼν ἐν δώμασι νύμφης Od. 5.6, μή τί τοι ἡγεμόνος γε ποθὴ μελέσθω Od. 10.505, Ἀργὼ πᾶσι μέλουσα (at whose name all hearts stir, the storied ...) Od. 12.70 (u.l. πασιμέλουσα). Cf. Od. 1.358, Od. 2.304, Od. 4.415 (bethink you of your ...), Od. 6.65, 270, Od. 7.208, Od. 9.20, Od. 13.362, Od. 17.594, Od. 18.421, Od. 22.12, etc.
Impers. : οὐκ ἔμελέν μοι ταῦτα μεταλλῆσαι (I cared not to ...) Od. 16.465. Cf. Od. 1.305.
To be concerned with, busied about.
With genit. : πλούτοιο μεμηλώς Il. 5.708, πτολέμοιο μεμηλώς (his mind set on it) Il. 13.297= 469.
acc. pl. neut. pf. pple. pass. μορύσσω.

Affirmative particle: οὐ μὲν σοί ποτε ἶσον ἔχω γέρας Il. 1.163. Cf. Il. 1.211, 216, 234, 269, 273, 514, Il. 2.145, 203, etc. : οὐ μὲν γάρ τι κακὸν βασιλευέμεν Od. 1.392. Cf. Od. 1.78, 173, 208, 222, 411, Od. 2.318, Od. 3.14, 236, etc.

In less emphatic use, serving to bring out a new point Il. 2.101, Il. 18.84, Il. 23.328, etc. : Od. 9.159, 320, etc.– μέν τοι Il. 4.318, etc. : Od. 4.157, etc.– μέν τε Il. 13.47, etc. : Od. 5.447, etc.

In adversative use : οὐδέ τι θυμὸς ἐδεύετο δαιτὸς ἐΐσης, οὐ μὲν φόρμιγγος (nor yet) Il. 1.603, πόθεόν γε μὲν ἀρχόν (but they ...) Il. 2.703. Cf. Il. 9.57 (under ἦ2 1.b.β), Il. 11.813, etc. : οὐ μέν σʼ οὐδὲ ἐῶσι θεοὶ κλαίειν Od. 4.805. Cf. Od. 10.65 (under ἦ2 1.b.β), etc.
Marking an alternative : οὐ ... οὐδὲ μὲν ... Il. 1.154, οὐδὲ ... οὐδὲ μὲν ... Il. 9.374, etc. Cf. Od. 8.553, Od. 22.415, etc.
To be eager, show eagerness or ardour, strive : μάλα περ μενεαίνων Il. 15.617. Cf. Il. 22.10 : Od. 5.341.
Of mental struggling : κτεινόμενος μενέαινεν (faced his fate) Il. 16.491.

p.gloss: To desire, be eager or anxious, long, strive, be minded, to do something, be set on doing it.

div.p: With infin. : κατακτάμεναι Il. 3.379, μηδὲ θεοῖς μενεαινέμεν ἶφι μάχεσθαι (let not your spirit carry you away so as to ...) Il. 5.606. Cf. Il. 4.32, Il. 13.628, Il. 15.507, Il. 21.33, 543, etc. : Od. 4.282, Od. 10.295, 322, Od. 11.392, 585, Od. 13.30, Od. 17.17, 185, Od. 20.315, Od. 21.125.
In reference to the eager course of a missile : ἆλτʼ ὀϊστός, καθʼ ὅμιλον ἐπιπτέσθαι μενεαίνων Il. 4.126.

To be enraged, to show or be filled with rage or bitterness, to rage : νήπιοι, οἳ Ζηνὶ μενεαίνομεν (against Zeus) Il. 15.104, Ἕκτορʼ ἀείκιζεν μενεαίνων (in his rage) Il. 24.22. Cf. Il. 19.58, 68, Il. 24.54 : Od. 1.20, Od. 6.330.
Of martial rage : Τρωσὶν μενεαίνων Il. 19.367.
[μένος + εἴκω1. Fitted to, satisfying, the spirit.]

Abundant, plentiful, satisfying, contenting, in abundance or plenty : δαῖτα Il. 9.90. Cf. Il. 23.29, 139, 650 : λἥΐδα Od. 13.273. Cf. Od. 5.166, 267, Od. 6.76, Od. 9.158, Od. 13.409, Od. 16.429, Od. 20.391.
Absol. : πάρα μενοεικέα πολλὰ δαίνυσθαι (abundance, to feast thereon to our heart's desire) Il. 9.227. Cf. Il. 19.144 : Od. 14.232.
3 sing. subj. μενοινάᾳ Il. 19.164. μενοινήῃσι Il. 15.82. From μενοινέω

To wish, desire, be bent upon : ὅ τι φρεσὶ σῇσι μενοινᾷς Il. 14.221, ὡς δʼ ὅτʼ ἂν ἀΐξῃ νόος ἀνέρος ... μενοινήῃσί τε πολλά (forms many wishes, i.e. wishes himself in this place or that) Il. 15.82. Cf. Od. 2.34, 275, 285, Od. 4.480, Od. 6.180, Od. 15.111, Od. 17.355.
To turn over in one's mind, to design, purpose : νόος οἱ ἄλλα μενοινᾷ Od. 2.92= Od. 13.381. Cf. Od. 11.532, Od. 18.283.
To turn over (in one's mind) with anxiety : τίη δὲ σὺ ταῦτα μετὰ φρεσὶ σῇσι μενοινᾷς; (why let that trouble thee?) Il. 14.264.
With dependent clause : μενοίνεον εἰ τελέουσιν Il. 12.59.

p.gloss: To desire, be eager or anxious, long, be minded, to do something.

div.p: Passion, vehement or commanding feeling or emotion in general : μ. ἄσχετε (whose passion defies restraint) Od. 2.85= Od. 17.406, Od. 2.303, ὄτρυνε μ. ἕκαστου (desire to see the marvel) Od. 8.15. Cf. Od. 14.262= Od. 17.431.
In pl. : ἐμῶν μενέων ἀπερωεύς (of my desires, of what I have set my heart upon) Il. 8.361.
In a more or less concrete sense : ἀνὰ ῥῖνας δριμὺ μ. προὔτυψεν Od. 24.319.
One's spirit, the spirit within one : αὐτόν με μ. ἄνωγε κεῖσʼ ἰέναι Il. 24.198. Cf. Il. 5.892, Il. 13.634.

Specifically, fury, rage : μένεος φρένες πίμπλαντο Il. 1.103, μ. Ἄρηος (the fury of battle) Il. 18.264. Cf. Il. 1.207, 282, Il. 7.210, Il. 9.679, Il. 19.202, Il. 21.305, Il. 22.346 : Od. 4.661, Od. 9.457, Od. 11.562, Od. 24.183.
In a more or less concrete sense : εἰ μὴ νὺξ διακρινέει μ. ἀνδρῶν (the eager fighters) Il. 2.387 : μ. Ἄρηος (the combat) Od. 16.269.
Distraction, frenzy. In reference to horses Il. 23.468.

Spirit, courage, stoutness : ἔν τοι στήθεσσι μ. πατρώϊον ἧκα Il. 5.125. Cf. Il. 5.2, 470, Il. 8.335, Il. 13.424, Il. 15.594, Il. 16.529, Il. 19.159, Il. 22.96, 459, Il. 24.6, etc. : ὄφρα οἱ μ. ἐν φρεσὶ θείω Od. 1.89. Cf. Od. 1.321, Od. 2.271, Od. 3.104, Od. 11.270, 515, Od. 12.279, Od. 13.387, Od. 19.493.
In reference to beasts Il. 17.20, Il. 20.172.

Might, vigour, power, strength : ἔτι μοι μ. ἔμπεδόν ἐστιν Il. 5.254. Cf. Il. 6.101, Il. 7.407, Il. 9.706, Il. 15.60, Il. 16.621, Il. 21.482, etc. : μ. καὶ χεῖρας Od. 11.502. Cf. Od. 20.19, Od. 21.426, Od. 22.226, Od. 24.520.
In reference to horses, etc. : σφῶϊν ἐν γούνεσσι βαλῶ μ. ἠδʼ ἐνὶ θυμῷ Il. 17.451 (the word as connected with θυμῷ coming under (4)). Cf. Il. 17.456, 742, Il. 23.390, 400, 524, Il. 24.442.
In reference to inanimate objects : πυρὸς μ. Il. 17.565. Cf. Il. 13.444= Il. 16.613= Il. 17.529, Il. 20.372.
In a more or less concrete sense : μ. χειρῶν ἰθὺς φέρον Il. 5.506. Cf. Il. 6.127, 502, Il. 8.178, Il. 12.166, Il. 15.510, Il. 20.374, etc. : μ. πνείοντες Od. 22.203.
In pl.: μένεα πνείοντες (πνείοντας) Il. 2.536, Il. 3.8, Il. 11.508, Il. 24.364. Cf. Il. 4.447= Il. 8.61.
Might or strength in exercise : μένεος σχήσεσθαι Il. 17.503. Cf. Il. 17.638, Il. 21.340.
With sim. periphrasis : κούρην φέρεν μ. ἡμιόνοιϊν Od. 7.2.
Also μένος Βορέαο Il. 5.524, ἀναπνείουσα πυρὸς μένος (breathing fire) Il. 6.182. Cf. Il. 12.18, Il. 23.177, 190, 238= Il. 24.792 : Od. 5.478, Od. 10.160, Od. 11.220, Od. 19.440.

The animating principle, the vital spirit, the soul, the life, life, one's life (cf. θυμός I1.b) : τοῦ λύθη ψυχή-τε μ. τε Il. 5.296= Il. 8.123 = 315. Cf. Il. 3.294, Il. 6.27, Il. 8.358, Il. 16.332, Il. 17.29, 298 : ἤϊά κε κατέφθιτο καὶ μένεʼ ἀνδρῶν Od. 4.363.
In reference to an animal Od. 3.450.
Aor. ἔμεινα Od. 10.53, Od. 14.244. μεῖνα Od. 14.292.
1 pl. ἐμείναμεν Od. 9.151, 306, 436, Od. 12.7. μείναμεν Il. 11.723.

To remain where one is, to remain, stay, tarry, abide, continue to be, in a specified or indicated place : οὐδέ σε λίσσομαι μένειν Il. 1.174, ἴση μοῖρα μένοντι (for him who stays behind) Il. 9.318, ἔνθʼ ἔμεινε (stayed his course, stopped) Il. 14.286, ὄφρα μένω (remain quiescent, take no action) Il. 24.658. Cf. Il. 1.492, Il. 2.298, Il. 6.258, Il. 10.370, Il. 16.239, Il. 17.721 (sticking together), Il. 18.64, Il. 19.42, Il. 20.22, Il. 22.5, etc. : μένʼ αὖθι Od. 2.369. Cf. Od. 3.427, Od. 4.447, Od. 6.295, Od. 7.259, Od. 9.97, Od. 12.373 (the comrades whom I left behind me), Od. 14.244, Od. 15.51, Od. 17.20, Od. 19.199, Od. 20.330, etc.– Of something inanimate : [ἔγχος] αὐτοῦ μεῖνεν Il. 13.564. Cf. Il. 9.610= Il. 10.90 : Od. 4.508.
To remain as one is, refrain, wait : δύντα δʼ ἐς ἠέλιον μενέω Il. 19.308. Cf. Od. 17.582.
To remain, continue, be, in a specified condition : ἕνα μῆνα μένων ἀπὸ ἧς ἀλόχοιο Il. 2.292. Cf. Il. 19.263 : Od. 20.23.
To stand firm, stand without motion, stand still : ὥς τε στήλη μένει ἔμπεδον Il. 16.434. Cf. Il. 17.436 : Od. 17.235.
Sim. of ships lying without motion Od. 13.100.
To await the coming, approach or return of (a person) : ὄφρα μένοιεν νοστήσαντα ἄνακτα Il. 13.37. Cf. Il. 20.480, Il. 21.609 : Od. 1.304, Od. 4.439, 847, Od. 9.232, Od. 15.346, Od. 22.181.
To await in an indicated posture the approach of : οὐδέ τις ἔτλη μεῖναι ἐπερχόμενον (to remain seated on his approach) Il. 1.535.
To await (an occurrence) or the coming or coming on of (a period of time) : Ἠῶ Il. 11.723. Cf. Il. 15.599 : Od. 9.151= Od. 12.7, Od. 9.306 = 436.
Absol. : ἔνθʼ ἔμενεν (bided his time) Od. 13.161.
With infin. : Τρῶας σχεδὸν ἐλθέμεν Il. 4.247. Cf. Od. 1.422= Od. 18.305, Od. 4.786, Od. 6.98.
With dependent clause : ὁππότε πύργος Ἀχαιῶν ἄλλος Τρώων ὁρμήσειεν (waiting till ...) Il. 4.333. Cf. Il. 11.666.

To
await the attack of, stand up to : Μενέλαον Il. 3.52, Τρῶας Il. 5.527= Il. 15.622. Cf. Il. 13.476, 836, Il. 15.165, 406, Od. 21.571, Il. 22.252 : Od. 9.57.
Of a beast : σῦς, ὅς τε μένει κολοσυρτὸν ἀνδρῶν Il. 13.472. Cf. Il. 22.93.
Of something inanimate : πέτρη, ἥ τε μένει ἀνέμων κέλευθα Il. 15.620.
Of facing the attack of a beast : μένουσι [κάπριον] Il. 11.418.

Absol., to await the foe, stand firm, stand one's ground : μενέμεν καὶ ἀμυνέμεναι ὤρεσσιν Il. 5.486, Αἰνείας οὐ μεῖνεν 571. Cf. Il. 5.522, Il. 11.317, Il. 12.79, Il. 14.375, Il. 15.539, Il. 16.659, Od. 21.310, etc. : οἴη Ἀλκινόου θυγάτηρ μένεν Od. 6.139. Cf. Od. 14.270.
Such as to cause anxiety, baneful, evil : ἔργα Il. 8.453, Il. 10.289, 524.
Absol. in neut. pl., baneful deeds : μέρμερα ῥέζων (ῥέζεν) Il. 11.502, Od. 21.217. Cf. Il. 10.48.

To turn (a thing) anxiously over in one's mind, to ponder or consider (it), meditate (it), have (it) in view : πολλά Od. 1.427, φόνον ἡμῖν Od. 2.325. Cf. Il. 20.17 : Od. 4.533, Od. 19.2 = 52, Od. 20.38, 41.
To think out or contrive : δόλον τόνδε Od. 2.93, Od. 24.128.
To think of, find : ἀμύντορά τινα Od. 16.256, 261.
Absol., to ponder, consider, deliberate, meditate : τρὶς μερμήριξεν Il. 8.169, ἔτι μερμήριζον (were hesitating) Il. 12.199. Cf. Od. 5.354, Od. 11.204, Od. 16.237, Od. 20.93.

div.head: a
div.p: With relative : ὅ τι κύντατον ἕρδοι Il. 10.503.

div.head: b
div.p: With clause introduced by ὡς (how) Il. 2.3.

div.head: d
div.p: With the first alternative expressed by an infin. and the second introduced by ἦ: μερμήριξε κύσσαι... ἦ... Od. 24.235.
With infin. expressing only one of the alternatives : διάνδιχα μερμήριξεν ἵππους στρέψαι (had half a mind to...) Il. 8.167. Cf. Od. 10.151, 438.
A cord or string : κατέδει μέρμιθι Od. 10.23.
Epithet of ἄνθρωποι and βροτοί of unknown meaning: μερόπων ἀνθρώπων Il. 1.250, μερόπεσσι βροτοῖσιν Il. 2.285. Cf. Il. 3.402, Il. 9.340, Il. 11.28, Il. 18.288, 342, 490, Il. 20.217 : Od. 20.49, 132.
Half-grey, grizzled : μ. περ ἐών Il. 13.361.

Adv., in the space separating two objects, between, midway : πολλὰ [δοῦρα] μεσσηγὺ ἐν γαίῃ ἵσταντο (in mid career) Il. 11.573= Il. 15.316. Cf. Il. 23.521 : μηδέ τι μεσσηγύς γε κακὸν πάθῃσιν (by the way) Od. 7.195.
In such a space in reference to abstractions : τὸ μὲν τελέει, τὸ δὲ καὶ μεσσηγὺ κολούει (short of fulfilment) Il. 20.370.

div.head: a
div.p: In local sense, between : ὤμων μεσσηγύς Il. 5.41, μεσηγὺ νηῶν καὶ ποταμοῦ καὶ τείχεος (in the space separating the ships and the river from the (city) wall) Il. 17.396. Cf. Il. 5.769, Il. 6.4, Il. 13.33, Il. 24.78, etc. : Od. 4.845, Od. 15.528, Od. 22.93, 341, 442 = 459.

div.head: b
div.p: Of reciprocal relation or action, between : κέλαδον καὶ ἀϋτὴν κουρήτων τε μεσηγὺ καὶ αἰτωλῶν Il. 9.549.
Holding an intermediate position in a scale of excellence, neither good nor bad Il. 12.269.
In a ship, a sort of box in which the mast was set (prob.= ἱστοπέδη) : ἱστὸν κοίλης ἔντοσθε μεσόδμης στῆσαν Od. 2.424= Od. 15.289.
In a house, prob., a base or pedestal supporting a column Od. 19.37, Od. 20.354.

The middle or midmost part of the ..., the middle or midst of the ...: μέσον ἱστίον Il. 1.481, Ἄργεϊ μέσσῳ (in the heart of ...) Il. 6.224. Cf. Il. 3.78, Il. 5.582, Il. 7.258, 267, Il. 8.68, Il. 11.167, Il. 16.231, Il. 20.254, Il. 23.241, etc. : πέλαγος μέσον Od. 3.174. Cf. Od. 1.344, Od. 2.37, Od. 4.400, Od. 12.80 (halfway up), 93 (waist-deep), etc.
In reference to a period of time : μέσον ἦμαρ (noon) Il. 21.111 : Od. 7.288.
In pl., the midst of the ... : μέσῃσι μετὰ δμῳῇσιν Od. 16.336. Cf. Il. 13.312, Il. 18.569.

Absol. : δουρὶ μέσον περόνησεν (in his middle) Il. 7.145, Il. 13.397, μέσσῃ δʼ ἐνὶ πῖλος ἀρήρει (app. so as to form a lining to protect the head from chafing) Il. 10.265, σφῆκες μέσον αἰόλοι (about the middle) Il. 12.167. Cf. Il. 13.534, Il. 16.623, Il. 20.413, 486, Il. 23.875 : ἐν μέσσῃ καθῖζεν Od. 5.326. Cf. Od. 5.487, Od. 10.196, Od. 20.306.

In pl. : στὰς ἐν μέσσοισιν Il. 7.384, ἕλκε μέσσα λαβών (grasping the middle of it) Il. 8.72, Il. 22.212, ἐνὶ μέσσῃς κλαῖεν Il. 24.84. Cf. Il. 4.212, Il. 11.35, 413, Il. 12.457, Il. 13.308, Il. 15.635, Il. 18.606, Il. 19.77, Il. 23.134, etc.: Od. 4.19, 281, 413, Od. 24.441.

div.head: a
div.p: μέσσῳ, in the midst : μέσσῳ ποταμοί [εἰσιν] Od. 11.157.

div.head: b
div.p: μέσσῷ μεσηγύ 2.a : μέσσῳ ἀμφοτέρων σκῆπτρα σχέθον Il. 7.277 : μέσσῳ δαιτυμόνων (among the...) Od. 8.66= 473.

div.head: c
div.p: μέσσῳ = μεσηγύ 2.b : μέσσῳ ἀμφοτέρων μητίσομαι ἔχθεα Il. 3.416.

div.head: a
div.p: ἐν μέσ(σ)ῳ, in the middle space, in the midst: ἔμʼ ἐν μέσσῳ καὶ Μενέλαον συμβάλετε μάχεσθαι Il. 3.69. Cf. Il. 3.90, Il. 10.474, Il. 17.375, Il. 18.264 : ἐν μέσσῳ στᾶσα Od. 12.20. Cf. Od. 9.429.
Sim. after a compound of ἐν : ἔνθορε μέσσῳ Il. 21.233. Cf. Il. 4.444 : Od. 12.443.

div.head: b
div.p: ἐς μέσ(σ)ον, into the middle space, in the midst : ἐς μέσσον ἰών Il. 3.77= Il. 7.55. Cf. Il. 4.79, 299, Il. 15.357, Il. 23.704, 814 : Od. 8.144, 262, Od. 17.447, Od. 18.89.
With genit. : ἐς μέσον ἀμφοτέρων Il. 6.120= Il. 20.159. Cf. Il. 3.266 = 341.– ἐς μέσον ἀμφοτέροισι δικάσσατε (impartially) Il. 23.574.

div.head: c
div.p: κατὰ μέσσον, through the midst : ἀντικρὺ κατὰ μέσσον Il. 16.285. Cf. Il. 4.541, Il. 5.8.
In neut. sing. : μέσ(σ)ον as adv., in the middle : νηῦς ἔθεεν μέσσον ὑπὲρ κρήτης (app., taking the mid-sea course) Od. 14.300.– = μεσηγύ 2..a : κὰδ δὲ μέσον τάφρου καὶ τείχεος ἶζον Il. 9.87.
Like μέσος 4.a: ἐν μεσσάτῳ ἔσκεν (just in the middle) Il. 8.223= Il. 11.6.
Etymologically, the middle part of the αὐλή, but used simply as= αὐλή.

In sense 1.a : ἀέκων ἔβη [λὶς] ἀπὸ μεσσαύλοιο Il. 17.112. Cf. Il. 11.548, Il. 17.657 : ὅτε οἱ
μέο σαυλον ἵκοντο ἡμέτεροι ἕταροι Od. 10.435 (app.= the αὐλή of Od. 9.184, etc.).
Planted or driven in up to the middle : ἔγχος Il. 21.172.
Towards, in the direction of, something : μετὰ δʼ ἰὸν ἕηκεν Il. 1.48.
Sim. indicating that action is directed in a particular way : μετὰ τυδέος υἱὸν ἕπουσαν (directing, looking after, him) Il. 10.516.
Among, in company with, others : μετὰ δʼ ἀνέρες οὓς ἔχε γῆρας Il. 18.515. Cf. Il. 2.446, 477.
Among others, in a company : μετὰ μῦθον ἔειπεν Il. 3.303, etc. Cf. Od. 12.319, Od. 18.2.
With, in addition to, others : μετὰ δʼ ἔσσεται κούρη Βρισῆος Il. 9.131, 273. Cf. Il. 15.67.
Coming after, following : μετὰ νέφος εἵπετο πεζῶν Il. 23.133.
After in time, afterwards, in succession : πρῶτος ἐγώ, μετὰ δʼ ὔμμες Od. 21.231.
Afterwards, in after days : μετὰ γάρ τε καὶ ἄλγεσι τέρπεται ἀνήρ Od. 15.400.
So as to face the rear or reverse one's position, round : μετὰ δʼ ἐτράπετο Il. 1.199. Cf. Il. 8.94.
In reference to change of position in a course or path : μετὰ δʼ ἄστρα βεβήκει (had crossed the meridian) Od. 12.312, Od. 14.483.
At intervals : μετὰ δʼ [ὅρμος] ἠλέκτροισιν ἔερτο Od. 15.460.

div.head: II
div.p: Prep. (commonly with anastrophe when immediately following the case-form).

div.head: α
div.p: In reference to the hands, arms or feet : μετὰ χερσίν (in ...) Il. 5.344, μετὰ ποσσίν Il. 19.110. Cf. Il. 11.4, Il. 15.717, etc. : Od. 3.281, Od. 4.300, Od. 5.49, Od. 21.245, etc.
To the jaws : μετὰ γένυσσιν Il. 11.416. Cf. Il. 13.200.
Sim. in reference to the φρένες regarded as having a double character : μετὰ φρεσίν (in...) Il. 4.245, Il. 9.434, Il. 18.419, etc. : Od. 4.825, Od. 10.438, Od. 16.436, etc.

div.head: β
div.p: Of position or relations between two persons or groups : ἦ φιλότητα μετʼ ἀμφοτέροισι βάλωμεν Il. 4.16. Cf. Il. 3.110, Il. 4.38, Il. 7.66, etc. : Od. 3.136, Od. 24.476, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: Among, amid, in the midst of, with : μετά σφισιν Il. 2.93. Cf. Il. 1.252, Il. 3.85, Il. 4.2, Il. 8.525, Il. 18.234, Il. 21.122, etc. : Od. 1.19, Od. 2.310, Od. 4.254, Od. 9.335, 418, Od. 10.204, etc.
In reference to things : μετʼ ἀστράσιν Il. 22.28, 317, μετὰ πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο (on the...) Il. 23.367. Cf. Il. 13.579, 668, Il. 15.118 : Od. 2.148, Od. 3.91, Od. 4.499, Od. 5.224= Od. 17.285.
With sing. sb. in collective sense : μεθʼ αἵματι Il. 15.118, μετὰ στροφάλιγγι κονίης (in...) Od. 21.503. Cf. Il. 19.50, Il. 22.49 : Od. 8.156, Od. 11.449.
Of division or distribution : δάσσαντο μετὰ σφίσιν Il. 1.368.

div.head: a
div.p: Between (with notion of motion) : ἔφερον ἅρμα μετὰ Τρῶας καὶ Ἀχαιούς (between the fighting lines) Il. 11.533= Il. 17.458.

div.head: b
div.p: So as to be among or with, to, towards, to join : βεβήκει μετὰ δαίμονας ἄλλους Il. 1.222. Cf. Il. 1.423, Il. 3.264, Il. 5.264, Il. 17.149, etc. : ἄνδρας μέτα οἰνοποτῆρας ἤϊεν Od. 8.456. Cf. Od. 3.168, Od. 6.115, Od. 11.563, Od. 23.83, etc.
In hostile sense Il. 5.152, Il. 6.21, Il. 13.301 (or perh. here simply to join), Il. 17.460, etc. : Od. 6.133.
In reference to things : μετὰ νῆας Il. 5.165, Il. 12.123. Cf. Il. 2.376, Il. 6.511, etc. : μετὰ δαῖτας (to share in them) Od. 22.352.
With sing. sb. in collective sense : ἀνάγοντο μετὰ στρατὸν Ἀχαιῶν Il. 1.478. Cf. Il. 5.573, Il. 7.115, Il. 14.21, Il. 20.33, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: Without notion of motion, among : θυμὸν ὄρινε πᾶσι μετὰ πληθύν Il. 2.143. Cf. Il. 9.54 : οἳ ἀριστεύουσι μεθʼ ἡμέας Od. 4.652 (or this might come under f). Cf. Od. 16.419.

div.head: d
div.p: Going after or behind, following, following up : μετὰ κλέος ἵκετʼ Ἀχαιῶν (following up the rumour of the expedition) Il. 11.227. Cf. Il. 11.357, Il. 13.364, 492, 513, Il. 18.321 : μεθʼ ἡμιόνους ἔρχεσθαι Od. 6.260. Cf. Od. 2.406, etc.

div.head: e
div.p: Following, after, in succession to : τὸν δὲ μετʼ Ἀτρεΐδαι [ἦλθον] Il. 8.261. Cf. Il. 8.289, Il. 18.96, Il. 23.227, 354, etc. : Od. 11.260, Od. 15.147, etc.

div.head: f
div.p: In comparisons, after, next to : κάλλιστος μετὰ Πηλεΐωνα Il. 2.674. Cf. Il. 7.228, Il. 9.140, Il. 12.104, Il. 16.146, etc. : Od. 2.350, Od. 8.117, 583, Od. 11.310, etc.–

div.head: g
div.p: Following, taking the line of, in consonance with : μετὰ σὸν καὶ ἐμὸν κῆρ Il. 15.52. Cf. Il. 18.552.

div.head: h
div.p: After, for, in order to find or get, in quest or search of : βῆ ῥʼ ἰέναι μετὰ Νέστορα Il. 10.73. Cf. Il. 7.418, Il. 11.700, Il. 13.247, 252, Il. 16.536, etc. : πλέων μετὰ χαλκόν Od. 1.184. Cf. Od. 2.206, Od. 13.415, Od. 16.151, Od. 20.153, Od. 21.17 (to recover it), etc.
Sim. : πόλεμον μέτα (for...) Il. 20.329. Cf. Il. 7.147, Il. 13.291.
In reference to looking : σκεψάμενος μεθʼ ἑταίρους (for...) Od. 12.247.
With genit., among, along with, with : μετὰ βοιωτῶν ἐμάχοντο Il. 13.700, τῶν μέτα παλλόμενος Il. 24.400. Cf. Il. 21.458 : Od. 10.320, Od. 16.140.
There is among specified persons : οὐ γάρ τις μέτα τοῖος ἀνὴρ ἐν τοίσδεσιν Od. 21.93.
Fig., to choose a fresh theme Od. 8.492.
To adopt changed or different counsels : μετεβούλευσαν ἄλλως Od. 5.286.
