Without expressed object Il. 11.235= Il. 17.48, Il. 13.147 = Il. 15.278= Il. 17.731, Il. 23.819.
Sim. in mid. of reciprocal action Il. 14.26= Il. 16.637.
App. implying no more than striking with the hand : χείρεσσʼ ἀσπίδα νύσσων Il. 16.704.
To give one a nudge (with the elbow) : ἀγκῶνι νύξας Od. 14.485.
Acc. νῶϊ. Also νώ Il. 5.219 : Od. 15.475.
Pron. of the 1st person dual, we : καὶ νῶϊ μεδώμεθʼ ἀλκῆς Il. 4.418, νῶϊν ἐπέντυε μώνυχας ἵππους Il. 8.374. Cf. Il. 8.428, Il. 22.88, etc. : Od. 4.160, 172, Od. 15.475, etc.
Our (of two persons) : λέχος Il. 15.39 : ὄπα Od. 12.185.
Without cease, cessation, pause, relaxation of effort, blenching : μάχην ἔχουσιν Il. 14.58. Cf. Il. 17.413.
= νωλεμές. : κίνυντο φάλαγγες Il. 4.428. Cf. Il. 5.492, Il. 13.3, 780 : πίεζεν Od. 4.288. Cf. Od. 9.435, Od. 11.413, Od. 12.437, Od. 20.24.
To distribute or give out among a company : σπλάγχνα Od. 20.252.
Without expressed object Il. 1.471= Il. 9.176 := Od. 3.340 = Od. 21.272, Od. 7.183, Od. 13.54= Od. 18.425.
To handle, wield, move, control : σκῆπτρον Il. 3.218. Cf. Il. 5.594, Il. 7.238, Il. 15.677 : Od. 10.32, Od. 12.218, Od. 21.245, 393, 400, Od. 22.10.
To put in motion, ply (the limbs, etc.) : γούνατʼ ἐνώμα Il. 10.358, Il. 22.144. Cf. Il. 15.269, Il. 22.24.
In reference to the mind, to apply it (skilfully) to the matter in hand, have it in (constant) practice or readiness : νόον πολυκερδέα νωμῶν Od. 13.255.
Sim. in reference to the contents of the mind : κέρδεʼ ἐνώμας Od. 18.216. Cf. Od. 20.257.
Nameless, the very name lost : ὅπως ἀπὸ φῦλον ὄληται νώνυμον Od. 14.182.
Unknown, little known, obscure : οὐδέ τι λίην οὕτω νώνυμός ἐστιν [ἥδε γαῖα] Od. 13.239.
App., gleaming, glancing, or the like.
The back : οὐκ ἂν ἐν αὐχένι πέσοι βέλος οὐδʼ ἐνὶ νώτῳ Il. 13.289. Cf. Il. 5.147, Il. 20.279, Il. 21.69, Il. 23.714 : Od. 17.463.
The back of an animal cut off for use as food, the chine Il. 9.207 : Od. 8.475.
In pl., app., slices cut from the back : νώτοισι γέραιρεν Il. 7.321 : Od. 14.437. Cf. Od. 4.65.
In pl. in sing. sense : μετὰ νῶτα βαλών Il. 8.94. Cf. Il. 13.547, Il. 20.414 : Od. 6.225.
Of the surface of the sea : ἐπʼ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης Il. 2.159, Il. 8.511, Il. 20.228 : Od. 3.142, Od. 4.313, 362, 560= Od. 5.17 = 142= Od. 17.146.
Remissness, supineness, tardiness in action : βραδυτῆτί τε νωχελίῃ τε Il. 19.411.
-ή, -όν. Yellow. Of horses, bay or chestnut Il. 9.407, Il. 11.680.
Of hair, yellow, fair Il. 1.197, Il. 23.141 : Od. 13.399, 431.
As a personal epithet, of the fair hair, fair-haired. Of Meleager Il. 2.642.
Such as may fitly be given by a host to a guest : δῶρα Od. 24.273.

Absol. in neut., a present given by a host to a guest, or given one to the other by persons between whom the ξεῖνος relationship exists (see ξεῖνος 2) : ἀλλήλοισι πόρον ξεινήϊα Il. 6.218. Cf. Il. 10.269, Il. 11.20 : Od. 8.389, Od. 9.267.
Sarcastically : τοῦτό (i.e. the stroke with the spear) τοι ἀντὶ ποδὸς ξεινήϊον [ἔσται] Od. 22.290. Cf. Od. 9.370.
Absol. in neut. pl., fare or good things put before a guest : παράθες οἱ ξεινήϊα Il. 18.408. Cf. Od. 3.490, Od. 4.33.
3 sing. ξείνισε Il. 6.217. ξείνισσε Il. 3.232, Il. 6.174.
To receive or entertain hospitably, treat as an honoured guest Il. 3.207, 232, Il. 6.174, 217 : Od. 3.355, Od. 7.190, Od. 14.322, Od. 19.194 = Od. 24.271, Od. 19.217, Od. 24.266, 288.

p.gloss: That guards the obligations arising from the relationship of guest and host and the claim of strangers to protection.

div.p: Epithet of Zeus Il. 13.625 : Od. 9.271, Od. 14.284.
Absol. in neut., a present given by a host to a guest Od. 9.229, 365, Od. 19.185.
Absol. in neut. pl., fare or good things put before a guest Il. 11.779, Il. 18.387 := Od. 5.91, Od. 14.404, Od. 15.188.

div.head: a
div.p: A foreigner, one belonging to another land : ἐπʼ ἀνθρώους ξείνους ἠδʼ οἷσιν ἀνάσσεις Il. 24.202.
One not of one's own immediate folk : ξεῖνοί τε καὶ αὐτοῦ βώτορες Od. 14.102. Cf. Od. 17.382.

div.head: b
div.p: A stranger, one who comes into, or finds himself in, a land not his own : εἰσῆλθε μυκήνας ξ. Il. 4.377. Cf. Il. 4.387 : Od. 7.24, Od. 18.106 (wanderers or vagabonds), Od. 19.333 (travellers), Od. 21.292.

Such a person regarded as being under the guardianship of Zeus, as entitled to protection and aid : πρὸς διός εἰσι ξεῖνοί τε πτωχοί τε Od. 6.208= Od. 14.58. Cf. Od. 8.546, Od. 9.270, 478, Od. 14.57, Od. 16.108, Od. 18.222, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: A stranger, a person whom one has not seen before, an unknown person who presents himself before one : πόθεν τοι ξ. ὅδʼ ἵκετο; Od. 16.57. Cf. Od. 1.120, Od. 4.26, Od. 6.209, Od. 8.28, Od. 14.414, Od. 17.10, Od. 18.401, Od. 20.129, etc.
Vocativally Od. 1.123, Od. 3.71, Od. 4.371, Od. 6.187, etc.
Vocativally by a ξ. to one of those among whom he has come Od. 8.166, Od. 14.53.

One of two persons (in pl. the persons) dwelling at a distance from each other between whom there exists a special tie of friendship and mutual hospitality : ξ. μοι πατρώϊός ἐσσι Il. 6.215. Cf. Il. 6.224, 231, Il. 13.661, Il. 15.532, Il. 17.150, 584, Il. 21.42 : ξ. ἐμός ἐστιν Od. 11.338. Cf. Od. 1.105, 176, 187, 313, Od. 9.18, Od. 15.196, Od. 19.191, Od. 24.104, etc.
A host, one's host : ξείνια παρέθηκεν, ἅ τε ξείνοις θέμις ἐστίν Il. 11.779. Cf. Od. 8.208, Od. 9.268, Od. 19.371.
A guest, one's guest : ξεινοδόκοι καὶ ξ. Od. 8.543. Cf. Od. 3.350, Od. 15.54, 73, 74, Od. 20.295= Od. 21.313, Od. 21.27.

Hospitable bounty :
μίξεσθαι ξενίῃ (in mutual hospitality) Od. 24.314. Cf. Od. 24.286.
That serves as a symbol of the obligations of a guest in reference to his host or of the claims of a stranger to protection : ἴστω ξενίη τράπεζα Od. 14.158= Od. 17.155= Od. 20.230.
Absol. in neut. pl. = ξείνοις3 Od. 15.514, 546.
Absol. in neut., the dry land, the shore : ποτὶ ξερὸν ἠπείροιο Od. 5.402.
Of the Trojan horse : ἵππῳ ἔνι ξεστῷ Od. 4.272.
3 sing. aor. ἔξεσε Il. 5.81. ξέσσε Od. 5.245, Od. 17.341, Od. 21.44. (ἀμφι-)
To remove roughness or irregularities from the surface of, smooth, work up Od. 5.245, Od. 17.341 = Od. 21.44, Od. 23.199.
With ἀπό, to slice off : ἀπὸ δʼ ἔξεσε χεῖρα Il. 5.81.
A piece of wood, a post Il. 23.327.
In pl., wood for burning, firewood : ξύλα πολλὰ λέγεσθε Il. 8.507. Cf. Il. 8.547, Il. 18.347, Il. 21.364, Il. 24.778 : Od. 3.429, Od. 8.436, Od. 14.418, Od. 15.322, etc.
See σύν. ξυμ-, ξυν-. See συμ-, συν-.
In common : τεύχεʼ ἀμφότεροι ξυνήϊα ταῦτα φερέσθων Il. 23.809.
Absol. in neut. pl. ξυνήϊα, a common store : οὔ τί που ἴδμεν ξυνήϊα κείμενα πολλά (laid up in abundance) Il. 1.124.
-ή, -όν. Common : γαῖʼ ἔτι ξυνή [ἐστιν] Il. 15.193. Cf. Il. 16.262.
A razor. Fig. : ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἵσταται ἀκμῆς ἢ . . . ἠὲ . . . Il. 10.173.
[neut. of ξυστός, vbl. adj. from ξύω. That which is worked smooth.]
Some kind of long pole used in sea-fighting Il. 15.388, 677.
To remove irregularities from the surface of, scrape smooth : λίστροισιν δάπεδον ξῦον Od. 22.456.
To treat so as to produce a smooth surface upon : ἑανόν, ὅν οἱ Ἀθήνη ἔξυσʼ ἀσκησασα Il. 14.179.

div.head: ὁ, ἡ, τό
div.p: Genit. masc. and neut. τοῖο Il. 1.380, 493, etc. : Od. 3.334, 388, etc.
Genit. dual τοῖϊν Il. 11.110, etc. : Od. 18.34.
Nom. pl. τοί Il. 1.447, Il. 2.52, etc. : Od. 1.112, 250, etc.
Fem. ταί Il. 3.5, etc. : Od. 6.90, etc.
Genit. pl. fem. τάων Il. 4.46, Il. 5.320, etc. : Od. 2.119, Od. 7.117, etc.
Dat. τῇσι Il. 6.298, etc. : Od. 6.101, etc. τῇς Il. 5.750, etc. : Od. 4.721, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: As anaphoric pronoun of the 3rd person, he, she, it : ὁ γὰρ νοῦσον ἀνὰ στρατὸν ὦρσεν Il. 1.9. Cf. Il. 1.12, 29, 43, 58, 221, etc. : Od. 1.9, 13, 31, 113, 249, 277, etc.–ὁ (οἱ) μὲν . . . ὁ (οἱ) δὲ . . ., one (some) . . . the other ((the) others) . . . : οἱ μὲν δάμεν, οἱ δὲ λίποντο Il. 12.14. Cf. Il. 2.90, Il. 18.499, etc. : Od. 1.24, Od. 5.477, Od. 7.104, Od. 10.85, etc.
So in resumption in a second clause : νῆας ἔπηξε, πολὺν δʼ ὅ γε λαὸν ἀγείρας βῆ Il. 2.664. Cf. Il. 3.409, etc. : Od. 2.327, etc.
Of the 1st person : ὁ δʼ ἀλλοδαπῷ ἐνὶ δήμῳ πολεμίζω Il. 19.324.

div.head: b
div.p: Sometimes to be translated this, that, in pl. these (those) things, matters, etc. : τό τοι κὴρ εἴδεται εἶναι Il. 1.228, τῶν οὐκ ἄν τι φέροις Il. 1.301. Cf. Il. 1.318, Il. 17.228, etc. : Od. 1.10, 74 (from that time), Od. 9.393, Od. 14.444, Od. 24.255, etc.
With γε: εἰ τό γʼ ἄμεινον Il. 1.116, etc. : μὴ μητέρʼ ἅζευ τό γε (to that point) Od. 17.401, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: In dat. sing. fem. τῇ, in that place or spot, there : τῇ τόν γε μένον Od. 4.847. Cf. Il. 8.327, Il. 11.520, etc. : Od. 12.62, etc.
Thither : τῇ γʼ ἐλθόντες Il. 6.435. Cf. Il. 15.360, etc. : Od. 8.556.

With sb. or proper name in apposition : ἡ δʼ ἅμα τοῖσι γυνὴ κίεν Il. 1.348, τοὺς δὲ κατὰ πρύμνας ἔλσαι Ἀχαιούς Il. 1.409. Cf. Il. 4.20, 391, 502, Il. 5.449, etc. : Od. 1.439, Od. 2.365, Od. 3.450, Od. 4.353, Od. 5.94, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: The article of contrast : παῖδα δʼ ἐμοὶ λύσαιτε, τὰ δʼ ἄποινα δέχεσθαι (and on the other side accept the ransom) Il. 1.20, ἦ τῶν πλεόνων Λυκίων ἀπὸ θυμὸν ἕλοιτο (more Lycians instead) Il. 5.673. Cf. Il. 1.340, Il. 2.217, 278, Il. 4.399, etc. Also in Od. passim.

With adjectives, numerals, genitives, etc. : τῇ δεκάτῃ Il. 1.54, τὸν ἐμὸν χόλον Il. 4.42, τοὺς τέσσαρας Il. 5.271, τὴν αὐτοῦ Il. 9.342. Cf. Il. 1.6, 165, 198, Il. 6.201, 435, Il. 8.525, Il. 9.320, Il. 11.613, Il. 16.358, Il. 23.265, etc. Also in Od. passim.

div.head: b
div.p: The defining article: ὁ γέρων Il. 1.33, τὸν ὄνειρον Il. 2.80. Cf. Il. 1.35, 552, Il. 2.275 (conveying a hostile or contemptuous tone), 351, Il. 5.265, 308, 320, Il. 7.412, Il. 10.97, Il. 11.142, Il. 14.280, Il. 20.147, Il. 23.75, etc. Also in Od. passim.–With an infin. : τὸ φυλάσσειν Od. 20.52.
As relative (accented throughout; except in Il. 1.125, Il. 9.167 : Od. 4.349 = Od. 17.140 following the antecedent, and most commonly referring to a definite antecedent).

div.head: a
div.p: μῆνιν, ἣ μυρίʼ Ἀχαιοῖς ἄλγεʼ ἔθηκεν Il. 1.2. Cf. Il. 1.36, 72, 234, 319, 321, 336, etc. : ἔτος, τῷ οἱ ἐπεκλώσαντο νέεσθαι Od. 1.17. Cf. Od. 1.23, 97, 344, 430, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: With τε: συσί, τῶν τε σθένος οὐκ ἀλαπαδνόν Il. 5.783. Cf. Il. 2.262, etc. : Od. 1.338, Od. 3.73, etc.

div.head: c
div.p:
With subj. and κεν: δῶρα φερέμεν, τά κε θυμὸν
ἰήνῃ Il. 24.119.

div.head: α
div.p: With fut., subj. or opt. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table at end III.B.a 1,

div.head: β
div.p: With subj. in a simile : ἐκ νήσου, τὴν δήϊοι ἀμφιμάχωνται Il. 18.208.

div.head: α
div.p: In dat. sing. fem. τῇ, in or at the place or spot in which, in or at which place or spot, where : τῇ ἔμελλε διεξίμεναι Il. 6.393. Cf. Il. 11.499, Il. 23.775, etc. : Od. 4.565, Od. 5.442, etc.
In which way or manner, as : τῇ περ δὴ καὶ ἔπειτα τελευτήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν Od. 8.510.
To the place or spot in which, to where : εἴ κε φεύγω τῇ περ κλονέονται Il. 21.554.

div.head: β
div.p: In acc. sing. neut. τό, wherefore : τὸ καὶ κλαίουσα τέτηκα Il. 3.176, τό μοι ἔστι ταλαύρινον πολεμίζειν Il. 7.239. Cf. Il. 12.9, Il. 17.404, etc. : Od. 8.332.
With dat. : ᾗ γυναικί Il. 6.516. Cf. Il. 22.127 (of lovers' converse and dalliance), 128.
One who holds familiar converse, is admitted to intimacy, with another : μίνως Διὸς ὀαριστής Od. 19.179.
Of the commerce of foemen Il. 17.228.
Of grappling with the foe Il. 13.291.
That does deeds of violence, violent : ἀνέρα Il. 22.418. Cf. Il. 5.403.
Epithet or a name of Athene Il. 5.747= Il. 8.391 := Od. 1.101, Od. 3.135, Od. 24.540.
Epithet of spears Il. 3.357, Il. 4.529, Il. 5.790, Il. 11.456, etc.
As a disyllable Od. 7.261, Od. 14.287. =ὀγδόατος. Il. 7.223, 246 : Od. 7.261= Od. 14.287.
Thus, a box or tray for carrying things Od. 21.61.
A barb of an arrow Il. 4.151, 214.

In reaping, the line taken by a reaper advancing through the field : δράγματα μετʼ ὄγμον πῖπτον (following the line of the reaper, in line on his left) Il. 18.552, βασιλεὺς ἑστήκει ἐπʼ ὄγμου 557 (i.e. watching the reapers from the line of the nearest). Cf. Il. 11.68.
Cargo taken in for the return voyage, a home-cargo (opposed to φόρτος) : ἐπείγετʼ ὦνον ὁδαίων Od. 15.445. Cf. Od. 8.163.
With the teeth : ὀ. ἕλον οὖδας (bit the dust) Il. 11.749, Il. 19.61, Il. 24.738. Cf. Il. 2.418, Il. 22.17 : Od. 1.381= Od. 18.410= Od. 20.268, Od. 22.269.

div.head: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε
div.p: Dat. pl. masc. and neut. τοίσδεσσι Il. 10.462 : Od. 2.47, 165, Od. 13.258. Masc τοίσδεσι Od. 10.268, Od. 21.93.

This person or thing (in reported speech generally (and properly) referring to what belongs to or concerns the speaker ; cf. οὗτος) : τοῦδʼ ἕνεκα Il. 1.110, τήνδε θεῷ πρόες 127. Cf. Il. 1.257, 275, 302, Il. 2.5, 236, etc. : Od. 1.169, 371, 396, Od. 2.162, 191, etc.
With sb., etc., this : τόδʼ ἐέλδωρ Il. 1.41. Cf. Il. 1.214, 234, 287, Il. 2.252, etc. : Od. 1.232, Od. 2.93, 280, 317, etc.

In deictic or predicative sense = here : Ἕκτορος ἥδε γυνή (this is . . .) Il. 6.460. Cf. Il. 5.175, Il. 9.688, Il. 15.286, Il. 19.140, etc. : ξείνω δή τινε τώδε (here are . . .) Od. 4.26. Cf. Od. 1.185, Od. 6.206, Od. 11.141, Od. 16.205, etc.
In dat. sing. fem. τῇδε, here : τῇδε τετεύξεται ὄλεθρος Il. 12.345. Cf. Il. 17.512, Il. 24.139 : Od. 5.113, Od. 6.173, Od. 12.186.
To go, find passage, make one's way : ἐπὶ νῆας Il. 11.569.
A journeyer, wayfarer, passenger, passer-by Il. 16.263: Od. 7.204, Od. 11.127, Od. 13.123, Od. 17.211, Od. 23.274.
A reward for bearing one company Od. 15.506.
[app. a locative fr. ὁδός + πορ- as in πόρος.]
The first syllable lengthened metrically οὐδός Od. 17.196.

A way, path, track, passage, road : ἐπεὶ πρὸ ὁδοῦ ἐγένοντο (local genit., forward on their way) Il. 4.382, παρὲξ ὁδοῦ κλινθήτην Il. 10.349, ἀμφὶς ὁδοῦ δραμέτην (local genit., apart on their way) Il. 23.393. Cf. Il. 6.15, 391, Il. 7.143, Il. 16.374, etc.: Od. 5.237, Od. 6.264, Od. 8.107, Od. 9.261, Od. 10.103, etc.

A going, journey, voyage, course : τὴν ὁδὸν ἣν Ἑλένην ἀνήγαγεν (on that voyage on which . . .) Il. 6.292. Cf. Il. 1.151, Il. 9.626 : ἐπειγόμενός περ ὁδοῖο Od. 1.309. Cf. Od. 1.444, Od. 2.285, Od. 3.316, Od. 4.393 (in your absence on a long journey), Od. 6.165, Od. 8.444, Od. 16.138, Od. 21.20, etc.
Means of journeying or passage, facilities for a journey : πάρ τοι ὁδός (your way lies open) Il. 9.43 : ὁδὸν ᾔτεον Od. 10.17. Cf. Od. 12.334.
Dat. pl. ὀδοῦσι Il. 5.75, Il. 11.114, etc.
In reference to bodily pain, a pain or pang : ὀδύνη διὰ χροὸς ἦλθεν Il. 11.398.
In pl., pains, pangs : ἀχθομένην ὀδύνῃσιν Il. 5.354. Cf. Il. 4.117, Il. 5.399, Il. 12.206, Il. 15.60, etc. : Od. 9.415, 440, Od. 17.567.
In reference to mental pain, grief, sorrow, distress : ἀζηχὴς ὀ. Ἡρακλῆος (for . . ) Il. 15.25.
In pl., griefs, sorrows, distresses : ἐμοὶ ὀδύνας κάλλιπεν Od. 1.242. Cf. Od. 2.79, Od. 4.812, Od. 19.117.
Stilling or allaying pain, soothing: φάρμακα Il. 5.401= 900, ῥίζαν Il. 11.847.
3 sing. aor. subj. ὀδύρεται Il. 23.222 : Od. 4.740.

To make lament, weep, wail, mourn, sorrow, grieve : ὀδύρετο δάκρυα λείβων Il. 18.32. Cf. Il. 9.591, 612, Il. 22.79, Il. 23.154, 222, 224, Il. 24.48, 128, 166, 549 : Od. 1.55, Od. 4.194, Od. 5.160, Od. 8.33, Od. 14.129, Od. 18.203, Od. 23.241, etc.
With genit. of person mourned for : τῶν πάντων οὐ τόσσον ὀδύρομαι ὡς ἑνός Il. 22.424 := Od. 4.104. Cf. Od. 4.819, Od. 14.40, 142, 174, Od. 15.355.
With genit. of something not attained mourned for : γάμου Od. 21.250.
To make lament or complaint, set forth one's wrongs : εἴ που κεῖνος ἐξελθὼν λαοῖσιν ὀδύρεται Od. 4.740.
To lament, weep for, mourn : ἕταρον Il. 19.345. Cf. Il. 24.714, 740: Od. 1.243, Od. 4.100, 110.
To long for in sorrow, be sick for to the point of tears : πατρίδα γαῖαν Od. 13.219. Cf. Od. 5.153, Od. 13.379.
With infin., to express by lamentation one's longing to do something : οἶκόνδε νέεσθαι Il. 2.290.
To be angry, wroth, incensed, to rage : ὀδυσσαμένοιο τεοῖο (in thy wrath) Il. 8.37= 468, ἐπεὶ ὠδύσατο Ζεύς (has conceived wrath against us) Il. 18.292.
With dat. of person : τίνύ οἱ τόσον ὠδύσαο ; Od. 1.62. Cf. Il. 6.138 : Od. 5.340, 423 (cherishes wrath), Od. 19.275, 407.
A branch or shoot : φύλλα καὶ ὄζους Il. 1.234. Cf. Il. 2.312, Il. 4.484, Il. 6.39, Il. 10.467, Il. 14.289, Il. 16.768, Il. 21.245 : Od. 12.435.

A scion or child (but in this sense perh. another word ὀ- = ἀ-2 + ζ- = σδ-, σεδ-, root of ὁδός, a companion or follower) : ὄζος Ἄρηος Il. 2.540, 704, 745, 842, Il. 12.188, Il. 23.841, Il. 24.474. Cf. Il. 2.663, Il. 3.147 =Il. 20.238.
3 sing. plupf. (in impf. sense) ὀδώδει Od. 5.60, Od. 9.210.
To have a certain scent, smell; of a scent, to spread, come, reach the sense : τηλόθʼ ὀδμὴ κέδρου τε θύου τʼ ὀδώδει Od. 5.60. Cf. Od. 9.210.
From which place or spot, whence : ὅθεν ῥέεν ὕδωρ Il. 2.307. Cf. Il. 10.200, Il. 11.758 : Od. 3.319, 321, Od. 4.358 (see ἀπό II.1.a), Od. 22.460.
Sim. : ἐς σικελούς, ὅθεν κέ τοι ἄξιον ἄλφοι Od. 20.383.
In reference to a starting - point : τοῦ χώρου ὅθεν τέ περ οἰνοχοεύει (the spot from which the round is begun) Od. 21.142.
In reference to source, origin or birth, whence : γένος μοι ἔνθεν ὅθεν σοί Il. 4.58. Cf. Il. 2.852, 857.
To a source from which one draws : ὅθεν ἱδρεύοντο Od. 7.131, Od. 17.206.
To a source of (imagined) light Od. 11.366 (see εἴδω I.1).

In or at the place or spot in which, in or at which place or spot, where : λήμνῳ ἐν, ὅθι μιν λίπον Il. 2.722. Cf. Il. 2.572, Il. 3.145, Il. 4.41, 217, Il. 5.8, Il. 8.83, etc. : ἐν δαπέδῳ, ὅθι περ πάρος Od. 4.627. Cf. Od. 1.50, Od. 2.338, Od. 3.326, Od. 4.127, 426, Od. 5.280, Od. 9.50, etc.
With subj. or opt. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table at end III.B.a 1,
To the place or spot in which, to where : ἴθυνεν ὅθι ζωστῆρος ὀχῆες σύνεχον Il. 4.132, etc. Cf. Od. 1.425, etc.
With neg., not to care for, trouble oneself about, have regard for.
With genit. : οὐδʼ ὄθομαι κοτέοντος (I care not for your wrath) Il. 1.181.
With infin., to hesitate to do something, shrink from doing it : οὐκ ὄθεται ἦτορ ἷσον ἐμοὶ (ἶσόν οἱ) φάσθαι Il. 15.166, 182.
Sim. with pple. : οὐκ ὄθετʼ αἴσυλα ῥέζων Il. 5.403.
In pl., clothes or wrappings (prob. of linen) : ἀργεννῇσι κσλυψαμένη ὀθόνῃσιν Il. 3.141. Cf. Il. 18.595.
Of horses, having hair of the same colour, one in coats Il. 2.765.
3 pl. impf. pass. ὠΐγνυντο Il. 2.809, Il. 8.58. (ἀναοίγω.)
To draw back (a bar in order to open a door) ,
To broach or draw (wine) : οἴνου, τὸν ὤϊξεν ταμίη Od. 3.392.
To cause to swell. Fig. : χόλος, ὅς τε καὶ ἄλλων οἰδάνει νόον Il. 9.554.
Sim. in pass. : οἰδάνεταί μοι κραδίη χόλῳ (swells with . . . ) Il. 9.646.
To swell : ᾤδεε χρόα πάντα (acc. of part affected, his flesh became swollen) Od. 5.455.
A swelling. Of water : ποταμὸς οἴδματι θύων (in flood) Il. 21.234. Cf. Il. 23.230 (with swelling surface).
Of horses, of the same age, one in years Il. 2.765.
Wretched, miserable, unhappy, ill-starred : ὀ. περὶ πάντων ἔπλεο Il. 1.417. Cf. Il. 13.569 : Od. 3.95=Od. 4.325, Od. 4.197, 832.
Causing, bringing in its train, pain or grief, sorrowful, woful : πολέμοιο Il. 3.112. Cf. Od. 8.540, Od. 11.182=Od. 16.38, Od. 13.337.
Sorrow, grief, woe, distress, hardship : πόνον τʼ ἐχέμεν καὶ ὀϊζύν Il. 13.2. Cf. Il. 6.285, Il. 14.480 : Od. 3.103, Od. 4.35, Od. 5.289, Od. 7.211, 270, etc.
The result of pains or painful toil Il. 15.365.
To suffer grief, distress, anxiety, hardship Il. 3.408: Od. 4.152, Od. 23.307.
With cognate acc., to suffer : ἧς εἵνεκʼ ὀϊζύομεν κακὰ πολλά Il. 14.89.
The steering-oar of a ship Il. 19.43 : Od. 9.483 = 540.
In pl. app. of a single oar : ἐπεὶ νηὸς οἰήϊα νωμᾷς Od. 12.218.
Perh., guides on the yoke for the reins Il. 24.269.

To one's house or home, home, homewards : οἰ. ἴμεν Il. 1.170, οἰ. δόμεναι πάλιν (hand over to be borne to my home) Il. 7.79= Il. 22.342. Cf. Il. 1.19, Il. 2.154, Il. 3.72, Il. 4.103, Il. 7.335, etc. : Od. 2.176, Od. 4.520, Od. 5.108, Od. 8.102, Od. 10.35, etc.
A house servant, a servant in general: ὅ οἱ βιότοιο μάλιστα κήδετο οἰκήων Od. 14.4. Cf. Il. 5.413, Il. 6.366 : Od. 4.245, Od. 14.63, Od. 16.303, Od. 17.533.
To live, dwell, abide, have one's home : οἴκεον ἐν πλευρῶνι Il. 14.116. Cf. Od. 6.204, Od. 9.200, 400.
To live in, dwell in, inhabit : ὑπωρείας ᾤκεον Ἴδης Il. 20.218.
In pass., of a city, to be a habitation, continue in being, stand : οἰκέοιτο πόλις Πριάμοιο Il. 4.18.
In aor. pass. in mid. sense, of a people, to settle, organize or dispose themselves : τριχθὰ ᾤκηθεν καταφυλαδόν Il. 2.668.
A house or abode : οἳ περὶ Δωδώνην οἰκίʼ ἔθεντο Il. 2.750. Cf. Od. 2.154, Od. 21.215.
Of the house or realm of Hades Il. 20.64.
Of the home of the Dawn Od. 12.4.
Of a wasps' nest Il. 12.168, Il. 16.261.
From one's house or home : δέπας, ὃ οἰ. ἦγεν Il. 11.632.
From one's store, from one's own resources (cf. οἶκος 3) : καὶ οἴκοθεν ἄλλʼ ἐπιθεῖναι Il. 7.364, 391. Cf. Il. 23.558, 592.
At one's house or home, at home : τοιαῦτα καὶ αὐτῷ οἰ. κεῖται Od. 21.398. Cf. Il. 8.513 : Od. 3.303, Od. 19.237.
At one's house or home, at home : οἰ. ἔσαν Od. 1.12. Cf. Il. 1.113, Il. 24.240 : Od. 8.324, Od. 13.42, Od. 15.15, 178.

To one's house or home, home, homewards : ἔβαν οἶκόνδε ἕκαστος Il. 1.606. Cf. Il. 2.158, 290, Il. 4.180, Il. 6.189, Il. 23.856, etc. : Od. 1.17, 317, Od. 5.204, Od. 6.159, Od. 11.410 (here, app., simply to the palace), Od. 13.125, Od. 23.221, etc.
To the part of a house allotted to one, to one's own quarters (cf. οἶκος 2) : ἡ θαμβήσασα πάλιν οἶκόνδε βεβήκει Od. 1.360=Od. 21.354. Cf. Od. 3.396, Od. 23.292.

A house or abode (sometimes, as in Eng. house, thought of along with the inhabitants or contents) : ἡμετέρῳ ἐνὶ οἴκῳ Il. 1.30. Cf. Il. 3.233, Il. 6.56, 490, 500, Il. 7.127, Il. 8.284, Il. 9.147, 289, Il. 15.498, Il. 17.738, Il. 24.471, 572 : μέλλε ποτὲ οἶκος ὅδʼ ἀφνειὸς ἔμμεναι Od. 1.232. Cf. Od. 1.248, 251, 258, Od. 2.45, Od. 4.4, Od. 6.9, Od. 7.314, Od. 9.35, Od. 11.389, etc.
App. including the curtilage of the house : χῆνʼ ἀτιταλλομένην ἐνὶ οἴκῳ Od. 15.174. Cf. Od. 19.536.
In pl. in the same sense as the sing. : ἐκ νέκυς οἴκων φόρεον Od. 24.417.
Applied to a particular part of a house (cf. Od. 19.598 and οἶκόνδε 2).

div.head: a
div.p: To Penelope's quarters : εἰς οἷκον ἰοῦσα Od. 1.356 =Od. 21.350. Cf. Od. 4.717.

div.head: b
div.p: App. to a detached building a ppropriated to mill-workers : φήμην ἐξ οἴκοιο γυνὴ προέηκεν ἀλετρίς Od. 20.105.
One's store (cf. οἴκοθεν 2) : οὐ σύ γʼ ἂν ἐξ οἴκου οὐδʼ ἅλα δοίης Od. 17.455.
3 sing. aor. ᾤκτειρε Il. 11.814, Il. 16.5, Il. 23.534.
To pity, take pity on, feel pity for, feel sorry for : τὸν ἰδὼν ᾤκτειρεν Il. 11.814, Il. 16.5 =Il. 23.534. Cf. Il. 23.548, Il. 24.516.
The most pitiable, miserable or wretched : θανάτῳ Od. 11.412, Od. 24.34. Cf. Od. 23.79.
Absol. : τοῦτʼ οἴκτιστον πέλεται δειλοῖσι βροτοῖσιν Il. 22.76. Cf. Od. 12.258, 342.
In neut. pl. οἴκτιστα as adv., in the most miserable or wretched wise : ὄπως οἴκτιστα θάνοιεν Od. 22.472.
Pity, compassion, sympathy with one in trouble or distress Od. 2.81, Od. 24.438.
Pitiable : κοιμήσατο χάλκεον ὕπνον οἰκτρός Il. 11.242.
Comp. οἰκτρότερος : οἰκτρότερʼ ἄλλʼ ἀγορεῦσαι (more moving) Od. 11.381.
In neut. pl. οἰκτρά as adv., pitiably, so as to move compassion, expressing great grief : ὀλοφυρομένη Od. 4.719. Cf. Od. 10.409, Od. 19.543, Od. 24.59.
Care or thought for one's house or worldly estate Od. 14.223.
Sim. in pl. : αἰετοῦ οἴματʼ ἔχων Il. 21.252.
To spring, swoop, pounce : οἴμησεν ὥς τʼ αἰετός Il. 22.308 : = Od. 24.538. Cf. Il. 22.140, 311.
A lay or poem : θεός μοι ἐν φρεσὶν οἴμας παντοίας ἐνέφυσεν Od. 22.347. Cf. Od. 8.74, 481.
A crying out in distress or pain, weeping, wailing Il. 4.450=Il. 8.64, Il. 22.409, 447, Il. 24.696 : Od. 20.353.

To cry out in or express grief, distress, pain or disappointment : γνὺξ ἔριπʼ οἰμώξας (with a cry of pain) Il. 5.68. Cf. Il. 3.364, Il. 7.125, Il. 12.162, Il. 16.290, Il. 22.33, etc. : Od. 9.395, 506=Od. 11.59, Od. 12.370, Od. 13.198, Od. 18.398.
To get (wine) for oneself, to supply oneself with wine Il. 7.472, Il. 8.506, 546.
Heavy with wine, drunken, in one's drunkenness : ἐρεύγετο οἰνοβαρείων Od. 9.374. Cf. Od. 10.555, Od. 21.304.
With soil fit for producing wine, vine-bearing : ἀλωῆς Od. 1.193, Od. 11.193.
In neut. as sb., vineyard land Il. 9.579.
Full of wine, bearing wine in abundance : νῆσος Od. 15.406.
To drink one's wine : ἃς ὑπίσχεο οἰνοποτάζων (sitting over your wine) Il. 20.84. Cf. Od. 6.309, Od. 20.262.
A drinker of wine : ἄνδρας μέτα οἰνοποτῆρας ἤϊεν (to join the company at their wine) Od. 8.456.
-ου, ὁ (ϝοῖνος. Cf. L. vinum, Eng. wine).
Nom. pl. masc. pres. pple. οἰνοχοεῦντες Od. 3.472.

3 sing. impf. ἐοινοχόει, ἐῳνοχόει (ἐϝοινοχόει) Il. 4.3 : Od. 20.255. οἰνοχόει Il. 1.598 :
Od. 15.141.
To pour out wine for drinking, act as cup-bearer : ἐοινοχόει μελανθεύς Od. 20.255. Cf. Od. 4.233, Od. 15.141, 323.
To pour out (wine) for drinking : οἶνον οἰνοχοεῦντες Od. 3.472.
One who pours out wine for drinking, a cup-bearer : οἰνοχόος ἐπαρξάσθω δεπάεσσιν Od. 18.418, Od. 21.263. Cf. Il. 2.128 : Od. 9.10, Od. 18.396.
Epithet of πόντος, wine-dark, purple Il. 2.613, Il. 5.771, Il. 7.88, Il. 23.143, 316 : Od. 1.183, Od. 2.421, Od. 3.286, Od. 4.474, Od. 5.132, etc.
Epithet of oxen, app., of the characteristic dark hue of most of the species, i.e. dark brown Il. 13.703 : Od. 13.32.
To make drunk; in pass., to become drunk : μή πως οἰνωθέντες ἀλλήλους τρώσητε (in an access of drunkenness) Od. 16.292=Od. 19.11.
Strengthening οἶος by reduplication (cf. αἰνόθεν αἰνῶς, μέγας μεγαλωστί).
App., man to man : οἰόθεν οἶος μαχέσασθαι Il. 7.39. Cf. Il. 7.226.
3 sing. aor. ὀΐσατο [ι] Od. 1.323, Od. 9.213, Od. 19.390.
Pple. ὀϊσάμενος Od. 9.339, Od. 10.232, 258, Od. 15.443, Aor. in pass. form ὠΐσθην Od. 16.475.

To think deem, fancy, imagine, suspect, expect : αἰεὶ ὀΐεαι (are always suspecting something) Il. 1.561. Cf. Il. 9.453 : τῷ ἑπόμην ὀϊόμενός περ (though boding that no good would come of it) Od. 14.298. Cf. Od. 9.339, Od. 15.443, Od. 17.586, Od. 24.401 (beyond our hopes).
To bethink oneself of something to be avoided : ὀΐσατο μὴ . . . Od. 19.390.–ὀΐω parenthetically, I ween Il. 8.536, Il. 13.153 : Od. 2.255, Od. 16.309, Od. 23.261.
Impers., to appear, seem : ὧδέ μοι ὀΐεται, ὡς ἔσεταί περ Od. 19.312.

div.head: a
div.p: To think of, have occur to one : ἅ πέρ κʼ οἴοιτο καὶ ἄλλος Od. 17.580.

div.head: b
div.p: To bode, dwell on the thought of : κῆρας Il. 13.283.

div.head: c
div.p: To be full of the thought of, be impelled to : γόον Od. 10.248=Od. 20.349.

div.head: d
div.p: With dependent clause : τόδε καὐτὸς ὀΐεαι, ὥς κεν ἐτύχθη (can imagine for yourself how . . . ) Od. 3.255.

div.head: e
div.p: To suspect the existence of : δόλον Od. 10.380.

div.head: f
div.p: To expect, look for the coming of : κεῖνον Od. 2.351. Cf. Od. 20.224.–

div.head: g
div.p: To intend, purpose, have in view : τά γʼ οὐκ ὀΐω (I will see that that does not happen) Od. 13.427=Od. 15.31.

div.head: a
div.p: With pres., pf. or aor. infin., to think, suppose, surmise, deem, suspect : κατανεῦσαί σε Il. 1.558, τὸν ἐνὶ κλισίῃσι κεῖσθαι Il. 11.834, πηλῆα τεθνάμεν Il. 19.334. Cf. Il. 5.894, Il. 10.551, Il. 13.262, 273, Il. 14.454, Il. 17.641, 687, Il. 23.467 : Od. 1.173, Od. 3.27, Od. 4.453, 754, Od. 10.193, Od. 14.214, Od. 19.568, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: With fut. infin., to think, expect, deem, ween : ἄμμε παλιμπλαγχθέντας ἂψ ἀπονοστήσειν Il. 1.59. Cf. Il. 1.78, Il. 4.12, Il. 5.252, Il. 6.341, Il. 9.315, Il. 11.609, Il. 12.66, etc. : Od. 1.201, Od. 2.198, Od. 3.226, Od. 6.173, Od. 8.203, Od. 9.213, Od. 11.101, etc.

To intend, propose, have a mind, be minded : οὐδέ (σοι) ὀΐω ἄφενος ἀφύξειν (I have no notion of doing anything of the sort) Il. 1.170. Cf. Il. 1.296 : νῦν σευ ὀΐω πειρήσεσθαι (am going to . . .) Od. 19.215.
Lonely, solitary, remote Il. 13.473, Il. 17.54, Il. 19.377, Il. 24.614 : Od. 11.574.

div.head: a
div.p: Of such nature, kind or sort as, such as : οἷος πάρος εὔχεαι εἶναι Il. 4.264. Cf. Il. 5.126, 304, Il. 7.208, Il. 9.105, 447, etc. : ἀνὴρ οἷος Ὀδυσσεὺς ἔσκεν Od. 2.59. Cf. Od. 2.118, Od. 3.480, Od. 5.422, Od. 15.379, Od. 19.255, etc.
Correlative with τοῖος. See τοῖος 1.a. See also τοιόσδε 1.a, τοιοῦτος.

div.head: b
div.p: With infin., such as to . . . : οἷός τε πατρὸς ἀέθλια ἀνελέσθαι Od. 21.117. Cf. Od. 19.160, Od. 21.173.
Introducing similes Il. 4.75, Il. 5.554, Il. 7.63, Il. 11.62, etc. : Od. 6.102.
With subj. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table at end III.B.a 1, (D) (20) (31).

In causal sense (= ὅτι τοῖος) : τὸν χόλος λάβεν οἷον ἄκουσε (because of what he had heard) Il. 6.166, οἷʼ ἀγορεύεις (since you say such things) Il. 18.95. Cf. Il. 2.320, Il. 5.758, Il. 14.95, Il. 24.630, etc. : οἷʼ ἀγορεύεις (to judge by what you say) Od. 4.611, οἷος κεῖνος ἔην βουλευέμεν (for such a man he was to . . .) Od. 14.491. Cf. Od. 5.183, 303, Od. 17.479, Od. 18.143, 338, Od. 22.217, etc.
Giving a reason in anticipation : οἷος κείνου θυμὸς ὑπέρβιος, οὔ σε μεθήσει Od. 15.212. Cf. Il. 8.450, Il. 18.262 : Od. 17.514.

Exclamatory in advbl. and other constructions : οἷον δὴ θαυμάζομεν Ἕκτορα (to think how we . . . !) Il. 5.601, οἷόν τινά φασι βίην Ἡρακληείην εἶναι (what a man they say he was !) 638, οἷον ἔειπες (what a thing is this that you have said !) Il. 7.455. Cf. Il. 13.633 (even as now . . .), Il. 15.287, Il. 17.471, 587 (if now you . . .), Il. 21.57, etc. : Od. 1.32 (to think how . . .!), 410, Od. 4.242, Od. 11.429, 519, Od. 17.248, etc.

In object clauses, of what nature, kind or sort, what kind of a . . ., what : γνοίης χʼ οἵου φωτὸς ἔχεις παράκοιτιν Il. 3.53. Cf. Il. 2.192, 194 (what he said), Il. 5.222, Il. 11.653, Il. 15.94, 97, etc. : οὐκ ἀΐεις οἱον κλέος ἔλλαβεν; Od. 1.298. Cf. Od. 4.689, Od. 8.244, Od. 9.348, Od. 15.20, Od. 19.219, etc.
In neut. οἷον as adv. (see also (4)).

div.head: a
div.p: Even as, as : οἷον ὅτε πρωτόν περ ἐμισγέσθην φιλότητι Il. 14.295. Cf. Od. 19.233.

div.head: b
div.p: In what manner, how : οὐχ ὁράᾳς οἷον . . .; Il. 15.555.
With an adj., how : οἷον ἐεθσήεις κεῖται Il. 24.419. Cf. Od. 19.494.

div.head: c
div.p: Seeing that : οἷον ἔθʼ εὕδεις Il. 24.683. Cf. Od. 2.239, Od. 14.392.
In neut. pl. οἷα as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Even as, as : οἷα θεάων λεπτὰ ἔργα πέλονται Od. 10.222. Cf. Od. 8.365.

div.head: b
div.p: With τε: οἷά τε φύλλα Od. 7.106. Cf. Od. 3.73=Od. 9.254.

With no one near, unaccompanied, alone, by oneself : καθήμενος οἶος Il. 8.207. Cf. Il. 2.822, Il. 3.143, Il. 8.444, Il. 9.438, Il. 12.349, etc. : Od. 1.331, Od. 2.11, 70, Od. 4.367, Od. 9.188, Od. 10.281, etc.

Without countenance, support or aid, from one's own resources, alone, by oneself : οἶον μάχεσθαι Il. 4.156. Cf. Il. 4.304, Il. 5.304, Il. 7.42, Il. 13.481 (in my need), Il. 16.100, 243, etc. : ὃν αὐτὸς κτήσατο οἶος Od. 14.450. Cf. Od. 1.79, Od. 9.410.

With no one or nothing in the same predicament or case
or doing the same thing, with no one having the same ability, alone, only, nothing but : ὄφραμὴ οἶος ἀγέραστος ἔω Il. 1.118, κλέος οἶον ἀκούομεν Il. 2.486, ὅς μοι οἶος ἔην (i.e. the others count for nothing) Il. 24.499. Cf. Il. 1.198, 398, Il. 2.247, Il. 5.641, Il. 6.403, Il. 9.190, 638, Il. 11.74, etc. : Od. 1.13, 354, Od. 2.84, Od. 3.424, Od. 6.139, Od. 8.230, Od. 10.95, Od. 14.244, 482, Od. 16.133, Od. 22.130, etc.
In neut. οἶον as adv., only, solely, exclusively : οὐδʼ ἔτι κεῖνον στεναχίζω οἶον, ἐπεὶ... (I have not only to mourn my loss, for . . .) Od. 1.244. Cf. Il. 9.355.
Clad only in a χιτών Od. 14.489.
To leave alone, leave by himself or to itself : Τρώων οἰώθη καὶ Ἀχαιῶν φύλοπις (i.e. by the departure of the gods) Il. 6.1. Cf. Il. 11.401.
To shoot an arrow or arrows Il. 4.196 = 206, Il. 8.269 : Od. 8.216, Od. 12.84, Od. 22.119.
With genit. of person aimed at : ὀΐστευσον μενελάου Il. 4.100.
Of osier, wattled : ῥίπεσσιν οἰσυΐνῃσιν Od. 5.256.
One's fate, fate that comes upon one: κακὸν οἶτον ἀναπλήσαντες Il. 8.34= 354 = 465. Cf. Il. 3.417, Il. 9.563, Il. 24.388 : Od. 1.350, Od. 3.134, Od. 8.489, 578, Od. 13.384.
To go or come, take or make one's way Il. 5.790, Il. 15.640 : Od. 3.322.

To go or come, take or make one's way, proceed : ᾠχόμεθʼ ἐς Θήβην Il. 1.366. Cf. Il. 1.380, Il. 5.495, Il. 11.357, Il. 22.223 (will go and . . . ), Il. 23.564, etc. : πότʼ ᾤχετο; Od. 4.642. Cf. Od. 1.260, Od. 2.383, Od. 9.47, Od. 13.415, Od. 24.333 (when I journeyed thither), etc.
Of inanimate objects : ἀνὰ στρατὸν ᾤχετο κῆλα θεοῖο Il. 1.53. Cf. Il. 13.505= Il. 16.615.
So of a wind : ὥς μʼ ὄφελʼ οἴχεσθαι προφέρουσα κακὴ ἀνέμοιο θύελλα Il. 6.346. Cf. Od. 20.64.
Cf. something immaterial : Ὄσσα κατὰ πτόλιν οἴχετο πάντῃ Od. 24.413.

With the notion of leaving a place prominent, to go away or off, depart, take one's departure, leave : ὅτʼ ἂν (εἴ κεν) Ἀχαιοὶ οἴχωνται ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν Il. 7.460= Il. 15.499. Cf. Il. 2.71, Il. 13.627, Il. 14.311, 361, Il. 19.356 : εἴ κεν Ἄρης οἴχοιτο Od. 8.353. Cf. Od. 8.356, Od. 13.286, Od. 16.24= Od. 17.42, Od. 16.142, Od. 17.104, 294, Od. 19.183, 260 = 597=Od. 23.19.
Of immaterial things : θυμὸς ᾤχετʼ ἀπὸ μελέων Il. 13.672=Il. 16.607. Cf. Il. 22.213, Il. 23.101.

To have gone, be gone : ἐπεὶ ᾤχοντο (had gone) Il. 4.382, γαιήοχος οἴχεται εἰς ἅλα δῖαν Il. 15.223. Cf. Il. 5.511, Il. 11.288, Il. 13.782, Il. 17.588, Il. 19.346, Il. 23.577 : Od. 1.242, 410, Od. 4.166, 634, 639, 665, 707, 821, Od. 8.294, Od. 13.216, Od. 14.25, Od. 19.193 (since he had left for . . . ), Od. 24.225.
Of a heavenly body : φάος οἴχετ [αι] ὑπὸ ζόφον Od. 3.335.
Of immaterial things : πῇ τοι μένος οἴχεται ; Il. 5.472. Cf. Il. 13.220, Il. 24.201.
One skilled in drawing omens from the behaviour of birds, an augur Il. 2.858, Il. 17.218.
A bird : πέλαγος, ὅθεν τέ περ οὐδʼ οἰωνοὶ αὐτόετες οἰχνεῦσιν Od. 3.321. Cf. Od. 11.605, Od. 16.216.

div.head: a
div.p: A bird of prey : ἑλώρια κύνεσσιν οἰωνοῖσί τε πᾶσιν Il. 1.5. Cf. Il. 2.393, Il. 8.379, Il. 11.395, 453, Il. 13.831, Il. 17.241, Il. 22.335, 354, Il. 24.411 : Od. 3.259, 271, Od. 14.133, Od. 24.292.

div.head: b
div.p: A bird of omen : οἰωνοῖσι πείθεσθαι Il. 12.237. Cf. Il. 24.292, 293 = 311, Il. 24.310 : Od. 15.532, Od. 17.160.
Applied to an omen drawn from such a bird : οὐκ οἰωνοῖσιν ἐρύσατο κῆρα Il. 2.859. Cf. Il. 12.243, Il. 13.823 : Od. 1.202.
To shrink from doing something, hesitate to do it.
With infin. : ἀρχέμεναι πολέμοιο ὄκνεον Il. 20.155. Cf. Il. 5.255.
Shrinking from action, hesitation : ὄκνῳ εἴκων Il. 10.122, Il. 13.224. Cf. Il. 5.817.
App. to deal in sharps ; hence, to squabble, quarrel : πανθυμαδὸν ὀκριόωντο Od. 18.33.
Jagged, rough : χερμαδίῳ Il. 4.518. Cf. Il. 8.327, Il. 12.380, Il. 16.735 : Od. 9.499.
[no doubt for κρυόεις, the form suggested by ὀκριόεις.]
Causing shuddering. Fig. : δᾶερ ἐμεῖο κυνὸς κακομηχάνου ὀκρυοέσσης (κακομηχάνοο κρυοέσσης) Il. 6.344, πολέμου ἐπιδημίου ὀκρυόεντος (ἐπιδημίοο κρυόεντος) Il. 9.64.
[ὀκτ-, ὀκτώ + -α- (on analogy of numerals in -α) + κνήμη.]
The eighteenth : ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῃ (sc. ἡμέρῃ), on the eighteenth day Od. 5.279 = Od. 7.268, Od. 24.65.
Happy in the protection and aid of a δαίμων, happy, fortunate.
Happy, fortunate, prosperous : ἀμφὶ λαοὶ ὄλβιοι ἔσσονται Od. 11.137. Cf. Od. 11.450, Od. 17.354, Od. 18.218, Od. 23.284, Od. 24.36, 192.
Bringing good luck : δῶρα, τά μοι θεοὶ ὄλβια ποιήσειαν Od. 13.42.
In neut. pl. ὄλβια, happiness, good fortune, prosperity : θεοὶ ὄλβια δοῖεν Od. 7.148, Od. 8.413, Od. 24.402.
With special reference to material prosperity, wealthy, rich, of great power or influence : σὲ τὸ πρὶν μὲν ἀκούομεν ὄλβιον εἶναι Il. 24.543. Cf. Od. 17.420=Od. 19.76, Od. 18.138.
Happiness, good fortune, prosperity : οὔ μοι τοιοῦτον ἐπέκλωσαν θεοὶ ὄλβον Od. 3.208. Cf. Od. 4.208, Od. 6.188, Od. 4.19, 123=Od. 20.200, Od. 18.273.
With special reference to material prosperity, wealth, riches, much substance, great power or influence : ὄλβῳ τε πλούτῳ τε μετέπρεπε Μυρμιδόνεσσιν Il. 16.596. Cf. Il. 24.536 : Od. 14.206.
Fatal, baneful, deadly : ὀλέθριον ἦμαρ. See ἦμαρ 4.i.

Destruction, bane, death, evil fate : οὐδέ τί οἱ τό γʼ ἐπήρκεσεν ὄλεθρον Il. 2.873. Cf. Il. 6.16, Il. 11.120, Il. 13.773, Il. 18.129, etc. : Od. 1.11. Cf. Od. 2.152, Od. 8.579, Od. 10.250, Od. 14.300, Od. 16.411 (the fate intended for him), etc.
A kind or mode of death Il. 10.174, Il. 22.325, Il. 24.735 : Od. 3.93, Od. 10.115, Od. 15.268, etc.
In pass., to perish, die : ὀλέκοντο λαοί Il. 1.10. Cf. Il. 16.17.
A destroyer or slayer : φίλης κεφαλῆς ὀλετῆρα Il. 18.114.
[a ppl. form fr. ὀλιγη-, ὀλίγος + πέλω.
Thus, hardly able to stir, with little life in one's limbs, weak, feeble : ἄπνευστος καὶ ἄναυδος κεῖτʼ ὀλιγηπελέων Od. 5.457. Cf. Il. 15.24, 245 : Od. 19.356.
Weakness, feebleness : μή με στίβη ἐξ ὀλιγηπελίης δαμάσῃ Od. 5.468.
ὀλιγοδρανέων [a ppl. form fr. ὀλίγος + δράω. Able to do little.]
Showing weakness or feebleness, with feeble utterance : τὸν ὀλιγοδρανέων προσέφη Il. 15.246=Il. 22.337. Cf. Il. 16.843.
Not much, little : ὀλίγος ἔτι θυμὸς ἐνῆεν Il. 1.593.
Of small extent : ὀλίγη ἦν ἀμφὶς ἄρουρα Il. 3.115. Cf. Il. 10.161, Il. 12.423, Il. 16.68, Il. 17.394.
Of no great size, small : σάκος Il. 14.376. Cf. Il. 16.825 : Od. 12.252, Od. 20.259.
Of a wave, not rising high, inconsiderable Od. 10.94.
Of utterance, carrying no great volume of sound, small : ὀπί Od. 14.492.
Of persons, of small stature, short, of small build : ὀλίγος τε καὶ οὐτιδανὸς καὶ ἄκικυς Od. 9.515. Cf. Il. 2.529.
Sim. of Eris: ἥ τʼ ὀλίγη πρῶτα κορύσσεται (rears her head but a little way) Il. 4.442.
In reference to time, of no great duration, short : ἐπιδραμέτην ὀλίγον χρόνον Il. 23.418. Cf. Il. 19.157.
Of small value : δόσις ὀλίγη τε φιλη τε Od. 6.208, Od. 14.58 (see δόσις).
Absol. : ὀλίγον τε φίλον τʼ ἔχων Il. 1.167.
In neut. sing. ὀλίγον as adv., not much, little : ὀ. τί μʼ ἧσσον ἐτίμα Od. 15.365. Cf. Il. 5.800, Il. 12.452.
A little, slightly : καὶ εἴ κʼ ὀ. περ ἐπαύρῃ [βέλος] Il. 11.391. Cf. Il. 17.538, Il. 19.217, Il. 23.424, 789 : στιβαρώτερον οὐκ ὀλίγον περ Od. 8.187. Cf. Od. 8.547, Od. 10.24, Od. 19.244.
App., leaving a small interval : ἱππῆες ὀ. μετεκίαθον (came up close) Il. 11.52.
Slowly, taking one's time, without haste : ὀ. γόνυ γουνὸς ἀμείβων Il. 11.547.
In genit. ὀλίγου, all but, nearly, almost : ὀλίγου σε κύνες διεδηλήσαντο Od. 14.37.
To miss one's footing, slip : ὄλισθε θέων Il. 23.774.
To slip out of position : ἔκ οἱ ἧπαρ ὄλισθεν (i.e., app., the edge projected through the wound) Il. 20.470.

div.head: A
div.p: 2 sing. subj. ὀλέσῃς Il. 1.559. ὀλέσσῃς Il. 5.250, Il. 10.452, Il. 11.433 : Od. 19.81.
3 sing. ὀλέσῃ Il. 2.4. ὀλέσσῃ Il. 1.205, Il. 18.92 : Od. 2.330.

div.head: B
div.p: Mid. 3 sing. fut. ὀλεῖται Il. 2.325, Il. 7.91 : Od. 24.196.

div.head: a
div.p:
To destroy, cause the destruction of, kill, slay, cause the death of, make away with : πολέας Ἀχαιῶν Il. 1.559, Il. 2.4, εὐχωλὴ ἀνδρῶν ὀλλύντων Il. 4.451= Il. 8.65. Cf. Il. 8.449, 472, 498, Il. 10.201, Il. 11.83, Il. 15.66, Il. 17.647, Il. 21.216, Il. 22.360, Il. 24.609 : Od. 2.330, Od. 9.40, Od. 11.318, Od. 23.319,
Od. 24.528.
To bring down destruction or ruin on the head of, be the death of: μαῖα, τίη μʼ ἐθέλεις ὀλέσαι; Od. 19.482.
Sim.: ἑή τέ μιν ὤλεσεν ἀλκή Il. 16.753.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to inanimate objects, to destroy, bring to nothing: νῆας Il. 8.498. Cf. Od. 12.349, Od. 13.399, 431, Od. 23.319.

div.head: c
div.p: To destroy, lay waste (a city) Il. 9.188, Il. 19.60.

div.head: d
div.p: To consume, bring to nothing (goods or substance): βίοτον ἀπὸ πάμπαν ὀλέσσει Od. 2.49.

div.head: e
div.p: In reference to faculties or qualities, to cause to perish, destroy, deprive one of: ἔκ τοι θεοὶ φρένας ὤλεσαν Il. 7.360=Il. 12.234. Cf. Od. 4.668, Od. 18.181, 252=Od. 19.125, Od. 21.284.

div.head: f
div.p: To counteract, be a remedy against: ὄλεσσε κήτεος ὀδμήν Od. 4.446.

To lose, incur the loss of, be deprived of: θυμόν Il. 1.205. Cf. Il. 5.250, Il. 8.358, Il. 13.763, Il. 24.46, 242, etc.: ἑταίρους Od. 2.174. Cf. Od. 12.350, Od. 19.81, 265, 274, Od. 21.88, Od. 23.68, Od. 24.93, etc.
To incur the loss of under one's leadership, lose, throw away: πολὺν λαόν Il. 2.115=Il. 9.22. Cf. Il. 22.104, 107: Od. 7.60, Od. 24.428.

div.head: II
div.p: In pf. and plupf. act. and in mid. and pass.

div.head: a
div.p: To be destroyed, perish, die: κεῖνοι σφετέρῃσιν ἀτασθαλίῃσιν ὄλοντο Il. 4.409, ὀλλυμένων Δαναῶν Il. 8.202, ἀνὴρ ὤριστος ὄλωλεν Il. 16.521. Cf. Il. 3.428, Il. 4.451, Il. 8.34, Il. 11.83, Il. 13.349, etc.: Od. 1.7, 380, Od. 3.89, Od. 10.123, Od. 14.68, Od. 15.90, Od. 17.319, Od. 19.277, etc.
With cognate acc.: σύ κεν κακὸν οἶτον ὄληαι Il. 3.417. Cf. Il. 21.133.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to inanimate objects, to be destroyed, perish, come to nothing, disappear: μή μοι νήματʼ ὄληται Od. 2.98=Od. 19.143=Od. 24.133. Cf. Od. 10.132, Od. 15.91.

div.head: c
div.p: Of a city, to be destroyed or laid waste: ὅτʼ ἄν ποτʼ ὀλώλῃ Ἴλιος Il. 4.164=Il. 6.448. Cf. Il. 13.772.

div.head: d
div.p: Of goods, substance or the like, to be consumed, destroyed, brought to nothing: ἀνδρὸς ἑνὸς βίοτον νήποινον ὀλέσθαι Od. 1.377=Od. 2.142, ὄλωλε πίονα ἔργα Od. 4.318.

div.head: e
div.p: Of abstractions, to perish, be lost, vanish: ὅου κλέος οὔ ποτʼ ὀλεῖται Il. 2.325, ὤλετό μοι νόστος Il. 9.413, ὕπνος ὄλωλεν (ὀλώλει) Il. 10.186, 187. Cf. Il. 7.91, Il. 9.415: Od. 1.168, Od. 24.196.
To be lost, go astray: ἵππους, αἵ οἱ ὄλοντο Od. 21.22.
App., a cylindrical piece of wood for use as a roller: ὅλμον ὣς ἔσσευεν (sc. the mutilated body) Il. 11.147.
An ecstatic religious shout of women Il. 6.301.
To shout in exultation or triumph (always of women) Od. 22.408, 411.
Sim. of an ecstatic shout of women at a religious ceremony Od. 3.450, Od. 4.767.
[app. for ϝολοϝ-οί-τροχος, fr. ϝελυ-, ϝελϝ-, (ϝ)είλω + τρέχω. The -οι- not explained.]

Also ὀλοιός Il. 1.342, Il. 22.5. Destructive, baneful, deadly, painful, mischievous, bringing mischief Il. 3.133, Il. 9.305, Il. 11.71, Il. 13.629, 665, Il. 14.139, Il. 16.567, 849, Il. 22.65, Il. 23.10, Il. 24.487, etc.: Od. 2.100, Od. 3.135, Od. 9.82, Od. 11.276, Od. 12.68, 113, Od. 22.200, etc.
Superl. ὀλοώτατος Il. 22.15: Od. 4.442 (here of two terminations).
Absol. in neut. pl. ὀλοά, mischief: τῷ ὀλοὰ φρονέων Il. 16.701.
Having mischief in his mind, malign Od. 1.52, Od. 10.137, Od. 11.322.
Applied to animals Il. 2.723, Il. 15.630, Il. 16.21.
Lamentable, piteous, tearful: ἔπος Il. 5.683 (or here perh. rather, beseeching (cf. ὀλοφύρομαι. 6)), Il. 23.102: Od. 19.362.

To make lament, sorrow, weep, mourn, grieve: ὀλοφυρόμενος (ὀλοφυρομένη) ἔπεα προσηύδα Il. 5.871=Il. 11.815, Il. 18.72. Cf. Il. 15.114 = 398, Il. 21.106: Od. 2.362, Od. 4.719, Od. 10.418, Od. 11.418, Od. 13.199, Od. 22.447, etc.
To lament, weep for, mourn: παῖδα Od. 19.522. Cf. Il. 24.328.
With genit. of person pitied: Δαναῶν Il. 8.33= 464. Cf. Il. 8.202, Il. 16.17, Il. 22.169.
To feel for, pity, take pity upon, compassionate, be touched by the plight of: τὸν πατὴρ ὀλοφύρατο δάκρυ χέοντα Il. 8.245=Il. 17.648. Cf. Il. 11.656, Il. 16.450: Od. 4.364, Od. 10.157.
With infin., app., to bewail the necessity of doing something: πῶς ἄντα μνηστήρων ὀλοφύρεαι ἄλκιμος εἶναι; (why not pluck up heart to face them?) Od. 22.232.
App., to beseech. Parenthetically: καί μοι δὸς τὴν χεῖρʼ, ὀλοφύρομαι Il. 23.75.
Crafty, cunning, malign: δήνεα κίρκης Od. 10.289.
Absol. in neut. pl. ὀλοφώϊα, wiles, craft, cunning: ὀλοφώϊα τοῖο γέροντος Od. 4.410, ὀλοφώϊα εἰδώς (with craft or cunning in his heart) Od. 4.460 (see εἴδω III.12).
Some kind of grain (perh. the same as ζειαί) Il. 5.196, Il. 8.564.
To make a common din or murmur of voices, burst into uproar: μνηστῆρες ὁμάδησαν Od. 1.365=Od. 4.768=Od. 18.399, Od. 17.360, Od. 22.21.
A throng, concourse, company: ἐς Τρώων ὅμαδον κίεν Il. 7.307, ἐνὶ πρώτῳ ὁμάδῳ μάχεσθαι (in the forefront of the battle) Il. 17.380. Cf. Il. 15.689.
A roar or murmur of voices, uproar: ὅμαδος ἦν Il. 2.96. Cf. Il. 9.573, Il. 10.13, Il. 12.471=Il. 16.296, Il. 16.295, Il. 19.81, Il. 23.234: Od. 10.556.
Of the roaring of wind Il. 13.797.
To do something together or at the same moment, coincide in action: ἐξ οἴκου βῆσαν ὁμαρτήσαντες ἅμʼ ἄμφω Od. 21.188. Cf. Il. 12.400.
To act as a companion or attendant Il. 24.438.
To keep up with something, vie with it in speed: οὐδέ κεν ἴρηξ κίρκος ὁμαρτήσειεν Od. 13.87.
Doing something together or at the same moment, acting coincidently Il. 13.584.
Gathered together, assembled: ἐπεὶ ὁμηγερέες ἐγένοντο Il. 1.57, Il. 24.790. Cf. Il. 2.789, Il. 7.415, Il. 15.84, Il. 24.84, 99: Od. 2.9=Od. 8.24=Od. 24.421.
To call together, assemble: ὁμηγυρίσασθαι Ἀχαιοὺς εἰς ἀλορήν Od. 16.376.
An assembled company: θεῶν μεθʼ ὁμήγυριν ἄλλων Il. 20.142.
One of the same age as another, his fellow in years: ὁμηλικίη μοί ἐσσι Od. 22.209. Cf. Il. 20.465: Od. 3.49, Od. 6.23.
In reference to two persons, of like age or years: εἰ ὁμηλικίη γε γενοίμεθα Il. 13.485.
In collective sense, those of the same age as another, his fellows in years or contemporaries: πᾶσαν ὁμηλικίην ἐκέκαστο Il. 13.431. Cf. Il. 3.175, Il. 5.326: Od. 2.158, Od. 3.364.
Of the same age, of like years: ὁμήλικές εἰμεν Od. 15.197. Cf. Od. 24.107.
Absol., one of the same age as another, his fellow in years: νίψον σοῖο ἄνακτος ὁμήλικα Od. 19.358.
In pl., those of the same age as another, his fellows in years or contemporaries: μετὰ πάντας ὁμήλικας ἔπλευ ἄριστος Il. 9.54. Cf. Od. 16.419.
With dat.: ὡμήρησέ μοι παρʼ ἑταίρων ἄγγελος Od. 16.468.
In a body: ἕποντο Il. 15.277, Il. 17.730.
Keeping close together, maintaining close contact: ἐμάχοντο Il. 12.3.
To come together, gather together, assemble, meet Od. 4.684, Od. 21.156.
To be gathered together, form a band or company: περὶ κεῖνον Od. 24.19.
To associate, consort, keep company with.
With dat.: μνηστῆρσιν Od. 2.21, 288, 381, Od. 16.271, Od. 18.167. Cf. Il. 1.261.
With παρά: οὕνεκα πὰρ παύροισιν ὁμιλεῖς Od. 18.383.
To keep (with others), countenance or support them: μετὰ Τρώεσσιν ὁμιλεῖ Il. 5.834.
To company (with the foe), engage in fight, carry on the fight, take part in the battle, join battle: ἐνὶ πρώτοισιν ὁμιλεῖ Il. 18.194. Cf. Il. 11.502, Il. 16.641, 644, Il. 18.535, 539, Il. 19.158.
With dat.: Δαναοῖσιν Il. 11.523, Il. 13.779. Cf. Od. 1.265=Od. 4.345=Od. 17.136.
Senses (4) and (3) united: τυδεΐδην οὐκ ἂν γνοίης ποτέροισι μετείη, ἠὲ μετὰ Τρώεσσιν ὁμιλέοι ἦ μετʼ Ἀχαιοῖς Il. 5.86.

An assembly, concourse, company: πολλὸς χορὸν περιίσταθʼ ὁ. Il. 18.603. Cf. Il. 7.183, 186, Il. 22.462, Il. 23.651, 804, 813, Il. 24.712: Od. 1.225, Od. 8.109, Od. 15.328, Od. 16.29, Od. 17.67, 564, 590, Od. 23.303.
In dat. ὁμίλῳ, in a body: ἦλθον ὁμίλῳ προτὶ ἄστυ Il. 21.606. Cf. Il. 13.50, 87.
In reference to inanimate objects: οὔ τι μεμιγμένον ἐστὶν ὁμίλῳ [σημάτων] (the mass of . . .) Od. 8.196.

A throng gathered for or engaged in battle, the battle-throng: ἐρχόμενον προπάροιθεν ὁμίλου Il. 3.22. Cf. Il. 4.86, Il. 5.334, Il. 11.546 (in the direction of his friends), Il. 12.191, Il. 17.149 (to his friends), 471, Il. 19.402, Il. 20.178 (so far forth from the . . .). etc.: Od. 8.216, Od. 11.514.
Sim.: μνηστήρων ἐς ὅμιλον ἀκοντίσαι (ἀκόντισαν) Od. 22.263, 282.
So of a host in bivouac Il. 10.231, 338, 433, 499, 517, 545.
Of a body of men gathered to attack or attacking a beast: λέων ἀνδρῶν ἐν ὁμίλῳ Od. 4.791. Cf. Il. 15.588, Il. 20.173.
Of a cloud of dust: κονίης ὀμίχλην Il. 13.336.
The eye. Always in pl.: ὄμματα καὶ κεφαλὴν ἴκελος διί Il. 2.478. Cf. Il. 1.225, Il. 3.397, Il. 8.349, Il. 10.91, Il. 23.66, Il. 24.343:=Od. 5.47, Od. 1.208, Od. 5.492, Od. 16.179, Od. 24.3.
The face or countenance: οὐκ ἴδον ὄμματα φωτός Il. 11.614. Cf. Il. 3.217 (keeping his face turned to the earth).
Fut. in mid. form ὀμοῦμαι Il. 1.233, Il. 9.132, Il. 21.373: Od. 20.229.
Imp. ὄμοσον Od. 2.373. ὄμοσσον Il. 1.76, Il. 10.321, Il. 14.271, Il. 19.108.
Infin. ὀμόσαι Il. 19.187. ὀμόσσαι Od. 5.178, Od. 10.299, 343. (ἀπ-, ἐπ-)

To make an affirmation, give an undertaking, indicate a resolve, under the sanction of an oath, to swear: σκῆπτρον λάβε καί οἱ ὄμοσσεν Il. 10.328. Cf. Il. 3.279, Il. 14.278, 280, Il. 19.260, 265: Od. 2.378=Od. 10.346, Od. 12.304=Od. 15.438=Od. 18.59, Od. 14.392.
With cognate acc.: μέγαν ὅρκον Il. 1.233. Cf. Il. 9.132, Il. 19.108, Il. 20.313, etc.: Od. 4.253, Od. 5.178, Od. 10.299, Od. 20.229, etc.
To swear to the truth of (something): ταῦτʼ ἐγὼν ἐθέλω ὀμόσαι Il. 19.187.
To swear to (an undertaking): τόδʼ ὀμοῦμαι Il. 21.373.
With pres., aor. or pf. infin. indicating what is affirmed: μή ποτε τῆς εὐνῆς ἐπιβήμεναι Il. 9.132, 274, Il. 19.175: νῆα κατειρύσθαι καὶ ἐπαρτέας ἔμμεν ἑταίρους Od. 14.331, Od. 19.288.
With ἦ μέν and fut. infin. indicating what is undertaken or resolved: ἦ μέν μοι πρόφρων ἀρήξειν Il. 1.76. Cf. Il. 10.321, etc.
Without ἦ μέν: μή ποτʼ ἐς οὔλυμπον αὖτις ἐλεύσεσθαι Ἄτην Il. 19.127. Cf. Il. 20.313, Il. 21.373: Od. 5.178=Od. 10.343, Od. 10.299.
With μὴ μέν and aor. infin.: μὴ μὲν πρὶν Ὀδυσῆʼ ἀναφῆναι, πρίν γε . . . Od. 4.253.
Without μέν: μὴ μητρὶ τάδε μυθήσασθαι, πρίν γε . . . Od. 2.373.
With clause: μή τις ἐμὲ χειρὶ βαρείῃ πλήξῃ Od. 18.55. Cf. Od. 12.298.
To invoke in sanction of an oath, swear by: στυγὸς ὕδωρ Il. 14.271. Cf. Il. 15.40.
Born of the same mother: κασίγνητον ὁμογάστριον Il. 24.47. Cf. Il. 21.95.
With ἐξ: δοιοὺς θάμνους ἐξ ὁμόθεν πεφυῶτας (from the same root or stem) Od. 5.477.
Of πόλεμος: ὁμοιΐου π(τ)ολέμοιο (ὁμοιΐοο πτολέμοιο) Il. 9.440, Il. 13.358, 635, Il. 15.670, Il. 18.242, Il. 21.294: Od. 18.264, Od. 24.543.

Like, the like, resembling: οὔ ποθʼ ὁμοίης ἔμμορε τιμῆς (i.e. very different (from that of common men)) Il. 1.278, οὔ πω πάντες ὁμοῖοι ἀνέρες ἐν πολέμῳ Il. 12.270. Cf. Il. 4.410, Il. 5.441: χρώς τοι οὐκέθʼ ὁμοῖος (like what it was) Od. 16.182, παῦροι Ἀχαιῶν ἦσαν ὁμοῖοι (like him) Od. 19.240.–

Absol.: ὁππότε τὸν ὁμοῖον ἀνὴρ ἐθέλῃσιν ἀμέρσαι (one as good as himself) Il. 16.53: ὡς αἰεὶ τὸν ὁμοῖον
ἄγει θεὸς ὣς τὸν ὁμοῖον (as heaven brings one like, so it brings his like) (ὥς seems to be better read than ὡς) Od. 17.218.

With dat.: τρήρωσι πελειάσιν Il. 5.778, κόμαι χαρίτεσσιν ὁμοῖαι (like the Graces' . . .) Il. 17.51. Cf. Il. 2.553, Il. 9.305, Il. 10.216, 437, Il. 14.521, Il. 17.475, Il. 23.632: Od. 2.121, 276, Od. 3.468, Od. 6.16, 231=Od. 23.158, Od. 8.14, Od. 19.203, Od. 23.163.
With complementary infin.: τῷ οὔ πώ τις ὁμοῖος γένετʼ ἀνὴρ κοσμῆσαι ἵππους Il. 2.553. Cf. Il. 10.437, Il. 14.521, Il. 17.475.
The same, one and the same: εἴ μοι ὁμοίη μοῖρα τέτυκται Il. 18.120. Cf. Il. 18.329.
In pass., to be made like, to liken oneself to, vie with.
With dat.: ἶσον ἐμοὶ φάσθαι καὶ ὁμοιωθήμεναι ἄντην Il. 1.187. Cf. Od. 3.120.
To shout together in encouragement, urge comrades to action with shouts: ὁμόκλεον ἀλλήλοισιν Il. 15.658.

To shout together in rebuke, reproach or menace: πάντες ὁμοκλήσαντες ἔχον ἵππους (rasing a shout to daunt the foe) Il. 15.354: μνηστῆρες πάντες ὁμόκλεον Od. 21.360. Cf. Od. 19.155, Od. 21.367, Od. 22.211, Od. 24.173.
Of a single person, to shout an order.
With acc. and infin.: ἦ λαοὺς ἐς τεῖχος ὁμοκλήσειεν ἀλῆναι Il. 16.714.
To shout in encouragement or with a view to urging on to action: μέγα Τρώεσσιν ὁμόκλα Il. 18.156. Cf. Il. 20.365, Il. 23.337, 363.

In rebuke or reproach: δείνʼ ὁμοκλήσας προσέφη Ἀπόλλων Il. 5.439. Cf. Il. 2.199, Il. 6.54, Il. 16.706, Il. 24.248, 252.– In menace: τῇ ῥʼ ἔχʼ ὁμοκλήσας (raising a shout to daunt the foe) Il. 16.378. Cf. Il. 20.448: Od. 14.35.
A rebuke or reproach: ἄνακτος (πατρὸς) ὑποδείσαντες ὁμοκλήν Il. 12.413=Il. 23.417 = 446, Il. 24.265. Cf. Od. 17.189.
A menacing or threatening shout: ἔχε τρόμος ἀνδρὸς ὁμοκλῇ Il. 6.137, μάχῃ ἔνι μεῖναι ὁμοκλήν (to stand up to the shouting foe) Il. 16.147.
A shouter. In encouragement: τοῖο ἄνευθεν ἐόντος ὁμοκλητῆρος ἀκούσας (i.e. he heard his voice as he urged on his horses) Il. 23.452.
In menace: μή τις ὀπίσσω τετράφθω ὁμοκλητῆρος ἀκούσας (before the shouts of the foe) Il. 12.273.
Aor. pple. mid. ὀμορξάμενος, -η Il. 18.124: Od. 8.88, Od. 11.530. (ἀπ-)
To wipe off or away: ἀπʼ ἰχῶ χειρὸς ὀμόργνυ Il. 5.416.
In mid., to wipe away from one's face: δάκρυʼ ὀμορξάμενος Od. 8.88. Cf. Il. 18.124: Od. 11.527, 530.
The same, one and the same: οὐ πάντων ἦεν ὁμὸς θρόος Il. 4.437. Cf. Il. 13.354, Il. 15.209, Il. 23.91, Il. 24.57: Od. 10.41, Od. 17.563.
With dat.: ἥ κέν τοι ὁμὸν λέχος εἰσαναβαίνοι Il. 8.291.
Common, in which all take part: τῶν ὁμὸν ἵατατο νεῖκος Il. 13.333.
To the same spot: τῶν ὁμόσʼ ἦλθε μάχη (they joined battle) Il. 13.337. Cf. Il. 12.24.
Entitled to be held in the same estimation, equally to be honoured: εἴ μʼ ὁμότιμον ἐόντα καθέξει Il. 15.186.
In the same place, together Il. 23.84.
Into the same place, together: θῆρας ὁμοῦ εἰλεῦντα Od. 11.573.

At the same time, together, both at once: εἰ ὁμοῦ πόλεμός τε δαμᾷ καὶ λοιμὸς Ἀχαιούς Il. 1.61. Cf. Il. 4.122, Il. 11.127, 245, Il. 17.362, 745, Il. 20.499: Od. 5.294=Od. 9.69=Od. 12.315, Od. 9.75=Od. 10.143, Od. 12.67, 178, 424.
With dat., along with, with, among: νεφέεσσιν Il. 5.867. Cf. Il. 15.118: Od. 4.723, Od. 15.365.
To be of like mind with another Od. 6.183.
To feel with another, sympathize with him Od. 9.456.
Oneness or likeness of mind, concord: ὁμοφροσύνην ὀπάσειαν Od. 6.181.
So in pl.: ἥδʼ ὁδὸς καὶ μᾶλλον ὁμοφροσύνῃσιν ἐνήσει Od. 15.198.
In reference to the mind, like that of another, having the same inclinations. Of animals: οὐδὲ λύκοι τε καὶ ἄρνες ὁμόφρονα θυμὸν ἔχουσιν Il. 22.263.
Epithet of shields (cf. ὀμφαλός 2) Il. 4.448, Il. 6.118, Il. 12.161, Il. 22.111, etc.: Od. 19.32.
Of the yoke of a chariot, furnished with a boss (cf. ὀμφαλός 3) Il. 24.269.
The navel: οὖτα παρʼ ὀμφαλόν Il. 4.525. Cf. Il. 13.568, Il. 20.416, Il. 21.180.
Fig., the centre: νήσῳ ἐν ἀμφιρύτῃ, ὅθι τʼ ὀ. ἐστι θαλάσσης Od. 1.50.
A boss on a shield Il. 11.34, Il. 13.192.
A boss on the yoke of a chariot Il. 24.273.
A voice. Always of a divine voice or inspiration: ἐπισπόμενοι θεοῦ ὀμφῇ Od. 3.215=Od. 16.96. Cf. Il. 2.41, Il. 20.129.
All the same, nevertheless: ὅμως δʼ οὐ λήθετο χάρμης Il. 12.393. Cf. Od. 11.565.

Alike, equally, likewise: ἄμφω ὁμῶς φιλέουσα Il. 1.196= 209. Cf. Il. 15.98, Il. 17.422: νυκτὶ ὁμῶς πλείειν (i.e. as well as by day) Od. 15.34, ὁμῶς ἐφοίτων (with one consent) Od. 24.415. Cf. Od. 4.775, Od. 8.542, Od. 23.332.

Preceding clauses joined by . . . τε . . . τε, τε καί, alike: πλῆθεν ὁμῶς ἵππων τε καὶ ἀνδρῶν Il. 8.214, κάτθανʼ ὁμῶς ὅ τʼ ἀεργὸς ἀνὴρ ὅ τε . . . Il. 9.320. Cf. Il. 11.708, Il. 15.257, Il. 17.644, Il. 21.521, Il. 24.73: Od. 10.28, 80=Od. 15.476, Od. 24.63.
In the same manner, to the same degree: οὐκέθʼ ὁμῶς τιμῆς ἔσεαι Il. 9.605. Cf. Il. 21.62.
With dat., equally with, like as: ὁμῶς τοι ἤπια οἶδεν Od. 13.405=Od. 15.39. Cf. Il. 5.535, Il. 14.72, Il. 9.312:=Od. 14.156.
A vision seen in sleep, a dream: οὐκ ὀ., ἀλλʼ ὕπαρ ἐσθλόν Od. 19.547. Cf. Il. 10.496: Od. 20.90.
In generalized sense, dreams: καὶ γάρ τʼ ὀ. ἐκ διός ἐστιν Il. 1.63.
To his . . . (with the -δε doubled): ὅνδε δόμονδε Il. 16.445: Od. 1.83=Od. 14.424=Od. 20.239=Od. 21.204, Od. 3.272, Od. 17.527, Od. 20.329.

Something that
benefits, a means of aid, an aid, benefit, help: ἐφράσατο μέγʼ ὄνειαρ Od. 4.444. Cf. Od. 15.78.
Of a person: πᾶσιν ὄνειαρ Il. 22.433. Cf. Il. 22.486.
In pl., good things, good cheer: παρά σφιν ὀνείατα μυρία κεῖται Od. 10.9. Cf. Od. 15.316.
In pl., goods, substance: τοσσάδʼ ὀνείατʼ ἄγοντα Il. 24.367.
Conveying blame or censure, reproachful, reviling, abusive: μῦθον Il. 21.393, 471. Cf. Il. 1.519, Il. 2.277, Il. 16.628, Il. 21.480: Od. 18.326.
Absol. in neut. pl., reviling, abuse: ὀνειδείοισιν ἐνίσσων Il. 22.497.
To use words of blame or censure, speak in abuse or reviling: μετέειπε νείκει ὀνειδίζων Il. 7.95.
To make matter of blame or reproach, cast in one's teeth: ἀλκήν μοι ὀνείδισας (i.e. the want of it) Il. 9.34: τὴν γαστέρʼ ὀνειδίζων Od. 18.380.
With dependent clause: ὀνείδισον ὡς ἔσεταί περ (speak out to him and tell him how it will be) Il. 1.211, ἧσαι ὀνειδίζων ὅτι . . . (casting in his teeth that . . .) Il. 2.255.
In pl., words of blame, censure, reproach, abuse, reviling: λέγʼ ὀνείδεα Il. 2.222. Cf. Il. 1.291, Il. 2.251, Il. 3.242, 438, Il. 9.460, Il. 20.246: Od. 17.461.
In pl., shame, disgrace: αἳ ἐμῇ κεφαλῇ κατʼ ὀνείδεα χεῦαν Od. 22.463.
A cause or source of reproach or blame: ἐμοί κʼ ὀνείδεα ταῦτα γένοιτο Od. 6.285. Cf. Il. 16.498, Il. 17.556.
One busied with dreams, one skilled in the interpretation of dreams Il. 1.63, Il. 5.149.
A vision seen in sleep, a dream: θεῖός μοι ἐνύπνιον ἦλθεν ὀ. Od. 14.495. Cf. Il. 2.80, Il. 5.150: Od. 4.841, Od. 6.49, Od. 11.207, 222, Od. 19.535, 555, 560, 562, 568, Od. 20.87, Od. 24.12.
The state of one who is dreaming, a dream, the land of dreams: ἔν περ ὀνείρῳ Od. 19.541, 581=Od. 21.79. Cf. Il. 22.199.
3 sing. fut. ὀνήσει Il. 7.172, Il. 8.36, 467: Od. 23.24.

To be of service to, confer benefit upon, benefit, profit, help: Ἀχαιούς Il. 7.172. Cf. Il. 1.395, 503, Il. 5.205, Il. 9.509, Il. 24.45: σὲ τοῦτό γε γῆρας ὀνήσει (will benefit you so far, you may thank your years for that) Od. 23.24. Cf. Od. 14.67.
Without expressed object: βουλήν, ἥ τις ὀνήσει Il. 8.36= 467.

In mid., to get good, benefit, profit, help or enjoyment from something, be the better for it: καὐτὸς ὀνήσεαι Il. 6.260. Cf. Il. 7.173: πρὸς δʼ αὐτοὶ ὀνησόμεθα (will get some enjoyment for ourselves) Od. 14.415.
With genit. of that from which good is derived: τί σευ ἄλλος ὀνήσεται; Il. 16.31: δαιτὸς ὄνησο (make the best of it, be thankful for what you have got) Od. 19.68.
In aor. pple., blessed (cf. οὐλόμενος): ἐσθλός μοι δοκεῖ εἶναι, ὀνήμενος Od. 2.33.
-ατος, τό. Also οὔνομα Il. 3.235, Il. 17.260: Od. 6.194, Od. 9.355.
The name or fame of a person or of something: Ἰθάκης γε καὶ ἐς Τροίην ὀ. ἵκει Od. 13.248. Cf. Od. 24.93.
To address by name: πατρόθεν ἐκ γενεῆς ὀνομάζων ἄνδρα ἕκαστον Il. 10.68. Cf. Il. 22.415: Od. 4.278.

In the recurring formula ἔπος τʼ ἔφατʼ ἔκ τʼ ὀνόμαζεν app. meaning no more than to address (the name is often not given in the reported speech, and in Od. 6.254 and Od. 10.319 is not known to the speaker. In Od. 8.194 the name cannot have been used, as it was not then known to the Phaeacians. In Od. 17.215 Melantheus cannot have known any name by which to address the disguised Odysseus. In Od. 14.52 the disguised Odysseus knew Eumaeus's name, but cannot be supposed to have used it) Il. 1.361, Il. 3.398, Il. 6.253, Il. 7.108, etc.: Od. 2.302, Od. 3.374, Od. 4.311, Od. 7.330, etc.
To speak of or mention by name, utter the name of: τὸν καὶ οὐ παρεόντʼ ὀνομάζειν αἰδέομαι Od. 14.145.
To name, tell the name of Od. 4.551.
To name, specify, detail, enumerate: δῶρα Il. 18.449. Cf. Il. 9.515, Od. 24.339.
3 sing. opt. ὀνόσαιτο Il. 4.539, Il. 13.127, Il. 17.399.

Pple. ὀνοσσάμενος Il. 24.439. Here app. should come as 2 pl. pres. οὔνεσθε, u.l. in Il. 24.241 (see above). To think little of, make light of, look upon or treat with contempt or scorn, disparage: ἔργον Il. 4.539. Cf. Il. 9.55, Il. 13.127, 287, Il. 14.95=Il. 17.173, Il. 17.25, 399, Il. 24.439: Od. 8.239, Od. 21.427.
With dependent clause: ἦ ὀνόσασθʼ ὅτι . . . ; (seems it so light a thing that . . . ?) Il. 24.241: ἦ ὄνοσαι ὅτι . . . ; (is it not enough that . . . ?) Od. 17.378.
To address or call to by name, call upon by name: ἑταῖρον Il. 10.522, Il. 16.491, Il. 23.178, Il. 24.591.
To call upon by name in adjuration: θεούς Il. 14.278.
To name, tell the name or names of, enumerate by name: πληθύν Il. 2.488. Cf. Od. 11.328, 517.
To disclose a person's name Od. 11.251.
To name, appoint: σόν με θεράποντʼ ὀνόμηνεν Il. 23.90.
To name, specify, detail, enumerate: δῶρα Il. 9.121. Cf. Od. 4.240.
With fut. infin.: ὄρχους μοι ὀνόμηνας δώσειν πεντήκοντα Od. 24.341.
To be named: κακοΐλιον οὐκ ὀνομαστήν Od. 19.260= 597= Od. 23.19.
To be made light of or treated with indifference: ὀῶρα Il. 9.164.
Dat. pl. ὀνύχεσσι in passages cited.
In pl., an eagle's talons: νεβρὸν ἔχοντʼ ὀνύχεσσιν Il. 8.248. Cf. Il. 12.202 = 220: Od. 2.153, Od. 15.161.
[ὀξύς + βέλος. The force of the second element app. obscured.]
Epithet of an arrow: ὀϊστός Il. 4.126.
Epithet of spears Il. 5.50, 568, Il. 7.11, Il. 14.443, etc.: Od. 19.33, Od. 20.306.

Sharp, keen, with sharp point or edge: δοῦρε δύω ὀξέα Il. 11.44. Cf. Il. 10.135, Il. 11.392, Il. 12.56 (pointed), 447 (coming to a point), Il. 15.711, etc.: Od. 1.99, Od. 3.443, Od. 5.411 (jagged), Od. 12.74 (rising to a point), etc.
Epithet of weapons or parts thereof Il. 1.190, Il. 4.185, 214, 490, 530, etc.: Od. 2.3, Od. 4.700, Od. 10.145, Od. 14.271, Od. 22.265, etc.
Sim. of cutting instruments: ἐρινεὸν ὀξέϊ χαλκῷ τάμνεν Il. 21.37. Cf. Il. 23.412: Od. 12.173.
Fig. of the beams of the sun, piercing, penetrating Il. 17.372.
In reference to perception with the eye, quick.
In superl., with infin.: ὀξύτατον εἰσοράασθαι Il. 14.345. Cf. Il. 17.675.
Of sound, shrill, piercing: ἀϋτή Il. 15.313.
Of pain or grief, sharp, piercing: ὀδύναι Il. 11.268, 272. Cf. Il. 11.269, Il. 16.518, Il. 19.125, Il. 22.425: Od. 11.208, Od. 19.517.
As epithet of Ares, eager, impetuous Il. 7.330.
As epithet of battle, keen, fierce: ὀξὺν Ἄρηα Il. 2.440, Il. 4.352=Il. 19.237, Il. 8.531=Il. 18.304, Il. 11.836, Il. 17.721.
In neut. sing. ὀξύ as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Of perceiving with the eye, with keen glance, quickly: νόησεν Il. 3.374=Il. 5.312, Il. 5.680, Il. 8.91, 132, Il. 11.343, Il. 15.649, Il. 20.291. Cf. Od. 5.393.
Sim. of perceiving with the ear, quickly (the exercise of the power of hearing being thought of as keen like a glance): ἄκουσεν Il. 17.256.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to sound, shrilly, piercingly: βοήσας Il. 17.89. Cf. Il. 18.71, Il. 20.52, Il. 22.141.
In neut. pl. ὀξέα as adv., in reference to sound, shrilly, piercingly: κεκλήγων Il. 2.222. Cf. Il. 12.125, Il. 17.88.
In neut. sing. superl. ὀξύτατον as adv., of perceiving with the eye, with keenest glance, most quickly: οὔτʼ ὀξύτατον δέρκεται ὄσσε Il. 23.477.

To cause to go with, accompany or attend, a person, send with him: ὤπασά οἱ πομπόν Il. 13.416. Cf. Il. 16.38, Il. 18.452, Il. 24.153, 461: Od. 9.90=Od. 10.102, Od. 10.204, Od. 13.68, Od. 15.310, Od. 20.364.
To cause to follow a person as chief, give a person rule over: πολύν μοι ὤπασε λαόν Il. 9.483.
In mid., to attach to oneself, take with one, as companion: κήρυκα καὶ ἑταῖρον Od. 10.59. Cf. Il. 10.238, Il. 19.238.

To make over, give as a present, give, present: πατρόκλῳ κόμην ὀπάσαιμι φέρεσθαι (I am ready to . . ., I can do no better than . . .) Il. 23.151. Cf. Il. 17.196: χρυσέην ἠλακάτην Od. 4.131. Cf. Od. 4.619=Od. 15.119, Od. 8.430, Od. 13.121, 305, Od. 24.283.

With less definite object, to cause to attend upon a person, attach to him, give, grant, bestow: κάλλος Il. 6.157. Cf. Il. 7.205, Il. 8.141, Il. 12.255, Il. 14.358, 491, Il. 15.327, Il. 16.730, Il. 17.566, Il. 21.570, Il. 22.51 (i.e. as a dowry): ὁμοφροσύνην Od. 6.181. Cf. Od. 3.57, Od. 8.498, Od. 13.45, Od. 14.62, Od. 15.320, Od. 18.19, Od. 19.161, Od. 21.214, Od. 23.210, Od. 24.201.
To press hard upon, chase, pursue: Ἀχαιούς Il. 8.341. Cf. Il. 5.334, Il. 17.462.
In pass.: [ποταμὸς] ὀπαζόμενος Διὸς ὄμβρῳ (driven onwards) Il. 11.493.
Of an abstraction, to bear hard upon, oppress: γῆράς μʼ (σʼ) ὀπάζει Il. 4.321, Il. 8.103.
Having the same father Il. 11.257, Il. 12.371. (See κασίγνητος 1.b.)
In whichever direction, whithersoever: ἄρχʼ, ὅππῃ σε κραδίη κελεύει Il. 13.784. Cf. Il. 20.25 and Il. 22.185 (as . . .): Od. 1.347, Od. 14.517=Od. 15.339, Od. 16.81=Od. 21.342, Od. 18.242.
With subj. or opt. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table at end III.B.a 1,

In what direction, whither: πάπτηνεν ἕκαστος ὅπῃ φύγοι ὄλεθρον (to see where he could turn to escape . . .) Il. 14.507=Il. 16.283, εἰσορόων χρόα, ὅπῃ εἴξειεν (to see where he might find an opening) Il. 22.321. Cf. Od. 8.573, Od. 22.43.
In what spot, where: εἴφʼ ὅπῃ ἔσχες νῆα Od. 9.279. Cf. Od. 9.457.
In what direction or quarter: οὐ γὰρ ἴδμεν ὅπῃ ζόφος οὐδʼ ὅπῃ ἠώς, οὐδʼ ὅπῃ . . . οὐδʼ ὅπῃ . . . Od. 10.190.
To be in attendance on a person, attend him as a follower, retainer or henchman Il. 2.184, Il. 24.368.
Of an inanimate object, to be carried or borne by a person, accompany him: ἀνεμώλιά μοι ὀπηδεῖ [τόξα] Il. 5.216.

Of a divinity, to cause his protecting or favouring power to go with or attend on a person, act as his protector or guardian: διί, ὅς θʼ ἱκέτῃσιν ἅμʼ αἰδοίοισιν ὀπηδεῖ Od. 7.165= 181. Cf. Od. 9.271, Od. 19.398.
Of abstractions, to attend upon a person, be attached to him, be given, granted, bestowed on him: ἀρετὴν σήν, ἥ τοι ὀπηδεῖ Od. 8.237. Cf. Il. 17.251.
To regard with awe or reverence, stand in awe of, observe: μητρὸς ὠπίζετʼ ἐφετμήν Il. 18.216. Cf. Od. 13.148, Od. 14.283.
To pay regard or heed to, direct one's thoughts to, think of: ἔμʼ οὐδὲν ὀπίζεο Il. 22.332.

To eye: τί ὀπιπεύεις πολέμοιο γεφύρας; (instead of advancing to the fight) Il. 4.371, οὔ σʼ ἐθέλω βαλέειν ὀπιπεύσας
(holding you in talk and looking out for a weak spot) Il. 7.243 : ὀπιπεύσεις γυναῖκας (will be ogling the maids) Od. 19.67.
The watch (kept by the gods) on the deeds of men, their regard for righteousness and reprobation of evil-doing : θεῶν ὄπιν οὐκ ἀλέγοντες Il. 16.388. Cf. Od. 20.215, Od. 21.28.
So without θεῶν : οὐκ ὄπιδα φρονέοντες Od. 14.82. Cf. Od. 14.88.

div.head: a
div.p: Behind, in rear, in the hinder part : στῆ ὄπιθεν Il. 1.197, πρόσθε λέων, ὄπιθεν δὲ δράκων Il. 6.181. Cf. Il. 2.542, Il. 11.397, Il. 13.289, Il. 17.718 (covering the rear), Il. 19.397 (following him), etc. : σανίδας ἐκδῆσαι ὄπισθεν Od. 22.174 (i.e. his feet and hands were to be bound together behind him and were to be made fast to the boards). Cf. Od. 4.357, Od. 5.167, Od. 6.307, Od. 8.527, Od. 13.84, Od. 15.34, Od. 19.436.–τὰ ὄπισθεν, the hinder partsIl. 11.613.

div.head: b
div.p: Behind, remaining behind, while another departs or others depart : ὄπισθε μένων Il. 9.332. Cf. Od. 10.209, Od. 11.72, Od. 15.88, Od. 17.201.– τοὺς ὄπιθεν Ἀχαιούς Il. 13.83 (the laggards).
Absent : τῶν ὄπιθεν Od. 11.66 (those left at home).

div.head: c
div.p: Towards the rear : ὄπιθεν σάκος βάλεν (behind his back) Il. 11.545.

Of time, afterwards, hereafter, there-after, in the future, in time to come, late : ταῦτʼ (τὰ) ὄπισθεν ἀρεσσόμεθα Il. 4.362, Il. 6.526. Cf. Il. 9.515 and 519 (for the future), Il. 12.34 : κακῶς ὄπιθεν φρονέουσιν (i.e. they are awaiting their opportunity) Od. 18.168. Cf. Od. 2.270, 278, Od. 14.393, Od. 22.55, Od. 23.249, 261.

div.head: II
div.p: With genit., of place, behind, in rear of : ὄπισθε μάχης Il. 13.536= Il. 14.430. Cf. Il. 5.595, Il. 17.468, Il. 24.15.
Of direction, backwards, back : ἀνεχάζετο τυτθὸν ὀπίσσω Il. 5.443. Cf. Il. 3.218, 261, Il. 12.205, Il. 20.119, etc. : Od. 8.375, Od. 11.149, Od. 12.410.
In reference to the exercise of a mental faculty : πρόσσω καὶ ὀπίσσω (see πρόσσω 1).
Back to the same place, back again : ὀπίσω κίε Od. 16.150. Cf. Od. 7.326.
Sim. : ὄφρʼ ἐξεμέσειεν ὀπίσσω ἱστὸν αὖτις Od. 12.437.

Of place, behind, in rear : ἐξακέονται ὀπίσσω (follow and . . .) Il. 9.507, αὐτὰρ ὀπίσσω ἡ πληθὺς ἐπὶ νῆας ἀπονέοντο (behind the screen covering their retreat) Il. 15.304. Cf. Il. 15.735, Il. 17.752, Il. 21.30, Il. 22.137.
Sim. : τῷ ἄλγεα κάλλιπʼ ὀπίσσω (left behind her) Od. 11.279. Cf. Il. 3.160 : Od. 23.119.

Of time, afterwards, hereafter, thereafter, in the future, in time to come, later : τρῳαί μʼ ὀπίσσω μωμήσονται Il. 3.411. Cf. Il. 4.37, Il. 6.352, 450, Il. 15.497, etc. : Od. 1.222 (for the time to come), Od. 2.179, Od. 6.273, Od. 11.433, Od. 14.137, Od. 18.132, etc.
As quasi-sb. : ἐς ὀπίσσω Od. 18.122= Od. 20.199.
Here prob. should come pres. infin. mid. ὅπλεσθαι Il. 19.172, Il. 23.159 (for ὁπλεῖσθαι). To get ready, make ready, prepare : ἄμαξαν Od. 6.73.
In mid., to make ready (a meal) for oneself, prepare oneself (a meal) : δεῖπνον ὅπλεσθαι Il. 19.172, Il. 23.159.
3 sing. aor. mid. ὡπλίσατο (ὁ-) Il. 23.301, 351. ὡπλίσσατο Il. 11.86. ὁπλίσσατο Od. 2.20, Od. 9.291, 311, 344, Od. 10.116.
To deck, array : ὅπλισθεν γυναῖκες (came in their finery) Od. 23.143.
To get ready, make ready, prepare : κυκειῶ Il. 11.641 : νῆες ὁπλίζονται πόντον ἔπι (are set their courses over . . .) Od. 17.288. Cf. Il. 24.190 : Od. 2.289.

div.head: a
div.p: To get or make oneself ready, make one's preparation : ἔξω ἰὼν ὁπλίζετο Od. 14.526.
With infin. : ὁπλίζοντο νέκυας ἀγέμεν Il. 7.417.

div.head: b
div.p: To get ready, harness (one's horses) Il. 23.301, 351.

div.head: c
div.p: To make ready (a meal) for oneself, prepare oneself (a meal) : δεῖπνον Il. 11.86 : Od. 9.311, Od. 10.116, δόρπον Od. 2.20, Od. 4.429 = 574, Od. 9.291, 344, Od. 12.292, Od. 16.453.

div.head: d
div.p: To don one's harness, make ready or prepare for the fray : Τρῶες ἀνὰ πτόλιν ὁπλίζοντο Il. 8.55. Cf. Od. 24.495.
An implement, appliance, tool : ὅπλʼ ἐν χερσὶν ἔχων Od. 3.433. Cf. Il. 18.409, 412.
Specifically, a rope or cable : ἐμὲ κατέδησαν ὅπλῳ Od. 14.346. Cf. Od. 21.390.
In pl., the tackle of a ship landed from her when not in use and taken on board before putting to sea : πάντʼ ἐν νηῒ ὅπλʼ ἐτίθει Od. 2.390. Cf. Od. 6.286, Od. 10.404, 424, Od. 12.410.
Specifically, the running tackle : ὅπλων ἅπτεσθαι Od. 2.423, δησάμενοι ὅπλα 430. Cf. Od. 11.9, Od. 12.151, Od. 15.288.
In pl., warlike array, harness, armour : ὅπλοισιν ἔνι δεινοῖσιν ἐδύτην Il. 10.254, 272. Cf. Il. 18.614, Il. 19.21.
-η, comp. Younger : ὁπλότερος γενεῇ Il. 2.707. Cf. Il. 4.325 : Od. 19.184, Od. 21.370.
Youthful rather than old : αἰεὶ ὁπλοτέρων ἀνδρῶν φρένες ἠερέθονται (the younger generation, the class of youths) Il. 3.108, χαρίτων μίαν ὁπλοτεράων (one of the youthful . . .) Il. 14.267, 275.
Youngest, the youngest : Νέστορος ὁπλοτάτη θυγάτηρ Od. 3.465. Cf. Il. 9.58 : Od. 7.58, Od. 11.283, Od. 15.364.

p.gloss: As relative, of whatever sort or kind.

div.p: With subj. or opt. in conditional relative sentences (with τοῖος as correlative). For the examples and constructions see Table at end II.B.b, (III) (D) (29).
In object clauses, of what sort or kind : ὁπποίης ἐπὶ νηὸς ἀφίκεο Od. 1.171= Od. 14.188.
With the indefinite ἄσσα : εἰπέ μοι ὁπποῖʼ ἄσσα εἵματα ἕστο Od. 19.218.
Fig-juice used to curdle milk for cheese Il. 5.902.
As relative, as many as : κτήμαθʼ ὁπόσσα τοί ἐστιν (all your possessions) Od. 22.220.
Absol. : ὁπόσσον ἐπέσχε πυρὸς μένος (the space that the fire covered) Il. 23.238= Il. 24.792.
In object clauses, how many or great, what : ὄφρʼ εἴπῃς ὁππόσα κήδεʼ ἀνέτης Od. 14.47.

div.head: a
div.p: With indic. : ὁππότε μιν ξυνδῆσαι ἤθελον Il. 1.399. Cf. Il. 8.230, Il. 11.671, Il. 14.317, etc. : Od. 4.731, Od. 5.125, Od. 18.409, Od. 23.345.

div.head: α
div.p:
With
subj. or opt. in relative sentences corresponding to sentences with εἰ 4. For the examples and constructions see Table at end II.B.a 1, b, (D) (7).–

div.head: β
div.p: In conditional relative sentences. See Table III.B.a 1 2 (3) (5), b.1, (D) (12) (16) (20) (26) (31) (34) (35) (37) (54) (59).–

div.head: γ
div.p: With subj. introducing similes : ὡς ὁπότε . . . Il. 11.305 : Od. 4.335= Od. 17.126.
Against the time when : δέγμενος ὁππότʼ ἀφορμηθεῖεν (watching for the time when . . .) Il. 2.794. Cf. Il. 4.229, Il. 10.189, etc. : Od. 20.386.
At which time, when : ἔσσεται ἠώς, ὁππότε τις καὶ ἐμεῖο Ἄρῃ ἐκ θυμὸν ἕληται Il. 21.112. Cf. Il. 13.817.
In an object clause : ἴδμεν ὁππότε νεῖτʼ ἐκ Πύλου; Od. 4.633.
In object clauses, in what place, where : δμώων κέ τεο πειρηθεῖμεν, ὅπου τις νῶϊ τίει Od. 16.306 (i.e. at the various ἔργα of 314). Cf. Od. 3.16.
In indirect questions and object clauses, whence : ἐρέσθαι, ὁ. οὗτος ἀνήρ (where he comes from) Od. 1.406. Cf. Od. 3.80, Od. 14.47.
In reference to origin : εἰπὲ τεὸν γένος, ὁ. ἐσσί Od. 19.162.
As relative, where : ὁππόθι πιότατον πεδίον Καλυδῶνος Il. 9.577.
In an object clause : σάφα εἰπέμεν ὁππόθʼ ὄλωλεν Od. 3.89.
With subj. in a relative sentence corresponding to sentences with εἰ 4 : ὁππόσʼ ἐπέλθω Od. 14.139 (see Table at end II.D.3).

p.gloss: As relative, whichever of the two.

div.head: a
div.p: With indic. : ἡμέων ὁπποτέρῳ θάνατος τέτυκται Il. 3.101. Cf. Il. 3.321.

div.head: b
div.p: With subj. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table at end (III) (D) (20) (26).

div.head: c
div.p: In pl. in reference to two bodies of men.
With opt. in a conditional relative sentence. See Table (III) (D) (54).
In object clauses, which of the two : Ζεὺς τό γε οἷδεν, ὁπποτέρῳ θανάτοιο τέλος πεπρωμένον ἐστίν Il. 3.309. Cf. Il. 3.317, Il. 22.130 : Od. 12.57.
In pl. in reference to two bodies of men Il. 5.33.
So in reference to two pairs of horses Il. 23.487.
In an object clause, from which quarter : οὐδʼ ἂν ἔτι γνοίης ὁπποτέρωθεν Ἀχαιοὶ κλονέονται Il. 14.59.
Roasted, roast : κρέα Il. 4.345 : Od. 12.396, κρειῶν Od. 16.50.
A scout : ὀπτῆρας ὄτρυνα νέεσθαι Od. 14.261= Od. 17.430.
To take or have to wife, marry : ὅς [μιν] ἀναφανδὸν ὄπυιεν Il. 16.178, τὴν ὤπυιε ἀμφιγυήεις Il. 18.383. Cf. Il. 13.379, 429, Il. 14.268 : Od. 2.207, 336, Od. 4.798, Od. 15.21, Od. 16.386.
Absol. in pres. pple., a married man : οἱ δύʼ ὀπυίοντες Od. 6.63.
In pass., of the woman, to be taken to wife, be married : ἐξ αἰσύμηθεν ὀπυιομένη Il. 8.304.
The presentation of something to the sight, sight of something : ὅπως ἤντησας ὀπωπῆς Od. 3.97= Od. 4.327, Od. 17.44.
The faculty of sight, vision : ἁμαρτήσεσθαι ὀπωπῆς Od. 9.512.
Late summer, harvest-time : ἀστέρʼ, ὅς τʼ ὀπώρης εἶσιν (in . . .) Il. 22.27.
Distinguished from θέρος Od. 11.192, Od. 12.76, Od. 14.384.
Of, that comes in, late summer or harvest-time : ἀστέρι Il. 5.5. Cf. Il. 16.385, Il. 21.346 : Od. 5.328.

In such way or manner as, as.
(a)

With indic. : ἔρξον ὅπως ἐθέλεις Il. 4.37 : Od. 13.145. Cf. Od. 14.172, Od. 15.111, etc.–
(b)
With subj. or opt. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table at end III.B.a 1 2,
In object clauses, in what way or manner, how.

div.head: a
div.p: With indic. : κατάλεξον ὅπως ἤντησας ὀπωπῆς Od. 3.97. Cf. Il. 10.545, etc. : Od. 4.109 (thinking how . . .), etc.
With fut. : οὐδʼ ἴδμεν ὅπως ἔσται τάδε ἔργα Il. 2.252. Cf. Il. 4.14, etc. : Od. 13.376, 386, Od. 19.557, etc.
After a past tense : ἑλίσσετο μερμηρίζων ὅππως χεῖρας ἐφήσει Od. 20.29.

div.head: b
div.p: With subj., pure or with κεν : οὐδέ ἑ λήθει ὅππως τανύσῃ Il. 23.324. Cf. Il. 3.110, Il. 10.225, Il. 17.144, etc. : φράζεσθαι ὅππως κε μνηστῆρας ἀπώσεαι Od. 1.270. Cf. Od. 1.77, etc.–

div.head: c
div.p: With opt. : μερμήριξεν ὅππως ἐξαπάφοιτο Il. 14.160. Cf. Il. 1.344, etc. : Od. 3.129, Od. 9.554, etc.
In final clauses, so that, in order that.

div.head: a
div.p: With fut. : ὅπως ἀντάξιον ἔσται Il. 1.136. Cf. Od. 1.57.

div.head: b
div.p: With subj. : λοχῶσιν ὅπως ἀπὸ φῦλον ὄληται Od. 14.181. Cf. Od. 3.19.–

div.head: c
div.p: With opt. : ὅπως κῆρας ἀλάλκοι Il. 21.548. Cf. Od. 6.319, Od. 13.319, etc.
When : ὅπως ἴδον αἷμα Il. 11.459. Cf. Il. 12.208 : Od. 3.373, Od. 22.22.
Pres. infin. mid. ὁράασθαι Od. 16.107, Od. 18.4, Od. 20.317. From ὅρημαι (cf. δίζημαι).
2 sing. pres. mid. ὅρηαι Od. 14.343. From ὀπ-
2 sing. fut. in mid. form ὄψεαι Il. 4.353, Il. 8.471, Il. 9.359, Il. 24.601 : Od. 24.511. ὄψει Od. 12.101. ὄψῃ Il. 23.620.
In act. and mid., to look, gaze : θαύμαζον ὁρόωντες Od. 7.145. Cf. Il. 20.23 : Od. 4.47= Od. 10.181.

To direct one's sight, look, gaze, in a specified direction : θεοὶ ἐς πάντες ὁρῶντο Il. 22.166. Cf. Il. 1.350, Il. 3.325, Il. 16.646, Il. 17.637, Il. 24.633 : Od. 5.439, Od. 18.344, Od. 20.373, Od. 23.91.
To look at or upon, gaze upon.

In act. and mid. : αἰεὶ τέρμʼ ὁρόων (keeping his eyes
upon it) Il. 23.323 : τὸν ὁρῶντο Od. 15.462. Cf. Od. 8.459.
To look to something, consider it, judge by it.
In act. and mid. : ἐς γενεὴν ὁρόων Il. 10.239 : ἐς μέγεθος ὁρώμενος Od. 18.219.
To look to, attend to, something : ἐς ἐμὰ ἔργʼ ὁρόωσα Od. 19.514.

In act. and mid., to have sight of, see, behold : τῶν ἄλλων οὔ τις ὁρᾶτο [αὐτήν] Il. 1.198, οὔ πω τοιόνδε λαὸν οὔπωπα Il. 2.799. Cf. Il. 3.234, Il. 5.120, Il. 11.651, Il. 13.99, Il. 14.343, etc. : Od. 1.229, Od. 3.93, Od. 11.156, 450, Od. 13.357, Od. 14.343, etc.
With indefinite object : ὁρόων ἀκάχημαι Od. 8.314. Cf. Od. 4.226, Od. 21.123.

With complementary pple. or adj. : ὅτι θνῄσκοντας ὁρᾶτο Il. 1.56. Cf. Il. 3.306, Il. 5.244, Il. 8.471, Il. 9.359, etc. : μάλα σʼ ὁρόω καλόν τε μέγαν τε Od. 1.301= Od. 3.199. Cf. Od. 18.143, Od. 24.511.
With complementary clause : οὐχ ὁράᾳς ὅτι . . .; Il. 7.448. Cf. Il. 4.347, Il. 15.555, Il. 21.108 : Od. 8.313, Od. 17.545.
The infin. used epexegetically : εἶδος μάλα μέγας ἦν ὁράασθαι Od. 18.4.
To visit, go to see, see.
In mid. : ὀψόμεναί τε γέρονθʼ ἅλιον καὶ δώματα πατρός Il. 18.141. Cf. Il. 14.200, 205 = 304, 301 : Od. 23.360.
To admit to one's presence, see : οὐδέ σε μήτηρ ὄψεται Od. 15.516.
Of mental vision : ὁρόων θάνατον Il. 20.481, οἷος ὅρα πρόσσω καὶ ὀπίσσω Il. 18.250 : Od. 24.452.
The length of the outstretched arms, a fathom Il. 23.327 : Od. 9.325, Od. 10.167.
Pres. pple. (fr. ὀρέγνυμι) ὀρεγνύς Il. 1.351, Il. 22.37.
Mid. 3 sing. aor. ὠρέξατο Il. 5.851, Il. 23.99. ὀρέξατο Il. 6.466, Il. 13.20, 190.
3 pl. pf. ὀρωρέχαται Il. 16.834. 3 pl. plupf. ὀρωρέχατο Il. 11.26.
To hold or stretch out (a hand or the hands) : χεῖρας ὀρεγνύς Il. 1.351, Il. 22.37. Cf. Il. 15.371, Il. 24.743 : Od. 9.527, Od. 12.257, Od. 17.366.
So in mid. : ἀνδρὸς παιδοφόνοιο ποτὶ στόμα χεῖρʼ ὀρέγεσθαι Il. 24.506 (but χείρʼ (i.e. χειρί) may be read, bringing the passage under 3a. Cf. Il. 23.99 there cited).
To hold out, offer for acceptance, bestow, give : Θέτις ὤρεξε [δέπας] πιοῦσα (i.e. held it out to return it) Il. 24.102 : αἴ κέν τις κοτύλην καὶ πύρνον ὀρέξῃ Od. 15.312. Cf. Od. 17.407.
With immaterial object, to yield, grant, bestow, give : κῦδος Il. 5.33, εὖχος Il. 12.328, τάχος Il. 23.406, etc. : κῦδος Od. 4.275.

div.head: a
div.p: To stretch out one's limbs, make a stretch, stretch, reach : τρὶς ὀρέξατʼ ἰών (made three strides) Il. 13.20 : ὀρέξασθαι μενεαινων (to reach out a hand to me) Od. 11.392. Cf. Od. 21.53.
So κυάνεοι δράκοντες ὀρωρέχατο (were astretch, i.e. were represented with heads outstretched) Il. 11.26.
With genit. of that towards which one reaches out : οὗ παιδὸς ὀρέξατο Il. 6.466.
With dat. of the part employed : ὠρέξατο χερσίν Il. 23.99.
So ἵπποι ποσσὶν ὀρωρέχαται (are astretch, are in their full stride) Il. 16.834.

div.head: b
div.p: To make a lunge or thrust.
With dat. of the weapon : ὠρέξατʼ ἔγχεϊ Il. 5.851. Cf. Il. 4.307.
With this dat. and genit. of the person attacked : ὀρέξατο δουρὶ Ἕκτορος Il. 13.190.
With acc. of part reached : ἔφθη ὀρεξάμενος σκέλος (ὦμον) (app. a construction ad sensum, got his blow in first and struck . . .) Il. 16.314, 322. Cf. Il. 23.805.
Of spears, held out or presented for action : μελίῃσιν Il. 2.543.
dat. pl. of ὄρος + τροφ-, τρέφω.]
Bred in the mountains, mountain-bred. Of lions Il. 12.299, Il. 17.61 : Od. 6.130, Od. 9.292.
[ὀρεσ-, ὄρος + (poss.) a second element conn. with κοῖτος, κεῖμαι.]
Thus, couching in the mountains : φηρσίν Il. 1.268 : αἶγας Od. 9.155.
[comp. fr. ὀρεσ-, ὄρος. Of the mountains (as opposed to the valleys).]
Mountain-bred : δράκων Il. 22.93 : λύκοι ἠδὲ λέοντες Od. 10.212.
A mountain nymph. Defining νύμφη Il. 6.420.
Thus, of oxen, to stretch themselves out, plunge Il. 23.30.
In neut. pl. ὄρθια as adv., in shrill tones : ἤϋσεν Il. 11.11.
Epithet of oxen, with upright horns Il. 8.231, Il. 18.573 : Od. 12.348.
Epithet of ships, with sterns running up into a tall ornamental projection (ἄφλαστον, κόρυμβοκόρυμβον) with tall sterns Il. 18.3, Il. 19.344.
Upright, erect : ἔγχεά σφιν ὄρθʼ ἐλήλατο Il. 10.153. Cf. Il. 24.359.
In or to an upright posture, upright, erect : ὀρθῶν ἑσταότων Il. 18.246. Cf. Il. 23.271 = 456 = 657 = 706 = 752 = 801 = 830, Il. 24.11 : Od. 12.51 = 162, 179, Od. 18.241, Od. 21.119.
To set upright, set on one's legs again Il. 7.272, Il. 23.695.
In pass., to stand up, rise up : ὀρθωθεὶς ἔνδυνε χιτῶνα Il. 10.21.
To assume from a recumbent a partially upright posture, raise oneself : ἕζετο ὀρθωθείς Il. 2.42, Il. 23.235. Cf. Il. 10.80.
2 sing. ὤρινας Od. 8.178. ὄρινας Od. 14.361, Od. 15.486.
Pass. 3 sing. aor. ὠρίνθη Il. 16.509. ὀρίνθη Il. 5.29, Il. 16.280, Il. 18.223.
Nom. pl. masc. pple. ὀρινθέντες Od. 22.23.
To put into a state of commotion, stir, agitate, trouble : ὀρινομένη θάλασσα (raised in billows) Il. 2.294. Cf. Il. 9.4, Il. 11.298 : Od. 7.273.
To put into violent motion : ῥέεθρα (brought them down in spate) Il. 21.235.
With personal object, to throw into confusion or disorder, strike with panic : μνηστῆρας Od. 24.448.
