In pass., of men, to be thrown into confusion or disorder, be put to disorderly rout, be struck with panic : ὀρινομένους ὑπὸ καπνοῦ Il. 9.243. Cf. Il. 11.521, 525, Il. 14.14= Il. 15.7, Il. 14.59, Il. 16.377 : ὀρινθέντες
κατὰ δῶμα (rushing in confusion) Il. 22.23.
Sim. of a single person : σοὶ ὀρινομένῳ κατὰ δῶμα (rushing in your rage) Od. 22.360.
With immaterial object, to stir up, bring about, cause : ὀρυμαγδόν Il. 21.313. Cf. Il. 24.760.
In reference to the heart or mind, to stir, rouse, agitate, trouble, touch : θυμόν Il. 2.142. Cf. Il. 5.29, Il. 9.595, Il. 16.509, Il. 24.585, etc. : Od. 4.366, Od. 17.47, 216, Od. 18.75, etc.
[app. neut. of ὅρκιος, adj. fr. ὅρκος.]
In pl., sacrificial victims or other offerings in sanction of an oath, oath-offerings: κήρυκες ἀνὰ ἄστυ θεῶν φέρον ὅρκια (the gods being to be invoked as witnesses) Il. 3.245. Cf. Il. 3.269.
In sing., an oath-sacrifice : οὐχ ἄλιον πέλει ὅρκιον (our . . .) Il. 4.158.
ὅρκια τάμνειν, to make a compact with the sanction of an oath, enter into a solemn treaty or agreementIl. 2.124, Il. 3.73 = 256, Il. 3.94, 105, 252, Il. 4.155, Il. 19.191 : Od. 24.483.
Hence, in pl., a compact, treaty, agreement : συνθεσίαι τε καὶ ὅρκια Il. 2.339. Cf. Il. 3.107, 280, 299, 323, Il. 4.67 = 72, 157, 236, 269, 271, Il. 7.69, 351, 411, Il. 22.262, 266 : Od. 24.546.
In pl., an oath : ὅρκια τοι δώσω Od. 19.302.
Something invoked in sanction of an oath, something by which one swears : ὅ τοι μέγας ἔσσεται ὁ. Il. 1.239. Cf. Il. 2.755, Il. 15.38 := Od. 5.186.
The taking of an oath, swearing : ἀνθρώπους ἐκέκαστο κλεπτοσύνῃ θʼ ὅρκῳ τε (i.e. false swearing) Od. 19.396.
A chain or string of objects Od. 24.8.
To stir up, bring about : πόλεμον Il. 10.28 : Od. 4.146.

To turn over, revolve, ponder, consider, debate, have in contemplation, meditate : ταῦτα Il. 1.193= Il. 11.411= Il. 17.106= Il. 18.15, Il. 10.507. Cf. Il. 10.4 : δολιχὸν πλόον Od. 3.169. Cf. Od. 3.151, Od. 4.120= Od. 5.365 = 424, Od. 4.732, 793, 843, Od. 7.83, Od. 18.345, Od. 23.86.
Absol. : ὣς ὁ γέρων ὥρμαινεν Il. 14.20. Cf. Il. 16.435, Il. 21.64, Il. 22.131 : Od. 6.118.
With relative : ὅρμηναν ἅ περ . . . Od. 2.156.
To incite, urge, spur on : ὅρμησέ μʼ ἐς πόλεμον Il. 6.338.
To stir up, bring about : πόλεμον Od. 18.376.

div.head: a
div.p: With genit. of what is attacked : ὁππότε πύργος Ἀχαιῶν Τρώων ὁρμήσειεν Il. 4.335.

div.head: b

p.gloss: To put oneself in act or motion to do something.

div.p: With infin. : ὁσσάκι ὁρμήσειε στῆναι ἐναντίβιον Il. 21.265. Cf. Il. 13.64, Il. 22.194.

To address oneself to motion, take one's way, proceed, speed, start, start up to do something : ὁρμᾶτʼ ἐκ θαλάμοιο Il. 3.142. Cf. Il. 9.178, Il. 13.754, Il. 14.313 : οὐδʼ ὁρμηθέντος ἄκουσα (that he had gone) Od. 4.728. Cf. Od. 4.282, Od. 13.82.
Sim. : ὁρμηθεὶς θεοῦ (starting from (the inspiration of) the god, stirred by the god) Od. 8.499.

In hostile sense, to rush, make a rush, make onslaught, attack : ἐναντίω οἱ ὁρμηθήτην Il. 5.12, δεύτερος ὡρμᾶτʼ ἔγχεϊ 855. Cf. Il. 13.496, 512, 526, 559, 562, Il. 15.529, Il. 16.402, 467, Il. 17.530, 605, Il. 18.269, Il. 19.236, Il. 22.312, Il. 23.817 : Od. 12.126.
With genit. of the person attacked : ὁρμήθη Ἀκάμαντος Il. 14.488. Cf. Il. 21.595.
To make a rush in order to strip a fallen foe : ὡρμήθη μεμαὼς ἀπὸ τεύχεα δῦσαι Il. 13.182, ὁρμηθέντος ἀκόντισεν Il. 13.183. Cf. Il. 13.188, 190.

p.gloss: To put oneself in act or motion to do something.

div.p: With infin. : διώκειν ὁρμήθησαν Il. 10.359. Cf. Il. 8.511.

p.gloss: To be eager to do something.

div.p: With infin. : ἦτόρ οἱ ὁρμᾶτο πτολεμίζειν Il. 21.572.
An inciting, urging, starting : ἐμὴν ποτιδέγμενος ὁρμήν (waiting on the word from me) Il. 10.123, θηρὸς ὑφʼ ὁρμῆς (in terror of the beast) Il. 11.119. Cf. Od. 2.403.
A rush, onset, starting : πυρὸς ὁρμῇ (the rage of the . . .) Il. 11.157 : ὑπὸ κύματος ὁρμῆς (the shock of the . . .) Od. 5.320, μελέη μοι ἔσσεται ὁρμή (my endeavour) 416.
Sim. : ἐς ὁρμὴν ἔγχεος ἐλθεῖν (that I may come within spear-cast of him) Il. 5.118.
In hostile sense, a rush or attack : μόγις μευ ἔκφυγεν ὁρμήν Il. 9.355.
A rush to strip a fallen foe Il. 4.466.
In pl., struggles of war, fighting, battling : Ἑλένης ὁρμήματα (about . . ., for the sake of . . .) Il. 2.356, 590.
To bring (a ship) to anchor, moor (her) Il. 14.77: Od. 3.11, Od. 4.785, Od. 8.55.
To draw up (a ship) on shore Od. 12.317.
A chain worn round the neck Il. 18.401 : Od. 15.460, Od. 18.295.
An anchorage, moorings, a landing-place Il. 1.435 : = Od. 15.497, Od. 13.101.
Dat. pl. ὀρνίθεσσι Il. 17.757 : Od. 22.303. ὄρνισι Il. 7.59.
With a specific name added : ὄρνισιν αἰγυπιοῖσιν Il. 7.59. Cf. Od. 5.51, Od. 19.548.

Distinguished as a bird of omen : ὅ τʼ ἐκ Διὸς ἤλυθεν ὀ. Il. 8.251, ὀ. σφιν ἐπῆλθεν Il. 12.200. Cf. Il. 10.277, Il. 12.218, Il. 13.821 := Od. 15.160 = 525, Od. 2.155, 159, Od. 15.531, Od. 20.242, Od. 24.311.
Applied to a person : μή μοι αὐτὴ ὀ. κακὸς πέλευ Il. 24.219.
Infin. ὀρνύμεναι Il. 17.546. ὀρνύμεν Il. 9.353 : Od. 10.22.
To rouse, startle, cause to flee : [νεβρὸν] ἐξ εὐνῆς Il. 22.190.
To raise, cause to rise or stand up : Ὀδυσῆα ἀπʼ ἐσχαρόφιν Od. 7.169.

To rouse, cause to bestir oneself, incite to action, spur on, urge on, set on, send: Σαρπηδόνα ἐπʼ Ἀργείοισιν Il. 12.293. Cf. Il. 4.439, Il. 5.8, Il. 7.38, Il. 9.539, Il. 10.518, etc. : Od. 3.167, Od. 4.712, Od. 16.154, Od. 21.100, Od. 23.348, 367.

p.gloss: To rouse, incite, set on, to do something.

div.p: With infin. : μάχεσθαι Il. 13.794. Cf. Il. 12.142, Il. 17.273 : Od. 23.222.
With inanimate object : πυρὴν καήμεναι Il. 23.210.

In general, to stir up, bring about, set going, raise, send, inspire : νοῦσον ἀνὰ στρατόν Il. 1.10, ἐν σθένος ὦρσεν ἑκάστῳ Il. 2.451. Cf. Il. 4.16, Il. 8.335, Il. 9.353, 533, Il. 11.53, 544, Il. 13.362, Il. 14.522, Il. 15.718, Il. 17.423, Il. 18.218, Il. 23.14, 108, 153, Il. 24.507 : Od. 3.161, Od. 4.113, 183, Od. 10.457, Od. 17.46, Od. 19.249, Od. 20.346, Od. 23.144, 231.

div.head: II
div.p: In mid., in pf. and plupf. act., and also (Il. 13.78 : Od. 8.539) in redup. aor. act.

To be set in motion, stirred up, raised, to rise, spring up : ὡς ὅτε κῦμα θαλάσσης ὄρνυται Il. 4.423. Cf. Il. 3.13, Il. 5.865, Il. 7.64, Il. 11.151, Il. 14.395, Il. 23.214 : κονίη ἐκ κρατὸς ὀρώρει (rose) Od. 11.600.

To rouse or bestir oneself, address oneself to motion, set to work, speed, rush, be moved, move : ὦρτο διὲκ προθύρου Il. 15.124, ὅτε τʼ ὤρετʼ Ἀχιλλεύς (shook off his inactivity) Il. 22.102. Cf. Il. 2.398, Il. 4.421, Il. 8.474, Il. 19.2, Il. 23.759, etc. : ἐξ οὗ ὤρορʼ ἀοιδός (was moved to song) Od. 8.539. Cf. Od. 1.347, Od. 14.499, Od. 19.377 (is torn), 524, Od. 22.364, Od. 24.496.
Of the limbs : εἰς ὅ κε γούνατʼ ὀρώρῃ (play their part) Il. 9.610= Il. 10.90. Cf. Il. 11.477, Il. 22.388 : Od. 18.133.
Sim. : μένος μοι ὤρορεν (is roused) Il. 13.78. Cf. Il. 11.827.
With infin. indicating a purpose : ὦρτο πόλινδʼ ἴμεν Od. 7.14. Cf. Il. 12.279, Il. 13.62, Il. 23.488 : Od. 2.397.
So of inanimate objects : ὦρτο δʼ ἐπὶ λιγὺς οὖρος ἀήμεναι Od. 3.176. Cf. Il. 14.397.
With fut. pple. : ὦρτʼ ἀγγελέουσα Il. 8.409= Il. 24.77 = 159. Cf. Od. 8.256.
In imp., rouse, bestir yourself (yourselves) ! speed ! up ! come ! come forward ! Il. 3.250, Il. 4.204, 509, Il. 5.109, etc. : Od. 21.141, Od. 22.395.
To stand up or forth : ὤρνυτʼ Ἀγαμέμνων Il. 3.267. Cf. Il. 7.162, 163, Il. 23.288, etc. : Od. 8.111.
To rise or start up from a recumbent or sitting position : ἀπὸ θρόνου ὦρτο Il. 11.645. Cf. Il. 11.2, Il. 24.515 : ὄρνυτʼ ἐξ εὐνῆφιν Od. 2.2. Cf. Od. 3.405, Od. 4.307, Od. 5.2, Od. 8.2, 3, Od. 23.348.

In hostile sense, to rush, make a rush, spring, make onslaught, attack : δεύτερον ὄρνυτο χαλκῷ Il. 3.349. Cf. Il. 5.13, 17 = Il. 16.479, Il. 5.590, Il. 11.129, 343, Il. 17.45, Il. 20.158, 164, Il. 21.248, Il. 23.689.

In general, to be stirred up, brought about, set going, raised, to be on foot, come into being, spring up, rise, be manifested, seen, heard : πόλεμος ἀλίαστος ὄρωρεν (is on foot) Il. 2.797, πολὺς ὀρυμαγδὸς ὀρώρει 810= Il. 8.59 : = Od. 24.70. Cf. Il. 3.87, Il. 4.436, Il. 5.532, Il. 8.135, Il. 9.573, Il. 12.177 (raged), Il. 17.397, Il. 19.363, etc. : Od. 8.343, 380, Od. 10.122, Od. 14.412, 522, Od. 16.98 = 116, 215, Od. 20.267, Od. 22.308, Od. 24.48, 184.
To set in motion, stir up, raise, send : ὀρόθυνον ἐναύλους (bring them down in flood) Il. 21.312 : ἀέλλας Od. 5.292.
To rouse, incite to action, spur on, urge on Il. 10.332, Il. 13.351, Il. 15.572, 595 : Od. 18.407.
[ὀρ-, ὁράω. Cf. οὖρος2, ἐπίουρος, θυραωρός, πυλαωρός.]

To keep an eye on something, watch : ἐπὶ δʼ ἀνὴρ ἐσθλὸς ὀρώρει (superintended the work) Il. 23.112 : ἐπὶ δʼ ἀνέρες ἐσθλοὶ ὄροντο (did watchful service) Od. 3.471, ἐπὶ δʼ ἀνέρες ἐσθλοὶ ὄρονται (tend the flocks) Od. 14.104.
This form as ablative Il. 4.452, Il. 11.493.

A mountain or hill : οὔρεα σκιόεντα Il. 1.157, ἀπʼ Ἰδαίων ὀρέων Il. 8.170. Cf. Il. 2.456, Il. 3.34, Il. 4.452, Il. 12.146, Il. 13.17, etc. : Od. 2.147, Od. 3.287, Od. 5.283, Od. 6.102, Od. 8.569, Od. 11.243, etc.
To rush, speed, spring, dart : ἐς δίφρον ὀρούσας Il. 11.359, 743. Cf. Il. 2.310, Il. 12.83, Il. 20.327, Il. 21.182, Il. 24.80.
Of an inanimate object : ἐκ κλῆρος ὄρουσεν (jumped out) Il. 3.325.
Of the flight or course of a weapon Il. 13.505= Il. 16.615, Il. 21.593.
Of sleep : ἐφʼ ὕπνος ὄρουσεν Il. 23.232.
In hostile sense, to rush, spring, make onslaught, attack : ἐν πρῶτος ὄρουσεν Il. 11.92, 217. Cf. Il. 14.401, Il. 15.726, Il. 16.258, 430.
Of a beast of prey Il. 15.635.
Reeds used for thatching, thatch : ὄροφον ἀμήσαντες Il. 24.451.
A branch : ἐρινεὸν τάμνεν ὄρπηκας (double acc. of whole and part) Il. 21.38.
A back or subsidiary door (in the passages cited app. giving access from the μέγαρον to the λαύρη) Od. 22.126, 132, 333.
Formed by digging : τάφρον Il. 8.179, Il. 9.67, Il. 10.198, Il. 20.49. Cf. Il. 12.72, Il. 15.344, Il. 16.369.
A sound or noise : δρυτόμων ἀνδρῶν Il. 16.633.
A noise or din caused by clashing or striking : ὀρυμαγδὸν φιτρῶν καὶ λάων Il. 21.313. Cf. Od. 9.235.
In reference to a river, a roaring or rushing Il. 21.256.
Din, noise, shouting, tumult : πολύς Il. 2.810= Il. 8.59, Il. 4.449= Il. 8.63, Il. 10.185 : Od. 24.70.– A din, noise, shouting, tumult : ἀνιηθεὶς ὀρυμαγδῷ Od. 1.133. Cf. Il. 17.424, 741.
With the notion of noise obscured : ἐρύεσθαι ὑπὸ Τρώων ὀρυμαγδοῦ (from the hands of the . . .) Il. 9.248. Cf. Il. 10.539, Il. 17.461.
To form by digging, dig : τάφρον Il. 7.341, 440 : Od. 21.120, βόθρον Od. 10.517, Od. 11.25.
To dig up, get out of the ground Od. 10.305.
Orphan, fatherless Il. 6.432, Il. 11.394.–ἦμαρ ὀρφανικόν. See ἦμαρ 4 (j).
Orphan, deprived of one's parents : ἐλίποντο ὀρφαναὶ ἐν μεγάροισιν Od. 20.68.
A leader or chief. Applied to heroes Il. 2.837, Il. 6.99, Il. 14.102, Il. 17.12, etc. : Od. 3.400, Od. 4.156, Od. 10.538, Od. 15.167, etc.
=ὀρχηστήρ. : ὀρχηστήν περ ἐόντα (tauntingly in reference to the agility of Meriones) Il. 16.617. Cf. Il. 24.261.
Dancing, the dance Od. 1.152, 421= Od. 18.304, Od. 17.605
Dancing, skill in the dance : ὅσσον περιγιγνόμεθʼ ἄλλων ὀρχηστυῖ Od. 8.253. Cf. Il. 13.731.
Dat. pl. fem. ᾗς Il. 2.341, etc. ᾗσι Il. 5.54, etc. : Od. 6.272, etc.

div.head: I
div.p: Demonstrative pronoun, he, etc. οὐδʼ οἳ ἄναρχοι ἔσαν Il. 2.703. Cf. Il. 6.59, Il. 21.198, etc. : Od. 4.389, 653.

div.head: a
div.p: ὃς Χρύσην ἀμφιβέβηκας Il. 1.37, ᾧ ἔπι πολλὰ μόγησα 162, ἄντυγες αἳ περὶ δίφρον [ἦσαν] Il. 11.535. Cf. Il. 1.94, 289, 603, 604, Il. 2.73, etc. : Od. 1.1, 54, 69, 108, 161, 191, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: With τε: οἵ τε θέμιστας εἰρύαται Il. 1.238. Cf. Il. 1.86, Il. 2.470, etc. : Od. 1.52, Od. 4.826, Od. 5.4, etc.

In causal sense : τόδε μέγʼ ἄριστον ἔρεξεν, ὃς τὸν λωβητῆρʼ ἔσχʼ ἀγοράων (seeing that he has . . ., for he has . . .) Il. 2.275. Cf. Il. 5.403, Il. 8.34, Il. 12.235, Il. 16.204, Il. 22.236, etc. : Od. 1.8, Od. 4.724, Od. 9.274, Od. 10.338, Od. 12.281, Od. 18.114, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: With subj., pure or with κεν: τιμὴν ἀποτινέμεν, ἥ τε καὶ ἐσσομένοισι μετʼ ἀνθρώποισι πέληται Il. 3.287, κλητοὺς ὀτρύνομεν, οἵ κʼ ἔλθωσι Il. 9.165. Cf. Il. 21.127, etc. : Od. 4.29, Od. 13.400, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: With subj. or opt. in relative sentences corresponding to sentences with εἰ 4. For the examples and constructions see Table at end II.B.a 2, (D) (4) (16).
In conditional relative sentences. See Table III.B.a 1 2 (3),

div.head: b
div.p: With subj. in similes : ἀστέρʼ, ὅς τε μάλιστα λαμπρὸν παμφαίνῃσιν Il. 5.5. Cf. Il. 10.184, Il. 16.387, etc. : Od. 13.31, etc.

In object clauses : γνώσῃ ὅς θʼ ἡγεμόνων κακὸς ὅς τέ νυ λαῶν, ἠδʼ ὅς κʼ ἐσθλὸς ἔησιν Il. 2.365. Cf. Il. 7.171, Il. 20.21, Il. 21.609, Il. 23.498, etc. : οὐδέ τι οἶδα οἵ τʼ ἐσάωθεν οἵ τʼ ἀπόλοντο Od. 3.185. Cf. Od. 2.156, Od. 8.576, Od. 10.110, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: In or at the place or spot in which, in or at which place or spot, where : ᾗ ῥʼ ἴδε γυμνωθέντα βραχίονα Il. 12.389. Cf. Il. 12.33, Il. 13.53, 679, Il. 15.448, 616, Il. 16.377, Il. 20.275, Il. 22.324, Il. 23.420: χῶρον, ᾗ οἱ πέφραδʼ ὑφορβόν Od. 14.2.

div.head: b
div.p: Whither : ὄφρʼ ἀφίκοντο, ᾗ μιν ἀνώγει Il. 13.329. Cf. Il. 6.41, Il. 21.4 : Od. 12.81.
With subj. in a conditional relative sentence. See Table (III) (D) (26).

div.head: c
div.p: In such way or manner as, as : ᾗ τελέει περ Il. 8.415. Cf. Il. 9.310.
With subj. in conditional relative sentences. See Table (III) (D) (31) (34).

div.head: a
div.p: Because, since, seeing that, in that : χωσαμένη ὃ . . . Il. 9.534. Cf. Il. 9.564, Il. 13.166, Il. 20.283, Il. 21.150, etc. : Od. 1.382, Od. 2.45, Od. 4.206, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: That, how : λεύσσετε τό γε πάντες ὅ μοι γέρας ἔρχεται ἄλλῃ Il. 1.120. Cf. Il. 5.433, Il. 8.32, 362, Il. 9.493, etc. : Od. 3.146, Od. 4.771, Od. 12.295, Od. 13.340, etc.
In neut. pl. ἅ with τε, in such manner as, as : ἅ τε παρθένος ἠΐθεός τʼ ὀαρίζετον Il. 22.127.
In neut. ὅ with prepositions in temporal expressions.

div.head: a
div.p: With opt. : τεύχοιμι διαμπερές, εἰς ὅ κʼ Ἴλιον ἕλοιεν Il. 15.70.

div.head: β
div.p: With subj. in conditional relative sentences. See Table at end III.B.a 2, (D) (2).

div.head: α
div.p: From the time when, since (cf. ἐκ (II) 12.a) : ἐξ οὗ διαστήτην (taking up the tale from the point when . . .) Il. 1.6. Cf. Il. 8.295, Il. 13.778, Il. 24.638, 766 : ἐξ οὗ ἔβη Od. 2.27. Cf. Od. 2.90, Od. 11.168, Od. 16.142, Od. 18.181, etc.

div.head: β
div.p: Since which time : ἐξ οὖ κενταύροισι καὶ ἀνδράσι νεῖκος ἐτύχθη Od. 21.303.
That which is right or permitted.
With infin. : οὐδʼ ὁσίη κακὰ ῥάπτειν ἀλλήλοισιν Od. 16.423. Cf. Od. 22.412.

Such in number, quantity or volume as, as many or much as, such as : ὅσοι θεοί εἰσʼ ἐν Ὀλύμπῳ (all the gods in . . .) Il. 1.566 (θεοί attracted into the relative clause), ὅσοι οὐ βουλῆς ἐπάκουσαν Il. 2.143, ἀγηγέραθʼ ὅσσοι ἄριστοι [ἦσαν] (as many as were . . ., the whole number of the . . .) Il. 4.211. Cf. Il. 2.125, 249 (of all who . . .), 468, 681, Il. 3.57, Il. 5.267, Il. 9.55 (of all the . . .), 401, etc. : Od. 1.11, 278, Od. 2.209, Od. 3.108, 186, 312, Od. 7.68 (of all the women who . . .), Od. 8.36, 214 (in all contests that are practised), Od. 11.329, Od. 12.86, etc.
With subj. or opt. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table at end III.B.a 1 2 (3), (D) (12) (13) (14) (56).

In reference to magnitude or extent, of such magnitude, size, extent or importance as: ὅσον τʼ ἐπὶ λᾶαν ἵησιν (as far as . . .) Il. 3.12, ὅση δύναμίς γε πάρεστιν (as far as my strength goes) Il. 8.294. Cf. Il. 2.616, Il. 7.451, Il. 8.213, Il. 10.351, Il. 17.368, Il. 23.190, etc. : τοῦ ὅσον τʼ ὄργυιαν ἀπέκοψα (i.e. τόσον ὅση ὄργυια γίγνεται) Od. 9.325, ὅσον τʼ ἐπὶ ἥμισυ (i.e. ἐφʼ ὅσον τὸ ἥμισυ γίγνεται) Od. 13.114. Cf. Od. 9.322, Od. 10.113, 517, etc.
With subj. : ὅσσον τίς τʼ ἔδαφος νηὸς τορνώσεται Od. 5.249.
With infin. in this sense Od. 5.484 (such a thing as might . . .).
In causal sense (= ὅτι τόσος) : κεχολωμένοι ὅσσοι ὄλοντο (because so many . . .) Il. 16.546. Cf. Il. 24.630 : Od. 4.75, Od. 22.46.

In object clauses, how many, who, what, how much, how great : οὐδέ τι οἶδε πένθεος, ὅσσον ὄρωρεν Il. 11.658. Cf. Il. 2.492, etc. : μυθεόμην ὅσʼ ἐμόγησεν Od. 4.152. Cf. Od. 3.105, Od. 4.241, Od. 10.45, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: To such an extent as, as greatly as, as much as, as far as : ὅσσον γιγνώσκω Il. 13.222. Cf. Il. 5.860 (as loudly as . . .), Il. 9.177, Il. 23.327, etc.: Od. 3.395, Od. 7.108, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to distance, as far as : ὅσσον ἀνὴρ ἴδεν Il. 5.770. Cf. Il. 9.354 (and no further), Il. 23.517, etc. : Od. 5.400, Od. 8.229, Od. 16.290, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: In object clauses, to how great an extent, how much, how greatly : ὅσσον φέρτερός εἰμι Il. 1.186. Cf. Il. 1.516, etc. : Od. 7.327, Od. 8.102, etc.
A rumour or report Od. 1.282, Od. 2.216.
With opt. in conditional relative sentences (with τοσσάκι as correlative). See Table at end III.B.b 1.
How much. In causal sense : ὁσσάτιον ἀπώλεσε λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν (seeing that he has smitten so much . . .) Il. 5.758.
neut. dual. The eyes, one's eyes : ὄσσε οἱ πυρὶ ἐΐκτην Il. 1.104. Cf. Il. 1.200, Il. 3.427, Il. 4.461, Il. 11.453, Il. 13.3, etc. : Od. 4.186, 704, Od. 5.151, Od. 12.232, Od. 13.401, etc.
In reference to lions : ὄσσε καλύπτων Il. 17.136 : ἔν οἱ ὄσσε δαίεται Od. 6.131.
With quasi-cognate acc. : κάκʼ ὀσσόμενος (looking bale, with baleful look) Il. 1.105.
To look at, look for : ὀσσόμενος πατέρʼ ἐνὶ φρεσίν (keeping his father's image before his mind's eye) Od. 1.115.
Of something inanimate : πέλαγος, ὀσσόμενον ἀνέμων κέλευθα (watching for, biding) Il. 14.17.
To bode, portend, betoken : κακὸν ὀσσομένη Il. 24.172. Cf. Od. 2.152.
To bode, forbode, have a presentiment of, apprehend : κάκʼ ὄσσετο θυμός Od. 10.374. Cf. Od. 18.154.
Locative ὀστεόφι Od. 16.145. This form as ablative Od. 14.134.
As genit. (or perh. as instrumental of material; see below) Od. 12.45.

A bone : πέρησεν ὀ. αἰχμή Il. 4.460. Cf. Il. 4.174, Il. 5.67, Il. 7.334, Il. 11.97, Il. 12.185, etc. : πολὺς ἀμφʼ ὀστεόφιν θίς (there is a great heap of bones; or perh., taking ὀστεόφιν as instrumental of material, a heap (is made) of bones) Od. 12.45. Cf. Od. 1.161, Od. 5.426, Od. 9.293, Od. 11.219, Od. 18.96, etc.
In pl., the osseous bodily framework as typifying the body : λίπʼ ὀστέα θυμός Il. 12.386, Il. 16.743, Il. 20.406 : Od. 12.414. Cf. Od. 11.221.
In reference to an animal Od. 3.455.
Nom. sing. masc. ὅτις Il. 3.279, Il. 19.260, etc. : Od. 1.47, Od. 2.350, Od. 5.445, etc. The two elements separated by an enclitic ὅ κέν τις Od. 16.257.
Genit. sing. neut. ὅτευ Od. 17.421, Od. 19.77. ὅττεο Od. 1.124, Od. 22.377. ὅττευ Od. 17.121.
Dat. sing. masc. ὅτεῳ Il. 12.428, Il. 15.664 : Od. 2.114.
Acc. sing. masc. ὅτινα Od. 8.204, Od. 15.395.
Nom. pl. neut. ὅτινα Il. 22.450 (else-where ἅσσα q.v.).

Who, which, with an indefinite force, whoever (whatever) he (it) may be: θεοπρόπιον ὅ τι οἶσθα Il. 1.85, τίπτʼ ἀλᾶσθε, ὅ τι δὴ χρειὼ τόσον ἵκει; (on what account do you wander thus, in respect of which . . .?) Il. 10.142. Cf. Il. 3.286, Il. 5.175, Il. 21.103, Il. 23.43, etc. : ἥ τις σύ πέρ ἐσσι θεάων Od. 4.376. Cf. Od. 2.114, Od. 5.445, Od. 7.150, Od. 8.550, Od. 17.53, etc.
With τε Il. 23.43 : Od. 2.114 cited above.
With final force : ὄνομʼ εὕρεο ὅττι κε θῆαι Od. 19.403. Cf. Il. 17.640 : Od. 16.257.

div.head: a
div.p: With subj. in relative sentences corresponding to sentences with εἰ 4. For the examples and constructions see Table at end II.B.a 1, (D) (6).

div.head: b
div.p: With subj. or opt. in conditional relative sentences. See Table II.B.b, III.B.a 1 2 (5),b.1, C.a.5, (D) (12) (13) (14) (15) (17) (19) (20) (26) (28) (29) (45) (54) (55) (56) (57) (58) (61).

In object clauses, who, what : ὅς κʼ εἴποι ὅ τι τόσσον ἐχώσατο (why) Il. 1.64, ἔσπετε οἵ τινες ἡγεμόνες ἦσαν Il. 2.487. Cf. Il. 3.192, Il. 10.503, Il. 11.612, Il. 14.195, Il. 16.424, etc. : Od. 1.124, 401, Od. 3.16, Od. 4.61, Od. 7.17, Od. 8.28, Od. 22.450, etc.

div.head: α
div.p: ὅτε Τρώεσσιν ἐν ἀγρομένοισιν ἔμιχθεν Il. 3.209. Cf. Il. 1.397, Il. 2.303, 471, etc. : Od. 1.16, Od. 2.314 (now that I am . . .), Od. 3.180, Od. 4.145, etc.

div.head: β
div.p: So ᾔδεα μὲν ὅτε . . . οἶδα δὲ νῦν ὅτε . . . (I knew what it meant when . . .) Il. 14.71 : ἦ οὐκ οἶσθʼ ὅτε . . .; (what happened when . . .) Od. 16.424.

div.head: γ
div.p: Introducing similes : ὡς ὅτε . . . Il. 2.209, Il. 3.33, Il. 4.275, etc. : Od. 5.432, Od. 12.251, Od. 13.31, etc.– ὡς ὅτʼ ἂν . . . Il. 12.41 : Od. 10.410.

div.head: α
div.p: ὅτʼ ἄν with subj. like 1.a.β ὄφρα ἰδῇ (ἰδῇς) ὅτʼ ἂν ᾧ (σῷ) πατρὶ μάχηται (μάχηαι) (i.e. what it is to fight with . . .) Il. 8.406, 420.

div.head: β
div.p: With subj. in a relative sentence corresponding to sentences with εἰ 4. See Table at end II.B.a 1.

div.head: γ
div.p:
With fut., subj. or opt. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table III.B.a 1 2 (3),
b.1.2.3, C.a.6, (D) (9) (12) (17) (20) (26) (32) (34) (35) (37) (45) (51) (52) (54) (55) (56) (57) (58).

div.head: δ
div.p: With subj. introducing similes : ὡς ὅτε Il. 2.147, Il. 4.130, 141, Il. 5.597, Il. 6.506, etc. : Od. 5.328, Od. 6.232= Od. 23.159, Od. 9.391, Od. 19.518, Od. 20.25.

div.head: ε
div.p: With πρίν with subj. and ἄν or opt. See πρίν 6.b 6.c
Against the time when : ποτιδέγμενον ἀγγελίην, ὅτʼ ἀποφθιμένοιο πύθηται (waiting for the tidings which shall tell him that . . .) Il. 19.337.
At which time, when : ἔσσεται ἦμαρ ὅτʼ ἄν ποτʼ ὀλώλῃ Ἴλιος Il. 4.164. Cf. Il. 2.351, Il. 8.373 (the day will come when . . .), 475, etc. : Od. 18.272.
So ἦ οὐ μέμνῃ ὅτε . . . (the time when . . . how . . .) Il. 15.18, Il. 20.188, Il. 21.396 : Od. 24.115.– εἰς ὅτε κε . . . (against the time when . . .) Od. 2.99= Od. 19.144= Od. 24.134.
When, after that, as soon as : ὅτε δὴ σχεδὸν ἦσαν Il. 3.15. Cf. Il. 1.432, 493, Il. 6.191, etc. : Od. 1.332, Od. 3.269, 286, etc.
Since, from the time when : ἐμοὶ χλαῖναι καὶ ῥήγεα ἤχθεθʼ, ὅτε κρήτης ὄρεα νοσφισάμην Od. 19.338. Cf. Il. 21.81, 156 : Od. 24.288.
While : ὅτε δή ῥʼ ἐπὶ νῆʼ ᾔομεν, τόφρα . . . Od. 10.569.
When, whereas : ὅτε τʼ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσιν Od. 12.22.
Since, seeing that : ὅτʼ ὀνείδεα βάζεις Od. 17.461. Cf. Od. 13.129.
ὅτε μή without expressed vb., unless, except : ὅτε μὴ διὶ πατρί Il. 16.227.
With ἄλλοτε. See ἄλλοτε 2.–ὁτέ alone, at another time, again Il. 16.690, Il. 17.178.

Because, since, seeing that, in that : ὅτι ῥα θνῄσκοντας ὁρᾶτο Il. 1.56. Cf. Il. 2.255, Il. 5.326, Il. 14.407, Il. 16.35, Il. 21.411, etc. : ὅττι μιν ὣς ὑπέδεκτο Od. 14.52. Cf. Od. 5.340, Od. 8.238, Od. 15.342, Od. 22.36, Od. 23.115, etc.
That : οὐδέ μιν ἠγνοίησεν ὅτι . . . Il. 1.537. Cf. Il. 5.349, Il. 6.231, Il. 7.448, etc. : οὐκ ἀΐεις ὅτι . . .; Od. 18.11. Cf. Od. 13.314, Od. 16.131, etc.
Quickly, featly, deftly : δεῖπνον ἔθηκας Il. 19.317. Cf. Il. 3.260 : Od. 19.100.
Deft, rendering ready service Il. 1.321, Il. 6.381 : Od. 1.109, Od. 4.23 = 217, Od. 4.38.
A summons : ἄλλην ὀτρυντὺν ποτιδέγμενος Il. 19.234. Cf. Il. 19.235.
Genit. sing. masc. pple. ὀτρύναντος Il. 10.356, Il. 15.744.

To rouse to action, urge on, stir up, set on, encourage, urge, press, incite, exhort, summon, call upon, dispatch, send, to do something or to proceed somewhither for some purpose : ὀτρύνων πόλεμόνδε Il. 2.589, πυμάτας ὤτρυνε φάλαγγας Il. 4.254. Cf. Il. 3.249, Il. 4.73, Il. 10.38 (to play the . . .), 356, Il. 15.59, Il. 19.349, Il. 24.143, etc. : Od. 1.85, Od. 2.74, Od. 6.254, Od. 11.226, Od. 15.37, Od. 17.75, Od. 22.241, Od. 24.405, etc.
To rouse or stir (a person's spirit) : ὄτρυνε μένος ἑκάστου Il. 5.470. Cf. Il. 5.563, Il. 12.266, etc. : Od. 8.15.

With infin. : ἰέναι Il. 2.94, μάχεσθαι Il. 4.294, ἀνδρῶν δυσμενέων δῦναι στρατόν Il. 10.220. Cf. Il. 5.496, Il. 16.495, Il. 17.654, Il. 23.49, Il. 24.24, etc. : Od. 2.244, Od. 8.90, Od. 9.518, Od. 14.261, Od. 18.61, etc.
With fut. pple. : ἀγγελέουσαν Il. 8.398= Il. 11.185. Cf. Il. 19.156 : Od. 15.40.
To hasten on, speed, bring about : πομπήν Od. 7.151, Od. 11.357. Cf. Od. 2.253.
To send, cause to appear : εἴδωλον Od. 11.214.
To dispatch or send (a message) Od. 16.355.
To press for, urge one's claim to, importune for : πομπήν Od. 8.30.
In mid., to rouse oneself to action, take action, to put oneself in motion, bestir oneself, set oneself, get ready, to do something : ὑμεῖς ὀτρύνεσθαι ἅμʼ ἠοῖ Od. 7.222.
With infin. : ὀτρύνοντο νέκυς ἀγέμεν Il. 7.420. Cf. Il. 14.369 : Od. 10.425, Od. 17.183.
Before a vowel οὐκ (οὐχ). Also οὐκί Od. 238, Il. 15.137, etc.: Od. 1.268, Od. 11.493, etc. οὐχί Il. 15.716, Il. 16.762.
Negative particle, commonly denying a predication (cf. μή).
In gen. negation : τὴν οὐ λύσω Il. 1.29. Cf. Il. 1.24, 152, Il. 2.2, 238, etc. : οὐκ οἶδα Od. 1.216. Cf. Od. 1.42, 236, Od. 3.14, Od. 24.29, etc.
Repeated Il. 1.114, Il. 23.43, etc. : Od. 3.27, etc.
With participles Il. 4.224, Il. 7.185, etc. : Od. 2.50, Od. 11.66, etc.
With adjectives, adverbs or adverbial expressions Il. 2.214, Il. 5.366, Il. 8.360, etc. : Od. 2.251, Od. 4.846, Od. 17.153, etc.
Not merely negativing a verb but expressing the opposite meaning. See ἐάω 4, ἐθέλω 3, φημί 6.

div.head: a
div.p: With indic. when the protasis precedes the apodosis (the only exception to the rule being Od. 9.410) : εἰ δέ τοι οὐ δώσει ἑὸν ἄγγελον, . . . Il. 24.296. Cf. Il. 4.160, Il. 15.162, Il. 20.129 : Od. 2.274, Od. 12.382, Od. 13.144.
For the converse construction see μή 6.c.

div.head: b
div.p: With subj. : εἰ δʼ ἂν ἐμοὶ τιμὴν τίνειν οὐκ ἐθέλωσιν, . . . Il. 3.289. Cf. Il. 20.139.

div.head: a
div.p: With subj. : ὅτινας οὐκ ἐθέλῃσιν . . . Il. 15.492.

div.head: b
div.p: With indic. : ὅσοι οὐ βουλῆς ἐπάκουσαν Il. 2.143. Cf. Il. 7.236, Il. 18.363, etc. : Od. 3.349.
After μή (cf. οὐδέ 6, οὐκέτι 3) : μὴ χόλον οὐκ ἐρύσαιτο Il. 24.584. Cf. Il. 1.28, 566, Il. 10.39.
With infin. after vbs. of saying, thinking, etc. : ἅ τινʼ οὐ πείσεσθαι ὀΐω Il. 1.289. Cf. Il. 17.174, etc. : Od. 3.28, Od. 5.342, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: In questions expecting an affirmative answer : οὐ νεμεσίζῃ; Il. 5.872. Cf. Il. 2.194, Il. 7.448, etc. : Od. 1.60, Od. 2.312, Od. 5.23, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: With opt. and ἄν in questions constituting a form of polite or affectionate imperative : οὐκ ἂν δή μοι ἐφοπλίσσειας ἀπήνην; Od. 6.57. Cf. Il. 3.52, Il. 5.32, Il. 10.204, etc. : Od. 7.22.

div.head: α
div.p: In no way, not at all, by no means Il. 1.224, Il. 3.306, Il. 12.270, Il. 14.143, etc. : Od. 8.540, Od. 12.208, Od. 16.143, etc.

div.head: β
div.p: In reference to the future Od. 5.358, Od. 10.174.

div.head: c
div.p: οὔ πώ ποτε, οὐ . . . πώ ποτε, never yetIl. 1.106, 154, Il. 3.442, Il. 14.315 : Od. 12.98, Od. 21.123, Od. 23.328.

div.head: d
div.p: οὔ πως, οὐ . . . πως, in no wise, not at all, by no meansIl. 4.158, Il. 7.217, Il. 12.65, Il. 13.114, Il. 14.63, etc. : Od. 2.130, Od. 5.103, Od. 11.158, Od. 15.49, Od. 16.196, etc.

div.head: α
div.p: οὔ τις, οὔ τι, οὐ . . . τις, οὐ . . . τι, no one, nothing : οὔ τις σοὶ χεῖρας ἐποίσει Il. 1.88, τῶν οὐκ ἄν τι φέροις 301. Cf. Il. 1.271, 511, 547, 562, Il. 3.365, Il. 5.475, Il. 7.197, etc. : Od. 2.121, 191, 199, 411, Od. 3.192, Od. 4.106, Od. 5.11, Od. 6.176, etc.
With sb., no : οὔ τις ἀνήρ Il. 13.222. Cf. Il. 5.761, Il. 18.192, etc. : Od. 10.202, Od. 13.423, etc.–

div.head: β
div.p: οὔ τι, οὐ . . . τι as adv., in no wise, not at all : οὔ τί μοι αἴτιοί εἰσιν Il. 1.153, οὐ μὲν γάρ τι καταθνητός γε τέτυκτο Il. 5.402. Cf. Il. 1.588, Il. 2.338, Il. 3.11, Il. 4.286, Il. 6.102, etc. : Od. 1.75, 78, 173, Od. 2.235, 240, 282, Od. 3.367, Od. 4.199, etc.
Dat. pl. οὔασι Il. 12.442. ὠσί Od. 12.200.
An ear or handle of a drinking vessel (cf. ὠτώεις) Il. 11.633.

The surface of the earth, the earth, the ground : ὕπτιος οὔδει ἐρείσθη Il. 7.145. Cf. Il. 11.749, Il. 12.448, Il. 14.468, Il. 16.612, Il. 23.283, etc. : Od. 8.376, Od. 9.135, 242, 459, Od. 13.395, Od. 22.269, 467.
A floor or pavement : πέπλον κατέχευεν πατρὸς ἐπʼ οὔδει Il. 5.734= Il. 8.385. Cf. Il. 24.527 : Od. 23.46.
To the ground : οὐ. πελάσσαι Od. 10.440. Cf. Il. 17.457.
Negative particle, in general use corresponding to οὐ as μηδέ to μή.

Adversatively, but not, yet not (cf. δέ 1) : βάλεν, οὐδʼ ἔρρηξεν χαλκός Il. 3.348. Cf. Il. 2.419, 753, Il. 3.302, Il. 4.127, 477, Il. 5.621, etc. : Od. 2.182, Od. 3.143, Od. 4.675, Od. 5.81, Od. 8.344, Od. 9.230, etc.
In continuation, and not, nor (cf. δέ 2) : ὃν ἠτίμησʼ Ἀγαμέμνων, οὐδʼ ἀπέλυσε θύγατρα Il. 1.95. Cf. Il. 1.97, 170, 173, 220, 330, 406, etc. : Od. 1.166, 296, 410, Od. 2.36, 82, 203, 296, etc.

Preceded by a negative, nor (sometimes rather to be translated or) : οὐ δέμας οὐδὲ φυήν Il. 1.115. Cf. Il. 1.132, 154, 155, 160, 181, 262, etc. : οὔ τι νοήμονες οὐδὲ δίκαιοι Od. 2.282. Cf. Od. 2.44, 63, 185, 210, 270, Od. 4.201, 240, Od. 6.201, etc.
Not even : οὐδέ με τυτθὸν ἔτεισεν Il. 1.354, οὐδʼ οἳ τόσοι ἦσαν Il. 3.190, ὅ γʼ ἄρʼ οὐδὲ θεὸν μέγαν ἅζετο Il. 5.434. Cf. Il. 4.387, Il. 9.351, etc. : Od. 1.6, 18, Od. 3.115, Od. 12.62, etc.
Preceded by a negative : οὔ τις . . . οὐδʼ ἢν . . . Il. 1.90, οὐκέτʼ ἔπειτα . . . οὐδʼ ἠβαιόν Il. 2.380. Cf. Il. 2.489, Il. 3.443, etc. : Od. 1.204, Od. 2.118, Od. 3.14, etc.
To be translated neither : οὐδὲ γὰρ αὐτῷ ὕπνος ἐπὶ βλεφάροισιν ἐφίζανεν Il. 10.25. Cf. Il. 16.852, etc. : οὐδʼ ὄπιθεν κακὸς ἔσσεαι Od. 2.270. Cf. Od. 17.273, etc.
Reechoing a negative for emphasis (cf. μηδέ 5) : οὐ μὰν οὐδʼ Ἀχιλεὺς μάρναται Il. 4.512, etc. : οὐ μέν σʼ οὐδὲ ἐῶσι κλαίειν Od. 4.805. Cf. Od. 5.212, Od. 8.159, etc.
After μή: μὴ ματήσετον, οὐδʼ ἐθέλητον . . . Il. 5.233. Cf. Il. 15.164, Il. 24.569.
With infin. : ἐπεὶ οὐδέ σε πεισέμεν οἴω Il. 5.252, etc. Cf. Od. 13.335, etc.

Giving a reason or explanation, for not (cf. δέ 3) : οὐδέ τί που ἴδμεν ξυνήϊα κείμενα πολλά Il. 1.124, οὐδέ τί πω σάφα ἴδμεν Il. 2.252. Cf. Il. 6.360, Il. 9.613, Il. 12.113, Il. 16.60, etc. : Od. 2.369, Od. 3.23, Od. 9.143, Od. 11.463, Od. 13.238, etc.
Sim. with γάρ : οὐδὲ γὰρ ἡμετέρῃ βραδυτῆτι Τρῶες . . . Il. 19.411.
With ἐπεί: ἐπεὶ οὐδὲ ἔοικεν (for it is not fitting) Il. 1.119. Cf. Il. 5.252, Il. 17.270, etc.
Introducing a negative principal clause after a temporal protasis (cf. δέ 4) : ὅτε δὴ . . . οὐδὲ μὲν εὕδοντας εὗρον Il. 10.181. Cf. Od. 10.18.

Repeated, the first connecting in one of the foregoing constructions with what precedes and the second attaching itself to a particular word : οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδʼ οἳ ἄναρχοι ἔσαν Il. 2.703, 726, οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδὲ Τρῶας εἴασεν εὕδειν (did not let them sleep either) Il. 10.299. Cf. Il. 17.24, etc. : οὐδέ κεν ἄλλως οὐδὲ θεὸς τεύξειεν Od. 8.176, οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδʼ ἔνθεν περ ἀπήμονας ἦγον ἑταίρους (not even thence) Od. 10.551.

Repeated for emphasis : οὐδὲ γὰρ οὐδέ κεν αὐτὸς ὑπέκφυγε κῆρα (not even he) Il. 5.22, ἐπεὶ οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδὲ ἔοικε . . . (for of a surety it is not seemly) Il. 12.212, οὐδὲ γὰρ οὐδʼ ἐμέ φημι λελασμένον ἔμμεναι ἀλκῆς (neither do I . . .) Il. 13.269. Cf. Il. 6.130, Il. 18.117 : οὐδὲ γὰρ οὐδέ τις ἄλλος . . . (for never yet did . . .) Od. 8.32, Od. 10.327. Cf. Od. 21.319.
Not any, no : κτέρας Il. 10.216. Cf. Il. 22.513 : Od. 4.350= Od. 17.141.
Absol. in masc., no one : οὐδενὶ εἴκων Il. 22.459 := Od. 11.515.
In neut., nothing : οὐδὲν ἐοργώς Od. 22.318. Cf. Od. 9.34, Od. 18.130.

In neut. as adv., not at all, in no wise, by no means : οὐ. ἔτεισας Il. 1.244. Cf. Il. 1.412= Il. 16.274, Il. 22.332, Il. 24.370 : Od. 4.195, 248, Od. 9.287, Od. 11.563, Od. 19.264, Od. 20.366, Od. 22.370.
Not worth caring for, not worth a thought Il. 8.178.
Opposed to οὐ πρό, nor asideIl. 14.18 (v.l. οὐδʼ ἑτέρωσε. See ἑτέρωσε).

A threshold, a block or row of blocks standing more or less above the surrounding level and forming the lower part of a
doorway or gateway, in the case of the μέγαρον raised considerably and of considerable width, and so affording room for sitting or standing (see αὔλειος, λάϊνος, μέλινος 2, χάλκεος) : ἔστη ἐτʼ οὐδὸν ἰών Il. 6.375. Cf. Il. 9.404, 582 : τὸν κατʼ οὐδοῦ βάντα προσηύδα Πηνελόπεια Od. 4.680 (no doubt the threshold of the μέγαρον.

App. he has followed the suitors into the μ., and as he is coming out again P. sees him from her quarters, addresses him, and comes down (cf. 760) to speak to him), ἐπʼ οὐδοῦ ἶζε θαλάμοιο 718 (app., a block of wood or stone at the foot of the stairs leading to the θ. (P. is below; cf. 760)), ἐς μυχὸν ἐξ οὐδοῦ Od. 7.87, ὑπʼ αὐλῆς οὐδόν 130 (= οὐδὸν αὔλειον). Cf. Od. 7.135, Od. 10.62; Od. 17.575 (sc. θαλάμοιο; see 506), Od. 18.17, Od. 21.43, Od. 22.2, etc.
A verge or edge ascribed to the gulf of Tartarus Il. 8.15.

Fig. : γήραος οὐ., app. not so much the threshold as the stage of old age, old age itself (the threshold being thought of as within the room as in Od. 17.339) Il. 22.60, Il. 24.487 : Od. 15.246, 348, Od. 23.212.
The udder of an animal Od. 9.440.
Fig, in reference to richness of soil : Ἄργος, οὖθαρ ἀρούρης Il. 9.141= 283.
In general use corresponding to οὐ as μηκέτι to μή.

In reference to the present or past, no more, no longer : ἔνθʼ ἐμοὶ οὐκέτʼ ἐρητύετο θυμός Il. 9.462, οὐκέτι δῶρʼ ἐτέλεσσαν (i.e. they changed their minds) 598, οὐκέτι δύναμαι παρμενέμεν Il. 15.399. Cf. Il. 13.515, 701, 761, Il. 15.727= Il. 16.102, Il. 17.238, 603, 623, Il. 19.343, Il. 21.391, Il. 22.384 : Od. 1.189, 297, Od. 3.241, Od. 4.12, Od. 5.153, Od. 11.456, Od. 12.205, 223 (i.e. he gave up the idea), Od. 15.23, Od. 18.215, Od. 20.137, Od. 22.226, etc.

Indicating the reaching of a limit, point, pitch : Ἀχαιΐδες, οὐκέτʼ Ἀχαιοί (whom I can now no longer call . . .) Il. 2.235, Il. 7.96, μαίνεται οὐκέτʼ ἀνεκτῶς (he has come to the point of being unbearable) Il. 8.355. Cf. Il. 4.539, Il. 7.357, Il. 8.427, Il. 9.164, Il. 10.118, Il. 11.610, Il. 12.73, 231= Il. 18.285, Il. 13.116 : οὐκέτι καλὰ διὲκ μεγάροιό γʼ ὀΐω ἂψ ἀναχωρήσειν (your insolence is such that . . .) Od. 17.460. Cf. Od. 9.350, Od. 15.10, Od. 20.223.

In reference to the future, no more, no longer, no further : οὐκέτʼ ἀνάβλησις ἔσσεται Il. 2.379. Cf. Il. 8.352, Il. 9.418 = 685, Il. 9.605, Il. 11.823, Il. 12.125, Il. 13.747, Il. 21.565 : Od. 2.238, 285, Od. 8.150, Od. 11.176, Od. 12.56, Od. 13.128, Od. 18.145, Od. 19.166, Od. 20.180, Od. 22.27, Od. 24.460.
After μή : μὴ οὐκέτι φυκτὰ πέλωνται Il. 16.128.
Never more, never in the future : οὐκέτι πῆμά ποτʼ ἔσσεαι Il. 10.453.
Barley grains sprinkled at a sacrifice : ἑτέρῃ ἔχεν οὐλὰς ἐν κανέῳ Od. 3.441.
Deadly,baleful : ἀστήρ Il. 11.62 (app. Sirius as in Il. 22.27).
Curly-headed, with crisp or curly hair Od. 19.246.
aor. pple. mid. of ὄλλυμι. For the sense cf. ὀνήμενος under ὀνίνημι 2.]
Whole, entire : ἄρτον Od. 17.343, μηνί Od. 24.118.

In neut. sing. οὖλον as adv. : οὖλον κεκλήγοντες Il. 17.756, 759 (app., shrieking a cry of destruction, uttering a death-shriek; or perh. the word should be referred to next, in sense close in texture, and thus in full, unbroken, cry).
[for ϝολ-νος. Cf. L. vellus, Eng. wool.]
Woolly, close or thick in texture, thick : ταπήτων Il. 16.224. Cf. Il. 24.646 : Od. 4.50= Od. 17.89, Od. 4.299= Od. 7.338, Od. 10.451, Od. 19.225.
Of hair, crisp, curly Od. 6.231= Od. 23.158.
In voc. οὖλε as a salutation Od. 24.402 (health be to thee).
Affirmative particle : φημὶ γὰρ οὖν κατανεῦσαι κρονίωνα (for I do declare that . . .) Il. 2.350 : τλήτω ἔμπης οὖν ἐπιμεῖναι ἐς αὔριον (for all his impatience to be gone) Od. 11.351.
In the first of correlative clauses : μήτʼ οὖν . . . μήτε . . . Il. 8.7, οὔτʼ οὖν . . . οὔτε . . . οὔτε . . . Il. 17.20. Cf. Il. 20.7, etc. : Od. 1.414, Od. 16.302, etc.
In the second : οὔ τις . . . οὐδʼ οὖν . . . Od. 9.147, οὔτε . . . οὔτʼ οὖν . . . Od. 11.200.

Particle of transition, so, then, now : οἱ δʼ ἐπεὶ οὖν ἤγερθεν Il. 1.57. Cf. Il. 3.21, Il. 9.550, Il. 15.232, Il. 22.475, etc. : πρῶτʼ οὖν λούσαντο Od. 23.142. Cf. Od. 2.123, Od. 3.34, Od. 4.49, 780, Od. 16.478, Od. 17.226, Od. 21.57, etc.
In the sense of οὗ ἕνεκα: πρήξαντα [τοῦτο] οὕνεκα δεῦρʼ ἱκόμεσθα Od. 3.61.
Wherefore, so that : ἡ δʼ Ἄτη σθεναρή, οὕνεκα πάσας ὑπεκπροθέει Il. 9.505.

Because, since, seeing that, in that : οὕνεκα τὸν Χρύσην ἠτίμασεν Il. 1.11. Cf. Il. 1.111, Il. 2.580, Il. 6.386, Il. 7.140, Il. 14.192, etc. : Od. 3.53, Od. 4.482, Od. 7.10, 300, Od. 8.200, Od. 13.332, etc.
That, to the effect that : ἀγγελίην ἐρέοντα οὕνεκά οἱ σῶς ἐσσι Od. 15.42. Cf. Il. 11.21 : Od. 5.216, Od. 13.309, etc.
App. a patronymic in form. Cf. Ὑπερίων.]

The heavenly gods Il. 5.373 = Il. 21.509, Il. 5.898 (here app. the sons of Uranus, i.e. the Titans; cf. Il. 15.225), Il. 21.275, Il. 24.547.– θεοὶ οὐρανίωνες Il. 1.570, Il. 17.195, Il. 24.612 : Od. 7.242= Od. 9.15, Od. 13.41.

From heaven or the heavens : ἦλθεν οὐ. Il. 1.195, οὐ. ὑπερράγη αἰθήρ Il. 8.558= Il. 16.300 (the action thought of as wrought from the firmament, the phenomena of the clouds being ascribed to Zeus). Cf. Il. 1.208, Il. 11.184, Il. 17.545, Il. 23.189 : Od. 5.294= Od. 9.69 = Od. 12.315, Od. 6.281, Od. 9.145, Od. 20.31.–
Reaching the heavens, very tall : ἐλάτη Od. 5.239.

The firmament, heaven, the heavens : κνίση οὐρανὸν ἷκεν Il. 1.317, οὐρανόθι πρό (in the front of heaven) Il. 3.3. Cf. Il. 2.153, Il. 4.44, Il. 7.423, Il. 8.16, Il. 14.174, etc. : Od. 1.54, Od. 4.400, Od. 9.20, Od. 12.404, Od. 13.269, etc.

The heavens as the abode of the gods : [θέτις] ἀνέβη οὐρανὸν οὔλυμπόν τε Il. 1.497. Cf. Il. 5.749, 750, Il. 6.108, Il. 19.128, 130, 351, etc. : ἀθανάτοισι τοὶ οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἔχουσιν Od. 1.67. Cf. Od. 7.199, Od. 11.316, etc.
The tail of an animal : οὐρῇσι περισσαίνοντες Od. 10.215. Cf. Il. 20.170 : Od. 17.302.
A limit or boundary, a boundary-stone : οὖρον ἀρούρης Il. 21.405.

(The distance between) the side limits of an area ploughed by such and such an animal in a given time, the length of the furrow being regarded as constant : ὅσσον ἐν νειῷ οὖρον πέλει ἡμιόνοιϊν (this ploughing-range of mules being taken as a rough standard of distance) Od. 8.124.
The regular range of the δίσκος taken as a sim. standard.
In pl. : ὅσσα δίσκου οὖρα πέλονται Il. 23.431.
A trench by which ships drawn up on land could be dragged down to the sea, a launching-way : οὐροὺς ἐξεκάθαιρον Il. 2.153.

A fair wind, a favouring breeze : τοῖσιν ἴκμενον οὖρον ἵει Ἀπόλλων Il. 1.479. Cf. Il. 7.5 : ὅτʼ ἄψ θεοὶ οὖρον στρέψαν (i.e. caused the wind to veer to a favourable direction) Od. 4.520. Cf. Od. 2.420, Od. 3.176, Od. 4.357, Od. 5.167, Od. 11.7, etc.
A wind, without implication of a particular direction : πρίν τινα κεκριμένον καταβήμεναι οὖρον Il. 14.19.
A guardian, protector, warder, watcher : οὖρος Ἀχαιῶν Il. 8.80, Il. 11.840, Il. 15.370 = 659 : Od. 3.411. Cf. Od. 15.89.
3 sing. pf. pass. οὔτασται Il. 11.661, Il. 16.26.
To strike or wound by a thrust or lunge : οὔτασε χεῖρα δουρί Il. 5.336. Cf. Il. 5.56, Il. 11.338, Il. 12.427, Il. 14.424, etc. : Od. 11.536.
With cognate acc. : ἕλκος, ὅ με βροτὸς οὔτασεν ἀνήρ Il. 5.361.
In mid. of reciprocal action : καί νύ κε δὴ ξιφέεσσʼ αὐτοσχεδὸν οὐτάζοντο Il. 7.273.
To wound by the cast of a weapon Il. 16.467.
To thrust a weapon into, pierce (a shield) : μέσον σάκος οὔτασε δουρί Il. 7.258. Cf. Il. 13.552, 607, 646, Il. 15.528.
3 sing. pa. iterative οὐτήσασκε Il. 22.375 οὔτασκε Il. 15.745.
Nom. pl. masc. pple. of this aor. in pass. sense οὐτάμενοι Il. 11.659, Il. 13.764, Il. 14.128, 379, etc. : Od. 11.40.
Acc. sing. fem. in sim. sense οὐταμένην Il. 14.518, Il. 17.86.
Infin. οὐτάμεναι Il. 21.68, 397 : Od. 9.301, Od. 19.449. οὐτάμεν Il. 5.132, 821.
To strike or wound by a thrust or lunge : πλευρὰ οὔτησε ξυστῷ Il. 4.469. Cf. Il. 5.132, Il. 6.64, Il. 11.659, Il. 14.128, etc. : Od. 9.301, Od. 11.40, Od. 19.449, 452, Od. 22.293, 294, 356.
In pass. construction with cognate acc. : ψυχὴ κατʼ οὐταμένην ὠτειλὴν ἔσσυτο (the wound thus inflicted) Il. 14.518. Cf. Il. 17.86.
To thrust a weapon into, pierce (a shield) : ἀσπίδος ὀμφαλὸν οὖτα Il. 13.192. Cf. Il. 13.561.
To thrust (at a shield), deliver a blow (upon it) : οὔτησε κατʼ ἀσπίδα Il. 11.434=Il. 17.43. Cf. Il. 21.400.
In general use corresponding to οὐ as μήτε to μή.
With infin. : οὔτʼ ἐς δαῖτʼ ἰέναι Il. 9.487, etc. Cf. Od. 16.203, etc.
Of no account, worthless, sorry, good for nothing : δειλός τε καὶ οὐτιδανός Il. 1.293. Cf. Il. 11.390 : Od. 8.209 (useless, blind to his own interests), Od. 9.460, 515.
Absol. : ἐπεὶ οὐτιδανοῖσιν ἀνάσσεις (men of nought) Il. 1.231. Cf. Od. 18.383 (v.l. οὐκ ἀγαθοῖσιν).

This person or thing (in reported speech generally (and properly) referring to what belongs to or concerns the person spoken to; cf. ὅδε) : λαοὺς οὐκ ἐπέοικε παλίλλογα ταῦτʼ ἐπαγείρειν Il. 1.126, ἐθέλοιμʼ ἂν τοῦτο γενέσθαι Il. 12.69 (here referring to the speaker's own wish). Cf. Il. 1.140, 286, 525, 564, Il. 2.326, 760, Il. 3.177, 178, Il. 4.415, Il. 5.187, 257, Il. 9.617, etc. : Od. 1.82, 159, 174, 179, 350, 390, Od. 2.74, 253, Od. 3.46, 47, 359, Od. 4.551, etc.
With sb., etc., this : τοῦτο ἔπος Il. 1.419. Cf. Il. 5.761, Il. 7.456, Il. 14.471, Il. 16.30, etc. : Od. 1.340, Od. 2.124, Od. 12.219, Od. 16.263 (these champions of yours), etc.
In much the sense of the definite article : οὐκ ἔσθʼ οὗτος ἀνήρ, ὅς κε... (the man who ...) Od. 6.201.
In deictic or predicative sense=here : τίς δʼ οὗτος ἔρχεαι οἶος; Il. 10.82. Cf. Il. 10.477, Il. 11.650, etc. : Od. 7.48, Od. 20.377, etc.

In this or that way or manner, thus, so (often (and properly) referring to what concerns the person spoken to; cf. ὧδε) : οὕτω διὶ μέλλει φίλον εἶναι Il. 2.116. Cf. Il. 1.131, 564, Il. 4.189, Il. 5.218, Il. 13.309 (app., so much as on the left), 825 (as surely), etc. : Od. 3.223, 358, Od. 4.485, Od. 5.146, Od. 8.465, Od. 9.262, etc.
Correlative with ὡς Il. 4.178, etc. : Od. 4.148, etc.
In that case, in consequence, thus, then : οὕτως οὔ τίς οἱ νεμεσήσεται Il. 10.129. Cf. Il. 11.382, Il. 21.412 : Od. 2.334, Od. 18.255=Od. 19.128, etc.–
Introductory, so, so then : οὕτω δὴ μεθήσομεν; Il. 15.553. Cf. Il. 2.158, etc. : Od. 5.204.
Sim. : ταῦτα μὲν οὕτω πάντα πεπείρανται Od. 12.37.
Thus we see that ..., so true it is that ... : οὕτως οὐ πάντεσσι θεοὶ χαρίεντα διδοῦσιν Od. 8.167.
With imp., as you are, as I tell you, without more ado, straightway, at once : στῆθʼ οὕτως ἐς μέσσον Od. 17.447. Cf. Il. 22.498.
In milder sense, app. little more than prithee : ἀμφίπολοι, στῆθʼ οὕτω ἀπόπροθεν Od. 6.218.

p.gloss: Qualifying an adj., pple. or adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Thus, so : καλὸν οὕτω Il. 3.169. Cf. Il. 7.198 (so ...as that would imply), Il. 9.40, etc. : οὕτω χρηΐζοντι Od. 11.340. Cf. Od. 3.315, Od. 4.543, Od. 13.239 (not so very... as to justify that), etc.
To owe, be liable for or indebted in : χρεῖος Il. 11.688. Cf. Od. 8.332, 462, Od. 21.17.
In pass., to be owing or due : οἷσι χρεῖος ὀφείλετο Il. 11.686. Cf. Il. 11.698 : Od. 3.367.

In impf. or aor. with infin. of what one ought to do or be doing : νῦν ὄφελεν κατὰ πάντας ἀριστῆας πονέεσθαι Il. 10.117. Cf. Il. 18.367 (why should I not ...?), Il. 19.200 : Od. 4.472 (what you should do is to ...).
Of what one ought to have done : τιμήν πέρ μοι ὄφελλεν ἐγγυαλίξαι Il. 1.353, μὴ ὄφελες λίσσεσθαι Il. 9.698 (ὄφελες μὴ...) Cf. Il. 23.546.
In impf. or aor. with infin. expressing a vain wish that something were the case : ἀνδρὸς ὤφελλον ἀμείνονος εἶναι ἄκοιτις (would that I were ...) Il. 6.350. Cf. Od. 4.97.
Expressing a wish that something had been the case : ἀγγελίης, ἥ μὴ ὤφελλε γενέσθαι Il. 18.19. Cf. Il. 17.686, Il. 19.59 : Od. 2.184, Od. 8.312.
So with αἴθε in the same tenses expressing a wish in reference to the present : αἴθʼ ὄφελες παρὰ νηυσὶν ἀδάκρυτος ἧσθαι (would that you were sitting...) Il. 1.415. Cf. Il. 3.40, Il. 14.84, Il. 18.86.
In reference to the past : αἴθʼ ὤφελλʼ ὁ ξεῖνος ἄλλοθʼ ὀλέσθαι (would that he had...) Od. 18.401. Cf. Il. 3.40, Il. 18.86, Il. 24.254 : Od. 13.204.
So with ὡς in reference to the present : ὡς ὄφελέν τις ἀνδρῶν ἄλλος ἔχειν (would that it were another's lot) Il. 4.315. Cf. Od. 1.217.

To the past : ὡς ὤφελες αὐτόθʼ ὀλέσθαι (would that you had ...) Il. 3.428. Cf. Il. 3.173, Il. 6.345, Il. 7.390, Il. 1.380, Il. 21.279, Il. 22.426, 481, Il. 24.764 : Od. 5.308, Od. 11.548, Od. 14.68, 274, Od. 24.30.

div.head: ὀφέλλω2.
div.p: 3 sing. aor. opt. ὀφέλλειε Il. 16.651 : Od. 2.334. (ἐξ-)
To increase, add to, cause to wax, intensify : πόνον Il. 2.420, Il. 16.651, οὔ τι χρὴ μῦθον ὀφέλλειν (to make long speeches) Il. 16.631. Cf. Il. 3.62, Il. 4.445, Il. 20.242 : Od. 2.334, Od. 16.174.
In pass., to become greater, wax great : ὀφέλλετο μένος Il. 23.524.
To cause (waves) to swell : μάλιστα κύματʼ ὀφέλλει Il. 15.383.
To make (a house) rich, store (it) with substance Od. 15.21.
In pass., of a house, to wax rich, grow great : αἶψα οἶκος ὀφέλλετο Od. 14.233.
With personal object, to exalt, magnify : ὄφρʼ ἂν Ἀχαιοὶ ὀφέλλωσί ἑ τιμῇ Il. 1.510 (or perh. make rich; see under τιμή 6).
Good, use, help : αἴ κʼ ὀ. τι γενώμεθα Il. 13.236. Cf. Il. 17.152, Il. 22.513.
A serpent or snake Il. 12.208 (the lengthening of the first syllable unexplained).

div.head: b
div.p: With subj., pure or with κεν or ἄν : ὄφρα τελέσσῃ Il. 1.82, ὄφρα κε οἶνον ἐνείκω Il. 6.258, ὄφρʼ ἂν ἵκηται Il. 15.23. Cf. Il. 12.281, Il. 16.10, Il. 22.192, Il. 24.431, etc. : Od. 4.588, Od. 6.304, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: With opt. : ὄφρʼ ἐξεμέσειεν Od. 12.437. Cf. Il. 10.571.
With ἄν: ὄφρʼ ἄν ἄγοιεν Od. 17.298.

div.head: a
div.p: With indic. : ὄφρα μήνιεν Il. 2.769. Cf. Il. 5.788, Il. 11.266, etc. : Od. 1.233, Od. 8.181, Od. 20.136, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: With subj. in conditional relative sentences. For the examples and constructions see Table at end III.B.a 1 2, (D) (12) (13) (20) (34) (43) (44).

div.head: a
div.p: With indic. : ὄφρʼ ἀμφεπένοντο Il. 4.220. Cf. Il. 11.357, Il. 14.358, etc. : Od. 10.125.

div.head: b
div.p: With subj. in conditional relative sentences. See Table III.B.a 1, (D) (26) (35).
For a time : ὄφρα μὲν βοῦς βόσκεν, αὐτὰρ ἐτεὶ... Il. 15.547.
In final clauses, in order that, so that.

div.head: a
div.p: With subj. : ὄφρα μὴ οἶος ἀγέραστος ἔω Il. 1.118. Cf. Il. 1.133, 147, 158, 185, 524, etc. : Od. 1.85, 88, 174, 310, Od. 2.329, Od. 3.15, etc.
With κεν: ὄφρα κε γνῶμεν Il. 22.382. Cf. Il. 2.440 : Od. 3.359, Od. 10.298, Od. 16.234, Od. 19.45, etc.
With ἄν: ὄφρʼ ἄν ἐκεῖθι δαῖτα πτωχεύῃ Od. 17.10. Cf. Od. 18.364, Od. 22.377.

div.head: b
div.p: With κεν: ὄφρα χʼ ἁλίπλοα τείχεα θείη Il. 12.26.
With ἄν: ὄφρʼ ἂν ἵκοιο Od. 10.65. Cf. Od. 24.334.

div.head: c
div.p: With fut. : ὄφρʼ εἴσεται Il. 8.110, Il. 16.242. Cf. Od. 4.163, Od. 17.6, Od. 18.419.
A clause with ὄφρα instead of infin. : λελιημένος ὄφρα τάχιστα τεύχεα συλήσειεν Il. 4.465. Cf. Il. 5.690, Il. 6.361, Il. 16.653.

p.gloss: Set on the brow of a hill, mountain-built.

div.p: One of the eyebrows; in pl., the eyebrows : ἐπʼ ὀφρύσι νεῦσεν Il. 1.528, τὸν ὑπʼ ὀφρύος οὖτα Il. 14.493. Cf. Il. 13.88, Il. 14.236, Il. 15.102, Il. 23.396, etc. : Od. 4.153, Od. 8.86, Od. 12.194, Od. 16.164, etc.
In pl., the brow or edge of a hill : καθῖζον ἐπʼ ὀφρύσι καλλικολώνης Il. 20.151.
Intensive, strengthening ἄριστος, by far, the veryIl. 1.69, Il. 2.761, Il. 3.110, etc. : Od. 3.129, Od. 8.123, Od. 9.420, etc.
In sing. sense, a chariot (viewed as including all the parts thereof) : ἐξ ὀχέων ἆλτο Il. 3.29. Cf. Il. 4.306, Il. 5.28, 107, 219, 369, etc.
One who conducts water in a conduit or ditch Il. 21.257.
A means of securing a helmet on the head Il. 3.372.
In pl., the fastenings of a belt : ζωστῆρος ὀχῆες Il. 4.132, Il. 20.414.

A bar or bolt for securing a gate or door within : οὐδʼ ἐρρήξαντʼ ἂν πύλας καὶ μακρὸν ὀχῆα Il. 12.291 (here and in Il. 13.124 app. the same as the ὀχῆες of Il. 12.455). Cf. Il. 12.121, 455, 460, Il. 13.124, Il. 21.537, Il. 24.446, 566 (in Il. 24. app. identical with the ἐπιβλής of 453) : Od. 21.47, Od. 24.166.
In pass., to be carried or borne : ἵπποι ἀλεγεινοὶ ὀχέεσθαι (for being carried, i.e. they are hard to drive) Il. 10.403=Il. 17.77, νηυσὶν ὀχήσονται (will be carried off in ...) Il. 24.731.
Sim. in mid. : πολέεσσιν ὀχήσατο κύμασιν (rode) Od. 5.54.
To carry (an affliction) with one, be unable to flee from (it) : ἥν ἄτην Od. 21.302.
To have laid upon one, endure : ὁϊζύν Od. 7.211. Cf. Od. 11.619.
To indulge in, practise : νηπιάας Od. 1.297.
[ϝεχ- as in ὀχέω. Cf. L. vehe-mens.]

To be moved in mind or spirit, be troubled or agitated, express or manifest emotion, trouble or agitation : τὴν μέγʼ ὀχθήσας προσέφη Il. 1.517, ὄχθησαν θεοί 570. Cf. Il. 11.403, Il. 23.143, etc.: Od. 4.30, Od. 21.248, Od. 23.182, etc.
In pl., the banks of a river : παρʼ ὄχθας σαγγαρίοιο Il. 3.187. Cf. Il. 4.475, 487, Il. 6.34, Il. 11.499, Il. 12.313, Il. 14.445, Il. 18.533, Il. 21.10, 337 : Od. 6.97.
The shore of the sea Od. 9.132.
The sides of a ditch Il. 15.356.
To raise, lift : ἐπʼ ἄμαξαν ἀπʼ οὔδεος Il. 12.448. Cf. Od. 9.242.
Something that affords safety or security : λιμένες νηῶς ὀχοί Od. 5.404.

A voice : ἄειδον ἀμειβόμεναι ὀπὶ καλῇ Il. 1.604. Cf. Il. 3.221, Il. 14.150, Il. 16.76, Il. 18.222, Il. 22.451 : ἤκουσα ὄπα Πριάμοιο θυγατρός Od. 11.421. Cf. Od. 5.61, Od. 10.221, Od. 12.52, 160, 185, 187, 192, Od. 14.492, Od. 20.92, Od. 24.60.
With special reference to what is uttered : ξυνέηκε θεᾶς ὄπα Il. 2.182=Il. 10.512. Cf. Il. 7.53, Il. 11.137, Il. 20.380, Il. 21.98 : Od. 24.535.
Not early, late : ὀψὲ δύοντα βοώτην Od. 5.272. Cf. Il. 21.232.
Long after, after a long interval : ὀψὲ μετὰ νῶϊ κίεν Od. 3.168.
After the lapse of a long time, late : ὀψέ περ ἐλθών Od. 23.7. Cf. Od. 9.534, Od. 11.114=Od. 12.141.
At a late stage, late in the day : καὶ ὀψέ περ υἷας Ἀχαιῶν ἐρύεσθαι Il. 9.247.
To desire to see, go to view.
With genit. : ἀϋτῆς καὶ πολέμοιο Il. 14.37.
Of a generation later than one's own, late-born : τί σευ ἄλλος ὀνήσεται ὄ περ; Il. 16.31.
Absol. in pl., the men of the generations to come, posterity Od. 1.302=Od. 3.200.
Having reference to a date in the far future, pointing far forward : τέρας Il. 2.325.
Exercise of the power of vision : ὄψει οὔ πω σὺ ἐμοὺς ἴδες (with your eyes) Il. 20.205. Cf. Od. 23.94.
The fact of seeing something, the sight of ... : πατρὸς ὄψιν ἀτυχθείς Il. 6.468.
To be fulfilled in the far future : τέρας Il. 2.325.
A piece of cooked meat Il. 9.489.
In pl., such meat : σῖτον καὶ οἶνον ὄψα τε Od. 3.480. Cf. Od. 5.267, Od. 6.77.
A relish : κρόμυον ποτῷ ὄψον Il. 11.630.
App., a reef in the sea Od. 5.405, 411.
All of bronze : ἄορ Od. 8.403. Cf. Il. 20.102 : Od. 11.575.
[παν- as in παγχάλκεος. + χαλκός.]=παγχάλκεος. : κυνέη Od. 18.378. Cf. Il. 22.102.

Wholly, altogether, entirely, quite, to the full (in negative statements and injunctions commonly rather strengthening the negation than attaching itself closely to the verb, etc., and to be translated at all, by any means, in any wise, or the like ; cf. πάμπαν) : π. ἀκαχήμενος (bereft of all comfort) Il. 5.24, σοὶ οὔ πω π. θεοὶ κοτέουσιν Il. 14.143. Cf. Il. 10.99, Il. 12.67, Il. 13.747, Il. 14.95, Il. 15.196, Il. 16.538, etc. : οἶκον π. διαρραίσει Od. 2.49, μηδὲ π. δείδιθι Od. 4.825. Cf. Od. 2.279, Od. 4.755, Od. 10.236, Od. 13.133, Od. 15.327, Od. 22.236, etc.
Of a surety, verily : π. νύκτα φυλάξεις Od. 22.195. Cf. Od. 17.217.
A boy : παιδνὸς ἐών Od. 21.21, Od. 24.338.
To play, sport Od. 6.100, 106, Od. 7.291, Od. 8.251 (show us your skill in sport), Od. 23.147 (dancing).

A song of propitiation addressed to Apollo in his character of healer (cf. Il. 16.514-529), and app. as thus identified with Παιήων, the Healer, who, however, appears to be represented as a separate person(cf. Il. 5.401, 899, 900 : Od. 4.232) : καλὸν ἀείδοντες παιήονα Il. 1.473.
Of islands : Ἴμβρου Il. 13.33, Il. 24.78 : Χίοιο Od. 3.170, Σάμοιο Od. 4.671=Od. 15.29, Od. 4.845, Ἰθάκην Od. 11.480.
Of roads, rough, stony Il. 12.168, Il. 17.743 : Od. 17.204.

In reference to age, boy : μή τί μευ ἠΰτε παιδὸς πειρήτιζε Il. 7.235. Cf. Il. 2.289, Il. 6.467, Il. 8.271, Il. 11.558, 710, Il. 16.260, etc. : Od. 4.32, 665, 688, Od. 6.300, Od. 18.216, Od. 21.95, Od. 22.358.

div.head: a
div.p: A son : Πριάμοιο παῖδες Il. 1.255. Cf. Il. 1.393, Il. 2.205, Il. 5.386, Il. 6.26, Il. 10.170, Il. 11.783, etc. : παῦροι παῖδες ὁμοῖος πατρὶ πέλονται Od. 2.276. Cf. Od. 1.207, Od. 3.196, Od. 4.164, Od. 7.149, Od. 9.519, Od. 11.299, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: A daughter : παῖδʼ ἐμοὶ λύσαιτε φίλην Il. 1.20. Cf. Il. 1.443, 447, Il. 3.175, Il. 5.880, Il. 22.51 : ὅσσα ἔοικε φίλης ἐπὶ παιδὸς ἕπεσθαι Od. 1.278=Od. 2.197. Cf. Od. 4.13, 263, Od. 7.65, 300, 313, Od. 8.488, Od. 10.139, Od. 11.604, Od. 18.323.

div.head: c
div.p: Without distinction of gender : ἵνα παισὶν ἀεικέα μισθὸν ἄρηται Il. 12.435. Cf. Il. 4.131, Il. 5.408, Il. 7.334, Il. 8.57, Il. 10.422, Il. 15.497, etc. : Od. 3.381, Od. 5.394, Od. 7.70, Od. 9.115, Od. 10.5, Od. 11.431, Od. 13.62, etc.

div.head: d
div.p: Used by elders in addressing younger persons : μηκέτι, παῖδε φίλω, πολεμίζετε Il. 7.279.
To make oneself conspicuous : παιφάσσουσα διέσσυτο λαόν (dazzling) Il. 2.450.
Long ago, long ere this : π. κʼ ἦσθα ἐνέρτερος οὐρανιώνων Il. 5.898. Cf. Il. 21.432 : Od. 19.282, Od. 20.222, Od. 23.29.

Long, of old (referring to time long past or comparatively recent) : π. πολέμων ἐΰ εἰδώς Il. 4.310, ὀϊστὸν ἔχεν π. Il. 23.871. Cf. Il. 7.89, Il. 16.441=Il. 22.179, Il. 22.301, Il. 23.331 : Od. 5.240, Od. 17.366, Od. 18.309.
With pres. : μοῖραν ἔχει π. (has long had it) Od. 20.293.
In the past, formerly : ἠμὲν π. ἠδʼ ἔτι καὶ νῦν Il. 9.105.
With sb. in adjectival use, of olden days : τόδε ἔργον π., οὔ τι νέον γε Il. 9.527.
Old in years, aged, old Il. 3.386, Il. 17.561 : Od. 22.395.
Absol., an old man : ἤ νέος ἠὲ π. Il. 14.108.
In comp., old rather than young, of the older generation : ὡς ἀθάνατοι τιμῶσι παλαιοτέρους ἀνθρώπους Il. 23.788.
Of the days of old, that lived long ago, old : Ἴλου Il. 11.166. Cf. Il. 11.372.
Of long standing, old : ξεῖνος Il. 6.215.
The old, the accustomed : λέκτροιο Od. 23.296.
Absol. in pl., those of old : οὐδὲ παλαιῶν, τάων αἳ... (the women of old days) Od. 2.118.
Absol. in neut. pl., things of old, the wisdom of ancient days: παλαιά τε πολλά τε εἰδώς Od. 2.188, Od. 7.157, Od. 24.51.
Constructed long ago, long in use, old : νῆες Od. 2.293.
That has been long stored up, old : οἴνοιο Od. 2.340.
Put forth long ago, old : θέσφατα Od. 9.507=Od. 13.172.
Of old renown, old-world : δρυός Od. 19.163.
To wrestle : φιλομηλεΐδῃ ἐπάλαισεν (with ...) Od. 4.343=Od. 17.134. Cf. Il. 23.621, 733.

The hand (thought of in reference to its grasp) : ἐν παλάμῃς φορέουσιν Il. 1.238. Cf. Il. 3.128, 338, Il. 5.558, Il. 8.111, Il. 15.677, etc. : Od. 1.104, Od. 2.10, Od. 5.234, Od. 17.4, 231, Od. 19.577=Od. 21.75.
Pf. pple. pass. πεπαλαγμένος, -ου Il. 6.268 : Od. 22.184, 402, Od. 23.48.
To spatter, sprinkle : ἐγκέφαλος ἔνδον ἅπας πεπάλακτο Il. 11.98=Il. 12.186=Il. 20.400.
To bespatter, besprinkle, wet, befoul : παλάσσεθʼ αἵματι θώρηξ Il. 5.100. Cf. Il. 6.268, Il. 11.169, 535=Il. 20.500, Il. 17.387, Il. 20.504 : Od. 13.395, Od. 22.184, 402 = Od. 23.48, Od. 22.406.
Brought together again Il. 1.126 (till they be ...).
In neut. παλιμπετές as adv., to where one came from, back : ὥς κε π. ἀπονέωνται Od. 5.27.
In the direction contrary to that desired, back : ἄψ ἐπὶ νῆας ἔεργε π. Il. 16.395.
To drive back from one's goal, foil, baffle Il. 1.59 : Od. 13.5.

To where one came from, back again, back : π. ᾤχετο Il. 1.380, π. κίε θυγατέρος ἧς (app. genit. of point attained, returned to ...) Il. 21.504. Cf. Il. 6.189, Il. 8.399, Il. 9.408, Il. 16.87, Il. 24.462, etc. : Od. 1.360, Od. 6.110, Od. 7.280, Od. 9.95, Od. 16.467, Od. 19.533 (i. e. to her father's), etc.
Sim. : ἐξελκομένοιο π. (drawn back the way it had entered) Il. 4.214.
Strengthened by αὖτις Il. 5.257, Il. 17.533, Il. 23.229 : Od. 14.356, Od. 15.431.
Away from an object, away, aside : ὄσσε π. κλίνασα Il. 3.427. Cf. Il. 13.3, Il. 21.415, 468.
With genit. : π. τράπεθʼ υἷος (from ...) Il. 18.138. Cf. Il. 20.439.
In a backward direction, backwards : χειρὶ π. ἐρύσασα Il. 5.836.
With notion of contradiction, against a person : οὔ τις π. ἐρέει (will gainsay you) Il. 9.56.
With notion of repetition, again. Strengthened by αὖτις : οὔ μιν π. αὖτις ἀνήσει θυμὸς νεικείειν ... Il. 2.276.
With notion of restoration, back : δόμεναι π. Il. 1.116, Il. 7.79=Il. 22.342. Cf. Il. 22.259.
Sim. : π. ὅ γε λάζετο μῦθον Il. 4.357 : Od. 13.254 (see λάζομαι).
So in reference to restoration to a state : π. ποίησε γέροντα Od. 16.456.
With genit. : αὐτοῖο π. χύτʼ ἀήρ (left him so that he again became visible) Od. 7.143.
To be taken back, revocable : οὐκ ἐμὸν παλινάγρετον Il. 1.526.
Consisting in paying back or requital : παλίντιτα ἔργα (works of vengeance, revenge) Od. 1.379=Od. 2.144.

Of bows, curving
back, i. e. bent back in the centre to form a handle; or perh. a general epithet, springing back, elastic Il. 8.266, Il. 10.459, Il. 15.443 : Od. 21.11, 59.
Flowing back, with backward flow : παλιρρόθιόν μιν πλῆξε [κῦμα] Od. 5.430. Cf. Od. 9.485.
[for παλι-ίωξις, fr. παλι-, πάλιν + ἰωκ-, ἰωκή.]
A pursuit back, a retreat : εἴ κε π. γένηται Il. 12.71. Cf. Il. 15.69, 601.
A concubine : ἔμʼ ὠνητὴ τέκε μήτηρ, π. Od. 14.203. Cf. Il. 9.449, 452.
App. imp. pl. aor. mid. πεπάλασθε Il. 7.171.
(For these two forms prob. πεπάλεσθε, πεπαλέσθαι should be read.)
To shake, poise, away, brandish, wield (a spear or missile) : δοῦρε δύω πάλλων Il. 3.19. Cf. Il. 5.304, Il. 16.117, 142, Il. 22.320, etc.
In pass., to throb, vibrate, beat : πάλλεται ἦτορ Il. 22.452. Cf. Il. 22.461.
App., to be tripped up, trip : ἐν ἀσπίδος ἄντυγι πάλτο Il. 15.645.
To shake (lots) together : κλήρους ἐν κυνεῃ πάλλον (πάλλομεν) Il. 3.316=Il. 23.861 : Od. 10.206.
Absol., to shake the lots Il. 3.324, Il. 7.181, Il. 23.353.

In mid., to cast lots : κλήρῳ πεπάλασθε Il. 7.171, ἐγὼν ἔλαχον ἅλα παλλομένων (partitive genit., of us when we cast lots) Il. 15.191, τῶν μέτα (with them) παλλόμενος κλήρῳ λάχον ... Il. 24.400. Cf. Od. 9.331.
To sprinkle, scatter, strew : ἐπʼ ἄλφιτα πάλυνεν Il. 11.640, ἄλφιτα πάλυνον (app. in water to make porridge) Il. 18.560. Cf. Od. 10.520, Od. 11.28, Od. 14.77.
To sprinkle, besprinkle, powder, cover lightly : ὅτε χιὼν ἐπάλυνεν ἀρούρας Il. 10.7. Cf. Od. 14.429.
All black, black all over Od. 3.6, Od. 10.525, Od. 11.33.
[παν-, πᾶς reduplicated with assimilation of the Od. 13..]

Wholly, altogether, entirely, quite (in negative statements and injunctions commonly rather strengthening the negation than attaching itself closely to the verb, etc., and to be translated at all, by any means, in any wise, or the like ; cf. πάγχυ) : πολέμου ἀποπαύεο π. Il. 1.422, οὐδʼ ὅ γε π. χάζετο Il. 12.406. Cf. Il. 9.435, Il. 13.111, 761, Il. 14.91, Il. 17.406, Il. 20.376, etc. : βίοτον ἀπὸ π. ὀλέσσει Od. 2.49, οὐδʼ Ἀγαμέμνονι π. ἑήνδανεν Od. 3.143. Cf. Od. 4.693, Od. 8.552, Od. 11.528, Od. 16.375, Od. 20.140, etc.
The first of all, taking the lead : π. ὑφαίνειν ἤρχετο μῆτιν Il. 7.324=Il. 9.93.
In neut. sing. πάμπρωτον as adv., first of all, as the first thing, to start with : νῆας π. ἐρύσσαμεν Od. 4.577. Cf. Od. 4.780, Od. 10.403, 423, Od. 11.2.
Sim. in neut. pl. πάμπρωτα, first of all, before all others : τοῦ κε π. παρὰ δῶρα φέροιο Il. 4.97. Cf. Il. 17.568.

To shine, gleam, glitter : ἀστέρα, ὅς τε μάλιστα λαμπρὸν παμφαίνῃσιν Il. 5.6, στήθεσι παμφαίνοντας (app., their (naked) breasts glistening (instead of their armour)) Il. 11.100. Cf. Il. 6.513, Il. 11.30, 63, Il. 14.11, Il. 19.398, Il. 22.26.
To shine, gleam, glitter : τεύχεα παμφανόωντα Il. 5.295. Cf. Il. 2.458, Il. 5.619, Il. 6.473, Il. 18.206 Il. 23.613, etc. : Od. 4.42, Od. 13.29, Od. 19.386, Od. 22.121.
Glancing or gleaming all over : ζωστήρ Il. 4.186, Il. 10.77. Cf. Il. 4.215, Il. 11.236, 374, Il. 13.552.
Quite tenderly reared, delicately nurtured Od. 13.223.
That has ill fortune to the full, dogged by evil fate Il. 24.255, 493.
All of silver : κρητῆρα Od. 9.203, Od. 24.275.
App., cut off from his equals in years Il. 22.490.
Destined to be cut off untimely, shortlived Il. 24.540.
[παν-, πᾶς + δῆμος, in sense town. Cf. ἐπιδημεύω.]
Roving through all the town, vagabond : πτωχός Od. 18.1.
All the day long : ᾧ τε π. ἕλκητον βόε πηκτὸν ἄροτρον Od. 13.31.

All the day long : πανημέριοι θεὸν ἱλάσκοντο (i.e. all the rest of the day) Il. 1.472, ὥς κε πανημέριοι κρινώμεθʼ Ἄρηϊ Il. 2.385. Cf. Il. 11.279, Il. 17.180, 384, Il. 18.209, Il. 19.168 : Od. 3.486 =Od. 15.184, Od. 4.356 (in a day's sail), Od. 11.11, Od. 12.24.
With all spirit, i. e. fiercely, bitterly : ὀκριόωντο Od. 18.33.

All the night long : εὗδον παννύχιοι Il. 2.2. Cf. Il. 2.24 = 61, Il. 7.476, 478, Il. 8.508, 554, Il. 10.2=Il. 24.678, Il. 18.315, 354, Il. 23.105, 217 : Od. 1.443, Od. 2.434 (i. e. all the rest of the night), Od. 7.288, Od. 12.429.
In neut. sing. πάννυχον as adv. : τί π. ἀωτεῖς; Il. 10.159.
From whom proceed all omens by voices or sounds : Ζηνί Il. 8.250.
[παν-, πᾶς + ὀπ-. See ὁράω. Cf. ὑπόψιος.]
Seen by all, conspicuous : πανόψιον ἔγχος ἑλοῦσα Il. 21.397.
Coming all together, in a body, in full force Il. 2.12, 29 = 66, Il. 11.709, 725.

In all directions,
every way : κατὰ στρατὸν ᾤχετο π. Il. 5.495. Cf. Il. 1.384, Il. 6.81, Il. 11.156, Il. 14.413, Il. 23.463, etc. : Od. 2.383, Od. 12.233, Od. 21.394, 405, Od. 24.355, 413.

On every side, all about, all round : π. ὀρώρει πῦρ Il. 12.177. Cf. Il. 5.739, Il. 12.430, Il. 13.736, Il. 16.111, Il. 17.354, Il. 23.34, 127, Il. 24.799 : π. οἱ βεβλήαται εὐναί (i.e. now in one place, now in another) Od. 11.193. Cf. Od. 24.208.
From all quarters, directions, parts, from every side : π. ἐκ κευθμῶν Il. 13.28. Cf. Il. 16.110, Il. 21.364, Il. 23.112, 689 : Od. 17.171.
= πάντῃ 2 : λαμπόμενος πυρὶ π. (all about him) Il. 15.623. Cf. Od. 14.270, Od. 17.439.

Of all sorts or kinds : ἀνέμων (blowing from all quarters, all the winds) Il. 2.397, Il. 17.56, δόλους Il. 3.202, δρόμου (in all directions and at all speeds) Il. 18.281, ἀϋτμήν (of every desired degree of force) 471. Cf. Il. 15.642, Il. 20.249, Il. 22.268, Il. 23.308, 314 : Od. 1.142, Od. 3.119, Od. 4.725, Od. 6.77, 234, Od. 15.246, Od. 17.486 (taking all forms), etc.

In all directions, every way : π. ἐποιχόμενος Il. 5.508, π. ἀκούειν Il. 16.515 (the power of hearing being thought of as projected towards the source of the sound; cf. Il. 4.455 cited under τηλόσε). Cf. Il. 12.266, Il. 13.649, Il. 17.674, 680, Il. 18.479 : Od. 11.606, Od. 17.209, 366, Od. 22.24, 380.
For ἀσπὶς π. ἐΐση see ἶσος 5.b.
By all means. Strengthening a negative : π. οὐκ ἄν με τρέψειαν (the whole band of them shall not . . .) Il. 8.450 : π. οὔ τί με λήθεις (of a surety you do not . . .) Od. 19.91. Cf. Od. 20.180.
The last of all : π. ἤλυθεν ἄλλων Il. 23.532. Cf. Il. 23.547 : Od. 9.452.
Used by a daughter in affectionate address Od. 6.57.
To call one (dear) father : οὐδέ τί μιν παῖδες παππάζουσιν Il. 5.408.

To look narrowly about one, peer, throw one's glance round, glance : ἀμφὶ ἓ παπτήνας Il. 4.497= Il. 15.574. Cf. Il. 8.269, Il. 11.546, Il. 13.551, Il. 17.84, 603, 674, Il. 22.463, Il. 23.464, 690 : Od. 11.608, Od. 12.233, Od. 17.330, Od. 19.552, Od. 22.24, 380, Od. 24.179.
With dependent clause : πάπτηνεν ἕκαστος ὅπῃ φύγοι ὄλεθρον Il. 14.507= Il. 16.283 := Od. 22.43. Cf. Il. 12.333, Il. 13.649 : Od. 22.381.
To look about for, throw one's glance round in quest of : μαχάονα Il. 4.200. Cf. Il. 17.115.
(Commonly with anastrophe when immediately following the vb. or case-form (and see Il. 3.440)). Also in forms πάρ, παραί (which does not suffer anastrophe).

Beside, by, near, someone or something : παρὰ νύκτας ἴαυον Il. 9.470. Cf. Il. 1.611, Il. 3.135, Il. 4.330, Il. 5.112, Il. 11.512, etc. : παραὶ λεχέεσσι κλιθῇναι Od. 1.366. Cf. Od. 1.132, Od. 3.267, Od. 4.305, Od. 5.196, Od. 6.18, etc.
At hand, ready to aid, at command : πάρα θεοί εἰσι καὶ ἡμῖν Il. 3.440.
Sim. : παρά τε σχεῖν ὅσσα . . . Il. 23.50.
Past, passing by, something : παρά τις κιών Il. 16.263. Cf. Od. 12.82.
Aside, away : παραί οἱ ἐτράπετʼ ἔγχος Il. 11.233= Il. 13.605.
Denoting turning or bending of a person's mind : παρά μ ἤπαφε δαίμων Od. 14.488.

div.head: a
div.p: Beside, by, near, in the company of : παρὰ νηυσίν Il. 1.26. Cf. Il. 1.329, 358, Il. 2.355, Il. 7.135, Il. 20.53, etc. : παρʼ Ἀτρεΐδῃ Od. 3.156. Cf. Od. 4.443, 595, Od. 5.119, Od. 7.203, Od. 11.178, Od. 15.386, etc.
With locative : παρὰ ναῦφιν Il. 8.474. Cf. Il. 12.302, etc.
In pregnant sense : πὰρ δέ οἱ ἔστη Il. 21.547. Cf. Il. 1.405, Il. 3.262, Il. 13.617, etc. : Od. 1.142, Od. 3.37, Od. 13.122, Od. 17.572, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: In the house, establishment or land of, in the hands or power of : ἐπεὶ φιλέεσθε παρʼ αὐτῇ Il. 13.627. Cf. Il. 4.1, Il. 17.324, Il. 19.148, Il. 23.411, Il. 24.212, etc. : παρὰ μητρὶ κεῖσθαι Od. 15.127. Cf. Od. 1.123, Od. 8.420, Od. 11.175, 460, 490, Od. 13.204, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: Set alongside in contemplation, beside, along with : παρὰ καὶ κακῷ ἐσθλὸν ἔθηκεν Od. 15.488.

div.head: a
div.p: In reference to motion ending beside or near a person or thing, beside, by, near : ἐς δίφρον ἔβαινε παραὶ Διομήδεα Il. 5.837. Cf. Il. 3.406, Il. 7.190, Il. 11.314, etc. : στῆ παρὰ σταθμόν Od. 1.333. Cf. Od. 8.469, Od. 17.96, Od. 22.333, etc.
Sim. in reference to striking with a weapon, missile, etc. : παρὰ οὖς ἔλασε ξίφει Il. 11.109. Cf. Il. 4.480, 518, Il. 5.146, Il. 12.204, Il. 21.491, etc. : Od. 22.82.
So in reference to a weapon struck Il. 16.115.
In reference to visiting a person, to : πὰρ Μενέλαον οἴχετο Od. 13.414. Cf. Il. 18.143 : Od. 1.285.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to motion alongside of a thing, along, by : βῆ παρὰ θῖνα θαλάσσης Il. 1.34. Cf. Il. 1.347, Il. 10.54, Il. 11.558, Il. 17.297, Il. 18.576, Il. 23.225, etc. : παρὰ Μίμαντα Od. 3.172. Cf. Od. 4.432, Od. 15.295, Od. 24.11, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: Without notion of motion in reference to action or existence in a region alongside of a person or thing, along, by : ἕρδον ἑκατόμβας παρὰ θῖνʼ ἁλός Il. 1.316. Cf. Il. 1.463, Il. 2.522, 604, Il. 3.272, Il. 4.487, Il. 12.313, Il. 17.290, etc. : πρασιαὶ παρὰ νείατον ὄρχον πεφύασιν Od. 7.127. Cf. Od. 6.89, Od. 12.32, Od. 14.347, Od. 19.553, Od. 22.127, etc.

div.head: d
div.p: In reference to motion past something, past, passing : παρʼ Ἴλου σῆμʼ ἐσσεύοντο Il. 11.166, οὖτα παρʼ ἀσπίδα (getting within the guard of the shield) Il. 16.312. Cf. Il. 5.293, Il. 6.42, etc. : Od. 4.802, etc.

div.head: e
div.p: Beyond, in excess of : πὰρ δύναμιν Il. 13.787. Cf. Od. 14.509.

div.head: a
div.p: From beside, or simply, from : φάσγανον ἑρυσσάμενος παρὰ μηροῦ Il. 1.190, πλευρά, τά οἱ παρʼ ἀσπίδος ἑξεφαάνθη (beyond it, outside its shelter) Il. 4.468. Cf. Il. 2.596, 787, Il. 8.533, Il. 11.1, Il. 13.211, etc. : ἀνιόντα παρʼ Ἴλου Od. 1.259. Cf. Od. 3.347, 431, Od. 8.289, Od. 12.70, Od. 15.58, etc.
With ablative : παρὰ ναῦφιν Il. 12.225 : Od. 14.498.

div.head: b
div.p: With vbs. of taking, receiving, bringing or the like, from, at the hands of : ὅττι ῥά οἱ γαμβροῖο πάρα φέροιτο Il. 6.177. Cf. Il. 4.97, Il. 11.795, Il. 18.137, Il. 24.429, 502, etc. : ὄφρα πομπῆς τύχῃς παρὰ πατρὸς ἐμοῖο Od. 6.290. Cf. Od. 14.452, Od. 15.158, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: In reference to source or origin : ἄλλος κε πὰρ Διὸς χόλος ἐτύχθη Il. 15.122.
To a point from which action takes place : φθεγξάμενος παρὰ νηός Il. 11.603.

There is (are) by or present : πάρα γὸρ
καὶ ἀμείνονες ἄλλοι Il. 23.479.
There is (are) available or at one's command or disposal, there is (are) here or there for or aiding one.

With or without dat. : πάρʼ ἔμοιγε καὶ ἄλλοι Il. 1.174. Cf. Il. 5.603, 604, Il. 9.43, 227, Il. 20.98, Il. 21.192 : πάρα τοι δίφρος τε καὶ ἵπποι, πὰρ δέ τοι υἶες ἐμοί Od. 3.324. Cf. Od. 3.351, Od. 4.559= Od. 5.16= Od. 17.145, Od. 5.141, 489 (here for παρέωσιν), Od. 9.125, Od. 16.45, Od. 17.452, Od. 22.106.
It is possible : ἐπεὶ οὐ μέν τι πάρα προνοῆσαι ἄμεινον Od. 5.364.
With dat. : παρβεβαῶτʼ ἕστασαν ἀλλήλοιιν (fronted the foe holding united course) Il. 13.708.
Sim. of accompanying another in a chariot : Ἕκτορι παρβεβαώς (standing beside him (as charioteer)) Il. 11.522.
In mid., to set down (a stake) beside others or by the side of an umpire; hence, to set at hazard, risk (cf.> παρατίθημι2) : αἰὲν ἐμὴν ψυχὴν παραβαλλόμενος Il. 9.322.
To act as παραιβάτης : Ἄντιφος παρέβασκεν Il. 11.104.
App., risking the experiment : ἐπειρᾶτʼ ἐρεθιζέμεν Ἥρην, παραβλήδην ἀγορεύων (drawing her fire, provoking a retort, provokingly) Il. 4.6.
3 sing. pf. παρμέμβλωκε (παρ-, παρα-) Il. 4.11, Il. 24.73.
With dat. : τῷ Ἀφροδίτη αἰεὶ παρμέμβλωκεν (attends, protects) Il. 4.11. Cf. Il. 24.73.
With sidelong or furtive glance Il. 9.503 (of the λιταί (see λιτή) as figuring an offender, who cannot look the injured person in the face).

p.gloss: To be beside, be in attendance upon.

div.p: With dat. : παρεγίγνετό σφι δαιτί (attended upon them at the . . .) Od. 17.173.

p.gloss: To sleep, go to sleep, take one's rest, beside.

div.p: With dat. : παρέδραθέ μοι Od. 20.88. Cf. Il. 14.163.
To receive from another : σῆμα Il. 6.178.
To do work in attendance upon, serve.
With dat. : οἷά τε τοῖς ἀγαθοῖσι παραδρώωσι χέρηες Od. 15.324.
With dat. : ἔοικά τοι παραείδειν Od. 22.348.
In pass., to hang down by the side, on one side : παρηέρθη κάρη Il. 16.341.
[παραι- 2 + βα-, βαίνω. He that goes beside.]
The fighting man in a warchariot as distinguished from the ἡνίοχος or driver : παραιβάται ἡνίοχοί τε Il. 23.132.
3 sing. aor. παρήϊξε Il. 5.690, Il. 8.98, 3 pl. παρήϊξαν Od. 11.615.
To dart past Il. 5.690, Il. 8.98, Il. 20.414.
With acc. : ἵπποι με παρήϊξαν Il. 11.615.
Persuasion : ὀαριστὺς πάρφασις Il. 14.217 (winning dalliance). Cf. Il. 11.793= Il. 15.404.
To throw down in readiness : ὕλην Il. 23.127.
In Il. 23.683 (ζῶμά οἱ παρακάββαλεν) the sense required seems to be put about him.
In mid., to lie down beside, lie with.
With dat. : πῇ παρκατέλεκτο Il. 9.565. Cf. Il. 9.664.
To be beside one, at one's hand or laid up, in readiness or for use, be there : ὀϊστόν, ὅ οἱ παρέκειτο τραπέζῃ Od. 21.416. Cf. Il. 24.476 : Od. 14.521.
Fig., to lie before one as a matter of choice. Impers. : νῦν ὑμῖν παράκειται ἐναντίον ἠὲ μάχεσθαι ἢ φεύγειν Od. 22.65.
To bend or turn (something) aside : κεφαλήν Od. 20.301.
To turn aside, deviate from the course, swerve Il. 23.424.
To let hang by one's side Il. 13.597.
With dat. : λαοδαμείῃ Il. 6.198. Cf. Il. 2.515, Il. 16.184 : Od. 11.242.
In reference to Here and Zeus Il. 14.237.
>To Boreas and the mares of Erichthonius Il. 20.224.
In mid., to go past, pass by : τόν Od. 6.310.

p.gloss: To remain with (a person), keep (him) company.

div.p: With dat. : οὐκέτι τοι δύναμαι παρμενέμεν Il. 15.400.
So to stand by in the fight : οὐδέ τις αὐτῷ Ἀργείων παρέμεινεν Il. 11.402. Cf. Il. 13.151.
To remain or abide with a person Od. 3.115.
With dat. and infin. : τοῖς ἄλλοισιν οἴκαδʼ ἀποπλείειν Il. 9.417, 684. Cf. Il. 15.45.
To heap or pile up in readiness for use : σῖτον παρενήνεον ἐν κανέοισιν Od. 1.147. Cf. Od. 16.51.
To swim, make one's way by swimming, along the shore.
[app. formed fr. παρά as ἄναντα fr. ἀνά.]
3 sing. aor. παρέπεισε Il. 7.120, Il. 13.788, Il. 23.606.
3 sing. aor. subj. παραιπεπίθῃσι (παραι-, παρα-) Od. 22.213.
To induce to an act or a course of action, persuade, prevail upon, win over Il. 7.120= Il. 13.788, Il. 14.208, Il. 23.37, 606 : Od. 14.290, Od. 22.213, Od. 24.119.
To conduct or pilot (safely) past a danger Od. 12.72.
To cause to deviate from the proper course : παρεπλάγχθη οἱ ἄλλῃ ἰός (went wide) Il. 15.464.

p.gloss: To drive from one's course and away from.

div.p: With genit. : κυθήρων Od. 9.81. Cf. Od. 19.187.
To disturb or derange (the mind) Od. 20.346.
Of spits projecting from the shore, on which the seas break aslant : ἠϊόνας Od. 5.418= 440.
To sail past a place Od. 12.69.
Of wind, to blow past something : ἵνα μή τι παραπνεύσειʼ ὀλίγον περ Od. 10.24 (i.e. so that none of the winds might slip past the fastening of the bag).
Absol. in pl., words of persuasion : παραρρητοῖσι πιθέσθαι Il. 13.726.
To balk or thwart a person : παρέσφηλεν γὰρ Ἀπόλλων (caused him to miss his aim) Il. 8.311.
To make or order differently : οὐδέ κεν ἄλλως Ζεὺς αὐτὸς παρατεκτήναιτο (could help us) Il. 14.54 : ἔπος κε παρατεκτήναιο (tell a story differing from the truth, a cozening tale) Od. 14.131.
Aor. opt. mid. παραθείμην Od. 15.506, Od. 19.150.
Nom. pl. masc. pple. παρθέμενοι Od. 2.237, Od. 3.74, Od. 9.255. From παρτιθέω
To set or place beside a person : ἐπεὶ δαίδας παραθεῖτο (παραθείμην) (had had them set) Od. 2.105= Od. 24.140, Od. 19.150. Cf. Od. 5.92.
With dat. : τράπεζαν, τὴν ἥν οἱ παρέθηκεν Od. 21.29. Cf. Od. 4.133, Od. 9.326.
To set (food or drink) before a person : ξείνιά τʼ εὖ παρέθηκεν Il. 11.779. Cf. Od. 1.139, 141, Od. 18.120, etc.
With dat. : ἀμφιπόλῳ, ἥ οἱ βρῶσίν τε πόσιν τε παρτιθεῖ Od. 1.192. Cf. Il. 18.408, Il. 23.810 : Od. 4.66, Od. 14.76, Od. 16.49.
In mid., to set at hazard, risk (cf. παραβάλλω) : σφὰς παρθέμενοι κεφαλάς Od. 2.237. Cf. Od. 3.74= Od. 9.255.
To run past a point, pass a point at a run Il. 10.350, Il. 22.157.

p.gloss: To run past, outstrip in a race.

div.p: To rush aside in affright : παρέτρεσσάν οἱ ἵπποι Il. 5.295.
To turn away from the point, put off : παρατροπέων με Od. 4.465.
To bend the mind of, win over : θεοὺς θυέεσσι παρατρωπῶσιν Il. 9.500.
To use persuasion to, endeavour to induce to an act or a course of action, urge Od. 16.279, Od. 18.178 (talk me not into this).
To speak in comfortable terms to : μένʼ εἰς ὅ κε μύθοις ἀγανοῖσι παραυδήσας ἀποπέμψῃ (cheer you on your way) Od. 15.53.
To speak comfortably of, minister false comfort in regard to : θάνατον Od. 11.488.
To pass a point in safety Od. 12.99.
Pres. pple. mid. παραιφάμενος (παραι-, παρα-) Il. 24.771. παρφάμενος (παρ-, παρα-) Il. 12.249 : Od. 2.189.
With dat. and infin. : μητρὶ παράφημι πατρὶ ἐπὶ ἦρα φέρειν Il. 1.577.
To induce to a course of action, persuade, prevail upon, win over.
In mid. : παρφάμενος ἐπέεσσιν Il. 12.249. Cf. Il. 24.771 : Od. 2.189.
To use evasive speech to, put off.
In mid. : μνηστῆρας μαλακοῖς ἐπέεσσι παρφάσθαι Od. 16.287= Od. 19.6.
3 sing. aor. opt. παραφθαίησι (app. formed on the analogy of subjunctives in -ῃσι) Il. 10.346.
To outstrip, get ahead of : ἄμμε Il. 10.346. Cf. Il. 22.197.
The skin of a panther Il. 3.17, Il. 10.29.
In pres. and in impf. (or non-sigmatic aor.; see ἕζομαι).
To seat oneself, sit down, take one's seat, beside a person : παρέζεο καὶ λαβὲ γούνων Il. 1.407.

p.gloss: To seat oneself, sit down, take one's seat, beside.

div.p: With dat. : σοὶ παρέζετο Il. 1.557. Cf. Il. 5.889 : Od. 4.738, Od. 20.334.
The cheeks : ὦχρός μιν εἷλε παρειάς Il. 3.35. Cf. Il. 11.393, Il. 18.123, Il. 22.491, Il. 24.794 : Od. 1.334, Od. 4.198, Od. 8.522, Od. 11.529, Od. 18.172, etc.
In reference to eagles : δρυψαμένω ὀνύχεσσι παρειάς Od. 2.153.
3 sing. opt. παρείη Il. 22.20 : Od. 2.62, Od. 18.370.
Infin. παρέμμεναι Il. 18.472 : Od. 4.640. παρεῖναι Il. 22.298 : Od. 5.105, 129, Od. 17.347.
3 sing. παρέσσεται Il. 1.213, Il. 9.135, 277, Il. 18.466. παρέσται Il. 10.217.

To be by or present, be in a specified or indicated place, be present at something, be with one, be here or there : πάρεστέ τε, ἴστε τε πάντα (are present (at all that happens)) Il. 2.485, ἐν δαίτῃσι παρέσται Il. 10.217. Cf. Il. 15.325, 665, Il. 22.298, Il. 24.475 (in attendance) : Od. 8.491, Od. 11.66, Od. 14.145, Od. 15.74, 335.
With dat., to be present or in company with, be with : ἄγασθέ μοι ἄνδρα παρεῖναι Od. 5.129, ἐγώ γέ τοι παρέσσομαι (shall be found at your side) Od. 13.393. Cf. Il. 11.75 : Od. 4.640, Od. 5.105.
To be present at : μάχῃ Od. 4.497.

To be available or at one's command or disposal, be here or there for one : ἵπποι οὐ παρέασιν Il. 5.192, Il. 14.299. Cf. Il. 8.294, Il. 9.135 = 277, Il. 13.786 : Od. 13.247, Od. 14.444, Od. 17.457, Od. 18.370, Od. 23.128–In neut. pple. pl., one's resources, one's store : χαριζομένη παρεόντων (genit. of material, from her store) Od. 1.140= Od. 4.56= Od. 7.176= Od. 10.372= Od. 15.139= Od. 17.95.
With dat., to be available to, be there or at command for : εἴ μοι δύναμίς γε παρείη Il. 22.20. Cf. Il. 1.213, Il. 18.466, 472 : Od. 2.62, Od. 8.417, Od. 14.80.
Of a quality, to be present in, be found in: αἰδὼς οὐκ ἀγαθὴ κεχρημένῳ ἀνδρὶ παρεῖναι Od. 17.347.
To pass a point, go past or by : μή ἑ λάθοι παριών Od. 4.527. Cf. Od. 17.233.
To use persuasion, endeavour to induce a person to a course of action. urge (something) upon him : αἴσιμα παρειπών Il. 6.62, Il. 7.121. Cf. Il. 11.793= Il. 15.404.
To persuade, win over, talk over : μή σε παρείπῃ Il. 1.555. Cf. Il. 6.337.
Out along : νῆχε π. (along the shore) Od. 5.439.
Passing a point, past : π. ἐλάαν Od. 12.47, 109.

Aside from the straight line, diverging : π. ἀγορευέμεν (app., to wrong purpose) Il. 12.213 : οὐκ ἂν ἄλλα π. εἴποιμι (away from the point) Od. 4.348= Od. 17.139, ἄλλα π. μεμνώμεθα (passing from him) Od. 14.168, ταῦτα π. ἐρέουσα (to bring me this false news) Od. 23.16.
Out beside something : στῆ π. (forth beside him) Il. 11.486.
Out, off : ὦσα [νῆα] π. Od. 9.488 (perh. implying a sidelong movement).

div.head: a
div.p: Along and outside of : νῆσος π. λιμένος τετάνυσται (i.e. across the mouth) Od. 9.116.

div.head: a
div.p: Along, alongside of : π. ἅλα Il. 9.7.

div.head: b
div.p: Past, leaving on one side or behind, passing, beyond : σῆμα π. Ἴλοιο Il. 24.349. Cf. Il. 23.762 : Od. 12.55, 276, 443 (on the further side of), Od. 15.199.
Sim. : π. νόον (in defiance of . . .) Il. 10.391, Il. 20.133, δῶρα π. Ἀχιλῆα δέχεσθαι (behind, his back) Il. 24.434.

div.head: c
div.p: Out beyond : π. τειχίον αὐλῆς Od. 16.165, 343.
To slip past, elude (a person) : μή σε π. ἄεθλα Il. 23.314.
3 sing. aor. παρήλασε Od. 12.186. παρέλασσε Il. 23.382, 527.

div.head: a
div.p: To drive one's chariot past another, outstrip him in the race : ἤ κε παρέλασσʼ ἢ ἀμφήριστον ἔθηκεν Il. 23.382. Cf. Il. 23.427.

div.head: b
div.p: To sail past a specified point : οὔ πώ τις τῇδε παρήλασεν Od. 12.186.

div.head: a
div.p: To drive past, out-strip, in the chariot-race : παρέλασσέ κέ μιν Il. 23.527. Cf. Il. 23.638.
To use shifts, evade the issue Od. 21.111.
In mid., to draw off to oneself, gain by trickery : δῶρα Od. 18.282.
To pass by, slip past, make good one's passage : παρεξελθεῖν πεδίοιο (local genit.) Il. 10.344 : ῥεῖα παρεξελθοῦσα Od. 10.573.

p.gloss: To get oneself past, defeat, frustrate.

div.p: To pass, make good one's passage Od. 12.62, Od. 16.357.
In reference to the passage of a wave Od. 5.429.
With acc., to go past, pass, leave on one side or behind : τεὸν βωμόν Il. 8.239.
To overreach, get the better of, outwit Il. 1.132 : Od. 13.291.
3 sing. aor. subj. παράσχῃ Il. 3.354 : Od. 15.55.

To furnish, provide, supply, present, give, grant : δῶρα Il. 19.140, 147. Cf. Il. 18.556, Il. 23.835 : ἀρετήν Od. 18.133. Cf. Od. 4.89, Od. 6.28, Od. 8.39, Od. 14.250, Od. 15.490, Od. 18.317, 360, Od. 19.113, Od. 20.8.
To afford, show, manifest : φιλότητα Il. 3.354 : Od. 15.55.
A cheek ornament for a horse : παρήϊον ἔμμεναι ἵππων (general pl., for some horse) Il. 4.142.
To sit by or beside a person : ὡς μή μοι τρύζητε παρήμενοι Il. 9.311. Cf. Il. 24.652 : Od. 1.339, Od. 13.411, Od. 14.375, Od. 17.521, Od. 18.231, Od. 19.209.
With dat., to sit by or beside : παρήμενός μοι τέρπειν Od. 19.589.
To sit at, by, in the enjoyment of : δαιτὶ παρήμενος Od. 1.26. Cf. Od. 17.456.
To abide, be, by or with : σύεσσιν Od. 13.407.

p.gloss: To sit idle, doing nothing, by or beside.

div.p: The traces attaching the παρήορος (see παρήορος. 2) Il. 8.87, Il. 16.152.
[παρ-, παρα- 2 + ἠορ-, ἀείρω. Hung on at the side, dangling loosely. Cf. συνήορος, τετράοροι.]
Loose or uncontrolled in mind, flighty Il. 23.603.
As sb., an extra trace-horse attached to a chariot Il. 16.471, 474.
nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. mid. παρατίθημι.
A young unmarried woman, a maid, a maiden, a girl Il. 2.514, Il. 18.593, Il. 22.127, 128 : Od. 6.33, 109, 228.
In pass., to hang down by the side of something, to hang down loosely : παρείθη μήρινθος Il. 23.868.
2 sing. aor. παρ-έστης Il. 3.405, Il. 5.116, Il. 10.290.
Infin. παρεστάμεναι Il. 15.255, Il. 17.563, Il. 21.231 : Od. 4.827, Od. 20.94.

To take up a position, take one's stand, come and stand, by or beside a person or thing, come up to or approach a person : τὸν ἐρητύσασκε παραστάς Il. 2.189. Cf. Il. 3.405 (have come here), Il. 4.212, Il. 7.188, Il. 12.60, Il. 17.119, Il. 24.303 (presented herself), etc.: πέλεκυν ἔχων παρίστατο Od. 3.443. Cf. Od. 7.341, Od. 8.218, Od. 10.109, Od. 15.123, Od. 17.73 (went up to him), Od. 23.87, etc.

p.gloss: To take up a position, take one's stand, come and stand, by or beside, come up to, approach.
