Reaching to the feet : δέρμα λέοντος Il. 10.24= 178, ἀσπίδα (i.e. such as to cover the whole of the bearer when the rim rested on the ground) Il. 15.646.
[ποδ-, πούς + ἄνεμος. Like the wind in feet.]
Swift-footed : ἵππους Il. 2.764, Il. 17.614. Cf. Il. 10.316, Il. 23.262 (app. with transference of epithet from horses to drivers), 376.

In local sense : τίς π. εἰς ἀνδρῶν; Il. 21.150 : Od. 1.170= Od. 10.325= Od. 14.187= Od. 15.264= Od. 19.105= Od. 24.298, Od. 7.238 (or poss. these passages may be referred to (2)). Cf. Od. 3.71= Od. 9.252, Od. 16.57.
In indirect construction : εἰρώτα (εἴροντο) τίς εἴη καὶ π. ἔλθοι Od. 15.423, Od. 17.368.
In reference to race or origin. In indirect construction : οὐκ οἶδα π. γένος εὔχεται εἶναι (whence in the matter of race, i.e. of what stock he claims to be) Od. 17.373.
From some or any place or quarter : ἐλθών ποθεν Od. 1.115, Od. 20.224. Cf. Od. 1.414, Od. 2.351, Od. 7.52, Od. 14.374, Od. 18.376, Od. 21.195, Od. 24.149.
In reference to finding, somewhere : εἴ ποθεν ἐξεύροι Il. 18.322.
From any source : εἴ ποθεν ἄλλα γένοιτο Il. 9.380. Cf. Od. 5.490, Od. 22.62.

To feel the want of, long for, yearn for, mourn for, a person or thing absent or lost: ἀϋτήν τε πτόλεμόν τε Il. 1.492. Cf. Il. 5.414, Il. 23.16, Il. 24.6 : τοίην κεφαλήν Od. 1.343. Cf. Od. 9.453, Od. 11.196 (sick with hope of it deferred), Od. 12.110, Od. 18.204, Od. 19.136.
To miss, to feel the want of, be at a loss on account of or distressed by the absence or want of : ἀρχόν Il. 2.703 = 726, 778. Cf. Il. 2.709, Il. 5.234, Il. 11.161, Il. 15.219 : Od. 22.387.
To miss, remark the absence or loss of : πρίν [μʼ] αὐτὴν ποθέσαι Od. 2.375. Cf. Od. 4.748, Od. 13.219, Od. 16.287= Od. 19.6.
A longing, yearning or mourning for a person or thing absent or lost : σῇ ποθῇ (through mourning for you) Il. 19.321.

A missing a person or thing, a feeling at a loss or in distress on account of his or its absence or loss : Ἀχιλλῆος Il. 1.240. Cf. Il. 6.362, Il. 11.471, Il. 14.368, Il. 17.690, 704 : Od. 2.126, Od. 8.414, Od. 10.505.
In what place ? where ? π. τοι πόλις; Od. 1.170= Od. 10.325= Od. 14.187= Od. 15.264= Od. 19.105= Od. 24.298.
Somewhere : ἠέ ποθι πτολέμοιο μέγα στόμα [τεύχων] Il. 10.8.
In negative or conditional contexts, anywhere : οὐδέ ποθι νέφος ἐστίν Od. 20.114. Cf. Il. 13.309 : Od. 17.195.
In any part : οὐδέ ποθι μιαρός Il. 24.420.
Qualifying an expression, haply, I ween, no doubt, as it would seem : ἀλλά ποθι Ζεὺς αἴτιος Od. 1.348. Cf. Il. 13.630, Il. 19.273, Il. 24.209.
= ποθή 1 Il. 17.439 : Od. 4.596, Od. 11.202 (mourning for you), Od. 14.144.

To make, construct, form, fabricate, fashion, prepare : δῶμα Il. 1.608, σάκος Il. 7.222. Cf. Il. 6.316, Il. 7.339, 435, Il. 15.363, Il. 20.12, etc. : Od. 1.239, Od. 4.796, Od. 5.253, Od. 6.10, Od. 8.373, Od. 17.207, etc.
To make or prepare (a bed) : πεποίηταί τοι εὐνή Od. 7.342.
To make, bring about, cause, cause to come into existence or take place : φόβον Il. 12.432, αἴθρην Il. 17.646. Cf. Il. 12.30, Il. 13.120 : Od. 1.250= Od. 16.127, Od. 5.452, Od. 19.34.
To put (into a person's mind), suggest : ἐνὶ φρεσὶν ὦδε νόημα ποίησεν Od. 14.274.
In mid. : πέντε ἡγεμόνας ποιήσατο Il. 16.171.
To make, cause to be (so and so).
With complementary adj. : ἄφρονα ποιῆσαι καὶ ἐπίφρονʼ ἐόντα Od. 23.12. Cf. Il. 1.461= Il. 2.424 := Od. 3.458= Od. 12.361, Od. 1.235, Od. 9.327, 524, Od. 13.42.
With sim. sb. : μὴ σέ γε βασιλῆα ποιήσειεν Od. 1.387. Cf. Il. 24.537, 611: Od. 16.456, Od. 17.271.
With infin. : ἐπεί σε θεοὶ ποίησαν ἱκέσθαι οἶκον Od. 23.258.
To do, effect, perform : ἦ σοὶ ἄριστα πεποίηται; Il. 6.56.
In mid. : οὐδέ τινʼ ἄλλην μύθου ποιήσασθαι ἐπισχεσίην ἐδύνασθε (could put forward no other plea) Od. 21.71.
Grassy, grass-clad : ἄγκεα Od. 4.337= Od. 17.128. Cf. Il. 20.9 := Od. 6.124.
Of places, grassy, with grassy meadows Il. 2.503, Il. 9.150 = 292 : Od. 16.396.
Made, constructed, fabricated : σάκεος πύκα ποιητοῖο Il. 18.608. Cf. Il. 5.466 : Od. 1.333= Od. 8.458= Od. 16.415= Od. 18.209= Od. 21.64, Od. 1.436, Od. 22.455.
Epithet of various products of art, well made, constructed or fabricated (εὐποίητος): δόμοις Il. 5.198, τρίποδος Il. 23.718. Cf. Il. 10.262, Il. 12.470, Il. 23.340 : Od. 13.306.
To make, form, fashion, with curious art Il. 18.590.
In pl., broidery, ornamental variegated work in wool : κάλλιστος ποικίλμασιν Il. 6.294 := Od. 15.107.

p.gloss: Of many and various devices or wiles.

div.p: Absol. in voc. addressed to Odysseus : ποικιλομῆτα Od. 13.293.
Parti-coloured, marked with patches of a different colour or shade, dappled : παρδαλέῃ Il. 10.30 : ἐλλόν Od. 19.228.

p.gloss: Wrought or ornamented with curious art, elaborately wrought or ornamented.

div.p: With reference to broidery or ornamental variegated work in wool, etc. : πέπλον Il. 5.735= Il. 8.386. Cf. Il. 14.215, 220, Il. 22.441 : Od. 18.293.– Of various products of art : ἅρματα ποικίλα χαλκῷ (with . . ., i.e. having the metal parts curiously wrought) Il. 4.226, Il. 10.322, 393, θώρηκα Il. 16.134. Cf. Il. 3.327, Il. 4.432, Il. 5.239, Il. 6.504, Il. 10.75, 149, 501, 504, Il. 12.396, Il. 13.181, 537= Il. 14.431, Il. 14.420 : κλισμόν Od. 1.132. Cf. Od. 3.492= Od. 15.145 = 190.
Elaborately contrived, intricate, complicated : δεσμόν Od. 8.448.
Absol., to tend one's flock, act as shepherd : ποιμαίνων (ποιμαίνοντʼ) ἐπʼ ὄεσσιν Il. 6.25, Il. 11.106.
In pass., of flocks, to roam the pastures : αἶγας καὶ ὄϊς, τά οἱ ἄσπετα ποιμαίνοντο Il. 11.245.

A shepherd (in Od. 10.82 app. including herdsman and this sense is possible in all the passages except Il. 5.137, Il. 12.451, Il. 13.493 and Il. 16.354, where the sense shepherd (in Il. 16.354 including goatherd) is required) Il. 3.11, Il. 4.455, Il. 5.137, Il. 8.559, Il. 12.451, Il. 13.493, Il. 16.354, Il. 18.162, Il. 23.835 : Od. 4.87 Od. 10.82.

Of kings and chiefs, π. λαῶν, shepherd of the host. Applied to AgamemnonIl. 2.243, 254, 772= Il. 7.230, Il. 4.413, Il. 10.3, Il. 11.187, 202, Il. 14.22, Il. 19.35, 251, Il. 24.654 : Od. 3.156, Od. 4.532, Od. 14.497.
Of or pertaining to a flock : σταθμὸν ποιμνήϊον (a sheep-farm) Il. 2.470.
A blood-price, a sum paid as compensation and satisfaction by a homicide to the family of the slain man : εἵνεκα ποινῆς ἀνδρὸς ἀποφθιμένου Il. 18.498. Cf. Il. 9.633, 636.
In reference to requital or vengeance for men slain in battle Il. 13.659, Il. 14.483, Il. 16.398, Il. 21.28 (to pay the price of his blood in their persons).
So of the vengeance taken on the Cyclops Od. 23.312.
Something given in recompense for loss or deprivation, amends : ποινὴν γανυμήδεος (for the loss of . . .) Il. 5.266. Cf. Il. 17.207.
A sum to be paid by an enemy as compensation for loss or damage, an indemnity : μαχήσομαι εἵνεκα ποινῆς Il. 3.290 (= τιμήν 286, 288).
Of what nature, kind, or sort ? ποῖοί κʼ εἶτʼ Ὀδυσῆϊ ἀμυνέμεν; (what sort of helpers would he find you?) Od. 21.195.
Without special reference to nature, etc., what ? ποίῃ νηΐ σʼ ἤγαγον; Od. 16.222.
Carrying on an indirect question : ἐρέσθαι ὁππόθεν οὗτος ἀνήρ, ποίης δʼ ἐξ εὔχεται εἶναι γαίης Od. 1.406.

Rather exclamatory than interrogative, expressing surprise or anger : ποῖον τὸν μῦθον ἔειπες (what a word is this that you have said !) Il. 1.552. Cf. Il. 4.350, Il. 8.209, etc. : Od. 1.64, Od. 3.230, Od. 21.168, etc.
Absol. : ποῖον ἔειπες Il. 13.824. Cf. Il. 23.570 : Od. 2.85= Od. 17.406, Od. 2.243.

To show activity, exert oneself, be busy : διὰ δώματα ποιπνύοντα (bustling about) Il. 1.600. Cf. Il. 8.219 (to bestir himself and . . .), Il. 14.155 (showing himself everywhere), Il. 18.421 (nimbly played their part), Il. 24.475 (were doing busy service) : Od. 3.430 (busied themselves), Od. 20.149 (bestir yourselves and . . .).
Of or for war, warlike : ἔργα Il. 2.338, Il. 5.428, Il. 7.236, Il. 11.719, Il. 13.727, 730, τεύχεα Il. 7.193 : ἔργα Od. 12.116.
Pple. πολεμίξων Il. 10.451, Il. 15.179. πτολεμίξων Il. 13.644.

To fight, do battle, take part in the fight, engage in fight : ἐπεί κε κάμω πολεμίζων Il. 1.168, πολεμίζειν οὐκ εἴασκον Il. 5.802. Cf. Il. 2.328, Il. 4.300, Il. 5.520, Il. 8.428, Il. 9.318, etc : Od. 13.315= Od. 15.153, Od. 14.240.
Of single combat Il. 3.67, Il. 7.152, Il. 15.179, Il. 20.85, etc.
To fight, engage in fight, do battle, with.
With dat. : πολεμιζέμεναι Τρώεσσιν Il. 9.337. Cf. Il. 2.121, Il. 11.279, Il. 16.89, Il. 19.168, 325 : Od. 3.86.
With the dat. suppressed : ῥηΐτεροι πολεμίζειν (to fight with) Il. 18.258.
With dat. : εἰ σοὶ πτολεμίξω Il. 21.463. Cf. Il. 3.435, Il. 7.42, 169, Il. 9.356, Il. 15.539.
With cognate acc. : πόλεμον πολεμίζειν Il. 2.121, Il. 3.435.
With implied notion of stoutness : πολεμιστὰ μετʼ ἀνδράσιν Il. 16.492.
To the fight : κηρύσσειν Il. 2.443, ὀτρύνων 589. Cf. Il. 2.872, Il. 4.264, Il. 7.209, Il. 13.186, Il. 18.452, etc. : Od. 21.39.

War, battle, armed conflict, fighting : πόλεμος καὶ λοιμός Il. 1.61, ἀϋτήν τε πτόλεμόν τε 492. Cf. Il. 1.422, Il. 2.384, Il. 5.388, Il. 6.328, 492, Il. 8.35, etc. : Od. 1.12, Od. 4.146, Od. 5.224, Od. 10.553, Od. 11.537, Od. 14.222, etc.

A battle, armed conflict, fight (in some of the passages more or less of a local sense (field of battle) may be discerned) : ἐς πόλεμον θωρηχθῆναι (for the fray) Il. 1.226, ὁππότʼ ἄρξειαν πολέμοιο Il. 4.335, ἐκφερέμεν πολέμοιο Il. 5.234, λιπὼν πόλεμον Il. 6.254. Cf. Il. 1.491, Il. 3.435, Il. 5.132, Il. 6.480, Il. 11.524, Il. 12.436, Il. 13.11, Il. 17.735, Il. 21.610, etc. : Od. 8.519, Od. 24.43.
In concrete sense, a fighting force or throng, an army or host : πόλεμον κορύσσων (setting the battle in array) Il. 2.273. Cf. Il. 9.604, Il. 13.536, etc.
The art of war, war, fighting : ἰδρείῃ πολέμοιο Il. 16.359. Cf. Il. 9.440, Il. 16.811.
In pl. : πολέμων ἐῢ εἰδώς Il. 4.310.
To go about, go to and fro : κατὰ ἄστυ Od. 22.223.
To found (a city) : οὔ πω Ἴλιος ἐν πεδίῳ πεπόλιστο Il. 20.217.
= πολίτης: κοσμησάμενος πολιήτας (the men of his own city) Il. 2.806.

p.gloss: Of an indeterminate lightish hue (app. without reference to colour), grey, greyish.

div.p: Of the sea (app. referring orig. to the light hue of shallow water) Il. 1.350, Il. 4.248, Il. 15.190, Il. 20.229, etc.: Od. 2.261, Od. 4.580, Od. 5.410, Od. 6.272, Od. 11.75, etc.
In reference to hair, of the hue assumed in old age, grey or white Il. 22.77.
In reference to the head or chin, covered with grey or white hair : κάρη, γένειον Il. 22.74, Il. 24.516 : κεφαλῆς Od. 24.317.
In reference to men, grey- or white-headed Od. 24.499.
Nom. pl. πόλιες Od. 15.412. πόληες Il. 4.45, 51 : Od. 19.174.
Genit. πολίων Il. 1.125, Il. 2.117, Il. 3.400, etc. : Od. 24.418.
Acc. pl. πόλιας Od. 8.560, 574. πόλεας Il. 4.308. πόλεις Il. 2.648, Il. 9.328, Il. 18.342, 490. πόληας Od. 17.486.
A town or city (cf. ἄστυ) Il. 1.19, Il. 2.12, Il. 4.4, Il. 5.473, etc. : Od. 1.170 (your native city), Od. 2.154, Od. 3.85, Od. 5.101, etc.
With the name of a particular town in apposition : πόλιν Τροίην Il. 1.129. Cf. Il. 2.739, Il. 6.152, Il. 9.530, Il. 11.711 : Od. 11.510.
In genit. : Ἰλίου πόλιν Il. 5.642. Cf. Il. 7.345 : Od. 10.416.
πόλις ἄκρη (ἀκροτάτη), the highest part of a city, the citadel : ἐν πόλει ἄκρῃ Il. 6.88, 297, 317, Il. 7.345, ἐν πόλει ἀκροτάτῃ Il. 22.172. Cf. Il. 6.257, Il. 20.52, Il. 22.383.
So without ἄκρη : ὣς φάτʼ ἀπὸ πτόλιος θεός Il. 4.514. Cf. Il. 17.144 (see ἄστυ).
With special reference to the inhabitants or community : Τρώων πόλις ἐπὶ πᾶσα βέβηκεν (the whole cityful of them) Il. 16.69, ὄφελος πτόλεΐ τε καὶ αὐτῷ Il. 17.152. Cf. Il. 3.50, Il. 24.706.
In pl., the dwellers in a town or city, the citizens : ὅθεν ἱδρεύοντο πολῖται Od. 7.131, Od. 17.206. Cf. Il. 15.558, Il. 22.429.
-ή, -όν, πολύς, -ύ, πουλύς (the last fem. Il. 5.776, Il. 8.50, Il. 10.27 : Od. 4.709). From πολύς genit. πολέος Il. 4.244, Il. 5.597, Il. 23.475, 521, 562 : Od. 2.126, Od. 8.405, Od. 20.25.

In pl., of great number, many : πολλὰς ψυχάς (many a . . .) Il. 1.3, πολέες περ ἐόντες Il. 5.94. Cf. Il. 2.91, Il. 3.99, Il. 4.143, Il. 5.383 (many a one of us), Il. 6.296, etc. : πολλῶν ἀνθρώπων Od. 1.3, τὰ πολλὰ κατάνεται (these things, many as they are, are wasted, our great substance dwindles away) Od. 2.58 = Od. 17.537. Cf. Od. 1.4, Od. 2.166, Od. 3.262, Od. 4.3, Od. 8.217, Od. 9.352 (of the multitudes of men), etc.
In sing. with nouns of multitude, consisting of many individuals, numerous, great, vast : πολὺν ὅμιλον Il. 5.334. Cf. Il. 8.472, Il. 13.472, etc. : Od. 8.109, Od. 17.67, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: Absol. in masc. and fem. pl. πολλοί (πολλαί), πολέες, many men or women, many a man or woman, many : ὡς ὀλέσῃς πολέας Il. 1.559, ἐκπρεπἔ ἐν πολλοῖσιν (in the multitude) Il. 2.483, πολλῇσι κήδεʼ ἐφῆπτο Il. 6.241. Cf. Il. 1.242, Il. 2.161, Il. 4.230, Il. 5.176, Il. 9.73, etc. : Od. 4.257, Od. 8.17, Od. 13.239, Od. 20.30, Od. 21.367, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: οἱ πολλοί, the greater part of an indicated number, most of them(cf. 4.b) : τῶν πολλῶν Ἄρης ὑπὸ γούνατʼ ἔλυσεν Il. 24.498.

div.head: a
div.p: Absol. in neut. pl. πολλά, many things, much: ὅτι οἱ π. διδοῦσιν Il. 2.255. Cf. Il. 1.156, Il. 9.320, Il. 10.4, Il. 11.684, Il. 14.67, etc. : Od. 1.427, Od. 2.102, Od. 4.81, Od. 6.174, Od. 11.83, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: τὰ πολλά in sense sim. to that of 3.b : τὰ π. ἐτώσια θῆκεν Od. 22.273.

In sing., of great amount, quantity, abundance or volume, much : πολὺν λαόν Il. 2.115, πολὺς ὀρυμαγδός 810, πολλὸν φῦκος Il. 9.7. Cf. Il. 3.381, Il. 6.525, Il. 9.469, Il. 10.6, Il. 13.804, etc. : Od. 2.126, Od. 4.258, Od. 5.323, Od. 6.86, Od. 14.136, etc.

So in pl. with sb. in collective sense : κρέα πολλά Il. 8.231. Cf. Il. 8.507, Il. 9.97 (much folk), 116 (many men), Il. 18.560, Il. 24.556, etc. : ἔεδνα πολλά (a great dowry) Od. 1.278, ὄψα πολλά Od. 5.267. Cf. Od. 1.112, Od. 9.266, Od. 11.379, Od. 19.64, etc.

div.head: a
div.p: In reference to extension in space, wide, broad, far-stretching : πολέος πεδίοιο Il. 4.244, πολλός τις ἔκειτο (like some monster extended long and large) Il. 7.156. Cf. Il. 10.27, Il. 20.249, etc.: Od. 2.364, etc.
Absol. : ἐπὶ πολλὸν ἑλίσσεται (wheels wide) Il. 23.320.

div.head: b
div.p: Of great size, large : τύμβον οὐ πολλόν Il. 23.245. Cf. Od. 12.45.

div.head: c
div.p: Of great length, long : πολλὴν ὁδόν Od. 21.20.
So of time, long : πολὐν χρόνον Il. 2.343, Il. 3.157, Il. 12.9 : Od. 2.115, Od. 4.543, 594, etc. Cf. Od. 12.407, etc.
In neut. sing. πολλόν, πολύ, as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Greatly, much, in a high degree, to a great extent, far : πολὺ πρίν Il. 9.250. Cf. Il. 19.113, etc. : Od. 2.167.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to position or motion, far : πολὺ πρὸ ἑτάρων Il. 4.373, πολλὸν ἀποπλαγχθείς Il. 13.592. Cf. Il. 6.125, Il. 14.30, Il. 17.342, Il. 22.459, etc. : πολλὸν διήφυσε σαρκός (partitive genit., making an extensive wound) Od. 19.450. Cf. Od. 4.811, Od. 5.350, Od. 6.40, Od. 11.515, Od. 14.339, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: With a vb. of preference, much, far : πολὺ βούλομαι Il. 1.112. Cf. Il. 17.331 : Od. 17.404.

div.head: d
div.p: With vbs. of excelling, rivalling or falling short, much, far, by much, by far : πολλὸν κείνων ἐπιδεύεαι ἀνδρῶν Il. 5.636, πολλὸν ἐνίκα Il. 18.252. Cf. Il. 9.506, Il. 13.815, Il. 17.142, Il. 19.219, etc. : Od. 1.253, Od. 3.121, Od. 21.185, etc.

div.head: e
div.p: With comparatives and superlatives, much, far, by much, by far : πολλὸν ἄριστος Il. 1.91, πολὺ μεῖζον 167. Cf. Il. 1.169, Il. 3.41, Il. 4.51, Il. 6.479, Il. 11.162, etc. : Od. 1.113, Od. 3.250, Od. 7.321, Od. 8.129, Od. 11.239, etc.

div.head: f
div.p: Often, oft, time and again : πολλόν μοι ἐπέσσυτο θυμός Il. 9.398.
In neut. pl. πολλά as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Greatly, much, in a high degree, intensely, to a great extent : π. μόγησα Il. 1.162, π. ἀεκαζομένη Il. 6.458, π. μετακλαύσεσθαι (bitterly) Il. 11.764. Cf. Il. 8.22, Il. 9.348, Il. 11.557, Il. 16.826, Il. 17.66 (loudly), Il. 23.116 (with much play of the heels), Il. 24.328, etc. : π. μοι κραδίη πόρφυρεν Od. 4.427. Cf. Od. 1.1, Od. 13.221, 277, Od. 14.65, 67, Od. 17.393 (in many words), etc.
In great numbers : ἄθλων οἷά τε π. πέλονται Od. 8.160.

div.head: b
div.p: With vbs. of entreating, enjoining or persuading, repeatedly, with anxious iteration, with insistence or assiduity, earnestly, pressingly, strongly : π. ἠρᾶτο Il. 1.35, π. ἐπέτελλεν Il. 4.229, π. ἀπεμυθέομην Il. 9.109. Cf. Il. 5.358, 528, Il. 9.183, Il. 11.782, Il. 17.431, etc. : Od. 3.54, 264, 267, Od. 4.433, Od. 10.521, etc.
Sim. : π. κεν ἀθανάτοισιν ἀνὰ χεῖρας ἀείραι Il. 7.130.

div.head: c
div.p: Often, oft, time and again : π. πρὸς ἠέλιον κεφαλὴν τρέπεν Od. 13.29. Cf. Il. 2.798, Il. 9.568, Il. 17.430, Il. 24.391, 755 : Od. 5.389, Od. 9.128, Od. 11.536.

div.head: d
div.p: Far and wide : π. ἴθυσε μάχη Il. 6.2.
Epithet of Odysseus Il. 9.673= Il. 10.544, Il. 11.430 : Od. 12.184.
Epithet of war or battle : πολέμοιο Il. 1.165, Il. 20.328 : Od. 11.314.
So κάματος πολυάϊξ, the weariness of many assaultsIl. 5.811.
The object of many prayers, called upon in many prayers : θεός Od. 6.280.
The subject of many prayers, longed for in many prayers : [πάϊς] Od. 19.404.
With many deeps or recesses : λιμένος Il. 1.432 : = Od. 16.324, Od. 10.125, Od. 16.352, ἁλός Od. 4.406.
Rich in oxen : ἄνδρες πολυβοῦται Il. 9.154= 296.

p.gloss: Bringing the glad changes of the year.

div.p: Displaying much curious workmanship, elaborately or richly wrought or adorned : θώρηκος Il. 3.358, ἀσπίδα Il. 11.32, κλισμῷ Il. 24.597, etc. : θάλαμον Od. 6.15, χρυσός Od. 13.11, ὅρμον Od. 18.295.
Skilled in curious arts : σιδόνες Il. 23.743.
Epithet of war or battle : Ἄρηα Il. 3.132, Il. 8.516=Il. 19.318, πόλεμον Il. 3.165, Il. 22.487, ὑσμίνη Il. 17.544.
The subject of many tears, much to be wept for Il. 24.620.
Accompanied by many tears, tearful : γόοιο Od. 19.213= 251= Od. 21.57.
Abounding in trees, treey Od. 4.737, Od. 23.139, 359.
Having many bands or cords, held together by much cordage : σχεδίης Od. 5.33, Od. 7.264.
Bringing (her parents) a great bride-price (cf. ἀλφεσίβοιος); or perh., bountiful (cf. ἠπιόδωρος) : ἄλοχος Il. 6.394, Il. 22.88 : Od. 24.294.
Gathered together from many quarters : ἐπίκουροι Il. 11.564.
Much desired or to be desired, lovely, charming, sweet : ἥβην Od. 15.366. Cf. Od. 15.126, Od. 23.126, Od. 23.354.
Epithet of a place : θήβῃ Od. 11.275.
Bold, dauntless : μένος Il. 17.156, Il. 19.37 : Od. 13.387.
Very shrewd or astute Od. 15.459, Od. 23.82.
Bearing much fruit, fruitful : ἀλωή Od. 7.122. Cf. Od. 24.221.
In pl. : πολυκερδείῃσι νόοιο Od. 23.77. Cf. Od. 24.167.
Veryshrewd, astute or cunning : νόον Od. 13.255.
App., having many rowlocks (cf. κληΐς 3). Epithet of ships Il. 2.74, 175, Il. 7.88, Il. 8.239, Il. 13.742, Il. 15.63, Il. 23.248 : Od. 8.161, Od. 20.382, Od. 23.19, Od. 23.324.
Called together from many quarters Il. 4.438, Il. 10.420.
Epithet of the sea : πόντῳ Od. 4.354, Od. 6.204, Od. 19.277.
Much or elaborately wrought Il. 6.48 = Il. 10.379 = Il. 11.133 : = Od. 21.10, Od. 14.324.
Elaborately or richly adorned : θαλάμοιο Od. 4.718.
With many mountain-spurs, hilly : Ἐτεωνόν Il. 2.497.
Rich in sheep or goats Il. 2.705, Il. 14.490.
Epithet of Odysseus Il. 1.311, Il. 3.200, Il. 4.329, etc.: Od. 2.173, Od. 4.763, Od. 5.214, etc.
Skill or cunning in contrivance Od. 23.321.
Of many devices, resourceful, never at a loss : ἐπεὶ π. ἐστιν Od. 1.205.
Epithet of Odysseus (always in voc.) Il. 2.173, etc. : Od. 5.203, Od. 24.192, etc.
Wooed by many Od. 4.770, Od. 14.64, Od. 23.149.
Of many words, having a flow of language Il. 3.214 : Od. 2.200.
[πολυ-, πολύς + παιπάλη, fine flour, fig. of subtlety or wiliness.]
Full of wiles, crafty : φοίνικες Od. 15.419.
Full of sorrows, sorrowful, woeful Il. 9.563 : Od. 14.386, Od. 23.15.
Epithet of Mount Ida Il. 8.47, Il. 14.157, Il. 15.151, etc.
In neut. pl. as adv., in right bitter fashion Od. 16.255.
Tossed about or roving from shore to shore Od. 17.425, Od. 20.195.
Widely dispersed, spread over the face of the earth : ἀνθρώπων Il. 2.804. Cf. Od. 11.365.
Much sighing, full of sorrows Od. 19.118.
Causing many sighs, grievous, baneful Il. 1.445, Il. 11.73, Il. 15.451.
= πολύτλας. : θυμός Il. 7.152 : πολυτλήμων εἰμί Od. 18.319.
That has suffered much, torn by suffering : γέροντες Od. 11.38.
Full of holes : σπόγγοισιν Od. 1.111, Od. 22.439, 453.
Conversant with drugs or medicaments Il. 16.28.
Knowing many charms or spells Od. 10.276.
Where many voices are heard, voiceful : ἀγορήν Od. 2.150.
Knowing many tales or songs : ἀοιδός Od. 22.376.
Epithet of the earth: γαῖαν πολυφόρβην Il. 9.568, πολυφόρβου γαίης Il. 14.200, 301.
Of great intelligence or sense, sensible, discreet.
Absol. : ἐφέηκε πολύφρονά περ χαλεπῆναι Il. 18.108. Cf. Od. 14.464.
As epithet of Hephaestus, of high intellectual capacity, ingenious, skilful Il. 21.367 : Od. 8.297, 327.
In sim. sense as epithet of Odysseus Od. 1.83 = Od. 14.424 = Od. 20.239 = Od. 21.204, Od. 20.329.
Fig. of the heavens (cf. χάλκεον οὐρανόν Il. 17.425) Il. 5.504 : Od. 3.2.
Epithet of a net : δικτύῳ Od. 22.386.
One who conducts, escorts, sees safe, a guide, escort, protector : οἵ τοι πομπῆες ἔσονται Od. 3.325. Cf. Od. 3.376, Od. 4.362, Od. 13.71, Od. 20.364.
To conduct, escort, see safe : αὐτή μιν πόμπευον Od. 13.422.

div.head: a
div.p: Conduct, escort, guidance, seeing safe : θεῶν ὑπὸ πομπῇ Il. 6.171. Cf. Od. 5.32, Od. 7.193, Od. 13.151, 180.

div.head: b
div.p: A conducting, escorting, seeing safe : ἐκ πομπῆς ἀνιοῦσαν Od. 8.568= Od. 13.150 = 176.

A dispatching or speeding on one's way, an arranging for or presiding over one's departure : ὄφρα πομπῆς τύχῃς Od. 6.290, οὐκέτι φαίνετο π. (i.e. they had lost their favouring wind) Od. 10.79. Cf. Od. 5.173, 233, Od. 7.151, 191, 317, Od. 8.30, 31, 33, 545, Od. 9.518, Od. 10.18, Od. 11.332, 352, 357, Od. 13.41, Od. 19.313.

One who conducts, conveys, escorts, sees safe, a guide, escort, protector : τῷ ἅμα πομπὸν ἕπεσθαι Od. 4.162. Cf. Il. 13.416, Il. 16.671, 681, Il. 24.153, 182, 437, 439, 461 : Od. 4.826, Od. 8.566 = Od. 13.174.
To labour or work with one's hands, work, toil : ὅπλα, τοῖς ἐπονεῖτο Il. 18.413. Cf. Il. 7.442 : Od. 16.13, Od. 20.159 (did their work).
To work at : ὄφρα ταῦτα πονεῖτο Il. 18.380.
To produce by work, make, construct : τύμβον Il. 23.245.

To be busy, be much occupied, busy oneself, have or engage in toil or labour, exert oneself : ᾔδεε ἀδελφεὸν ὡς ἐπονεῖτο Il. 2.409. Cf. Il. 9.12, 348, Il. 10.70, 116, 117, 121 : Od. 9.250 = 310 = 343, Od. 17.258 and Od. 20.281 (the attendants).
To be busied or engaged, busy oneself (with or about something) : πεπόνητο καθʼ ἵππους (i.e. they were taking up all his attention) Il. 15.447. Cf. Il. 24.444.
To busy oneself about, be engaged or engage oneself in, see to : τάδʼ ἀμφὶ πονησόμεθα Il. 23.159. Cf. Od. 15.222, Od. 22.377.
To attend to, look to, set in order : ὅπλα Od. 11.9, Od. 12.151.

To be engaged in the toil and moil of war, take part in the fight, fight : ὅ μιν ἴδοντο πονεύμενον (at work with his spear) Il. 4.374, πονέοντο καθʼ ὑσμίνην Il. 5.84= Il. 5.627. Cf. Il. 13.288, Il. 20.359.

Labour, toil, work, trouble : ἐπεὶ παύσαντο πόνου Il. 1.467 = Il. 2.430=Il. 7.319. Cf. Il. 4.26, 57, Il. 5.567 (all they had gone through), 667 (they were too busy), Il. 6.77 (the chief burden), Il. 10.164 : Od. 2.334, Od. 8.529, Od. 11.54 (they had so many other things to attend to), Od. 16.478 = Od. 24.384, Od. 23.249.
In pl., toils, troubles, difficulties : τὸν Ζεὺς ἐνέηκε πόνοισιν Il. 10.89. Cf. Il. 10.245, 279: Od. 4.818, Od. 13.301, Od. 20.48.
Hardship, suffering, distress : ἄνευθε πόνου καὶ ἀνίης Od. 7.192. Cf. Il. 22.488 : Od. 13.423.
So, app., πότε κέν τις ἀναπνεύσειε πόνοιο; Il. 19.227 (referring to the hardship of fasting).

Referring specially to the toil and moil of war, war, fighting : καὶ πόνος ἐστὶν ἀνιηθέντα νέεσθαι (we have e'en had fighting enough to disgust a man and send him home) Il. 2.291, ἰαχή τε π. τε Il. 4.456. Cf. Il. 2.420, Il. 5.517, Il. 6.525 (have to bear this heavy burden of war), Od. 11.430, Il. 12.348, Il. 13.2, Il. 14.480, Il. 15.416 (fought their fight), Il. 21.137, Il. 22.11 (app., the slaughtering of them), etc. : Od. 12.117.
In concrete sense, a fighting throng : ἔβη ἂμ πόνον ἀνδρῶν Il. 13.239=Il. 16.726=Il. 17.82.
The field of battle : φέρον ἐκ πόνου Il. 14.429. Cf. Il. 17.718.
The result of toil, weariness Il. 6.355.
From the open sea : κῦμα ποντόθεν ὀρνύμενον Il. 14.395.
Towards the open sea, seawards : φέρεν π. θύελλα Od. 10.48.
Into the sea : π. βαλὼν βέλος Od. 9.495.
To traverse the sea, sail the sea Od. 5.277, 278, Od. 7.267.
Epithet of ships Il. 1.439, Il. 2.771, Il. 3.46, etc. : Od. 12.69, Od. 14.339, Od. 15.284, etc.
-ου, ὁ. Ablative ποντόφιν Od. 24.83. The sea, the deep sea, the high sea, the open sea Il. 1.350, Il. 2.145, 665, Il. 3.47, Il. 4.276, etc.: Od. 1.4, Od. 2.263, Od. 3.15, Od. 4.359, Od. 7.109, etc.
With ἅλς : π. ἁλός (the deep of the sea) Il. 21.59.
Distinguished in terms from the land : πείρατα γαίης καὶ πόντοιο Il. 8.479. Cf. Od. 4.821, Od. 5.294, Od. 16.367, etc.
From the heavens : ἐξ αἰθέρος ἔμπεσε πόντῳ Od. 5.50. Cf. Il. 14.258.

Always with ὦ (ὤ), expressing contextually surprise, a being struck by something, grief, anger, remonstrance, rebuke, disappointment, a being balked of something, a drawing of special attention to something, or the likeIl. 1.254, Il. 2.272 (look you now!), Il. 8.427 (ah well !), Il. 13.99, Il. 15.467 (ah me !), Il. 16.745 (see now !), Il. 17.171, Il. 22.373 (why, look you !), etc. : Od. 1.32 (to see now how . . . !), Od. 4.169, 333, Od. 5.286, Od. 9.507, Od. 10.38, etc.
To sack or ravage (a town or land) Il. 4.308 : Od. 14.264= Od. 17.433.
A narrow strip of water, a channel : ἐν πορθμῷ Ἰθάκης τε σάμοιό τε (between . . . and . . .) Od. 4.671=Od. 15.29.
In a spear, a metal ferrule, or perh. a lashing of wire, securing the tongue of the head (see καυλός 1.a) in the shaft Il. 6.320= Il. 8.495.
A place where a river may be passed, a ford Il. 2.592, Il. 14.433=Il. 21.1=Il. 24.692.–πόροι ἁλός, the paths of the seaOd. 12.259.
Nom. sing. fem. fut. pple. πορσανέουσα Il. 3.411. Also πορσύνω.
Of a wife, to prepare (and share) (her husband's bed) : κείνου πορσανέουσα λέχος Il. 3.411 : τῷ ἄλοχος λέχος πόρσυνεν Od. 3.403. Cf. Od. 7.347.

Of disturbed water, gleaming, glancing : πορφύρεον κῦμα ποταμοῖο Il. 21.326, ἀμφὶ κῦμα στείρῃ πορφύρεον μεγάλʼ ἴαχεν (flashing as it fell off on each side of the cutwater) Il. 1.482 := Od. 2.428. Cf. Il. 16.391 : Od. 11.243, Od. 13.85 (the white wake).
So in reference to the light reflected from (the irregular surface of) a cloud : πορφυρέῃ νεφέλῃ πυκάσασα ἕ αὐτήν Il. 17.551.
Applied to the sinister gleam figured to play on (the cloud or mist of) death : πορφύρεος θάνατος Il. 5.83=Il. 16.334=Il. 20.477.
To the lurid gleam of the rainbow set against a storm-cloud : πορφυρέην ἶριν Il. 17.547.
To the warm hue of blood : αἵματι πορφυρέῳ Il. 17.361.

Of bright hue, bright, brilliant, gay : δίπλακα Il. 3.126, Il. 22.441, φᾶρος Il. 8.221, τάπησιν Il. 9.200, ῥήγεα Il. 24.645, πέπλοισιν 796 : χλαῖναν Od. 4.115= 154, Od. 19.225, ῥήγεα Od. 4.298=Od. 7.337, Od. 10.353, φᾶρος Od. 8.84, σφαῖραν 373, δίπλακα Od. 19.242, τάπητας Od. 20.151.
Of the disturbed sea, to heave Il. 14.16.
Fig., of the heart, to be troubled, moved, stirred : πολλά οἱ κραδίη πόρφυρεν Il. 21.551. Cf. Od. 4.427 = 572=Od. 10.309.
3 sing. subj. πόρῃ Il. 6.228 : Od. 22.7. πόρῃσι Od. 2.186, Od. 16.77, Od. 20.335.
Pple. πεπρωμένος, -ου Il. 3.309, Il. 15.209, Il. 16.441, Il. 22.179.
To give, put into another's hands, hand to him : σήματα λυγρά Il. 6.168.

To give, make another the owner of, present, make a present of : ξεινήϊα Il. 6.218, τεύχεα Il. 7.146. Cf. Il. 10.546, Il. 11.353, Il. 15.441, Il. 16.86, 143=Il. 19.390, Il. 17.196, Il. 19.21, Il. 23.92, 277, 540, 893, Il. 24.234 : Od. 2.186, Od. 4.130, 617, Od. 9.267, Od. 16.77, etc.
To cause (a woman) to conceive (a child) : πόρεν οἱ ἀγλαὸν υἱόν Il. 16.185.
To pay (a bride-price or ransom) : ἀπερείσια ἕδνα Il. 16.178, λύμην τρὶς τόσσα πορών Il. 21.80. Cf. Il. 16.190, Il. 22.472 : Od. 11.282, Od. 19.529.
To give in marriage : ἀνδρὶ πόρον παράκοιτιν Il. 24.60. Cf. Od. 10.7.
Sim. in reference to a concubine Il. 9.667.

To give, furnish, supply, to another for his use or to meet his needs : φάρμακα Il. 4.219 : Od. 4.228, σῖτον καὶ μέθυ 745. Cf. Od. 5.321, 372, Od. 6.228, Od. 8.477, Od. 9.360, Od. 10.302, Od. 12.302, Od. 14.460, Od. 19.255.
Of immaterial things, to give, grant, allow, bestow, confer : μαντοσύνην Il. 1.72. Cf. Il. 24.30 : Od. 10.494, Od. 20.71, Od. 22.7.
To inflict or send (evil) : κακά Od. 9.460, πένθος Od. 19.512.
With infin., to grant, allow : πόρε Διὸς κούρῃσιν ἕπεσθαι τιμήν (let them have their meed of honour) Il. 9.513.
With the infin. suppressed : κτείνειν ὅν κε θεός γε πόρῃ Il. 6.228.
In pf. pass., to be decreed by fate, to be fated or destined : ὁπποτέρῳ θανάτοιο τέλος πεπρωμένον ἐστίν Il. 3.309.
Impers. with acc. and infin.: ἄμφω πέπρωται ὁμοίην γαῖαν ἐρεῦσαι Il. 18.329.
Of a person, to be fated, to have his lot or portion fixed, in a specified way (see αἶσα 4) : ὁμῇ πεπρωμένον αἴσῃ Il. 15.209. Cf. Il. 16.441=Il. 22.179.
Whither ? πόσε φεύγετε; Il. 16.422 : Od. 6.199, πόσʼ ἴμεν; Od. 10.431.
In neut., a temple of Poseidon : Od. 6.266.
For how many days? In indirect question Il. 24.657.
Which in a series of numbers? πόστον ἔτος ἐστίν, ὅτε . .; (how many years is it since . . .?) Od. 24.288.
To, towards or into the or a river Il. 21.13, 120 : Od. 10.159.
With the name of a particular river added, the river . . . : ποταμὸν κηφισόν Il. 2.522. Cf. Il. 2.659, Il. 5.544, Il. 11.499, etc. : Od. 14.258=Od. 17.427.
Of ocean : ποταμοῖο ῥέεθρα Ὠκεανοῦ Il. 14.245. Cf. Il. 18.607, Il. 20.7 : Od. 11.639, Od. 12.1.
Personified, a river-god : ποταμοὶ καὶ γαῖα, ὑμεῖς μάρτυροι ἔστε Il. 3.278. Cf. Il. 5.544, Il. 20.7, Il. 21.136, etc. : Od. 11.238.

To fly about, fly hither and thither : αἱ μέν τʼ ἔνθα ἅλις πεποτήαται, αἱ δέ τε ἔνθα (are on the wing) Il. 2.90, ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ποτῶνται 462 : ψυχὴ ἀποπταμένη πεπότηται (hovers about) Od. 11.222, ὡς ὅτε νυκτερίδες ποτέονται Od. 24.7.
When? πότʼ ᾤχετο; Od. 4.642. Cf. Il. 19.227.

div.head: a
div.p: In time past, in days of old, formerly, once, once upon a time : ὥς ποτʼ ἐπʼ εἰρήνης Il. 2.797. Cf. Il. 1.39, 260, 453, Il. 2.547, Il. 3.180, 205, Il. 4.106, etc. : τήν ποτε πρίατο Od. 1.430. Cf. Od. 3.84, Od. 4.342, Od. 6.162, Od. 7.9, 59, Od. 8.76, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to the future, at some time, some day, in days to come, yet : ἦ ποτʼ Ἀχιλλῆος ποθὴ ἵξεται υἷας Ἀχαιῶν Il. 1.240. Cf. Il. 1.205, 213, Il. 4.164, 182, etc. : τάχʼ ἄν ποτε καὶ τίσις εἴη Od. 2.76. Cf. Od. 2.342, Od. 3.216, Od. 8.461, 567, etc.

In negative or conditional contexts, at any time, ever : εἴ ποτε δὴ αὖτε χρειὼ ἐμεῖο γένηται Il. 1.340. Cf. Il. 1.155, 166, 490, Il. 2.202, Il. 4.410, Il. 5.700, Il. 10.453, etc. : οὐδέ ποτʼ ἔσβη οὖρος Od. 3.182. Cf. Od. 2.26, 203, Od. 3.127, Od. 4.360, 566, Od. 5.39, 151, Od. 8.562, etc.
In pl. in an indirect question, which of two groups: οὐκ ἂν γνοίης ποτέροισι μετείη Il. 5.85.
App., flight : ποτῇ ἀνεδύσετο λίμνης (flew up from . . .) Od. 5.337.
Absol. in neut. pl., birds : τῇ οὐδὲ ποτητὰ παρέρχεται Od. 12.62.

div.head: I
div.p: Adv. Besides, in addition, too : ποτὶ δʼ ἄσπετα δῶρα δίδωμι Od. 20.342. Cf. Il. 10.108, Il. 16.86.

div.head: II
div.p: Prep. (With anastrophe when immediately following the case-form.)

div.head: a
div.p: On, upon, against : οὐδέ μιν παῖδες ποτὶ γούνασι παππάζουσιν Il. 5.408 : νῆάς γε ποτὶ σπιλάδεσσιν ἔαξαν κύματα Od. 3.298. Cf. Od. 5.401, Od. 8.378.
In pregnant sense : ποτὶ σκῆπτρον βάλε γαίῃ Il. 1.245. Cf. Il. 4.112, Il. 20.420 : μή με βάλῃ ποτὶ πέτρῃ Od. 5.415. Cf. Od. 2.80, Od. 6.310, Od. 8.190, Od. 9.289, Od. 11.423,

div.head: b
div.p: In the direction of, towards : towards : τὸν ποτὶ οἷ εἷλεν Od. 24.347.

div.head: a
div.p: Indicating arrival at point : ἄστυ πότι Il. 17.419 : ἐπεὶ ἵκευ ἐμὸν ποτὶ δῶ Od. 13.4. Cf. Il. 21.505 : Od. 3.488, Od. 6.297, etc.
Sim. : ἐξ ἱστὸν ἄραξε ποτὶ τρόπιν (right (down) to the keel, at the keel) Od. 12.422.
In reference to sitting on something : ἢ ποτὶ βωμὸν ἵζοιτο Od. 22.334. Cf. Od. 22.379.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to speech : ποτὶ Πρίαμον φάτο Il. 24.353. Cf. Il. 24.598.
In reference to the sight : παπαταίνοντες ποτὶ τοίχους Od. 22.24.

div.head: c
div.p: In reference to the direction in which action takes place, towards, against : ἐκλύσθη θάλασσα ποτὶ κλισίας Il. 14.392. Cf. Il. 14.394, 396 (app. with an object to be supplied), Il. 17.264 : Od. 5.402, Od. 12.71.

div.head: d
div.p: In reference to placing or leaning against something : ποτὶ τοῖχον ἀρηρότες Od. 2.342. Cf. Il. 23.510 : Od. 18.102.

To placing beside something : ποτὶ τύμβον δείμομεν πύργους (τεῖχος ἔδειμαν) Il. 7.337, 436 (i.e., app., including the mound in the fortification, the wall starting from each side of it). Cf. Il. 12.64 (i.e. the wall comes next).

div.head: e
div.p: In reference to position, in the direction of, towards : ὅσσοι [ναίουσι] ποτὶ ζόφον Od. 13.241. Cf. Il. 11.622, Il. 23.869.

div.head: f
div.p: In reference to time, at the approach of, towards : ποτὶ ἕσπερα Od. 17.191.

With genit. In reference to position maintained by one moving person in relation to another, towards, on the side of (something) : αὐτὸς δὲ ποτὶ πτόλιος πέτετʼ αἰεί (kept on the city side of him) Il. 22.198.
To wait for (a coming or expected event or person), await, look out for : ἐμὴν ὁρμήν Il. 10.123. Cf. Il. 19.234 : ἡμέας Od. 9.545. Cf. Od. 2.403, Od. 7.161, Od. 24.396.
With clause : ποτιδέγμενοι ὁππότʼ ἄρʼ ἔλθοι Il. 7.415. Cf. Od. 23.91.
Absol. : ποτιδέγμενοι ἤματα πάντα (waiting on here indefinitely) Od. 2.205, Od. 21.156. Cf. Il. 2.137 and Il. 9.628 (looking for our coming).
To await or anticipate with apprehension : ἀγγελίην Il. 19.336. Cf. Od. 22.380.
To expect, look for, the receipt of (something) : δῶρον Od. 2.186.
Available for, ready to be taken at or to be used in connexion with, one's evening meal Od. 9.234, 249.
To come, be brought, to a specified place : ἐς Ὀρχομενόν Il. 9.381.
Nom. pl. fem. pf. pple. ποτιπεπτηυῖαι.
With genit.: ἀκταὶ λιμένος ποτιπεπτηυῖαι (sinking down in front of it and so closing it in) Od. 13.98.
To engage agreeably the attention of, entertain Il. 15.401.

[ποτι-, προσ- 3 + φωνήεις in sim.
sense fr. φωνή.]
Endowed with speech : εἰ ποτιφωνήεις γένοιο Od. 9.456.
What befalls one, one's lot or fate : ὃν πότμον γοόωσα Il. 16.857 = Il. 22.363. Cf. Od. 10.245.

Evil fate or destiny, bane, death : θάνατον καὶ πότμον Il. 2.359, Il. 15.495, Il. 20.337, εἰ πότμον ἀναπλήσῃς βιότοιο (a fate that ends thy life) Il. 4.170. Cf. Il. 4.396, Il. 6.412, Il. 7.52, Il. 11.263, Il. 18.96, Il. 21.588, Il. 22.39 : Od. 2.250, Od. 3.16 (the manner of his death), Od. 4.196, 339, 562, Od. 11.197, Od. 19.550, Od. 24.471, etc.
=πότνια. πότνα θεά, mighty goddessOd. 5.215, Od. 13.391, Od. 20.61.
[ποτ- as in δεσπότης, master. Cf. δέσποινα.]
Mistress, queen : πότνια θηρῶν, Ἄρτεμις Il. 21.470.
Something drunk or to be drunk, drink, liquor Il. 1.470, Il. 11.630, Il. 9.175 :=Od. 1.148=Od. 3.339=Od. 21.271, Od. 2.341, Od. 9.205, 348, 354.
Carrying on an indirect question : ἐρέσθαι ὁππόθεν οὗτος ἀνήρ ... ποῦδέ νύ οἱ γενεή Od. 1.407.
Whither? where? ποῦ τοι ἀπειλαὶ οἴχονται; Il. 13.219.
In negative or conditional contexts, anywhere : οὐδέ τί που ἴδμεν ξυνήϊα Il. 1.124. Cf. Il. 6.330, Il. 19.327, etc.: εἴ που ὄπωπας Od. 3.93. Cf. Od. 7.320, Od. 11.458, Od. 14.44, etc.
Somehow, haply: ἤν πού τι φόως γένωμαι Il. 16.39. Cf. Il. 7.39, Il. 15.571, etc.: Od. 4.512, Od. 13.418, etc.

In negative or conditional contexts, in any way, haply: εἴ τί που ἔστιν Od. 4.193, μή πού τις ἐπαγγείλῃσιν 775. Cf. Il. 9.371, Il. 10.511, Il. 11.366, Il. 13.293, etc.: Od. 2.71, Od. 10.486, Od. 12.300, Od. 15.403, etc.

Qualifying an expression, haply, I ween, no doubt, as it would seem: θεός που σοὶ τό γʼ ἔδωκεν Il. 1.178, οὕτω που διὶ μέλλει φίλον εἶναι Il. 2.116. Cf. Il. 3.43, Il. 6.438, Il. 9.628, Il. 10.326, etc.: οἵ πού μʼ ἀσχαλόωσι μένοντες Od. 1.304, Ζηνός που τοιήδε γʼ αὐλή Od. 4.74. Cf. Od. 2.164, Od. 4.756, Od. 6.155, Od. 8.255, Od. 11.139, etc.

Sim. in questions, direct and indirect, can it be that? haply, it may be that: οὕτω που ἔλπεαι υἷας Ἀχαιῶν ἀπτολέμους ἔμεναι; Il. 9.40, ἤ ῥʼ ἔτι που σχήσουσιν Ἕκτορα Il. 11.820. Cf. Il. 13.456, etc.: Od. 6.125, 200, Od. 8.584, Od. 13.234, etc.
The sea-polypus, the octopus or cuttle-fish Od. 5.432.

One of the feet, one's foot; in dual and pl., the feet, one's feet: χωλὸς ἕτερον πόδα Il. 2.217, ὑπὸ ποσσίν Il. 8.443, οὐδὲ χθόνα μάρπτε ποδοῖιν Il. 14.228. Cf. Il. 1.591, Il. 2.44, Il. 9.523 (i.e. their coming hither), Il. 13.205, Il. 19.92, etc.: Od. 1.96, Od. 4.149, Od. 6.39 (on foot), Od. 15.45, Od. 20.365, Od. 22.20, etc.
Of animals. Of horses Il. 2.466, Il. 5.504, Il. 9.124, Il. 13.36, Il. 16.794, etc.
Of dogs Od. 19.228 (in his paws). Cf. Il. 8.339: Od. 19.444.
Of birds Il. 23.854, 866: Od. 15.526 (in its claws).

With special reference to speed in running or in the race: ποσὶν οὔ πως ἔστιν ἐρίζειν (in swiftness of foot) Il. 13.325. Cf. Il. 15.642, Il. 20.410, Il. 22.160, Il. 23.444, 792, etc.: Od. 8.103, 206 (in the race), 230, etc.
πόδας ὠκύς, swift-footed. Epithet of Achilles Il. 1.58, 84, 148, 215, 364, 489, Il. 9.196, Il. 11.112, etc.
Sim.: πόδας ταχύς. Of Achilles Il. 13.348, Il. 17.709, Il. 18.354, 358.
Of Antilochus Il. 18.2.–πόδας ὠκέα as epithet of Iris Il. 2.790, 795, Il. 8.425, etc.
Epithets of animals. Of the hare: πόδας ταχὺς πτώξ Il. 17.676.
Of the dog: κύνες πόδας ἀργοί Il. 18.578: Od. 2.11.
Of the horse: πόδας αἰόλος ἵππος Il. 19.404.
A projecting spur of a hill: ὑπαὶ πόδα νείατον Ἴδης Il. 2.824. Cf. Il. 20.59.
A sheet of a sail, a rope or strap attached to one of the lower corners of it and used to extend it or alter its direction Od. 5.260, Od. 10.32.
The midriff: βάλʼ (ἔβαλʼ) ἧπαρ ὑπὸ πραπίδων Il. 11.579=Il. 13.412=Il. 17.349.
The heart, breast, soul, mind, as the seat or a seat

div.head: a
div.p: Of the faculty of perception or knowledge, of the wits: ὅς τʼ ὀλίγον περ ἐπιψαύῃ πραπίδεσσιν Od. 8.547.

div.head: b
div.p: Of the faculty of contriving, devising, designing, of ingenuity: ποίησεν ἰδυίῃσι πραπίδεσσιν Il. 1.608. Cf. Il. 18.380, 482, Il. 20.12: Od. 7.92.

div.head: c
div.p: Of the emotions, of grief or sorrow: ἦ κέ μοι αἰνὸν ἀπὸ πραπίδων ἄχος ἔλθοι Il. 22.43. Cf. Il. 24.514.
A bed of herbs Od. 7.127, Od. 24.247.
To be pre-eminent, conspicuous, distinguished, noted: ἔπρετε καὶ διὰ πάντων Il. 12.104. Cf. Od. 8.172, Od. 18.2 (was noted for his ...).
The eldest: π. Διὸς θυγάτηρ Ἄτη Il. 19.91. Cf. Od. 3.452.
That is senior in dignity. Of Here: π. θεά, queen of heavenIl. 5.721=Il. 8.383, Il. 14.194 = 243.
A meed of honour: πρώτῳ τοι μετʼ ἐμὲ π. ἐν χερὶ θήσω Il. 8.289.
The first-born: π. Ἀντηνορίσης (the first-born son of ...) Il. 11.249.
Comp. πρεσβύτερος, the elder: πρεσβύτερος σύ ἐσσι Il. 11.787.

Absol. in pl., the elders, the seniors: πρεσβυτέροισιν Ἐρινύες αἰὲν ἕπονται
Il. 15.204.
Superl. πρεσβύτατος, the first-born, the eldest: πρεσβυτά-την με τέκετο κρόνος (app. with an admixture of the sense senior in dignity) Il. 4.59, πρεσβύτατος γενεῇ Il. 6.24. Cf. Il. 11.740.
Absol.: πρεσβυτάτην ὤπυιε θυγατρῶν Il. 13.429. Cf. Il. 21.143: Od. 13.142 (he must mean, after himself. He is represented as the elder in Il. 15.204 cited under (1)).
3 sing. aor. ἔπρησε Od. 2.427. πρῆσε Il. 1.481, Il. 16.350.
Nom. pl. masc. pple. πρήσαντες Il. 7.429, 432.
Of wind, to blow into, swell by blowing: ἔπρησεν ἄνεμος ἱστίον Od. 2.427. Cf. Il. 1.481.
To eject by blowing, spirt out: αἷμʼ ἀνὰ στόμα Il. 16.350.
To burn, consume (with or in fire): πυρὸς θύρετρα (genit. of material) Il. 2.415. Cf. Il. 7.429, 432.
[προ- 1 + ἠν-, face. Cf. ἀπηνής, ὑπηνήτης. With the face forward.]
Of inanimate objects, to utter ruin or destruction: πρηνὲς βαλέειν Πριάμοιο μέλαθρον Il. 2.414.
Accomplishment, result, issue: οὔ τις πρῆξις πέλεται γόοιο (no profit comes of it) Il. 24.524: οὔ τις πρῆξις ἐγίγνετο μυρομένοισιν (their weeping profited them nothing) Od. 10.202= 568.
An affair or business Od. 3.72=Od. 9.253, Od. 3.82.
Acc. sing. masc. pple. πρήξαντα Od. 3.60.
To pass over, traverse: ἅλα Od. 9.491.
To traverse a space, pass, advance, make one's way: ἵνα πρήσσωμεν (ἵνα πρήσσῃσιν) (ὄφρα πρήσσωμεν) ὁδοῖο (local genit., may get upon our (his) way) Il. 24.264: Od. 3.476, Od. 15.47, 219.
To accomplish (a journey or course): κέλευθον Il. 14.282, Il. 23.501: Od. 13.83.

To accomplish, do, carry out, effect, perform: πρῆξαι οὔ τι δυνήσεαι Il. 1.562, οὔ τι πρήξεις ἀκαχήμενος υἷος (it will profit you nothing to mourn for him) Il. 24.550. Cf. Il. 11.552=Il. 17.661: ἐὺ πρήσσεσκον ἕκαστα (were charged with the due arrangements) Od. 8.259. Cf. Od. 2.191, Od. 3.60, Od. 16.88, Od. 19.324.
Absol.: ἔπρηξας καὶ ἔπειτα (you have got your way after all) Il. 18.357.
To buy, acquire by purchase Od. 1.430, Od. 14.115, 452, Od. 15.483.

Before, heretofore, theretofore, in time past, formerly: ὡς πρίν Il. 2.344, καὶ πρίν περ μεμαώς Il. 5.135, μένος ὃ πρὶν ἔχεσκες 472. Cf. Il. 3.132, 430, Il. 5.127, Il. 9.523, etc.: Od. 3.408, Od. 4.212, 724, Od. 5.334, Od. 6.4, Od. 10.393, Od. 11.484, etc.

Before the arrival of a specified or indicated time past or future, earlier, sooner: πρίν μιν καὶ γῆρας ἔπεισιν (ere that) Il. 1.29, πρὶν ὑποφθὰς δουρὶ περόνησεν (before he could use his club) Il. 7.144, πρὶν κνέφας ἦλθεν Il. 8.500. Cf. Il. 7.390, Il. 9.250, Il. 14.424, Il. 18.283, Il. 23.190 (before the due time), Il. 24.551, etc.: Od. 2.198, Od. 3.117, Od. 11.632, Od. 13.427, Od. 14.334, Od. 21.36, etc.
With or without τό, up to a point of time, so long: τὸ πρὶν μὲν ἀναίνετο Od. 3.265, πρὶν οὔ τι νεμεσσητὸν κεχολῶσθαι Od. 22.59.

With aor. infin., before ... ing ...: πρὶν γνώμεναι Il. 2.348, πρὶν ἐλθεῖν υἶας Ἀχαιῶν (before their coming) Il. 9.403. Cf. Il. 1.98, Il. 4.115, Il. 6.81, Il. 8.453, Il. 12.172, Il. 15.588, etc.: Od. 1.210, Od. 2.128, Od. 4.255, Od. 6.288, Od. 10.385, Od. 13.124, Od. 15.210, etc.
So with ἤ: πρίν γʼ ἢ ἕτερόν γʼ αἵματος ἆσαι Ἄρηα Il. 5.288, Il. 22.266.
With pres. infin.: πρὶν ... ἄγειν θʼ ἑκατόμβην Il. 1.98. Cf. Od. 19.475.
With subj.: πρίν γʼ ἔμʼ ἴδηαι Il. 18.135. Cf. Il. 18.190, Il. 24.781: Od. 10.175, Od. 13.336, Od. 17.9.
With opt.: πρὶν πειρήσαιτʼ Ἀχιλῆος Il. 21.580.

div.head: a
div.p: With indic.: πρίν γʼ ὅτε δὴ θάλαμος ἐβάλλετο Il. 9.588. Cf. Il. 12.437: Od. 4.180, Od. 13.322, Od. 23.43.

div.head: b
div.p: With ἄν and subj.: πρίν γʼ ὅτʼ ἄν ἑνδεκάτη γένηται Od. 2.374. Cf. Od. 4.477.

div.head: c
div.p: With opt.: πρίν γʼ ὅτε σʼ ὄψου ἄσαιμι Il. 9.488.

In two co-ordinate clauses, anticipatory in the first and resuming in the second: οὐδʼ ὅ γε πρὶν λοιγὸν ἀπώσει, πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πατρὶ δόμεναι κούρην Il. 1.97. Cf. Il. 2.348, Il. 7.481, Il. 18.189, Il. 24.781, etc.: Od. 4.254, 475, Od. 19.475, etc.
Sawn, cut or fashioned with the saw: ἐλέφαντος Od. 18.196, Od. 19.564.
Forward, forwards, forth: πρὸ γὰρ ἧκεν Ἥρη Il. 1.195. Cf. Il. 1.208, 442, Il. 4.382 (see ὁδός 1), Il. 15.360, Il. 16.188, etc.: Od. 21.21.
In front, before: πρὸ δούρατʼ ἔχοντο Il. 17.355. Cf. Il. 13.799, 800: Od. 5.385.
In temporal sense, before: πρὸ ἐόντα (the past) Il. 1.70.
Beforehand: ἐπεὶ πρό οἱ εἴπομεν Od. 1.37.
In front of, before: πρὸ ἄστεος Il. 15.351. Cf. Il. 5.96, 789, Il. 9.708, Il. 19.292, etc.: Od. 10.105, Od. 24.468.
With locative: ἠῶθι πρό (see ἠώς 1). Ἰλιόθι πρό (see Ἰλιόθι). οὐρανόθι πρό (see οὐρανός 1).
In reference to chieftainship: πρὸ φθίων Il. 13.693. Cf. Il. 13.699.
Before the face of, in subjection to: ἀθλεύειν πρὸ ἄνακτος ἀμειλίχου Il. 24.734.
Under compulsion of: πρὸ φόβοιο Il. 17.667.
In front of, in advance of: πρὸ ἑτάρων μάχεσθαι Il. 4.373.
In advance of, preceding: πρὸ δʼ ἄρʼ αὐτῶν κύνες ἤϊσαν Od. 19.435. Cf. Il. 10.286, Il. 17.726, Il. 23.115.
In defence of, defending, protecting: πρὸ Τρώων ἑσταότα Il. 24.215. Cf. Il. 8.57, Il. 22.110.
In reference to a champion, on behalf of Il. 4.156.
In temporal sense, before, sooner than: καί τε πρὸ ὁ τοῦ ἐνόησεν Il. 10.224. Cf. Od. 15.524, Od. 17.476.
Sloping, forming a declivity: χώρῳ Il. 21.262.
To go forward: ἄστρα προβέβηκεν (have got far forward in their course) Il. 10.252.

p.gloss: To go before, advance in front of.

div.p: With genit.: πολὺ προβέβηκας ἁπάντων Il. 6.125.
In pf. of the state or condition of going before; hence, to be pre-eminent, to excel, surpass; ὅ τε κράτεϊ προβεβήκῃ (in ...) Il. 16.54.
With genit.: ὅσον προβέβηκας ἁπάντων Il. 23.890.
Nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. προ-βαλόντες Il. 11.529.
3 pl. aor. mid. προβάλοντο Il. 1.458, Il. 2.421, Il. 23.255: Od. 3.447.
To throw forward or forth: νότος βορέῃ προ-βάλεσκε [σχεδίην] (surrendered it) Od. 5.331.
In mid.: ἐπεὶ οὐλοχύτας προβάλοντο (had sprinkled them) Il. 1.458=Il. 2.421: =Od. 3.447.
Fig.: ἔριδα προ-βαλόντες (app., throwing it forward, dashing forward in combat) Il. 11.529 (cf. Il. 3.7 cited under προφέρω 2).
To throw before or in front.
In mid.: θεμείλια προβάλοντο (set them in the face of the mound) Il. 23.255.
Hence, in mid., to excel, surpass.
With genit.: σεῖό κε νοήματι προβαλοίμην (in ...) Il. 19.218.
Cattle, flocks and herds Il. 14.124, Il. 23.550.
To advance: ὑπασπίσια προβιβῶντι (προβιβῶντος) Il. 13.807, Il. 16.609. (With προβιβάντι, προβιβάντος from προβίβημι. as uu. ll.)
To stride along forwards, make one's way or advance with a stride: κραιπνὰ ποσὶ προβιβάς Il. 13.18. Cf. Il. 13.158: Od. 15.555, Od. 17.27. (And see προβιβάω.)
Projecting, jutting out: σκοπέλῳ Il. 2.396, στήλας Il. 12.259, πέτρῃ Il. 16.407: ἀκταί Od. 5.405, Od. 10.89, Od. 13.97.

To go or come forward or forth: τὴν ἴδε προμολοῦσα χάρις Il. 18.382. Cf. Il. 18.392, Il. 21.37 (making a descent upon it): Od. 4.22, Od. 15.468, Od. 19.25 (to leave their quarters), Od. 21.239 = 385, Od. 24.388.
To shout in front: προ-βοῶντε μάχην ὤτρυνον Ἀχαιῶν (cheering their followers on) Il. 12.277.
A projecting rock: ἐπὶ προβόλῳ Od. 12.251.
With genit.: κλυταιμνήστρης [μιν] προβέβουλα (prefer her to ...) Il. 1.113.
[comp. of προγενής, fr. προ- 3 + γεν-, γίγνομαι. Born before.]
Older: ὁ γὰρ προγενέστερος ἦεν Il. 2.555. Cf. Il. 9.161, Il. 23.789: Od. 2.29, Od. 4.205, Od. 19.244.
Old rather than young: ὃς Φαιήκων προγενέστερος ἦεν (was an elder among the ...) Od. 7.156=Od. 11.343, οὐδʼ οἳ προγενέστεροι ἦσαν (the elders among us) Od. 24.160.
To come forward, appear, come in sight Il. 18.525.
[προ- 3 + γον-, γεν-, γίγνομαι. Those born before.]
To know something beforehand: μή πώς με προδαεὶς ἀλέηται (forming a suspicion) Od. 4.396.
A place where one may lie in wait, a lurking-place.
In pl.: δεδεγμένος ἐν προδοκῇσιν Il. 4.107.
A space in front of the door of the μέγαρον, app. the part of the line of the αἴθουσα into which the door opened: εὗρεν ἐνὶ προδόμῳ δέπα Od. 15.466. Cf. Il. 9.473 (see θάλαμος 1.a).

Used as a sleeping-place for visitors Il. 24.673 (Priam and the herald in Achilles's dwelling):=Od. 4.302 (Telemachus and Pisistratus in Menelaus's house) (cf. Il. 24.644:=Od. 4.297). Cf. Od. 15.5, Od. 20.1 (the disguised Odysseus in his own house), 143 (the same in the same).
A space in front of the door of the dwelling of Eumaeus Od. 14.5.
To stand in front of someone and debar (him from doing something).
With infin.: πάντας προέεργε ἐπὶ νῆας ὁδεύειν Il. 11.569.
3 pl. aor. subj. mid. προΐδωνται Od. 13.155.
To direct one's glance forward, look forward or before one: ὀξὺ μάλα προϊδών Od. 5.393. Cf. Il. 22.275.
To catch sight of, descry, see: τὰ προϊδόντες Il. 18.527. Cf. Il. 17.756.
To catch sight of beforehand: μή πώς με προϊδὼν ἀλέηται (catching sight of me before the time) Od. 4.396.
To row one's ship forward, row it to a specified place Od. 13.279.
To row (one's ship) forward, row (it) to a specified place: νῆʼ εἰς ὅρμον προέρεσσαν Il. 1.435:=Od. 15.497. Cf. Od. 9.73.
To draw down (a ship) in order to launch her Il. 1.308, Il. 9.358.
To project, jut out: πύργῳ ἐπὶ προὔχοντι (a projecting angle of the wall) Il. 22.97. Cf. Od. 6.138, Od. 10.90, Od. 12.11, Od. 19.544, Od. 24.82.
In mid., to have in front of one: προὔχοντʼ ἐννέα ταύρους (i.e. they faced the sea with the bulls in front of them) Od. 3.8.
To be in front in a race: τὸν προὔχοντα δοκεύει Il. 23.325, φράσσαθʼ ἵππον προὔχοντα 453.
App., from the foundations onwards, i.e. by the roots (cf. πρόρριζος): προθέλυμνα χαμαὶ βάλε δένδρεα Il. 9.541. Cf. Il. 10.15.
App., with base advanced: σάκεϊ Il. 13.130.
3 sing. pa. iterative προθέεσκε Il. 22.459: Od. 11.515.
To flee before a pursuer Il. 10.362.
To rush to the fray in front of others: πολὺ προθέεσκεν Il. 22.459: =Od. 11.515.
Fig., of speech, to dash forward (for utterance) Il. 1.291.
To leap or spring forward Il. 14.363, Il. 17.522, 523.
In pl.: ᾗσι προθυμίῃσι πεποιθώς (his heart full of ardour for the fray) Il. 2.588.
The gateway of the αὐλή Il. 24.323: Od. 1.119, Od. 3.493=Od. 15.146 = 191.
So in pl. (cf. θύρη 2..b): στῆμεν ἐνὶ προθύροισιν Il. 11.777. Cf. Il. 18.496, Il. 22.71: Od. 1.103, Od. 4.20, Od. 7.4.
Of the gate of the steading of Eumaeus Od. 14.34.

The doorway of the μέγαρον: κεῖται ἀνὰ πρόθυρον τετραμμένος Il. 19.212 (i.e. the doorway of the chief room of the hut): εἶκε προθύρου Od. 18.10. Cf. Od. 18.101, 386, Od. 20.355, Od. 21.299, Od. 22.474.
Of such a doorway in the palace of Zeus Il. 15.124.
To send forth or dispatch on a mission or errand or to take up an occupation: ἐμὲ Ζεὺς τῷ ἐπαλεξήσουσαν προΐαλλεν Il. 8.365. Cf. Il. 11.3: Od. 15.370.
To send away or dispatch for use: σιάλων τὸν ἄριστον Od. 14.18.
To send, dispatch: πολλὰς ψυχὰς Ἄϊδι Il. 1.3. Cf. Il. 5.190, Il. 6.487, Il. 11.55.
To send forth, throw, hurl, launch, let fly (a missile): ἔγχος Il. 3.346. Cf. Il. 3.355, Il. 8.297, Il. 13.662, Il. 20.438, etc.: Od. 24.519 = 522.
Absol., to throw, make a throw, make one's throw: ὣς φάμενος προέηκεν Il. 5.290.
To throw or let fall (fishing tackle) Od. 12.253.
To send from oneself, let fall from one's grasp: πόδα Od. 19.468. Cf. Od. 5.316.
To let fall (a word), send forth or utter (speech) Od. 14.466, Od. 20.105.
Of a river, to send or roll (its waters): Τιταρησσόν, ὅς ῥʼ ἐς πηνειὸν προϊεῖ ὕδωρ Il. 2.752.

To send forth or dispatch on a specified or indicated mission or to a specified destination: Βρισηΐδος εἵνεκα κούρης Il. 1.336, Ταλθύβιον νῆας ἔπι ἰέναι Il. 3.118. Cf. Il. 1.326, Il. 7.468, Il. 9.442, Il. 10.125, Il. 11.201, Il. 12.342, etc.: Od. 2.147, Od. 4.161, Od. 8.399, Od. 12.9, Od. 16.328, etc.
To let go, surrender: τήνδε θεῷ πρόες Il. 1.127.
Of something immaterial, to send: ἀγγελίας Od. 2.92=Od. 13.381. Cf. Il. 11.270, Il. 16.241.
[genit. of προίξ, gift. Of one's bounty, as a free gift (genit. of material).]
Without repayment or reimbursement: χαρίσασθαι Od. 13.15.
App., without paying for it, with impunity: γεύσεσθαι Ἀχαιῶν Od. 17.413.
To set in front, put forward Il. 4.156.
Of birds, to keep settling (ever) forwards Il. 2.463.
3 sing. aor. mid. προ-καλέσσατο Il. 7.218, 285, Il. 13.809.
In mid., to summon or invite to the fight or to a contest, challenge, defy, dare: μαχέσασθαι ἐναντίον Il. 3.432. Cf. Il. 7.39, 50, 218, 285, Il. 13.809: Od. 8.142.
=προκαλέω. Il. 3.19, Il. 4.389, Il. 5.807, Il. 7.150: Od. 8.228, Od. 18.20 (to fisticuffs).
To be set before one, be set to one's hand: ὀνείαθʼ ἑτοῖμα προκείμενα. See Il. 9.91, etc., cited under ἑτοῖμος 1.
Of report or fame, heard of old; or perh., heard forwards, handed on by tradition Il. 20.204.
App., row after row, in rows or ranks: [νῆας] προκρόσσας ἔρυσαν Il. 14.35.
In mid., of the sea, to roll forward Il. 14.18.
Absol. in pf. pass. pple. pl., the picked men, the flower: Ἀθηναίων προλελεγμένοι Il. 13.689.
Aor. pple. προλιπών Od. 3.314, Od. 15.11, Od. 23.120.
To leave, forsake, abandon, leave to one's own devices or to one's (or its) fate: κτήματα Od. 3.314=Od. 15.11 (with ἄνδρας in the same lines simply leaving behind you). Cf. Il. 17.275: Od. 13.331.
Of a quality, to forsake (one), fail (him): οὐδέ σε μῆτις Ὀδυσσῆος προλέλοιπεν Od. 2.279.
To leave, quit, withdraw from: πηοὺς καὶ πατρίδα γαῖαν Od. 23.120.
To act or pose as champion Il. 3.16.
To fight with in front of the others.
With dat.: μηκέτʼ Ἀχιλλῆϊ προμάχιζε Il. 20.376.
To fight in front of the others Il. 17.358.
With genit.: ἁπάντων (to advance beyond them) Il. 11.217.
[προ- 2 + μάχομαι. He who fights in front.]
In pl., the front rank, the fighting line, the forefront of the battle: ἐν προμάχοισι φανέντα Il. 3.31. Cf. Il. 4.253, 495, Il. 5.134, 250, Il. 11.188, 358, etc.: Od. 18.379, Od. 24.526.
In pass., to have sexual intercourse with in anticipation of another.
With dat.: παλλακίδι προμιγῆναι Il. 9.452 (app., to take an opportunity of anticipating his father and so making felt the contrast between the two).
[perh. formed fr. *πρόμνηστις, abstract noun fr. προ- 1 + μένω. Cf. ἀγχιστῖνοι.]
Each waiting his turn before going forward, one after another: ἐπήϊσαν Od. 11.233, ἐσέλθετε Od. 21.230.

Absol., a leading fighter, a champion:
ἐκ πάντων πρόμος ἔμμεναι Ἕκτορι (against Hector) Il. 7.75. Cf. Il. 3.44, Il. 7.116, 136, Il. 15.293, Il. 22.85: Od. 11.493.
To perceive or detect beforehand, have an inkling of: δόλον Il. 18.526.
In front, before: π. κιών Il. 15.260. Cf. Il. 15.355 (going before them), Il. 16.319 (at his feet): Od. 4.225 (before his eyes).
With genit. in geographical sense: νῆσος αἰγύπτου π. (lying off ...) Od. 4.355.

div.head: a
div.p: Before, sooner than, someone else: π. ἰδών Il. 10.476.
Before another, preceding him in time: εἶμι π. (will go first) Od. 17.277. Cf. Od. 17.282.

div.head: b
div.p: Before the happening of something: π. σφι φάνη μέγα ἔργον Ἄρηος (ere that) Il. 11.734. Cf. Il. 22.197.

div.head: c
div.p: In time past, formerly: οὔ τις ἀνὴρ π. μακάρτατος οὔτʼ ἄρʼ ὀπίσσω Od. 11.483.
Strengthened form of, but hardly to be distinguished from, πᾶς.
In sing., all the, the whole: πρόπαν ἦμαρ (all the day long) Il. 19.162, Il. 24.713, Il. 1.601:=Od. 9.161 = 556=Od. 10.183 = 476=Od. 12.29=Od. 19.424, Od. 24.41.
In pl., all the: νῆας προπάσας Il. 2.493.
To send or dispatch on an errand.
With complementary fut. pple.: ἄξοντα κύνα Il. 8.367.
To dispatch on one's way, arrange for the departure of: ἐς Μενέλαον Od. 17.117.
To send on ahead of oneself: τὸν προὔπεμψα σὺν ἑτάροισιν Od. 17.54. Cf. Od. 24.360.
Nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. προπεσόντες.
To bend the body forward (so as to swing to the oar): προπεσόντες ἔρεσσον Od. 9.490, Od. 12.194.
To set the foot forward, to advance, march along Il. 13.158, 806.
In neut. sing. προπρηνές as adv., forwards: σκῆπτρον οὔτʼ ὀπἰσω οὔτε π. ἐνώμα Il. 3.218.
In pass., of a wanderer, to be rolled on and on, be tossed ever onwards: δεῦρʼ ἵκετο προπροκυλινδόμενος Od. 17.525.
In mid., to grovel before the face of.
With genit.: πατρὸς Διός Il. 22.221 (the genit. app. depending on one προ- (προ- 2), the other προ- strengthening the vb. (προ- 4)).
Of rivers, streams, etc., to flow forward or forth, flow, send their waters: ἅλαδε Il. 5.598, Il. 12.19. Cf. Il. 21.260, 366, Il. 22.151: Od. 5.444, Od. 10.351.
From the roots onwards, by the roots, roots and all (cf. προ-θέλυμνος): ὡς ὅτʼ ἐξερίπῃ δρῦς π. Il. 14.415. Cf. Il. 11.157.
For, to equip, something: πρὸς δʼ ἄρα πηδάλιον ποιήσατο Od. 5.255.
Besides, in addition, too: πρὸς δʼ ἄμφω ῥῆξε τένοντε Il. 5.307. Cf. Il. 12.102, Il. 13.678, Il. 22.59: Od. 14.415, Od. 16.291, Od. 19.10, Od. 20.41.

div.head: a
div.p: Making contact with, upon, against: πρὸς περόνῃ καταμύξατο χεῖρα Il. 5.425: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται Od. 5.329. Cf. Od. 5.434.
With locative: ὡς ὅτε πρὸς κοτυληδονόφιν λάϊγγες ἔχονται Od. 5.433.
In pregnant sense: πέτρῃς πρὸς μεγάλῃσι βαλόν Od. 7.279. Cf. Od. 9.284, 459.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to position, in the direction of, towards: τέτραπτο πρὸς ἰθύ οἱ Il. 14.403.

div.head: c
div.p: Besides, in addition to: πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος Od. 10.68.

div.head: a
div.p: To, towards, in the direction of: εἶμʼ αὐτὴ πρὸς Ὄλυμπον Il. 1.420. Cf. Il. 1.609, Il. 2.310, Il. 5.398, Il. 6.41, Il. 8.74, Il. 15.58, etc.: Od. 2.258, 298, Od. 7.131, Od. 9.315, Od. 10.278, etc.
In hostile sense, against: ἐστρατόωντο πρὸς τείχεα Θήβης Il. 4.378. Cf. Il. 12.332, Il. 17.471.
Indicating arrival at a point: πρὸς τεῖχος ἀφικάνει Il. 6.388. Cf. Od. 19.458, etc.
In opposition to, against the will of: πρὸς δαίμονα φωτὶ μάχεσθαι Il. 17.98. Cf. Il. 17.104.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to speech or directing the voice, to: καί με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν Il. 2.59. Cf. Il. 2.156, Il. 3.155, Il. 5.274, Il. 8.364, etc.: Od. 4.803, Od. 5.298, Od. 10.34, etc.
Sim. in reference to swearing: ὤμοσε πρὸς ἔμʼ αὐτόν Od. 14.331, Od. 19.288.
In reference to conversation, with: πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἐνέποντες Il. 11.643. Cf. Od. 23.301.
In reference to the sight, to, towards: παπταίνοντι πρὸς πέτρην Od. 12.233. Cf. Od. 13.29, etc.

div.head: c
div.p: In reference to the direction in which action takes place, towards, against: πρὸς κῦμα χανών Od. 12.350. Cf. Od. 17.237.

div.head: d
div.p: In reference to wounding or striking a part of the body, in: βεβλήκει πρὸς στῆθος Il. 4.108. Cf. Il. 11.144, Il. 21.424, etc.: Od. 9.301, etc.

div.head: e
div.p: In reference to placing or leaning against something: ἅρματʼ ἔκλιναν πρὸς ἐνώπια Il. 8.435:=Od. 4.42. Cf. Il. 22.112, Il. 23.171, etc.: Od. 1.127, Od. 22.120, etc.
Sim.: Ἀμφινόμου πρὸς γοῦνα καθέζετο (sat down leaning against ...) Od. 18.395. Cf. Od. 23.90.

div.head: f
div.p: In reference to position, in the direction of, towards: πρὸς Τρῶας τετραμμένοι Il. 5.605. Cf. Od. 9.26, Od. 13.240, etc.–

div.head: g
div.p: In reference to exchanging things with a person: ὃς πρὸς Διομήδεα τεύχεʼ ἄμειβεν Il. 6.235.

div.head: a
div.p: In reference to position or to the taking place of some phenomenon, in the direction of, towards: πρὸς ἁλὸς κᾶρες ...πρὸς θύμβρης δʼ ἔλαχον λύκιοι Il. 10.428, φόως γένετʼ ἠμὲν πρὸς νηῶν καὶ πολέμοιο Il. 15.670. Cf. Od. 13.110, 111, Od. 21.347.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to coming from a specified quarter: ἀλώμενος ἵκετʼ ἐμὸν δῶ, ἠὲ πρὸς ἠοίων ἦ ἑσπερίων ἀνθρώπων Od. 8.29.
Sim.: πρὸς διός εἰσι ξεῖνοι Od. 6.207, Od. 14.57.

div.head: c
div.p: At the hands of, from, by: τιμὴν ἀρνύμενοι πρὸς Τρώων Il. 1.160, ἦ σοι ἄριστα πεποίηται πρὸς Τρώων; Il. 6.57. Cf. Il. 6.525, Il. 16.85, etc.: Od. 11.302, Od. 18.162.
By the commission of: οἵ τε θέμιστας πρὸς Διὸς εἰρύαται Il. 1.239.

div.head: d
div.p: Before the face of: οὐδʼ ἐπιορκήσω πρὸς δαίμονος Il. 19.188. Cf. Il. 1.339, 340.
In entreaty, in the name of, by: νῦν σε πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι Od. 13.324. Cf. Od. 11.67.– At the bidding of: πρός κʼ ἄλλης ἱστὸν ὑφαίνοις Il. 6.456.
To bring to an indicated place : τίς δαίμων τόδε πῆμα προσήγαγεν; (has brought hither) Od. 17.446.
To rush in an indicated direction : ἦ λίσσοιτο προσαΐξας Ὀδυσῆα (run up to him and . . .) Od. 22.337. Cf. Od. 22.342, 365.
With dat. : προσάλειφεν ἑκάστῳ φάρμακον ἄλλο Od. 10.392.
To bring help or succour to, help, aid.
With dat. : ἤ τί οἱ χἠμεῖς προσαμύνομεν Il. 2.238.
Absol, to bring succour, make defence, show fight for someone or something Il. 5.139, Il. 16.509.
Nom. pl. neut. pf. pple. προσαρηρότα.
In pf., to be fitted to something : ἐπίσσωτρα προσαρηρότα Il. 5.725.
3 dual non-thematic impf. προσαυδήτην Il. 11.136, Il. 22.90.
To speak to, address, accost : κερτομίοισι διὰ προσηύδα Il. 1.539. Cf. Il. 4.192, 256, Il. 5.30, Il. 6.144, Il. 11.136, etc. : Od. 1.252, Od. 3.41, Od. 9.345, Od. 11.99, Od. 14.484, etc.
Without expressed object, to make address, speak Il. 4.24, Il. 7.225, Il. 12.353, etc. : Od. 10.400, Od. 14.79, Od. 15.62, etc.
To say in way of address, speak, utter : ἔπεα πτερόεντα Il. 4.92, 203, Il. 5.871, Il. 16.706, etc. : Od. 2.362, Od. 4.25, Od. 10.377, Od. 16.22, etc.

With double construction of (1) and (2), to address words to : ἔπεά μιν πτερόεντα προσηύδα Il. 1.201. Cf. Il. 4.69, Il. 5.242, Il. 12.365, Il. 13.94, etc. : Od. 1.122, Od. 4.77, Od. 10.265, Od. 16.7, etc.
3 sing. aor. mid. προσεβήσετο Il. 2.48, Il. 14.292 : Od. 21.5, 43.
To go one's way, proceed, in a specified direction : προσέβη τρηχεῖαν ἀταρπόν (advbl. acc., by a . . .) Od. 14.1.

p.gloss: To go to or towards, approach.

div.p: With acc. : κνημοὺς Ἴδης Il. 23.117. Cf. Od. 19.431.
In mid. : Ὄλυμπον Il. 2.48. Cf. Il. 14.292.

p.gloss: To step upon, set foot upon.

div.p: With acc. In mid. : κλίμακα Od. 21.5, οὐδόν 43.
Without expressed object : λὰξ προσβάς (setting his foot upon upon the corpse) Il. 5.620, Il. 16.863.
To smite. Of the rays of the sun : Ἠέλιος νέον προσέβαλλεν ἀρούρας Il. 7.421 := Od. 19.433.
In mid., to give heed to, direct one's attention to : ταύτην οὐ προτιβάλλεαι Il. 5.879.

p.gloss: To direct the sight to, look towards.

div.p: With acc. : πατέρα προσεδέρκετο Od. 20.385. Cf. Il. 16.10 : Od. 17.518.
To speak to, address, accost : Κάλχαντα Il. 1.105. Cf. Il. 1.206, Il. 8.138, Il. 11.602, Il. 16.432, Il. 17.11, etc. : Od. 1.178, Od. 2.39, Od. 4.461, Od. 6.56, Od. 8.144, etc.
Without expressed object, to make address, speak Il. 24.361 : Od. 4.234, Od. 24.350, 393.
With double acc. of the person addressed and of what is said : ὄφρα τί μιν προτιείποι Il. 22.329.
To approach, draw near, draw up : ζωὸν προσιόντα Il. 5.515= Il. 7.308. Cf. Il. 5.682, Il. 10.339, Il. 11.742, Il. 13.615 : Od. 16.5.
Of the sea, to roar, or, perh., to break in foam, against.
With acc. : κύματα, τά τε προσερεύγεται αὐτήν Il. 15.621.

div.head: a
div.p: In front of, before, preceding, someone or something (often with the notion of defence) : π. σάκεα σχέθον Il. 4.113, π. στᾶσα 129. Cf. Il. 5.300, 315, Il. 6.17, Il. 13.440, etc. : π. δέ οἱ ποίησε γαλήνην Od. 5.452. Cf. Od. 22.400, Od. 24.155.
With genit. : τάων οὔ τοι ἐγὼ π. ἵσταμαι Il. 4.54. Cf. Il. 5.56, 107, Il. 7.224, Il. 9.473, etc. : στῆ π. αὐτοῦ Od. 7.21. Cf. Od. 8.524, Od. 15.164, Od. 22.4, Od. 24.540.

div.head: b
div.p: Before, in the front part : π. λέων Il. 6.181.

div.head: c
div.p: In front or in advance of others : ὁππότεροι π. ἵπποι Il. 23.487. Cf. Il. 23.572, etc.
With genit. : οἶος π. ἄλλων Il. 4.304.

div.head: a
div.p: Before, in time past, in days of old : οὖ καὶ π. ἀρίστη φαίνετο βουλή Il. 7.325. Cf. Il. 1.251, Il. 12.33, Il. 20.28, Il. 23.570, etc. : π. μοι ἀεικέλιος δέατʼ εἶναι Od. 6.242. Cf. Od. 17.371, Od. 22.432, Od. 24.52.
In adjectival use : τῶν π. ἀνδρῶν Il. 9.524.

div.head: b
div.p: Before another or others, first : ἔγνω π. Il. 13.66, Il. 24.698. Cf. Il. 3.317, 346, Il. 5.851 : Od. 9.370.
With genit., before, sooner than : ὄφρα π. ἄλλων θάνατον ἐπίσπῃ (that he may be the foremost to perish) Il. 2.359.

div.head: c
div.p: Before the arrival of a specified or indicated time past or future, earlier, sooner : π. μιν μοῖρʼ ἀμφεκάλυψεν (ere that) Il. 12.116 : μὴ π. κλέος γένηται, πρὶν . . . Od. 23.137. Cf. Od. 17.7, Od. 23.223.
To be put upon something, be put in position : οὔατʼ οὔ πω προσέκειτο Il. 18.379.
Involving a close tie, that binds closely together Od. 21.35.

p.gloss: To cause to lean, set, support, against.

div.p: With dat. : βέλος προσέκλινε κορώνῃ Od. 21.138= 165.
In pass., to lean or be supported (so as to be) close to.
With dat.: πατρὸς ἐμοῖο θρόνος ποτικέκλιται αὐτῇ (is set close to the queen's) Od. 6.308.
In mid., to lay oneself down, recline, beside or at the feet of another : εἶσέ τέ [με] καὶ προσέλεκτο Od. 12.34.
To bring into contact with, cause to touch.
With dat. : ἄκρῃ προσπελάσας [νῆα] (dashing it against a . . .) Od. 9.285.
To be brought into contact with, touch.
With dat. : νήσῳ προσεπίλνατο νηῦς (made the island) Od. 13.95.

Of water, to beat up against something : κῦμα χιόνα προσπλάζον
ἐρύκεται Il. 12.285.
With dat. : λίμνη προσέπλαζε γενείῳ Od. 11.583.
To fold to one's bosom, embrace Od. 11.451.
To greet, convey good wishes to Od. 8.478.
With double acc. of the person addressed and of what is said : ὄφρα τί μιν προσπτύξομαι Od. 17.509.
Before one : ἐλαύνων πρόσσοθεν ἵππους Il. 23.533.
To make one's way to, proceed to.

Of the direction of motion, forwards, onwards, on : δοῦρʼ ὄρμενα πρόσσω Il. 11.572. Cf. Il. 11.615, Il. 12.274, Il. 13.291, Il. 15.543, Il. 16.265 (straight for his object), 382, Il. 17.734, Il. 18.388 : νῆα πρόσω φέρε κῦμα Od. 9.542. Cf. Od. 21.369.

In reference to the exercise of a mental faculty : νοῆσαι ἅμα πρόσσω καὶ ὀπίσσω (to look before and after, be capable of reasoning from the past to the future) Il. 1.343. Cf. Il. 3.109, Il. 18.250 : Od. 24.452.
Of change of position, forwards : πρόσσω κατέκυψεν Il. 16.611= Il. 17.527.
Of position, forwards, facing one's front : πρόσω τετραμμένος Il. 17.598.
To set or place in an indicated position : λίθον, ὃν προσέθηκεν Od. 9.305.
[προσ-, app. with sense before one's very eyes, in one's view + φα-, φαν-, φαίνω. (As if) newly revealed.]
Without expressed object, to make address, speak Il. 2.172, Il. 5.439, Il. 10.369, etc. : Od. 10.422, Od. 11.565, Od. 15.9.
To say in way of address, speak, utter.
With double construction of (1) and (2) : τὴν οὔ τι προσέφη Il. 1.511. Cf. Il. 4.401, Il. 5.689= Il. 6.342, Il. 8.484, Il. 21.478 : Od. 20.183.
Attached to, forming part of, something : θρῆνυν προσφυέʼ ἐκ κλισίης Od. 19.58.
To grow to; hence, to attach oneself to something : τοῦ μέσον ἧπαρ ἔχοιμι ἐσθέμεναι προσφῦσα (burying my teeth in it) Il. 24.213.

p.gloss: To attach oneself to, seize, grasp.

div.p: Without expressed object, to make address, speak Od. 5.159, Od. 10.109.
With double acc. of the person addressed and of what is said : οὐδέ τί μιν προσεφώνεον Il. 1.332, Il. 8.445.
[προσ- 1 + ὦπα. The part beside the eyes, the region of the eyes.]
Acc. προσώπατα Od. 18.192. The face, visage, countenance : χαρίεν Il. 18.24. Cf. Od. 15.332, Od. 20.352.
In pl. in the same sense : πρόσωπα καὶ χεῖρʼ ἀπομόργνυ Il. 18.414. Cf. Il. 7.212, Il. 19.285 : Od. 8.85, Od. 18.173 (ἀμφί advbl., πρόσωπα acc. of part affected), 192, Od. 19.361.
To carry a cutting process forward in a specified direction : κορμὸν ἐκ ῥίζης προταμών (cutting it into shape) Od. 23.196.
In reference to priority in time, to cut off something before : πρίν γʼ ὅτε σʼ ὄψου ἄσαιμι προταμών (cutting thee off the first morsel) Il. 9.489.
In mid., to cut (a furrow) before or in front of one Od. 18.375.
That is in front : ἐν προτέροισι πόδεσσιν (his fore-paws) Od. 19.228.
Sooner, earlier : οὔ τις π. τόν γʼ εἴσεται (before you) Il. 1.548, π. γεγόνει (had been born before him, was the elder) Il. 13.355. Cf. Il. 17.14, Il. 19.219, Il. 21.440 : Od. 2.31, 43.
With genit., sooner than, before : ἐμέο π. ἐπέγρετο Il. 10.124.
With πρίν: οὐκ εἴων προτέρην αἵματος ἆσσον ἴμεν, πρὶν . . . (to do so before . . ., until I should . . .) Od. 11.88.
In neut. sing. πρότερον as adv., sooner Il. 14.467.

div.head: a
div.p: Doing, succeeding in doing, something before another, anticipating him, taking the lead or initiative, assuming the aggressive, commencing, first (cf. πρῶτος 5..a) : ὁππότεροι πρότεροι πημήνειαν Il. 3.299, πρότερος προΐει ἔγχος Il. 5.15. Cf. Il. 3.351, Il. 4.67, Il. 5.276, Il. 8.253 (cutting in), Il. 16.569, Il. 19.183, etc. : Od. 3.13, Od. 16.460, Od. 20.394, Od. 24.23, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: Sim. in oblique cases of one to whom action is directed before another, first (cf. πρῶτος 5..b) : ὑμῖν πὰρ προτέροισι πυρὸν ἔθηκεν Il. 8.188. Cf. Il. 15.157 : Od. 3.50, 53.
Belonging to time past : ἐπὶ προτέρων ἀνθρώπων (in the days of the men of old) Il. 5.637, Il. 23.332. Cf. Il. 11.691, Il. 21.405 : Od. 8.223, Od. 11.630.
Absol. in pl., the men of old : οἱ πρότεροι Il. 4.308.
Born sooner, older : π. καὶ ἀρείων Il. 2.707, Il. 23.588 : Od. 19.184. Cf. Il. 15.166, 182.
Belonging to the past as opposed to the present, the former . . ., one's former . . .: ἀνδρός Il. 3.140. Cf. Il. 3.163, 429 : Od. 15.22, Od. 19.504, Od. 22.264 (to add to the former wrongs).
The preceding . . . : ἠοῖ τῇ προτέρῃ Il. 13.794. Cf. Il. 21.5, Il. 23.790 (of the last generation and the men who lived then).
Absol. : τῇ προτέρῃ (sc. ἡμέρῃ), the day before Od. 16.50.
Further, further on, to a greater distance : ἦ πῄ με π. πολίων ἄξεις; (local genit., among the cities) Il. 3.400. Cf. Il. 5.672 : Od. 5.417.
Forwards, towards one's front, onwards, on : ἴθυσαν Il. 4.507.

Forward, on (contextually, in reference to persons entering or advancing into a house, in) : βάτην (entered)
Il. 9.192, ἄγε (brought them in) 199, βάτην (pursued their way) Il. 10.469, ἔπεο (come in) Il. 18.387 := Od. 5.91, ἐς δʼ αὐτοὺς προτέρω ἄγε Od. 4.36, πλέομεν (pursued our course) Od. 9.62 = 105 = 565 = Od. 10.77 = 133, νῆες κίον (set sail) Od. 9.64, βὰν ἰέναι Od. 15.109.

In reference to prolongation or continuance of action or a state of things, further, yet further, longer : προτέρω κʼ ἔτʼ ἔρις γένετο (would have gone yet further) Il. 23.490, εἴ κʼ ἔτι προτέρω γένετο δρόμος (had continued) 526. Cf. Od. 4.667 (see ἄρχω 1.a), Od. 14.356, Od. 24.475.
To cause to go forth, let go forth : τὰ προτετύχθαι ἐάσομεν (regard these things as gone on their way, put them out of our minds, let bygones be bygones) Il. 16.60, Il. 18.112= Il. 19.65.

div.head: I
div.p: Adv. Besides, in addition, too : ἐκ χροὸς ἕλκε δόρυ, προτὶ δὲ φρένες αὐτῷ ἕποντο (i.e. the spear drew out the midriff with it) Il. 16.504. Cf. Od. 17.379.

div.head: a
div.p: On, upon, in pregnant sense : βαλλόμενα προτὶ γαίῃ Il. 22.64.

div.head: b
div.p: In the direction of, towards : τὴν προτὶ οἶ εἷλεν Il. 21.507. Cf. Il. 20.418.

div.head: a
div.p: To, towards, in the direction of : ἔρχονται προτὶ ἄστυ Il. 2.801. Cf. Il. 3.116, Il. 7.310, Il. 10.336, Il. 11.26, etc. : Od. 4.9, Od. 7.2, Od. 8.517, Od. 9.147, etc.
Indicating arrival at a point : ἵκοντο προτὶ ἄστυ Od. 24.154. Cf. Od. 13.181.
In reference to attaching or suspending : κρεμόω
[τεύχεα] προτὶ νηόν (i.e. will carry them there and hang them up) Il. 7.83.

div.head: b
div.p: In reference to speech, to : προτὶ ὃν μυθήσατο θυμόν Il. 17.200, 442 := Od. 5.285 = 376.

div.head: c
div.p: In reference to the direction in which action takes place, towards, against : προτὶ πέτρας κῦμα ῥοχθεῖ Od. 12.59.
With genit. In reference to that from which one derives something : τά σε προτί φασιν Ἀχιλλῆος δεδιδάχθαι Il. 11.831.
With dat. Of something immaterial : τόδε κῦδος Ἀχιλλῆϊ προτιάπτω (grant it to him) Il. 24.110.
To force to take, drive into, a specified course : ἐπὶ νῆας ἀπὸ στρατόφι Il. 10.347.
To set or place before one : ἦέ μιν ᾖσι κυσὶ προὔθηκεν Il. 24.409 : τραπέζας (set ready for the feast) Od. 1.112.
With acc. : ἑὸν υἱὸν προτιμυθήσασθαι Od. 11.143.
To direct the eyes towards, look at Od. 7.31, Od. 23.365.
To bode, forebode, have a presentiment of, apprehend : ὄλεθρον Od. 5.389, θάνατον Od. 14.219.
Absol., to see one's fate before one, forebode it Il. 22.356.
App., the cut place in front, i.e. the navel Il. 11.424.
The forestays of a mast (cf. ἐπίτονος) Il. 1.434 : Od. 2.425= Od. 15.290, Od. 12.409.
3 sing. aor. subj. mid. προτράπηται Od. 11.18.
To go forward or take one's way in a specified direction. Of the sun : ὅτʼ ἂν ἂψ ἐπὶ γαῖαν ἀπʼ οὐρανόθεν προτράπηται Od. 11.18. Cf. Od. 12.381.
To turn and flee in a specified direction : ἐπὶ νηῶν Il. 5.700.
Fig., to betake oneself to something, yield oneself up to it : ἄχεϊ προτραπέσθαι Il. 6.336.
Turning right away in an indicated direction, in downright flight, headlong (cf. προτρέπω. (2)) : φοβέοντο Il. 16.304.
To dash or press forwards : Τρῶες προὔτυψαν ἀολλέες Il. 13.136= Il. 15.306= Il. 17.262.
Of passion : ἀνὰ ῥῖνας δριμὺ μένος προὔτυψεν (burst forth) Od. 24.319.
Impf. act. and pass. προὔφαινον, προὐφαινόμην.
Acc. sing. masc. aor. pple. pass. προφανέντα Od. 24.160.
To show forth, show, display : τέραα Od. 12.394.
Intrans., to give forth light, be visible : οὐδὲ σελήνη προὔφαινεν Od. 9.145.

In pass., to come into view, appear, make one's appearance, present oneself : προφανέντε ἀνὰ πτολέμοιο γεφύρας Il. 8.378, τὰ προπέφανται ἅπαντα (lie open to view) Il. 14.332. Cf. Il. 17.487, Il. 24.332 : Od. 13.169, Od. 24.160.–Impers. : οὐδὲ προὐφαίνετʼ ἰδέσθαι (there was not light enough to see) Od. 9.143.

A profession or declaration. Adverbially in acc., as the cause that moves one, as the occasion (cf. ἐπίκλησις 2, χάρις 2.b) : κλαίουσα, ἐπὶ δὲ στενάχοντο γυναῖκες, Πάτροκλον πρόφασιν, σφῶν δʼ αὐτῶν κήδεʼ ἑκάστη Il. 19.302 (i.e. his death was the immediate occasion, and each had her own griefs as well).
With genit. : εὐνῆς πρόφασιν (for the sake of . . .) Il. 19.262.
Comp. προφερέστερος, -η, better, more skilled or serviceable : ἐμεῖο προφερέστεροι Od. 21.134. Cf. Il. 10.352 : Od. 8.221.
Superl. προφερέστατος, the best, the most skilled : ἅλματι πάντων προφερέστατος ἦεν (at . . ., in . . .) Od. 8.128.
To bear or carry in a specified or indicated direction or to a specified or indicated destination : ὡς ὄρνις νεοσσοῖσι προφέρῃσι μάστακα Il. 9.323. Cf. Il. 6.346, Il. 17.121 : Od. 20.64.
To put forth, display : κρατερὸν μένος Il. 10.479.
To bring forth, utter (abuse) : ὀνείδεα Il. 2.251.
To cast in one's teeth : δῶρʼ Ἀφροδίτης Il. 3.64.
To offer (battle) (cf. Il. 11.529 cited under προβάλλω 1).
To display, engage in (rivalry) : ἔριδα προφέρουσαι Od. 6.92.
To flee from, escape from, escape, elude : μένος καὶ χεῖρας Ἀχαιῶν Il. 6.502. Cf. Il. 7.309, Il. 14.81 : Od. 11.107, Od. 22.325.
Zealously, earnestly, seriously Il. 5.810, 816, Il. 6.173, Il. 7.160, Il. 17.224.

Displaying zeal, eagerness, earnestness : ὄμοσσον ἦ μέν μοι π. ἀρήξειν (zealously) Il. 1.77, πῶς τίς τοι π. ἔπεσιν πείθηται; (with alacrity) 150. Cf. Il. 1.543 (readily gratifying me), Il. 8.23 (with a will), 175 (really meaning it), Il. 9.480 (with hearty hospitality), Il. 10.290 (with zealous solicitude), Il. 14.71, 357 (with all your energies), Il. 17.353 (with good spirit), Il. 21.500 (boldly), Il. 22.303, Il. 23.647 (gladly) : Od. 2.230= Od. 5.8 (with honest zeal), Od. 2.387 (willingly), Od. 5.143 (with sincere thought for his good), 161 (without grudging), Od. 8.498 (in full measure), Od. 9.355 (give me more and plenty), Od. 10.386 (in good earnest), Od. 13.359 (take thought for me and . . .), 391, Od. 14.54 (with hearty hospitality), 406 (should be fain to . . .), Od. 19.398 (solicitously), Od. 20.372, Od. 23.314.
Of the heart, zealous, eager, earnest : θυμῷ πρόφρονι (in earnest, really meaning it) Il. 8.40= Il. 22.184, Il. 24.140. Cf. Il. 10.244 : Od. 16.257.
In pass., of bodies of men, to pour or stream in a specified direction : τῇ προχέοντο πεφυζότες Il. 21.6. Cf. Il. 2.465, Il. 15.360.
App., utterly : ὀλέσθαι Od. 14.69. Cf. Il. 21.460.
App., of sitting, full on the ground, with limbs extended on the ground : καθεζομένη Il. 9.570.
The place where a river flows into the sea, its mouth : ἐπὶ προχοῇσι ποταμοῖο Il. 17.263. Cf. Od. 5.453, Od. 11.242.
In reference to Ocean, app., its stream : ἐν προχοῇς Ὠκεανοῖο Od. 20.65.
A vessel for holding water to be poured on the hands Il. 24.304 : Od. 1.136= Od. 4.52= Od. 7.172= Od. 10.368= Od. 15.135= Od. 17.91.
A vessel from which to pour wine into the cups Od. 18.397.
On foot : πρυλέες ῥώοντο (Ἕκτορι ἑπώμεθα) Il. 11.49= Il. 12.77.
Absol. in pl., fighters on foot, footmen : ἡγεμόνα πρυλέων Il. 15.517.
With the notion on foot not prominent, fighters in gen. : τὸν πρώτοισι μετὰ πρυλέεσσι δάμασσας Il. 21.90. Cf. Il. 5.744.
The stern (of a ship) : τῆς (sc. νηὸς) πρύμνη ἀείρετο Od. 13.84.
Without νηός, a ship's stern : ἐν πρύμνῃ καθέζετο Od. 15.285. Cf. Il. 1.409, Il. 8.475, Il. 14.32, Il. 15.385, Il. 16.124, Il. 18.76, 447.

In apposition with νηῦς : νηῒ πάρα πρύμνῃ Ἀγαμέμνονος (by the stern of . . . 's ship) Il. 7.383. Cf. Il. 10.35, 570, Il. 11.600, Il. 12.403, Il. 13.333, 762, Il. 14.51, 65, Il. 15.248, 435, 704, 722, Il. 16.286, Il. 19.135 : Od. 2.417, Od. 12.411, Od. 13.75 (at the stern), Od. 15.206, 223.
From, in the direction from, beginning with, the stern : πρύμνηθεν ἐπεὶ λάβε [νῆα] (by the stern) Il. 15.716.
Cables for mooring a ship's stern to the shore : κατὰ πρυμνήσιʼ ἔδησαν Il. 1.436. Cf. Il. 1.476 : Od. 2.418, Od. 9.137, 178 = 562= Od. 11.637= Od. 12.145= Od. 15.548, Od. 12.32, Od. 15.286, 498, 552.

The hindmost or endmost part of the . . ., the base or root of the . . . (in the case of a part of the body denoting the end next the body) : γλῶσσαν πρυμνήν Il. 5.292, ἄγνυτον ὕλην πρυμνὴν ἐκτάμνοντες (at the bases of the boles) Il. 12.149, ἐξέρυσε πρυμνοῖο βραχίονος ἔγχος Il. 13.532. Cf. Il. 13.705, Il. 16.314, 323 : Od. 17.504.
Superl. πρυμνότατος : πρυμνότατον κατὰ νῶτον (i.e. where the back and shoulder join) Od. 17.463.
At the base : λᾶας πρυμνὸς παχύς Il. 12.446.
App. in neut. as sb., the root (of the . . .) : πρυμνὸν ὕπερ θέναρος Il. 5.339.
App. in neut. as adv., by the root : ἐξ ὀδόντας ὦσε δόρυ πρυμνόν Il. 17.618.
The base or foot of a mountain : ἐν πρυμνωρείῃ Ἴδης Il. 14.307.
Lately, recently, the other day : τὸν σὺ π. κτεῖνας Il. 24.500. Cf. Il. 5.832.
In the first bloom of youth : κοῦροι πρωθῆβαι Od. 8.263. Cf. Il. 8.518.
Too early, untimely : σοὶ π. παραστήσεσθαι ἔμελλε μοῖρα Od. 24.28.
In neut. pl. πρωϊζά as adv., just before : χθιζά τε καὶ π. Il. 2.303 (see χθιζός 3).
In neut. sing. πρώϊον as adv., early this morning : νευρήν, ἣν ἐνέδησα π. Il. 15.470.
A rock, cliff, bluff Il. 8.557= Il. 16.299, Il. 12.282, Il. 17.747.
A ship's bow or prow. In apposition with νηῦς : ἴκρια νηὸς πρῴρης Od. 12.230.
Strengthened form of, but gen. hardly to be distinguished from, πρῶτος.

div.head: a
div.p: Like πρῶτος 5.a : νηὸς ἀποθρῴσκοντα πολὺ πρώτιστον Ἀχαιῶν Il. 2.702. Cf. Il. 14.442 : Od. 14.220, Od. 19.447.

div.head: b
div.p: Like πρῶτος 5.b : ἅς τοι πρωτίστῳ δίδομεν Il. 2.228. Cf. Il. 16.656.
In neut. sing. πρώτιστον as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: First, in the first place, first of all : πῦρ μοι π. γενέσθω Od. 22.491.

div.head: b
div.p: Like πρῶτος 6.c.β : Ἀρτέμιδι π. ἐπεύξατο Od. 20.60.

div.head: c
div.p: Like πρῶτος 6 (j) : οἶον ὅτε π. ἐλείπετε πατρίδα γαῖαν (when first you . . .) Od. 10.462.
In neut. pl. πρώτιστα as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Like πρῶτος 6.b : π. λέων γένετο Od. 4.456.

div.head: b
div.p: Like πρῶτος 6.c.α : π. δύσετο χαλκόν Od. 22.113. Cf. Il. 9.168.

div.head: c
div.p: Like πρῶτος 6.c.β Κάλχαντα π. προσέειπεν addressed him first Il. 1.105. Cf. Il. 2.405, Il. 18.478 : Od. 3.57, 419, Od. 13.404= Od. 15.38 (go to him first of all).

div.head: d
div.p: Like πρῶτος 6.i : ἐμὲ π. ἕταροι λίσσοντο Od. 9.224.

div.head: e
div.p: Like πρῶτος 6 (l) : ἐξ οὖ τὰ π. ἑπόμην Ἀγαμέμνονι (ever since . . .) Od. 11.168.
First-born (of the year) : ἀρνῶν (the firstlings) Il. 4.102= 120= Il. 23.864 = 873.
App., put together for the first time, newly made : δίφροι Il. 5.194, ἄμαξαν Il. 24.267.
Of a ship,app., making her first voyage Od. 8.35.

In reference to position, the most advanced in a specified or indicated direction, the first or foremost : οἱ πρῶτοί τε καὶ ὕστατοι Il. 2.281. Cf. Il. 4.480 (in the forefront of the fray), Il. 6.445, Il. 8.83, Il. 12.260 (against the face of the works), 315, 321, Il. 14.31 (next the plain), 75 (next the sea), Il. 15.634, 654 (next the plain), 656, Il. 16.394, Il. 18.579, Il. 21.90 : Od. 8.197, Od. 15.36 (the first in your course), Od. 18.379.

The foremost or front part of the . . ., the front of the . . . : ἐν πρώτῳ ῥυμῷ Il. 6.40, Il. 16.371. Cf. Il. 8.411 (just in front of the gate, at the entrance to it), Il. 15.340 (in the front of the fight), Il. 17.380, 471, Il. 19.50, Il. 20.173, 275 (the edge), 395, Il. 22.66 (before the house-door), Il. 24.272 : Od. 1.255 (just within the door), Od. 21.422 (the top of the . . .), Od. 22.250.
Absol., the winner in a contest : ἄεθλα τῷ πρώτῳ Il. 23.265.
In neut. pl. τὰ πρῶτα, the first prizeIl. 23.275, 538.

div.head: a
div.p: Those who stand or advance in or to the front of the fray, the front rank : ἐνὶ πρώτοισι μάχεσθαι Il. 9.709. Cf. Il. 4.341, Il. 5.536, Il. 8.337, Il. 11.61, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: The most promnent in some sphere of activity : μετὰ πρώτοισι πονεῖτο (with the best) Il. 9.12.

div.head: c
div.p: The first in social rank, the leading men Od. 6.60.

div.head: d
div.p: Gen., the most distinguished, the first : ἐν πρώτοισιν ὀΐω ἔμμεναι Od. 8.180. Cf. Il. 15.643.

div.head: a
div.p: Being the first to do something, first, giving a lead, showing the way, taking the initiative, doing something before another, anticipating him (cf. πρότερος 4..a) : πρῶτος κελόμην Il. 1.386, οὐδὲ σέθεν θεοὶ λελάθοντο, πρώτη δὲ Διὸς θυγάτηρ (i.e. she was the first to bethink her of you) Il. 4.128, πρώτῳ στρεφθέντι (i.e. he was the first to flee) Il. 5.40.
