Cf. Il. 4.343, 459, 457, Il. 5.38, Il. 6.5, Il. 10.532, Il. 13.809, Il. 16.812, Il. 20.161 (leaving his fellows the first), etc. : Od. 1.113, Od. 3.36, Od. 8.216, Od. 11.51, Od. 22.212, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: Sim. in oblique cases of that to which action is first directed or which is first affected in some way, first (cf. πρότερος 4..b) : τίνα πρῶτον ἐξενάριξαν; Il. 5.703, πὰρ σοὶ πρώτῳ πασάμην ἀκτήν (i.e. formed thus a tie with you first of the Greeks) Il. 21.76. Cf. Il. 5.829, Il. 10.18, Il. 13.46, Il. 17.553, etc. : Od. 2.39, Od. 4.452, Od. 6.176, Od. 7.237 (I will begin by asking you), Od. 8.462, Od. 9.14, Od. 11.235, Od. 21.304, etc.
In neut. sing. (τὸ) πρῶτον and pl. (τὰ) πρῶτα as adv.

div.head: (i)
div.p: πρῶτον ἀντιάσαντες (forming a screen to cover the retreat) Il. 15.297.

div.head: (ii)
div.p: ἱππῆας πρῶτα στῆσεν Il. 4.297, πρῶτα περὶ τέρμα βαλούσας (leading) Il. 23.462.

div.head: b
div.p: First, in the first place, first of all, to begin with (as opposed to subsequent action).

div.head: (i)
div.p: βουλὴν πρῶτον ἷζεν Il. 2.53, πρῶτον μίνωα τέκεν (this was the beginning of the race) Il. 13.450. Cf. Il. 3.315, Il. 6.179, Il. 11.628, Il. 14.170, Il. 23.237, etc. : Od. 2.190, Od. 4.411, Od. 8.120, Od. 12.39, Od. 13.117, Od. 16.173, Od. 24.240, etc.

div.head: (ii)
div.p: αὐέρυσαν πρῶτα Il. 1.459. Cf. Il. 2.73, Il. 3.330, Il. 5.458, Il. 9.32, Il. 11.244, Il. 21.343, etc. : γυρῇσίν μιν πρῶτʼ ἐπέλασσε Od. 4.500 (taken up by 502; this was the first stage of his fate), ναυσίθοον πρῶτα Ποσειδάων γείνατο (this was the beginning of the race) Od. 7.56. Cf. Od. 10.154, 519, Od. 11.158, Od. 18.192, Od. 23.131, etc.

div.head: (ii)
div.p: ἴστω Ζεὺς πρῶτα Il. 19.258 := Od. 19.303, Od. 14.158= Od. 17.155= Od. 20.230, ἦ πρῶτʼ ἐξερέοιτο (anticipate him, begin the conversation) Od. 4.119.

div.head: (i)
div.p: οὐρῆας πρῶτον ἐπῴχετο (they were the first to be attacked) Il. 1.50.

div.head: (ii)
div.p: Ὀρσίλοχον πρῶθʼ ἕλεν (he was the first man slain) Il. 8.274. Cf. Il. 11.301, Il. 16.694, Il. 23.262 : πρῶτʼ ἐς πύλον ἐλθέ (let Pylus be your first goal) Od. 1.284, δέσποιναν πρῶτα κιχήσεαι Od. 7.53, αὐτόν σε πρῶτα σάω (let your own safety be your first care) Od. 17.595. Cf. Od. 13.228, Od. 17.573.
Sim. : ἔνθεν μιν ἐδέγμην πρῶτα φανεῖσθαι Od. 12.230 (i.e. he thought he should catch sight of her from that position sooner than from elsewhere).

div.head: d
div.p: In reference to the first doing or occurrence of something, for the first time, first.

div.head: (i)
div.p: ὅθι πρῶτον λιπέτην ἅλα Il. 14.284 (they did not leave it till they reached that point), πρῶτον ὑπηνήτῃ (newly) Il. 24.348 : Od. 10.279. Cf. Il. 14.295, Il. 16.113.

div.head: (iii)
div.p: ὅθι πρῶτʼ ἐμβασίλευεν (had his first period of kingship) Il. 2.572, οὐ νῦν πρῶτʼ ἄντʼ Ἀχιλῆος στήσομαι Il. 20.89. Cf. Il. 16.811 : Od. 15.420.

div.head: (iv)
div.p: τοῖος οἷόν μιν τὰ πρῶτʼ ἐνόησα Od. 1.257. Cf. Od. 8.268.

div.head: e
div.p: With a temporal conjunction, when first, as soon as : ἐπὴν δὴ πρῶτα κατευνηθέντα ἴδησθε Od. 4.414.

div.head: f
div.p: At first, to begin with (implying a subsequent change).

div.head: (ii)
div.p: πόντῳ πρῶτα κορύσσεται [κῦμα] Il. 4.424. Cf. Il. 4.442 : Od. 11.640.

div.head: (iii)
div.p: πεζὸς τὰ πρῶτʼ ἤλυθεν Il. 17.612. Cf. Il. 23.523.–

p.gloss: Before doing something, as a preliminary, first.

div.head: (i)
div.p: ἄλλην χρὴ πρῶτον ὁδὸν τελέσαι Od. 10.490.

div.head: (ii)
div.p: πρῶτα θεῶν εἰρώμεθα βουλάς Od. 16.402. Cf. Il. 10.344.–

div.head: h
div.p: In reference to preference or choice, first, before anything else : πρῶτον τοῦ πατρὸς ἑλοίμεθα νόστιμον ἦμαρ Od. 16.149.–

div.head: i
div.p: At once, straightway : οὕνεκά σʼ οὐ τὸ πρῶτον, ἐπεὶ ἴδον, ὧδʼ ἀγάπησα Od. 23.214.–

div.head: j
div.p: Marking the time of an action or occurrence as a point of departure, a beginning, an opening of a new era.

div.head: (i)
div.p: ὅτε σε πρῶτον ἔπλεον ἁρπάξας (since first I . . .) Il. 3.443, ὅθι πρῶτον ἐξαίνυτο θυμόν (where he began by slaying him) Il. 5.848, ὅτε με πρῶτον τέκε μήτηρ (and so brought me into all this woe) Il. 6.345, ἀλκήν μοι πρῶτον ὀνείδισας (you began it by reflecting on my valour) Il. 9.34, ὅτε πρῶτον λίπον Ἑλλάδα (when first I . . .) 447 : ὁππότε κε πρῶτον πελάσῃς νῆα Θρινακίῃ (then will come the time for prudence) Od. 11.106, ὅθι πρῶτον γενόμην (where I had my first being) Od. 14.141, ὅτε μιν πρῶτον τέκε μήτηρ Od. 19.355.

div.head: (ii)
div.p: τὸ πρῶτον ἀάσθη (and so brought his fate upon him) Od. 4.509.

div.head: (iii)
div.p: ἐξ ἧς πρῶτα καὶ ἡμέας ἵκετο πένθος (first came upon us) Od. 23.224.

div.head: (iv)
div.p: μῆνιν ἄειδε . . . ἐξ οὗ τὰ πρῶτα διαστήτην (take up the tale from the point when first . . ., i.e. from the beginning of the quarrel) Il. 1.6, ᾗ τὰ πρῶτα πύλας ἐσᾶλτο (began the attack) Il. 13.679.–

div.head: k
div.p:
Denoting fixity of determination, purpose or condition,
or that something is done or brought about finally or completely, once for all.

div.head: (i)
div.p: ὥς οἱ ὑπέστην πρῶτον Il. 15.75, ὥς σφιν πρῶτον ἀπήχθετο Ἴλιος Il. 24.27, ἐπεί με πρῶτον ἔασας 557. Cf. Il. 1.319, Il. 19.136 : Od. 4.6, Od. 13.127, 133.

div.head: (ii)
div.p: ὡς τὸ πρῶτον ὑπέστην Il. 4.267, ὅππως τὸ πρῶτον τανύσῃ [ἵππους] (from the start) Il. 23.324.

div.head: (iii)
div.p: ὥς οἱ πρῶτα δόσαν γέρας Il. 1.276, ἐπεὶ δὴ πρῶτα δαμάσθη (let us accept that and make the best of it) Il. 19.9.–

div.head: l
div.p: Denoting inevitability of consequence or of the continuance of a state or condition on the doing or occurrence of something, (when) once . . ., (since) once . . ., (who) once . . .

div.head: (i)
div.p: εὖτʼ ἄν πρῶτον ὁμιλήσωσι φάλαγγες Il. 19.158. Cf. Il. 13.285 : ὅτε πρῶτον κρήτης ὄρεα νοσφισάμην (ever since . . .) Od. 19.338. Cf. Od. 3.320, Od. 10.328.

div.head: (ii)
div.p: ἐπεὶ δὴ τὸ πρῶτον ἐγείνατο παῖδα Od. 4.13, ἐπεὶ τὸ πρῶτον ἀνέκραγον (and so committed myself) Od. 14.467.

div.head: (iii)
div.p: ἐπεὶ δὴ πρῶτα τομὴν λέλοιπεν Il. 1.235. Cf. Il. 17.427 : ἐπεί κε πρῶτα λίπῃ ὀστέα θυμός Od. 11.221. Cf. Od. 3.183.

div.head: (iv)
div.p: ἐπὴν τὰ πρῶτα γένηται Il. 6.489. Cf. Il. 12.420 : Od. 8.553.
Having borne offspring for the first time. Of a cow Il. 17.5.
To sneeze : Τηλέμαχος μέγʼ ἔπταρεν Od. 17.541.
Epithet of arrows Il. 4.117, Il. 5.171, Il. 16.773, Il. 20.68.
Of words, fig., winged : ἔπεα πτερόεντα Il. 1.201, Il. 3.155, Il. 4.69, Il. 5.242, etc. : Od. 1.122, Od. 2.269, Od. 4.25, Od. 9.409, etc.
In pl., a bird's wings : σὺν πτερὰ πυκνὰ λίασθεν Od. 23.879. Cf. Il. 19.386, Il. 24.319.
App. in sing. in the same sense : ὠκεῖαι ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα Od. 7.36.
A bird's wing : ὑπὸ πτέρυγος βάλεν Il. 23.875. Cf. Il. 2.316, 462 : Od. 2.149.
To crouch, cower : κείμην πεπτηώς (cowering for concealment) Od. 14.354. Cf. Od. 14.474, Od. 22.362.
To cower, stoop, bend low, in apprehension Od. 8.190.
To strike with dismay : πτῆξε θυμὸν Ἀχαιῶν Il. 14.40.
With the name of a particular town in genit. : Ἰλίου εὖ ναιόμενον π. Il. 2.133. Cf. Il. 2.538, Il. 4.33=Il. 8.288, Il. 13.380, Il. 21.433 : Od. 1.2, Od. 3.485, Od. 15.193.
A branch of a tree or shrub : ἐξ ὕλης πτόρθον κλάσε φύλλων Od. 6.128.
The parts brought together in folding, a fold : πρόσθε οἱ πέπλοιο πτύγμʼ ἐκάλυψεν (folded the loose part of her robe about him) Il. 5.315.
Of a writing-tablet, folding, i.e. double, made of two hinged pieces which could be closed on each other and (no doubt) in some way secured : πίνακι Il. 6.169.
A fold or cleft in the furrowed side or top of a hill : κατὰ πτύχας Οὐλύμποιο Il. 11.77. Cf. Il. 20.22 (in a cleft) : Od. 19.432.
One of the layers of hide or metal forming a shield Il. 7.247, Il. 18.481, Il. 20.269, 270.
A shovel by which grain, etc., to be winnowed was thrown against the wind ( = ἀθηρηλοιγός) Il. 13.588.
Aor. pple. fem. πτύξασα Od. 1.439, Od. 6.111, 252, Od. 19.256. (προσ-)

In pass. : ἔγχεα πτύσσοντο θρασειάων ἀπὸ χειρῶν σειόμενα Il. 13.134, doubtfully explained as bent to the strain as they were brandished, or formed a serried mass (presenting the appearance of folds or layers).
[πτωκ-, πτώσσω. The cowering or timid animal.]
Joined with λαγωός : πτῶκα λαγωόν Il. 22.310.
To cower or crouch in fear or from cowardice, shrink from the fray Il. 4.371, Il. 5.634, Il. 7.129, Il. 21.26.
With acc. of the person from whom one shrinks : οὐδʼ ἄν ἔτι δὴν ἀλλήλους πτώσσοιμεν Il. 20.427.
Sim. of birds : νέφεα πτώσσουσαι (shrinking from the region of the clouds, flying low) Od. 22.304.
To cringe in humility; hence, to go about begging : πτώσσων (πτώσσειν) κατὰ δῆμον Od. 17.227, Od. 18.363.
To go about begging, beg one's bread : προτὶ ἄστυ ἀπονέεσθαι πτωχεύσων Od. 15.309. Cf. Od. 18.2, Od. 19.73.
To beg (one's bread) : ὄφρʼ ἂν ἐκεῖθι δαῖτα πτωχεύῃ Od. 17.11. Cf. Od. 17.19.
With ἀνήρ: ἄλλος τις π. ἀνήρ Od. 21.327.
Fighting with the fists, boxing : πυγμαχίης ἄεθλα (for . . .) Il. 23.653. Cf. Il. 23.665.
One who fights with the fists, a boxer Od. 8.246.
[πυγών, a measure of length derived from the forearm, a cubit.]
Of a cubit's length Od. 10.517, Od. 11.25.
A trough or box holding grain for feeding poultry Od. 19.553.
A base or support : δύω ὑπὸ [δέπαϊ] πυθμένες ἦσαν Il. 11.635 (app. the base of the hollow part ran out again after contraction to form a foot).
A leg of a tripod : χρύσεά σφʼ ὑπὸ κύκλα ἑκάστῳ πυθμένι θῆκεν (fitted a wheel under each leg) Il. 18.375.
The base of a tree, the part of the trunk next the ground Od. 13.122, 372, Od. 23.204.
To affect with decomposition, make rotten, rot : ὀστέα Il. 4.174.
In pass., to suffer decomposition, decompose, rot, decay : οὗ ὀστέα τύθεται ὄμβρῳ Od. 1.161. Cf. Il. 11.395 : Od. 12.46.

In reference to construction, closely, without breaks or interstices, so as to give good shelter or protection : πύλας π. στιβαρῶς ἀραρυίας (both closely fitted and strong) Il. 12.454, σάκεος π. ποιητοῖο Il. 18.608. Cf. Od. 1.333=Od. 8.458=Od. 16.415=Od. 18.209=Od. 21.64, Od. 1.436, Od. 22.455.
In reference to complete protection afforded by armour: Λυκίων (Τρώων) π. θωρηκτάων (wearing the goodly breastplate) Il. 12.317, Il. 15.689, 739.
In reference to things coming thick and fast : πρίν γʼ ὅτε δὴ θάλαμος π. ἐβάλλετο (was struck by many a dart) Il. 9.588.
In reference to the exercise of mental faculties, with close devotion to the subject in hand, shrewdly, astutely : νόον π. περ φρονεόντων Il. 9.554, Il. 14.217.
In reference to attention or care, with close attention, with anxious care : π. [μιν] ἔτρεφεν Il. 5.70.
Pf. pple. pass. πεπυκασμένος Il. 14.289 : Od. 22.488.
Nom. pl. neut. πεπυκασμένα Il. 2.777, Il. 23.503.

To put something round or about (something), cover, cover up, for protection, concealment or decency : νέκυν πυκάσας Il. 24.581. Cf. Il. 2.777, Il. 14.289, Il. 17.551 : ῥάκεσιν πεπυκασμένος Od. 22.488.
To protect, shield : πύκασεν κάρη [κυνέη] Il. 10.271.
To shelter or conceal (oneself) : μή πως ἐντὸς πυκάζοιεν σφέας αὐτούς Od. 12.225.
To cover the surface of by way of ornamentation : ἅρματα χρυσῷ πεπυκασμένα Od. 23.503.
In reference to something growing upon and covering a surface : πρίν σφωϊν ἰούλους πυκάσαι γένυς λάχνῃ Od. 11.320.
Of grief overwhelming (a person) : Ἕκτορʼ ἄχος πύκασε φρένας Il. 8.124= 316, Il. 17.83.
Shrewd in counsel, clever : γραίης Od. 1.438.
Close in texture, dense, thick : πυκινὸν νέφος Il. 5.751=Il. 8.395, νεφέλην Il. 16.298.

Of things placed close together or at short intervals, close-set, thick : πυκινοῖσι λίθοισιν Il. 16.212. Cf. Il. 12.57, Il. 13.133=Il. 16.217, Il. 21.245, Il. 24.453, 798 : ὀδόντες πυκνοί Od. 12.92. Cf. Od. 5.329, 433, 480, Od. 14.12, Od. 19.520, Od. 23.193.
Of things appearing together in a limited space, numerous, many : πυκναὶ σμώδιγγες ἀνέδραμον Il. 23.716.

In reference to construction, closely constructed or made, well fitted together, without breaks or interstices, affording good shelter, protection or security : πυκινὸν δόμον Il. 10.267, Il. 12.301, ἀσπίδα ῥινοῖσιν πυκινήν (made of closely fitted . . .) Il. 13.804. Cf. Il. 14.167 = 339, Il. 15.529, Il. 19.355 : Od. 6.134, Od. 7.81, 88, Od. 13.68, Od. 14.521, 529, Od. 23.229.
Sim. of something natural, thick, affording close covert : ἐν λόχμῃ πυκινῇ Od. 19.439. Cf. Od. 19.442.
Sim. of a bed, such as to afford good protection, warm, cosy : πυκινὸν λέχος Il. 9.621, 659 : Od. 7.340=Od. 23.291, Od. 23.177, 179.
Letting nothing escape from within, holding its contents, tight, well-fenced : δέρμασιν ἐν πυκινοῖσιν Od. 2.291, πυκινοὺς κευθμῶνας Od. 10.283.
Of grief, overwhelming : πυκινὸν ἄχος Il. 16.599. Cf. Od. 19.516.

Consisting of many individual persons or things, dense, close, thick : πυκιναὶ φάλαγγες Il. 4.281, Il. 5.93. Cf. Il. 7.61, Il. 11.118, Il. 13.145, 199, 680, Il. 14.349, Il. 18.320, Il. 23.122, 879 : ἐκ πυκινῆς ὕλης Od. 6.128. Cf. Od. 5.53, 471, Od. 10.150, 197, Od. 14.473.
Doing something at short intervals, thick-coming, coming thick and fast : πυκινοῖσι βελέεσσιν Il. 11.576. Cf. Od. 14.36.
Falling quickly one after the other, falling fast or in a shower : ὣς πυκνὰ καρήατα δάμνατο λαῶν Il. 11.309. Cf. Il. 11.454 : τιναξάσθην πτερὰ πυκνά Od. 2.151. Cf. Od. 4.153.
Of the mind, or mental faculties, shrewd, astute, sagacious, wise : Διὸς πυκινὸν νόον Il. 15.461. Cf. Il. 14.294 (though . . .).

Displaying shrewdness, astuteness, sagacity, or wisdom, shrewd, astute, sagacious, wise, shrewdly or cunningly devised or contrived : τυκινὴν βουλήν Il. 2.55=Il. 10.302, Il. 9.76, πυκινὸν λόχον Il. 4.392, Il. 24.779 : Od. 11.525. Cf. Il. 3.202, 208, Il. 6.187, Il. 7.375, Il. 11.788, Il. 18.216, Il. 24.75, 282 = 674, 744 : Od. 3.23, Od. 19.353.
Absol. in neut. pl. πυκινά, shrewdness, astuteness: πυκινὰ φρονέοντι Od. 9.445.
In neut. sing. πυκινόν as adv., in reference to grief which overwhelms one, heavily, sorely : πυκινόν περ ἀχεύων Od. 11.88.
In neut. pl. πυκινά, πυκνά, as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: With short intervals between : πήρην, πυκνὰ ῥωγαλένη (full of rents) Od. 13.438=Od. 17.198=Od. 18.109.

div.head: b
div.p: At short intervals, often, much : ὣς πυκίνʼ ἀναστενάχιζεν Il. 10.9. Cf. Il. 18.318, Il. 21.417.

In reference to construction, closely, without breaks or interstices, so as to give good shelter or protection : θύρας π. ἀραρυίας Il. 9.475. Cf. Il. 21.535 : Od. 2.344, Od. 21.236 = 382, Od. 22.155, 258 = 275, Od. 23.194.
In reference to grief which overwhelms one, heavily, sorely : π. ἀκαχήμενον Il. 19.312. Cf. Od. 19.95, Od. 20.84, Od. 23.360.
Shrewdly, wisely : π. τοι ὑποθησόμεθα (for your good) Il. 21.293. Cf. Od. 1.279.
Epithet of Hades Il. 8.367, Il. 13.415 : Od. 11.277.
He that watches the gate, a gate-keeper Il. 21.530, Il. 24.681.

div.head: a
div.p: A gate of a city or other place Il. 2.809, Il. 4.34, Il. 5.466, Il. 6.80, Il. 9.573, Il. 12.175, etc.

div.head: b
div.p: In pl. of a single gate (as consisting of two wings) : πυλέων ἐξέσσυτο Il. 7.1. Cf. Il. 3.145, Il. 5.646, 749, Il. 8.15, Il. 12.120, Il. 13.124, Il. 22.99, Il. 24.709, etc. : Od. 14.156.
Of the gates of dreams : ἐν ὀνειρείῃσι πύλῃσιν Od. 4.809. Cf. Od. 19.562.
Of the gates of the sun Od. 24.12.
Born at Pylus, sprung from Pylus : βασιλῆος Il. 2.54, ἵπποι Il. 23.303.
Of position, the last, the hindmost : φάλαγγας Il. 4.254.
Absol. in pl., those in the rear, the rear rank : ἐν πυμάτοισι κελεύων Il. 11.65.
That is at the extremity of something : ἄντυξ ἣ πυμάτη θέεν ἀσπίδος (at its edge) Il. 6.118.

The extreme part of the . . ., the extremity of the . . .: ἐξ ἐπιδιφριάδος πυμάτης (its edge) Il. 10.475, ῥινὸς ὕπερ πυμάτης (the top of it) Il. 13.616, ἄντυγα πὰρ πυμάτην σάκεος (the edge of the rim) Il. 18.608.
The last in sequence or time : δρόμον Il. 23.373, 768. Cf. Od. 2.20.
In oblique cases of that to which action is last directed or which is last affected in some way, last : οὖτιν πύματον ἔδομαι Od. 9.369. Cf. Il. 11.759, Il. 22.66 : Od. 7.138.

div.head: a
div.p: In neut. sing. πύματον as adv., for the last time.
With ὕστατον in the same sense : π. πε καὶ ὕστατον Il. 22.203 : Od. 20.116.

div.head: b
div.p: With ὕστατα in the same sense : ὕστατα καὶ π. Od. 4.685, Od. 20.13.
With the fist : πὺξ ἀγαθόν (the great boxer) Il. 3.237, οὐ πύξ γε μαχήσεαι (will never box again) Il. 23.621. Cf. Il. 23.634 (at boxing), 660 (to box) : Od. 8.103, 130, 206, Od. 11.300.

Fire : ὄσσε οἱ πυρὶ λαμπετόωντι ἐΐκτην Il. 1.104. Cf. Il. 2.340 (to the flames with . . .), 415 (genit. of material, with fire), Il. 5.4, 215 (commit to the flames), Il. 6.182, Il. 12.177, Il. 14.396, etc. : Od. 4.418, Od. 5.490, Od. 9.390, Od. 12.68, Od. 16.290, Od. 17.23, Od. 19.39, etc.
Funeral-fire, the flames of the pyre : ὄφρα πυρός με λελάχωσιν Il. 7.79. Cf. Il. 15.350, Il. 23.76, etc. : Od. 24.65.

The result of the application of fire to prepared combustible material, fire; when a particular mass of fire is referred to, a fire : ἐν πυρὸς αὐγῇ Il. 9.206, ἐν νηυσὶ πῦρ βαλέειν Il. 13.629. Cf. Il. 8.521, 563, Il. 9.211, Il. 15.420, Il. 16.122, Il. 18.344, Il. 19.376, etc. : Od. 3.341, Od. 5.59, Od. 6.305, Od. 8.426, 501, Od. 14.518, Od. 17.572, Od. 22.481, etc.
Of watch-fires : ἔνθα πῦρ κήαντο Il. 9.88 (i.e. each band lighted its fire).
A smith's tongs : γέντο πυράγρην Il. 18.477. Cf. Od. 3.434.
To bring the influence of fire to bear upon, harden by fire : [ῥόπαλον] Od. 9.328.
In line : π. σφέας αὐτοὺς ἀρτύναντες Il. 12.43 (in line of battle). Cf. Il. 13.152, Il. 15.618.

A fortified wall securing a city or strong place; in pl., walls, ramparts : ἧντʼ ἐπὶ πύργῳ Il. 3.153, δείμομεν πύργους Il. 7.338. Cf. Il. 6.373, Il. 7.437 (hardly to be distinguished from τεῖχος), Il. 8.165, Il. 9.574, Il. 12.36, 332 (the part of the wall under his charge), Il. 15.737, Il. 16.700, Il. 18.274, Il. 22.97 (a projecting angle of the wall), Il. 24.443, etc. : Od. 6.262.
Fig. of a person : τοῖός σφιν π. ἀπώλεο (so mighty a wall of defence was lost in thee) Od. 11.556.
A tower erected for defence on such a wall : φέρων σάκος ἠΰτε πύργον Il. 7.219=Il. 11.485=Il. 17.128. Cf. Il. 4.462.
A body of troops formed in line : δέκα πύργοι Ἀχαιῶν Il. 4.347, πάπτηνεν ἀνὰ πύργον Ἀχαιῶν (the line of defenders) Il. 12.333. Cf. Il. 4.334.
To surround with a wall, fortify : Θήβης ἕδος πύργωσαν Od. 11.264.
The fire of a sacrifice : πυρὴν ἐμπλησέμεν ἐσθλῶν Od. 10.523=Od. 11.31.
Charred (at the end to prevent rotting) Il. 13.564.
[πῦρ + καίω. A place where fire is kindled.]
A funeral-pyre : νεκροὺς πυρκαϊῆς ἐπενήνεον Il. 7.428= 431. Cf. Il. 23.158, 225, 228, 231, 237, 250=Il. 24.791.
A wheaten cake or loaf Od. 15.312, Od. 17.12, 362.
In pl. : πυροί τε ζειαί τε Od. 4.604. Cf. Il. 11.69 : Od. 9.110, Od. 19.112.
Wheat-bearing : ἀρούρης Il. 12.314. Cf. Il. 14.123, Il. 21.602.
To attend to, keep up, a fire.
Absol. in pres. pple. pl. : πυρπολέοντας ἐλεύσσομεν (could see men tending their fire) Od. 10.30.
A beacon-fire or signal-fire : πυρσοὶ φλεγέθουσιν Il. 18.211.
With negative, in no wise, not at all : μὴ δή πω χάζεσθε Il. 15.426. Cf. Il. 4.184, 234, Il. 17.422, Il. 22.279 : Od. 23.59.

With negative, not yet, never yet : ἐσθλὸν δʼ οὔτε τί πω εἶπας ἔπος οὔτʼ ἐτέλεσσας Il. 1.108. Cf. Il. 1.542, Il. 2.419, Il. 7.433, Il. 11.497, Il. 16.76, Il. 22.9, Il. 23.73, etc. : οὐδέ πω ὥρη εὕδειν Od. 11.373. Cf. Od. 3.23, Od. 11.161, Od. 23.315, etc.
In reference to the future : μὴ δή πω λυώμεθʼ ἵππους Il. 23.7. Cf. Il. 18.134, Il. 24.553 : Od. 22.431.
Nom. pl. masc. pres. pple. πωλεύμενοι Od. 2.55, Od. 17.534.
3 sing. pa. iterative πωλέσκετο Il. 1.490, Il. 5.788 : Od. 11.240. (ἐπι-)

To go or come habitually or regularly, use or be wont to go or come : εἰς ἀγορής Il. 1.490. Cf. Il. 5.350, 788 : δεῦρο (frequents this spot) Od. 4.384, οὔ τι πάρος γε πωλέαι (it has not been your wont to come hither) 811, ἐπʼ Ἐνιπῆος ῥέεθρα (haunted them) Od. 11.240. Cf. Od. 2.55=Od. 17.534, Od. 9.189, Od. 22.352.
A means of protecting or securing the contents of something : ἴδε π. (the lid) Od. 8.443. Cf. Il. 4.116 (the top), Il. 16.221 (the lid) : Od. 2.353 (with stoppers), Od. 8.447, Od. 9.314.

How? in what way or manner? by what means? πῶς τοι δώσουσι γέρας; Il. 1.123, πῶς κε κῆρας ὑπεξέφυγεν; Il. 22.202. Cf. Il. 7.36, Il. 10.61 (in what sense?), 243, Il. 11.838, Il. 17.327, Il. 18.188, Il. 19.81, Il. 24.519: Od. 1.171, Od. 3.22, Od. 8.352, Od. 10.64, Od. 15.195, Od. 18.31, Od. 20.129, etc.

How? why? for what cause, inducement or reason? on what ground or pretext? πῶς τίς τοι πείθηται; Il. 1.150, πῶς ἐθέλεις ἅλιον θεῖναι πόνον; Il. 4.26. Cf. Il. 4.351, Il. 9.437 (how could I bring myself to stay?), Il. 17.149 (how can we look to you to . . .?), Il. 18.364, Il. 21.481, Il. 24.203 (what can induce you to . . .?) : Od. 1.65, Od. 9.351 (what will bring anyone here?), Od. 10.337, Od. 22.231.
How? in what state or condition? πῶς αἱ φυλακαί; Il. 10.408. Cf. Il. 14.333 (how would it be?) : Od. 18.223.–πῶς γὰρ νῦν; how then? Il. 10.424.
How? of what nature or kind? πῶς ὔμμιν ἀνὴρ ὅδε φαίνεται εἶναι; Od. 11.336.
Somehow, haply : αἴ κέν πως θωρήξομεν υἶας Ἀχαιῶν Il. 2.72. Cf. Il. 1.66, 408, Il. 13.807, Il. 22.346, etc. : Od. 9.317, Od. 10.147, Od. 12.113, Od. 22.91, etc.
In negative or conditional contexts, in any way, haply : εἴ πως τόδε πᾶσι φίλον γένοιτο Il. 4.17. Cf. Il. 3.436, Il. 5.250, Il. 16.60, etc. : Od. 4.388, Od. 12.224, 288, Od. 16.148, etc.
Qualifying an expression, I ween, it would seem : ἀεί πώς μοι ἐπιπλήσσεις Il. 12.211. Cf. Il. 14.104.
To fly. Of missiles : λίθοι πωτῶντο θαμειαί Il. 12.287.
A flock (of sheep) : πώεα οἰῶν Il. 11.678. Cf. Il. 3.198, Il. 11.696, Il. 15.323, Il. 18.528 : νομεὺς ὣς πώεσι μήλων Od. 4.413. Cf. Od. 11.402, Od. 12.129, 299, Od. 14.100, Od. 24.112.

div.head: b
div.p: A magic wand. Of that of Hermes Il. 24.343. := Od. 5.47, Od. 24.2.
Such a wand used by Athene in effecting transformations of Odysseus Od. 13.429, Od. 16.172, 456.
App. to be taken as= ῥαφή: βοείας ῥάψε χρυσείῃς ῥάβδοισιν (i.e. with wire) Il. 12.297.
Pliant: ἱμάσθλην χερσὶν ἔχε ῥαδινήν Il. 23.583.
To sprinkle, besprinkle : ῥαίνοντο κονίῃ Il. 11.282, αἵματʼ ἐρράδατο Il. 12.431. Cf. Od. 20.150 (i.e. with water), 354.
A smith's hammer : γέντο ῥαιστῆρα κρατερήν Il. 18.477.
To smite, break in pieces, shiver : φάσγανον ἐρραίσθη Il. 16.339.
To disintegrate, scatter : ἐγκέφαλός κε ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ Od. 9.459.
To smite, afflict, shipwreck (a person) Od. 5.221, Od. 6.326.
To smite, wreck (a ship) Od. 13.151, 177, Od. 23.235.
An old or worn piece of cloth Od. 6.178.
An old or tattered garment Od. 13.434, Od. 14.342, 349.
In pl., tattered garments, rags : ζώσατο ῥάκεσιν Od. 18.67. Cf. Od. 14.512, Od. 18.74, Od. 19.507, Od. 21.221, Od. 22.1, 488.
Mended with patches, patched : χιτῶνα Od. 24.228, κνημῖδας 229.
To sew or stitch together, stitch : βοείας Il. 12.296.
To devise, contrive, plan, plot : κακά Il. 18.367 : Od. 3.118, Od. 16.423. Cf. Od. 16.379, 422.
A stitch or seam : ῥαφαὶ ἐλέλυντο ἱμάντων Od. 22.186.
The backbone and immediately adjoining flesh, the chine : συὸς ῥάχιν Il. 9.208.
(ῥέα in Iliad only. A monosyllable in Il. 12.381, Il. 13.144, Il. 17.461, Il. 20.101, 263).

Easily, with ease, without effort or difficulty, readily : ῥέα πάλλεν Il. 5.304, ὅπως ἵπποι ῥεῖα διέλθοιεν (without giving the driver trouble, without shying) Il. 10.492. Cf. Il. 2.475, Il. 3.381, Il. 8.179, Il. 11.802, Il. 12.381, Il. 13.90 (with effortless stride), 144 (without check), Il. 16.745 (nimbly), Il. 17.461, Il. 18.600 (smoothly), Il. 20.263 (without check, straight), Il. 24.567, etc. : Od. 2.322 (without more ado), Od. 3.231, Od. 4.207, Od. 6.108, 300, Od. 10.573, Od. 17.265, 273 (you saw it at once), 305, Od. 23.188.
At ease, at one's ease : θεοὶ ῥεῖα ζώοντες Il. 6.138 : Od. 4.805, Od. 5.122.
Without thinking of the consequences, lightly, readily : ἄλλον κεν θεῶν ῥεῖα κατευνήσαιμι Il. 14.245.
Sim. : τούτοισι ταῦτα μέλει ῥεῖα (they enjoy themselves with no thought for the morrow) Od. 1.160.
A stream : ποταμοὶ καὶ ῥέεθρα Od. 11.157.
In pl., the streams or waters (of a river) : καϋστρίου ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα Il. 2.461. Cf. Il. 7.135, Il. 8.369, Il. 14.245, Il. 17.749, Il. 21.9, Il. 23.205, etc. : Od. 3.292, Od. 6.317, Od. 11.240.
In pl., the flow or course of a river : ἄψορρον κῦμα κατέσσυτο ῥέεθρα (i.e. in the proper channel) Il. 21.382.
Aor. pple. neut. pass. ῥεχθέν, -έντος Il. 9.250, Il. 17.32, Il. 20.198.
To do, act : ὧδε ῥέξαι Il. 2.802. Cf. Il. 7.353, Il. 9.453 (did as she bade me), Il. 22.259, Il. 24.661 : Od. 9.352.
With acc. of person affected by the action : κακῶς οἵ πέρ μιν ἔρεζον Od. 23.56.

To do, perform, accomplish : τόδε μέγʼ ἄριστον Il. 2.274, ῥεχθέντος κακοῦ Il. 9.250. Cf. Il. 5.374, Il. 10.51, Il. 11.502, Il. 14.62, Il. 15.586, Il. 19.90, Il. 22.305, Il. 23.494, etc. : Od. 1.47, Od. 2.232, Od. 4.205, Od. 8.148 (wins), Od. 11.272, Od. 16.381, Od. 20.314, Od. 22.46, Od. 23.222, etc.
Absol. in aor. pple. neut. pass. : ῥεχθὲν δέ τε νήπιος ἔγνω (i.e. is wise after the event) Il. 17.32=Il. 20.198.

With double acc. of what is done and of the person affected : ξεινοδόκον κακὰ ῥέξαι Il. 3.354. Cf. Il. 2.195, Il. 4.32, Il. 5.373=Il. 21.509, Il. 9.647, Il. 10.49, Il. 24.370 : Od. 2.72, 73, Od. 4.690, Od. 18.15, Od. 22.209, 314.
Without expressed object, to do or offer sacrifice : ἄλλος ἄλλῳ ἔρεζε θεῶν Il. 2.400. Cf. Il. 8.250, Il. 9.536 : Od. 12.344, Od. 14.251.
Explained as, the limbs : ψυχὴ ἐκ ῥεθέων πταμένη Il. 16.856=Il. 22.362. Cf. Il. 22.68.
To incline or sink downwards : ῥέπεν αἴσιμον ἦμαρ Ἀχαιῶν Il. 8.72. Cf. Il. 22.212.
nom. pl. neut. pf. pple. pass. ῥυπάω.
Of a river or stream, to flow, run : ποταμοὶ κατʼ ὄρεσφι ῥέοντες Il. 4.452. Cf. Il. 5.88, 773, Il. 6.172, Il. 16.389, 391, Il. 17.751, Il. 18.403, Il. 21.256, 271 : Od. 10.513, Od. 19.207.
For εὐρὺ ῥέω, εὐρὺ ῥέων see εὐρύς 2.a.
Of streaming blood : ἀμφὶ νέκυν ἔρρεεν αἷμα Il. 23.34.
Of streaming sweat : κατὰ νότιος ῥέεν ἱδρώς (streamed down) Il. 11.811, Il. 23.715. Cf. Il. 16.110, Il. 23.688 : Od. 11.600.
Of the rain of thick-coming missiles : τῶν ἐκ χειρῶν βέλεα ῥέον Il. 12.159.
Of bristles dropping off all together : τῶν ἐκ μελέων τρίχες ἔρρεον Od. 10.393.
With dat. of that which flows : ῥέεν αἵματι γαῖα (ran with blood) Il. 4.451=Il. 8.65, Il. 15.715, Il. 20.494.

To flow, run, flow or run forth, gush forth : ὅθεν ῥέεν ὕδωρ Il. 2.307. Cf. Il. 3.300, Il. 4.140, Il. 5.339, 340 (i.e. when a god is wounded), Il. 13.539, 655=Il. 21.119, Il. 17.86, 438 : Od. 9.140, 290, Od. 11.36, Od. 17.209, Od. 19.204.
So in aor. pass. : ἐπεὶ ἐκ μέλαν αἷμα ῥύη Od. 3.455.
Of speech : ἀπὸ γλώσσης ῥέεν αὐδή Il. 1.249.
With dat. of that which flows : ἡ μὲν [πηγὴ] ὕδατι λιαρῷ ῥέει (runs with . . .) Il. 22.149. Cf. Od. 5.70.

The broken water or surf beside the beach : ἐπὶ ῥηγμῖνι θαλάσσης (at the edge of the breakers) Il. 1.437, Il. 8.501. Cf. Il. 2.773, Il. 16.67 : Od. 4.430 = 575=Od. 9.169 = 559=Od. 10.186, Od. 4.449, Od. 9.150 = 547=Od. 12.6, Od. 15.499.
The surf or broken surface (of the sea) : ἄκρον ἐπὶ ῥηγμῖνος ἁλός Il. 20.229 (see ἄκρος 3). Cf. Od. 12.214.
Mid. 3 pl. aor. ἐρρήξαντο Il. 12.291. ῥήξαντο Il. 11.90.
To smash, crush : ὀστέον Il. 12.185, Il. 16.310, Il. 20.399.
In pass., of the sea, to break, become surf : περί σφισι κῦμα ῥήγνυτο Il. 18.67. Cf. Il. 4.425.
To rend, rive, penetrate, perforate : θώρηκας Il. 2.544. Cf. Il. 3.348=Il. 7.259=Il. 17.44, Il. 13.439, 507=Il. 17.314, Il. 20.268=Il. 21.165.

To break asunder or in two, sever, cause to part, snap or give way : ἱμάντα Il. 3.375, ἔχματα πέτρης Il. 13.139. Cf. Il. 5.307, Il. 8.328, Il. 12.459, Il. 15.464, Il. 16.587 : ἱτοῦ προτόνους Od. 12.409.
With ἀπό, to break off, cause to part from a fastening : ῥῆξεν ἀπὸ λόφον Il. 15.537.
To break (opposed ranks) : φάλαγγα Il. 6.6. Cf. Il. 7.141, Il. 11.538, Il. 15.615, 617.
In mid. : ῥηξάμενος Δαναῶν στίχας Il. 13.680. Cf. Il. 11.90, Il. 13.718, Il. 15.409.
To lay open by breaking, break or make a way through (a barrier) : θαλάμοιο θύρας Il. 9.476. Cf. Il. 12.198, 262, 341, Il. 13.124, Il. 17.751.
In mid. : τεῖχος ῥηξάμενοι Il. 12.90. Cf. Il. 12.224, 257, 291, 308, 418, 440.
Absol., to break a way through a barrier.
In mid. : ἀργαλέον μοί ἐστι μούνῳ ῥηξαμένῳ θέσθαι κέλευθον Il. 12.411.
In mid. : ἐν αὐτοῖς ἔριδα ῥήγνυντο Il. 20.55.

App., a cloth, prob. of wool, laid on the rough bedding for the comfort of the sleeper (cf. λίνον 3) : κώεά τε ῥῆγός τε λίνοιό τε λεπτὸν ἄωτον Il. 9.661. Cf. Il. 24.644 :=Od. 4.297=Od. 7.336, Od. 3.349, 351, Od. 6.38, Od. 11.189, Od. 13.73 (here app. simply laid on the deck of the ship), 118, Od. 19.318, 337, Od. 20.141, Od. 23.180.
App., a similar cloth thrown over the back of a chair : ἔβαλλε θρόνοις ἔνι ῥήγεα καθύπερθʼ, ὑπένερθε δὲ λῖθʼ ὑπέβαλλεν Od. 10.352.
dat. sing. neut. aor. pple. pass. εἴρω2.
With complementary infin. : τάφρος οὐχ ὑπερθορέειν ῥηϊδίη (easy to . . .) Il. 12.54. Cf. Il. 20.265.

So in impers. use :
ῥηΐδιόν [ἐστι] θεοῖσι κυδῆναι βροτόν Od. 16.211.
Easy to understand or follow : ἔπος Od. 11.146.

Easily, with ease, without effort or difficulty : ἐνίκα ῥ. Il. 4.390. Cf. Il. 9.184, Il. 11.114, Il. 12.448, Il. 16.690 (i.e. by his divine power), Il. 17.283, Il. 22.140 (with smooth flight), etc. : ῥ. ἀφελὼν θυρεόν Od. 9.313. Cf. Od. 8.376, Od. 14.196 (could go on relating . . .), Od. 16.198, Od. 21.92, 407, etc.
Without thinking of the consequences, lightly : τοὺς σάωσας ῥ., ἐπεὶ οὔ τι τίσιν γʼ ἔδεισας ὀπίσσω Il. 22.19.
The easiest or happiest, the most free from care : βιοτή Od. 4.565.
In neut. pl. ῥηΐτατα as adv., with the greatest ease, with the least effort : ὅς κε ῥʼ ἐντανύσῃ βιόν Od. 19.577= Od. 21.75.
With complementary infin. : ῥηΐτεροι πολεμίζειν (to fight with) Il. 18.258. Cf. Il. 24.243.
That may be rent or torn : ἀνδρί, ὃς χαλκῷ ῥηκτὸς [εἴη] Il. 13.323.
Might to break the ranks of the foe Od. 14.217.
That breaks the ranks of the foe (cf. ῥήγνυμι 5). Epithet of Achilles Il. 7.228, Il. 13.324, Il. 16.146, 575 : Od. 4.5.
Discourse, talk : ἀκούεις μύθων ἡμετέρων καὶ ῥήσιος Od. 21.291.
To beat time : ῥήσσοντες ἁμαρτῇ ἕποντο Il. 18.571.
Stated, specified, agreed upon : μισθῷ ἔπι ῥητῷ Il. 21.445.
A (verbal) agreement, a bargain or covenant Od. 14.393.
Horrible, a thing to shudder at : Ἑλένης Il. 19.325.

To be physically affected by fear as if by cold, shudder with fear, dread or apprehension : ῥίγησεν Ἀγαμέμνων Il. 4.148. Cf. Il. 4.150, 279, Il. 5.596= Il. 11.345, Il. 11.254, Il. 12.208, 331, Il. 15.34, 436, 466, Il. 16.119.
Sim. : αἰεί μοι θυμὸς ἐρρίγει μὴ . . . (was in constant terror lest . . .) Od. 23.216.
To shudder at, dread, shrink from : πόλεμον Il. 5.351, οὐκ ἔρριγα μάχην (it is not my wont to shrink from the fight) Il. 17.175.
With infin. : ὄφρα τις ἐρρίγῃσι ξεινοδόκον κακὰ ῥέξαι Il. 3.353, τούτῳ ἔρριγʼ ἀντιβολῆσαι (does not care to meet him) Il. 7.114.
To be physically affected by a sudden summons or announcement, be fluttered or thrown into agitation : ὣς φάτο, ῥίγησεν δʼ ὁ γέρων Il. 3.259. Cf. Od. 5.116, 171.
Colder : ποτὶ ἕσπερα ῥʼ ἔσται Od. 17.191.
More to be feared or dreaded, worse : τό οἱ (τοι) καὶ ῥίγιον ἔσται (it will be the worse for him (you)) Il. 1.325, 563. Cf. Il. 11.405: Od. 20.220.
The most to be feared or dreaded.
Absol. in neut. pl. : ῥίγιστα τετληότες εἰμέν (the worst extremities) Il. 5.873.
Cold : εἴ με μεθήῃ ῥῖγος Od. 5.472.
To be cold, feel cold : οὐκ ἐφάμην ῥιγωσέμεν Od. 14.481.
The root of a tree or plant : δρύες ῥίζῃσιν μεγάλῃσιν ἀραρυῖαι Il. 12.134. Cf. Il. 9.542, Il. 21.243 : Od. 10.304, Od. 12.435, Od. 23.196.
The prepared root of a plant used medicinally : ἐπὶ δὲ ῥίζαν βάλε πικρήν Il. 11.846.
In pl., the roots of the eye, the attachments of the eye within the orbit : σφαραγεῦντο [γλήνης] πυρὶ ῥίζαι Od. 9.390.
To furnish with roots : ἔνθα οἱ ἀλωὴ ἐρρίζωται (there grows his vineyard with its trees) Od. 7.122.
Fig. : νῆʼ ἐρρίζωσεν ἔνερθεν (fixed immovably) Od. 13.163.
Speedily, quickly, with haste : δεῖπνον ἕλοντο Il. 8.54. Cf. Il. 24.799.
In short space, soon : λέπτʼ ἐγένοντο Il. 20.497.
-οῦ, ἡ, also ῥινόν, τό Il. 10.155 : Od. 5.281 (ϝρινός, ϝρινόν).
The stripped-off skin of a beast, a hide : ἕρπον ῥινοί Od. 12.395. Cf. Il. 7.474.
A prepared hide. Used for sleeping or sitting upon : ὑπὸ δʼ ἔστρωτο ῥινὸν βοός Il. 10.155 : ἥμενοι ἐν ῥινοῖσι βοῶν Od. 1.108.
For wearing : ἕσσατο ῥινὸν λύκοιο Il. 10.334.
A layer of leather forming part of a shield Il. 7.248, Il. 13.406, 804.
Leather : κυνέην ῥινοῦ Il. 10.262, δοῦπος . . .ῥινοῦ τε βοῶν τε (of leather and the shields thereof, i.e. of the leather shields) Il. 16.636. Cf. Il. 20.276 : Od. 12.423.
A shield : σύν ῥʼ ἔβαλον ῥινούς Il. 4.447= Il. 8.61, ῥινοῖσι βοῶν φράξαντες ἐπάλξεις (of ox-leather) Il. 12.263. Cf. Il. 5.308 : Od. 5.281.
The skin of a man : περὶ ῥινοὶ μινύθουσιν (their skins) Od. 12.46. Cf. Od. 14.134, Od. 22.278.
So in pl. : ἔνθα κʼ ἀπὸ ῥινοὺς δρύφθη (would have had his skin stripped off) Od. 5.426. Cf. Od. 5.435.
A peak or pinnacle of a mountain Il. 8.25, Il. 14.154, 225= Il. 19.114 : Od. 9.191.
A rock or reef projecting into the sea Od. 3.295.
The rush or rapid or impetuous flight of a missile : λᾶος ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς Il. 12.462 : Od. 8.192.
The range or carry of a missile : ὅσση αἰγανέης ῥ. τέτυκται Il. 16.589.
The rush of wind Il. 15.171, Il. 19.358.
The rush or furious onset of a warrior : οἵ κʼ ὄλωνται ἀνδρὸς ἑνὸς ῥιπῇ Il. 8.355.
To throw to and fro, toss : ῥιπτάζων κατὰ δῶμα θεούς Il. 14.257.
Absol., to make one's throw : τὸ τρίτον ἔρριψεν αἴας Il. 23.842.
Of the operation of wind: τὰς ἄνεμος ῥίπτασκε ποτὶ νέφεα Od. 11.592.
To jerk or pull in a specified direction : [ἰχθὺν] θύραζε Od. 12.254.
ῥινός, ἡ (an initial consonant app. lost).
The nose : ἀμβροσίνη ὑπὸ ῥῖνα θῆκεν Od. 4.445. Cf. Il. 5.291, Il. 13.616 : Od. 18.86.
So in pl., the nose (as containing the two nostrils) : ἀπʼ οὔατα ῥῖνάς τʼ ἀμήσαντες Od. 21.301. Cf. Il. 14.467, Il. 16.503, Il. 23.395 : Od. 22.475.
With special reference to the nostrils : αἷμʼ ἀνὰ στόμα καὶ κατὰ ῥῖνας πρῆσεν Il. 16.349. Cf. Il. 19.39, Il. 23.777 : Od. 5.456, Od. 22.18, Od. 24.318.
In pl., wicker-work : φράξε σχεδίην ῥίπεσσι οἰσυΐνῃσιν Od. 5.256.
Of a stream of water poured over something : ἔνιψʼ ὕδατος ῥοῇσιν Il. 16.229.
Of waves, rushing, breaking in uproar : κῦμα Od. 5.412.
Whistling: πολλῇ ῥοίζῳ πρὸς ὄρος τρέπε μῆλα Od. 9.315.
The whizzing of missiles in flight : ὀϊστῶν ῥοῖζον Il. 16.361.
A pomegranate-tree : ὄγχναι καὶ ῥοιαὶ καὶ μηλέαι Od. 7.115= Od. 11.589.
The stream or waters (of a river) : ἱκόμεσθα ῥόον Ἀλφειοῖο Il. 11.726. Cf. Il. 12.25, Il. 16.151, Il. 18.402, Il. 21.16, 147, 219, 241, 263, 306, 369 : Od. 5.449, Od. 6.85, Od. 11.21, Od. 12.1.

The moving waters of a river, its current : βέβρυχεν μέγα κῦμα ποτὶ ῥόον (as it meets the current) Il. 17.264, πρὸς ῥόον ἀΐσσοντος (against the current) Il. 21.303 : νῆα κατʼ Ὠκεανὸν ποταμὸν φέρε κῦμα ῥόοιο (the moving stream of its current) Od. 11.639. Cf. Od. 5.451.
The flow or wash of the sea : βόμβησαν ἐρετμὰ κατὰ ῥόον Od. 12.204. Cf. Od. 5.327.
A current or set of the sea : κῦμά με ῥόος τʼ ἀπέωσεν Od. 9.80. Cf. Od. 14.254.

The flow or course of a river : ποταμοὺς ἔτρεψε νέεσθαι κὰρ ῥόον (i.e. in their proper channels) Il. 12.33, πᾶσι [ποταμοῖσι] ῥόον πεδίονδε τίθησιν (turns their course to the . . .) Il. 17.750 : ἄψ ἔφερε [κρήδεμνον] κῦμα κατὰ ῥόον (down its stream) Od. 5.461.
Sim. in reference to water used in irrigation : ὡς ὅτʼ ἀνὴρ ὀχετηγὸς ὕδατι ῥόον ἡγεμονεύῃ (guides its flow) Il. 21.258.
A club or cudgel. Used for beating an ass Il. 11.559, 561.
A stick or staff for support in walking : δός μοι, εἴ ποθί τοι ῥ. τετμημένον ἐστί, σκηρίπτεσθαι Od. 17.195.
Such a stick used as a weapon of offence : ἠὲ μεταΐξας ῥοπαλῳ ἐκ θυμὸν ἔλοιτο Od. 17.236.
Of the stick carried by the Cyclops Od. 9.319.
Of the sea, to roar, dash in uproar : ῥόχθει μέγα κῦμα Od. 5.402. Cf. Od. 12.60.
In a stream : ῥ. ἀφειοῖο (on whom riches flowed) Od. 15.426.
Acc. sing. masc. pres. pple. ῥυπόωντα Od. 24.227.
Acc. pl. neut. ῥυπόωντα Od. 6.87, Od. 13.435.
Nom. pl. neut. pf. pple. pass. ῥερυπωμένα Od. 6.59.
To be dirty or squalid : ῥυπόωντα ἕστο χιτῶνα Od. 24.227. Cf. Od. 6.87, Od. 13.435.
So in pf. pass. : εἵματα, τά μοι ῥερυπωμένα κεῖται Od. 6.59.
Cattle, etc., driven off by way of reprisal : ῥύσιʼ ἐλαυνόμενος Il. 11.674.
That guards the city : Ἀθηναίη ῥυσίπτολι Il. 6.305 (u. l. ἐρῦσίπτολι).
Drawn, wrinkled Il. 9.503 (of the λιταί (see λιτή) as figuring an offender with his face wrinkled by the mental struggle caused by his reluctance to ask pardon).
To haul or pull about, maltreat : δμῳάς Od. 16.109= Od. 20.319.
A hauling or pulling about, maltreatment Od. 18.224.
A (skilful) drawer (of the bow or of arrows) : ῥυτῆρα βιοῦ καὶ ὀϊστῶν Od. 21.173. Cf. Od. 18.262.
In pl., the reins of a chariot : [ἵπποι] ἐν ῥυτῆρσι τάνυσθεν (pulled in the governance of, pulled at, the reins) Il. 16.475.
A keeper or guard : σταθμῶν ῥυτῆρα Od. 17.187, 223.
Prob, drawn out of the earth, dug, quarried : λάεσσιν Od. 6.267, Od. 14.10.

Full of rents or
holes, rent, torn : Ἑκτόρεον χιτῶνα δαΐξαι ῥωγαλέον (so as to pierce it with many a hole) Il. 2.417. Cf. Od. 13.435, 438= Od. 17.198= Od. 18.109, Od. 14.343.
In pl., app., passages forming continuations or branches of the λαύρη: ἀνὰ ῥῶγας μεγάροιο Od. 22.143.
3 pl. aor. ἐρρώσαντο Il. 24.616 : Od. 23.3, Od. 24.69. (ἐπιρρώομαι).
To move nimbly, speed along : ὑπʼ ἀμφίπολοι ῥώοντο ἄνακτι Il. 18.417.
Of nimble motion of the limbs : ὑπὸ κνῆμαι ῥώοντο Il. 18.411= Il. 20.37. Cf. Od. 23.3.
Of movement in the dance Il. 24.616.
Of rhythmical movement as part of a ceremony Od. 24.69.
To rush to the fray : αὐτοὶ πρυλέες ῥώοντο Il. 11.50. Cf. Il. 16.166.
Of a horse's mane, to stream (with the wind) Il. 23.367.
Cut brushwood used for sitting upon : ῥῶπας ὑπέχευε δασείας Od. 14.49. Cf. Od. 16.47.
Small growing trees and shrubs, brushwood Il. 13.199, Il. 21.559, Il. 23.122 : Od. 14.473.
A break or sudden dip (in the ground) : ῥωχμὸς ἔην γαίης Il. 23.420.
Of dogs, etc., to show delight or fondness, fawn : νόησε σαίνοντας κύνας Od. 16.6. Cf. Od. 10.217, 219, Od. 17.302 (wagged his tail).
Dat. pl. σακέεσσι Od. 14.477. σάκεσσι Il. 17.354 : Od. 16.474. σάκεσι Il. 4.282, Il. 17.268 : Od. 14.479.
To sound the trumpet. Fig. : ἀμφὶ σάλπιγξεν οὐρανός (re-echoed as with the trumpet's sound) Il. 21.388.
A board or plank : σανίδας ἐκδῆσαι ὄπισθεν Od. 22.174.
One of the boards fixed on the framework and forming the face of a gate : πύλαι σανίδες τʼ ἐπὶ ἀραρυῖαι Il. 18.275. Cf. Il. 12.453, 461.
In pl., the two wings of a gate or door, a gate or door : σείων κολλητὰς σανίδας Il. 9.583. Cf. Il. 12.121, Il. 21.535 : Od. 2.344, Od. 21.137 = 164 (against the . . .), Od. 22.128, Od. 23.42.
Boarding ; in the passage cited, app. a wooden stage or platform raised above the earthen floor of a room : ἐφʼ ὑψηλῆς σανίδος βῆ· ἔνθα δὲ χηλοὶ ἕστασαν Od. 21.51.
-η, -ον, σῶς (the first only in comp. σαώτερος Il. 1.32).

Free from harm, safe, unharmed, unhurt, safe and sound, in good case : σαώτερος ὥς κε νέηαι (the safer) Il. 1.32, λαὸν σῶν ἔμμεναι 117. Cf. Il. 5.531= Il. 15.563 (find safety), Il. 7.310, Il. 8.246, Il. 15.497, Il. 16.252 : Od. 4.98, Od. 15.42, Od. 16.131, Od. 19.300.
Of things, safe, unharmed, whole, intact : οὔτʼ ἠέλιον σῶν ἔμμεναι οὔτε σελήνην Il. 17.367.
Free from danger, in safety, safe, not liable to be harmed : ὅππως σόοι μαχέοιντο (i.e. with the least risk possible) Il. 1.344. Cf. Il. 22.332.
So of things : ἵνα περ τάδε τοι σόα μίμνῃ Il. 24.382 : Od. 13.364.
Sure to come or happen, inevitable : σῶς τοι (μοι) ὄλεθρος Il. 13.773 : Od. 5.305, Od. 22.28.
Soundness of sense, good sense, discretion, prudence Od. 23.13.
So in pl. : σαοφροσύνῃσι νοήματα πατρὸς ἔκευθεν Od. 23.30.
Of sound or good sense, discreet Il. 21.462 : Od. 4.158.
Nom. pl. masc. pple. σώοντες (σαόοντες) Od. 9.430.
3 sing. non-thematic impf. σάω Il. 16.363, Il. 21.238.
Infin. σαωσέμεναι Il. 13.96. σαωσέμεν Il. 9.230, Il. 19.401.

To save from imminent or present danger, bring off safely, rescue from or bring safe through peril or trouble : τὼ νῶϊ πόλινδε σαώσετον (bring us off in safety to the city) Il. 5.224, ἐκ πολέμου Il. 11.752. Cf. Il. 5.23, Il. 8.363, Il. 9.78, Il. 12.123 (give him way to the ships and safety), Il. 15.503, Il. 19.401, Il. 21.238, etc. : Od. 3.185, 231 (bring him safe home), Od. 4.288, 444, 513, 753, 765, Od. 5.130, 452, Od. 9.430, Od. 10.286, 473, Od. 22.357, 372.
In reference to things : νῆας Il. 9.230, πόλιν καὶ ἄστυ Il. 17.144. Cf. Il. 9.424, 681, Il. 10.44, Il. 13.96.
In mid., to bring oneself off safely, get off unharmed : ἔνθεν οὔ τι σαώσεαι Od. 21.309.
To rescue from the foe, bring or carry off from hostile hands : τὸν νέκυν περ ἐόντα σαῶσαι Il. 24.35. Cf. Il. 5.469, Il. 15.427, Il. 17.149, 692.
To preserve from danger, keep from harm, see safe, stand by : φράσαι εἴ με σαώσεις Il. 1.83. Cf. Il. 22.56 : αὐτόν σε σάω (look after yourself) Od. 17.595. Cf. Od. 13.230.
In reference to things : ταῦτα Od. 13.230.
In neut. sing. σαρδάνιον as adv., of smiling, app. scornfully, bitterly Od. 20.302.
The flesh of the body : διήφυσε σαρκός (partitive genit.) Od. 19.450.
In pl. : σάρκες περιτρομέοντο μέλεσσιν Od. 18.77. Cf. Il. 8.380= Il. 13.832 : Od. 9.293, Od. 11.219.
The butt-end (of a spear) (app.= οὐρίαχος) Il. 10.153.

In reference to knowledge, with full understanding, clearly, with certainty, well : οὔ πω σ. οἶσθʼ οἷος νόος Ἀτρεΐωνος Il. 2.192. Cf. Il. 2.252, Il. 5.183, Il. 7.226, Il. 12.228, Il. 15.632, Il. 20.201 = 432 : Od. 1.202, Od. 2.108= Od. 24.144, Od. 4.730, Od. 17.153, 307, 373, Od. 24.404.
In reference to speech, with clearness of exposition, plainly, fully, without concealment : ἀγγελίην, ἥν χʼ ἡμῖν σ. εἴποι Od. 2.31. Cf. Od. 2.43, Od. 17.106.
With certainty or clear knowledge : σ. εἰπέμεν ὁππόθʼ ὄλωλεν Od. 3.89.
App., truly, correctly : μὴ ψεύδεʼ ἐπιστάμενος σ. εἰπεῖν Il. 4.404.
To put out, quench (fire) Il. 16.293, Il. 23.237, 250= Il. 24.791.
To quell, destroy, crush : πάντων ἀνθρώπων μένος Il. 16.621.
Intrans. In non-sigmatic aor., of a fire, to go out : οὐδέ ποτʼ ἔσβη πῦρ Il. 9.471.
Of wind, to cease to blow, fall : οὐδέ ποτʼ ἔσβη οὖρος Od. 3.182.
To be restrained from doing (something) by sensitiveness to the opinion of others, shrink from doing (it), think shame to do (it) (cf. αἰδέομαι 2) : σεβάσσατο τό γε θυμῷ Il. 6.167, 417.
Sensitiveness to the opinion of others, fear of what others may think or say, shame ( = αἰδώς 2) : σέβας σε θυμὸν ἰκέσθω Il. 18.178.
Wonder : σέβας μʼ ἔχει εἰσορόωντα (εἰσορόωσαν) Od. 3.123, Od. 4.75, 142, Od. 6.161, Od. 8.384.
To be moved by respect for the opinion of others, fear what others may think or say, think shame (cf. αἰδέομαι 4) : οὔ νυ σέβεσθε; Il. 4.242.
To shake, cause to quiver or vibrate : σανίδας Il. 9.583. Cf. Il. 15.321 : Od. 3.486= Od. 15.184.
To shake or brandish (a spear) : σείων ἐγχείην Il. 5.563. Cf. Il. 3.345, Il. 13.135, 558, Il. 22.133.
In pass., to shake or quiver : ἀμφί οἱ κροτάφοισι σείετο πήληξ Il. 13.805. Cf. Il. 14.285, Il. 20.59.
In mid., to change one's position suddenly, start : σείσατʼ εἰνὶ θρόνῳ Il. 8.199.

Dat. σέλαϊ Il. 17.739. σέλᾳ Il. 8.563 : Od. 21.246. Blaze, glow, brightness : ἥατο σέλᾳ πυρός Il. 8.563. Cf. Il. 8.509, Il. 15.600, Il. 17.739, Il. 18.214, Il. 19.17 (i.e. of fire), 366, 374, 375, 379 : δαΐδων σ. Od. 18.354. Cf. Od. 21.246.
A thunderbolt : δαιόμενον ἧκε σ. Il. 8.76.
3 sing. aor. σεύατο Il. 6.505, Il. 7.208, Il. 14.227 : Od. 5.51.
3 sing. opt. σεύαιτο Il. 17.463, Il. 20.148, Il. 23.198.
(ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπισσεύω, κατα-, μετασσεύομαι).

div.head: I
div.p: To set in motion : ἐξ ἀμφοτέροιιν αἷμʼ ἔσσευα (caused it to spirt forth) Il. 5.208, Διωνύσοιο τιθήνας σεῦε κατὰ Νυσήϊον (chased them) Il. 6.133, ὅλμον ὥς [ϝʼ] ἔσσευεν (hurled the body) Il. 11.147. Cf. Il. 11.293 (sets on), 294, Il. 14.413 (sent him spinning), Il. 15.681 (urging them on), Il. 20.189 (chased you), 325 (caused him to shoot up) : Od. 6.89 (drove them), Od. 14.35 (scattered them).
In mid. : εἴ περ ἄν αὐτὸν σεύωνται κύνες (seek to drive him off) Il. 3.26. Cf. Il. 11.549 (drive off)= Il. 15.272 (chase), Il. 20.148 (should chase him).

To set oneself in motion, to hasten, speed, rush : νῆας ἔπʼ ἐσσεύοντο Il. 2.150, σεύατʼ ἔπειτα (made eager way) Il. 7.208. Cf. Il. 2.808, 809 = Il. 8.58, Il. 6.505, Il. 9.80, Il. 11.167 (were in flight), 415 (are afoot, bestir themselves), 419, Il. 14.227, 519, Il. 16.585, Il. 17.678, Il. 21.167 (spirted forth), Il. 22.22 (at full speed), 146 : Od. 5.51 (made his way), Od. 9.447 (bring up the rear), Od. 14.34, 456, Od. 19.448, Od. 24.466.

p.gloss: To set oneself to do something.

div.p: With infin. : ὅτε σεύαιτο διώκειν Il. 17.463.
Of something inanimate, to begin to do something.
With infin. : ὄφρʼ ὕλη σεύαιτο καήμεναι Il. 23.198.
In pf., to be in a state of eagerness or excitement : ποσσὶν ἔσσυμαι ἀμφοτέροισιν (with both my feet, I cannot keep my feet still) Il. 13.79 : θυμός μοι ἔσσυται ἤδη (is eager to be off) Od. 10.484.

In pple., in a state of eagerness, eager, set or bent upon something : ἦ σε καὶ ἐσσύμενον κατερύκω; (delay you in your haste) Il. 6.518. Cf. Il. 11.554= Il. 17.663, Il. 13.57, 142, 315, 630, 787, Il. 16.9, Il. 24.404 : Od. 15.73.
With complementary genit. : καὶ ἐσσύμενός περ ὁδοῖο Od. 4.733.
With complementary infin. : ἐσσυμένους πολεμίζειν Il. 11.717. Cf. Od. 4.416.
To coop up in or as in a pen : σήκασθέν κε κατὰ Ἴλιον Il. 8.131.
One who sweeps out pens Od. 17.224.
A pen or fold for sheep, goats or cattle Il. 18.589 : Od. 9.219, 227, 319, 439, Od. 10.412.
A distinguishing mark : γνῶ κλήρου σ. ἰδών Il. 7.189.
A spot or patch of white hair on the forehead of a horse, a star Il. 23.455.
A peg or something similar stuck in the ground to mark the distance of a throw (cf. τέρμα 2) : ὑπέρβαλε σήματα πάντων Il. 23.843. Cf. Od. 8.192, 195.

div.head: a
div.p: Something indicating that a stage or point has been reached Od. 11.126, Od. 23.273.

div.head: b
div.p: Something indicated to a person for guidance of his action Il. 23.326.

div.head: d
div.p:
Something adduced as proof, an evidence : σ. ἀριφραδὲς ἄλλο τι δείξω Od. 21.217. Cf. Od. 19.250= Od. 23.206, Od. 23.73, 110, 188, 202, 225,
Od. 24.329, 346.

div.head: e
div.p: A guest-token, the credentials brought by a guest to satisfy his host as to his identity : ᾔτεε σ. ἰδέσθαι Il. 6.176. Cf. Il. 6.178.
So in pl.: πόρε σήματα λυγρά Il. 6.168.
A sign from heaven, a portent or omen : ἔνθʼ ἐφάνη μέγα σ. Il. 2.308. Cf. Il. 2.353, Il. 4.381, Il. 8.171, Il. 9.236, Il. 13.244, Il. 22.30 : Od. 21.413.
An omen or presage of human origin Od. 20.111.

A mound of earth or stones erected over and marking a grave, a grave-mound or barrow (= τύμβος) : παρὰ σήματι Ἴου Il. 10.415. Cf. Il. 2.814, Il. 6.419, Il. 7.86, 89, Il. 11.166, Il. 21.322, Il. 23.45, 255, 257, Il. 24.16, 51, 349, 416, 755, 799, 801 : Od. 1.291, Od. 2.222, Od. 11.75.
A wooden post erected on and marking a grave : ξύλον . . . σῆμά τευ βροτοῖο πάλαι κατατεθνηῶτος Il. 23.331.
To put a distinguishing mark upon, mark.
In mid. : κλῆρον ἐσημήναντο ἕκαστος Il. 7.175.
To point out, show, indicate : τέρματα Il. 23.358= 757.
To indicate, tell about : ἕκαστα Od. 12.26.
With dat. : πᾶσι Il. 1.289. Cf. Il. 1.296, Il. 2.805.
To take command, act as leader : πένθʼ ἡγεμόνας ποιήσατο σημαίνειν Il. 16.172.
To act as master : ἐπὶ δμῳῇσι γυναιξίν Od. 22.427.
To be in command of, command, be in charge of.
With dat. : φυλάκεσσιν Il. 10.58. Cf. Il. 17.250.
To superintend work, act as superintendent or overseer : σήμαινεν Ὀδυσσεύς Od. 22.450. Cf. Il. 21.445.
To guide or direct the actions of, act as counsellor to.
He who guides the horses, a charioteer (= ἡνίοχος (1)) Il. 8.127.
He who drives the cattle or sheep, a herdsman or shepherd Il. 15.325.
To-day, this day : τούτῳ Ζεὺς κῦδος ὀπάζει σ. Il. 8.142. Cf. Il. 11.431, Il. 19.103, Il. 20.127, 211: Od. 17.186, 252, Od. 18.377.
For to-day : παύσωμεν πόλεμον Il. 7.30. Cf. Il. 7.291.
3 sing. aor. subj. pass. σαπήῃ Il. 19.27.
In pf. and pass., to undergo natural decomposition or decay, rot : οὐδέ τί οἱ χρὼς σήπεται Il. 24.414. Cf. Il. 2.135 (lie rotted away), Il. 19.27.

Physical strength, power, might, vigour : ἐν σ. ὦρσεν ἑκάστῳ Il. 2.451. Cf. Il. 8.32, Il. 9.351, Il. 11.827, Il. 12.224, Il. 16.542, Il. 18.274 (see ἔχω I 14), Il. 20.361, etc. : Od. 8.136, Od. 21.282, Od. 22.237.
Of animals : λέοντος σ. Il. 5.139. Cf. Il. 5.783, Il. 12.42, Il. 17.22, etc. : Od. 18.373.
Of inanimate objects : οὐδέ τι πρώονα σθένεϊ [ποταμοὶ] ῥηγνῦσι ῥέοντες Il. 17.751.
σ. τινός, like βίη 5, periphrasis for a person : σ. Ἰδομενῆος Il. 13.248. Cf. Il. 23.827.
Sim.: σ. Ὠρίωνος (the constellation) Il. 18.486, σ. Ὠκεανοῖο 607, Il. 21.195.
The strength of life, vital force : αὐδὴ καὶ σ. Il. 18.420.
A (fattened and full-grown) domestic swine or pig Il. 21.363 : Od. 2.300, Od. 10.390, Od. 14.19, Od. 20.163.

Epithet of various things : ἡνία Il. 5.226, 328, Il. 8.116, 137, Il. 11.128, Il. 17.479, εἵματα Il. 22.154, δέσματα 468 : θρόνῳ Od. 5.86, εἵματα Od. 6.26, ῥήγεα 38, Od. 11.189, Od. 19.318, 337, Od. 23.180, ἡνία Od. 6.81, ῥήγεϊ Od. 13.118, χιτῶνα Od. 15.60, Od. 19.232, ὑπερώϊα Od. 16.449, Od. 18.206, Od. 19.600, Od. 22.428.
In imp. σίγα, be silent ! hush ! Il. 14.90 : Od. 14.493, Od. 17.393, Od. 19.42, 486.

In dat. σιγῇ, in silence, keeping silence, without speech, restraining the lips : ἴσαν Il. 3.8. Cf. Il. 3.134, 420, Il. 4.431, Il. 7.195, Il. 19.255 : Od. 4.776, Od. 7.30, Od. 13.76, Od. 15.391, Od. 18.142, Od. 19.502, Od. 21.388.
Without construction : σιγῇ νῦν (let no more be said) Od. 15.440.
Epithet of the heavens regarded as a vault of burnished metal, the iron . . . Od. 15.329= Od. 17.565.

As if of iron : ὀρυμαγδός (unwearying, ceaseless, incessant) Il. 17.424, θυμός (hard as iron, inflexible) Il. 22.357, πυρὸς μένος (relentless) Il. 23.177, ἦτορ (not to be turned from its course, daring all) Il. 24.205, 521 : κραδίη (stout as iron) Od. 4.293, θυμός (not open to compassion or sympathy) Od. 5.191, σοὶ σιδήρεα πάντα τέτυκται (you are all of iron) Od. 12.280, ἦτορ (unfeeling) Od. 23.172.
Various things made of iron. The point of an arrow : τόξῳ [πέλασε] σίδηρον Il. 4.123.
A bar of iron or something of the sort : ὀφθαλμοὶ ὡς εἰ κέρα ἕστασαν ἠὲ σίδηρος Od. 19.211. Cf. Od. 19.494.

Collectively, implements or weapons of iron : πολιὸν σίδηρον (i.e. the articles of iron proposed as prizes) Il. 23.261, τίθει ἰόεντα σίδηρον 850 (defined in the next line) : διοϊστεῦσαι (διοϊστεύσειν) (εἴ κε διοϊστεύσω) σιδήρου (i.e. the axe-heads set up to be shot through by the suitors) Od. 19.587, Od. 21.97 = 127, Od. 21.114, Cf. Il. 6.48= Il. 10.379= Il. 11.133 : = Od. 21.10, Od. 14.324, Od. 16.294 = Od. 19.13, Od. 21.3 = 81 = Od. 24.168, Od. 21.61, 328, Od. 24.177.
To hurt, harm, do mischief to : εἴ κε σίνηαι [βόας] Od. 11.112= Od. 12.139. Cf. Il. 24.45.
To harry, despoil : οἵ σφεας σινέσκοντο Od. 6.6.
To lay violent hands upon, carry off to destruction : ἑταίρους Od. 12.114.
Ravening : λῖν σίντην Il. 11.481, λύκοι σίνται Il. 16.353. Cf. Il. 20.165.
To take one's meals, eat : ἐν τῷ σιτέσκοντο Od. 24.209.

Food other than flesh-meat (definitely in this sense or distinguished in terms from meat) : σῖτον ἐπένειμε, ἀτὰρ κρέα νεῖμεν Ἀχιλλεύς Il. 9.216, Il. 24.625 : σῖτον ὄψα τε Od. 3.479, ἀνέμισγε σίτῳ φάρμακα λυγρά Od. 10.235. Cf. Od. 1.139= Od. 4.55= Od. 7.175= Od. 10.371= Od. 15.138= Od. 17.94 = 259, Od. 1.147, Od. 4.623,
Od. 9.9, Od. 10.290, 375, Od. 12.19, Od. 14.449, 456, Od. 15.334, Od. 16.51, Od. 17.335, 412, Od. 20.254, Od. 22.21.

Food in general without these distinctions : σίτου ἵμερος Il. 11.89. Cf. Il. 19.44, 163, Il. 24.129, 602, 613, 619 : ἐπὶ χθονὶ σῖτον ἔδοντες Od. 8.222, Od. 9.89 = Od. 10.101. Cf. Od. 4.60, Od. 6.99, Od. 14.455 (the leavings of the meal), Od. 16.83, Od. 17.418, 457, 558, Od. 18.360, Od. 20.130, Od. 24.395, 489.
App., to injure or harm in some way : θεός ἑ σιφλώσειεν Il. 14.142.
To be silent, cease from talking : σιωπᾶν λαὸν ἀνώγει Il. 2.280. Cf. Il. 23.568 : εἰ γὰρ σιωπήσειαν Ἀχαιοί (cease their clamour) Od. 17.513.

In silence, keeping silence, without speech, restraining the lips : ἰδὼν ἐς παῖδα σ. Il. 6.404. Cf. Il. 4.412, Il. 7.427, Il. 9.190, 620, Il. 14.310 (without telling of my intention), Il. 18.556 : Od. 1.325, 339, Od. 10.140, Od. 13.309, Od. 15.463.
With ἀκήν : ἀκὴν ἐγέοντο σ. See ἀκήν 2.
To limp, halt, walk lame : σκάζων ἐκ πολέμου Il. 11.811. Cf. Il. 19.47.

p.gloss: That is on the left side, the left ...

div.p: In fem. σκαιή (sc. χείρ), the left hand : σκαιῇ ἔγχος ἔχων Il. 16.734. Cf. Il. 1.501, Il. 21.490.
That lies to the left of a spectator : ῥίον Od. 3.295.
To frisk, gambol, skip along : ποσὶ σκαίροντες Il. 18.572. Cf. Od. 10.412.
Some kind of vessel for milk Od. 9.223.
3 sing. aor. ἐσκέδασε Il. 7.330. σκέδασε Il. 17.649, Il. 20.341, Il. 23.162 : Od. 13.352.
Imp. σκέδασον Il. 19.171, Il. 23.158 : Od. 8.149. (ἀπο-, δια-)
To shed in drops : αἷμα Il. 7.330.
To cause (a body of men) to disperse, dismiss (it) : λαόν Il. 19.171. Cf. Il. 23.158, 162.
To disperse or scatter (mist) Il. 17.649, Il. 20.341 : Od. 13.352.
To scatter, dismiss (cares) : σκέδασον ἀπὸ κήδεα θυμοῦ Od. 8.149.
A (disorderly) scattering, a rout : μνηστήρων σκέδασιν Od. 1.116, Od. 20.225.
To dry up, shrivel up, parch : χρόα Il. 23.191.
Shelter, protection, cover : ἀνέμοιο (from the ...) Od. 5.443 = Od. 7.282, Od. 6.210, Od. 12.336.
A place affording shelter, protection or cover : εἶσαν ἐπὶ σ. Od. 6.212.
To afford shelter from, ward off : κῦμα Od. 13.99.
To look, look about : σκέπτεο νῦν, αἴ κεν ἴδηαι ... Il. 17.652.
To look, turn one's eyes, in a specified direction : ἐς νῆα Od. 12.247.
To look out for, watch : ὀϊστῶν ῥοῖζον Il. 16.361.
A staff : σκη-πανίῳ ἀμφοτέρω κεκόπων Il. 13.59. Cf. Il. 24.247.
To lean or support oneself in walking (upon something) : ἄκοντι σκηπτόμενον Il. 14.457.
To lean upon a staff for support in walking, walk with a staff : ἐδύσετο δώματα σκηπτόμενος Od. 17.338. Cf. Od. 17.203 = Od. 24.158.
Epithet of βασιλῆες Il. 1.279, Il. 2.86 : Od. 2.231 = Od. 5.9, Od. 4.64, Od. 8.41.
Absol. in the sense of βασιλεύς : τοὶ ἅμʼ ἕποντο σκηπτοῦχοι Od. 8.47. Cf. Il. 14.93.
A stick or staff for support in walking : ἕλε σ. παχύ, βῆ δὲ θύραζε Il. 18.416. Cf. Od. 13.437, Od. 14.31, Od. 17.199, Od. 18.103 (i.e. to be used in defence).

div.head: a
div.p: By a priest : σ. καὶ στέμμα θεοῖο Il. 1.28. Cf. Il. 1.15 = 374.

div.head: b
div.p: By a king or chief : Ζεύς οἱ ὑπὸ σκήπτρῳ ἐδάμασσεν [Ἄργείους] Il. 6.159. Cf. Il. 2.46, 101, 186, 199, 206, 265, 268, Il. 7.412, Il. 9.38, 99, 156, 298, Il. 18.557 :Od. 3.412, Od. 11.569.

A staff in the custody of a herald and handed by him to one wishing to speak in an assembly in token of his right to a hearing : ἐν κῆρυξ χειρὶ σ. ἔθηκεν Il. 23.568. Cf. Il. 1.234, 245, Il. 2.279, Il. 3.218, Il. 10.321 (the speaker offering the staff which he holds), 328, Il. 18.505 (app. a single staff held by the speakers in succession is meant) : Od. 2.37, 80.
To lean, apply oneself, apply one's weight : σκηριπτόμενος χερσίν τε ποσίν τε (pushing with his hands and scrambling with his feet) Od. 11.595.
To support oneself in walking Od. 17.196.
To throw shadow over, bring into darkness, darken : ἄρουραν Il. 21.232.
3 pl. impf. pass. σκιόωντο. (κατα-) = σκιάζω. : σκιόωντο πᾶσαι ἀγυιαί Od. 2.388 = Od. 3.487 = 497 = Od. 11.12 = Od. 15.185 = 296 = 471.
To be scattered or dispered : ὑψόσʼ ἄχνη σκίδναται Il. 11.308. Cf. Il. 16.375.
Of men, to disperse, go each his own way : κατὰ κλισίας τε νέας τε Il. 1.487. Cf. Il. 19.277 = Il. 23.3, Il. 24.2 : Od. 1.274, Od. 2.252, 258.
Of water, to run dispersed : κρῆναι, ἡ μὲν ἀνὰ κῆπον σκίδναται Od. 7.130.
Shadowy, shady : νέμεϊ Il. 11.480 : ἄλσος Od. 20.278.
A shadow : σκιῇ εἴκελον ἤ καὶ ὀνείρῳ Od. 11.207. Cf. Od. 10.495 (like shadows).

On which shadows fall or play, having the surface diversified with patches of dark or shadow, shadowy : οὔρεα Il. 1.157, νέφεα Il. 5.525, Il. 11.63, Il. 12.157 : Od. 8.374, Od. 11.592. Cf. Od. 5.279 = Od. 7.268.
Faintly lighted, shadowy, dim : μέγαρα Od. 1.365 = Od. 4.768 = Od. 18.399, Od. 10.479, Od. 11.334 = Od. 13.2, Od. 23.299.
Crooked. Fig., unjust, inequitable: θέμιστας Il. 16.387.

In pl., palisades, pales or stakes fixed in the ground in a close row, vertical or inclined, as a defence : ὕπερθε σκολόπεσσιν ἠρήρει [τάφρος] Il. 12.55. Cf. Il. 7.441, Il. 8.343 = Il. 15.1, Il. 9.350, Il. 12.63, Il. 15.344, Il. 18.177 (app. those on the wall of the city; cf. the next passage) : Od. 7.45.
A natural prominence, a rock or crag Il. 2.396 : Od. 12.73, 80, 95, 101, 108, 220, 239, 430.
To direct one's look to something, observe it : μάλα περ σκοπιάζων Il. 14.58.
To look out for something, watch : δηρὸν καθήμενος ἐσκοπίαζον Od. 10.260.
To spy upon : ἄνδρας δυσμενέας Il. 10.40.
A spot from which one can command a view, a look-out place : ἥμενος ἐν σκοπιῇ Il. 5.771. Cf. Il. 4.275, Il. 20.137, Il. 22.145 : Od. 4.524, Od. 10.97 = 148, 194, Od. 14.261 = Od. 17.430.
A mountain peak : σκοπιαὶ καὶ πρώονες Il. 8.557 = Il. 16.299.
A looking out, a look-out or watch : σκοπιὴν ἔχεν Od. 8.302.
One stationed to look out or watch, a look-out : τὸν ἀπὸ σκοπιῆς εἶδε σ. Od. 4.524. Cf. Il. 2.792, Il. 18.523, Il. 24.799 : Od. 16.365, Od. 22.156.
One stationed to keep an eye on the competitors in a race Il. 23.359.
One set to watch the actions of others, an overseer : δμῳάων σ. ἐσσι Od. 22.396.
One who goes to observe the movements or dispositions of an enemy, a spy Il. 10.324, 526, 561.
A mark or aim : οὐδέ τι τοῦ σκοποῦ ἤμβροτον Od. 21.425. Cf. Od. 22.6.–ἀπὸ σκοποῦ, wide of the mark : οὐκ ἀπὸ σκοποῦ μυθεῖται Od. 11.344.
Not born in open wedlock, conceived in stealth : σκότιόν ἑ γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 6.24.
In the dark (part of the) month, i.e. moonless : νύξ Od. 14.457.
-ου, ὁ. Darkness: ποτὶ σκότον ἐτράπετο (away from the light) Od. 19.389.
To be angry or wroth with, feel resentment against.
With dat. : μή μοι σκυδμαινέμεν Il. 24.592.
To be angry or wroth, bear resentment Il. 8.483, Il. 9.198.
To be angry or wroth with, feel resentment against.
With dat. : διὶ πατρί Il. 4.23 = Il. 8.460. Cf. Il. 24.113, 134 : Od. 23.209.
A puppy: κύων ἀμαλῇσι περὶ σκυλάκεσσι βεβῶσα Od. 20.14. Cf. Od. 9.289, Od. 12.86.
A worker in leather : σκυτοτόμων ὄχʼ ἄριστος Il. 7.221.
To give forth a loud sound : σμαραγεῖ πόντος (roars) Il. 2.210. Cf. Il. 2.463 (re-echoes with the cries of the birds), Il. 21.199 (crashes).
[cf. σμερδνός. and L. mordeo, to bite.]
Terror-striking, awe-inspiring, dread, terrible, daunting : δράκων Il. 2.309. Cf. Il. 12.464, Il. 13.192, Il. 18.579, Il. 20.65, 260, Il. 21.401 : σ. αὐτῇσι φάνη Od. 6.137. Cf. Od. 11.609, Od. 12.91.
In neut. sing. σμερδαλέον as adv.

div.head: a
div.p: Terribly, dauntingly: δέδορκεν Il. 22.95 : ἐβόησεν Od. 24.537. Cf. Od. 9.395.
Violently : ἀμφὶ πήληξ σ. κροτάφοισι τινάσσετο Il. 15.609.

div.head: b
div.p: Loudly, piercingly, vehemently, with ringing or re-echo : νῆες κονάβησαν Il. 2.334 = Il. 16.277. Cf. Il. 2.466, Il. 8.92, Il. 13.498, Il. 15.648, Il. 18.35, Il. 19.399, Il. 21.255, 593 : ἐβόησεν Od. 8.305. Cf. Od. 10.399, Od. 17.542.
In neut. pl. σμερδαλέα as adv.
In neut. sing. σμερδνόν as adv. = σμερδαλέος. 2.b : βοόων Il. 15.687, 732.
To wipe off : ἁλὸς χνόον Od. 6.226.
To consume (with fire), burn : πυρὶ νῆας Il. 9.653.
In pass., to be consumed (with fire), blaze : ὡς εἰ ἅπασα Ἴλιος πυρὶ σμύχοιτο Il. 22.411.
A mass or lump of iron. Used for distance-throwing as a trial of strength or skill Il. 23.826, 839, 844.
A cinerary urn (= λάρναξ 2) : ὣς ὀστέα νῶϊν ὁμὴ σ. ἀμφικαλύπτοι Il. 23.91.
Genit. pl. fem. σέων (scanned as one syllable) Il. 5.818.
With the article : τὸ σὸν γέρας Il. 1.185. Cf. Il. 16.40, etc. : Od. 2.403, Od. 14.512, etc.
Absol.: ἐπὶ σοῖσι καθήμενος (where your heritage is) Od. 2.369. Cf. Il. 23.83.
As predicative adj., thine : εἰ σός εἰμι Od. 9.529.
[app. fr. σπάρτος, broom (i.e. the common, hardly the Spanish, broom).]
Ropes or cables (properly of broom) Il. 2.135.
3 sing. aor. ἔσπασε Il. 12.395, Il. 13.178. σπάσε Il. 5.859.
Genit. sing. neut. aor. pple. pass. σπασθέντος Il. 11.458.
To draw, pull, pluck, in a specified direction : ἐκ δόρυ σπάσεν αὖτις Il. 5.859. Cf. Il. 11.458, Il. 12.395, Il. 13.178.
In mid., to draw (one's sword) : σπασσάμενος ἄορ παρὰ μηροῦ Il. 16.473 : = Od. 10.439 = Od. 11.231. Cf. Od. 22.74.
Sim. of drawing a spear from its σῦριγξ: ἐκ σύριγγος ἐσπάσατʼ ἔγχος Il. 19.387.
To pull off or pluck (something growing).
In mid. : σπασάμην ῥῶπάς τε λύγους τε Od. 10.166.

In pl., clothes, clothing,
articles of attire : σπεῖρα κάκʼ ἀμφʼ ὤμοισι βαλών Od. 4.245. Cf. Od. 6.179.
A covering wherewith to honour a dead body Od. 2.102, Od. 19.147 = Od. 24.137.
The sail of a ship Od. 5.318, Od. 6.269.

To pour out wine as a drink-offering, make libation : διὶ πατρί Il. 6.259, Il. 24.287. Cf. Il. 9.177, 657, 712, Il. 16.227, 253, Il. 23.196 : σπείσας ἔπιεν οἶνον Od. 18.151. Cf. Od. 3.45, 342, Od. 4.591, Od. 7.137, Od. 12.363, Od. 13.39, Od. 21.264, etc.
To pour out (wine) in way of libation : σπείσας οἶνον Od. 14.447. Cf. Il. 11.775.
Seed. Fig. : σπέρμα πυρὸς σώζων Od. 5.490.
In mid., to put oneself in eager motion, be in act, to do something.
With infin. : ὁπότε σπερχοίατʼ Ἀχαιοὶ φέρειν Ἄρηα Il. 19.317.
In mid., to put forth one's efforts, exert oneself : σπερχομένοιο γέροντος (giving his impetuosity way) Il. 24.248 : ὁπότε σπερχοίατʼ ἐρετμοῖς (shoud ply their oars) Od. 13.22.
In mid. pple., with speed, in haste, hastily, without loss of time : σπερχόμενος ἐσύλα τεύχεα Il. 11.110. Cf. Il. 23.870, Il. 24.322 : Od. 9.101, Od. 15.60.
Sim. of the eager motion of a ship : νηῦς ἠπείρῳ ἐπέκελσε σπερχομένη Od. 13.115.
Intrans. for reflexive, of wind, to rush, blow furiously : ὁπότε σπέρχοιεν ἄελλαι Od. 3.283. Cf. Il. 13.334.
Dat. pl. masc. pres. pple. σπευδόντεσσιν Il. 17.745.
To hasten on with (something), lose no time in getting (it) done, accomplish (it) with speed : ταῦτα χρὴ σπεύδειν Il. 13.236 : ἐπεὶ σπεῦσε τὰ ἃ ἔργα Od. 9.250, 310, 343.
To press, urge, the accomplishment of (something) : γάμον σπεύδουσιν Od. 19.137.
In mid., to speed, hasten, hurry : σπεύσομαι εἰς Ἀχιλῆα Il. 15.402.
So intrans. for reflexive : ἤϊξε σπεύδουσα Il. 11.119.

Intrans. for reflexive, to put oneself in eager motion for some end, show eagerness, zeal, or alacrity : σπεύδοντα μάχην ἐς κυδιάνειραν Il. 4.225, οὓς σπεύδοντας ἴδοι (eager for the fray) 232. Cf. Il. 8.293.

Intrans. for reflexive, to put forth one's efforts, exert oneself : τὸ οὔ τις ἐπεφράσατο σπευδόντων (such was their haste) Il. 5.667, ἐφομαρτεῖτον καὶ σπεύδετον (show your speed) Il. 8.191, Il. 23.414, περὶ πατρόκλοιο θανόντος σπεύσομεν Il. 17.121, τὸν εὗρε σπεύδοντα (hard at work) Il. 18.373, τὼ σπεύδοντε πετέσθην (at the top of their speed) Il. 23.506, σπεύσατέ μοι (get to work) Il. 24.253. Cf. Il. 17.745, Il. 18.472, Il. 23.767 : Od. 24.324.
Of unknown meaning. Commonly explained as wide : διὰ σπιδέος πεδίοιο Il. 11.754.
A rock or reef in or projecting into the sea : νῆας ποτὶ σπιλάδεσσιν ἔαξαν κύματα Od. 3.298, σπιλάδες τε πάγοι τε Od. 5.405 (the two words difficult to distinguish). Cf. Od. 5.401.

The entrails (such as the heart, liver and spleen) of an animal killed as under ἱερεύω 1 or (2) : ἐπεὶ σπλάγχνα πάσαντο Il. 1.464 = Il. 2.427 : = Od. 3.461 = Od. 12.364. Cf. Il. 2.426 : Od. 3.9, 40, Od. 20.252, 260.
A sponge : σπόγγῳ ἀμφὶ πρόσωπʼ ἀπομόργνυ Il. 18.414. Cf. Od. 1.111, Od. 20.151, Od. 22.439, 453.
Smouldering ashes, embers : ὡς ὅτε τις δαλὸν σποδιῇ ἐνέκρυψεν Od. 5.488.
Smouldering ashes, embers : μοχλὸν ὑπὸ σποδοῦ ἤλασα πολλῆς Od. 9.375.
In pl., an agreement ratified by libations : σπονδαί τʼ ἄκρητοι καὶ δεξιαί Il. 2.341 = Il. 4.159.
Exertion, effort : ἄτερ σπουδῆς τάνυσε τόξον Od. 21.409.–ἀπὸ σπουδῆς, in earnest, seriously : εἰ τοῦτον [μῦθον] ἀπὸ σπουδῆς ἀγορεύεις Il. 7.359 = Il. 12.233.

div.head: a
div.p: With haste or speed, without loss of time : ἀνάβαινε Od. 15.209.

div.head: b
div.p: With much ado, with difficulty : ἐξήλασσαν [ὄνον] Il. 11.562. Cf. Il. 2.99 (i.e. they could hardly be got to do so), Il. 5.893, Il. 13.687, Il. 23.37 : ἤλυξαν ὄλεθρον Od. 3.297. Cf. Od. 13.279, Od. 24.119.
Of fighting, stand-up, close (as opposed to the use of missiles) : ἄριστος τοξοσύνῃ, ἀγαθὸς δὲ καὶ ἐν σταδίῃ ὑσμίνῃ Il. 13.314. Cf. Il. 13.713.
Absol. in fem. (sc. ὑσμίνη), stand-up fighting : ἐνὶ σταδίῃ μέλπεσθαι Ἄρηϊ Il. 7.241. Cf. Il. 13.514.
Such fighting as opposed to the use of missiles : ἐπιστάμενος μὲν ἄκοντι, ἐσθλὸς δʼ ἐν σταδίῃ Il. 15.283.
To introduce into something in drops : πατρόκλῳ ἀμβροσίην καὶ νέκταρ στάξε κατὰ ῥινῶν Il. 19.39 (the word applying strictly to νέκτορ only). Cf. Il. 19.348, 354.

A device employed by carpenters, etc., a line rubbed with chalk or the like and drawn tight along a surface so as to leave on its removal a straight line marked thereon for the workman's guidance : ὥς τε σ. δόρυ νήϊον ἐξιθύνει Il. 15.410 : ἐπὶ στάθμην
ἴθυνε [δοῦρα] (to the line) Od. 5.245. Cf. Od. 17.341 = Od. 21.44, Od. 21.121, Od. 23.197.
To the steading : σ. ἀπονέεσθαι Od. 9.451.

The establishment of a shepherd or herdsman, a farm-house with its outbuildings : λίς, ὃν κύνες ἀπὸ σταθμοῖο δίωνται Il. 17.110. Cf. Il. 2.470, Il. 12.304, Il. 16.642, Il. 19.377 : Od. 14.32, 358, Od. 15.306, Od. 16.45, 66, 156, 163, 318, Od. 17.26, 200.
In the μέγαρον, one of a group of columns surrounding the hearth and supporting the roof : στῆ παρὰ σταθμὸν τέγεος Od. 1.333 = Od. 8.458 = Od. 16.415 = Od. 18.209 = Od. 21.64. Cf. Od. 17.96.
A weight: σταθμὸν ἔχουσα καὶ εἴριον Il. 12.434.
The uprights of the ἴκρια of the σχεδίη of Odysseus Od. 5.252.
Of a horse, that has been confined in a stall, stalled Il. 6.506 = Il. 15.263.
A stake or pale : σταυροὺς ἐκτὸς ἔλασσεν Od. 14.11. Cf. Il. 24.453.
A level, a plummet used for determining levels ,
[ἵππους] σταφύλῃ ἐπὶ νῶτον ἐΐσας (i.e. of equal height as measured by a level across their backs) Il. 2.765.
A bunch or cluster of grapes Il. 18.561 : Od. 5.69, Od. 7.121, Od. 24.343.
Stiff fat, tallow or suet : ἐκ δὲ στέατος ἔνεικε μέγαν τροχόν Od. 21.178 = 183 (scanned as a disyllable, or the vowel before στ- allowed to be short).
To trample under foot : νέκυας Il. 11.534. Cf. Il. 20.499.
To tread or tramp (clothes) in washing Od. 6.92.
The handle of an axe Od. 21.422.
A narrow or confined space in which a body of persons is cooped up : εἴλεον [δμῳὰς] ἐν στείνει Od. 22.460.
A narrow or confined space within which free movement is impossible : στεῖνος γάρ, ὅθι τρώσεσθαι ὀΐω Il. 12.66.
A narrow part (of a track) Il. 23.419.
A position or state of difficulty, a strait or pass : μή πω χάζεσθε μάχης ἐν στείνεϊ τῷδε Il. 15.426. Cf. Il. 8.476.
To confine within a narrow space, coop up : στείνοντο λαοί Il. 14.34.
To make narrow : θύρετρά κέ τοι φεύγοντι στείνοιτο (would seem all too narrow) Od. 18.386.
To impede the freedom of movement of, cumber : ἀρνειὸς λάχνῳ στεινόμενος Od. 9.445.
To fill to the point of overcrowding or oppression.
With genit. : στείνοντο σηκοὶ ἀρνῶν Od. 9.219.
With dat. : οὐ δύναμαι προχέειν ῥόον στεινόμενος νεκύεσσιν Il. 21.220.
Intrans., to be oppressed by a feeling of fulness : μέγʼ ἔστενε κῆρ (he was oppressed as to the heart, his heart was full to bursting) Il. 10.16. Cf. Il. 18.33 : Od. 21.247.
With ἦτορ as subject : ἔν οἱ κραδίῃ στένει ἦτορ Il. 20.169.
Hence, to give audible vent to the feeling, to groan or moan : ἐπὶ δʼ ἔστενε δῆμος Il. 24.776.
Of the moaning of the swelling sea Il. 23.230.
Narrow, strait : ὁδῷ Il. 7.143, Il. 23.416 (in the latter passage a narrow part of the track). Cf. Il. 23.427.
Absol., a narrow passage, a strait : στεινωπὸν ἀνεπλέομεν Od. 12.234.
The stem or cutwater of a ship : ἀμφὶ κῦμα στείρῃ ἴαχεν Il. 1.482 : = Od. 2.428.
Of a cow, that has not calved : βοῦν Od. 10.522 = Od. 11.30, Od. 20.186.
To go, take or make one's way, proceed : ἐνθάδε στείχοντες Il. 2.287. Cf. Il. 2.833 = Il. 11.331, Il. 9.86, Il. 16.258 : Od. 7.72, Od. 9.418, 444, Od. 11.17, Od. 17.204, Od. 23.136.
Acc. sing. masc. aor. pple. στείλαντα Od. 14.247.
To get ready, equip, fit out : νῆα Od. 2.287. Cf. Od. 14.247, 248.
In mid., to get oneself ready, array oneself : ἄλλοι στέλλεσθε Il. 23.285.
To set in array : οὓς ἑτάρους στέλλοντα Il. 4.294.
To furl (a sail) : ἱστία στεῖλαν ἀείραντες Od. 3.11.
To lower (a sail) : ἱστία στέλλοντας Od. 16.353.
To dispatch, send : ἀγγελίην ἐπὶ τυδῆ στεῖλαν Il. 4.384 (see ἀγγελίη).
To urge, incite : μάχην ἐς κυδιάνειραν Il. 12.325.
A fillet or chaplet of wool born by a priest : σκῆπτρον καὶ στέμμα θεοῖο Il. 1.28.
In pl. in the same sense : στέμματʼ ἔχων ἐν χερσὶν Ἀπόλλωνος χρυσέῳ ἀνὰ σκήπτρῳ (to denote his being a suppliant) Il. 1.14 = 373.
To be oppressed by a feeling of fulness.
In mid. : μέγα στεναχίζετο θυμῷ (his heart was full to bursting) Il. 7.95.
To groan or moan : ἠρνεῖτο στεναχίζων Il. 19.304. Cf. Il. 23.172, 225: Od. 1.243, Od. 9.13, Od. 11.214, Od. 16.188, 195, Od. 24.317.
To give forth a heavy sound under repeated pressure, rumble.
In mid. : ὑπὸ δὲ στεναχίζετο γαῖα λαῶν ἱόντων Il. 2.95. Cf. Il. 2.784.
In mid. : περὶ δὲ στεναχίζετο δῶμα Od. 10.454.
Of the roaring of a beast Il. 16.489.
Of the roaring of rushing water Il. 16.391.
Of the rushing sound of horses in rapid motion.
In mid. : ὣς ἵπποι μεγάλα στενάχοντο θέουσαι Il. 16.393.
In mid. : τοὺς στενάχοντο γοῶντες Od. 9.467.

To recall with grief the doings of (a
person), bewail the consequences of his actions : Ἄτην αἰεὶ στενάχεσκεν Il. 19.132.
Resisting force, rigid, stout : βοέῃς Il. 17.493.
Fig., of the heart, hard, unyielding.
In comp. : σοὶ αἰεὶ κραδίη στερεωτέρη ἐστὶ λίθοιο Od. 23.103.
Firmly fixed, not to be displaced : ὡς ὅτε τις στερεὴ λίθος Od. 19.494.
With genit. : στερέσαι με τῆς ληΐδος Od. 13.262.
So as to give rigidity or power of resistance : [κυνέη] ἱμᾶσιν ἐντέτατο σ. Il. 10.263.
So as to prevent movement, tight, fast : ἐμὲ κατέδησαν σ. Od. 14.346.
Without relaxation of pressure, with constant strain : νῶτα ἑλκόμενα σ. Il. 23.715.
Resisting persuasion, inflexibly, sternly : ἠρνεῖτο σ. Il. 23.42. Cf. Il. 9.510.
In pl. in the same sense : εὐρύτερος στέρνοισιν (in the . . .) Il. 3.194. Cf. Il. 13.282, 290.
Lightning, the lightning flash Il. 10.154, Il. 11.66.
Flash, gleam : χαλκοῦ Il. 11.83, Il. 19.363 : Od. 4.72, Od. 14.268 = Od. 17.437.

p.gloss: (Prob. orig. a voc. turned into a nom.) Gatherer of lightnings.

div.p: To press forward, essay eagerly : στεῦτο διψάων (in his thirst) Od. 11.584.

p.gloss: To put oneself forward to do something, make as though one would do it.

div.p: With infin. : στεῦταί τι ἔπος ἐρέειν Il. 3.83.

p.gloss: To hold oneself out as willing or able to do something, promise to do it.

div.p: With infin. : στεῦτο Τρωσὶ μαχήσεσθαι Il. 5.832. Cf. Il. 18.191.
With infin. : στεῦτο νικησέμεν Il. 2.597. Cf. Il. 9.241.
With infin. : στεῦτʼ ἀπολεψέμεν οὔατα Il. 21.455.
To declare positively, assert with confidence, insist.
With infin. : στεῦται Ὀδυσῆος ἀκοῦσαι Od. 17.525.
A circlet for the head, a coronal Il. 18.597.
The brow of a hill Il. 13.138.

To set or dispose round or about something : τείρεα, τά τʼ οὐρανὸς ἐστεφάνωται (is set round with them, has them set around it as a crown) Il. 18.485 : νῆσον, τὴν πέρι πόντος ἐστεφάνωται Od. 10.195. Cf. Il. 5.739.
To set upon something as a central figure : ἀσπίδι δʼ ἐπὶ Γοργὼ ἐστεφάνωτο Il. 11.36.
To set round something so as to envelop it : ἀμφί μιν νέφος ἐστεφάνωτο Il. 15.153.
To set round something so as to envelop it : ἀμφί οἱ κεφαλῇ νέφος ἔστεφεν Il. 18.205.
In reference to something immaterial, to put round as a crown or so as to adorn : μορφὴν ἔπεσι στέφει Od. 8.170.
Locative στήθεσφι Il. 2.388. This form as ablative Il. 11.374, Il. 14.150, 214.

In pl. in reference to a single person : χιτῶνα περὶ στήθεσσι δαΐξαι Il. 2.416. Cf. Il. 3.332, Il. 4.420, Il. 5.317, Il. 6.65, Il. 9.490, Il. 10.9, etc. : Od. 11.609, Od. 16.174, Od. 18.69, Od. 20.62.

div.head: a
div.p: In pl. as above : ἐν στήθεσσι μένος βάλεν Il. 5.513. Cf. Il. 5.125, Il. 17.570.

div.head: b
div.p: Of wrath or resentment : Ἥρῃ οὐκ ἔχαδε σ. χόλον Il. 4.24 = Il. 8.461. Cf. Il. 18.110.
In pl. as above : εἰ χόλον αὐτῆμαρ καταπέψῃ, ἀλλʼ ἔχει κότον ἐν στήθεσσιν ἑοῖσιν Il. 1.83.
Sim. of rage : ὁππότε μένος οὐ τόσον ᾖσιν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἐμοῖσιν Il. 19.202.

div.head: c
div.p: In pl. as above : πένθος ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἀέξων Il. 17.139.

div.head: d
div.p: In pl. as above : μή τί τοι ἄλλο ἐν στήθεσσι κακὸν μελέτω ἔργον Od. 2.304.

div.head: e
div.p: In pl. as above : οὐ τοῦτο ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἔολπεν Od. 21.317.

div.head: f
div.p: In pl. as above of βουλή : ἔγνως ἐμὴν ἐν στήθεσι βουλήν Il. 20.20. Cf. Il. 17.470.
Of μῆτις : ἥν τινα μῆτιν ἐνὶ στήθεσσι κέκευθεν Od. 3.18.
Of a purpose, etc. : τοῦτον νόον, ὅν τινά οἱ νῦν ἐν στήθεσσι τιθεῖσι θεοί Od. 2.125. Cf. Il. 4.309.
Of an idea or notion: οὔ τοι τοιοῦτον ἐνὶ στήθεσσι νόημα Od. 17.403.

div.head: a
div.p: In pl. in reference to a single person : ἐν ἐμοὶ αὐτῇ στήθεσι πάλλεται ἠ. Il. 22.452. Cf. Il. 1.189 : Od. 17.47, Od. 20.22.

div.head: b
div.p: In pl. as above : Ἀχιλλῆος κ. γηθεῖ ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν Il. 14.140. Cf. Od. 1.341, Od. 7.309, Od. 16.275.

div.head: c
div.p: In pl. as above : ἐμοὶ κ. ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἰάνθη Od. 4.549.

div.head: d
div.p: Of θυμός : δαΐζετο θ. ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν Ἀχαιῶν Il. 9.8 = Il. 15.629. Cf. Il. 2.142, Il. 4.289, Il. 13.808, Il. 15.322, etc. : Od. 2.90, Od. 10.461, Od. 20.328.

div.head: e
div.p: Of νόος : ὅς τε καὶ ἄλλων οἰδάνει ἐν στήθεσσι νόον Il. 9.554.
In pl. as above : σοὶ ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἀτάρβητος ν. ἐστίν Il. 3.63. Cf. Il. 13.732 : Od. 10.329, Od. 13.255, Od. 20.366.

div.head: f
div.p: In pl. as above: αἰεί τοι τοιοῦτον ἐνὶ στήθεσσι ν. Od. 13.330. Cf. Il. 24.41.
A block of wood or a stake set in the ground to contain the face of an earthwork (cf. θεμείλια) : στήλας προβλῆτας ἐμόχλεον Il. 12.259.
A post or a block or pillar of stone set upon a sepulchral mound : στήλῃ κεκλιμένος ἐπὶ τύμβῳ Ἴλου Il. 11.371. Cf. Il. 13.437, Il. 16.457 = 675, Il. 17.434 : Od. 12.14.
3 sing. aor. ἐστήριξε Il. 4.443. στήριξε Il. 11.28.
To set, fix : οὐρανῷ ἐστήριξε κάρη Il. 4.443. Cf. Il. 11.28.
In pass., to be propped against something, lean upon it. Fig. : πάντῃ κακὸν κακῷ ἐστήρικτο (one trouble followed closely on another) Il. 16.111.
In mid., to plant oneself firmly, find firm footing : οὐδὲ πόδεσσιν εἶχε στηρίξασθαι Il. 21.242.
So intrans. for reflexive : οὐδέ πῃ εἶχον στηρίξαι ποσίν Od. 12.434.
In comp. : δίσκον στιβαρώτερον ἢ οἵῳ φαίηκες ἐδίσκεον Od. 8.187.
Of weapons, strongly made, stout : ἔγχος Il. 16.141= Il. 19.388, Il. 16.802, Il. 5.746= Il. 8.390 := Od. 1.100. Cf. Il. 22.307.
Strong, stout, capable of resisting great force : σάκος Il. 3.335= Il. 16.136= Il. 19.373, Il. 18.478, 609.
Strongly, stoutly, so as to be capable of resisting great force : πύλας πύκα στιβαρῶς ἀραρυίας Il. 12.454.
To be bright or resplendent, shine : κάλλεΐ τε στίλβων καὶ εἵμασιν Il. 3.392, χιτῶνας ἦκα στίλβοντας ἐλαίῳ (glossy) Il. 18.596. Cf. Od. 6.237.
Elsewhere only in nom. pl. στίχες and acc. στίχας.

A line or rank of foot-soldiers or charioteers : Φωκήων στίχας ἵστασαν Il. 2.525, ἵππους ἔρυξαν ἐπὶ στίχας Il. 3.113. Cf. Il. 3.196, Il. 4.90, Il. 7.61, Il. 11.91, Il. 15.279, Il. 17.84, Il. 20.362 (i.e. the enemy's line of battle), etc. : Od. 1.100.
Of hunters drawn up in line Il. 12.47, 48.
A regiment or detachment of troops : τῆς ἰῆς στιχὸς ἦρχε Μενέσθιος Il. 16.173.
To go, take or make one's way, proceed, march : εἰς ἀγορήν Il. 2.92. Cf. Il. 3.266 = 341, Il. 4.432, Il. 18.577.
Of a ship, to make her way, sail Il. 2.516 = 680 = 733, Il. 2.602.

div.head: a
div.p: The mouth of a harbour, the entrance to it Od. 10.90.

div.head: b
div.p: The mouth of a passage, the opening by which one enters or leaves it : σ. λαύρης Od. 22.137.

div.head: c
div.p: The mouth or outfall of a river : ὅτε δὴ ποταμοῖο κατὰ σ. ἷξεν Od. 5.441. Cf. Il. 12.24.

div.head: d
div.p: The front, i.e. the point, of a weapon : ξυστὰ κατὰ σ. εἱμένα χαλκῷ Il. 15.389.

div.head: e
div.p: ἠϊόνος στόμα Il. 14.36 (the two containing capes being app. likened to jaws, and the curving shore to the hollow of the mouth).

div.head: f
div.p: πτολέμοιο σ. Il. 10.8 (war being app. likened to the jaws of a devouring monster). Cf. Il. 19.313, Il. 20.359.
The throat : κατὰ στομάχοιο θέμεθλα Il. 17.47.
To groan or moan : ἁδινὸν στοναχῆσαι Il. 18.124.
Causing groanings, woeful, pitiable : κήδεα Od. 9.12.
Epithet of missile weapons : βέλεα Il. 8.159= Il. 15.590, Il. 17.374 : Od. 24.180. Cf. Od. 21.12, 60.
Sim. of battle : Τρώων ἀϋτήν Od. 11.383.
Marked by or associated with groanings : ἀοιδήν (dolorous) Il. 24.721 : εὐνήν, ἥ μοι στονόεσσα τέτυκται (whereon I lie and make lament) Od. 17.102= Od. 19.595.
A groaning or moaning : τῶν σ. ὄρνυτο Il. 10.483, Il. 21.20 : Od. 22.308, Od. 24.184. Cf. Od. 23.40.
The agony of strife or conflict : ὀφέλλουσα στόνον ἀνδρῶν Il. 4.445. Cf. Il. 19.214.
To give a smooth or level surface to, dispose evenly : ἀνθρακιήν Il. 9.213.
To spread (bedding) : εὗδʼ, ὑπὸ δʼ ἔστρωτο ῥινὸν βοός Il. 10.155. Cf. Il. 24.645 := Od. 4.298= Od. 7.337, Od. 13.73, Od. 20.2.
Sim. of spreading something to sit upon : δέρμα αἰγός Od. 14.50.
To prepare (a bed) by spreading the bed-clothes, make (it) up : λέχος Il. 9.621, 659, 660. Cf. Il. 24.648 : Od. 4.301, Od. 7.340= Od. 23.291, Od. 23.171, 177.
Absol., to make one's bed : χαμάδις στορέσας Od. 19.599.
To be on a campaign, be in the field : παρʼ ὄχθας σαγγαρίοιο Il. 3.187. Cf. Il. 4.378.

An army or host, encamped, on the move, or in the field : νοῦσον ἀνὰ στρατὸν ὦρσεν Il. 1.10, ἅλιον στρατὸν ἤγαγεν ἐνθάδʼ Ἀχαιῶν Il. 4.179, ἐπὶ δεξιόφιν παντὸς στρατοῦ Il. 13.308. Cf. Il. 1.53, Il. 2.207, Il. 5.495, Il. 9.78, Il. 11.730, Il. 13.38, Il. 16.73, Il. 19.352, Il. 24.112, etc. : Od. 2.30, 42, Od. 11.559, Od. 20.89, Od. 24.81.
Including the hosts on both sides of a conflict : ἐς στρατὸν ἐλθὲ Τρῶας καὶ Ἀχαιούς Il. 4.70.
A number or host (of men) : ὀλλύντʼ Ἀργείων πουλὺν στρατόν Il. 8.472.
Turning easily : στρεπτὴ γλῶσσʼ ἐστὶ βροτῶν (capable of uttering all kinds of speech, voluble, glib) Il. 20.248.

Epithet of
the χιτών Il. 5.113, Il. 21.31.
Yielding to influence, open to entreaty or reason : στρεπταὶ φρένες ἐσθλῶν Il. 15.203. Cf. Il. 9.497.
To be subjected to continual pressure or adverse influence, be pressed or squeezed to exhaustion : δηθὰ στρεύγεσθαι ἐν δηϊοτῆτι Il. 15.512.
Of a slow death by starvation Od. 12.351.
To cause to whirl round; in pass., of the eyes, to go wheeling round (in dizziness) : στρεφεδίνηθεν ὄσσε Il. 16.792.
(ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, μετα-, περι-, ὑπο-)
To turn, bend, deflect : εἰς Ἔρεβος στρέψας
To turn or guide (one's horses) in a specified direction : ἵππους ἐπὶ νῆα Od. 15.205.
To wheel (one's horses) round : ἵππους στρέψαι (so as to face the foe) Il. 8.168. Cf. Il. 13.396 and Il. 20.488 (in flight).
Absol., to wheel one's team round : ὁπότε στρέψαντες ἱκοίατο τέλσον ἀρούρης Il. 18.544. Cf. Il. 18.546.
Absol., to guide one's horses round something : αἰεὶ τέρμʼ ὁρόων στρέφει ἐγγύθεν Il. 23.323.
To wheel or turn (one's horses) so as to keep them in a desired relative position : ὅς οἱ σχεδὸν ἔστρεφε ἵππους Il. 17.699.
Absol. : ὑπὸ δʼ ἔστρεφον ἡνιοχῆες Il. 5.505.
To cause (a wind) to veer : ὅτʼ ἂψ θεοὶ οὖρον στρέψαν Od. 4.520.

div.head: a
div.p: To turn oneself about, turn round : πρώτῳ στρεφθέντι μεταφρένῳ ἐν δόρυ πῆξεν (i.e. turning his horses to flight) Il. 5.40, εὖτʼ ἔμελλε στρέψεσθʼ ἐκ χώρης ὅθι . . . Il. 6.516. Cf. Il. 5.575, Il. 12.428, Il. 15.645, Il. 16.308, 598, Il. 18.139 : Od. 16.352.
To turn one's body so that it lies face upwards : ἀώτου στρεφθεὶς ἐχόμην Od. 9.435.

div.head: b
div.p: To turn oneself hither and thither : ὡς ὅτʼ ἂν κάπριος στρέφεται Il. 12.42. Cf. Il. 12.47.
To turn one's recumbent body (this way and that), lie tossing : ἐστρέφετʼ ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα Il. 24.5.

div.head: c
div.p: Of a heavenly body, to revolve : αρκτον, ἥ τʼ αὐτοῦ στρέφεται Il. 18.488 := Od. 5.274.
Explained as a whippingtop : στρόμβον ὣς ἔσσευε βαλών Il. 14.413.
A whirl or whirling cloud (of dust) : ἐν (μετὰ) στροφάλιγγι κονίης Il. 16.775, Il. 21.503 : Od. 24.39.
To twist (yarn) into threads, spin (it) : ἠλάκατα Od. 18.315.
A rope or cord : ἐν στρόφος ἦεν ἀορτήρ (serving as a shoulder-strap) Od. 13.438= Od. 17.198= Od. 18.109.
To twist (yarn) into threads, spin (it) : ἠλάκατα στρωφῶσα Od. 6.53, 306, Od. 17.97. Cf. Od. 7.105.
In mid., to turn oneself hither and thither, go about, move about : πατρὸς κατὰ μέγαρα στρωφᾶσθαι Il. 9.463. Cf. Il. 13.557, Il. 20.422.
